findings.title: Spectral node in a same-family morph re-prepares the FFT (malloc/free) twice per sample and keeps the wet path silent
findings.problem: processSameFamily rebuilds the blended params every sample and calls blendedAdapter_.setParams(bp). interpolateParams starts fftSize at 0 (:497) and adds the truncated per-node terms `result.fftSize += static_cast<int>(w * p.fftSize)` (:606). With Spectral as the dominant node and any second Experimental-family node (Chaos, Formant, Granular, Fractal, Stochastic, or a second Spectral), the weights are rarely dyadic, so the sum lands one below the power of two. Example: 2 nodes at (0,0) and (1,0), cursor at (0.3,0), w = 0.845 / 0.155, gives 1730 + 317 = 2047. routeParamsToProcessor then sees `p.fftSize != spectral_.getFftSize()` (2047 != 2048) and calls spectral_.prepare(sampleRate_, 2047) (adapter.cpp:894-896). prepare rounds that back to 2048 (spectral_distortion.h:150-154), so the mismatch comes back on the next call. Because BandProcessor::process feeds L and R through the same MorphEngine (band_processor.h:487-488), this happens twice per sample per band.
findings.why_wrong: spectral_distortion.h:144 says prepare is 'NOT real-time safe (allocates memory)'. It calls stft_.prepare, which runs fft_.prepare: pffft_new_setup plus three pffft aligned mallocs (fft.h:157-166). It then calls Window::generate, which returns a new std::vector (stft.h:72, window_functions.h:282), and does the same for overlapAdd_. prepare also clears writeIndex_/samplesAvailable_ (stft.h:84-85), so the STFT never collects fftSize samples and SpectralDistortion::process returns 0.0f every call (spectral_distortion.h:243). Window::generate is not noexcept but is called from a noexcept prepare, so a bad_alloc on the audio thread ends in std::terminate. Integer fields must not be re-derived per sample in a way that differs from the processor's own canonicalised value.
findings.consequence: Normal use: morphing Spectral with any other Experimental type. Each band does about 88,200 malloc/free cycles per second at 44.1 kHz (more at higher rates), with pffft setup creation every time. The result is CPU spikes, xruns, and allocator contention with other plugins. The Spectral wet path outputs silence for the whole morph, so only the dry share (1-mix) and the other node's contribution are heard. Under memory pressure the host process aborts.
findings.suggested_fix: Treat fftSize (and the other int fields: magnitudeBits, iterations, stages) as discrete and take it from the dominant node, like the other discrete fields in interpolateParams. Also, never call spectral_.prepare from routeParamsToProcessor: prepare SpectralDistortion once at kMaxFFTSize in DistortionAdapter::prepare and add an RT-safe setFftSize(n <= prepared max) that only changes the active size and window index into preallocated buffers, or swap between preallocated instances. Test: a hidden [audit-probe] or unit case that builds a MorphEngine with nodes {Spectral, Chaos}, puts the cursor at (0.3,0) and processes 8192 samples. Assert that the output RMS is above 0 after fftSize samples. Count allocations with a global operator new hook (pattern used in other plugin RT tests) and assert zero during process().
findings.evidence: morph_engine.cpp:497 `result.fftSize = 0;` :606 `result.fftSize += static_cast<int>(w * static_cast<float>(p.fftSize));` :706-710 `blendedAdapter_.setType(nodes_[dominantNode].type); auto bp = interpolateParams(); ... blendedAdapter_.setParams(bp);`. distortion_adapter.cpp:893-896 `// Slot 1: FFT size — re-prepare if changed (allocates, but only on user param change) if (static_cast<std::size_t>(p.fftSize) != spectral_.getFftSize()) { spectral_.prepare(sampleRate_, ...p.fftSize); }`. spectral_distortion.h:150-157 round to pow2 then `fftSize_ = fftSize;`, :162 `stft_.prepare(...)`, :172-185 resize. fft.h:157 `setup_.reset(pffft_new_setup(...))`, :164-166 makeAlignedBuffer x3. stft.h:72 `window_ = Window::generate(window, fftSize, kaiserBeta);`, :84-85 index reset. band_processor.h:487-488 two process() calls on the same engine.
verifier_notes:
I traced the claim through the source and it holds up.

1. Family check. distortion_types.h:337-344 puts Chaos, Formant, Granular, Spectral, Fractal and Stochastic all in Experimental. With Spectral plus any of those, isSameFamily() returns true (morph_engine.cpp:385-397), so process() takes processSameFamily (:678-679).

2. Per-sample params. processSameFamily (:706-710) calls setType(dominant), then interpolateParams(), then blendedAdapter_.setParams(bp) on every sample. interpolateParams copies the dominant node's params (:419) and then sets result.fftSize = 0 (:497). It then adds `static_cast<int>(w * p.fftSize)` for each node whose weight is at least kWeightThreshold (:606). Each term is truncated on its own. The other node keeps the default fftSize = 2048 (distortion_adapter.h:179); processor_params.cpp:244 only writes fftSize for the Spectral type. Weights are normalized IDW values (:195-208, :227-240), and the snap to weight 1.0 only happens within kOnNodeThreshold = 0.001 (:23, :220-223). So almost every cursor position gives non-integer products, and the sum falls below a power of two: 0.845*2048 = 1730.56 -> 1730, plus 0.155*2048 = 317.44 -> 317, total 2047. It drops further when a third or fourth node is skipped by the threshold.

3. Re-prepare loop. setParams -> routeParamsToProcessor (distortion_adapter.cpp:173-175). For the Spectral case, `p.fftSize != spectral_.getFftSize()` (:894) leads to spectral_.prepare(sampleRate_, 2047) (:895). SpectralDistortion::prepare rounds up to 2048 and stores fftSize_ = 2048 (spectral_distortion.h:150-157), and getFftSize returns fftSize_ (:497-499). So the mismatch comes back on every call.

4. Allocation. prepare is documented as "NOT real-time safe (allocates memory)" (spectral_distortion.h:144). It calls stft_.prepare, which calls fft_.prepare: pffft_new_setup plus three makeAlignedBuffer calls (fft.h:157-166). stft_.prepare also does `window_ = Window::generate(...)` (a new vector) and resizes (stft.h). On top of that come overlapAdd_.prepare, the spectrum prepares and vector resizes.

5. Silent wet path. stft_.prepare resets writeIndex_ and samplesAvailable_ to 0 every time it runs. canAnalyze() therefore never becomes true, overlapAdd has no samples available, and SpectralDistortion::process returns 0.0f (spectral_distortion.h ~:233-250).

6. Twice per sample. BandProcessor::process calls morphEngine_->process(left) and then process(right) on the same engine (band_processor.h:487-488). Morph is enabled in normal use (processor.cpp:125-126).

The finding's arithmetic and call path are correct, and I found nothing that guards against or caches this. This is allocation on the audio thread at per-sample rate in ordinary use, and it also mutes the wet signal, so critical severity is justified.

I could not refute this. Every link in the claimed path is in the source, and nothing upstream guards it.

1. Same-family routing. distortion_types.h:337-344 puts Chaos, Formant, Granular, Spectral, Fractal and Stochastic in DistortionFamily::Experimental. MorphEngine::isSameFamily (morph_engine.cpp:385-397) only compares families and has no exception for Experimental. So process() (:675-679) sends any all-Experimental node set to processSameFamily. The comment at distortion_types.h:337 says "Experimental - Parallel blend with output crossfade". The code does not do that, so the comment does not document the current behaviour as a design decision; it shows the code differs from the stated intent.

2. Per-sample setParams with a truncated fftSize. processSameFamily (:706-710) calls setType(dominant), then interpolateParams(), then setParams(bp) on every sample. interpolateParams copies the discrete fields from the dominant node (:419). It then zeroes fftSize (:497) and accumulates `static_cast<int>(w * p.fftSize)` from every node above threshold (:606). Non-Spectral nodes keep the default fftSize of 2048 (distortion_adapter.h:179), and Spectral nodes hold a power of two from processor_params.cpp:244. With non-dyadic weights the truncated sum is not a power of two (for example 1730 + 317 = 2047).

3. Re-prepare on the audio thread. setParams (distortion_adapter.cpp:173-175) calls routeParamsToProcessor. When the dominant type is Spectral, :894-896 calls spectral_.prepare whenever p.fftSize != getFftSize(). spectral_distortion.h:150-157 rounds 2047 back up to 2048. The mismatch therefore comes back on every call. prepare is documented "NOT real-time safe (allocates memory)" (:144) and calls stft_.prepare, overlapAdd_.prepare and several vector resizes (:162-185). stft.h:72 regenerates the window, and stft.h:84-85 resets writeIndex_ and samplesAvailable_. So canAnalyze never becomes true, and process() returns 0.0f (spectral_distortion.h:243).

4. Doubled per sample. BandProcessor::process (band_processor.h:487-488) calls morphEngine_->process twice per sample, once for L and once for R. morphEnabled_ is forced true for every band (processor.cpp:125).

5. Nothing pins it. No test in plugins/disrumpo/tests uses Spectral inside a MorphEngine; Spectral appears only in the adapter and oversampling tests.

Reachability: a normal user action (Spectral plus any other Experimental node, cursor off a node and off any exact dyadic split) triggers it. The only escapes are the cursor sitting exactly on a node, or weights that make every w*fftSize an integer, and neither holds during a morph. Critical severity is justified: allocation runs at 2x the sample rate per band, and the Spectral wet path is silent.

I traced the full chain in the source and could not refute it. Severity stays critical.

1. The path is reachable in normal use. Spectral, Chaos, Formant, Granular, Fractal and Stochastic all map to DistortionFamily::Experimental (distortion_types.h:337-344). isSameFamily (morph_engine.cpp:385-397) therefore returns true, and MorphEngine::process (morph_engine.cpp:675-680) takes processSameFamily on every sample. The processor always enables morph (processor.cpp:125-126, processor_state.cpp:893-894), and BandProcessor calls morphEngine_->process once for L and once for R on the same engine (band_processor.h:487-488).

2. The fftSize truncation is real. interpolateParams copies the dominant node's params, zeroes fftSize (morph_engine.cpp:497), then sums `static_cast<int>(w * p.fftSize)` (morph_engine.cpp:606). With two nodes at 2048 and weights 0.845 / 0.155, that gives 1730 + 317 = 2047. Any non-dyadic weight pair truncates below the true sum. A 1024/2048 mix lands between powers of two. Weights below kWeightThreshold (0.001) are dropped without renormalising, which also pushes the sum low. Only a cursor exactly on a node, or a dyadic split, gives an exact power of two.

3. The adapter re-prepares on every call. processSameFamily calls setType(dominant), then setParams(bp) on every sample (morph_engine.cpp:706-710). setParams calls routeParamsToProcessor with no change guard (distortion_adapter.cpp:173-175). In the Spectral case it compares p.fftSize with spectral_.getFftSize() and calls spectral_.prepare on a mismatch (distortion_adapter.cpp:893-896). SpectralDistortion::prepare rounds 2047 up to 2048 and stores 2048 (spectral_distortion.h:147-157), so the mismatch returns on the next sample. The trigger condition is Spectral as the dominant node. If another Experimental type dominates, the Spectral case never runs.

4. Each prepare allocates and wipes state. stft_.prepare calls fft_.prepare, which runs pffft_new_setup plus three makeAlignedBuffer calls (fft.h:157-166). It also assigns a fresh Window::generate vector (stft.h:72) and resets writeIndex_/samplesAvailable_ (stft.h:84-85). overlapAdd_.prepare does the same. All of this sits inside a noexcept function, so a bad_alloc ends in std::terminate.

5. The wet output is silent. Because the STFT is reset before each pushSamples completes a frame, canAnalyze never becomes true and overlapAdd never has samples available. SpectralDistortion::process returns 0.0f (spectral_distortion.h:222-243).

Impact: per band, 2 x fs pffft setups (O(N) twiddle computation), 4+ aligned mallocs/frees, two window vectors and an O(N) bin-frequency loop (spectral_distortion.h:179-183), every sample. That is about 88k re-prepares per second per band at 44.1 kHz, multiplied by the band count and any oversampling. It cannot run in real time, so xruns are certain. On top of that, the Spectral contribution is silent for the whole morph. The critical rating fits.

findings.title: Selecting Spectral, moving its FFT slot, or the first Spectral sample allocates on the audio thread
findings.problem: DistortionAdapter::prepare prepares spectral_ with the BLOCK size as its FFT size: `spectral_.prepare(sampleRate, maxBlockSize)` (:84). BandProcessor passes maxBlockSize_*8 = 4096 (band_processor.h:111-112, 124-125). DistortionParams::fftSize defaults to 2048 (distortion_adapter.h:179), and the slot map yields 512..4096 (processor_params.cpp:244). These paths therefore reach spectral_.prepare (pffft setup, aligned mallocs, Window::generate vectors): (a) a kNodeType change to Spectral, which runs processParameterChanges -> setMorphNodes (processor_params.cpp:899) -> MorphEngine::setNodes -> adapters_[i].setParams (morph_engine.cpp:136-139) inside Processor::process; (b) any edit or automation of the Spectral FFT slot; (c) the first processSameFamily sample on blendedAdapter_ once Spectral is dominant, even with a single active node (morph_engine.cpp:706-710). The code comment admits 'allocates, but only on user param change'. User param changes arrive on the audio thread.
findings.why_wrong: The project rule (CLAUDE.md 'Real-Time Audio Thread Safety', constitution Principle II, and the processor.cpp:183 banner) forbids allocation in process(). processParameterChanges runs at processor.cpp:191-192 inside process(). spectral_distortion.h:144 marks prepare as not RT-safe. prepare also calls the non-noexcept Window::generate from a noexcept function, so a failed allocation terminates the host.
findings.consequence: Choosing the Spectral type, loading a preset that contains it, or automating its FFT size causes malloc/free plus pffft setup on the audio thread. That means dropouts in low-latency sessions and priority inversion on the allocator lock. Each first selection allocates twice: once for the node adapter and once for the blended adapter. Across 4 bands x 5 adapters this repeats on every preset change.
findings.suggested_fix: Prepare every SpectralDistortion at kMaxFFTSize (4096 is the plugin maximum) in DistortionAdapter::prepare and give it an RT-safe size switch over preallocated buffers, or pre-create one instance per supported size (512/1024/2048/4096) and select by index. Remove the prepare call from routeParamsToProcessor. Test: an allocation-counting test (operator new hook) that sends a kNodeType=Spectral change and then FFT-slot changes through Processor::process with a ParameterChanges mock, and asserts zero allocations.
findings.evidence: distortion_adapter.cpp:84 `spectral_.prepare(sampleRate, static_cast<size_t>(maxBlockSize));`. distortion_adapter.h:179 `int fftSize = 2048;`. band_processor.h:124-125 `morphEngine_->prepare(sampleRate * kMaxOversampleFactor, static_cast<int>(maxBlockSize_ * kMaxOversampleFactor));` with maxBlockSize_ = 512. processor_params.cpp:899 `bandProcessors_[band].setMorphNodes(cache.nodes, cache.activeNodeCount);`. morph_engine.cpp:136-139 setType/setParams for all 4 adapters. processor.cpp:191-192 processParameterChanges is called inside process().
verifier_notes:
I traced the call path in source and it holds.

1. distortion_adapter.cpp:84 prepares spectral_ with maxBlockSize. BandProcessor passes maxBlockSize_*8 to both distortion_ and MorphEngine (band_processor.h:111-112, 124-125). MorphEngine::prepare forwards that size to all 4 adapters and blendedAdapter_ (morph_engine.cpp:57-60). So spectral_ starts at 4096, while DistortionParams::fftSize defaults to 2048 (distortion_adapter.h:179).

2. routeParamsToProcessor, case Spectral (distortion_adapter.cpp:893-896), calls spectral_.prepare whenever p.fftSize != getFftSize(). The comment there admits it allocates. SpectralDistortion::prepare (spectral_distortion.h:144-185) is documented "NOT real-time safe". It calls stft_/overlapAdd_/spectrum prepare and four std::vector::resize calls, all inside a noexcept function.

3. The path runs on the audio thread. Processor::process calls processParameterChanges (processor.cpp:191-192). A node-param change ends in bandProcessors_[band].setMorphNodes (processor_params.cpp:899). That calls BandProcessor::setMorphNodes, then MorphEngine::setNodes, then adapters_[i].setType/setParams for all 4 adapters (morph_engine.cpp:136-139). setParams calls routeParamsToProcessor (distortion_adapter.cpp:173-175). The FFT slot maps to 512..4096 (processor_params.cpp:244). So claims (a) and (b) are confirmed.

4. Claim (c) is confirmed and is worse than stated. MorphEngine::process runs per sample (morph_engine.cpp:686-688). processSameFamily calls blendedAdapter_.setParams(interpolateParams()) on every sample (morph_engine.cpp:706-710). interpolateParams computes fftSize as a sum of per-node static_cast<int>(w * fftSize) terms (morph_engine.cpp:606). Truncation and the kWeightThreshold skip mean that sum is usually not a power of two. Example: weights 0.3/0.7 over 2048 give 614 + 1433 = 2047. prepare() rounds that up to 2048 (spectral_distortion.h:151-154), so the next sample still sees 2047 != 2048 and prepares again. Whenever Spectral is the dominant node in an all-Experimental-family morph (Spectral shares a family with Formant/Granular/Fractal/Stochastic, distortion_types.h:143-147) and the cursor sits between nodes, the code reallocates and re-prepares the STFT on every sample. That is not just a one-off malloc on a parameter change.

I found no guard, preallocation, or deferral anywhere on this path. Severity upgrade: the per-sample re-prepare in (c) turns a one-off allocation on parameter changes into continuous allocation and a reset of the Spectral state on every sample.

I could not refute this. The source confirms it, and one path is worse than the finding says.

(1) The prepare size is wrong at setup. distortion_adapter.cpp:84 prepares spectral_ with maxBlockSize as the FFT size. band_processor.h:111-112 and 124-125 pass maxBlockSize_*kMaxOversampleFactor, where kMaxOversampleFactor = 8 (band_processor.h:47). That gives 4096 at a 512 host block and 8192 (clamped by spectral_distortion.h:148) at 1024 or more. DistortionParams::fftSize defaults to 2048 (distortion_adapter.h:179), so the first time params are routed for the Spectral type, the size check fails.

(2) The re-prepare runs on the audio thread. routeParamsToProcessor Spectral case, distortion_adapter.cpp:893-896: `if (p.fftSize != spectral_.getFftSize()) spectral_.prepare(...)`. The comment there admits it allocates. That prepare (spectral_distortion.h:144-184) is documented "NOT real-time safe": it calls stft_/overlapAdd_.prepare, inputSpectrum_/outputSpectrum_.prepare, and vector resizes. It is reached from setParams (:173-175). The callers are:
- processParameterChanges -> setMorphNodes (processor_params.cpp:899 and :954), then MorphEngine::setNodes -> adapters_[i].setParams (morph_engine.cpp:137-138), all inside process();
- MorphEngine::processSameFamily, which calls blendedAdapter_.setParams(bp) on EVERY SAMPLE (morph_engine.cpp:662-679, 706-710);

I found no guard: no RT-safe size switch, nothing preallocated at the maximum size, and no deferral to the UI thread or setActive.

(3) An aggravating path makes this worse than the finding claims. interpolateParams blends fftSize as `result.fftSize += static_cast<int>(w * p.fftSize)` (morph_engine.cpp:606). Each term is truncated, and nodes under kWeightThreshold are skipped. Two Spectral nodes at weights 0.3/0.7 and 2048 give 614 + 1433 = 2047. prepare() rounds that up to 2048 (spectral_distortion.h:151-154), so getFftSize() = 2048 != 2047. The check at :894 then fails on every sample: the blended adapter allocates and resets its STFT state once per sample while morphing between Spectral nodes. That costs CPU, allocates continuously, and corrupts the output. It goes beyond "first sample / on param change", so I recommend an upgrade.

The defect is real, and on the impact lens it is worse than the finding says.

Paths that reach the allocation:
- distortion_adapter.cpp:84 prepares spectral_ with maxBlockSize. BandProcessor sets that to 512*8 = 4096 (band_processor.h:111-112, 124-125). MorphEngine also prepares blendedAdapter_ (morph_engine.cpp:60).
- DistortionAdapter::setParams calls routeParamsToProcessor (distortion_adapter.cpp:173-175). In its Spectral case (:893-896) it calls spectral_.prepare whenever p.fftSize != getFftSize().
- spectral_distortion.h:144 marks prepare "NOT real-time safe (allocates memory)". It prepares the STFT and overlap-add stages (stft.h:78/81/266/269 vector::resize), resizes the SpectralBuffers (spectral_buffer.h:63-65), and resizes the phase, frequency and zero vectors (:172-185).
- processParameterChanges runs inside process() (processor.cpp:190-192). It calls setMorphNodes (processor_params.cpp:899), which reaches MorphEngine::setNodes. That calls setType/setParams on every adapter (morph_engine.cpp:136-139).
- So claims (a) and (b) hold: choosing Spectral or moving the FFT slot (processor_params.cpp:244, 512-4096) allocates on the audio thread. The default fftSize is 2048 (distortion_adapter.h:179) while the adapter is prepared at 4096, so the first Spectral setParams always re-prepares.

Why this is an upgrade:
- processSameFamily calls blendedAdapter_.setParams(interpolateParams()) on every sample (morph_engine.cpp:706-710, via processBlock :685-687). interpolateParams builds fftSize as a sum of truncated ints, `result.fftSize += static_cast<int>(w * p.fftSize)` (morph_engine.cpp:606), starting from 0 (:497).
- prepare rounds the size up to a power of two (spectral_distortion.h:150-154).
- Example: two Spectral nodes, both at FFT 2048, cursor weights 0.7/0.3. The sum is 1433 + 614 = 2047. prepare stores 2048, so 2047 != 2048 holds on every sample. The same happens with nodes at 2048/4096 and weights 0.5/0.5 (sum 3072, stored 4096).
- Spectral shares DistortionFamily::Experimental with Chaos, Formant, Granular, Fractal and Stochastic (distortion_types.h:337-341), and isSameFamily only compares that enum (morph_engine.cpp:385-397). So the same thing happens when Spectral is the dominant node beside any other Experimental node. That node keeps its default fftSize of 2048 in the weighted sum.
- Result: in an ordinary morph position the plugin re-prepares the STFT on every sample, which means hundreds of thousands of malloc/free calls per second. Each prepare also resets the STFT and overlap-add state, so the Spectral output is broken or near-silent, on top of the CPU spike and dropouts.

This is not limited to "the first sample". It is a sustained per-sample audio-thread allocation that the morph cursor alone triggers.

findings.title: Processor::setState mutates live DSP objects from the host thread with no handoff (data race, possible use-after-free)
findings.problem: setState runs on the host/UI thread and writes directly into objects the audio thread is using inside process(). It calls bandProcessors_[b].setGainDb/setPan/setMute (:440-442) and crossoverL_/R_.setCrossoverFrequency + setBandCount (:455-463), which reconfigure biquads and change numBands_ while crossoverL_.process runs (processor.cpp:473-474). It calls setMorphMode / setMorphSmoothingTime (:827-831), which reconfigure the smoothers. It calls setMorphNodes (:894), which overwrites MorphEngine::nodes_ (about 4 x 500 B structs) while interpolateParams reads them per sample, and calls setType/setParams on the adapters. For a Spectral node that reaches spectral_.prepare, which frees and replaces the pffft setup and buffers the audio thread may be inside. It calls modulationEngine_.setRouting (:798) while evaluateRoutings iterates, and it mutates customCurve_ with remove/add/sort (:552-569). bandMorphCache_ is also written by processParameterChanges on the audio thread. None of this is guarded by an atomic flag, a lock-free queue or a double buffer.
findings.why_wrong: VST3 hosts may call IComponent::setState while the component is active and processing: host preset load, undo, and project-level preset switches. The plugin must hand state to the audio thread (lock-free FIFO / pending-state swap applied at the top of process()) or otherwise make it safe. Only the three global atomics (:400-402) and bandCount_ are atomic. Every other write is a plain non-atomic race, which is undefined behaviour in C++.
findings.consequence: Loading a project-level preset while the transport runs can (a) tear MorphNode params mid-sample and give garbage types or parameters for a block, (b) make the crossover cascade run with half-updated band count and coefficients, causing clicks and a broken sum, and (c) for a Spectral node, crash the host with a use-after-free in pffft when fft_.prepare frees setup_ under the audio thread. Intermittent and hard to reproduce, which is typical for host-crash reports.
findings.suggested_fix: Parse the stream into a ProcessorStateSnapshot on the calling thread and publish it via an atomic pointer / SPSC slot. Apply it at the start of process(). This also fixes the setupProcessing-after-setState ordering problem. Never call prepare-class methods from setState. Test: an integration test that runs process() on one thread in a loop while another thread repeatedly calls setState with a v12 stream containing Spectral nodes and 4 bands. Run it under ASan/TSan (tests already support ASan) and assert no crash or NaN output.
findings.evidence: processor_state.cpp:440-442 `bandProcessors_[b].setGainDb(bs.gainDb); ... setMute(bs.mute);` :455-456 `crossoverL_.setCrossoverFrequency(c, freq);` :462-463 `crossoverL_.setBandCount(bandCount);` :827-831 setMorphMode / setMorphSmoothingTime :894-897 `bandProcessors_[b].setMorphNodes(...); setMorphPosition(...)` :552-569 customCurve_ remove/add/setBreakpoint. Compare processor.cpp:473-494, where the same objects are used per sample. morph_engine.cpp:131-140 setNodes overwrites nodes_ and calls setParams, which can reach distortion_adapter.cpp:895 spectral_.prepare (fft.h:157 setup_.reset).
verifier_notes:
I traced the claim through the code and could not refute it.

(1) The SDK allows this call pattern. extern/vst3sdk/pluginterfaces/vst/ivstcomponent.h:198-200 annotates setState as "[UI-thread & (Initialized | Connected | Setup Done | Activated | Processing)]", so a host may call it on the UI thread while process() runs.

(2) There is no handoff. A grep of plugins/disrumpo/src/processor for mutex, try_lock, pending, atomic_flag and stateLoad finds only the "NEVER use locks" comments (processor.h:13, processor.cpp:184). There is no pending-state slot or flag of any kind.

(3) setState writes live DSP objects directly:
- processor_state.cpp:440-442: bandProcessors_[b].setGainDb/setPan/setMute.
- :455-456: crossoverL_/R_.setCrossoverFrequency.
- :462-463: setBandCount.
- :798: modulationEngine_.setRouting.
- :827, :831: setMorphMode and setMorphSmoothingTime. MorphEngine::setSmoothingTime (morph_engine.cpp:125-129) reconfigures smootherX_/Y_.
- :894-897: setMorphNodes and setMorphPosition.
- :552-569: customCurve_ removeBreakpoint/addBreakpoint/setBreakpoint.
- :824-861: bandMorphCache_ written in place.

The same objects are used per sample at processor.cpp:473-474 (crossoverL_/R_.process) and :487/:494 (bandProcessors_[b].process).

(4) The use-after-free path exists. MorphEngine::setNodes (morph_engine.cpp:131-140) copies nodes_ wholesale and calls adapters_[i].setType/setParams. DistortionAdapter::setParams (distortion_adapter.cpp:173-175) calls routeParamsToProcessor. For a Spectral node, that reaches :894-895, which calls spectral_.prepare(sampleRate_, fftSize) whenever the FFT size differs. The code's own comment there says "allocates". That frees and replaces FFT buffers the audio thread may be inside at that moment.

Only inputGain_/outputGain_/globalMix_ (:400-402) and bandCount_ (:413) are atomic. Every other write is an unsynchronized data race with process(). The crash scenario needs a Spectral node whose FFT size changes during a preset load while audio is running. Hosts can do this (project preset switch, undo), so I keep the severity at high.

I could not refute this. Processor::setState (processor_state.cpp:361-920) writes straight into live DSP objects. Nothing synchronises those writes, and nothing documents them as a design decision.

What setState writes, with no handoff:
- Band gain, pan and mute, through bandProcessors_[b].setGainDb/setPan/setMute (:440-442).
- Crossover frequencies and band count, through crossoverL_/R_.setCrossoverFrequency (:455-456) and setBandCount (:462-463).
- The modulation routings, through modulationEngine_.setRouting (~:798).
- Morph mode and smoothing time, through setMorphMode and setMorphSmoothingTime (:827-831). MorphEngine::setSmoothingTime (morph_engine.cpp:125-129) reconfigures smootherX_/Y_ in place.
- The morph nodes, through setMorphNodes and setMorphPosition (:894-897). MorphEngine::setNodes (morph_engine.cpp:131-140) overwrites nodes_ and calls adapters_[i].setType/setParams/setCommonParams.
- The cache bandMorphCache_[b], which processParameterChanges also writes on the audio thread.

Only inputGain_, outputGain_, globalMix_ (:400-402) and bandCount_ (:415) are atomic.

The Spectral reallocation path exists. In distortion_adapter.cpp:894-895, setParams calls spectral_.prepare when fftSize changes, and the comment there says "allocates, but only on user param change". That path assumes it runs on the audio thread or while the plugin is inactive.

What I checked for a guard, and did not find:
- processor.h and processor_state.cpp contain no lock, pending-state slot or atomic swap, and no threading note.
- No Disrumpo test covers calling setState at the same time as process.
- The VST3 threading model allows IComponent::setState on the UI thread while the component is in the Processing state, so a real host can reach this.
- Sibling plugins in the same repo hand state over explicitly: Profundum uses a seqlock restore in processor.cpp:1231-1267 and Seraphis uses a forcePushAllPending_ flag. That shows the project treats this as a real hazard, not an accepted design choice.

One caveat: setState only reaches spectral_.prepare (the use-after-free path) if the loaded node's params.fftSize differs from the current size. The underlying data race on nodes_, the crossover state and the smoothers is unconditional, so it is confirmed regardless. The "high" severity stands.

The race is real and nothing guards it. processor_state.cpp:361-919 (setState) has no lock, flag or handoff. The only synchronised writes are the atomics at :400-402 and bandCount_ at :413, and the processor holds no other synchronisation primitive (processor.h:139-277 lists only std::atomic members). setState writes straight into live objects: bandProcessors_[b].setGainDb/setPan/setMute (:440-442), crossoverL_/R_.setCrossoverFrequency (:455-456) and setBandCount (:462-463), setMorphMode/setMorphSmoothingTime (:827-831), modulationEngine_.setRouting (:798), and bandProcessors_[b].setMorphNodes (:894). The audio thread uses those same objects per sample in processor.cpp:466-494 (crossoverL_.process, bandProcessors_[b].process).

The crash path holds. setMorphNodes (band_processor.h:247-256) calls MorphEngine::setNodes (morph_engine.cpp:131-152). setNodes copies nodes_ wholesale, then for each adapter calls setType first, which publishes currentType_=Spectral to the audio thread without synchronisation (distortion_adapter.cpp:142-149), and then setParams -> routeParamsToProcessor. That reaches distortion_adapter.cpp:894-895, `if (p.fftSize != spectral_.getFftSize()) spectral_.prepare(...)`.

The prepare actually fires on the host thread. DistortionAdapter::prepare calls spectral_.prepare(sampleRate, maxBlockSize) (distortion_adapter.cpp:84), so the FFT size equals the host block size. setState never calls mapShapeSlotsToParams (only processor_params.cpp:852/892 do), so a loaded Spectral node carries the default params.fftSize=2048 (distortion_adapter.h:179). With any block size other than 2048, the first setState that adds a Spectral node runs a re-allocating prepare on the host thread. In that window the audio thread can already see currentType_==Spectral and call into spectral_.process. The window is microseconds wide, but it is a real use-after-free.

The other consequences are glitch-level: torn biquad coefficients, half-copied MorphNode params, and a routing that is only partly written. The out-of-bounds risk is limited because bandsL/bandsR are fixed kMaxBands arrays and numBands is read once per block.

Hosts do trigger this: the VST3 SDK allows IComponent::setState from the UI thread while the component is active and processing (Reaper FX preset changes, host preset browsers). C++ undefined behaviour plus a reachable host crash on preset load during playback justifies high. No severity change.

findings.title: disconnect() destroys dataExchange_ that the audio thread dereferences in sendSpectrumBlock with no synchronisation
findings.problem: sendSpectrumBlock (called every block from processor.cpp:514) reads the plain std::unique_ptr dataExchange_ and calls getCurrentOrNewBlock()/sendCurrentBlock() on it. disconnect() on the UI thread calls dataExchange_->onDisconnect(other) and then dataExchange_.reset(). No atomic, flag or ordering ties the two together, and process() does not check whether the component is active. The SDK's fallback MessageHandler frees its aligned blocks in closeQueue (dataexchange.cpp:107-124).
findings.why_wrong: IConnectionPoint::disconnect is a UI-thread call. Nothing guarantees that every host has stopped process() first. A raw owning pointer read on one thread and reset on another is a data race (UB). If it happens mid-block the audio thread writes into a freed SpectrumBlock or calls through a destroyed handler.
findings.consequence: A host that tears down connections before setProcessing(false)/setActive(false), or on hot plugin removal or re-routing, can crash with a use-after-free in the spectrum send path. Rare but fatal.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not reset dataExchange_ in disconnect while active. Defer destruction to terminate()/setActive(false), or guard with an std::atomic<bool> spectrumSendEnabled_ that disconnect clears with release order before resetting (and that process reads with acquire), plus a handshake. Mirror whatever the other Krate plugins with DataExchange do so the fix is consistent. Test: a lifecycle test that calls disconnect while a worker thread loops process(), run under ASan.
findings.evidence: processor_messaging.cpp:78-81 `if (dataExchange_) { dataExchange_->onDisconnect(other); dataExchange_.reset(); }`. :124 `if (!dataExchange_) return;` :127 `auto block = dataExchange_->getCurrentOrNewBlock();` :146 `dataExchange_->sendCurrentBlock();`. processor.cpp:514 calls sendSpectrumBlock every block.
verifier_notes:
The code does match the description. processor_messaging.cpp:78-81 calls onDisconnect and then dataExchange_.reset(). Lines 124/127/146 read dataExchange_ in sendSpectrumBlock with no atomic. processor.cpp:514 calls sendSpectrumBlock every block. So the data race exists only if a host calls IConnectionPoint::disconnect while process() is running on another thread, and nothing I read shows that can happen.

(1) The documented VST3 lifecycle tears a plugin down in this order: setProcessing(false), setActive(false), disconnect, terminate. ivstmessage.h:81-83 marks disconnect as a UI-thread teardown call. Routing changes go through setBusArrangements/activateBus, not the component-controller connection, so the "hot removal or re-routing" scenario is asserted without evidence. The audio thread is also not running sendSpectrumBlock between deactivation and disconnect: processor.cpp:172-175 calls dataExchange_->onDeactivate() in setActive(false), before any disconnect.

(2) This is Steinberg's own reference pattern. hostcheckerprocessor.cpp:877-882 and the dataexchange sample (processor.cpp:229) call onDisconnect with no synchronisation. onDisconnect -> closeQueue (dataexchange.cpp:328-334) frees the queue blocks, so the SDK's own design already assumes disconnect never overlaps process(). The extra reset() adds no new reachable hazard.

(3) Every Krate plugin with DataExchange uses the same disconnect pattern: Innexus processor_messages.cpp:65-66, Membrum processor.cpp:1168-1171, Seraphis processor.cpp:1223-1228. Profundum's queueState_ release-store (processor.cpp:370) does not close the race either: the audio thread can pass the gate before the reset. So the consistent fix the finding asks for does not exist anywhere in the codebase.

I could not positively confirm a reachable failure; it depends on a host behaviour that the documented call sequence rules out. At most this is a low-severity hardening note, not a medium defect.

I could not confirm this as a Disrumpo defect. It follows the SDK's own lifecycle contract, the SDK sample does the same thing, and so does every other Krate plugin.

(1) Disrumpo's disconnect (plugins/disrumpo/src/processor/processor_messaging.cpp:78-82) calls onDisconnect and then reset(). The SDK's own onDisconnect (extern/vst3sdk/public.sdk/source/vst/utility/dataexchange.cpp:328-334) already calls closeQueue() (dataexchange.cpp:107-124), which frees every aligned block and nulls exchangeHandler. So the SDK's DataExchangeHandler assumes disconnect never runs while process() is running. Steinberg's own sample does the same: public.sdk/samples/vst/dataexchange/source/processor.cpp:227-230 calls audioBlockProcessor.onDisconnect(other) with no guard. Any race here would be inside the SDK utility itself, and the reset() adds nothing to it.

(2) Disrumpo also closes the queue on deactivate. processor.cpp:168/174 calls dataExchange_->onActivate / onDeactivate in setActive. VST3 only allows process() between setActive(true) and setActive(false), and connections are torn down during teardown after deactivation and before terminate. Moving a plugin's audio routing in a host does not disconnect the component from its controller. So the scenario is a host breaking the VST3 call order, which no conforming host does.

(3) The pattern is the same across the repo on purpose: innexus processor_messages.cpp:65-66, membrum processor.cpp:1170-1171, vorago processor.cpp:298-300, profundum processor.cpp:372-373 and seraphis processor.cpp:1224-1228 all call onDisconnect and then reset() in disconnect(). Seraphis and Vorago carry comments saying the reset is intended ("Released, not merely idled").

There is no Disrumpo-specific fault here. The case depends on a non-conforming host. Under a conforming host the SDK's own onDisconnect would be just as unsafe as the reset, so the claim does not hold as a plugin bug.

The code is as quoted. processor_messaging.cpp:78-81 calls onDisconnect then reset(); sendSpectrumBlock reads dataExchange_ at :124/:127/:146; processor.cpp:514 calls it from process(). But the claimed consequence, a use-after-free in a real host, cannot happen under the VST3 component lifecycle.

1. The queue is tied to activation. processor.cpp:167-168 calls onActivate (which opens the queue) in setActive(true), and :173-174 calls onDeactivate (which closes it and frees the fallback blocks) in setActive(false). The VST3 workflow ends with setProcessing(false) -> setActive(false) -> disconnect -> terminate. process() is only legal between setProcessing(true) and setProcessing(false), and disconnect comes after deactivation. So by the time disconnect runs, process() has stopped and the queue is already closed. onDisconnect's closeQueue (dataexchange.cpp:231-243) returns early when queueID is invalid, and reset() then frees an idle handler.

2. The SDK uses the same pattern and so assumes the same contract. HostCheckerProcessor::disconnect (extern/vst3sdk/public.sdk/samples/vst/hostchecker/source/hostcheckerprocessor.cpp:877-882) calls dataExchangeHandler->onDisconnect(other) with no synchronisation. That frees the queue's aligned blocks: the same memory the finding says the audio thread would write into. The extra reset() in Disrumpo only adds destruction of an already-closed handler. It opens no hazard that the SDK reference implementation does not already rely on hosts never triggering.

3. Membrum (plugins/membrum/src/processor/processor.cpp:1166-1174) and Innexus (processor_messages.cpp:65-66) use the identical disconnect+reset. So "mirror the other plugins" changes nothing, and no shipped host has shown this crash.

The hosts named (hot removal, re-routing) deactivate the component before tearing down its connections. IConnectionPoint connect/disconnect is the instantiation/teardown handshake, not a routing call. The scenario needs a non-conforming host that calls disconnect while process() is still running on another thread. That is a host spec violation, not a Disrumpo defect, and it would break the SDK sample too. Strictly speaking the unsynchronised unique_ptr is a theoretical data race, but it is not reachable under the documented lifecycle, so the "rare but fatal" medium-severity consequence does not hold.

findings.title: Default same-family path re-routes every adapter parameter twice per sample per band
findings.problem: MorphEngine::process runs once for L and once for R per sample (band_processor.h:487-488). Each call recomputes the IDW weights and isSameFamily. Any band whose nodes share a family takes processSameFamily, and that includes the default 1-node band. That path then runs setType + interpolateParams (about 120 fields, a 500 B struct by value) + setParams -> routeParamsToProcessor + setCommonParams -> toneFilter_.setCutoff, all per call. routeParamsToProcessor holds per-type coefficient work: Formant does two std::pow plus setVowel/setVowelBlend/filter updates (distortion_adapter.cpp:863-873), and AllpassResonant, FeedbackDist, Granular and Fractal have their own setter chains. In cross-family mode, any non-zero mod offset makes the same per-sample setParams loop run over all active adapters (:726-738). The work is bounded but scales as bands x 2 channels x samples x full parameter routing, all at host rate.
findings.why_wrong: Control-rate configuration (type selection, parameter routing, filter coefficient design) belongs at block rate or on change, not inside the per-sample inner loop. Per-sample std::pow and coefficient recomputation is the kind of avoidable audio-thread cost that the dsp-architecture performance budget (NFR CPU <15 % at 4 bands) does not allow for. It also makes setter side effects (crossfade restarts, state resets) run every sample, which is how the Spectral re-prepare above turned into a per-sample allocation.
findings.consequence: CPU use roughly doubles to several times what is needed with 4 bands of Formant/Allpass/Granular nodes, which raises xrun risk at small buffers and high sample rates. Any future setter that is not idempotent becomes a per-sample bug.
findings.suggested_fix: Compute weights, family and the interpolated params once per block, or when the smoothed cursor has moved more than a small epsilon, and only call setParams/setCommonParams when the result changes. Give L and R their own adapter or engine instances instead of advancing one engine twice. Measure with the existing performance tests (run alone via tools/run-cpu-tests.js) before and after.
findings.evidence: morph_engine.cpp:668-675 smoother.process + calculateMorphWeights + isSameFamily per call. :706 `blendedAdapter_.setType(...)` :708-710 `auto bp = interpolateParams(); ... blendedAdapter_.setParams(bp);` :716 `blendedAdapter_.setCommonParams(cp);`. distortion_adapter.cpp:173-175 setParams -> routeParamsToProcessor, :168-170 setCommonParams -> toneFilter_.setCutoff, :868-870 `std::pow(4.0f, ...)` x2. band_processor.h:487-488 `left = morphEngine_->process(left); right = morphEngine_->process(right);`
verifier_notes: The call path in the finding matches the source. band_processor.h:487-488 (base rate) and :753-754 (oversampled block) call morphEngine_->process() once for left and once for right on every sample. Morph mode is on by default: processor.cpp:125 calls setMorphEnabled(true), and morph_node.h:135 sets kDefaultActiveNodes = 1. MorphEngine::process (morph_engine.cpp:662-683) advances both smoothers, calls calculateMorphWeights (:170, which does weights_.fill plus the IDW loop) and isSameFamily on every call. isSameFamily (:385-388) returns true when activeNodeCount_ <= 1, so the default band always takes processSameFamily. That function (:691-719) runs the dominant-node search, blendedAdapter_.setType (distortion_adapter.cpp:142-161, which includes updateDCBlockerState), interpolateParams by value (its own second dominant-node search starts at :403), setParams, interpolateCommonParams and setCommonParams, all on each call. setParams (distortion_adapter.cpp:173-183) always calls routeParamsToProcessor. There is no early-out when values have not changed. For Formant that routing does two std::pow calls (:868, :870), plus setVowel and setVowelBlend, which forward into formantFilter_.setVowel/setVowelMorph (formant_distortion.h:208-225). Wavefolder types call std::pow inside wavefoldSmoothFilter_.setCutoff (:664-725), and Tape calls it in bodyFilter_ (:650). Granular, Fractal and Chaos each run their own setter chains (:851-930). setCommonParams (:168-171) calls toneFilter_.setCutoff (OnePoleLP) every time. In cross-family mode, any non-zero mod offset runs setCommonParams and setParams on every active adapter on every call (morph_engine.cpp:726-738). So the per-sample, per-channel control-rate routing the finding describes is real. Caveat: no CPU measurement was quoted, the work is bounded, and none of it allocates; the Spectral fftSize re-prepare at :909-911 only fires when the size changes. This is a real but unmeasured efficiency defect, not a correctness or RT-safety violation on its own, so I keep the stated medium severity rather than raise it.

The code does what the finding says, and I found no context that excuses it. band_processor.h:487-488 (and :753-754) call morphEngine_->process() once for L and once for R per sample. MorphEngine::process (morph_engine.cpp:662-683) runs the smoothers, calculateMorphWeights and isSameFamily on every call. The comment at :671 says "Recalculate weights if position changed", but no such check exists: calculateMorphWeights (:170-200) fills and recomputes the weights every time. isSameFamily (:385-388) returns true for activeNodeCount_ <= 1, so the default band takes processSameFamily. That path calls setType (:706), interpolateParams (:708, a full per-field weighted sum at :403-636), setParams (:710) and setCommonParams (:716) on every call, with no compare-before-set. On the adapter side, setCommonParams (distortion_adapter.cpp:168-171) always calls toneFilter_.setCutoff. setParams (:173-175) always calls routeParamsToProcessor. That routing does real per-type work: Formant has two std::pow plus setVowel/setVowelBlend (:862-874), RingSaturation one std::pow (:801), the folders and rectifiers std::pow for the smoothing cutoff (:664, :689, :699), AsymmetricFuzz std::pow (:650), and FeedbackDist, AllpassResonant, Granular and Fractal have their own setter chains (:812-938). The cross-family path re-routes every active adapter per call whenever any mod offset is non-zero (morph_engine.cpp:726-738). Nothing in the code or the specs documents this as a deliberate choice: specs/Disrumpo/dsp-details.md:2157 only says automation arrives at per-sample resolution, and nothing calls for re-routing at audio rate. No test pins the cost. The CPU tests in distortion_adapter_test.cpp (PT-DI-001/002/003, lines 1740/2128/2186) time adapters directly, not MorphEngine with Formant or Allpass nodes, and morph_weight_computation_test.cpp:205 times only the weight computation. So the defect stands. I recommend a downgrade because the impact is unmeasured. The work is bounded and does not allocate in the general case (the Spectral re-prepare at :894-896 runs only when fftSize changes, which is a separate finding). It breaks no hard real-time rule (no lock, allocation or I/O). It is an efficiency problem, not an rt-safety violation, and the "CPU doubles to several times" and xrun claims come with no number behind them.

The finding holds up under the impact lens. The redundant work is real and happens on every band by default, but no number backs the size of the CPU claim.

Default path:
- processor.cpp:125 calls setMorphEnabled(true) on every band at setup, and the default nodes (processor.cpp:114-121) are all SoftClip. So every band runs band_processor.h:485-488 (morphEngine_->process(left), then morphEngine_->process(right)).
- MorphEngine::process (morph_engine.cpp:662-683) advances the smoothers and recomputes calculateMorphWeights and isSameFamily on every call. It then enters processSameFamily (:691-719), which on every call runs:
  - setType (distortion_adapter.cpp:142-162: updateDCBlockerState plus a switch);
  - interpolateParams (morph_engine.cpp:403+: copies the whole DistortionParams struct by value, zeroes dozens of fields, then accumulates over the active nodes);
  - setParams, which goes to routeParamsToProcessor (distortion_adapter.cpp:173-175, 594+);
  - setCommonParams, which calls toneFilter_.setCutoff (:168-171).

The cost is worse than the finding says:
- On the oversampled paths, processOversampledBlock (band_processor.h:753-754) calls morphEngine_->process per OVERSAMPLED sample. That is 2x/4x/8x the host rate, not only bands x 2 channels x host samples.
- Per-type setter chains run per sample: two std::pow for Formant (distortion_adapter.cpp:868-870), one std::pow for AsymmetricFuzz, wavefold, rectify and Quantize (:650, 664, 673, 689, 699, 725), and RingSaturation in Fixed mode (:801). FeedbackDist, AllpassResonant, Granular and Chaos have their own setter chains (:812-886).
- In cross-family mode with any non-zero mod offset, the same full setParams/setCommonParams loop runs per sample over every active adapter (morph_engine.cpp:726-738).

Why the CPU tests miss it: the CPU-budget tests (distortion_adapter_test.cpp:1740, 2128, 2186, and oversampling_performance_tests.cpp) use a default BandProcessor or the bare adapter. band_processor.h:809 defaults morphEnabled_ to false, so none of them exercise the per-sample morph path.

Why not upgraded: I found no measurement of the actual overhead. For the default SoftClip type routeParamsToProcessor is a no-op (:605-607), so the cost there is mostly interpolateParams plus the tone-filter coefficient update. The "doubles to several times" figure is a plausible estimate, not a measured one. The setters I read look idempotent, so I see no correctness consequence beyond CPU. This is a bounded real-time efficiency defect, and medium fits. Severity unchanged.

findings.title: Each node-parameter change re-pushes all 4 nodes and re-routes 4 adapters, so a preset load does about 1000 full routings inside one process() call
findings.problem: Every node param (type, drive, mix, tone, bias, folds, bitDepth, each of the 10 shape slots) ends with bandProcessors_[band].setMorphNodes(cache.nodes, count) (:899). That copies the 4-node array twice (MorphEngine::nodes_ and BandProcessor::morphNodes_), calls setType+setParams+setCommonParams on all 4 adapters, recomputes the weights, and runs recalculateOversampleFactor/computeRawMorphWeights. A preset load or session restore through the controller (editParamWithNotify for all 272 node IDs) delivers every one of these in a single processParameterChanges call: 272 x 4 = 1088 routeParamsToProcessor calls, plus any Spectral re-prepares, before the first sample of that block.
findings.why_wrong: The processing cost of a block should not grow with the number of queued parameter changes times the adapter count. Changes should be coalesced, for example with a per-band dirty flag that is acted on once after the parameter loop.
findings.consequence: A CPU spike and likely dropout in the block where a preset loads, worst with 4 bands. Combined with the Spectral prepare path it multiplies allocations.
findings.suggested_fix: Set a per-band dirty bit in the node-param branch and call setMorphNodes once per dirty band after the parameter loop in processParameterChanges. Test: count setNodes calls (test hook or counter) for a ParameterChanges batch containing all node IDs of one band, and assert 1.
findings.evidence: processor_params.cpp:898-899 `// Push updated nodes to BandProcessor  bandProcessors_[band].setMorphNodes(cache.nodes, cache.activeNodeCount);` runs after every node-param switch. band_processor.h:247-255 setMorphNodes -> morphEngine_->setNodes + morphNodes_ copy + recalculateOversampleFactor. morph_engine.cpp:131-151 per-adapter setType/setParams/setCommonParams for all 4 plus calculateMorphWeights.
verifier_notes:
I could not refute the core claim; the source confirms it. In processor_params.cpp:830-899 every node-param case (type, drive, mix, tone, bias, folds, bitDepth, and the shape slots in the default branch at 880-895) falls through to `bandProcessors_[band].setMorphNodes(cache.nodes, cache.activeNodeCount)` at :899. Nothing is coalesced.

What one call costs:
- band_processor.h:247-255 setMorphNodes calls morphEngine_->setNodes, copies the array into morphNodes_, then runs recalculateOversampleFactor (:393-411). That function calls computeRawMorphWeights and calculateMorphOversampleFactor, then requestOversampleFactor.
- morph_engine.cpp:131-151 setNodes copies nodes_ and loops over all 4 adapters (setType, setParams, setCommonParams), then runs isSameFamily and calculateMorphWeights.
- distortion_adapter.cpp:173-175 setParams always calls routeParamsToProcessor (:594ff). Per type, that runs filter setCutoff calls (biquad coefficient math) and std::pow, for example at :650, :664, :868-870.
- distortion_adapter.cpp:170 setCommonParams also recomputes toneFilter_ cutoff.

Reachability: the controller preset-browser load path is controller.cpp:120-124, presetManager_ loadProvider -> loadComponentStateWithNotify (:1876-1896). It routes every parsed parameter through editParamWithNotify (:1868-1874), which calls performEdit. parseComponentState emits node IDs for every band and node: controller.cpp:553-565 covers type, drive, mix, tone, bias, folds and bitDepth, and :575 covers 10 shape slots. That is 17 x 4 nodes x 4 bands = 272 node IDs, which the host delivers to processParameterChanges in the following block or blocks. So the claim of 272 x 4 = 1088 adapter re-routings is accurate.

Overstated part: "multiplies allocations" through Spectral is wrong. distortion_adapter.cpp:894-896 calls spectral_.prepare only when p.fftSize differs from spectral_.getFftSize(). The redundant re-pushes carry unchanged params, so they do not re-prepare. Only the real fftSize change does, and it would do so even with coalescing.

The dropout consequence is an inference; no measurement was run. The work is bounded and does not allocate in the redundant pushes, so this is a CPU-spike and efficiency issue on a rare event (preset load), not a hard real-time-safety violation. "low" is the right severity.

I could not refute the mechanism. Nothing upstream coalesces these changes, the path is reachable in a real host, and no spec or code comment documents it as a design decision.

Mechanism, confirmed in source:
- processor_params.cpp:830-899: every node parameter (type, drive, mix, tone, bias, folds, bitDepth and shape slots 0-9, so 17 per node) ends with an unconditional `bandProcessors_[band].setMorphNodes(cache.nodes, cache.activeNodeCount)` at :899. There is no dirty flag and no deferral until after the parameter loop.
- band_processor.h:247-256: setMorphNodes calls morphEngine_->setNodes, copies the whole node array again into morphNodes_, then calls recalculateOversampleFactor() (:393-411). That runs computeRawMorphWeights (:576-615, with a sqrt per node) and requestOversampleFactor.
- morph_engine.cpp:131-152: setNodes copies nodes_, then for all 4 nodes (kMaxMorphNodes, not just the active ones) calls adapters_[i].setType, setParams and setCommonParams, then calculateMorphWeights.
- distortion_adapter.cpp:142-183, 594+: setParams always calls routeParamsToProcessor(), a per-type switch with several std::pow calls and filter setCutoff calls. setCommonParams calls toneFilter_.setCutoff.

Reachability, confirmed:
- controller.cpp:120-124: the preset manager's load provider is loadComponentStateWithNotify.
- controller.cpp:1876-1896: that function routes every parsed parameter through editParamWithNotify (:1868-1874), i.e. beginEdit/performEdit/endEdit.
- So a factory preset load sends every node ID to the processor as parameter changes. The host typically delivers them together in one processParameterChanges call: 4 bands x 4 nodes x 17 params = 272 changes, giving about 1088 adapter routings.
- The setState path is already coalesced (processor_state.cpp:894 calls setMorphNodes once per band), and so is setupActive (processor.cpp:126). Only the parameter-change path lacks it.
- I found no test that pins the call count.

Where the finding overstates:
- Each routing is cheap, bounded setter work. 1088 routings is roughly hundreds of microseconds, a spike rather than a certain dropout at normal buffer sizes. Very small buffers (32-64 samples) are at risk.
- "Multiplies allocations" is too strong. The Spectral re-prepare (distortion_adapter.cpp:893-896) only fires when fftSize differs from spectral_.getFftSize(). Repeat routings with an unchanged fftSize do nothing, so redundant pushes add at most an intermediate re-prepare while a node's type and slots arrive one by one; they do not add one per call. That allocation is its own defect.
- The per-change recalculateOversampleFactor can also start transient oversampling crossfades mid-load. That makes the coalescing fix more worthwhile, but it is not what this finding claims.

Low severity remains appropriate: a real, unbounded-by-design redundant-work pattern on the audio thread, with a modest real-world cost.

The redundant work is real. processor_params.cpp:898-899 calls bandProcessors_[band].setMorphNodes after every node param. band_processor.h:247-255 copies the nodes and runs recalculateOversampleFactor, and morph_engine.cpp:136-140 calls setType, setParams (which runs routeParamsToProcessor) and setCommonParams on all 4 adapters. What the finding gets wrong is the consequence: a CPU spike that likely causes a dropout.

1) Normal processing already does more of this same work in every block. BandProcessor calls morphEngine_->process once per sample per channel (band_processor.h:487-488 and :753-754). When all nodes are in the same family, MorphEngine::processSameFamily (morph_engine.cpp:706-716) calls blendedAdapter_.setType, setParams and setCommonParams on every one of those calls, so the full routing runs per sample. That is 2 x N x oversample-factor routings per band per block: 4096 per block at 512 samples with 4 bands and 1x, more with oversampling. With modulation active, processCrossFamily (morph_engine.cpp:726-737) also re-routes every active node per sample. The claimed 1088 extra routings, once per preset change, are a fraction of what every block already spends. At roughly 0.1-0.5 us per routing (a handful of setters, a few std::pow or filter-coefficient updates, distortion_adapter.cpp:594-909) that is about 0.1-0.5 ms, once. An extra cost that small, on a block that already carries several times that load, does not cause a dropout.

2) The claim that this "multiplies allocations" is false. The Spectral re-prepare is guarded by `if (fftSize != spectral_.getFftSize())` (distortion_adapter.cpp:894-896). Once it has prepared, repeated routings with the same params do not prepare again. Coalescing would remove at most one intermediate prepare, when a type change is followed by a different fftSize slot, and that allocation is a separate issue.

3) The trigger is narrower than the finding says. A host session restore or a host-side .vstpreset load goes through Processor::setState, which pushes nodes once per band (processor_state.cpp:894). Only the plugin's own preset browser, via Controller::loadComponentStateWithNotify -> editParamWithNotify (controller.cpp:1868-1896), sends the 272 node params as performEdits. The host may also spread those edits over several blocks rather than one.

The claimed consequence, a dropout at preset load with more allocations, does not follow at any meaningful level. The real CPU issue is the per-sample re-routing in processSameFamily, not the once-per-preset-change re-routing here.

findings.title: Same-family morph truncates fftSize to a non-power-of-2, so SpectralDistortion is re-prepared (pffft setup + vector alloc + state wipe) on every sample and its output is silent
findings.problem: interpolateParams starts result.fftSize at 0 and accumulates `static_cast<int>(w * fftSize)` per node, so every node's share is floored. For two nodes at fftSize 2048, w=0.6/0.4 gives 1228+819 = 2047, and so do w=0.7 and 0.9 (computed with float32 rounding). In processSameFamily the blended adapter is set to the dominant type and setParams(bp) runs on EVERY sample. When Spectral is dominant, routeParamsToProcessor compares 2047 with spectral_.getFftSize(). That returns 2048, because SpectralDistortion::prepare rounds up to a power of 2 (spectral_distortion.h:150-154). The two never match, so spectral_.prepare() runs on every call.
findings.why_wrong: A weighted mean of identical power-of-2 sizes must stay that size, and a discrete FFT size should come from the dominant node (as the other discrete fields do), not from a floored sum. prepare() is documented 'NOT real-time safe (allocates memory)': STFT::prepare calls Window::generate (returns a new std::vector, stft.h:72) and fft_.prepare calls pffft_new_setup (fft.h:157). It also resets samplesAvailable_ = 0 (stft.h:85), so canAnalyze() never becomes true and process() returns 0.0f.
findings.consequence: Any same-family morph in which a Spectral node is dominant (Spectral with Chaos, Formant, Granular, Fractal or Stochastic, or two Spectral nodes, all Experimental family), with the cursor anywhere except a few exact weights, does a heap allocation plus a pffft setup on every sample, twice per sample (L and R share the engine), for every band. The result is CPU spikes, dropouts, a hard RT violation, and a wet Spectral path that outputs silence instead of the effect.
findings.suggested_fix: Take fftSize (and magnitudeBits) from the dominant node, like spectralMode and the other discrete fields. If it must be interpolated, round to the nearest power of 2. Also compare the rounded value in the adapter, or cache the requested size so that an equal pow2 does not re-prepare, and never call prepare() from setParams on the audio thread. Test: a MorphEngine with 2 Spectral nodes at fftSize 2048, cursor at w=0.6, process 8192 samples; assert non-zero output RMS and that getFftSize() is stable. An allocation-counting hook around process() would catch the RT side.

Computed with fround: w=0.6 -> 2047, 0.7 -> 2047, 0.9 -> 2047, 0.5 -> 2048, 0.75 -> 2048.

Nodes below kWeightThreshold (0.001, morph_node.h:139) are skipped. I computed with Math.fround for two nodes at 2048. The sum is 2047 at w=0.6, 0.7, 0.9, 0.33 and 0.123, and 2048 only at 0.5 and 0.75. So almost every cursor position that is not on a node, or at a weight that gives exact integer shares, yields 2047.

The Spectral case at :894-896 compares `size_t(p.fftSize)` (2047) against `spectral_.getFftSize()`. SpectralDistortion::prepare rounds up to a power of 2 (spectral_distortion.h:150-154), so the stored size is 2048. The two never match, so prepare() runs on every sample.

The consequence holds: a hard real-time violation (allocation on the audio thread), likely CPU overload or dropouts, and a non-functional effect. It applies to any all-Experimental morph with a Spectral node dominant, which is a normal user configuration. No existing test covers a same-family Spectral morph; multi_node_distortion_test.cpp:564 only lists the type name. Critical severity is justified.

findings.title: Cross-family transition gain is discontinuous at weight 0.4 (jumps from 1.0 to 0.0), giving a -4.4 dB step mid-morph
findings.problem: calculateTransitionGain returns sin((w/0.4)*pi/2) for w<0.4, which reaches 1.0 as w approaches 0.4 from below. At w>=0.4 it switches to sin(((w-0.4)/0.2)*pi/2), which is 0.0 at w=0.4. The gain therefore drops from ~1 to 0 at w=0.4 and then ramps back to 1 at 0.6. processCrossFamily outputs sum(nodeOut * w * gain).
findings.why_wrong: A transition-zone gain has to be continuous and monotonic in the weight, or the morph clicks (FR-008, SC-002 within 1 dB, SC-003 artifact-free). The two branches do not meet at 0.4. Even away from the step, w*gain is not equal-power: at 0.5/0.5 the sum is 0.707.
findings.consequence: With 2 cross-family nodes of equal level, summed contributions are: wB=0.3999 -> 1.000 (0 dB), wB=0.4 -> 0.600 (-4.44 dB, instantaneous), 0.45 -> -3.35 dB, 0.5 -> -3.01 dB. The same step appears symmetrically near the other node. In Linear1D with nodes at x=0 and x=1, wB=0.4 sits at x~0.4495, so dragging, automating or LFO-modulating the morph cursor across it produces an audible level step and click on every pass. Any preset that morphs between families (for example SoftClip to Bitcrush) is affected.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the gain a single continuous function of w, for example a plain weight-normalized blend (gain=1, contributions w_i), or an equal-power law sqrt(w_i) normalized so that sum(g_i^2)=1. The <0.4 branch must end where the zone branch starts. Test: sweep the cursor in 1e-4 steps across x in [0.4,0.6] with 2 cross-family nodes fed a constant-level sine, and assert the per-step output RMS change is < 0.1 dB and the total level stays within 1 dB (SC-002).
findings.evidence: morph_engine.cpp:364-370 `if (weight < kTransitionZoneLow) { const float normalizedPos = weight / kTransitionZoneLow; ... equalPowerGains(normalizedPos, fadeOut, fadeIn); return fadeIn; }`; :374-378 `zonePos = (weight - 0.4)/(0.6-0.4); equalPowerGains(zonePos,...); return fadeIn;`. crossfade_utils.h:51-52 fadeIn = sin(position*pi/2). morph_engine.cpp:756 `output += nodeOutput * weight * gain;`. Computed: sum(w*g) = 1.0000 at wB=0.3999, 0.6000 at wB=0.4000, 0.7071 at 0.5. Linear1D wB=0.4 at x=0.4495. The only FR-008 test (morph_interpolation_test.cpp:313-343) asserts only that the weights sum to 1.

In calculateTransitionGain (352-379), any w in (0.001, 0.4) goes through the branch at 364-371: normalizedPos = w/0.4, then equalPowerGains returns fadeIn = sin(normalizedPos*pi/2) (crossfade_utils.h:50-53), which tends to 1.0 as w approaches 0.4 from below. At w=0.4 the zone branch at 374-378 takes over with zonePos=(w-0.4)/0.2=0, so fadeIn = sin(0) = 0. The two branches do not meet at 0.4: the gain falls from 1 to 0 there. calculateMorphWeights stores the gain per node at line 269. MorphEngine::process (662-683) recomputes it every sample from the smoothed cursor and sends cross-family node sets to processCrossFamily (721-760). That function skips a node whose gain is below the threshold (749) and otherwise adds nodeOutput*weight*gain (756). So with two equal-level nodes the sum is 0.3999*~1 + 0.6001*1 ~= 1.0 just below the boundary and 0 + 0.6*1 = 0.6 (-4.44 dB) at w=0.4. At 0.5/0.5 it is 2*0.5*sin(pi/4) = 0.707 (-3 dB). In Linear1D with nodes at 0 and 1, the inverse-square weights (195-207) give wB = x^2/(x^2+(1-x)^2), and wB=0.4 gives x = 0.8165/1.8165 = 0.4495, which matches the finding. The cursor smoothers (668-669) only slow the cursor down. The weight still crosses 0.4 between two samples, so the gain step lands inside one sample. findings.title: Adapter tone filter, DC blocker and morph smoothers use coefficients for 8x the sample rate but run at 1x (tone 4 kHz acts as about 500 Hz, max 8 kHz as about 1 kHz)
findings.problem: BandProcessor::prepare prepares morphEngine_ (and distortion_) at sampleRate * kMaxOversampleFactor (8). Every DistortionAdapter then calls toneFilter_.prepare(8*fs), dcBlocker_.prepare(8*fs, 10 Hz), and the tape-HF, body and wavefold-smooth filters at 8*fs, and MorphEngine configures its X/Y smoothers at 8*fs. The processor only ever calls the per-sample BandProcessor::process (1x), so these coefficients run at the host rate.
findings.why_wrong: OnePoleLP's coefficient is exp(-2*pi*fc/fs) (one_pole.h:138). With fs=8*fs_host and the filter clocked at fs_host, the real cutoff is fc/8. All Hz and ms quantities must be derived for the rate at which the filter is actually clocked.
findings.consequence: At 44.1 kHz the default tone of 4000 Hz becomes a ~500 Hz one-pole LP on every non-digital wet path, and the top of the range (8000 Hz) is ~1000 Hz. Because L and R are interleaved through the same engine, the per-channel figure is roughly 2x that for correlated signals, still far below the displayed value. The 10 Hz DC blocker becomes ~1.25 Hz (slow DC settling after bias changes on AsymmetricFuzz and the rectifiers). The morph smoothing time is 8x longer than set (halved again by the double L/R call), and tape flutter runs at 5.5/8 Hz. Disrumpo sounds heavily muffled and the Tone knob label is wrong by about 3 octaves.
findings.suggested_fix: Prepare the morph engine and adapters at the rate they are actually clocked: the host rate while the per-sample 1x path is live, or wire processBlock and re-prepare per factor. Do not prepare at 8x and run at 1x. Test: a processor-level render of a 1-band SoftClip node, drive 1, tone 8000 Hz, with a 4 kHz sine at -30 dBFS (linear region); assert output within 1 dB of input level. Today it reads about -12 dB.

Computed: a = exp(-2*pi*4000/352800) gives an effective 500.0 Hz at 44.1 kHz; 8000 Hz gives 1000.0 Hz.

How the 8x rate gets in: BandProcessor::prepare (band_processor.h:111-112) calls distortion_.prepare(sampleRate * kMaxOversampleFactor) and (band_processor.h:124-125) calls morphEngine_->prepare(sampleRate * kMaxOversampleFactor). kMaxOversampleFactor is 8 (band_processor.h:47). MorphEngine::prepare (morph_engine.cpp:51-52) configures smootherX_/smootherY_ at that rate and passes it to every adapter (morph_engine.cpp:57-60). DistortionAdapter::prepare (distortion_adapter.cpp:27-56) prepares toneFilter_, dcBlocker_ (10 Hz), tapeHfFilter_, bodyFilter_ and wavefoldSmoothFilter_ at the same rate. No code rescales cutoffs or times by the factor: a grep for oversampl* in distortion_adapter/morph_engine finds only doc comments.

How the filters actually run at 1x: Processor::process calls the per-sample bandProcessors_[b].process(bandL, bandR) at the host rate (processor.cpp:467-494, comment "FR-001a: sample-by-sample processing"). bandProcessors_[i].prepare(sampleRate_) receives the host rate (processor.cpp:106). BandProcessor::process (band_processor.h:473-496) calls morphEngine_->process / distortion_.process directly, with no oversampler. The oversampled path (processBlock -> processWithFactor -> processWithOversampling*, band_processor.h:519-760) exists, but processor.cpp never calls it.

Why the cutoff drops: OnePoleLP's coefficient is exp(-2*pi*fc/fs) with fs = 8*host (one_pole.h:138), and clampCutoff only limits fc to Nyquist (one_pole.h:141-144). Clocked at 1x, the real cutoff is fc/8. The tone filter is applied to every non-digital wet path (distortion_adapter.cpp:222-229, :583), and the user value is clamped to 200..8000 Hz (distortion_adapter.cpp:170). So at 44.1 kHz the default 4000 Hz acts as about 500 Hz, and 8000 Hz as about 1 kHz.

Why it is not a documented design choice: the comment at distortion_adapter.cpp:224 ("The tone filter (prepared at oversampled rate) would destroy the staircase") only exempts the digital types; it is a workaround for a symptom, not a design decision. No document in specs/Disrumpo describes running 8x-prepared state at 1x. Nothing I read upstream or in setActive corrects the rate.

Limit of this check: I did not run the suggested probe. The verdict rests on the source plus the reviewer's arithmetic (fc/8).

Severity: high stands. Every non-digital wet path is muffled by about 3 octaves against its label, and the DC blocker and morph smoothing times are wrong by the same factor of 8.

The defect is real and the consequence follows from the code. Each link I read:

2. distortion_adapter.cpp:27 toneFilter_.prepare(sampleRate) and :31 dcBlocker_.prepare(sampleRate, 10 Hz) both receive 8*fs. So do tapeHfFilter_ (:46), bodyFilter_ (:51) and wavefoldSmoothFilter_ (:55).
3. one_pole.h:138 computes coefficient_ = exp(-2*pi*fc/sampleRate_). The coefficient is therefore set for 8*fs. The Nyquist clamp at :143 uses 8*fs too, so tone 8000 Hz is never clamped.
4. The processor uses only the per-sample path. processor.cpp:467-499 loops over samples and calls bandProcessors_[b].process(bandL, bandR) at :494 (also :487 for discarded bands). processBlock and processWithFactor (band_processor.h:519, :627), the only routes into the oversamplers, are never called from processor.cpp (grep found no call). So band_processor.h:487-488 calls morphEngine_->process(left) and then process(right), which reaches blendedAdapter_.process or adapters_[i].process (morph_engine.cpp:662-718).
