- The result goes straight to blendedAdapter_.setParams at morph_engine.cpp:708-710. This is the same-family path, chosen by isSameFamily (:385-397, :675-678), so it runs whenever all nodes share a family, including identical types.
- Downstream only clamps: ring_saturation.h:187, feedback_distortion.h:486 and fractal_distortion.h:267 clamp to range, and distortion_adapter.cpp:777 clamps stages to 1-4. None of them round or restore the node value, so identical nodes still get a lower, weight-dependent value. The 0-to-1 clamp only hides the stages=1 at 0.5/0.5 case.

- The node-level mapping in processor_params.cpp:169, 185, 244, 257 does produce integer values the user can set, so this is reachable from a real host.

The severity of medium stands: the timbre changes and steps as the cursor moves between identical nodes.

The defect is real and it is reachable. One part of the claim (magnitudeBits) has no audible effect.

Truncation is confirmed in morph_engine.cpp. interpolateParams() starts from the dominant node's params (line 419), then zeroes the int fields: stages at :467, fftSize and magnitudeBits at :497-498, iterations at :505. It then adds a truncated term per node: `result.stages += static_cast<int>(w * static_cast<float>(p.stages))` at :576, and the same pattern for fftSize and magnitudeBits at :606-607 and iterations at :614. Nodes with w < kWeightThreshold are skipped (:529), which pushes the result further down.

2. The path is reachable. processSameFamily() (:691-719) calls interpolateParams() and blendedAdapter_.setParams() on every sample. That happens whenever isSameFamily() (:385-397) is true, and that check compares only the DistortionFamily. getFamily() (distortion_types.h:297-347) puts FeedbackDist in Dynamic, RingSaturation in Hybrid, and Fractal/Spectral in Experimental. So two Fractal nodes, two RingSat nodes or two FeedbackDist nodes all go through the truncating sum. Weights come from the smoothed cursor (:668-672), so any cursor position off a node gives fractional weights.

3. The values reach the DSP unrounded:
- distortion_adapter.cpp:929 `fractal_.setIterations(p.iterations)`. fractal_distortion.h:266 only clamps the value.
- distortion_adapter.cpp:777 `ringSaturation_.setStages(std::clamp(p.stages,1,4))`. ring_saturation.h:186 only clamps.
- distortion_adapter.cpp:818 `feedbackDist_.setStages(p.stages)`. feedback_distortion.h:485-490 clamps to at least 1 and calls configureAllFilters() each time the value changes.
- Value ranges come from processor_params.cpp:169/185 (stages 1-4) and :257 (iterations 1-8).

4. Size of the error. With two nodes at 0.6/0.4 and iterations 4: 2 + 1 = 3. At 0.5/0.5 the result is correct for even values (4 gives 2 + 2) but wrong for odd ones (5 gives 2 + 2 = 4; stages 3 gives 1 + 1 = 2). For N nodes the result can be up to N-1 units low (up to 3 with four nodes). Stages 1 at 0.5/0.5 gives 0, which the clamp turns back into 1, so that case is harmless.

For most cursor positions between two identical Fractal nodes, the iteration depth is one level below what the user set, and four-node layouts lose more. RingSat and FeedbackDist stages behave the same way. The value changes in whole steps at fractional weight crossings while the cursor moves or is automated. Each step is a sudden change in the processor's structure, so a timbre change with step edges is plausible as claimed. Medium severity holds.

5. One partial overstatement: magnitudeBits has no effect. The adapter never reads it; Spectral uses `spectral_.setMagnitudeBits(p.bitDepth)` at distortion_adapter.cpp:922. The fftSize truncation produces values that are not powers of two (0.6/0.4 of 2048 gives 1228 + 819 = 2047), which then trigger re-prepare at :894-895. The finding itself says that consequence belongs to a separate critical finding. It does not change this one's severity.

6. No existing guard was found. The adapter only clamps these values, and the interpolation does not round.

findings.title: Cross-family path leaves the last modulated drive/mix/tone/bias stuck in the node adapters when the mod offsets return to exactly 0
findings.problem: processCrossFamily re-applies node params plus modulation offsets to adapters_[i] only while some offset is non-zero. When every offset becomes exactly 0.0 (routing removed, source set to None, amount 0, macro at 0), the block is skipped and nothing restores nodes_[i].commonParams/params. The adapters keep the last modulated values until the next setNodes, which happens only on a node or band parameter change.
findings.why_wrong: With no modulation, the audio must follow the base node parameters. The same-family path recomputes from base every sample and behaves correctly, so the two paths disagree under identical modulation.
findings.consequence: Remove a drive routing while the LFO is at its peak and a cross-family band stays at drive +X*10 (up to +10) indefinitely. The sound then differs from the knob values and from a preset reload.
findings.suggested_fix: Track whether offsets were active on the previous sample or block. On the transition to all-zero, re-apply base params once (setCommonParams then setParams per active node). Better, compute the effective params per block in setDriveMixModOffset/setToneBiasModOffset instead of per sample. Test: cross-family band with drive offset 0.5 for one block, then 0. Assert adapters_[0].getCommonParams().drive equals the node's base drive and the output RMS equals the never-modulated render.

findings.title: Type changes, node activation and family-path switches reuse processor state without a reset or crossfade; picking Spectral on a node allocates on the audio thread
findings.problem: setNodes runs from processParameterChanges on the audio thread for every node parameter change. It calls setType/setParams on all 4 adapters, and DistortionAdapter::setType only sets currentType_ (no reset). The newly selected processor inside the adapter resumes with whatever delay-line, grain, hysteresis or filter content it had from its last use. The cross-family loop also skips nodes with weight below 0.001, so their adapters freeze and later restart on live audio with stale state. When a node type change flips allSameFamily_, output switches between blendedAdapter_ and adapters_ within one sample, with no crossfade. Every adapter's spectral_ is prepared with fftSize = maxBlockSize*8 = 4096, so the first setParams of a node set to Spectral (default fftSize 2048) calls spectral_.prepare(), which allocates inside process().
findings.why_wrong: State-holding processors need a reset or a short fade when they are (re)activated or re-assigned. Switching between two independent processing paths needs a crossfade. SpectralDistortion::prepare is documented not real-time safe.
findings.consequence: Clicks and bursts of old audio (FeedbackDist comb, Granular buffer, AllpassResonant ringing) when a node's type changes, when the active node count increases, or when a node's weight rises from 0. A level jump when a type change crosses a family boundary. Heap allocation on the audio thread when the user picks Spectral or moves its FFT-size slot.
findings.suggested_fix: Reset an adapter when its type changes (setType compares and calls reset of the new processor) and when a node goes from inactive to active. Crossfade over ~5 ms when allSameFamily_ flips. Pre-prepare spectral_ for all four FFT sizes (512-4096) at prepare time and switch between them without allocating. Test: process a FeedbackDist node, switch it to SoftClip and back. Assert no output above the input peak in the first 10 ms, and run an allocation counter around processParameterChanges when a node is set to Spectral.
findings.evidence: distortion_adapter.cpp:142-162 setType sets currentType_/DC flag/latency only; morph_engine.cpp:136-140 setType/setParams on all adapters in setNodes; :745 `if (weight < kWeightThreshold) continue;` (adapter not run); :678-681 path switch; processor_params.cpp:899 setMorphNodes on every node param; band_processor.h:124-125 prepare(..., maxBlockSize_*8) -> distortion_adapter.cpp:84 `spectral_.prepare(sampleRate, maxBlockSize)` then :894-895 re-prepare on fftSize mismatch.
verifier_notes:
I traced each part of the claim through the source and every part holds.

(1) The audio-thread call path is real. processor_params.cpp:839-899 handles kNodeType (type switch, then mapShapeSlotsToParams) and every other node parameter, then calls bandProcessors_[band].setMorphNodes(...) at :899 inside processParameterChanges. kBandActiveNodes does the same at :954. band_processor.h:247-249 forwards to MorphEngine::setNodes. morph_engine.cpp:136-140 then calls setType, setParams and setCommonParams on all 4 adapters.

(2) There is no reset on a type change. distortion_adapter.cpp:142-162 setType only assigns currentType_, calls updateDCBlockerState and sets the isBlockBased_/blockLatency_ fields. Nothing calls the newly selected processor's reset(). reset() (:98-136) is only reached from MorphEngine::reset (:72-94), not from setNodes.

(3) Skipped nodes freeze. morph_engine.cpp:745 and :749 `continue` before adapters_[i].process, so a node whose weight is below kWeightThreshold is not run and keeps its stale internal state until its weight rises again.

(4) The path switch has no crossfade. morph_engine.cpp:675-682 recomputes allSameFamily_ every sample and returns either processSameFamily (blendedAdapter_, a separate adapter instance) or processCrossFamily (adapters_[]). No crossfade state exists between the two.

(5) Picking Spectral allocates on the audio thread.
- band_processor.h:111-112/124-125 prepares the MorphEngine at maxBlockSize_*8 (kMaxOversampleFactor=8, line 47). morph_engine.cpp:57-60 passes that to every adapter. distortion_adapter.cpp:84 calls spectral_.prepare(sampleRate, maxBlockSize), whose second argument is the fftSize (spectral_distortion.h:145). With a 512-sample host block that is 4096.
- The node FFT slot maps to 512-4096 (processor_params.cpp:244), and the DistortionParams default is 2048 (distortion_adapter.h:179).
- distortion_adapter.cpp:893-896 re-prepares whenever p.fftSize != getFftSize(). Its own comment says "allocates, but only on user param change".
- SpectralDistortion::prepare is documented "NOT real-time safe (allocates memory)" (spectral_distortion.h:144). It calls stft_.prepare and overlapAdd_.prepare, which resize vectors (stft.h:78,81,266,269), plus FFT::prepare, which calls pffft_new_setup (fft.h:157).
- So choosing Spectral for a node from automation or the UI allocates inside process().

A related point outside the finding: processSameFamily (:706-710) calls blendedAdapter_.setParams every sample with an interpolated fftSize (morph_engine.cpp:606, a weighted sum). That value can be something like 2867. prepare rounds it up to a power of two, so the mismatch never resolves and the re-prepare could repeat every sample while two Spectral nodes morph. This makes the RT-safety part worse, not better.

Severity stays at medium: the allocation is a hard real-time violation that ordinary user actions trigger, and the stale-state and path-switch parts are audible-click hazards. Both have been confirmed in the code but not measured.

I could not refute this finding. The source confirms each part of it.

It never calls the new processor's reset(); reset() is only in DistortionAdapter::reset() at :98-136. morph_engine.cpp:136-140 setNodes calls setType/setParams/setCommonParams on all 4 adapters, and band_processor.h:247-255 setMorphNodes adds no reset. The callers are processor_params.cpp:899 (every node param change) and :954 (ActiveNodes change). Both are inside processParameterChanges, so they run on the audio thread.

(2) Frozen adapters restart with stale state. morph_engine.cpp:745 and :749 skip adapters_[i].process() while weight or transition gain is below kWeightThreshold, so those processors keep old state. transitionGains_ (:268-270) fades the node's gain in, but its state is still stale.

(3) The path switches with no crossfade. :675-682 recomputes allSameFamily_ on every sample and changes between blendedAdapter_ and adapters_ immediately. Nothing in specs/Disrumpo covers a crossfade for type or family switches (grep found nothing).

(4) Allocation on the audio thread is confirmed. The comment at distortion_adapter.cpp:893 even says "allocates, but only on user param change", and the processor's own header documents prepare as "NOT real-time safe" (spectral_distortion.h:144). STFT::prepare (stft.h:57,72) assigns `window_ = Window::generate(...)` and calls fft_.prepare, so it allocates on every call. The adapter is prepared at :84 with maxBlockSize, which is already ×8 (band_processor.h:111-112, :124-125). The factory default fftSize is 2048 (distortion_adapter.h:179) and the slot mapping covers 512-4096 (processor_params.cpp:244). So the first setParams on a Spectral node re-prepares inside process().

Why the severity should go up: the allocation is worse than the finding says. morph_engine.cpp:606 interpolates fftSize as `result.fftSize += static_cast<int>(w * p.fftSize)` with truncation per node. processSameFamily (:706-710) calls blendedAdapter_.setParams(bp) on every sample. Spectral, Granular and Fractal are one family (distortion_types.h:340-342). With two Spectral nodes at 2048 and weights 0.6/0.4, the sum is 1228+819=2047. spectral_.prepare rounds that to 2048 (spectral_distortion.h:150-154), so getFftSize() never equals the requested size. The check at :894 then fails on every sample, and the code allocates and resets its STFT on every sample while the cursor sits between nodes. That is a heap allocation on every sample plus broken spectral output. Nothing is guarded or documented as intentional.

I confirmed both halves of the finding from source. The one part I would weaken is the stale state of low-weight nodes.

ALLOCATION (confirmed, a real-time rule violation):
- band_processor.h:124-125 prepares MorphEngine with maxBlockSize_*kMaxOversampleFactor (8, band_processor.h:47).
- morph_engine.cpp:57-60 passes that size to every adapter and to blendedAdapter_.
- distortion_adapter.cpp:84 then calls spectral_.prepare(sampleRate, maxBlockSize). That gives an FFT size of 4096 at a 512 host block and 8192 (the kMaxFFTSize clamp, spectral_distortion.h:118) at 1024 and above.
- DistortionParams::fftSize defaults to 2048 (distortion_adapter.h:179).
- When a node becomes Spectral, processor_params.cpp:899 calls setMorphNodes. That reaches morph_engine.cpp:137-138 (setType, then setParams), then routeParamsToProcessor, and distortion_adapter.cpp:894-895 sees a size mismatch and calls spectral_.prepare(2048).
- That prepare is documented "NOT real-time safe (allocates memory)" (spectral_distortion.h:144). It calls stft/overlapAdd/FFT prepare, and FFT::prepare runs pffft_new_setup plus pffft_aligned_malloc (fft.h:117, 157).
- The same thing happens on the same-family path. processSameFamily calls blendedAdapter_.setType and setParams once per sample (morph_engine.cpp:706-710), so the first sample after a Spectral node becomes dominant re-prepares blendedAdapter_'s spectral_ too.
- Every move of the FFT-size slot re-prepares again.
- Only a host maxBlockSize of 256 or less avoids the very first allocation, because then 256*8 = 2048 matches the default.

STALE STATE (confirmed):
- setType (distortion_adapter.cpp:142-162) only sets currentType_, the DC-blocker state and the latency fields. It never resets the processor. reset() exists (:98-136) but setType and setNodes (morph_engine.cpp:131-152) never call it.
- So a re-selected FeedbackDist, Granular or AllpassSaturator resumes with whatever buffer content it had from its last use.
- Same family vs cross family is decided every sample (morph_engine.cpp:675-682). It switches hard between blendedAdapter_ and adapters_[i], with no crossfade, and the path being switched to may hold state from long ago. The result is a discontinuity at the moment the user changes a type.

WEAKER PART:
- The claim about nodes skipped below kWeightThreshold (:745) has lower impact than stated. A node whose weight rises from 0 brings its stale content in at roughly -60 dB weight and ramps it in, so it is not an abrupt burst.

SEVERITY:
- Every trigger is a discrete user action: a type change, the FFT-size slot, or the active-node count. Nothing fires continuously.
- The allocation happens once per such action. That is a genuine rule violation that can cause a dropout under load, but it does not cause a sustained failure.
- Medium is appropriate.

Separate observation, not part of this finding: band_processor.h:487-488 and :753-754 run L and R through the same morphEngine_ and so through the same stateful adapters. That L/R shared state is a distinct and likely more severe defect.

findings.title: Same-family interpolation blends DistortionParams fields whose meaning differs per type (Fuzz bias unipolar 1=centered vs Tube/SoftClip bipolar 0)
findings.problem: interpolateParams accumulates result.bias from every node in the family, but the field has type-specific semantics. Tube/Tape map it bipolar [-1,1] with 0 neutral (processor_params.cpp:56,63). Fuzz/AsymFuzz store it unipolar, where 1.0 is centered and 0 is maximum offset (processor_params.cpp:73,81; fuzz_processor.h:492 `biasOffset = (1 - bias)*0.8`). SoftClip/HardClip never set it and keep the default 0.0. The bias mod offset is then added and clamped to [-1,1] for every type (morph_engine.cpp:709).
findings.why_wrong: Interpolating one parameter between two types is only meaningful when it means the same thing on both. A SoftClip node (bias 0) and a centered Fuzz node (bias 1.0) at wFuzz = 0.6 give the dominant Fuzz bias 0.6, an offset of 0.32. The morph injects a gated, sputtery bias that neither endpoint has. Tube to Fuzz at 0.5/0.5 with the Tube neutral (0) and the Fuzz centered (1) gives the same distortion.
findings.consequence: Saturation-family morphs that include Fuzz/AsymFuzz change Fuzz character as the cursor moves, even when both nodes are at their neutral bias. A bias mod offset can push Fuzz bias negative, outside its domain.
findings.suggested_fix: Normalize per-type fields to a common semantic before interpolation (e.g. store fuzz bias as bipolar and convert in routeParams), or interpolate only between nodes of the same type (see the same-family hard-switch finding). Test: SoftClip+Fuzz same-family morph at wFuzz 0.6 with the Fuzz slot0 at 1.0 (centered); assert blendedAdapter_.getParams().bias maps to fuzz offset 0.
findings.evidence: morph_engine.cpp:425 `result.bias = 0.0f;` :534 `result.bias += w * p.bias;` :709 `bp.bias = std::clamp(bp.bias + biasModOffset_ * 2.0f, -1.0f, 1.0f);`; processor_params.cpp:56 `p.bias = slots[0] * 2.0f - 1.0f;` :73 `p.bias = slots[0];  // Fuzz bias is unipolar [0,1]`; distortion_adapter.h:81 `float bias = 0.0f; ///< Asymmetry [-1, 1]`; fuzz_processor.h:492 `const float biasOffset = (1.0f - biasValue) * 0.8f;`.
verifier_notes:
I traced the call path and the finding holds.

1. Same family. distortion_types.h:300-306 maps SoftClip, HardClip, Tube, Tape, Fuzz and AsymmetricFuzz all to DistortionFamily::Saturation. So isSameFamily() (morph_engine.cpp:385-397) returns true for a SoftClip+Fuzz or Tube+Fuzz node pair, and process() takes processSameFamily (morph_engine.cpp:678-679).

2. Blending. processSameFamily calls interpolateParams() (morph_engine.cpp:708). That function zeroes result.bias (line 425) and adds w * p.bias from every node above the weight threshold (line 534), whatever each node's type is. The blended adapter is then set to the dominant node's type (line 706), so the blended bias is read with the dominant type's meaning.

3. Bias means different things per type. In processor_params.cpp mapShapeSlotsToParams:
- Tube (line 56) and Tape (line 63) use bias in [-1,1], 0 = neutral.
- Fuzz (line 73) and AsymmetricFuzz (line 81) use bias in [0,1].
- SoftClip and HardClip (lines 42-52) never write bias, so it stays at its default of 0.

4. What Fuzz does with it. DistortionAdapter::routeParamsToProcessor passes p.bias straight to fuzz_.setBias for both Fuzz types (distortion_adapter.cpp:637, :646). FuzzProcessor::setBias clamps it to [0,1] (fuzz_processor.h:365). It then applies biasOffset = (1 - bias) * 0.8 (fuzz_processor.h:492), so 1 means centered and 0 means the largest offset.

5. Worked example. SoftClip (bias 0) and a centered Fuzz (bias 1.0) with Fuzz weight 0.6. The blended bias is 0.6 and Fuzz is dominant, so the offset is 0.4 * 0.8 = 0.32. Neither endpoint has that offset, so the sputter is real. Tube at neutral (0) and centered Fuzz (1) at 0.5/0.5 give 0.5, an offset of 0.4.

6. The mod offset. Line 709 clamps bias + mod to [-1,1] for every type. For Fuzz, FuzzProcessor::setBias clamps it again to [0,1], so a negative value cannot leave the domain. It does saturate at maximum offset, which is a minor point.

7. Another place with the same problem. The node-level kNodeBias parameter (processor_params.cpp:868-870) also maps bias as bipolar `value*2-1` for every type, Fuzz included.

The core defect stands. Medium severity fits: you hear it when morphing in the Saturation family with a Fuzz node in the mix, but nothing becomes unsafe.

I could not refute this. Nothing guards it or explains it away. getFamily (distortion_types.h:300-306) puts SoftClip, HardClip, Tube, Tape, Fuzz and AsymmetricFuzz all in the Saturation family, so a morph that mixes them takes processSameFamily (morph_engine.cpp:675-679). interpolateParams starts result.bias at 0 (morph_engine.cpp:425) and adds w*p.bias from every node above the weight threshold (:534). It does no conversion per type. processSameFamily then calls setType with the dominant node's type and passes the blended bias, plus 2*biasModOffset clamped to [-1,1] (:706-710).

The two bias meanings do not match. Tube and Tape map slots[0] to bipolar bias via *2-1 (processor_params.cpp:56,63). Fuzz and AsymFuzz store slots[0] as unipolar bias (:73,81). SoftClip and HardClip never write bias. It stays at its default of 0 (distortion_adapter.h:81), or at a stale value: on a type change only mapShapeSlotsToParams runs on the existing mn.params (processor_params.cpp:852), so a field the new type does not write keeps its old value. setParams passes p.bias straight to fuzz_.setBias for Fuzz/AsymFuzz (distortion_adapter.cpp:637,646). FuzzProcessor computes biasOffset = (1-bias)*0.8 (fuzz_processor.h:492), so bias 1 means centered. The claimed scenario holds: SoftClip (bias 0) and Fuzz (bias 1) at wFuzz 0.6 make Fuzz dominant, the blended bias is 0.6, and the offset is 0.32, which neither node has.

Spec dsp-details.md:1244-1251 says only that same-family morphs use one instance with interpolated parameters. Nothing in the spec or the code comments covers fields whose meaning differs by type, so this is not a documented design decision.

One part of the consequence is overstated. A negative bias from the mod offset cannot leave Fuzz's domain, because FuzzProcessor::setBias clamps to [0,1] (fuzz_processor.h:364-365). The negative value still means maximum offset, so the change in sound remains. The main defect stands, so I am not changing the medium severity.

I confirmed this from source. The only overstated part is the "outside its domain" sub-claim.

1. Fuzz and AsymFuzz are in the same family as SoftClip, HardClip, Tube and Tape. distortion_types.h:299-306 returns DistortionFamily::Saturation for all of them. So morph_engine.cpp:385-397 isSameFamily() is true for a SoftClip+Fuzz or Tube+Fuzz node set, and process() at :678-679 takes processSameFamily.

2. processSameFamily (:706) sets the adapter to the dominant node's type. It then calls interpolateParams(). That function zeroes result.bias at :425 and accumulates `w * p.bias` from every node with weight at or above the threshold at :534. No type-aware conversion happens. The bias mod offset is then applied at :709 as `clamp(bias + off*2, -1, 1)`.

3. The bias field means different things per type. processor_params.cpp:56 and :63 map Tube/Tape bias bipolar (slot*2-1, so 0 is neutral). :73 and :81 map Fuzz/AsymFuzz unipolar (raw slot). SoftClip and HardClip (:42-52) never write bias, so it stays at the default 0.0 (distortion_adapter.h:81). distortion_adapter.cpp:637 and :646 pass p.bias straight to fuzz_.setBias. fuzz_processor.h:492 computes `biasOffset = (1 - bias) * 0.8`, so 1.0 is centred and 0 gives the maximum DC offset. That offset is added before the clipper; the DC blocker only runs after it (:551).

4. Worked example: SoftClip (bias 0) at 0.4 and Fuzz (bias 1.0, centred) at 0.6. Fuzz is dominant, the blended bias is 0.6, and the pre-clip offset is 0.32 where it should be 0. With the default sustain of 0.5 (adapter.h:94), the fuzz drive is 0.1*100^0.5 = 1.0. A 0.32 DC shift on a unity-gain signal is a large asymmetry, giving even harmonics and gating on small signals. This is clearly audible. The reverse case is also wrong: Tube-dominant with a centred Fuzz neighbour gives the Tube a +0.4 bias.

Impact limits:
- The output stays bounded and DC-blocked, so there is no NaN or DC leak. The consequence is timbral: the morph produces a character neither endpoint has.
- The "bias pushed outside its domain" sub-claim is overstated. FuzzProcessor::setBias clamps to [0,1] (fuzz_processor.h:364-366), so a negative value just becomes the maximum-offset 0.
- It compounds with the dominant-type hard switch rather than standing alone.

Medium severity is appropriate: a real, audible, user-reachable morph-semantics defect, but no safety or real-time problem.

findings.title: 8x oversampling is unreachable even in the dormant code: the factor rounding caps at 4 while the global limit and an 8x cascade are offered; the crossfade double-clocks the shared engine
findings.problem: roundUpToPowerOf2Factor returns at most 4, and getRecommendedOversample's maximum is 4. calculateMorphOversampleFactor and getSingleTypeOversampleFactor can therefore never yield 8, even with Oversample Max = 8x. oversampler8xInner_ is still prepared (band_processor.h:105-107) and processWithOversampling8x exists. The crossfade path (band_processor.h:653-690) runs the old and new factor through the SAME morphEngine_ and applyOutputStage smoothers, so engine state and gain/pan/mute smoothers advance twice per sample during an 8 ms transition.
findings.why_wrong: FR-OS-001 offers 1/2/4/8x with the global limit acting as a cap. A limit of 8 that can never be reached is dead UI and dead memory. A crossfade between two paths must run independent state per path, or the comparison is between corrupted signals.
findings.consequence: No audible effect today, because oversampling is not wired (see the high finding). When it is wired, 8x will silently never engage and every factor change will corrupt filter and feedback state and the gain smoothers for 8 ms.
findings.suggested_fix: Either drop 8x from the parameter and spec, or allow a per-type 8x profile and extend the rounding. For the crossfade, keep a second engine/adapter set (or fade at the output of two independently stated paths) and advance the output-stage smoothers once per host sample. Test: oversampling_utils test asserting the factor is 8 when the limit is 8 and a node recommends 8; a crossfade test asserting the gain smoother reaches its target in the configured time during a factor change.

findings.title: Sweep LFO runs once per block, so its rate is divided by the host block size
findings.problem: Processor::process calls sweepLFO_.process() once per audio block. SweepLFO::process() (sweep_lfo.h) returns lfo_.process()*depth_. Krate::DSP::LFO::process advances phaseAcc_ by one per-sample increment (calculatePhaseIncrement(freq, sampleRate), lfo.h:499-502) on each call. Over a whole block the LFO phase therefore moves one sample's worth.
findings.why_wrong: FR-SWEEP-004 / FR-024 set the internal sweep LFO to 0.01-20 Hz. That requires one phase increment per sample, or numSamples increments per block. The shared ModulationEngine does this correctly: it ticks lfo1_/lfo2_ once per sample in its per-block loop (modulation_engine.h:216-221). The sweep LFO does not.
findings.consequence: The real sweep LFO rate is the set rate divided by the block size. At 512 samples / 44.1 kHz a 1 Hz sweep LFO has a period of about 512 s, and 20 Hz becomes about 0.04 Hz. In practice the sweep LFO is frozen. Its speed also changes with the host buffer size, so the same project sounds different at 128 and at 1024 samples. S&H and Random waveforms step once every ~blockSize*sr/rate samples.
findings.suggested_fix: Advance the sweep LFO numSamples times per block and use the last value. Or add an LFO advance(n) / per-sample sweep evaluation. Test (processor level, new [sweep] case): enable sweep and the sweep LFO at 1 Hz with depth 1. Render 2 s at block sizes 64 and 1024. Read kSweepModulatedFrequencyOutputId per block and assert about 2 periods (4 zero crossings of log2(f/base)) at both block sizes. Today the 1024-sample render shows none.

Compare modulation_engine.h:216-221 `for (size_t i = 0; i < safeSamples; ++i) { ... lfo1LastValue_ = lfo1_.process();`. tests/dsp/sweep_lfo_tests.cpp:150-190 tests only the wrapper called per sample; no processor-level sweep LFO test exists (grep for kSweepLFO in tests/ finds only dsp/sweep_lfo_tests.cpp).

The function has no per-sample loop around the sweep section: the only loops are band loops and the later sample loop at :467, and `sweepProcessor_.processBlock(data.numSamples)` follows at :370. The LFO is prepared with the true `sampleRate_` (processor.cpp:135, `sweepLFO_.prepare(sampleRate_)`), not a block-rate value, so nothing compensates. findings.title: Sweep envelope follower is fed one sample per block (inputL[0] only)
findings.problem: The sweep envelope follower is updated once per block with the first sample of the block: `float inputMono = (inputL[0] + inputR[0]) * 0.5f; (void)sweepEnvelope_.processSample(inputMono);`. The rest of the block is never seen.
findings.why_wrong: SweepEnvelope wraps Krate::DSP::EnvelopeFollower (RMS mode). Its attack/release coefficients are per-sample one-poles prepared for sampleRate (sweep_envelope.h prepare/setAttackTime). FR-026/027 attack 1-100 ms and release 10-500 ms assume one update per sample. Sampling one value per block also decimates the audio with no anti-aliasing: a 1 kHz tone sampled every 512 samples gives a pseudo-random value.
findings.consequence: Attack and release are stretched by the block size: 10 ms attack becomes about 5 s at 512 samples. The detected level is a sparse, aliased snapshot of sample 0, not the signal's RMS. So the envelope-driven sweep (FR-SWEEP-004 'Envelope follower') responds sluggishly and erratically, and its response depends on the host buffer size.
findings.suggested_fix: Loop sweepEnvelope_.processSample over all numSamples of (L+R)/2 and use the final level, as ModulationEngine does for its env follower (processEnvFollowerSample per sample, modulation_engine.h:224). Test: feed a 0.5-amplitude burst after silence with attack 10 ms. Assert that the reported modulated sweep frequency rises by at least 90 % of its final octave shift within 50 ms, at both 64- and 1024-sample blocks.
findings.evidence: processor.cpp:340-343 `if (sweepEnvelope_.isEnabled()) { float inputMono = (inputL[0] + inputR[0]) * 0.5f; (void)sweepEnvelope_.processSample(inputMono); }`. sweep_envelope.h processSample: `envelopeLevel_ = envelope_.processSample(input);` (one follower tick per call); prepare sets DetectionMode::RMS and setAttackTime(attackMs_).
verifier_notes: The defect is real; I could not refute it. In processor.cpp:340-343 the follower gets one sample per block: `if (sweepEnvelope_.isEnabled()) { float inputMono = (inputL[0] + inputR[0]) * 0.5f; (void)sweepEnvelope_.processSample(inputMono); }`. Here inputL is `data.inputs[0].channelBuffers32[0]` (processor.cpp:209). A grep of plugins/disrumpo/src/processor finds no other per-sample call to sweepEnvelope_.processSample. The only other uses are prepare (processor.cpp:136, with sampleRate_ = audio rate, not block rate), reset (161), the parameter setters in processor_params.cpp:468-489 and getModulatedFrequency (processor.cpp:359). SweepEnvelope::processSample (sweep_envelope.h:187-194) makes one call to envelope_.processSample per invocation. EnvelopeFollower::processSample (envelope_follower.h:164-188) advances processRMS once (312-326), a one-pole in the squared domain. Its coefficient is calculateCoefficient = exp(-2π / (timeMs*0.001*sampleRate_)) (envelope_follower.h:359-365), so it is per-sample at audio rate. A 10 ms attack at 44.1 kHz settles in about 441 ticks. At one tick per 512-sample block that is 441 blocks, about 5.1 s, which matches the finding's figure. The response therefore depends on block size. The input is also a one-sample snapshot per block, so it is a decimated, aliased reading of the signal rather than its RMS. getModulatedFrequency (sweep_envelope.h:204-226) maps envelopeLevel_ to 0 to +2 octaves, so the sluggish and erratic level reaches the sweep centre frequency directly (processor.cpp:358-368). Every part of the claimed call path checks out. I see no reason to change the severity: the FR-026/027 envelope-driven sweep is effectively broken at normal block sizes.

Confirmed from source. plugins/disrumpo/src/processor/processor.cpp:339-343 is the only place the sweep envelope is fed: `if (sweepEnvelope_.isEnabled()) { float inputMono = (inputL[0] + inputR[0]) * 0.5f; (void)sweepEnvelope_.processSample(inputMono); }`. A grep for sweepEnvelope_ across plugins/disrumpo finds no other processSample call; the other hits are prepare at :136, reset at :161, getModulatedFrequency at :359, and the setters in processor_params.cpp:468-489 and processor_state.cpp. So no per-sample loop anywhere else covers for it. SweepEnvelope::processSample (plugins/disrumpo/src/dsp/sweep_envelope.h:187-194) makes exactly one call to EnvelopeFollower::processSample per call. prepare (sweep_envelope.h:87-94) sets up the follower at the audio sample rate in RMS mode. EnvelopeFollower::calculateCoefficient (dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/envelope_follower.h:356-372) computes `coeff = exp(-2pi / (time_ms * 0.001 * sampleRate))`, a per-sample one-pole. Ticking it once per block therefore stretches attack and release by a factor of numSamples (10 ms becomes about 5 s at 512 samples), and the RMS detector sees one unfiltered snapshot of sample 0 per block. Nothing documents this as a design decision: there is no block-rate note in sweep_envelope.h or processor.cpp, and a grep of specs/Disrumpo for per-block or block-rate envelope behaviour matches nothing. The FR-026/027 ranges in sweep_envelope.h:29-39 assume real per-sample times. The tests in plugins/disrumpo/tests/dsp/sweep_envelope_tests.cpp call SweepEnvelope directly sample by sample, so they never exercise the processor's once-per-block call site and do not pin this behaviour. One mitigating note: the envelope is opt-in (enabled_ defaults to false, and the uidesc default-value is 0), so only sessions with Sweep Env enabled are affected. When it is enabled, the feature is effectively broken and depends on the host buffer size, so severity stays as reported.

The defect is confirmed, and the claimed consequence holds. In processor.cpp:340-343 the follower is ticked once per process() call with only `(inputL[0] + inputR[0]) * 0.5f`. processor.cpp:136 prepares it with `sweepEnvelope_.prepare(sampleRate_, setup.maxSamplesPerBlock)`, and sweep_envelope.h:87-92 passes the real sample rate to EnvelopeFollower in RMS mode. So its coefficients are per-sample. envelope_follower.h calculateCoefficient computes `exp(-2π / (timeMs*0.001*sampleRate))`, about 99 % settling in timeMs worth of samples. processRMS does one one-pole step on sample² per call. sweep_envelope.h:187-193 makes one envelope_.processSample call per processSample.

Quantified: 10 ms attack at 44.1 kHz needs about 441 ticks. At one tick per 512-sample block that is 441*512/44100 ≈ 5.1 s, at 64-sample blocks about 0.64 s, and at 1024 about 10.2 s. A 100 ms release becomes about 51 s at 512. The 1-100 ms / 10-500 ms ranges in FR-027 are scaled by the host buffer size, so the response depends on the host and its block size. The decimation point also holds. One un-filtered sample per block feeds the follower. For a periodic tone whose period divides the block length (e.g. 86.13 Hz = 44100/512, or any harmonic of it), sample 0 lands at the same phase every block. The follower can then read anywhere from 0 to full peak² rather than RMS (e.g. 0 if sample 0 sits on a zero crossing). For other tones the reading is a noisy snapshot that converges only statistically, and only over the stretched time constant.

Guards: processor.cpp:196 returns early when numSamples == 0, so the inputL[0] read itself is safe. No other code path ticks the follower. The modulated value goes straight to sweepProcessor_.setCenterFrequency (processor.cpp:358-368), so the error is audible as sweep motion. A grep of plugins/disrumpo/tests found no test of the processor-level sweep envelope, so nothing would catch this.

findings.title: Sweep band intensities use hard-coded 100/600/3000/12000 Hz centres, not the real bands (1-band mode goes silent)
findings.problem: Per-band sweep intensity is computed against the fixed `kBandCenterFreqs = {100, 600, 3000, 12000}`, taking the first numBands entries. The actual crossover frequencies and the band count are ignored.
findings.why_wrong: FR-SWEEP-001 says sweep focus moves through the spectrum relative to the bands that exist. A band's distance from the sweep centre must come from that band's own frequency range: for example the geometric centre of its crossover edges, with the full 20 Hz-20 kHz range in 1-band mode. A fixed 4-band table is only correct for one specific crossover layout.
findings.consequence: In 1-band mode the full-range band is evaluated at 100 Hz. With the default sweep (1 kHz, width 1.5 oct, intensity 0.5) that gives 0.5*exp(-0.5*(3.32/0.75)^2) = 2.8e-5 (-91 dB). Since the sweep multiplies the band input, turning Sweep on mutes the wet output. In 2-band mode (crossover at 632 Hz) the upper band, 632 Hz-20 kHz, is evaluated at 600 Hz, below its own range. Moving crossovers in the UI has no effect on where the sweep 'hits'. Sweeping to 5 kHz in a 4-band layout with crossovers at 200/1500/6000 Hz still favours the band labelled '3000 Hz'.
findings.suggested_fix: Derive each band's centre from crossoverL_ frequencies: sqrt(f_lo*f_hi) with edges 20 Hz and 20 kHz, and use the full range for 1 band. Pass that array to calculateAllBandIntensities. Test: 1 band, sweep enabled at default settings, sine at 1 kHz. Assert the output RMS is within 6 dB of the sweep-disabled level (today -91 dB). Also: 4 bands with moved crossovers, sweep centred on band 2's geometric centre, and assert band 2 gets the maximum intensity.
findings.evidence: processor.cpp:422-430 `static constexpr std::array<float, kMaxBands> kBandCenterFreqs = { 100.0f, 600.0f, 3000.0f, 12000.0f }; ... sweepProcessor_.calculateAllBandIntensities(kBandCenterFreqs.data(), numBands, sweepIntensities.data());`. Defaults: processor.h:224/227/230 baseSweepFrequency_ 1000, width norm 0.286 (1.5 oct), intensity norm 0.25 (0.5). crossover_network.h:253-265 log distribution gives a 632 Hz crossover for 2 bands.
verifier_notes:
I traced the code and the defect is real.

1. processor.cpp:422-424 defines `static constexpr std::array<float, kMaxBands> kBandCenterFreqs = {100, 600, 3000, 12000}`. Lines 429-430 pass `kBandCenterFreqs.data()` and `numBands` to `sweepProcessor_.calculateAllBandIntensities`. Nothing in the block reads the crossover frequencies. The only other caller of `getCrossoverFrequency` in the processor is processor_state.cpp:76, which handles state.

2. sweep_processor.h:263-285 evaluates `calculateGaussianIntensity(bandCenters[i], sweepCenterHz, widthOctaves_, intensity_)` against the table entries as given. The default falloff is Smooth (sweep_processor.h:355).

3. sweep_morph_link.h:143-165 computes the Gaussian:
   - distance = |log2(band) - log2(centre)|
   - sigma = width/2
   - result = intensity * exp(-0.5*(d/sigma)^2)

4. The defaults are:
   - baseSweepFrequency_ = 1000 Hz (processor.h:224)
   - width norm 0.286 (processor.h:227), which processor_params.cpp:397 and processor.cpp:282 map to 0.5 + 0.286*3.5 = 1.5 octaves, so sigma = 0.75
   - intensity norm 0.25 (processor.h:230), which processor_params.cpp:405 maps to 0.5

5. In 1-band mode the band is evaluated at 100 Hz: d = 3.32 oct, d/sigma = 4.43, so exp(-9.8) is about 5.5e-5, times 0.5 gives about 2.8e-5. That matches the finding's figure. In Sharp mode the value would be exactly 0, because 3.32 > 0.75.

6. band_processor.h:196-198 clamps that value and uses it as the sweep smoother target. band_processor.h:478-481 multiplies the band input (`left *= sweep`) before distortion, and lines 748-749 do the same on the oversampled path with `targetSweep_`. So the wet signal of the single full-range band drops to about -91 dB. Only the dry share of the global mix survives.

7. crossover_network.h:253-268 spreads the crossovers logarithmically from 20 Hz to 20 kHz. For 2 bands that puts the crossover at 10^(1.301+1.5), about 632 Hz. The upper band (632 Hz-20 kHz) is therefore evaluated at 600 Hz, below its own range, as the finding says.

8. Moving the crossovers does not change the sweep table, so the claim that moved crossovers have no effect is correct. The tests (sweep_band_intensity_test.cpp:32, sweep_processor_tests.cpp:309) only use their own fixed 8-entry centre arrays and call SweepProcessor directly, so the processor-level mapping is never tested.

Enabling Sweep at its defaults in 1-band mode mutes the wet output, which justifies high severity.

I could not refute this. The code does what the finding says, and nothing upstream or downstream guards it.
(1) plugins/disrumpo/src/processor/processor.cpp:422-430 declares a fixed `static constexpr std::array<float,kMaxBands> kBandCenterFreqs = {100,600,3000,12000}` and passes `kBandCenterFreqs.data(), numBands` to sweepProcessor_.calculateAllBandIntensities. crossoverL_ is never consulted, so 1-band mode evaluates its single band at 100 Hz. The comment there says "log-spaced for 4-band Bark scale", which assumes the 4-band layout. No other code path changes the table.
(2) plugins/disrumpo/src/dsp/sweep_processor.h:263-285 computes a Gaussian (Smooth) or linear (Sharp) falloff from the smoothed sweep centre for each bandCenters[i]. There is no floor and no normalisation to the bands that exist.
(3) plugins/disrumpo/src/dsp/band_processor.h:196-199 clamps the value to [0,1]. Lines 478-482 then multiply the band INPUT by it (`left *= sweep; right *= sweep;`) before distortion. This confirms the mute: the sweep is a gain on the band input, not a drive-only modulation.
(4) The defaults at processor.h:224/227/230 are 1000 Hz, width norm 0.286 and intensity norm 0.25, which match the finding's numbers. sigma=0.75 oct and a distance of 3.32 oct give about 0.5*exp(-9.8) ≈ 2.8e-5, so the wet path is effectively silent once Sweep is on in 1-band mode.
(5) Nothing in specs/Disrumpo documents a fixed band-centre table as a design decision. custom-controls.md:503 and the archived 007 spec FR-007 describe intensity "for a given band center frequency" and do not mention a constant table.
(6) The tests do not pin the processor wiring. tests/integration/sweep_band_intensity_test.cpp calls calculateAllBandIntensities with its own 8-entry kBandCenterFreqs. It never checks processor-level output for 1 or 2 bands with real crossover positions.
Reachability: a real host reaches this whenever a user enables Sweep with fewer than 4 bands or with moved crossovers. One limit: Sweep is opt-in, so this is not the default sound. In 1-band mode it still silences the wet path, and in other layouts it targets the wrong bands. High severity stands.

The defect is confirmed from source. At processor.cpp:422-430 the per-band sweep intensities are computed from the fixed `kBandCenterFreqs = {100, 600, 3000, 12000}`, taking the first numBands entries. Nothing reads the crossover frequencies, which the user can move (processor_params.cpp:992-993 calls crossoverL_/R_.setCrossoverFrequency). In sweep_morph_link.h:143-165 the Gaussian is intensity*exp(-0.5*(|log2 fb - log2 fc|/(width/2))^2). Defaults are baseSweepFrequency_ 1000 Hz, width norm 0.286 -> 0.5+0.286*3.5 = 1.50 oct, intensity norm 0.25 -> 0.5 (processor.h:224/227/230; sweep_processor.h kMaxIntensity 2.0). For 1 band the band is evaluated at 100 Hz: distance 3.32 oct / sigma 0.75 = 4.43, exp(-9.81) = 5.5e-5, times 0.5 = 2.75e-5, which is -91 dB. That number is applied as a gain on the band INPUT before distortion: band_processor.h:478-482 `left *= sweep` (and :748-749 `left[i] *= targetSweep_` on the oversampled path). It is clamped to [0,1] in setSweepIntensity (band_processor.h:196-198). globalMix_ defaults to 1.0, 100% wet (processor.h:141). So outputL = dry*0 + sum*wet (processor.cpp:502), and the wet path carries only a -91 dB input. Drive gain of 20-30 dB still leaves the output around -60 to -70 dB, so turning Sweep on in 1-band mode effectively mutes the plugin. The fault is not limited to 1-band mode. The band positions ignore the crossover layout in every band count, so moving crossovers never changes which band the sweep focuses. One mitigating factor: SweepProcessor enabled_ defaults to false (sweep_processor.h:348), so the user must switch Sweep on first. Even so, enabling a headline feature in 1-band mode silencing the output, and the sweep being mis-targeted in every other layout, justifies high severity. No test covers the processor-level mapping. The integration test sweep_band_intensity_test.cpp:32 uses its own 8-entry table and calls SweepProcessor directly, so it cannot catch this.

findings.title: Sweep 'intensity' scales band input level, so out-of-focus bands are muted instead of passing clean
findings.problem: The per-band sweep value multiplies the band's signal before distortion (`left *= sweep; right *= sweep;`). The wet output is only the sum of the bands (processor.cpp:502-503), so a band with intensity near 0 is removed from the output entirely, not left undistorted.
findings.why_wrong: FR-SWEEP-001 defines the sweep as 'Focused distortion intensity moving through frequency spectrum': the distortion amount should be focused, with the rest of the spectrum still passing. plans-overview.md does place a 'Sweep Intensity Multiply' at band input. But since there is no compensating make-up or dry path per band, the effect is a sweeping band-pass filter on the whole signal, not a sweeping distortion focus.
findings.consequence: Turning Sweep on in the default 4-band patch (centre 1 kHz, width 1.5 oct, intensity 0.5) gives band gains of 100 Hz: -91 dB, 600 Hz: -10 dB, 3 kHz: -25 dB and 12 kHz: -105 dB. Bass and top vanish from the wet signal at mix 100 %, and the result reads as a narrow band-pass at -10 dB, not 'distortion moving through the spectrum'.
findings.suggested_fix: Decide the semantics with the spec owner. Either apply the intensity to drive or wet-mix per band (out-of-focus bands pass dry), or apply make-up gain after the morph stage. Test: sweep enabled, broadband pink noise in, mix 100 %. Assert that the output level in a band far from the sweep centre stays within 3 dB of its sweep-disabled level while its THD drops.
findings.evidence: band_processor.h:478-482 `const float sweep = sweepSmoother_.process(); // Step 1: Apply sweep intensity BEFORE distortion/morph (per plan.md) left *= sweep; right *= sweep;`. specs/Disrumpo/specs-overview.md:275-277 'FR-SWEEP-001 ... Focused distortion intensity moving through frequency spectrum'. Gains computed with sweep_morph_link.h calculateGaussianIntensity (sigma=width/2) at the kBandCenterFreqs.
verifier_notes:
I could not refute this. The source does what the finding says.

Code path:
- processor.cpp:426-441: when sweep is enabled, SweepProcessor::calculateAllBandIntensities works out a Gaussian intensity for each band from the fixed band centres (processor.cpp:422-424: 100, 600, 3000, 12000 Hz). It hands each value to BandProcessor::setSweepIntensity.
- band_processor.h:196-198: setSweepIntensity clamps the value to [0,1] and sets it as the sweepSmoother_ target.
- band_processor.h:478-482: the smoothed value multiplies the band signal (`left *= sweep; right *= sweep;`) before the morph or distortion stage at 485-496. Nothing restores the level afterwards: lines 510-511 only apply gain, pan and mute.
- processor.cpp:481-503: the wet signal is just the sum of the processed bands, `outputL = inputL*dryMix + sumL*outputGain*wetMix`. There is no per-band dry or bypass path. So a band with intensity near 0 drops out of the wet output instead of passing through undistorted.
- If the distortion's own internal mix is below 1, its dry part sits after the multiply too, so that part is also attenuated.

Gaussian formula, sweep_morph_link.h:143-165: intensityParam * exp(-0.5*(d/sigma)^2), with sigma = width/2.

One correction to the finding's numbers. A normalized Sweep Intensity of 0.5 maps to 1.0, not 0.5: processor.cpp:289 and processor_state.cpp:488 both use `*2.0f`. At 1 kHz centre and 1.5 octave width that gives these band gains:
- 100 Hz: about -85 dB (the finding said -91)
- 600 Hz: about -4 dB (the finding said -10)
- 3 kHz: about -19 dB (the finding said -25)
- 12 kHz: about -99 dB (the finding said -105)

Every band is off by the same 6 dB, so the conclusion stands: the low and high bands vanish from the wet signal.

Related clamp issue: setSweepIntensity clamps to 1.0, so the 0-200% range in FR-SWEEP-002 can never boost a band. That fits the reading that the sweep acts as a level gate.

On intent: plans-overview.md:78 puts "Sweep Intensity Multiply" at the band input, and sweep_band_intensity_test.cpp:190 even asserts that zero intensity attenuates the output. The finding already acknowledges both. They show the multiply was implemented as planned, not that the band-pass result meets FR-SWEEP-001 ("Focused distortion intensity moving through frequency spectrum", specs-overview.md:275-276). The finding asks the spec owner to settle the semantics, which is a fair framing.

Medium severity is appropriate: with Sweep on at 100% mix, most of the spectrum disappears.

I found no context that clears the code. band_processor.h:478-482 multiplies the band's signal by the sweep value before distortion. Nothing downstream compensates for it: processor.cpp:492-503 sums the processed bands into sumL/sumR, and there is no per-band dry path or make-up gain. At wet mix 100 %, a band with intensity near 0 is therefore removed from the output.

The intensities come from processor.cpp:426-435, using the fixed centres {100, 600, 3000, 12000} Hz from processor.cpp:422-424. They are computed by sweep_morph_link.h:143-165, a Gaussian with sigma = width/2 scaled by the intensity parameter. With centre 1 kHz, width 1.5 oct and intensity 0.5, the 100 Hz band is 3.32 oct away, which gives exp(-9.8) * 0.5, about -91 dB. That matches the finding's numbers. The Sharp falloff (sweep_morph_link.h:167-170, "exactly 0.0 at the edge and beyond") silences a band completely.

The design docs back the finding, not the code:
- The retired spec specs/_archive2_/007-sweep-system/spec.md:126 says the per-band multiplier exists "so each band receives the appropriate amount of distortion".
- The same spec at :378 says "BandProcessor can accept an intensity multiplier from SweepProcessor to scale distortion intensity".
- tasks.md:307 (T067) says "multiply distortion gain or intensity per band".
- specs-overview.md:275-276 (FR-SWEEP-001) says "Focused distortion intensity moving through frequency spectrum".

None of these ask for the band's level to be removed. The only support for the current code is the plans-overview.md:78 box "Sweep Intensity Multiply" at band input, cited by the code comment. That diagram does not say where the multiplier acts, so it is not a recorded decision to mute out-of-focus bands.

There is a further mismatch the finding did not raise. band_processor.h:196-198 clamps the intensity to [0,1], but spec 007 FR-010 (spec.md:236) and the shared header both define a range of [0,2] (200 % means 2.0 at the centre). That ceiling is unreachable as implemented.

Tests: sweep_band_intensity_test.cpp:190-206 ("Zero sweep intensity attenuates output") and morph_band_integration_test.cpp:164-168 do pin the attenuation. They are unit checks written against the implementation, not a stated design ruling, and they do not establish that removing bands from the summed output is intended.

Reachability: sweep is a global toggle, but it is a user-facing feature that any user can enable, so the defect is reachable in a real host. Medium severity stands.

The finding describes the code and the numbers correctly. What it gets wrong is the claim that this breaks the spec: the behaviour is what the spec asked for.

What the code does:
- band_processor.h:478-482 multiplies the band input by the smoothed sweep value before morph/distortion.
- processor.cpp:426-440 sets that value per block from sweepProcessor_.calculateAllBandIntensities(), using fixed centres {100, 600, 3000, 12000} Hz (processor.cpp:422-424). When sweep is off, every band gets 1.0.
- processor.cpp:502-503 builds the wet signal only from the band sum. There is no dry path per band.
- With the defaults (sweep_processor.h:43/52/58: 1 kHz, 1.5 oct, intensity_ 0.5) and calculateGaussianIntensity (sweep_morph_link.h:143-165, sigma = 0.75 oct), I get 100 Hz -91 dB, 600 Hz -10.2 dB, 3 kHz -25.4 dB and 12 kHz -105 dB. These match the finding.

Why it is intended:
- The retired feature spec, recovered with `git show` on specs/007-sweep-system/spec.md, says at line 32: "verifying that bands within the sweep region receive increased distortion intensity while outer bands are attenuated." Removing the outer bands from the wet signal is the specified acceptance behaviour, not a deviation.
- FR-010 and the clarification at line 207 call for multiplicative scaling with centre = intensity parameter, so 50 % gives a 0.5 multiplier.
- specs/Disrumpo/plans-overview.md:75-81 puts "Sweep Intensity Multiply" at band input, ahead of the morph stage. The finding admits this.
- The tests pin the same behaviour: tests/integration/sweep_band_intensity_test.cpp:190-206 ("Zero sweep intensity attenuates output", requires |out| < 0.01) and morph_band_integration_test.cpp:164-165 ("silence before distortion").
- The sentence the finding relies on ("Focused distortion intensity moving through frequency spectrum", specs-overview) does not say that out-of-focus bands must pass clean. The more specific 007 spec says they are attenuated.

Impact: sweep is off by default, and turning it on gives exactly the attenuation the design specifies. No crash, NaN, click or state fault follows. Wanting out-of-focus bands to pass dry is a product-design change for the spec owner, not a conformance defect.

A side note for the report: the band centres are hardcoded and do not follow the actual crossover frequencies (processor.cpp:422-424). That is a separate issue.
corroborated_by_measurement: probe sweep:off-centre-band-level (11 kHz sine, centre 100 Hz): "level_off_dB -40.60, level_on_dB -165.36, delta_dB -124.76" (threshold "delta > -6 dB"). sweep:full-automation: "rms_on_dB -20.98, rms_off_dB -11.99". preset near-silent: "Sweep/Sharp_Focus -53.02; Synced_Pulse -46.67; High_Sweep -48.41; Low_Rumble -43.49". Code: band_processor.h:481 `left *= sweep;`; processor.cpp:422 `kBandCenterFreqs = { 100.0f, 600.0f, 3000.0f, 12000.0f }`

findings.title: Sweep-morph link is not in the DSP: works only with the editor open and ignores sweep LFO/envelope/mod motion
findings.problem: The processor never applies a sweep-morph link. SweepProcessor::getMorphPosition (sweep_processor.h:297) has no caller. The global kSweepMorphLink only sets a field, kSweepCustomCurveP* are no-ops, and kBandMorphXLink/YLink are explicitly 'UI-only ... no processor action' (processor_params.cpp:971-978). The only working link is the controller's MorphSweepLinkController. It is created in Controller::didOpen (controller.cpp:1454-1456), observes only the BASE kSweepFrequency parameter, and writes kBandMorphX/Y with setParamNormalized + performEdit from IDependent::update.
findings.why_wrong: FR-SWEEP-003 / spec item 'Morph position can be linked to sweep frequency' describes a DSP behaviour, and a processor must work without its controller (CLAUDE.md VST3 architecture). Sweep automation sources include the internal LFO and the envelope follower (FR-SWEEP-004). Their motion exists only in the processor (modulatedFreq), so a UI-thread link on the base parameter cannot follow them. A controller performEdit issued in response to host-driven parameter changes, with no beginEdit, also creates automation feedback.
findings.consequence: With the editor closed (offline bounce, render in place, most sessions) the morph link does nothing, so renders differ from what was heard with the GUI open. With the editor open, the sweep LFO, envelope follower and mod-matrix sweep routes never move the morph cursor, only the base frequency knob does. During host playback of sweep-frequency automation the controller emits MorphX/Y edits, which hosts in write/touch/latch mode record as new automation. The global 'Sweep Morph Link' and custom curve parameters have no audible effect at all.
findings.suggested_fix: Implement the link in Processor::process. After the sweep smoother runs, compute per-band link positions from normalizeSweepFrequency(smoothed modulatedFreq) using each band's X/Y link mode, which the processor must then consume. Apply them as the morph-position base before the mod-engine offsets. Remove the controller-side performEdit path. Test (processor level, no controller): band 0 X link = Sweep Freq, sweep LFO on. Render and assert that the band's morph position (via a test accessor, or an audible morph between two contrasting nodes) follows the LFO.
findings.evidence: visibility_controllers.cpp:154-158 `float sweepNorm = static_cast<float>(sweepFreqParam_->getNormalized()); for (int band = 0; band < 8; ++band) updateBandMorphFromSweep(...)`; :199-208 `controller_->setParamNormalized(...kBandMorphX, newX); controller_->performEdit(...kBandMorphX, newX);` (no beginEdit). controller.cpp:1354 `void Controller::didOpen`, :1454-1456 `morphSweepLinkController_ = new MorphSweepLinkController(this, sweepFreqParam);`. processor_params.cpp:971-978 `case BandParamType::kBandMorphXLink: case BandParamType::kBandMorphYLink: ... // UI-only params (sweep-morph link ...): no processor action`. grep: getMorphPosition() is referenced only at sweep_processor.h:297.
verifier_notes:
I traced the call path in the source and the finding holds.

1. The processor ignores the per-band link params. processor_params.cpp:971-980 puts kBandMorphXLink/kBandMorphYLink in the same `default:` case as other UI-only params; the comment says "UI-only params (sweep-morph link, ...): no processor action".

2. The global link only sets a field. processor_params.cpp:410-414 kSweepMorphLink calls sweepProcessor_.setMorphLinkMode() and does nothing else. The only reader of morphLinkMode_ that produces a value is SweepProcessor::getMorphPosition (sweep_processor.h:297-309). A grep over plugins/disrumpo/src and tests finds getMorphPosition called only in tests/dsp/sweep_processor_tests.cpp:334-425, never in processor/*.cpp. The processor sets band morph only from bandMorphCache_ plus mod-engine offsets (processor.cpp:127, 309-316). No sweep-derived position ever reaches setMorphPosition.

3. The custom curve params do nothing. processor_params.cpp:495-521: PointCount does `(void)pointCount;` and P0X..P7Y just `break` ("defer rebuild to process loop"). A grep finds no rebuild in processor.cpp. customCurve_ changes only in setState (processor_state.cpp:552-569).

4. The only working link lives in the controller. controller.cpp:1454-1456 creates MorphSweepLinkController inside the editor-open path, next to the morph pad and spectrum setup. It observes only the base kSweepFrequency Parameter object (visibility_controllers.cpp:120-130, 154-158). It writes MorphX/Y with setParamNormalized + performEdit and no beginEdit/endEdit (visibility_controllers.cpp:197-209).

Consequences that follow from this:
- With the editor closed, nothing implements the link.
- The sweep LFO, envelope follower and mod-matrix routes move the frequency only inside the processor, so the link never follows them.
- The global Sweep Morph Link mode has no audible effect; on the controller side it only drives a visibility controller (controller.cpp:1492-1495).
- The controller calls performEdit when the host changes kSweepFrequency, so host automation playback generates MorphX/Y edits, which is an automation feedback path.

Severity stays as reported. This is a functional feature gap that changes renders depending on whether the editor is open, but it is not a crash or real-time safety violation.

I could not refute it: the code confirms the claim, and nothing documents this as a design choice or guards against it.
(1) The processor never applies a per-band morph link. processor_params.cpp:971-979 groups kBandMorphXLink/kBandMorphYLink with expanded/selectedNode/displayedType as "UI-only params (sweep-morph link, ...): no processor action". No design note supports this. specs/Disrumpo/specs-overview.md:287-297 (FR-SWEEP-003/004) describes the link as a sweep feature alongside LFO/envelope automation, and roadmap.md M5 / plans-overview IT-006 list "Sweep with morph link" as a DSP milestone. The controller-only link has no processor-level test. findings.title: Two sweep-morph link curve implementations disagree; the live one swaps Ease In/Out against the spec
findings.problem: The link curves exist twice with different formulas. The live controller version (morph_link.cpp applyMorphLinkMode) uses EaseIn = sqrt(x), EaseOut = x^2, HoldRise holding until 0.5, and Stepped = floor(5x)/4 (5 levels). The DSP version (sweep_morph_link.h applyMorphLinkCurve, unit-tested but never called in the plugin) uses EaseIn = x^2, EaseOut = 1-(1-x)^2, HoldRise holding until 0.6, and Stepped = min(floor(4x),3)/3 (4 levels).
findings.why_wrong: specs/Disrumpo/dsp-details.md §8.1/8.2 defines EaseIn y = x^2, EaseOut y = 1-(1-x)^2, HoldRise flat until 60 % and Stepped floor(x*4)/3. The DSP copy matches that, but the copy that runs inverts Ease In/Out and changes HoldRise and Stepped. The tests (tests/dsp/sweep_morph_link_tests.cpp) cover only the dead DSP copy, and plugin_ids.h:647 documents a third variant (0, .25, .5, .75, 1).
findings.consequence: Users choosing 'Ease In' get the spec's Ease Out shape (fast start) and the reverse. Hold-Rise starts rising at a different sweep position, and Stepped has 5 steps instead of 4. Any move of the link into the processor (see the link finding) will change the sound of existing sessions unless one formula is chosen.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete morph_link.cpp's curve switch and call the shared applyMorphLinkCurve from one place, ideally the processor. Fix the plugin_ids.h:647 comment. Test: a table test that pins each MorphLinkMode at x = 0.25/0.5/0.75 against the dsp-details.md formulas and is run through the code path that drives audio.
findings.evidence: morph_link.cpp:44-65 `case MorphLinkMode::EaseIn: return std::sqrt(sweepNorm); case MorphLinkMode::EaseOut: return sweepNorm * sweepNorm; case MorphLinkMode::HoldRise: if (sweepNorm < 0.5f) return 0.0f; return (sweepNorm - 0.5f) * 2.0f; case MorphLinkMode::Stepped: return std::min(std::floor(sweepNorm * 5.0f) / 4.0f, 1.0f);` vs sweep_morph_link.h `case MorphLinkMode::EaseIn: return x * x; case MorphLinkMode::EaseOut: return 1.0f - (1.0f - x) * (1.0f - x); case MorphLinkMode::HoldRise: if (x < 0.6f) ... case MorphLinkMode::Stepped: return std::min(std::floor(x * 4.0f), 3.0f) / 3.0f;`. dsp-details.md:1264-1268 table.
verifier_notes: The core claim checks out. The live path is visibility_controllers.cpp:162-209. MorphSweepLinkController::updateBandMorphFromSweep calls applyMorphLinkMode (lines 194-195) and then calls setParamNormalized/performEdit on the band MorphX/Y. applyMorphLinkMode is in morph_link.cpp:44-65. EaseIn there is sqrt(x) (line 47), EaseOut is x*x (line 52), HoldRise holds until 0.5 and then returns (x-0.5)*2 (lines 56-59), and Stepped is min(floor(5x)/4, 1), five levels (line 65). The DSP copy is sweep_morph_link.h:81-118. There EaseIn is x*x (100), EaseOut is 1-(1-x)^2 (104), HoldRise holds until 0.6 and then returns (x-0.6)/0.4 (109-112), and Stepped is min(floor(4x),3)/3 (118). That copy matches specs/Disrumpo/dsp-details.md:1264-1268 and 1300-1317. The DSP copy's only plugin caller is SweepProcessor::getMorphPosition (sweep_processor.h:297-308). A grep of plugins/disrumpo/src finds no caller of getMorphPosition, so that copy only drives tests/dsp/sweep_morph_link_tests.cpp. The controller copy has its own test (tests/unit/morph_link_test.cpp), which pins the controller formulas. So the claim that the tests cover only the DSP copy is wrong: both copies are tested, each against its own formulas. One more correction: plugin_ids.h:647 ("0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0") is not a third variant. It describes the live controller formula, and the enum comments at 644-646 ("emphasizing low frequencies", "hold until mid-point") also follow the controller version. The controller copy follows the retired 006-morph-ui FR-034b-e wording cited in morph_link.cpp:6. That means two spec sources disagree, but the shipping behaviour still differs from the current reference doc dsp-details.md §8: Ease In and Ease Out are swapped, the HoldRise threshold is 0.5 instead of 0.6, and Stepped has 5 levels instead of 4. Duplicate, divergent implementations are confirmed. The secondary inaccuracies (the test-coverage claim and the 'third variant' claim) do not change the defect.

The finding treats two separate features as one. They share the MorphLinkMode enum but each has its own spec, and the live code matches the spec that governs it.

(1) The live code is morph_link.cpp:27-70 applyMorphLinkMode, called only by MorphSweepLinkController::updateBandMorphFromSweep (visibility_controllers.cpp:162-210, created at controller.cpp:1456). It drives the per-band kBandMorphXLink/kBandMorphYLink parameters (plugin_ids.h:190). Its spec is the 006-morph-ui feature, not dsp-details.md section 8:
- specs/_archive2_/006-morph-ui/spec.md:265-268, FR-034b: EaseIn "emphasizing low frequencies (more morph range allocated to bass)". FR-034c: EaseOut emphasizing highs. FR-034d: hold "until sweep reaches mid-point". FR-034e: steps "0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0".
- 006-morph-ui/plan.md:364-367 gives EaseIn as `std::pow(sweepNorm, 0.5f)`, "more range in bass".
