findings.title: setActive(true) and setupProcessing wipe every modulation routing and macro (ModulationEngine::reset clears routings_/macros_)
findings.problem: Processor::setActive(true) calls modulationEngine_.reset(). setupProcessing calls modulationEngine_.prepare(), which also ends in reset() (modulation_engine.h:123). The shared ModulationEngine::reset() does more than reset sources: it sets every routing to ModRouting{} and every macro to MacroConfig{} (modulation_engine.h:152-160). The routings and macros held by the processor live only inside the engine. Nothing re-applies them after the reset.
findings.why_wrong: setActive(true) and prepare are signal-state resets, not parameter resets. VST3 hosts activate after setState, and they re-activate on transport changes, sample-rate or offline-render changes, and plugin off/on. Routing amount, source and destination are user parameters. They must survive activation, the same way gains survive it (setupProcessing re-pushes bandStates_).
findings.consequence: In both host orders (setState before setupProcessing, or setState after setupProcessing but before setActive), all 32 mod routings and 4 macros are silently dropped. The mod matrix UI still shows them, but nothing modulates. The next host save writes empty routings, which makes the loss permanent. The same happens on a running instance whenever the host toggles activation. This is a SHARED-DSP-CONTRACT issue: ruinae_engine.h:197 also calls globalModEngine_.reset(), so check whether Ruinae re-applies its routings every block.
findings.suggested_fix: Split ModulationEngine::reset() into resetSources() (LFO phase, envelopes, smoothers, offsets) and a separate clearRoutings(). Use only the source reset from setActive and prepare. Alternatively, Disrumpo can keep a routing/macro cache and re-apply it after the reset. Test: set routings through processParameterChanges or setState -> setActive(false) -> setActive(true) -> getState must still contain the routings. Also assert that an LFO->InputGain routing still modulates the output after re-activation. Run the consumers of modulation_engine.h (node tools/header-consumers.js).
findings.evidence: processor.cpp:163-164 `// Reset modulation engine\n modulationEngine_.reset();`; processor.cpp:139 `modulationEngine_.prepare(sampleRate_, setup.maxSamplesPerBlock);`; modulation_engine.h:123 `reset();` (end of prepare); modulation_engine.h:152-160 `// Reset routings for (auto& r : routings_) { r = ModRouting{}; } // Reset macros for (auto& m : macros_) { m = MacroConfig{}; }`.
verifier_notes:
I traced the claim through the source and it holds.

1. Processor::setActive(true) calls `modulationEngine_.reset()` with no condition (plugins/disrumpo/src/processor/processor.cpp:163-164). setupProcessing calls `modulationEngine_.prepare(sampleRate_, setup.maxSamplesPerBlock)` (processor.cpp:139).
2. ModulationEngine::prepare ends with `reset();` (dsp/include/krate/dsp/systems/modulation_engine.h:123). reset() sets every `routings_` entry to `ModRouting{}` and every `macros_` entry to `MacroConfig{}` (modulation_engine.h:152-160). It is not just a source reset.
3. Disrumpo keeps no copy of the routings or macros. The engine member is a plain `Krate::DSP::ModulationEngine modulationEngine_;` (processor.h:247), and the only grep hits for setRouting/setMacro* in plugins/disrumpo/src are listed below. None of them runs in setActive, setupProcessing or process(), so nothing puts the data back after a reset.
   - processParameterChanges: read-modify-write via `getRouting(routIdx)` then `setRouting` (processor_params.cpp:551-572), plus the macro setters (processor_params.cpp:765-817).
   - setState: processor_state.cpp:751-798.
4. getState serializes straight from the engine (`modulationEngine_.getMacro(m)` and `modulationEngine_.getRouting(r)`, processor_state.cpp:288-308). After a reset it therefore writes empty routings and default macros, so the next save makes the loss permanent.
5. Lifecycle: VST3 hosts call setActive(true) after setComponentState when loading a project, and call it again when activation is toggled. Either way the restored routings and macros are wiped.
6. The existing test does not catch this. serialization_round_trip_test.cpp calls `setupProcessing` (line 59) before setState and never calls setActive afterwards, so its round trips pass.

The defect is real as described, and critical severity fits: it silently drops all user modulation on every project load.

The defect is confirmed from source. No guard, cache or re-apply step exists.

1. processor.cpp:163-164: setActive(true) calls `modulationEngine_.reset()`. processor.cpp:139: setupProcessing calls `modulationEngine_.prepare(...)`.
2. modulation_engine.h:96-124: prepare() ends with `reset();` at line 123.
3. modulation_engine.h:127-161: reset() resets the sources and smoothers. It also sets every routing to `ModRouting{}` (lines 152-155) and every macro to `MacroConfig{}` (lines 157-160).
4. Routings and macros are stored only inside the engine. A grep of plugins/disrumpo/src/processor for setRouting, setMacro, getRouting and routing finds only these writers:
   - processor_state.cpp:751-798: setState writes them through setMacroValue/Min/Max/Curve and setRouting.
   - processor_params.cpp:546-572 and 765-817: processParameterChanges writes them.
   - The only reader is getState (processor_state.cpp:289-306), which serializes them straight from `modulationEngine_.getRouting(r)` and `getMacro(m)`.
   - No processor-side copy exists, and neither setActive nor setupProcessing re-applies anything. setActive only resets DSP and the DataExchange, then calls sendModOffsetsMessage (processor.cpp:147-170).
5. A real host reaches this. Hosts call setState on project load before setupProcessing and setActive(true), and they toggle activation on sample-rate changes, offline renders and plugin off/on. Hosts do not re-send every parameter on activation. So the routings and macros loaded by setState are wiped, and the next getState writes empty routings. That makes the loss permanent.
6. No test pins or covers this. Six Disrumpo test files call setActive: processor_audio_output_test, multi_node_distortion_test, bitcrush_noise_repro_test, data_exchange_spectrum_test, morph_pad_test and node_editor_test. None checks that mod routings survive activation.
7. Nothing documents it as a Disrumpo design decision. The engine's own doc comment says "Reset all sources and routing state", so clearing routings is intended behaviour of the shared engine. Disrumpo calling it as a signal-state reset on activation is the bug.

Severity stays as filed. Every project reload silently drops the user's whole mod matrix, and the next save makes that loss permanent.

The defect is confirmed from source, and the claimed consequence does follow.

1. processor.cpp:163-164: setActive(true) calls `modulationEngine_.reset()`. processor.cpp:139: setupProcessing calls `modulationEngine_.prepare()`, and prepare ends in `reset()` (modulation_engine.h:123).
2. modulation_engine.h:152-160: reset() sets every `routings_[i] = ModRouting{}` and every `macros_[i] = MacroConfig{}`. Git history (05a3ddb7, 3a680b52, 3abeef52) shows this behaviour is long-standing, not new.
3. processor.h:247: the processor holds a plain `Krate::DSP::ModulationEngine modulationEngine_;` with no wrapper and no cache. Routings and macros are only ever written into the engine, in three places:
   - processor_params.cpp:546-572: setRouting on a routing parameter change.
   - processor_params.cpp:763-817: setMacro* on a macro parameter change.
   - processor_state.cpp:747-799: setState.
   Nothing re-applies them after a reset.
4. getState reads them back from the engine (processor_state.cpp:289 `getMacro`, :299 `getRouting`). After a reset the next save writes empty routings and default macros, so the loss becomes permanent.
5. No Disrumpo test covers this. A grep for getRouting in plugins/disrumpo/tests returns nothing, so no test checks that routings survive setActive.

Impact. The usual VST3 load order is initialize -> setupProcessing -> setState -> setActive(true). In that order setState restores the routings, then setActive(true) wipes them. So in effect every reloaded project loses all 32 mod routings and all 4 macro settings without warning, while the controller and UI still show them. The same loss happens on a running instance whenever the host re-activates the plugin, for example on a sample-rate or block-size change, or when the plugin is toggled off and on. Only a host that calls setState after setActive escapes it at load, and that host still hits it on the next re-activation. The result is silent data loss of user settings that becomes permanent on save, so the critical severity stands.

Cross-plugin check: Ruinae also calls `globalModEngine_.reset()` (ruinae_engine.h:197). However, its processor re-pushes every route from its parameter values (processor_params.cpp:494, `engine_.setGlobalModRoute(i, ...)`, which ends in `globalModEngine_.setRouting` at ruinae_engine.h:466). So the visible defect is specific to Disrumpo, because Disrumpo relies on the engine as the only store. The shared reset() contract, which clears both sources and routings, is still the trap that a fix should address.

findings.title: Processor getState writes literal 0 for per-band Morph Mode and Morph Smoothing
findings.problem: getState writes `writeInt8(0) // morphMode` and `writeFloat(0.0f) // morphSmoothing (ms)` for every band. The real values set through kBandMorphMode and kBandMorphSmoothing (processor_params.cpp:958-969) are never written. setState then applies them: setMorphMode(0) and setMorphSmoothingTime(0) (lines 827-831). Controller::parseComponentState pushes 0 to the UI params (controller.cpp:522-529).
findings.why_wrong: The host session format must round-trip every persistent parameter. The preset writer (controller.cpp:1829, 1834) writes the real mode and smoothing into the same layout, so the two writers disagree on identical fields.
findings.consequence: After any project save and reload, every band reverts to 1D Linear morph and 0 ms morph smoothing, which is lower than the engine's 10 ms default. Users who chose 2D Planar or Radial lose it, and morph moves click because smoothing is off. The UI shows the reverted values, so the loss is not obvious.
findings.suggested_fix: Cache morphMode and morphSmoothingMs in BandMorphCache. Write them in processParameterChanges and setState, and serialise the cached values in getState. Test: set kBandMorphMode = 2D Radial and smoothing = 200 ms on band 1, call getState, call setState on a fresh processor, then assert the engine's mode and smoothing and the bytes at the morphMode and smoothing offsets.
findings.evidence: processor_state.cpp:319 `if (!streamer.writeInt8(static_cast<Steinberg::int8>(0)))  // morphMode`; :323 `if (!streamer.writeFloat(0.0f))  // morphSmoothing (ms)`; :827-831 `bandProcessors_[b].setMorphMode(...morphMode...); ... bandProcessors_[b].setMorphSmoothingTime(morphSmoothing);`; controller.cpp:1829,1834 preset writer writes `getInt8FromList(...kBandMorphMode, 2)` and `smoothingNorm * 500.0f`.
verifier_notes: The defect is real. processor_state.cpp:319 writes `writeInt8(0) // morphMode` and :323 writes `writeFloat(0.0f) // morphSmoothing (ms)` for every band. Nothing in the processor stores these values: grep over src/ finds morphMode and morphSmoothing only in the state code. processor_params.cpp:958-969 sends kBandMorphSmoothing and kBandMorphMode straight to bandProcessors_[band].setMorphSmoothingTime / setMorphMode (band_processor.h:260-287, forwarded to MorphEngine) and never writes them into bandMorphCache_. On reload, processor setState (processor_state.cpp:813-831) reads the 0s and applies setMorphMode(Linear1D) and setMorphSmoothingTime(0) to every band. Controller::setComponentState -> parseComponentState (controller.cpp:513-529) pushes the same 0s to the kBandMorphMode and kBandMorphSmoothing params, so the UI shows the reverted values. Controller::getState/setState (controller.cpp:658-701) save only a version, two unused doubles and the MIDI CC mappings, so no controller-side copy survives either. The controller's preset writer (controller.cpp:1829, 1833-1834) writes the real mode and smoothing into the same layout, so the two writers disagree, as the finding says. No test in plugins/disrumpo/tests round-trips kBandMorphMode or kBandMorphSmoothing; they appear only in parameter_encoding_test.cpp ID checks. One detail of the consequence is wrong: the smoothing parameter's registered default is 0 ms (parameter_registration.cpp:719, RangeParameter 0..500, default 0.0). So losing smoothing only matters for users who raised it, and it is not a drop below a "10 ms default". Losing a chosen 2D Planar or Radial mode on every session reload is a real, silent change to the sound, so high severity stands.

The defect is real and I found nothing that guards it. processor_state.cpp:319 writes `writeInt8(0) // morphMode` and :323 writes `writeFloat(0.0f) // morphSmoothing (ms)` for every band. The processor never caches either value: processor_params.cpp:958-969 sends kBandMorphSmoothing (value*500) and kBandMorphMode (idx 0..2) straight to bandProcessors_[band] and never stores them in bandMorphCache_. On reload, processor_state.cpp:819-831 reads those bytes and applies them with setMorphMode(clamp(0)) and setMorphSmoothingTime(0). Controller::parseComponentState (controller.cpp:522-529) then pushes 0 to the UI params, so the editor shows the lost values. Both params are registered as automatable and user-facing (parameter_registration.cpp:687-693 StringListParameter "1D Linear/2D Planar/2D Radial" kCanAutomate, and :717-720 RangeParameter 0-500 ms kCanAutomate), and they appear in editor.uidesc (20 MorphMode/MorphSmooth hits). The controller's preset writer (controller.cpp:1829, 1833-1834) writes the real values into the same layout, which shows the processor's zeros are a defect and not a deliberate format choice. No comment or spec marks them as intentionally not persisted. No state round-trip test covers them: the tests that grep for these names are morph/oversampling DSP tests and parameter-encoding tests, not getState/setState round-trips. One correction to the consequence text: the controller's registered default for smoothing is 0 ms (parameter_registration.cpp:719), so the smoothing loss only matters when the user had raised it. The "lower than the engine's 10 ms default" framing is partly beside the point. The Morph Mode loss (2D Planar/Radial reverting to 1D Linear on every session reload) is a real silent loss of user state, so I keep severity high.

I could not refute the finding. The code confirms the defect and the consequence is real.

1. **The stored values are hard-coded.** processor_state.cpp:319 writes `writeInt8(static_cast<int8>(0)) // morphMode` and :323 writes `writeFloat(0.0f) // morphSmoothing (ms)` for every band. They are not real values.
2. **The real values are applied but never kept.** processor_params.cpp:958-969 sends kBandMorphSmoothing (value*500 ms) and kBandMorphMode (idx 0-2) straight to bandProcessors_ (setMorphSmoothingTime / setMorphMode). Nothing caches them, so getState has nothing to write. BandMorphCache holds only morphX, morphY, activeNodeCount and the nodes.
3. **Reload applies the zeros to the engine.** setState at processor_state.cpp:813-831 reads the bytes and calls `setMorphMode(clamp(morphMode))` and `setMorphSmoothingTime(morphSmoothing)`. After a project reload every band runs in Linear1D with 0 ms smoothing. The controller then pushes 0 / 500 to the UI (controller.cpp:523, :529). The preset writer at controller.cpp:1829/1833 does write the real values, so the two writers disagree on the same layout.
4. **The mode is user-facing and audible.** It is exposed in the editor (editor.uidesc:1326 CSegmentButton "1D, 2D, Radial"; :1330 ArcKnob for smoothing). morph_engine.cpp:179-247 computes the weights in very different ways per mode: Linear1D uses only X distance, Planar2D uses Euclidean XY, Radial2D calls calculateRadialWeights. With the cursor in the same place, a band set to 2D Planar or Radial gets different node weights after reload, so the distortion blend sounds different.

**Overstated parts:**
- The 0 ms smoothing equals the parameter's registered default (parameter_registration.cpp:719, default 0.0). So for smoothing, reloading lands on the UI default, not on something unusual. It is only below the engine's internal 10 ms (morph_engine.h:221).
- Losing smoothing only causes zipper noise or clicks when the morph position moves after reload (automation or pad drags). It does not change the steady-state sound.

**Severity:** high stands. A user-chosen setting that is visible in the UI and changes the sound is silently reset on every DAW session save and reload, in every host.

findings.title: setState does not restore the sweep width/intensity base atomics, so loaded width and intensity are overwritten on the next block
findings.problem: setState calls only sweepProcessor_.setWidth() and setIntensity(). process() overwrites both every block from baseSweepWidthNorm_ and baseSweepIntensityNorm_ (processor.cpp:276-290). Those atomics are written only by processParameterChanges (processor_params.cpp:396, 404), and their defaults are 0.286 and 0.25 (processor.h:227, 230). By contrast, baseSweepFrequency_ is updated in setState (line 482).
findings.why_wrong: The base value that process() reads is the parameter's source of truth. setState must write it, as it already does for the frequency.
findings.consequence: After a project reload, the sweep width runs at 0.5 + 0.286*3.5 = 1.5 oct and the intensity at 0.5 (50 % on the DSP's 0-200 % scale), whatever was saved. The controller shows the saved values. The next getState saves the defaults, which makes the loss permanent.
findings.suggested_fix: In setState, store sweepWidthNorm into baseSweepWidthNorm_ and sweepIntensityNorm into baseSweepIntensityNorm_ alongside the setter calls. Test: build a v12 stream with width 3 oct and intensity 150 %, call setState, process one block, then assert sweepProcessor_.getWidth()==3 and getIntensity()==1.5 and that getState returns the same normalized values.
findings.evidence: processor_state.cpp:485-488 `if (streamer.readFloat(sweepWidthNorm)) sweepProcessor_.setWidth(0.5f + sweepWidthNorm * 3.5f); if (streamer.readFloat(sweepIntensityNorm)) sweepProcessor_.setIntensity(sweepIntensityNorm * 2.0f);` vs processor.cpp:277-282 `const float baseWidthNorm = baseSweepWidthNorm_.load(...); ... sweepProcessor_.setWidth(kMinWidth + modWidthNorm * (kMaxWidth - kMinWidth));`; grep: baseSweepWidthNorm_ written only at processor_params.cpp:396.
verifier_notes: I traced the claim through the source and it holds. In processor_state.cpp:480-488, setState stores the loaded frequency into baseSweepFrequency_ (line 482). For width and intensity it only calls sweepProcessor_.setWidth(0.5f + n*3.5f) (line 486) and setIntensity(n*2.0f) (line 488). A grep for baseSweepWidthNorm_ and baseSweepIntensityNorm_ across plugins/disrumpo/src finds three kinds of hit and nothing else: the declarations with defaults 0.286f and 0.25f (processor.h:227, 230), the stores in processParameterChanges (processor_params.cpp:396, 404), and the loads in process() (processor.cpp:277, 286). The process() block at processor.cpp:276-290 runs on every block with no condition. It reads both atomics, passes them through modulationEngine_.getModulatedValue (the comment at line 254 says the offset is 0 when nothing is routed, so the base value comes back unchanged), and calls sweepProcessor_.setWidth(0.5 + n*3.5) and setIntensity(n*2). So the first process() after setState replaces the restored width and intensity with the defaults: 1.501 oct and 0.5, or whatever value was last sent through processParameterChanges. The VST3 host->processor state path does not push parameter changes back into the processor; setComponentState only updates the controller. getState (processor_state.cpp:89, 91) serializes sweepProcessor_.getWidth() and getIntensity(), so a save after one processed block writes the defaults and makes the loss permanent, as the finding says. This setState path also loads the stored state of every project and preset, so any saved state or preset with a non-default sweep width or intensity plays back wrong. The defect is confirmed and the high severity fits.

I could not refute this. The defect is in the source as described.

- **What setState does:** processor_state.cpp:485-488 reads sweepWidthNorm and sweepIntensityNorm and passes them only to sweepProcessor_.setWidth() and setIntensity(). The frequency, at line 482, is also stored into baseSweepFrequency_.
- **Where the atomics are written:** a grep over plugins/disrumpo/src finds baseSweepWidthNorm_ written only at processor_params.cpp:396 and baseSweepIntensityNorm_ only at processor_params.cpp:404. Their defaults are 0.286f and 0.25f (processor.h:227, 230).
- **What process() does:** processor.cpp:276-290 has no guard. Every block, after modulationEngine_.process (line 246), it calls sweepProcessor_.setWidth(0.5 + getModulatedValue(kSweepWidth, baseSweepWidthNorm_)*3.5) and setIntensity(getModulatedValue(kSweepIntensity, baseSweepIntensityNorm_)*2). The first block after a load therefore overwrites the restored values with the stale defaults, or with the values from the last parameter change.
- **Why the loss is permanent:** getState (processor_state.cpp:89, 91) serializes sweepProcessor_.getWidth() and getIntensity(). The next save writes the clobbered values.
- **No guard elsewhere:** there is no setActive reset, no reload of the atomics, and no comment marking this as a design decision. VST3 hosts are not required to send parameter changes to the processor after setState.
- **No test pins it:** state_persistence_test.cpp only checks the MIDI-mapping and window-size logic and the enum values. sweep_processor_tests.cpp only tests SweepProcessor on its own. No test does setState, then process, then getState.

A saved project or preset with a non-default sweep width or intensity reloads with the wrong sound, and the next save makes that permanent. High severity is appropriate.

I could not refute this. Every link in the claimed chain is in the source.

1. setState only calls the setters. processor_state.cpp:485-488 calls sweepProcessor_.setWidth(0.5f + sweepWidthNorm*3.5f) and setIntensity(sweepIntensityNorm*2.0f). It never stores to baseSweepWidthNorm_ or baseSweepIntensityNorm_. Line 482 does store to baseSweepFrequency_, so the frequency is restored and the other two are not.

2. The atomics have only one writer. A grep over plugins/disrumpo finds stores to baseSweepWidthNorm_ only at processor_params.cpp:396 and to baseSweepIntensityNorm_ only at processor_params.cpp:404. Their defaults are 0.286f and 0.25f (processor.h:227, 230).

3. process() overwrites the restored values on every block. processor.cpp:276-290 runs unconditionally, not gated on sweep enable. It loads both atomics, passes them through modulationEngine_.getModulatedValue, and calls sweepProcessor_.setWidth(0.5 + n*3.5) and setIntensity(n*2.0). So the first block after setState sets width to 0.5 + 0.286*3.5 = 1.501 oct and intensity to 0.5 (50 %), whatever was loaded.

4. The loss becomes permanent. getState serializes from the live DSP object: processor_state.cpp:89 writes (sweepProcessor_.getWidth()-0.5)/3.5 and line 91 writes getIntensity()/2. Once one block has run, the next save writes the defaults.

5. Nothing in the controller or host masks it on a project reload. Controller::setComponentState (controller.cpp:619) only updates the controller side, so the UI shows the saved values while the DSP runs the defaults. Hosts do not send parameter changes to the processor after setState, so processor_params.cpp:396/404 is never reached on a reload.

Impact: any saved project with sweep enabled and a non-default width or intensity sounds wrong after reload. For example, a saved 3 oct / 150 % sweep plays at 1.5 oct / 50 %, which audibly changes how many bands the sweep drives and how hard. The user sees the right knob values and cannot tell, and the next save writes the defaults over the saved values. There is no test coverage: the tests/ grep finds getWidth/getIntensity only in dsp/sweep_processor_tests.cpp, which tests the SweepProcessor in isolation, not the processor round-trip.

The trigger is narrower than "every session" because it needs sweep enabled and non-default values. It is still silent, permanent loss of user state, so high severity stands.

findings.title: Host-path setState never re-derives the type-specific DistortionParams from the restored shape slots
findings.problem: setState restores each node's type, drive, mix, tone, bias, folds, bitDepth, its 10 shapeSlots and the shadow. It then pushes the nodes with setMorphNodes. It never calls mapShapeSlotsToParams, a file-static function in processor_params.cpp:39 that is called only from processParameterChanges (lines 852, 892). Every other DistortionParams field (threshold, curve, sag, satStage, tape model, feedback, delayMs, vowel, fftSize, chaos and granular settings, ...) keeps whatever mn.params held before: defaults on a fresh instance, or the PREVIOUS patch's values on a live instance.
findings.why_wrong: setState has to produce the same DSP state as replaying the parameters, which is the path loadComponentStateWithNotify takes. The shape slots are the persisted source of truth for those fields.
findings.consequence: Loading a host-side preset (DAW preset menu, project undo, copy/paste of plugin settings) onto a running instance restores the node types with the previous patch's per-type parameters, or with defaults. The patch sounds wrong until the user touches a shape knob of each node, which then makes the sound jump. On a fresh project restore this is hidden by the setupProcessing reset finding, but it applies as soon as that is fixed.
findings.suggested_fix: Move mapShapeSlotsToParams into a shared header or a Processor member. In setState, call it for each node after the slots are read: reset mn.params to DistortionParams{} first, re-apply bias/folds/bitDepth, then map the slots. Test: load stream A (Tube with non-default slots) into an active processor and render; load stream B (Tape) and then stream A again; the render must match the first render within a tolerance.
findings.evidence: grep mapShapeSlotsToParams: only processor_params.cpp:39 (definition), :852, :892; processor_state.cpp:871 `bandMorphCache_[b].nodes[...].shapeSlots[s] = slotValue;` followed by :894 `bandProcessors_[b].setMorphNodes(...)` with no slot-to-param mapping.
verifier_notes: Confirmed from source. processor_state.cpp:852-862 restores only mn.type, commonParams (drive/mix/toneHz) and mn.params.bias/folds/bitDepth. Lines 865-874 write the 10 values into nodes[n].shapeSlots[s], and 878-888 fill shapeShadow. Lines 892-898 then call setMorphEnabled, setMorphNodes and setMorphPosition, and the function returns at 919 without touching mn.params again. Grep for mapShapeSlotsToParams over plugins/disrumpo/src finds only the file-static definition at processor_params.cpp:39 and its two callers in processParameterChanges (:852 after a type change, :892 after a shape-slot change). Grep for shapeSlots in src finds nothing in BandProcessor, MorphEngine or morph_node.h that maps slots into params (morph_node.h:43 is just the default initializer). So setMorphNodes is handed nodes whose type-specific DistortionParams fields (curve/knee, threshold/ceiling, sag/satStage, speed/tapeModel/hfRoll/flutter, and so on per processor_params.cpp:41-69 onward) are whatever mn.params held before: defaults on a fresh instance, or the previous patch's values on a live one. The persisted shape slots are not applied until a shape or type parameter change arrives through processParameterChanges. A host project reload or a host preset load that only calls IComponent::setState therefore restores the wrong per-type sound. High severity is justified, because every saved project with non-default shape knobs is affected.

Confirmed from source. processor_state.cpp:852-862 restores mn.type, commonParams (drive/mix/toneHz) and only mn.params.bias/folds/bitDepth. :865-888 restore shapeSlots and shapeShadow. :892-897 call setMorphNodes/setMorphPosition, and nothing re-derives the rest of DistortionParams. The only mapping from slots to params is mapShapeSlotsToParams, a file-static function at processor_params.cpp:39. Its only call sites are processor_params.cpp:852 (type change) and :892 (slot param change), both inside processParameterChanges. That mapping writes many type-specific fields that setState never touches: Tube sag and satStage (:57-58), Tape speed/tapeModel/hfRoll/flutter (:65-68), FeedbackDist feedback/delayMs/filter/limiter (:180-188), Chaos settings (:206-209), and others. I looked for anything that would make up for this and found nothing. (1) setActive (processor.cpp:144-178) only resets DSP state and does not rebuild the params. (2) setupProcessing (processor.cpp:111-127) rebuilds the cache as default MorphNodes, so it throws away the restored slots instead of mapping them. That is the separate reset issue the finding mentions. (3) The host path Controller::setComponentState (controller.cpp:619, comment at :147-148) uses setParamNormalized, not performEdit, so the processor never gets the shape params replayed. Only loadComponentStateWithNotify (:1876, via editParamWithNotify -> performEdit at :1872) replays them, and that is the plugin's own preset browser path, not the host's. (4) In src/dsp, shapeSlots is only declared, in morph_node.h:43. BandProcessor and MorphEngine do not read it, so setMorphNodes cannot derive params from it. (5) No test pins setState-to-params equivalence. The test hits for slots are multi_node_distortion_test.cpp:673 (the type-change shadow path) and distortion_adapter_test.cpp:888-904 (a replica of the mapping), and neither covers setState. Result: when a host loads a preset onto a live instance, the per-type fields keep the previous patch's values, or the defaults on a fresh instance. Nothing in specs or comments says this is intended. High severity is reasonable, because host preset load and undo of project state are common paths.

I could not refute this. The defect is real, and the consequence follows from the code I read.

1. The mapper is never called from setState. `mapShapeSlotsToParams` is defined file-static at processor_params.cpp:39. It is called in only two places, both in processParameterChanges: :852 (type change) and :892 (shape slot change). In setState (processor_state.cpp:852-862), each node gets type, commonParams drive/mix/tone and params.bias/folds/bitDepth. At :871 the 10 shapeSlots are written, and at :883 the shadow. setMorphNodes then runs at :894. Nothing maps the slots to DistortionParams in between.

2. The DSP reads only `params`, never the slots. BandProcessor::setMorphNodes (band_processor.h:247-255) forwards the nodes to MorphEngine::setNodes. MorphEngine pushes `nodes_[i].params` into the adapters (morph_engine.cpp:65, :138) and interpolates from `.params` (:419, :531, :734). A grep for shapeSlots in src/ finds only morph_node.h:43 (the default) and the processor files, so the slots are inert DSP-side until processParameterChanges maps them. The per-type fields (curve/knee, threshold/ceiling, sag/satStage, tape model/speed/hfRoll/flutter, feedback/delayMs, vowel, chaos/granular settings, and so on; mapping table processor_params.cpp:41-229) therefore keep whatever `mn.params` held before. On a running instance that is the previous patch's values. After the setupProcessing reset (processor.cpp:112-127) or on a fresh instance it is the defaults.

3. Nothing else replays the parameters on the host path. Only the plugin's own preset browser goes through loadComponentStateWithNotify, which calls performEdit (controller.cpp:120-124). That sends the slots through processParameterChanges, so they get mapped. A host-driven restore runs Processor::setState plus Controller::setComponentState with setParamNormalized and no performEdit (controller.cpp:147-148). So the processor's per-type params never get re-derived. The cases are a DAW preset menu, project recall, undo, or copy/paste of plugin state.

4. Impact. The editor shows the restored slot values, but the audio uses stale or default per-type settings. This can change the timbre a lot, for example the feedback amount and delay time, the tape model, the tube stage, or the formant vowel. The values only re-sync when the user moves a shape knob or changes the type, and then the sound jumps. Any node whose type is not SoftClip with default slots is affected, so in practice almost every patch (which factory presets are affected was not checked). It goes unnoticed in the plugin's own browser, which is probably why no test caught it. High severity is appropriate for a state-restore path giving the wrong sound in every host.
corroborated_by_measurement: probe preset levels: silent/near-silent: "Drums/Rectified_Drums -62.22 (bad, < -60)". Generator: tools/disrumpo_preset_generator.cpp:2630-2631 `setBandType(p.state.bandMorph[1], DistortionType::HalfRectify, 2.0f, 4500.0f); shapeHalfRect(..., 0.3f, 0.15f, true);`. The processor_params.cpp:124 slot map is `p.threshold = slots[0];`, but grep finds mapShapeSlotsToParams only at processor_params.cpp:852 and :892, never in processor_state.cpp. distortion_adapter.cpp:441 `float result = (input >= thresh) ? input : 0.0f;`

findings.title: Preset-browser load turns factory-preset crossover Hz into a linear normalized value that the processor decodes on a log scale, collapsing all crossovers below about 160 Hz
findings.problem: parseComponentState converts the stream's crossover Hz with param->toNormalized(freq). The parameter is a linear RangeParameter 20..20000 (parameter_registration.cpp:151-160). loadComponentStateWithNotify passes that value to the processor through performEdit (controller.cpp:1868-1873, 1887-1889). The processor decodes crossover values as log10 (processor_params.cpp:988-991). Processor getState and the factory presets store real Hz (processor_state.cpp:75-77).
findings.why_wrong: The load path must use the same normalization the processor decodes, which is log10. Session restore gives the processor Hz directly and is correct, so the two load paths disagree.

The divider UI, which is log-mapped, also shows the wrong positions after a host session restore. No test covers browser loads of crossover values (grep Crossover in tests/integration/preset gives one comment).

findings.title: User-preset writer encodes the active node count as round(norm*2)+2, so saved presets change 1->2 and 2->3 nodes
findings.problem: createComponentStateStream converts the kBandActiveNodes norm with round(norm*2)+2. The parameter is a 4-entry list (1..4, norm = (count-1)/3), as the parser and the processor assume (controller.cpp:526; processor_params.cpp:951-952).
findings.why_wrong: The preset writer must invert the parser: count = round(norm*3)+1, which matches what processor getState writes (cache.activeNodeCount, processor_state.cpp:321).
findings.consequence: Every user preset saved from the browser changes node counts on reload. 1 node (the default) becomes 2, 2 nodes become 3 (norm 1/3 -> round(0.67)+2), 3 nodes become 3 (norm 2/3 -> round(1.33)+2), and 4 nodes stay 4. A single-node patch reloads as a two-node morph between A and B, which sounds different.
findings.suggested_fix: Write static_cast<int>(std::round(activeNodesNorm * 3.0f)) + 1. Test: for counts 1..4, set the param, call createComponentStateStream, run parseComponentState on a fresh controller, and assert the count matches.
findings.evidence: controller.cpp:1830-1831 `float activeNodesNorm = getParamNorm(makeBandParamId(band, BandParamType::kBandActiveNodes)); int activeNodes = static_cast<int>(std::round(activeNodesNorm * 2.0f)) + 2;` vs controller.cpp:526 `setter(..., static_cast<double>(count - 1) / 3.0);`
verifier_notes: I traced the code and the defect is real. The parameter is a 4-entry StringListParameter with the strings "1","2","3","4" and default norm 0.0 (parameter_registration.cpp:699-706). The processor turns the norm into a count with idx = int(value*3+0.5), count = idx+1 (processor_params.cpp:951-952). The controller parser reads a raw count and stores norm (count-1)/3 (controller.cpp:525-526). kMinActiveNodes and kDefaultActiveNodes are both 1 (morph_node.h:132,135). The controller writer instead does activeNodes = round(norm*2)+2 (controller.cpp:1830-1832). That maps norm 0 to 2, norm 1/3 to round(0.667)+2 = 3, norm 2/3 to round(1.333)+2 = 3, and norm 1 to 4. So a count of 1 is saved as 2 and a count of 2 is saved as 3; 3 and 4 survive. This writer is the path that saves user presets: initialize() calls presetManager_->setStateProvider(... createComponentStateStream()) (controller.cpp:116-118), and loading goes through loadComponentStateWithNotify, which uses the parser at :524-526. On reload the parser clamps the written value to [1,4] and stores it as is, so a default one-node band comes back as a two-node morph. No test catches this: serialization_round_trip_test.cpp only writes kDefaultActiveNodes by hand (lines 796, 1267) and never calls createComponentStateStream. The old comment in plugin_ids.h:185 still says "[2, 3, 4]", which suggests the writer was left behind when the list grew to 1-4 entries. Severity high is fair, because the default patch changes on every save and load through the preset browser.

findings.title: User-preset writer scales the routing source by 12 instead of 13, so sources 7..13 are saved one slot lower
findings.problem: The routing source param is a 14-entry list (kUIModSourceCount = 14, plugin_ids.h:546). The processor and the parser both use a denominator of 13 (processor_params.cpp:555; controller.cpp:468-469). The preset writer instead uses getInt8FromList(makeRoutingParamId(r,0), 12), i.e. round(k/13*12).
findings.why_wrong: The encoder has to use the same (count-1) = 13 scale as the decoder.
findings.consequence: Indices 0..6 survive. Index 7 (Macro3) saves as 6 (Macro2), and indices 8..13 (Macro4, Chaos, Rungler, S&H, Pitch, Transient) each save one lower. Every user preset that routes one of those sources reloads modulated by the wrong source.
findings.suggested_fix: Use kUIModSourceCount - 1. Better, share one encode/decode helper between parse and write. Test: for every source index, set routing 0's source, call createComponentStateStream, parse the stream, and compare.
findings.evidence: controller.cpp:1815 `streamer.writeInt8(getInt8FromList(makeRoutingParamId(r, 0), 12));`; getInt8FromList = `std::round(param->getNormalized() * maxVal)` (:1700); parse :468-469 `/ static_cast<double>(kUIModSourceCount - 1)`.

2. The writer uses the wrong scale. controller.cpp:1815 calls `getInt8FromList(makeRoutingParamId(r, 0), 12)`, and getInt8FromList at :1699-1700 is `std::round(param->getNormalized() * maxVal)`. That gives round(k*12/13):
   - k=0..6 come out unchanged (6 -> 5.54 -> 6).
   - k=7 -> 6.46 -> 6, so Macro3 is saved as Macro2.
   - k=8 -> 7.38 -> 7, through k=13 -> 12. Every index from 7 to 13 drops by one.

3. Both readers treat the int8 as a raw index:
   - The controller parse at :465-469 clamps it to 0..13 and divides by (kUIModSourceCount - 1) = 13.
   - The processor setState at processor_state.cpp:767-770 casts it straight to Krate::DSP::ModSource. In modulation_types.h:36-50 the enum order is None=0 ... Macro3=7, Macro4=8, Chaos=9, Rungler=10, SampleHold=11, PitchFollower=12, Transient=13, the same order as the UI list.

4. This is the user-preset save path. controller.cpp:116-118 registers createComponentStateStream as the PresetManager state provider, and the load provider at :120-124 sends the stream back through loadComponentStateWithNotify.

So any user preset saved with a route source of Macro3 or higher reloads with the source one slot lower (Transient becomes Pitch, Chaos becomes Macro4, and so on). Every number above comes from the cited lines. I see no reason to change the high severity: the bug silently corrupts saved user presets.

findings.title: setState applies crossover frequencies before setBandCount, so the live band count drops or overwrites the saved values
findings.problem: setCrossoverFrequency(c, f) is called for each saved crossover before crossoverL_/R_.setBandCount(bandCount). CrossoverNetwork::setCrossoverFrequency returns early when index >= numBands_-1, using the network's CURRENT band count (crossover_network.h:127-130). setBandCount then redistributes: from 1 band it runs a fresh log distribution (crossover_network.h:280-284), and when increasing it inserts log midpoints (:287-290).
findings.why_wrong: The band count has to be applied first, or the frequencies stored unconditionally, so the saved values are applied whatever the instance's state was before.
findings.consequence: If a running instance is at 1 band and the user loads a host preset or undoes to a 4-band state, all three saved crossovers are discarded and replaced by 112/632/3556 Hz. From 2 bands, only crossover 1 survives and the other two are made up. The controller shows the saved Hz.
findings.suggested_fix: Call setBandCount(bandCount) before the crossover loop. Better, have setCrossoverFrequency always store crossoverFrequencies_[index] and apply it when the band becomes active. Test: on a prepared processor, set kBandCountId to 1 band, setState a 4-band stream with custom crossovers, then assert getCrossoverFrequency(0..2).
findings.evidence: processor_state.cpp:455-456 `crossoverL_.setCrossoverFrequency(c, freq); crossoverR_.setCrossoverFrequency(c, freq);` then :462 `crossoverL_.setBandCount(bandCount);`; crossover_network.h:128 `if (index < 0 || index >= numBands_ - 1) { return; }`.
verifier_notes:
I traced the code and the defect holds. processor_state.cpp:450-459 calls crossoverL_/R_.setCrossoverFrequency(c, freq) for each saved crossover, and only afterwards, at :462-463, calls setBandCount(bandCount). Before that point only the atomic bandCount_ has been updated (:413); the networks' numBands_ still holds the live value. crossover_network.h:127-130 returns early when index >= numBands_ - 1, without writing crossoverFrequencies_[index]. So with a live band count of 1, none of the three saved values is stored.

setBandCount (crossover_network.h:111-122) then calls redistributeCrossovers. From 1 band, :280-284 runs initializeLogarithmicDistribution (:253-268). With 4 bands that gives 20*10^(0.75k) = about 112/632/3556 Hz, which matches the finding. From 2 bands only index 0 was stored, and redistributeIncreasing (:301-365) makes up the other two at log midpoints. Decreasing the band count (4 to 2) works, because all indices pass the guard.

Nothing else restores the saved values. The per-block process() reads only bandCount_ (processor.cpp:257). The crossover parameter path (processor_params.cpp:984-994) uses the same guarded setter, and runs only if the host sends parameter changes. getState (processor_state.cpp:76) reads back the wrong, made-up values, so the loss also persists into the next save. No processor-level test covers this: getCrossoverFrequency appears only in tests/unit/crossover_network_test.cpp.

There is a related problem the finding does not cover. setupProcessing calls crossoverL_.prepare(sampleRate_, numBands) (processor.cpp:100-102), and prepare unconditionally re-runs initializeLogarithmicDistribution (crossover_network.h:89-90). So if setState runs before setupProcessing (the common case on project load), the restored crossovers are overwritten whatever the call order. The suggested fix (reorder, or store unconditionally) does not cover that path; prepare would also have to keep the stored frequencies. Severity stays medium: this is not real-time unsafe, but a preset loaded while the instance runs at a lower band count loses its crossovers and the processor disagrees with the controller.

I could not refute this, and the context does not cover it. processor_state.cpp:450-459 calls crossoverL_/R_.setCrossoverFrequency(c, freq) for each saved crossover first, and only then calls setBandCount(bandCount) at :462-463. CrossoverNetwork::setCrossoverFrequency (crossover_network.h:127-130) returns early when index >= numBands_ - 1, and numBands_ is still the live band count at that point. So it never stores crossoverFrequencies_[index] for crossovers that the live band count does not use.

setBandCount (:111-122) calls redistributeCrossovers. If the old count was 1 or less, it calls initializeLogarithmicDistribution() (:280-284) and replaces all crossovers with the log split. When the count goes up, redistributeIncreasing (:301-365) keeps only the old count's crossovers and fills the rest with log midpoints.

Nothing else re-applies the saved values. Grep shows the only writers are processor_params.cpp:344-345 and :992-993, which respond only to parameter changes, and processor.cpp:101-102 prepare(), which also resets to the log split. The processor's crossoverFrequencies_ atomic (processor.h:179) is never used. Under VST3, the controller's setComponentState/setParamNormalized does not send changes back to the processor, so the saved Hz values are lost on the audio side while the controller shows them.

It is partly masked: kDefaultBands = 4 (band_state.h:62, crossover_network.h:48), so a fresh instance at 4 bands loads any saved state correctly. Lowering the band count also keeps the right values. The failure needs an instance that is running at fewer bands than the saved state, for example a host preset load or undo after the user lowered the band count. That is a normal action in a real host. No comment or spec describes this as intended.

I confirmed the defect from source. The impact holds as claimed, at medium severity.

1. processor_state.cpp:413 stores bandCount_. The loop at :450-457 then calls crossoverL_/R_.setCrossoverFrequency(c, freq), and only after that do :462-463 call setBandCount(bandCount).

2. In crossover_network.h:127-130, setCrossoverFrequency returns early when index >= numBands_ - 1. numBands_ is the network's live count, so any saved crossover above the current count is dropped without a trace.

3. setBandCount (:111-122) then calls redistributeCrossovers. Coming from 1 band, :280-284 runs initializeLogarithmicDistribution (:253-268), which for 4 bands gives 10^(1.301 + 0.75k) = 112 / 632 / 3556 Hz. Coming from 2 or 3 bands, redistributeIncreasing (:301-365) keeps the surviving crossovers and inserts made-up log midpoints for the rest.

4. Nothing repairs this afterwards. The processor's crossoverFrequencies_ atomics (processor.h:179) are never used for this. setupProcessing (processor.cpp:101-102) only re-prepares to a log distribution. The only other writer is the param path (processor_params.cpp:992-993), and hosts do not echo the controller's restored params back to the processor.

5. The wrong values also persist. getState (processor_state.cpp:76) reads crossoverL_.getCrossoverFrequency(c), so re-saving the project writes the made-up frequencies into it.

6. There is no test for this. getCrossoverFrequency appears only in tests/unit/crossover_network_test.cpp; no processor-level setState round-trip checks the crossovers.

Trigger and size of the effect:
- It only fires when the running instance has fewer bands than the incoming state. A fresh instance defaults to 4 bands (band_state.h:62), so a first project load is not affected.
- A later host preset load or undo from a 1-3 band setting to a 3- or 4-band state is affected. That is a common workflow.
- The band split points move by large amounts (for example a saved 150 Hz becomes 112 Hz and a saved 1500 Hz becomes 632 Hz). Each band's distortion type then acts on a different part of the spectrum.
- The UI shows the saved Hz, which does not match what the audio is doing.
- There is no crash, NaN or real-time safety violation, so medium is right; no upgrade or downgrade.

A separate issue for the report: prepare() in setupProcessing (processor.cpp:101) also overwrites restored crossovers if a host calls setState before setupProcessing.

findings.title: Inserting ModSource::Rungler renumbered S&H/Pitch/Transient without a Disrumpo state migration
findings.problem: setState casts the stored source byte straight to Krate::DSP::ModSource. Commit 05a3ddb7 (2026-02-16) inserted Rungler = 10 and renumbered SampleHold 10->11, PitchFollower 11->12 and Transient 12->13 (modulation_types.h:47-50). Disrumpo stayed at kPresetVersion 9 until 2026-03-19 (342d04fd / f536a153). Released v0.9.0 (2026-02-02) and v0.9.1 (2026-02-03) wrote v9 streams with SampleHold=10, PitchFollower=11, Transient=12 (verified in git show disrumpo/v0.9.1). The controller parser (controller.cpp:466-469) also has no remap.
findings.why_wrong: Changing an enum that is persisted needs a version gate and a migration. Ruinae bumped its state version in the same commit; Disrumpo did not, so v9 streams are now ambiguous.
findings.consequence: Projects saved with Disrumpo 0.9.0/0.9.1 that route S&H, Pitch Follower or Transient now load as Rungler, S&H and Pitch Follower. The modulation behaves differently, and nothing tells the user.
findings.suggested_fix: Decide how to tell the streams apart: no v9 streams from Feb 16 to Mar 19 can be distinguished by version, so use release history or the presence of trailer fields. At minimum, remap 10/11/12 -> 11/12/13 for version <= 8, and record the v9 ambiguity in plugin_ids.h version history. Test: a v9 stream fixture captured from v0.9.1 with an S&H routing must load as ModSource::SampleHold. STATE-COMPAT.
findings.evidence: processor_state.cpp:769-770 `routing.source = static_cast<Krate::DSP::ModSource>(std::clamp(static_cast<int>(source), 0, ...kModSourceCount - 1));`; git show disrumpo/v0.9.1:dsp/.../modulation_types.h:47-49 `SampleHold = 10, PitchFollower = 11, Transient = 12`; v0.9.1 plugin_ids.h:622 `kPresetVersion = 9`; current modulation_types.h:47-50 `Rungler = 10, SampleHold = 11, PitchFollower = 12, Transient = 13`.
verifier_notes: I traced the code and the claim holds. Current processor_state.cpp:765-770 reads the routing source byte and casts it straight to Krate::DSP::ModSource. The only clamp is to [0, kModSourceCount-1]. There is no version-gated remap: grep finds no Rungler/remap logic near the routing read, and the only routing migration is the dest one at line 779 (`version <= 11 && dest >= kBandBaseI`). The current enum at dsp/include/krate/dsp/core/modulation_types.h has Rungler=10, SampleHold=11, PitchFollower=12, Transient=13. `git log -S'Rungler = 10'` shows this came in with 05a3ddb7 on 2026-02-16 (Macros rungler #175). `git show disrumpo/v0.9.1:dsp/include/krate/dsp/core/modulation_types.h` has SampleHold=10, PitchFollower=11, Transient=12 and kModSourceCount=13. The tag exists on origin (ls-remote 0fea2815). In v0.9.1, processor.cpp:1011 writes `writeInt8(static_cast<int8>(routing.source))`, the raw enum byte. Its setState (1443) clamps to 0..12, and the routing source param maps `value*12+0.5` (1823), so all 13 sources, S&H/Pitch/Transient included, could be routed and saved. v0.9.1 plugin_ids.h:622 has kPresetVersion=9. So did disrumpo/v0.9.4 (2026-03-15), which was built after the enum change. Version 9 streams therefore exist under both numberings and cannot be told apart by version. Current kPresetVersion is 12 (plugin_ids.h:690). The controller's setComponentState parser (controller.cpp:464-469) also maps the raw byte into the routing source param with no remap. As a result, a v0.9.0/v0.9.1 stream byte 10 (S&H) loads as Rungler, 11 (Pitch) as SampleHold, and 12 (Transient) as PitchFollower. This is the silent behaviour change the finding describes. Medium severity fits: it only hits old projects that used those three sources, but it changes the sound without any warning.

The defect is confirmed. I found no guard, migration or design note that covers it.

(1) Current load path. processor_state.cpp:765-770 reads the routing source byte and casts it straight to Krate::DSP::ModSource after a clamp to [0, kModSourceCount-1]. The only routing migration in this block is the v<=11 destination remap (kParamsPerBand 6->8). Nothing remaps source values. The controller parser at controller.cpp:466-469 also maps the raw byte straight to normalized `source/(kUIModSourceCount-1)`, with kUIModSourceCount=14 (plugin_ids.h:546), and has no remap either.

(2) The enum change. Current modulation_types.h:47-50 has Rungler=10, SampleHold=11, PitchFollower=12, Transient=13. `git show disrumpo/v0.9.1:dsp/include/krate/dsp/core/modulation_types.h` shows SampleHold=10, PitchFollower=11, Transient=12, with kModSourceCount=13.

(3) Disrumpo got no migration. Commit 05a3ddb7 (2026-02-16) says in its own message that it added a "ModSource enum migration for v<13 presets: increment source values >=10 by 1". That migration covers only Ruinae, whose state version went to 13. In Disrumpo the commit only changed hardcoded counts to kModSourceCount (controller.cpp and processor.cpp, a few lines each).

(4) Released streams can carry the old numbers. Both v0.9.0 and v0.9.1 exist on origin (`git ls-remote`). At v0.9.1:
- plugin_ids.h:622 has kPresetVersion = 9.
- The routing source StringListParameter (controller.cpp ~2023-2037) offers "S&H", "Pitch" and "Transient" at indices 10-12, so users could pick them.
- processor.cpp:1011 writes routing.source as a raw int8.

(5) The version number cannot tell the streams apart. disrumpo/v0.9.4 (2026-03-15) still has kPresetVersion = 9 but already uses the new enum (Rungler=10, SampleHold=11). Version 9 streams therefore exist with both numberings. The version history in plugin_ids.h (v9 -> v12) does not mention the source renumbering, and CHANGELOG.md mentions only the destination remap.

(6) No test pins this. Grepping plugins/disrumpo/tests for SampleHold or Rungler finds only an unrelated LFO waveform test.

Result: a project saved with Disrumpo 0.9.0 or 0.9.1 that routes S&H, Pitch or Transient now loads as Rungler, S&H or Pitch. Medium severity fits: the error is silent and changes the sound, but it only hits user projects from two early releases that used those three sources.

Confirmed from source and git history. Current loader: processor_state.cpp:765-770 reads the stored int8 source and casts it straight to Krate::DSP::ModSource, clamped to kModSourceCount-1. No version-gated remap exists. The only routing migration is the v<=11 dest re-index at :779-787, and the only Rungler gate is the v>=11 Rungler param block at :728. Released tags, checked against origin with git ls-remote: disrumpo/v0.9.0 (2026-02-02) and v0.9.1 (2026-02-03) both have kPresetVersion = 9 (plugin_ids.h:621/622) and modulation_types.h:47-49 SampleHold=10, PitchFollower=11, Transient=12. The v0.9.1 getState (processor.cpp:1009-1017) wrote writeInt8(static_cast<int8>(routing.source)) as the raw enum. The v0.9.1 controller (controller.cpp:2021-2038) offered 'S&H', 'Pitch' and 'Transient' at indices 10/11/12 in the Route Source list, so users could save those values. Commit 05a3ddb7 (2026-02-16) inserted Rungler=10 and renumbered the rest. The released disrumpo/v0.9.4 (2026-03-15) and v0.9.5 (2026-03-17) still had kPresetVersion = 9 with the new numbering (Rungler=10..Transient=13), so v9 streams from two released lineages are ambiguous by version alone. The bump to v10+ came only on 2026-03-19 (f536a153/342d04fd). Impact: a v0.9.0/0.9.1 project with an S&H routing now loads as Rungler, which is a different chaotic modulation shape. Pitch loads as S&H and Transient loads as Pitch Follower. Nothing warns the user. The scope is user projects saved during the roughly two weeks of the pre-1.0 0.9.0/0.9.1 releases, and only routings that use those three sources. A wrong modulation source on reload, with no crash, NaN or loud output, fits medium. Severity stays as claimed.

findings.title: setState adopts the stored instance ID, so duplicated instances collide in the SharedDisplayBridge registry and a controller can hold a dangling pointer
findings.problem: When the trailer is present, setState unregisters the processor's own random ID, sets instanceId_ to the stored ID and registers &sharedDisplay_ under it. registerInstance is a plain map assignment that overwrites any existing entry (shared_display_bridge.cpp:15-19), and unregisterInstance erases by ID (:21-25). Two live processors can end up with the same stored ID, for example after duplicating a track, copying plugin settings, or a project saved after that. In that case the second overwrites the first's entry, and terminate() of either erases the entry for both. The controller looks up the processor by the stored ID in setComponentState and keeps the raw pointer (controller.cpp:644-646).
findings.why_wrong: The registry key has to be unique per live processor. A restored ID is only usable when no other live instance holds it. Otherwise the processor should keep its fresh ID, and the controller should learn it through the connection, not from the shared stream.
findings.consequence: On hosts that need the Tier-3 fallback, instance A's editor can show instance B's spectrum. If B is then deleted, A's controller holds sharedDisplay_ pointing into B's freed processor. The 33 ms timer passes those FIFOs to the SpectrumDisplay (controller.cpp:1476-1486), a use-after-free. Innexus uses the same adopt-ID pattern (plugins/innexus/src/processor/processor_state.cpp), so this is CROSS-PLUGIN.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not adopt the stored ID when lookupInstance(storedId) returns another live entry. Better, stop deriving the controller's lookup key from the component state and send the live ID to the controller with an IMessage after connect. Make unregisterInstance(id, data) erase only when the entry's pointer matches. Test: two processors setState the same stream, then terminate one; lookupInstance must still return the survivor's display and never the terminated one's.
findings.evidence: processor_state.cpp:911-914 `SharedDisplayBridge::instance().unregisterInstance(instanceId_); instanceId_ = static_cast<uint64_t>(storedId); SharedDisplayBridge::instance().registerInstance(instanceId_, &sharedDisplay_);`; shared_display_bridge.cpp:18 `registry_[id] = data;`; processor.cpp:81 terminate `unregisterInstance(instanceId_);`; controller.cpp:645 `sharedDisplay_ = static_cast<SharedDisplay*>(...lookupInstance(instanceId_));`.
verifier_notes:
The mechanism holds when I trace it through the source. processor_state.cpp:907-915 reads the trailer, calls unregisterInstance(instanceId_), assigns instanceId_ = storedId and calls registerInstance(instanceId_, &sharedDisplay_). getState writes the live ID at processor_state.cpp:356, so a copied state (duplicated track or saved project) gives two live processors the same key. shared_display_bridge.cpp:18 is a plain `registry_[id] = data;` overwrite, and :24 `registry_.erase(id)` erases by key with no pointer check. terminate at processor.cpp:81 therefore removes the entry for whichever instance is registered under that ID. controller.cpp:641-646 derives the key from the component stream, then caches the raw pointer from lookupInstance in sharedDisplay_. That pointer is only cleared at controller terminate/willClose (controller.cpp:1581).

Where the defect bites depends on host call order. If a host calls procA.setState, procB.setState, then ctrlA.setComponentState, A's controller caches B's SharedDisplay. The Tier-3 timer (controller.cpp:1476-1486) then wires the spectrum display to B's FIFOs and dereferences sharedDisplay_->sampleRate. Tier 3 activates whenever no DataExchange block arrives within ~330 ms of didOpen (dataExchangeActive_ is set only in the message path at :1942). That happens in real hosts when process() is not being called, for example with the transport stopped. After B is deleted, both the cached pointer and the FIFOs handed to the SpectrumDisplay point into freed memory. With the common per-instance order (setState then setComponentState for each instance) the controller gets its own processor, so there is no UAF, but the registry entry is still clobbered or erased by the other instance.

No test or guard in the code checks for a duplicate ID before adopting it. The defect is real, but the UAF needs a particular host ordering plus the Tier-3 path, so medium severity is appropriate as stated.

The code matches the claim, and nothing in it guards against a collision. processor_state.cpp:903-917 unregisters the processor's own random ID (made at processor.cpp:42-44), adopts the stored int64, and calls registerInstance(storedId, &sharedDisplay_). shared_display_bridge.cpp:18 is a plain `registry_[id] = data;` that overwrites any existing entry. :24 is `registry_.erase(id)` with no check of who owns the entry. processor.cpp:81 terminate() erases by that shared ID. controller.cpp:641-646 reads the same trailer and keeps the raw pointer that lookupInstance returns. controller.cpp:1476-1486 later passes sharedDisplay_->inputFIFO/outputFIFO to spectrumDisplay_. That fallback does not need a host without IConnectionPoint. It fires whenever dataExchangeActive_ is still false after about 330 ms, and dataExchangeActive_ is only set at controller.cpp:1942 when a block arrives.

Nothing marks this as intentional. The only comment is "Re-register with the stored ID (supports state restore)". The header (shared_display_bridge.h:29) says the ID should be a "Unique instance identifier (random uint64)", and the adopt step breaks that once two instances restore the same stream. No Disrumpo test touches SharedDisplayBridge or instanceId: a grep of plugins/disrumpo/tests found nothing.

The 121 factory .vstpreset files do not carry the "KRAT" trailer (I grepped them for the little-endian bytes and found 0 of 121), so factory presets cannot cause a collision. Duplicated tracks, copied settings, and user presets saved through the host's getState do carry the ID (processor_state.cpp:355-356). So two live processors sharing one ID is reachable.

A wrong pointer or a use-after-free needs one more condition: another instance's processor setState must run between this instance's processor setState and its controller setComponentState. A project reload where the host restores all component states before the controllers would do it. That depends on the host, but nothing in the code prevents it. Separately, terminate() of either duplicate always deletes the survivor's registry entry. I am keeping the severity at medium: the defect is real and unguarded, but the use-after-free needs a specific host call order.

The mechanism is real. processor_state.cpp:911-914 unregisters the random ID, adopts the stored ID and re-registers it. shared_display_bridge.cpp:18 (`registry_[id] = data;`) overwrites the entry, and :24 (`registry_.erase(id)`) erases by ID only, with no check on the owner pointer. terminate (processor.cpp:81) erases by the adopted ID. Controller setComponentState (controller.cpp:644-646) caches the raw pointer it looks up. Two live instances can end up sharing one ID. Duplicating a track does it, and so does loading the same user or host-saved preset into two instances, because getState writes the ID trailer at processor_state.cpp:354-356. The factory generator does not write it.

The claimed consequence needs several conditions at once, so I recommend a downgrade:
(1) The pointer is only used by the Tier-3 path (controller.cpp:1476). That path engages only when no DataExchange block has arrived within about 330 ms of opening the editor (cleared at 1942-1943). Once engaged it stays on for that editor session, because spectrumDataAvailable_ is already true at 1944. So it is mostly a no-connection host, or an editor opened while the processor is idle.
(2) The common orderings do not produce a wrong lookup. On a per-instance sequential load (processor setState, then that controller's setComponentState) or on a duplication, each controller looks up the ID right after its own processor re-registered, so it caches its own SharedDisplay. Deleting either instance later erases the shared key but leaves the other controller's cached pointer valid, so the result is only a lost fallback, not a use-after-free. Crosstalk or a dangling pointer needs controller X's setComponentState to run after processor Y re-registered the same ID: an interleaved or batched load order, or a controller-only state push.
(3) willClose clears sharedDisplay_ at controller.cpp:1581, which limits the dangling window. The pointer only dangles if Y is destroyed between X's lookup and X's next editor close, and X's editor then opens or is open without DataExchange data.

Under those conditions the use-after-free is real: the timer reads sharedDisplay_->sampleRate and wires freed FIFOs into the SpectrumDisplay (1482-1484). The cross-plugin claim also holds: Innexus has the same pattern at innexus processor_state.cpp:708-717 and controller_state.cpp:528-537. Given how narrow the trigger is (a rare host or idle path, a shared ID and an interleaved load order), low fits better than medium.

findings.title: Closing the editor permanently disables the mod-slider overlay and the Tier-3 spectrum fallback until the host re-activates or reloads state
findings.problem: willClose sets cachedModOffsets_ = nullptr and sharedDisplay_ = nullptr. cachedModOffsets_ is set only when a 'ModOffsets' message arrives, and the processor sends it only from setActive(true) (processor.cpp:170). notify() also discards messages while editorClosing_ is true (controller.cpp:1962-1963). sharedDisplay_ is set only in setComponentState (controller.cpp:644-646). didOpen restores neither of them (controller.cpp:1354-1512).
findings.why_wrong: State that the editor needs has to be re-acquired on each didOpen, or kept for the life of the controller. Here it is cleared on every close but only obtained from one-time lifecycle events.
findings.consequence: After the user closes and reopens the editor in the same session, the modulation-amount overlay on the band sliders stops updating (the timer condition `if (cachedModOffsets_ && activeEditor_)` at :1470 is false). On hosts that rely on the SharedDisplayBridge fallback, the spectrum analyser stays blank after reopening (the condition at :1476 needs sharedDisplay_).
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the pointers across close and reopen and null them only in terminate or disconnect, or have didOpen request them again (for example, a 'RequestModOffsets' message the processor answers). Test: a controller test that delivers ModOffsets, then runs didOpen -> willClose -> didOpen and asserts that cachedModOffsets_ is non-null and the timer pushes offsets.
findings.evidence: controller.cpp:1518 `cachedModOffsets_ = nullptr;`; :1581 `sharedDisplay_ = nullptr;`; :1962-1963 `if (editorClosing_.load(...)) return EditControllerEx1::notify(message);`; processor.cpp:170 `sendModOffsetsMessage();` (only call site, inside setActive(true)); :1470 `if (cachedModOffsets_ && activeEditor_)`.
verifier_notes:
I traced the code and the defect is real. I could not refute it.

(1) cachedModOffsets_ is written in exactly one place: notify() on a "ModOffsets" message (controller.cpp:1966-1973). That message is built only in Processor::sendModOffsetsMessage (processor_messaging.cpp:149-165), and the only call to it is inside setActive(true) (processor.cpp:170).

(2) willClose sets cachedModOffsets_ = nullptr (controller.cpp:1518). It also leaves editorClosing_ = true (controller.cpp:1517) until the next didOpen. While that flag is set, notify() returns early (controller.cpp:1962-1963), so a ModOffsets message that arrives while the editor is closed is dropped as well.

(3) didOpen (controller.cpp:1354-1512) clears editorClosing_ and starts the timer. Nothing there requests or restores cachedModOffsets_. The timer guard `if (cachedModOffsets_ && activeEditor_)` (controller.cpp:1470) therefore stays false, and updateModSliders never runs after a reopen. ModSlider views do exist in editor.uidesc (5 occurrences). Clearing the pointer is not needed for safety either: it points into the processor's ModulationEngine array, which outlives the editor.

(4) sharedDisplay_ is written only in setComponentState (controller.cpp:645-646). willClose nulls it (controller.cpp:1581), and didOpen never looks it up again. On reopen the Tier-3 condition `!dataExchangeActive_ && sharedDisplay_ && ...` (controller.cpp:1476) is permanently false, because willClose also resets dataExchangeActive_ (controller.cpp:1582). The spectrum only stays blank on hosts that need the fallback. When DataExchange works, it reconnects the spectrum through onDataExchangeBlocksReceived (controller.cpp:1944-1949), so that part of the impact is limited to fallback hosts, as the finding says.

Both symptoms clear only when the host calls setActive(true) or setComponentState again. Medium severity fits: these are UI display features and audio is not affected.

I could not refute this. The defect is real and nothing upstream protects against it.
(1) controller.cpp:1518 `cachedModOffsets_ = nullptr;` and :1581 `sharedDisplay_ = nullptr;` run in willClose on every close.
(2) cachedModOffsets_ has exactly one assigner, notify() at controller.cpp:1966-1972, when a "ModOffsets" message arrives. The processor's only send site is processor.cpp:170 `sendModOffsetsMessage();`, inside the setActive(state=true) branch (processor.cpp:166-171). Opening or closing the editor does not trigger setActive.
(3) sharedDisplay_ has exactly one assigner, setComponentState at controller.cpp:637-651, which looks up SharedDisplayBridge using instanceId_. instanceId_ is still held after willClose, but didOpen never repeats the lookup.
(4) didOpen (controller.cpp:1354-1512) resets editorClosing_, spectrumDataAvailable_ and activeEditor_, then creates a new timer. That timer needs `cachedModOffsets_ && activeEditor_` (:1470) to call updateModSliders, and `!dataExchangeActive_ && sharedDisplay_ && !spectrumDataAvailable_` (:1476) to start the Tier-3 fallback. Neither pointer is ever restored, so after a close and reopen in the same session both branches stay dead until the host calls setActive(true) or setComponentState again.
(5) Clearing these pointers is not needed for safety. The comment at :1515-1516 says the goal is to stop races with timers and callbacks, but the timer is already stopped at :1519. The mod-offsets array belongs to the processor's modulationEngine_ and lives for the whole processor lifetime, not the editor's.
(6) No spec note or test justifies the reset. A grep over plugins/*controller*.cpp finds no other site that re-acquires either pointer. Innexus shows the same sharedDisplay_ pattern (controller.cpp:1183 nulls it, and it is set only in controller_state.cpp:536), which suggests the pattern was copied, not designed.
Severity stays medium: the effect is UI-only (no audio impact), but the mod overlay on the main editor visibly stops updating after any close and reopen.

The source confirms the defect. controller.cpp:1518 sets `cachedModOffsets_ = nullptr` in willClose, and nothing in didOpen (1354-1512) sets it again. The only place it is written is notify() at :1966-1973, which handles the "ModOffsets" message. The processor sends that message from exactly one place: processor.cpp:170, inside setActive(true), via sendModOffsetsMessage (processor_messaging.cpp:149-162). There is no request-reply path. It gets worse after the first close: editorClosing_ stays true from willClose (:1517) until the next didOpen (:1355), and notify() at :1962-1963 hands every message to the base class during that time. So a setActive(true) that happens while the editor is closed, for example after a sample-rate change, loses its ModOffsets message too. Recovery only happens if the host re-activates the processor while the editor is open. Result: after the first close and reopen, the timer check at :1470 `if (cachedModOffsets_ && activeEditor_)` is false. updateModSliders (:1979) never runs, and the newly created ModSlider views keep their default zero offset. The modulation overlay disappears in every host and every session after the first editor close, which is a very common user action. The audio path is not affected, because the ModulationEngine still applies the offsets in the processor. The spectrum part is real but narrow. sharedDisplay_ is nulled at :1581 and only set again in setComponentState (:645-646), so the Tier-3 fallback at :1476 is dead after a reopen. But Tier 3 only matters when neither the DataExchange API nor its IMessage fallback delivers data. In those cases dataExchangeActive_ is set again by onDataExchangeBlocksReceived (:1940-1948) after didOpen, so the spectrum works in mainstream hosts. Only hosts that depend on the SharedDisplayBridge lose the analyser. A host-triggered setComponentState, such as a project reload, brings Tier 3 back. Overall: a visual feedback feature breaks in every host, with no audio consequence and no crash risk, because both pointers are null-checked before use. That is consistent with the medium rating, so no severity change.

findings.title: MIDI-learn mappings: learning never completes, and 'Save Mapping with Preset' moves the mapping into storage that is never persisted
findings.problem: (1) The 'MIDI Learn' item calls midiCCManager_->startLearn and setParamNormalized(kGlobalMidiLearnActive). setParamNormalized never reaches the processor, and the processor has no case for that ID anyway (processor_params.cpp:326-363). Nothing in Disrumpo calls MidiCCManager::processCCMessage. kSweepDetectedCCOutputId is produced by the processor (processor.cpp:400-406) but nothing on the controller side consumes it. So a learn can never capture a CC. (2) 'Save Mapping with Preset' calls removeGlobalMapping and then addPresetMapping (moving the mapping into presetMappings_). Controller::getState serialises only serializeGlobalMappings (controller.cpp:665). serializePresetMappings has no caller outside tests, and createComponentStateStream does not include it either. (3) Changing mappings never calls restartComponent(kMidiCCAssignmentChanged), so hosts keep their cached IMidiMapping table.
findings.why_wrong: A persistence option has to persist somewhere, and the learn flow needs a CC-capture path. VST3 also requires restartComponent(kMidiCCAssignmentChanged) after the IMidiMapping table changes.
findings.consequence: Users cannot learn a CC from the context menu. Any mapping restored from controller state and then switched to 'Save Mapping with Preset' disappears on the next project save and reload.
findings.suggested_fix: Serialise presetMappings_ (in the controller state blob, or appended to the preset stream). Wire a capture path that completes learn, for example by reading kSweepDetectedCCOutputId in setParamNormalized, or through IMidiMapping-routed proxy params. Call componentHandler->restartComponent(kMidiCCAssignmentChanged) after any mapping change and after Controller::setState. Test: add a mapping, toggle it to per-preset, run getState -> setState on a fresh controller, and assert getMidiControllerAssignment still resolves.
findings.evidence: controller.cpp:1625-1626 `midiCCManager_->startLearn(paramId); setParamNormalized(makeGlobalParamId(GlobalParamType::kGlobalMidiLearnActive), 1.0);`; :1649-1650 `midiCCManager_->removeGlobalMapping(existingCC); midiCCManager_->addPresetMapping(existingCC, paramId, mapping.is14Bit);`; :665 `auto midiData = midiCCManager_->serializeGlobalMappings();`; grep processCCMessage|restartComponent in plugins/disrumpo/src: no hits; serializePresetMappings: only definition in shared/midi_cc_manager.cpp:322.
verifier_notes:
I traced each of the three claims through the code and all three hold.

(1) Learn never completes. The "MIDI Learn" item (controller.cpp:1623-1627) calls MidiCCManager::startLearn and setParamNormalized(kGlobalMidiLearnActive). The only code that completes a learn is MidiCCManager::processCCMessage (shared/midi/midi_cc_manager.cpp:127-146: addGlobalMapping, then learnModeActive_=false). A grep for processCCMessage under plugins/disrumpo/src finds nothing; its only callers are tests (midi_cc_manager_test.cpp, midi_learn_integration_test.cpp, state_persistence_test.cpp). kGlobalMidiLearnActive appears only in plugin_ids.h:69, parameter_registration.cpp:120 and controller.cpp:1412/1626. No processor case handles it. The processor's CC scan (processor.cpp:392-414) is driven by a different flag, midiLearnActive_, which is set from kSweepMidiLearnActive (processor_params.cpp:527-528). That scan writes kSweepDetectedCCOutputId. On the controller side that ID appears only in its registration (parameter_registration.cpp:307), and no setParamNormalized override reads it. So the context-menu learn can only be cancelled with Escape (controller.cpp:1409-1413). It never captures a CC.

(2) Per-preset mappings are lost. "Save Mapping with Preset" (controller.cpp:1646-1654) calls removeGlobalMapping, then addPresetMapping. That moves the mapping into presetMappings_ (midi_cc_manager.cpp:43-51, 53-59). Controller::getState (controller.cpp:664-671) serialises only serializeGlobalMappings, which walks globalMappings_ alone (midi_cc_manager.cpp:267-289). setState (controller.cpp:690-697) calls only deserializeGlobalMappings. serializePresetMappings (midi_cc_manager.cpp:322) has no caller in plugins/*/src, only tests. A mapping switched to per-preset therefore vanishes after a project save and reload.

(3) No host notification. A grep for restartComponent and kMidiCCAssignmentChanged in plugins/disrumpo/src returns nothing, so a mapping change or setState never tells the host to re-query IMidiMapping.

Medium severity is appropriate: this is a broken user-facing feature and a persistence loss, but audio is unaffected.

I could not refute this. Each claim checks out in the source, and nothing marks it as intentional.

(1) Learning never completes. controller.cpp:1623-1627 calls MidiCCManager::startLearn and then setParamNormalized(kGlobalMidiLearnActive, 1.0). That call changes only the controller's copy of the parameter; nothing is sent to the processor. The only other learn-related code in the controller is the Escape handler at controller.cpp:1409-1413, which cancels learning. The only place a learn is completed is MidiCCManager::processCCMessage (shared midi_cc_manager.cpp:127-146). Grepping plugins/ outside tests finds just its declaration and definition, so Disrumpo never calls it.

The processor's own learn scan (processor.cpp:392-414) is driven by midiLearnActive_, which follows kSweepMidiLearnActive (processor_params.cpp:527), not the global learn param. It only matches kLegacyMIDICCOutEvent and writes kSweepDetectedCCOutputId. The controller does not override setParamNormalized to read that ID; the grep shows only calls, no override and no use of kSweepDetectedCCOutputId outside parameter_registration.cpp:307. So nothing on either side can capture a CC for the context-menu learn.

(2) Per-preset mappings are not saved. The 'Save Mapping with Preset' action (controller.cpp:1646-1654) moves a mapping into presetMappings_. Controller::getState (controller.cpp:658-677) writes only serializeGlobalMappings, and setState (:679-701) reads only global mappings. serializePresetMappings and deserializePresetMappings (midi_cc_manager.cpp:322, :346) have no callers in plugins/ outside tests. The Disrumpo tests cover only the global-mapping round-trip (state_persistence_test.cpp:112-137, midi_learn_integration_test.cpp:104-108).
