(3) Hosts are never told the mapping changed. Grepping restartComponent and kMidiCCAssignmentChanged in plugins/disrumpo/src finds nothing.

Not intentional: specs/Disrumpo/dsp-details.md section 12 (around lines 1807-1855) specifies per-preset mappings, says they override global ones, and describes the right-click MIDI Learn workflow as a feature. No CHANGELOG or spec note records either gap as a known limitation.

Severity stays medium. This is a user-facing feature that is fully broken, but there is no audio or real-time-safety risk. Point (2) only matters for mappings that already exist, because point (1) means a real host can never create one.

Part (1) holds and it fully breaks the feature. controller.cpp:1623-1627: the "MIDI Learn" action calls midiCCManager_->startLearn(paramId) and setParamNormalized(kGlobalMidiLearnActive, 1.0). A grep of plugins/disrumpo/src finds no caller of MidiCCManager::processCCMessage; the only callers are tests (midi_cc_manager_test.cpp, midi_learn_integration_test.cpp, state_persistence_test.cpp). The processor never reads kGlobalMidiLearnActive. Its only learn flag comes from kSweepMidiLearnActive (processor_params.cpp:527-529). The processor's CC scan (processor.cpp:392-411) checks input events for kLegacyMIDICCOutEvent and writes kSweepDetectedCCOutputId. Nothing on the controller side reads that ID, and controller.h:435 assignedMidiCC_ stays at 128 because nothing in the controller assigns it (grep). So the context-menu learn can never capture a CC, and the sweep CC fallback in getMidiControllerAssignment (controller.cpp:720-723) is dead as well. Outside the toggle lambdas at controller.cpp:1650/1653 there is no addGlobalMapping/addPresetMapping call in src.

The impact of parts (2) and (3) is overstated. A mapping can only exist after a learn, which never completes, or after deserializeGlobalMappings at controller.cpp:695. That restores what getState wrote at :665, and getState can only have written an empty set. So getCCForParam at :1633 never succeeds in shipped code, and the "Clear MIDI Learn" and "Save Mapping with Preset" items never appear. The claimed loss of a per-preset mapping on reload cannot happen today. It is a latent defect (serializePresetMappings is never called; there is no restartComponent(kMidiCCAssignmentChanged)) that will bite as soon as learn is wired up.

Net consequence: the advertised MIDI Learn feature (FR-028/029/031) does nothing at all. The user picks "MIDI Learn" and no CC is ever bound. There is no audio, state-corruption or crash impact. Medium is fair for a user-facing feature that is completely non-functional, so I keep the severity. The fix plan should treat (2) and (3) as must-fix-together with (1), not as separate data-loss bugs.

findings.title: Controller::setState allocates a vector sized by an unvalidated int32 read from the stream
findings.problem: midiDataSize is read from the stream, and the code then calls std::vector<uint8_t>(midiDataSize) with no upper bound before reading.
findings.why_wrong: Corrupted or hostile controller state must not be able to trigger a multi-GB allocation, or a std::bad_alloc thrown across the VST3 ABI boundary (exceptions must not leave plugin entry points).
findings.consequence: A corrupt controller-state chunk with midiDataSize near 2^31 throws bad_alloc out of setState and can crash the host while it loads the project.
findings.suggested_fix: Clamp midiDataSize to a sane maximum, e.g. 4 + 128*6 bytes for 128 CC mappings, and reject the chunk otherwise. Test: a controller setState with midiDataSize = 0x7FFFFFFF returns without throwing.
findings.evidence: controller.cpp:690-692 `Steinberg::int32 midiDataSize = 0; if (streamer.readInt32(midiDataSize) && midiDataSize > 0) { std::vector<uint8_t> midiData(static_cast<size_t>(midiDataSize));`
verifier_notes: Re-derived from plugins/disrumpo/src/controller/controller.cpp:679-701. Controller::setState reads version (682); if version >= 2 it reads two doubles (687-688), then at 690-691 reads `Steinberg::int32 midiDataSize` and, if it is > 0, at 692 constructs `std::vector<uint8_t> midiData(static_cast<size_t>(midiDataSize))`. Nothing bounds it from above. The size is not checked against the stream length or against the serialized size of the MIDI CC mappings, which getState writes at 664-671. Up to 0x7FFFFFFF passes the `> 0` test. That value makes the vector allocate and zero about 2 GiB before state->read (693) can fail on the short stream. If the allocation fails, std::bad_alloc is thrown. A Grep for `try {` and `catch (` in controller.cpp finds no matches, and the VST3 SDK base classes add no exception guard, so the exception would leave a PLUGIN_API entry point. The quoted evidence matches the code exactly. Real hosts only hand back state the plugin wrote itself, so this takes a corrupt or hostile project file to trigger. Low severity is right.

I could not refute this. The code matches the quote at plugins/disrumpo/src/controller/controller.cpp:690-692. The value `Steinberg::int32 midiDataSize` comes from `streamer.readInt32` and is only checked for `> 0`. It is then used directly in `std::vector<uint8_t> midiData(static_cast<size_t>(midiDataSize));`. No upper bound is checked, and the stream's remaining length is not compared either.

Nothing upstream protects this path. In `Controller::setState` (controller.cpp:679-701) the only earlier check is `version >= 2`, and the two width/height doubles are read and ignored. A grep for try/catch in every plugin's controller*.cpp finds no handler around the allocation. The VST3 SDK does not catch exceptions at the `setState` entry either.

The writer side (controller.cpp:664-674, `getState`) only ever writes `serializeGlobalMappings().size()`, which is small. So the problem can only be hit with a corrupted or hand-crafted controller chunk. That makes it unreachable in normal use, but it is a real robustness defect, not an intentional design.

I found no spec note or code comment that documents this as accepted behaviour. I also found no test that pins it.

A smaller issue on the same path: `state->read` at line 693 passes `nullptr` for numBytesRead. A short read is therefore not detected, and the partly filled zero-initialised buffer is still passed to `deserializeGlobalMappings`.

Low severity fits: it needs corrupt state, it runs on the UI thread at load rather than the audio thread, and the fix is a cheap clamp.

The defect is real as described. plugins/disrumpo/src/controller/controller.cpp:690-692 reads `Steinberg::int32 midiDataSize` from the stream and, if it is greater than 0, constructs `std::vector<uint8_t> midiData(static_cast<size_t>(midiDataSize))` with no upper bound. Only after that does it call `state->read` (line 693). Nothing guards it: a grep for `try {` / `catch (` across the plugins' controller*.cpp files finds no handler in Disrumpo's controller, so a std::bad_alloc thrown here would leave the PLUGIN_API setState entry point. The matching writer, getState (664-671), only ever writes `serializeGlobalMappings().size()`, which is a small number of CC-mapping bytes. So any value in the hundreds of MB to GB range can only come from a corrupt or hostile chunk. Impact: the worst case is midiDataSize = 0x7FFFFFFF, which makes the vector allocate and zero-fill about 2 GiB. On a 64-bit host this usually succeeds, at the cost of a large commit spike, and is then freed after the short read. bad_alloc, and a possible host crash, only happens when memory is tight or the address space is 32-bit. The trigger needs a corrupted controller-state chunk in a project or preset. That is rare, and normal saves cannot produce it. Low severity is right, so no change. The fix is cheap: clamp to a sane maximum. This is local to Disrumpo; the same grep found no other plugin source with this pattern, only test code.

findings.title: Mode sub-controller destructors call unregisterControlListener on an already-destroyed child control (use-after-free on every type switch and on editor close)
findings.problem: BitwiseOpController, TemporalModeController and RingSatFreqModeController keep a raw CControl* to a child of their own template. In the destructor they call opControl_->unregisterControlListener(this). VSTGUI deletes the sub-controller in CView::beforeDelete, and CViewContainer::beforeDelete runs removeAll(true) first, so every child control is already freed when the controller destructor runs.
findings.why_wrong: CViewContainer::beforeDelete calls `CViewContainer::removeAll (true); CView::beforeDelete ();` (cviewcontainer.cpp:177-179). CView::beforeDelete then deletes the kCViewControllerAttribute controller (cview.cpp:263-270), and that attribute is set on the template root (uidescription.cpp:744). The control's impl->subListeners is freed memory by then.
findings.consequence: A heap write-after-free happens each time the TypeParams UIViewSwitchContainer (animation-time 0, removeAll and recreate) switches away from Temporal, Bitwise Mangler or Ring Saturation, in both the Shape tab and the expanded strip, and each time the editor closes with one of those types shown. Changing the distortion type is a core interaction. The result is a latent crash or heap corruption that ASan would flag. The same pattern exists in Iterum (delay_time_sync_controller.h:41-44) and Innexus (modulator_sub_controller.h:35-40), so the impact is cross-plugin.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the unregister from the destructor, since the control is gone and its listener list dies with it, as FractalModeController already does. Alternatively observe the control with IViewListener::viewWillDelete and null the pointer there. Test under ASan: open the editor, set DisplayedType to Temporal, switch to SoftClip, and close the editor.
findings.evidence: sub_controllers.h:283-286 `~BitwiseOpController() override { if (opControl_) opControl_->unregisterControlListener(this); }` ; vstgui cviewcontainer.cpp:178 `CViewContainer::removeAll (true);` before :179 `CView::beforeDelete ();` ; cview.cpp:264-270 deletes the controller ; editor.uidesc:1031 `template name="TypeParams_Temporal" ... sub-controller="TemporalMode"` inside the UIViewSwitchContainer at :1290 / :1340
verifier_notes:
The finding traces only the bare-VSTGUI teardown path (CViewContainer::beforeDelete, cviewcontainer.cpp:177-179, followed by CView::beforeDelete deleting the kCViewControllerAttribute controller, cview.cpp:263-271). On the paths it names, the sub-controller is gone well before that point. Disrumpo's editor is a VST3Editor (controller.cpp:730), and VST3Editor installs itself as the frame's ViewAddedRemovedObserver (vst3editor.cpp:1308).

Type switch: UIViewSwitchContainer::setCurrentViewIndex calls removeAll() on an attached container (uiviewswitchcontainer.cpp:126/132/138). removeAll(true) calls view->removed(this) on the template root BEFORE it forgets the root (cviewcontainer.cpp:565-574). CViewContainer::removed first runs removed() on each child, while the children are still owned by the root (cviewcontainer.cpp:1532-1535). It then calls CView::removed, which reaches parentFrame->onViewRemoved (cview.cpp:482-483), then CFrame::onViewRemoved, then the observer (cframe.cpp:1165-1166). VST3Editor::onViewRemoved then releases the sub-controller and removes the kCViewControllerAttribute (vst3editor.cpp:776-781; releaseSubController at 378-386 deletes a plain DelegationController).

So ~BitwiseOpController, ~TemporalModeController and ~RingSatFreqModeController (sub_controllers.h:283-286, 368-371, 444-447) run while opControl_/modeControl_/freqModeControl_ are still alive. The template-root container still holds them, so unregisterControlListener operates on live memory. Only after that does view->forget() reach CViewContainer::beforeDelete, which frees the children. At that point CView::beforeDelete no longer finds a controller attribute, so nothing is deleted twice.

Editor close follows the same order. VST3Editor::close calls getFrame()->removeAll(true) while the observer is still registered and the views are still attached (vst3editor.cpp:1407-1408). The sub-controllers are therefore released in onViewRemoved before any child control is freed.

The use-after-free the finding claims would need the template root to be deleted while detached, or with no VST3Editor observer. Neither the type-switch path nor the editor-close path does that. The same reasoning clears the cited Iterum and Innexus patterns, which also run under VST3Editor.

The finding traces only the unattached deletion path (CViewContainer::beforeDelete -> removeAll(true) -> CView::beforeDelete deletes the controller). In a running editor the views are attached to a frame, and that path never reaches these destructors while the controller attribute is still set. In the attached path VSTGUI deletes the sub-controller while its child controls are still alive.

1. Who receives the removal event. VST3Editor registers itself as the frame's observer (vst3editor.cpp:1308 `getFrame ()->setViewAddedRemovedObserver (this)`). CFrame::onViewRemoved forwards every removed view to that observer (cframe.cpp:1165-1166).

2. Order of removal. A view is removed from an attached container through CViewContainer::removed (cviewcontainer.cpp:1527-1535). It calls removed() on each child first, then CView::removed on itself, which calls `parentFrame->onViewRemoved (this)` (cview.cpp:482-483). The sub-controller attribute sits on the template root (uidescription.cpp:744; editor.uidesc:1031/1050/1097 put sub-controller= on the template root).

3. When the sub-controller dies. When the root's onViewRemoved runs, VST3Editor::onViewRemoved calls `VST3EditorInternal::releaseSubController (controller); view->removeAttribute (kCViewControllerAttribute);` (vst3editor.cpp:776-781). DelegationController is neither an IReference nor an FObject, so this is a plain delete (vst3editor.cpp:378-386). At that moment the Op/Mode/FreqMode control is still in the root's children list, and the list still holds a reference to it. The children are only forgotten later, in removeAll(true) inside the root's beforeDelete. So `opControl_->unregisterControlListener(this)` at sub_controllers.h:283-286, 368-371 and 444-447 runs on a live control.

4. Why the root's beforeDelete is harmless. By the time CView::beforeDelete runs on the root (cview.cpp:263-271), the attribute has already been removed, so it finds no controller to delete again.

5. Both trigger paths take the attached route.
   - Type switch: UIViewSwitchContainer calls removeAll() while attached (uiviewswitchcontainer.cpp:126/132/138). removeAll calls view->removed(this) when isAttached (cviewcontainer.cpp:566-567). On container removal it calls CViewContainer::removed before removeAll (uiviewswitchcontainer.cpp:181-184).
   - Editor close: VST3Editor::close calls `getFrame ()->removeAll (true)` with the observer still installed (vst3editor.cpp:1407-1408).
   The ParameterChangeListener's extra reference on the control is released in the same onViewRemoved pass (vst3editor.cpp:766-773, 156-166). That pass reaches children before the root, but the root's children list still keeps the control alive.

Only views that are created and destroyed without ever being attached would take the path the finding describes. A host-opened editor does not do that for these templates. The claimed use-after-free on every type switch and on editor close does not happen, and the matching Iterum and Innexus claims fail for the same reason.

The finding traces only the beforeDelete path and misses VST3Editor's view-removed hook. In real use, that hook deletes the sub-controller first, while its child controls are still alive.

1. The destructors are as quoted: sub_controllers.h:283-286, 368-371 and 444-447 call unregisterControlListener on a raw CControl* child of the template root. The templates are at editor.uidesc:1031, 1050 and 1097.

2. Disrumpo uses VSTGUI::VST3Editor (controller.cpp:730). VST3Editor makes itself the frame's view-added/removed observer (vst3editor.cpp:1308).

3. Type switch path. UIDescriptionViewSwitchController only listens to the switch control between switchContainerAttached and switchContainerRemoved (uiviewswitchcontainer.cpp:255-266). So setCurrentViewIndex only runs while the container is attached. With animation-time 0 it calls CViewContainer::removeAll() (uiviewswitchcontainer.cpp:138), and withForget defaults to true. Because the container is attached, removeAll calls view->removed(this) before it calls forget() (cviewcontainer.cpp:566-574).
   - CViewContainer::removed first calls removed() on every child, then CView::removed on itself (cviewcontainer.cpp:1527-1535).
   - CView::removed calls parentFrame->onViewRemoved (cview.cpp:482-483). That reaches VST3Editor::onViewRemoved (cframe.cpp:1165-1166).
   - VST3Editor::onViewRemoved finds the template root's kCViewControllerAttribute, calls releaseSubController (a plain delete for a DelegationController, vst3editor.cpp:378-386), and removes the attribute (vst3editor.cpp:776-781).
   - So the destructor runs while the child COptionMenu is still owned by the template root's child list. The unregister call hits a live object.
   - Only afterwards does forget() reach CViewContainer::beforeDelete, which runs removeAll(true) and then CView::beforeDelete. By then the attribute is gone, so cview.cpp:263-271 deletes nothing.

4. Editor close path. VST3Editor::close calls getFrame()->removeAll(true) (vst3editor.cpp:1408) while the frame and its subtree are still attached. That goes through CFrame::removeAll and CViewContainer::removeAll (cframe.cpp:1352-1362), so the same removed()/onViewRemoved sequence releases each sub-controller before any child is forgotten. UIViewSwitchContainer::removed also calls CViewContainer::removed before its own removeAll (uiviewswitchcontainer.cpp:176-185).

5. The beforeDelete-first order the finding describes would only happen if a template root carrying one of these sub-controllers were destroyed without ever being attached, or if no VST3Editor observer were present. Neither happens here: the switch container creates its views only after it is attached (uiviewswitchcontainer.cpp:166-172 and the attach-time valueChanged at ~line 256), and Disrumpo's controller code never calls createView or removeView on these templates by hand (grep found none).

The use-after-free cannot happen on a type switch or on editor close. The Iterum and Innexus cases cited would be safe the same way, since both run under VST3Editor.

findings.title: compactNodeSelectors_ dangles after a Main/Shape tab switch; willClose then calls deactivate() on the freed view
findings.problem: createCustomView stores a raw pointer to the auto-hide DynamicNodeSelector in compactNodeSelectors_[band]. That selector lives in BandNShapeTab, which is a page of a UIViewSwitchContainer (animation-time 0), so switching back to Main destroys it. The pointer is never cleared, and willClose later calls dns->deactivate() on it, which runs isActive_.exchange on freed memory.
findings.why_wrong: Views created inside a UIViewSwitchContainer page are destroyed on every page switch: removeAll() and addView of the new template, with no caching. A controller that caches such a view must clear the pointer when the view dies, through IViewListener::viewWillDelete or the view's destructor, or else must not cache it.
findings.consequence: Open the editor, click Shape on any band, click Main, then close the editor: willClose touches freed memory, a crash or heap corruption in normal use. The high-contrast loop at :1451 has the same hazard if the pages ever exist when it runs.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not cache the compact selector. Its destructor already calls deactivate(). Alternatively have DynamicNodeSelector notify the controller from its destructor so the slot is nulled. Test under ASan: an editor lifecycle test that toggles BandTabView 0->1->0 and then closes the editor.
findings.evidence: controller.cpp:1079-1081 `if (autoHideStr && *autoHideStr == "true") { ... compactNodeSelectors_[bandIndex] = nodeSelector;` ; :1546 `for (auto& dns : compactNodeSelectors_) { if (dns) { dns->deactivate(); dns = nullptr; } }` ; editor.uidesc:1293 the auto-hide selector is in template BandShapeTab ; :543 `UIViewSwitchContainer ... animation-time="0" template-names="Band1MainTab,Band1ShapeTab"`
verifier_notes:
I traced the call path from source and the defect is real.

1. How the pointer gets cached. editor.uidesc:1293 puts `DynamicNodeSelector ... auto-hide-single="true"` inside template BandShapeTab. Band1..4ShapeTab (uidesc:1296-1306) include that template, and those are pages of a `UIViewSwitchContainer animation-time="0" template-names="BandNMainTab,BandNShapeTab"` (uidesc:543/553/563/573). BandSubController::createView (sub_controllers.h:212-225) adds the band attribute and passes the call on to Controller::createView, which reaches controller.cpp:1068 `new DynamicNodeSelector`. Lines 1079-1081 store the raw pointer in compactNodeSelectors_[bandIndex]. Nothing calls remember(), and no view listener is attached.

2. Switching tabs frees the view. In UIViewSwitchContainer::setCurrentViewIndex (extern/vst3sdk/vstgui4/vstgui/uidescription/uiviewswitchcontainer.cpp:40-143), animationTime is 0, so it takes the `CViewContainer::removeAll(); addView(view)` branch at :138. removeAll forgets the children, so the old Shape page and its selector are deleted (refcount 1). UIDescriptionViewSwitchController::createViewForIndex (:205-211) builds a new view from the template on every switch, with no caching.

3. The pointer is never cleared. A grep for compactNodeSelectors_ finds only controller.h:364, controller.cpp:1081 (assign), :1451 (high-contrast loop in didOpen) and :1546 (willClose). The DynamicNodeSelector destructor (views/dynamic_node_selector.cpp:48-56) calls deactivate() and releases the parameter, but never tells the controller.

4. The freed memory is used. willClose at controller.cpp:1546 calls `dns->deactivate()`, which runs `isActive_.exchange(...)` (dynamic_node_selector.cpp:65) on the freed object. If the heap has reused that memory and the flag reads nonzero, it then calls `activeNodesParam_->removeDependent(this)` through a garbage pointer.

Repro: open the editor, click Shape on a band (the selector is created and cached), click Main (the selector is deleted), close the editor. willClose then touches freed memory, which is undefined behaviour.

The :1451 hazard is minor. willClose nulls the slots, and didOpen runs right after the views are created, so at that point the pointers are normally valid. The main defect is the willClose use-after-free. High severity fits: a normal UI sequence produces a use-after-free.

I could not refute this. The code confirms it.
(1) controller.cpp:1078-1081: when the view has auto-hide-single="true", createCustomView stores the raw `new DynamicNodeSelector` pointer in compactNodeSelectors_[bandIndex]. Nothing calls remember(), so the view's only owner is its parent container.
(2) controller.cpp only touches compactNodeSelectors_ at three places: the store at :1081, the high-contrast loop at :1451 (didOpen) and :1546 in willClose (`dns->deactivate(); dns = nullptr;`). No viewWillDelete or IViewListener hook clears it, and the sub-controllers do not either. BandSubController::createView in sub_controllers.h:212-225 only injects the band attribute and forwards to the controller.
(3) editor.uidesc:1293 puts the auto-hide selector in template BandShapeTab, and Band1..4ShapeTab (:1296-1305) wrap that template. editor.uidesc:543/553/563/573 declare `UIViewSwitchContainer animation-time="0" template-switch-control="BandNTabView" template-names="BandNMainTab,BandNShapeTab"`, driven by a user-facing Main/Shape CSegmentButton (:541 etc.).
(4) In extern/vst3sdk/vstgui4/vstgui/uidescription/uiviewswitchcontainer.cpp:126-139, setCurrentViewIndex calls removeAll() and then addView(newView). CViewContainer::removeAll defaults to withForget=true. Nothing caches pages, so switching back to Main frees the Shape page and its DynamicNodeSelector.
(5) dynamic_node_selector.cpp:48-50: the destructor calls deactivate(), but the controller's slot is never nulled. willClose:1546 then calls deactivate() on freed memory: isActive_.exchange at dynamic_node_selector.cpp:65, and possibly removeDependent through a garbage activeNodesParam_ if the freed bytes were reused.
(6) No test covers it. The only TabView test is the audio-only processor_audio_output_test.cpp:267. The defect is not documented as a design decision anywhere.
Reachable in normal use: open the editor, click Shape on a band, click Main, close the editor. In practice the freed isActive_ often still reads false, so the result may be silent UB rather than a crash every time. Heap reuse makes corruption or a crash possible. That fits the stated high severity, so no adjustment. The :1451 loop runs only in didOpen, when the pointers are fresh or were nulled by the previous willClose, so it is low-risk today.

I could not refute this. It is a real use-after-free.

Where the pointer is stored:
- controller.cpp:1078-1081 keeps the raw `DynamicNodeSelector*` in `compactNodeSelectors_[bandIndex]` when `auto-hide-single="true"`.
- Only three places touch that array (grep): controller.cpp:1081 (store), :1451 (high-contrast loop) and :1546 (willClose calls deactivate, then nulls it). Nothing clears it when the view is destroyed.

The path is reachable:
- editor.uidesc:1293 puts the auto-hide selector in template BandShapeTab. Band1-4ShapeTab (:1296-1306) include it through sub-controller BandShapeTabN.
- BandSubController::createView (sub_controllers.h:212-225) injects the band index and forwards custom views to the parent controller. So the selector does come from Controller::createCustomView.
- The page container is a UIViewSwitchContainer with animation-time="0" (editor.uidesc:543/553/563/573).

The view is destroyed on every tab switch:
- In the vendored VSTGUI, UIViewSwitchContainer::setCurrentViewIndex (uiviewswitchcontainer.cpp:40-128) calls `createViewForIndex`, which builds a fresh template each time and caches nothing (`uiDescription->createView(templateNames[index])`, :209).
- With animationTime == 0 it runs `removeAll(); addView(view);`. That forgets the Shape page and deletes the selector, since nothing else holds a reference to it.
- ~DynamicNodeSelector (dynamic_node_selector.cpp:48-56) calls deactivate() and releases activeNodesParam_. It does not tell the controller, so the cached pointer dangles.

willClose then touches freed memory:
- VST3Editor::close (vst3editor.cpp:1377-1378) calls delegate->willClose before teardown.
- controller.cpp:1546 then runs `dns->deactivate()` on the dangling pointer, i.e. `isActive_.exchange(false)` (dynamic_node_selector.cpp:65): a read-modify-write on freed heap.
- Trigger: open the editor, click Shape on any band, click Main, close the editor. That is ordinary use and needs no special host or settings.

Impact:
- If the freed block has not been reused, isActive_ still reads false (the destructor set it) and nothing visible happens.
- If the heap has reused it, which is likely under Windows LFH or macOS malloc while UI views churn, the exchange writes a zero byte into a live object. That is silent heap corruption.
- If the reused bytes happen to read true, removeDependent is called through a garbage activeNodesParam_ pointer and the plugin crashes.
- ASan flags it every time. In a release build it is intermittent corruption or a crash on editor close.

On the :1451 hazard: the high-contrast loop runs at editor open, before any tab switch, and willClose nulls the array on every close. So that loop is not a live hazard today.

Severity: High is justified for a use-after-free with a heap write on a normal UI path. No change.

findings.title: Morph pad never follows its parameters, and Morph Y is sent with performEdit only, so the controller's Morph Y value goes stale and preset saves lose it
findings.problem: The MorphPad is bound to MorphX through VST3Editor (setListener(editor), tag = MorphX), but it draws the cursor from its private morphX_/morphY_ and does not override setValue. Host automation, preset load, the sweep morph link and undo therefore never move the cursor. MorphY is written with controller_->beginEdit/performEdit/endEdit and never with setParamNormalized, so the controller-side MorphY parameter keeps its old value.
findings.why_wrong: EditController::performEdit only notifies the host; it does not change the controller's own Parameter value, and hosts do not echo the value back. Every other UI write path here (editParam, CrossoverDragBridge, VST3Editor's ParameterChangeListener::performEdit) calls setParamNormalized first. A bound control must also reflect parameter changes.
findings.consequence: (1) A user preset saved after a Y drag stores the stale Y: createComponentStateStream reads getParamNorm(kBandMorphY) at controller.cpp:1828, so the morph position is lost on save and recall. (2) Reopening the editor puts the cursor at the stale Y (controller.cpp:1016-1018). (3) MorphSweepLinkController reads the stale currentY (visibility_controllers.cpp:192). (4) Automated or preset-loaded morph positions are not displayed.
findings.suggested_fix: Call controller_->setParamNormalized(morphYParamId_, y) before performEdit (or use editParam). Make the pad an IDependent on its MorphX/MorphY parameters, or override setValue for X plus a dependent for Y, so that setMorphPosition follows parameter changes. Tests: drag the pad, then assert getParamNormalized(MorphY) equals the drag Y. Then setParamNormalized(MorphX/Y) and assert the pad's getMorphX/Y follow.
findings.evidence: morph_pad.cpp:687-689 `controller_->beginEdit(morphYParamId_); controller_->performEdit(morphYParamId_, static_cast<double>(morphY_));` (no setParamNormalized) ; morph_pad.cpp:478 and :568 draw from morphX_/morphY_ ; morph_pad.h overrides draw and the mouse handlers but not setValue ; controller.cpp:1004-1005 `morphPad->setTag(morphXParamId); morphPad->setListener(editor);`
verifier_notes:
I could not refute this. I traced it in the source and it holds.

(1) MorphY is never written into the controller. Every place the pad edits Y sends it to the host only:
- morph_pad.cpp:646-649 (double-click reset)
- morph_pad.cpp:687-689 (mouse down)
- morph_pad.cpp:746-748 (drag)
- morph_pad.cpp:820-823 (scroll wheel)
Each one calls controller_->beginEdit, then performEdit, then endEdit, and none calls setParamNormalized. controller_ is a plain Steinberg::Vst::EditControllerEx1* (morph_pad.cpp:71). controller.h does not override performEdit or setParamNormalized. EditController::performEdit only forwards to the component handler. The processor's only output parameters are the sweep frequency and the detected CC (processor.cpp:379-406), so nothing ever writes Y back into the controller. Every other write path does set the controller value first: visibility_controllers.cpp:198-208, controller.cpp:1180-1181 and 1871-1872, dynamic_node_selector.cpp:192-193, and VSTGUI's ParameterChangeListener::performEdit at vst3editor.cpp:231-232.

(2) X is not affected. The pad's tag is MorphX and its listener is the editor (controller.cpp:1004-1005), so valueChanged() goes through ParameterChangeListener::performEdit, which calls setParamNormalized first.

(3) The preset save is real. The in-plugin preset manager's state provider is createComponentStateStream (controller.cpp:116-117). That function reads getParamNorm(kBandMorphY) from the controller's own parameter object (controller.cpp:1691-1692, 1828), so it writes the stale Y.

(4) Reopening the editor seeds the pad from the stale value (controller.cpp:1016-1018). MorphSweepLinkController also reads the stale currentY (visibility_controllers.cpp:191-192).

(5) The pad does not follow its parameters. morph_pad.h overrides only draw, the four mouse handlers, update, and newCopy; there is no setValue or valueChanged override. drawCursor draws from morphX_/morphY_ (morph_pad.cpp:568). The pad's only IDependent subscription is the ActiveNodes parameter (morph_pad.cpp:80-84, 143-145). controller.cpp uses morphPads_ only for high-contrast mode (line 1448) and deactivate (line 1547). So when the editor's ParameterChangeListener sets the control value, the cursor does not move, and Y has no binding at all.

(6) No test covers this. morph_pad_test.cpp only checks the pad's own getMorphY() after it is set directly, never the controller's parameter value.

I am keeping severity high: user presets lose the morph Y position, which is the plugin's central control.

I found nothing that guards this, documents it as intended, or pins it with a test, so the defect stands.

(1) Y write path. Three paths call controller_->beginEdit/performEdit/endEdit(morphYParamId_) with no setParamNormalized first: double-click reset at morph_pad.cpp:646-649, drag start at :687-689 and wheel at :820-823. Mouse-move does the same with performEdit alone at :746-748. Every other UI write path in the controller calls setParamNormalized before performEdit: controller.cpp:1180-1181 and :1871-1872, keyboard_shortcut_handler.cpp:141-142, visibility_controllers.cpp:198-208, dynamic_node_selector.cpp:192-193. The controller does not override performEdit or setParamNormalized (nothing in controller.h). No IDependent or other listener anywhere updates kBandMorphY: a grep of src/ for kBandMorphY finds only the registration, the sub-controller tag map, the state-load setter, pad creation and the link controller. I found no evidence that the processor writes MorphY to outputParameterChanges.

(2) Consumers of the stale value. The PresetManager state provider is createComponentStateStream (controller.cpp:116-118), and it writes getParamNorm(kBandMorphY) at controller.cpp:1828. A preset saved from the in-plugin browser after a Y drag therefore stores the old Y. Pad creation also reads the stale morphYParam at controller.cpp:1011-1019. The CSlider bound to Band.MorphY (editor.uidesc:1272) does not move when the pad is dragged in Y.

(3) Pad does not follow its parameters. The cursor and connection lines draw from the private morphX_/morphY_ (morph_pad.cpp:478, :568), and there is no getValue() read anywhere in morph_pad.cpp. morph_pad.h does not override setValue/setValueNormalized. The pad's only IDependent subscription is ActiveNodes (morph_pad.cpp:79-90, :132-157). So when VST3Editor's parameter listener calls setValue on the tag-bound control (tag = MorphX, controller.cpp:1004-1005), the cursor stays put. The same is true for automation, preset load and the sweep link. The pad's MorphPadListener is never set (setMorphPadListener has no callers).

(4) Tests. tests/unit/morph_pad_test.cpp checks only the pad's local getMorphX/getMorphY and never checks the controller parameter.

One mitigation, which does not refute the finding: host project save goes through the processor's getState, and the processor did receive Y through performEdit. So the stale value hurts the in-plugin preset save, the editor display, the MorphY slider and the link controller (visibility_controllers.cpp:185-208), but not project recall. Because the in-plugin preset save and the display are user-visible, I keep the severity at high.

I could not refute this. Every link in the claim holds in the source.

(1) Morph Y never reaches the controller's own parameter. Every Y write in the pad is a bare performEdit: morph_pad.cpp:646-649 (double-click reset), :687-689 (mouse down), :746-748 (drag move) and :820-823 (keyboard nudge). No path calls setParamNormalized. listener_ never reaches the controller either: the controller has no implementation of onMorphPositionChanged (grep finds it only in views/morph_pad.*), and controller.cpp:1005 passes the VST3Editor as the CControl listener, which handles only the X tag. The Disrumpo Controller does not override performEdit, so EditController::performEdit only forwards to the host. The processor sends back only kSweepModulatedFrequencyOutputId and kSweepDetectedCCOutputId as output parameters (processor.cpp:379-406), so nothing echoes Morph Y back. Every other write site in the plugin sets the value first: controller.cpp:1180-1181, 1201-1202, 1228-1234, 1871-1872 and visibility_controllers.cpp:204-208.

(2) The preset save reads the stale value. The PresetManager state provider is createComponentStateStream (controller.cpp:116-117), and it writes getParamNorm(kBandMorphY) (controller.cpp:~1828). A user preset saved after a Y drag therefore stores the old Y. The host project save is not affected, because Processor::getState holds the real Y. MorphSweepLinkController reads the stale value (visibility_controllers.cpp:185-192), and so does the editor rebuild (controller.cpp:1013-1018).

(3) The cursor never follows its parameters. MorphPad does not override setValue. Its only IDependent hookup is ActiveNodes (morph_pad.cpp:79-90, and update() at :132-156 ignores any other parameter). The cursor is drawn from morphX_/morphY_. The only setMorphPosition call outside the pad is at editor creation (controller.cpp:1018). Host automation, preset load through loadComponentStateWithNotify, and the sweep morph link therefore update the parameter values but not the cursor. Undo, also named in the claim, I did not trace.

Impact: Y spans the full node layout, from the bottom-left/bottom-right nodes at 0 to the top nodes at 1 (morph_pad.cpp resetNodePositionsToDefault). A stale Y can recall a completely different node blend, so the consequence is silent loss of preset data in any host that does not call setParamNormalized after performEdit, which the VST3 spec does not require. On top of that, the main morph control's display is wrong under automation. High severity is justified.

findings.title: After a node type change the restored shape slots reach only the proxies, never the node's real kNodeShape params, so the controller holds the old type's slot values
findings.problem: copyDisplayedTypeToSelectedNode runs inside update() with isUpdating_ = true. It edits the node type and then writes the new type's shadow slots to the ten proxy params with editParam. Each proxy change synchronously re-enters update(), because FObject::changed -> triggerUpdates is synchronous, and update() returns at the isUpdating_ guard, so copyProxyToSelectedNode never runs. The selected node's real kNodeShape0..9 params keep the previous type's values.
findings.why_wrong: The proxy params are the UI view of the selected node. Every proxy edit must be mirrored into the real node param, which is what the controller serializes and what the host sees. The re-entrancy guard swallows the mirror for exactly the writes that most need it.
findings.consequence: Example: switch a node from Tube (slot0 = 0.8) to Fuzz. The UI shows Fuzz's restored or default slots (0.5); the processor uses its own shadow (0.5), which processor_params.cpp:844-852 loads independently; the controller's kNodeShape0 still says 0.8. A user preset saved now (controller.cpp:1851-1855) stores Tube's slot values under type Fuzz, and recalling it sounds different from what was saved. Host automation lanes also show stale values.
findings.suggested_fix: In copyDisplayedTypeToSelectedNode, also editParam the real node shape params (makeNodeParamId(band, node, kNodeShape0+s)) with newSlots, or temporarily clear isUpdating_ only for the mirror. Test: with the editor's NodeSelectionController active, change DisplayedType, then assert that each node kNodeShape param equals the proxy value.
findings.evidence: visibility_controllers.cpp:318-320 `if (isUpdating_) { return; }` ; :445-453 `shapeShadowPtr_->load(newTypeIdx, newSlots); ... editParam(makeBandParamId(band_, kProxyIndexToBandParam[4 + s]), newSlots[s]);` while isUpdating_ is still true (cleared at :337) ; fobject.cpp:196-201 changed() -> triggerUpdates (synchronous)
verifier_notes:
The defect is real. I traced it as follows.

1. Re-entry is synchronous and gets swallowed. NodeSelectionController::update sets isUpdating_ = true at visibility_controllers.cpp:322 and clears it at :337. The early return is at :318-320. editParam (:350-355) calls controller_->setParamNormalized. In the SDK that leads to Parameter::setNormalized (vstparameters.cpp:62-78), which calls changed() whenever the value differs. FObject::changed (fobject.cpp:196-201) then calls gUpdateHandler->triggerUpdates, which is doTriggerUpdates(..., false) (updatehandler.cpp:437-440): the synchronous path, not deferUpdates. The controller is registered as a dependent of every proxy param (:253-258), so each proxy write re-enters update() and returns at :318.

2. Nothing mirrors the restored slots into the node params. copyDisplayedTypeToSelectedNode (:413-455) calls editParam on the node's kNodeType (:443). It then calls editParam only on the band proxies kBandDisplayedShape0..9 (:445-453, via the kProxyIndexToBandParam map at plugin_ids.h:361-369). It never touches makeNodeParamId(band, node, kNodeShape0+s). Only copyProxyToSelectedNode (:392-411) would mirror them, and that is unreachable here because of step 1.

3. There is no other mirroring path. The controller does not override setParamNormalized or performEdit (grep found no Controller::setParamNormalized/performEdit). The processor treats the displayed/proxy band params as UI-only (processor_params.cpp:971-979). On kNodeType it restores its own shadow independently (processor_params.cpp:838-850). So the processor's slots and the controller's kNodeShape params diverge.

4. The consequence path holds. The controller-side preset serializer writes getParamNorm(makeNodeParamId(band, node, kNodeShapeN)) (controller.cpp:1851-1855), so it writes the stale previous-type values under the new type. No test in plugins/disrumpo/tests references NodeSelectionController or DisplayedType, so nothing covers this.

Side observation, not part of this finding: the controller passes shapeShadowStorage_[b].data() (controller.cpp:1460), a pointer to node 0's storage only. So the controller's save/load at :438/:447 ignores the selected node.

The audio is correct while the editor is open. The damage is to the controller state, the user presets it saves, and the host-visible param values. High severity stands.

I confirmed the defect from source and found nothing that guards against it.

1) visibility_controllers.cpp:318-322 sets isUpdating_=true and only clears it at :337. Inside that window, copyDisplayedTypeToSelectedNode (:413-455) calls editParam (:350-355 -> controller_->setParamNormalized) on the 10 proxy band IDs (kProxyIndexToBandParam[4+s], :448-453).

2) That notification is synchronous. Parameter::setNormalized (vstparameters.cpp:73-76) calls changed(). FObject::changed (fobject.cpp:196-201) calls gUpdateHandler->triggerUpdates. UpdateHandler::triggerUpdates (updatehandler.cpp:437-440) calls doTriggerUpdates(..., false), which is synchronous. So NodeSelectionController::update re-enters, hits the isUpdating_ guard at :318, and copyProxyToSelectedNode (:392-411) never runs. Nothing writes makeNodeParamId(band, node, kNodeShape0+s).

3) No other path mirrors proxy to node in the controller. A grep for kNodeShape0 in the controller finds only setState (:574), string formatting (:766) and createComponentStateStream (:1853). There is no Controller::setParamNormalized override. The processor ignores the proxy band IDs: processor_params.cpp:975-979 sends them to the default/no-action case. Meanwhile the processor loads its own shadow on the type change (:844-852). The processor and the controller's real node params therefore diverge.

4) It matters in a real host:
- NodeSelectionController is created per band whenever the editor opens (controller.cpp:1458-1461).
- The PresetManager state provider is createComponentStateStream (controller.cpp:116-118). That stream writes the controller's stale kNodeShape0..9 (:1851-1855) next to the updated shadow (:1857-1861). A user preset saved after a type change stores the old type's slots as the current slots.
- copySelectedNodeToProxies (:372-390) will also later copy the stale node values back into the proxies when the node is reselected.
- Host project state is unaffected, because it comes from the processor.

5) No test in plugins/disrumpo/tests references NodeSelectionController or DisplayedType, and I found no spec or comment that documents this as intended.

Severity stays high: changing a node's type is a common action, and saving a preset afterwards silently corrupts it.

Side note, separate from this finding: controller.cpp:1460 passes shapeShadowStorage_[b].data(), so shapeShadowPtr_ always points at node 0's shadow whichever node is selected.

I could not refute this. The source supports the defect and its consequence.

1. The guard swallows the mirror. update() sets isUpdating_=true at visibility_controllers.cpp:322 and calls copyDisplayedTypeToSelectedNode at :327. That function writes the proxies through editParam at :445-453, and editParam calls controller_->setParamNormalized at :352. In the SDK, Parameter::setNormalized calls changed() (vstparameters.cpp:76), and FObject::changed calls gUpdateHandler->triggerUpdates (fobject.cpp:196-201), which is the synchronous doTriggerUpdates path (updatehandler.cpp:437-440). The re-entrant update() therefore returns at :318-320, so copyProxyToSelectedNode (:392-411) never mirrors the value into makeNodeParamId(band,node,kNodeShapeN). Nothing else writes those params on a type change. The processor ignores the band-level proxy params: processor_params.cpp:971-979 treats kBandDisplayed* as UI-only and falls to the default case.

2. The processor and controller diverge. On kNodeType the processor loads its own shadow into mn.shapeSlots (processor_params.cpp:840-853). The controller's real kNodeShape0..9 params keep the old type's values.

3. Saved state is wrong. The controller-side preset save (controller.cpp:1851-1855) writes getParamNorm(kNodeShapeN), which still holds the old type's values, under the new type. On load (controller.cpp:568-576), setter() pushes those values back into the kNodeShape params, so the processor receives them for the new type (processor_params.cpp:880-892). The preset therefore sounds different from what the user heard when saving. Example: change Tube to Fuzz without touching a shape knob, save a preset, recall it, and Fuzz runs with Tube's slot values.

4. The UI is also affected. When the user re-selects the node, copySelectedNodeToProxies (:372-389) copies the stale real values into the proxies, so the knobs then disagree with what the processor is using. Host automation lanes and readbacks of kNodeShape show stale values.

Limits on impact: the host project save goes through processor getState (processor_state.cpp:344), which holds the right slots, so DAW session recall is not affected. A slot is repaired once the user moves its proxy knob. Still, "pick a type, save a preset" is the main preset workflow, so high severity stands. No test covers NodeSelectionController or the kBandDisplayedShape proxies; a grep of plugins/disrumpo/tests found nothing.

findings.title: NodeSelectionController hands every node's shadow storage to node A, so per-type slot memory of nodes B-D is never kept and is saved as defaults
findings.problem: shapeShadowStorage_ is std::array<std::array<ShapeShadowStorage, 4>, kMaxBands>, but each band's controller receives shapeShadowStorage_[b].data(), a pointer to node 0's storage. copyDisplayedTypeToSelectedNode saves and loads through that pointer without indexing by the selected node (visibility_controllers.cpp:430-447).
findings.why_wrong: The shadow has to be per node, just as the processor keeps cache.shapeShadow[node] (processor_params.cpp:845) and the serializer writes shapeShadowStorage_[b][n] for each n (controller.cpp:1857).
findings.consequence: Changing the type of node B, C or D overwrites node A's per-type memory and restores node A's slots into B's UI. Nodes B-D's shadows stay at their loaded or default values and are written that way into user presets. Even if the type-change mirror were fixed, the UI and DSP would disagree after the first type change on a non-A node.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass the whole per-band array (or the band index) to NodeSelectionController and index it with getSelectedNode() in save() and load(). Test: select node B, set slots on Tube, switch B to Fuzz and back to Tube, then assert B's slots are restored and node A's shadow is unchanged.
findings.evidence: controller.cpp:1459-1460 `new NodeSelectionController(this, static_cast<uint8_t>(b), shapeShadowStorage_[b].data());` ; controller.h:355 `std::array<std::array<ShapeShadowStorage, kMaxMorphNodesCtrl>, kMaxBands> shapeShadowStorage_;` ; visibility_controllers.cpp:438 `shapeShadowPtr_->save(oldTypeIdx, currentSlots);` with no node index
verifier_notes: I could not refute this. The source confirms it. controller.cpp:1458-1461 builds each band's NodeSelectionController with `shapeShadowStorage_[b].data()`, and controller.h:355 declares that storage as `std::array<std::array<ShapeShadowStorage, kMaxMorphNodesCtrl>, kMaxBands>`, so `.data()` is a pointer to node 0's ShapeShadowStorage. The constructor stores that pointer unchanged in `shapeShadowPtr_` (visibility_controllers.cpp:216-224; the member is a plain `ShapeShadowStorage*` at visibility_controllers.h:457). copyDisplayedTypeToSelectedNode (visibility_controllers.cpp:413-455) does look up `selectedNode = getSelectedNode()` (line 416), but uses it only for nodeTypeParams_ and nodeTypeId. The shadow calls are `shapeShadowPtr_->save(oldTypeIdx, currentSlots)` (line 438) and `shapeShadowPtr_->load(newTypeIdx, newSlots)` (line 447), with no `[selectedNode]` offset, so they always hit node 0's storage. This is the only place the pointer is used (Grep finds just lines 224/430/438/445/447). Meanwhile the controller keeps and serializes a separate shadow for every node: controller.cpp:586 fills `shapeShadowStorage_[b][n]` from state, and controller.cpp:1857 writes `shapeShadowStorage_[b][n]` for each n. So a type change on node B, C or D saves the currently shown slots into node A's per-type memory and loads node A's memory into the proxies, which copyProxyToSelectedNode then writes to node B. The shadows of B-D are never updated in the controller and get serialized with their loaded or default values. The reported mechanism and consequence match the code, and medium severity fits: the per-type slot memory of nodes B-D is lost and wrong slot values are restored, with no crash and no RT hazard.

I found nothing in the code that guards against this defect, so it stands. At controller.cpp:1459-1460 each band's NodeSelectionController is built with `shapeShadowStorage_[b].data()`. That is a pointer to element [b][0], node A's storage, while controller.h:355 declares the storage per band and per node (`std::array<std::array<ShapeShadowStorage, kMaxMorphNodesCtrl>, kMaxBands>`). The constructor stores the pointer as-is (visibility_controllers.cpp:216-224, `shapeShadowPtr_(shadowStorage)`). copyDisplayedTypeToSelectedNode reads getSelectedNode() at :416, but uses it only for the node-type param ID (:441). The shadow `save(oldTypeIdx, ...)` at :438 and `load(newTypeIdx, ...)` at :447 go through shapeShadowPtr_ with no node offset, so they always reach node 0's storage. A grep for shapeShadowStorage_/shapeShadowPtr_ across the controller directory finds only three other sites: the per-node read in parseComponentState (controller.cpp:586, `shapeShadowStorage_[b][n]`), the per-node write in createComponentStateStream (controller.cpp:1857), and the constructor call above. Nothing else ever updates nodes B-D's controller shadow. createComponentStateStream is the preset manager's state provider (controller.cpp:116-117), so user presets write nodes B-D's shadow exactly as it was last loaded or defaulted. Changing a type on node B or C saves into node A's per-type memory and loads node A's slots back into the proxies. I found no reset, clamp or design comment that makes this intentional, and no test pins the behaviour: grep of plugins/disrumpo/tests finds ShapeShadowStorage only in a comment at multi_node_distortion_test.cpp:241 and NodeSelectionController nowhere. Medium severity fits: it affects UI per-type slot recall and user-preset content, but the processor keeps its own shadow, so audio is not corrupted directly.

The defect is real, and I could not refute it.

Wiring:
- controller.h:355 declares shapeShadowStorage_ as std::array<std::array<ShapeShadowStorage, kMaxMorphNodesCtrl>, kMaxBands>.
- controller.cpp:1458-1461 passes shapeShadowStorage_[b].data() to each band's NodeSelectionController. That is a pointer to node 0's storage only.
- visibility_controllers.cpp:224 stores it as shapeShadowPtr_ (one ShapeShadowStorage*).
- copyDisplayedTypeToSelectedNode (visibility_controllers.cpp:413-455) gets selectedNode from getSelectedNode() (line 416) but uses it only for the type param ID. It calls shapeShadowPtr_->save(oldTypeIdx, currentSlots) at line 438 and shapeShadowPtr_->load(newTypeIdx, newSlots) at line 447 with no node offset. A type change on node B, C or D therefore overwrites node A's per-type memory for the old type, and loads node A's memory into the band proxies.

Comparison with the processor:
- The processor keeps a separate shadow per node: cache.shapeShadow[node] at processor_params.cpp:845-850 and 888.

What reaches saved presets:
- Controller-side shadows for nodes 1-3 are written only by setComponentState (controller.cpp:586). They are never updated by UI type changes.
- createComponentStateStream (controller.cpp:1857-1861) writes shapeShadowStorage_[b][n] for every n. That stream is the PresetManager state provider (controller.cpp:116-118).
- So user presets saved from the preset browser store stale shadows for nodes B-D and a contaminated shadow for node A.
- On load, processor_state.cpp:883 reads those shadows into the processor's per-node shadow, so the corruption carries into the DSP's per-type memory.

How bad it is (it supports medium, not higher):
- The active slot values are saved on their own (controller.cpp:1851-1855), so a reloaded user preset sounds right. The bad memory only shows once the user switches that node's type afterwards.
- The wrong values need a history. ShapeShadowStorage defaults every slot to 0.5, with fixed BitwiseMangler values (morph_node.h:102-113). In a fresh session where no other node was tweaked on the target type, loading from node A's shadow gives the same defaults the correct per-node shadow would. The visible error only appears after another node, or B itself, was on that type with edited slots.
- In-session, the proxies show node A's remembered values for B. kBandDisplayedType and the proxies are UI-only in the processor (processor_params.cpp:975-979), so the UI disagrees with the DSP, which restores from its correct per-node shadow.

There is no audio artifact, crash or NaN. It is a UI/state data-integrity defect that loses user per-type memory in saved presets. Medium is about right, so no severity change.

findings.title: DynamicNodeSelector is never bound to SelectedNode and maps the value inconsistently: with 2 nodes and B selected it highlights A, and the two selectors of a band do not follow each other
findings.problem: The uidesc declares the selector as class="CView", so UIDescription applies only the CView creator attributes (applyCustomViewAttributeValues(result, "CView", ...)). control-tag and listener are never applied, and VST3Editor never binds it. The view observes only ActiveNodes. createCustomView initializes it with setValueNormalized(paramNorm), where paramNorm = k/3 over 4 entries, but CSegmentButton decodes the index as min(N-1, floor(v*N)) over the current N segments.
findings.why_wrong: A selector of a list parameter must decode index = round(norm*3) and must follow external changes to that parameter. Each band has two instances (expanded strip, editor.uidesc:1337; Shape-tab compact, :1293) plus host automation, preset loads and clampSelectedNode, all of which can change SelectedNode.
findings.consequence: In a 2-node band with node B selected, every editor open or Shape-tab visit highlights A (floor(0.333*2) = 0) while the knobs show B. Clicking a node in the expanded strip leaves the Shape-tab selector on the old node, and preset recall or automation of Selected Node is not shown.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the view an IDependent on the SelectedNode parameter and set setSelectedSegment(round(norm*3)) clamped to N-1 in update() and at construction. Alternatively declare class="CSegmentButton" and drop the custom segment logic. Test: with ActiveNodes = 2 and SelectedNode = 1/3, construct the selector and assert getSelectedSegment() == 1; change SelectedNode and assert both selectors follow.
findings.evidence: controller.cpp:1072-1076 `nodeSelector->setValueNormalized(normalized);` ; vstgui csegmentbutton.cpp:529-530 `static_cast<uint32_t> (value * (segments.size ()))` ; dynamic_node_selector.cpp:90 `if (changedParam != activeNodesParam_) return;` ; uidescription.cpp:684-687 applies custom-view attributes for the declared class only ; editor.uidesc:1293 `class="CView" custom-view-name="DynamicNodeSelector"`
verifier_notes:
I traced the claim through the source and it holds.

(1) No binding. editor.uidesc:1293 and :1337 declare the view as class="CView" with custom-view-name="DynamicNodeSelector". In UIDescription::createViewFromNode (vstgui uidescription.cpp:682-687), controller->createView is called first and then only applyCustomViewAttributeValues(result, "CView", ...) runs. CView's creator does not handle control-tag or listener; CControlCreator does that at controlcreator.cpp:81-98. Controller::createCustomView (controller.cpp:1068-1086) calls setTag(selectedNodeParamId) but never setListener; the only setListener calls in the controller are on spectrumDisplay at :964 and morphPad at :1005. VST3Editor::verifyView (vst3editor.cpp:1047) creates a ParameterChangeListener only when control->getListener() == this, so no listener is ever attached to the SelectedNode parameter.

(2) The view only watches ActiveNodes. In dynamic_node_selector.cpp the constructor (:31-35) registers as a dependent of activeNodesParam_ only. update() returns early at :90 unless the changed parameter is ActiveNodes, and only rebuilds segments when the count changes (:96-99). Nothing pushes SelectedNode changes into dynamicNodeSelectors_ or compactNodeSelectors_: the only uses of those arrays are setHighContrastMode (:1450-1451) and deactivate (:1545-1546).

(3) The index mapping is inconsistent. createCustomView calls setValueNormalized(paramNorm) (controller.cpp:1072-1075), where the 4-entry StringListParameter (parameter_registration.cpp:758-764) gives k/3. CSegmentButton::getSelectedSegment uses getSegmentIndex = min(N-1, uint32(value*N)) (csegmentbutton.cpp:133-136, 524-530). With N=2 and node B selected (norm 0.3333), 0.333*2 = 0.67 truncates to 0, so A is highlighted. drawRect (:116, :137) highlights from getSelectedSegment(). The 3- and 4-node cases happen to decode correctly, so the defect is specifically the 2-node case plus the general lack of sync. Clicks encode newSelection/3.0 (:189), which is correct for the parameter, but nothing updates the band's other selector instance. The two instances at editor.uidesc:1293 and :1337 are each created independently.

Small caveat: the "Shape-tab" location of the :1293 instance is the reviewer's description, which I did not verify; it does not affect the defect.

No test covers this; dynamic_node_selector.cpp is only compiled into the tests (tests/CMakeLists.txt:144). Medium severity fits: the wrong selected node is shown in the UI, and audio is not affected.

I could not refute this. Every link in the claim checks out in the code.

(1) Nothing binds the selector to the parameter. The uidesc declares it as class="CView" (editor.uidesc:1293, :1337). UIDescription::createViewFromNode (vstgui uidescription.cpp ~683-687) applies attributes only for the declared class "CView", so control-tag and listener are never applied. DynamicNodeSelector is built with CSegmentButton(size), which leaves the listener null. controller.cpp:1070 sets the tag but no listener. VST3Editor::verifyView (vst3editor.cpp:1047) creates a ParameterChangeListener only when getListener()==this, so the editor never binds the view. The file's own comment says so (dynamic_node_selector.cpp:185 "Custom views don't have automatic VSTGUI ParameterChangeListener binding").

(2) The view never follows SelectedNode. The constructor (dynamic_node_selector.cpp:30-35) adds itself as a dependent of ActiveNodes only. update() returns early for any other parameter (line 90). The controller's dynamicNodeSelectors_ and compactNodeSelectors_ arrays are used only for high-contrast mode and deactivate (controller.cpp:1450-1451, 1545-1546). No code path pushes SelectedNode changes into either view. By contrast, NodeEditorBorder (node_editor_border.cpp:23-31, 74-81) does follow SelectedNode, so the border colour and the selector can disagree.

(3) The index decode is inconsistent. controller.cpp:1072-1075 calls setValueNormalized(paramNorm), where paramNorm = k/3 from a 4-entry StringListParameter (parameter_registration.cpp:757-764). CSegmentButton::getSelectedSegment uses getSegmentIndex = min(N-1, (uint32)(v*N)) (csegmentbutton.cpp:133-135, 523-530). With N=2 and B selected, 0.333*2 = 0.667, which truncates to segment 0, so A is highlighted. The controller's own decode, round(norm*3) at controller.cpp:600, picks B.

(4) The guards upstream do not help. clampSelectedNode only lowers an index that is above the maximum, so it does not touch this case. A UIViewSwitchContainer re-creating the Shape tab only re-runs the same faulty initialisation. No test in plugins/disrumpo/tests mentions DynamicNodeSelector or getSelectedSegment.

Nothing in specs or code comments describes this as intended. The defect is reachable in any 2-node band whose SelectedNode is B, and whenever automation or a preset changes SelectedNode while the editor is open. It is a UI-only defect with no audio impact, so I left the severity at medium.

I confirmed every link in the chain from source.

(1) Binding never happens. editor.uidesc:1293 and :1337 declare the view as `class="CView" custom-view-name="DynamicNodeSelector"`. uidescription.cpp:681-687 then calls applyCustomViewAttributeValues(result, "CView", ...) on the result of createView, so the CControl creator never runs: no control-tag and no listener are applied. VST3Editor::verifyView (vst3editor.cpp:1046-1047) creates a ParameterChangeListener only when `control->getListener() == this`. controller.cpp:1068-1086 calls setTag but never setListener. The SelectedNode parameter therefore never pushes values into either selector.

(2) The view does not watch SelectedNode itself. dynamic_node_selector.cpp:29-35 registers only on ActiveNodes, and update() at :88-92 returns early for any other parameter. The only setSelectedSegment call is at :253, inside rebuildSegments.

(3) The initial value is decoded inconsistently. controller.cpp:1072-1076 passes the parameter's normalized value k/3 to setValueNormalized. csegmentbutton.cpp:523-530 decodes the index as min(N-1, floor(v*N)) and :122-128 encodes it as idx/(N-1). With N=2 and B selected: 0.333*2 = 0.67, floor gives 0, so A is highlighted. N=3 and N=4 decode correctly (float 0.33333334f*3 rounds to 1.0f), so the defect is limited to the 2-node case, as the finding claims.

Impact is real. In the 2-node, B-selected state there is a further effect the finding does not mention. Clicking A is a no-op: csegmentbutton.cpp:325-327 finds newIndex equal to the displayed index, so dynamic_node_selector.cpp:187 sends no edit. The user must click B and then A to select A.

The two instances per band (compact in the BandShapeTab template, expanded in the node-editor strip) are separate objects with no link between them. MorphPad node clicks (morph_pad.cpp:620-624, onNodeSelected), host automation and preset loads all change SelectedNode, and none of them update either selector. NodeEditorBorder (node_editor_border.cpp:23-31, 74-81) does watch SelectedNode, so the border colour and the selector highlight visibly disagree.

The defect is UI-only: no audio effect and no state corruption. Because the selector misleads the user about which node they are editing and blocks selecting A in one state, medium severity stands.

findings.title: Sweep Morph Link is registered with 6 list entries but the processor and serializers use 8 modes
findings.problem: The StringListParameter has 6 strings (None, Linear, Inverse, Ease In, Ease Out, Ease In-Out; stepCount 5). The processor decodes round(v*7) over the 8-entry MorphLinkMode, and parseComponentState and createComponentStateStream also use kMorphLinkModeCount-1 = 7.
findings.why_wrong: The list must match the enum, with names in the enum's order (None, SweepFreq, InverseSweep, EaseIn, EaseOut, HoldRise, Stepped, Custom).
findings.consequence: The host's 'Inverse' selects EaseIn, 'Ease In' selects EaseOut, 'Ease Out' selects Stepped and 'Ease In-Out' selects Custom. InverseSweep and HoldRise cannot be selected. A preset value written as mode/7 is shown as a different list entry. The editor has no control for it (0 uidesc uses), and the custom-curve visibility threshold 0.93 (controller.cpp:1495) targets the wrong entry.
findings.suggested_fix: Register all 8 enum names in enum order, or reduce the enum. Test: for each list index i, assert that the processor decodes MorphLinkMode(i) and that the parse/write round trip is identity.
findings.evidence: parameter_registration.cpp:218-223 six appendString calls ; processor_params.cpp:412 `value * static_cast<float>(kMorphLinkModeCount - 1) + 0.5f` ; plugin_ids.h:640-649 8 modes ; controller.cpp:237 and :1737 use kMorphLinkModeCount - 1
verifier_notes:
The defect is real; the finding's line numbers are off by a few. parameter_registration.cpp:216-228 registers "Sweep Morph Link" as a StringListParameter with six appendString calls (None, Linear, Inverse, Ease In, Ease Out, Ease In-Out), so stepCount is 5. plugin_ids.h:640-653 defines MorphLinkMode with 8 values (None, SweepFreq, InverseSweep, EaseIn, EaseOut, HoldRise, Stepped, Custom), so kMorphLinkModeCount is 8. processor_params.cpp:412 decodes `value * (kMorphLinkModeCount - 1) + 0.5f`, which is round(v*7).

A host list index i sends v = i/5, so the processor gets round(7i/5): 0->None, 1->SweepFreq, 2->EaseIn (2.8), 3->EaseOut (4.2), 4->Stepped (5.6), 5->Custom. "Inverse" therefore selects EaseIn, "Ease In" selects EaseOut and "Ease Out" selects Stepped. InverseSweep and HoldRise can never be selected. That is exactly what the finding says.

The serializers also assume 8 modes:
- controller.cpp:237: setComponentState sets mode/7.
- controller.cpp:1737 with getInt8FromList (1699-1701): it writes round(norm*7).
- processor_state.cpp:95 and :491-493: they write the raw enum and clamp it to 0..7.

A stored mode such as 2 (InverseSweep) becomes 0.2857, which the 6-entry list shows as entry 1, "Linear". In editor.uidesc, "SweepMorphLink" appears once, only as the control-tag definition at line 49; no control uses it. So the parameter is reachable only through host automation or the generic UI, and it is mislabeled there.

One sub-claim is weaker than stated. The 0.93 visibility threshold (controller.cpp:1495) matches norm 1.0, which is list entry 5. The processor maps that entry to Custom, so the custom-curve panel does appear when the processor is in Custom mode. The real problem there is the label, not the threshold.

Severity stays medium. No editor control exposes the parameter, but it is automatable, its labels are wrong, two modes cannot be selected, and preset values are displayed as the wrong entries.

I confirmed the defect from source. The line numbers are slightly off: the block is at parameter_registration.cpp:215-228, not 212-224. That block registers the "Sweep Morph Link" StringListParameter with six appendString calls (None, Linear, Inverse, Ease In, Ease Out, Ease In-Out), which gives stepCount 5. The enum MorphLinkMode at plugin_ids.h:640-650 has 8 values (None, SweepFreq, InverseSweep, EaseIn, EaseOut, HoldRise, Stepped, Custom), and kMorphLinkModeCount = 8 (plugin_ids.h:653).

The processor decodes the value as int(v*7 + 0.5) (processor_params.cpp:412). The controller's state parse divides by kMorphLinkModeCount-1 (controller.cpp:237), and its writer uses getInt8FromList(..., kMorphLinkModeCount-1) (controller.cpp:1737).

With a 6-entry list the normalized values are i/5, so they decode as:
- list 1 (0.2) -> 1, SweepFreq
- list 2 (0.4) -> 2.8 -> 3, EaseIn
- list 3 (0.6) -> 4.2 -> 4, EaseOut
- list 4 (0.8) -> 5.6 -> 6, Stepped
- list 5 (1.0) -> 7, Custom

So InverseSweep (2) and HoldRise (5) cannot be reached from the host, and every label from "Inverse" on names the wrong mode.

The state round trip also loses information. A stored mode 2 becomes 2/7 = 0.286, which the list shows as index round(1.43) = 1, "Linear".

I found nothing that makes this intentional or guards it:
- No comment or spec explains the 6-entry list.
- No test covers the registration: the only test hits are the ID-encoding checks at parameter_encoding_test.cpp:59/69 and the morph_link_test curve-math tests.
- No uidesc control maps the parameter.

The claim about the 0.93 threshold at controller.cpp:1495 is partly overstated. The value 1.0 (the last list entry) does decode to Custom, so the curve editor appears when the processor really is in Custom mode; the problem is only that the entry is labeled "Ease In-Out". The core defect, a list/enum count and order mismatch at the VST boundary, is real and reachable through any host's generic parameter UI and automation. Medium severity is appropriate.

The mismatch is real, but it has no audible effect, so the severity should drop to low.

What I confirmed in the code:
- parameter_registration.cpp:216-228 registers a StringListParameter with 6 strings: None, Linear, Inverse, Ease In, Ease Out, Ease In-Out (stepCount 5).
- plugin_ids.h:640-650 defines 8 MorphLinkMode values: None, SweepFreq, InverseSweep, EaseIn, EaseOut, HoldRise, Stepped, Custom.
- processor_params.cpp:412 decodes the mode as int(v*7+0.5). Running each list index i/5 through that gives: 0->None, 1->SweepFreq, 2->EaseIn(3), 3->EaseOut(4), 4->Stepped(6), 5->Custom(7). InverseSweep and HoldRise cannot be reached. This matches the reviewer's mapping.
- The state paths use mode/7: controller.cpp:237, controller.cpp:1737 (getInt8FromList with maxVal 7) and processor_state.cpp:95/492. A list index survives the save/load round trip as the same displayed entry (for example 3->0.6->4->4/7=0.571->displayed index 3). Only the stored normalized value drifts.

Why the impact is much smaller than claimed:
1. The selected mode never reaches the audio. The only reader of SweepProcessor::morphLinkMode_ is getMorphPosition() (sweep_processor.h:297-309). Grep finds no caller of getMorphPosition( anywhere in plugins/disrumpo/src (the processor directory has no morph-link use). Choosing EaseIn instead of InverseSweep therefore changes nothing in the output: 0 dB, 0 samples.
2. The editor has no control for this parameter. editor.uidesc only declares control-tag SweepMorphLink=3588 at line 49 and no view uses it. The editor's morph-link behaviour comes from the per-band MorphXLink/YLink parameters (visibility_controllers.cpp:175-195), not from this sweep parameter.
3. The custom-curve visibility controller (controller.cpp:1492-1495, tag 9200, threshold 0.93) points at a container that does not exist: 9200 does not appear in editor.uidesc. The wrong threshold has no visible effect.
4. No test covers the parameter beyond the ID encoding (parameter_encoding_test.cpp:59,69).

What remains is cosmetic: in a host's generic editor or automation lane, a parameter that does nothing shows 6 names that do not match the 8-entry enum. It is real dead or inconsistent wiring and worth fixing for consistency, or removing, but it is not a medium-severity audible or state defect.

findings.title: Node param automation and edits from outside the editor never refresh the proxy knobs, so the UI shows stale values and jumps on the next touch
findings.problem: NodeSelectionController subscribes to SelectedNode, the 4 node Type params, DisplayedType and the proxies, but not to the selected node's real Drive/Mix/Tone/Bias/Shape0-9 params. All node params are registered kCanAutomate. When the host automates one, update() is never called and the bound proxy keeps its old value.
findings.why_wrong: The UI is bound only to the proxies (sub_controllers.h:136-160), so the proxies must mirror the real node params in both directions. Only the full-state parse path re-syncs them (controller.cpp:595-613).
findings.consequence: Drive/Tone/shape automation of the selected node is inaudible in the UI, because the knobs do not move. When the user then grabs the knob, copyProxyToSelectedNode sends the stale proxy value plus the drag delta, an audible jump.
findings.suggested_fix: Also addDependent on the selected node's ten-plus-four real params, re-subscribing on node change, and call copySelectedNodeToProxies when one of them changes. Test: with the controller active, setParamNormalized on the selected node's Drive and assert that DisplayedDrive follows.
findings.evidence: visibility_controllers.cpp:231-258 dependents registered: selectedNodeParam_, nodeTypeParams_[0..3], displayedTypeParam_, proxyParams_ only ; :331-335 the only proxy direction from a real param is via a type/selection change
verifier_notes:
I traced the claim through the source and it holds.

1. Subscriptions. The NodeSelectionController constructor (visibility_controllers.cpp:226-258) calls addDependent on exactly four groups: selectedNodeParam_ (:231-234), nodeTypeParams_[0..3] (:236-244), displayedTypeParam_ (:246-251) and proxyParams_ (:253-258). It never subscribes to the real node Drive/Mix/Tone/Bias/Shape0-9 params (the makeNodeParamId(..., kProxyIndexToNodeParam[i]) IDs).

2. update() (:310-338). The proxies are refreshed from the real params only in the selectedNodeParam_ branch (:328-330, copySelectedNodeToProxies). The else branch (:333-335) is reached only for node Type changes, and it calls only copySelectedNodeToDisplayedType.

3. Nothing else refreshes the proxies. Controller does not override setParamNormalized: the grep for Controller:: overrides in controller.cpp/.h shows only initialize, terminate, setComponentState, getState, setState, getMidiControllerAssignment, getParamStringByValue, getParamValueByString and notify. So host automation goes through EditControllerEx1::setParamNormalized and Parameter::changed(), which only notifies dependents. A grep across controller/ finds kProxyIndexToNodeParam used only at controller.cpp:609 (the full-state parse sync, :595-613) and visibility_controllers.cpp:380/:400.

4. The real node params can be automated. parameter_registration.cpp:912-960 registers Drive, Mix, Tone, Bias, Folds, BitDepth and Shape0-9 with kCanAutomate. The proxies (parameter_registration.cpp:804-822) are kNoFlags, so the host cannot automate them, and the UI is bound to them (sub_controllers.h:137-157).

5. The jump on the next touch. copyProxyToSelectedNode (:392-410) writes the proxy's current value (stale value plus the drag delta) to the real param with editParam, i.e. beginEdit/setParamNormalized/performEdit/endEdit. That overwrites the automated value with a jump.

Result: when the host automates the selected node's Drive, Tone or Shape, the displayed knob does not move, and the first user drag snaps the value. Medium severity fits: the UI desyncs and an audible jump follows a user action, but audio is not corrupted without that action.

Confirmed from source. The NodeSelectionController constructor (visibility_controllers.cpp:226-262) calls addDependent only on selectedNodeParam_ (233), nodeTypeParams_[0..3] (242), displayedTypeParam_ (250) and proxyParams_ (256). deactivate() (289-308) undoes exactly that set and nothing more. In update() (310-338), copySelectedNodeToProxies runs only when selectedNodeParam_ changes (328-330). Any other dependent change goes to copySelectedNodeToDisplayedType (334), which reaches only the type proxy.

I looked for a path that would guard this and found none. controller.cpp does not override setParamNormalized; its overridden entry points are only initialize, terminate, setComponentState, getState, setState, getMidiControllerAssignment, getParamStringByValue, getParamValueByString and notify (lines 95-1960). Grepping every addDependent under src/controller turns up no subscriber on node Drive/Mix/Tone/Bias/Shape params. The only other place that copies real values into the proxies is the state-parse path (controller.cpp:606-613).

The real params are automatable. For example node Drive is registered with kCanAutomate at parameter_registration.cpp:912-915. The UI controls bind to the proxy tags (sub_controllers.h:137-157). So when the host automates a node param through setParamNormalized, the proxy knob does not move. When the user then grabs the knob, copyProxyToSelectedNode (392-411) writes the stale proxy value plus the drag delta to the real param, and that is an audible jump.

Nothing pins this. No test under plugins/disrumpo/tests mentions NodeSelectionController or DisplayedDrive. I found no comment or spec note calling one-way sync a design decision.

I could not refute this. The defect is real, and the consequence is as claimed.

1) What the controller listens to. The NodeSelectionController constructor (visibility_controllers.cpp:226-258) calls addDependent only on these params:
- selectedNodeParam_
- nodeTypeParams_[0..3]
- displayedTypeParam_
- the 14 proxyParams_

It never subscribes to the selected node's real Drive, Mix, Tone, Bias or Shape0-9 params.

2) What update() does (visibility_controllers.cpp:326-335). Only three changes copy real values into the proxies, through copySelectedNodeToProxies (lines 372-389):
- a change of SelectedNode
- a type change, through the else branch (line 334, which only calls copySelectedNodeToDisplayedType)
- a proxy edit, which goes the other way (copyProxyToSelectedNode)

3) No other path catches it.
- Controller has no setParamNormalized override. A grep for "Controller::setParamNormalized" in src/controller found nothing.
- The only other site that syncs the proxies is the state parse at controller.cpp:595-613, which runs on setComponentState / preset load.
- Nothing else in src references kProxyIndexToNodeParam: grep shows only controller.cpp:609 and plugin_ids.h.
- No test touches DisplayedDrive or NodeSelectionController: the grep of tests/ was empty.

4) Automation can only land on the real params. parameter_registration.cpp:804-822 registers every Displayed* proxy with kNoFlags, so hosts do not offer automation lanes for them. The real node params at :912-934 (and the shape params after them) are kCanAutomate, and the host shows them as named lanes such as "B1 N1 Shape 0". So every host automation, and every generic-editor or remote edit of the selected node, reaches the controller only through setParamNormalized on the real param ID. The dependents of that Parameter are notified, but the NodeSelectionController is not one of them, so the proxy, and with it the knob bound to it (sub_controllers.h:134-137), stays stale.
