5) The jump on the next touch. copyProxyToSelectedNode (visibility_controllers.cpp:392-408) writes the proxy's absolute value to the real param through editParam, which does beginEdit, performEdit and endEdit. A drag that starts from the stale knob position therefore moves the real param from its automated value to the stale value plus the drag delta.
- The jump can be as large as Drive's full 0-10 range, or Tone's 200-8000 Hz range.
- The host gets it as a touch on the real ID, so in touch or latch mode it is recorded too.

6) Scope. Only the selected node of each band is shown, so the defect is limited to that node's 14 params. That is still the main editing surface. The defect produces no NaN and does not break state. Medium severity is about right: the UI is wrong during a common workflow (automating Drive), and touching the knob causes an audible jump of up to the full parameter range. That is more than cosmetic, but it is not a crash or a corruption.

findings.title: Global keyboard hook swallows arrow, Tab, Escape and (after one Tab) Space keys for every focused view, which breaks text entry on Linux and acts on hidden controls behind the preset browser
findings.problem: The frame keyboard hook marks every arrow key as consumed (handleArrowKey always returns true), every Tab, Escape whenever a callback exists (always, controller.cpp:1408-1415), and Space whenever focusedBandIndex_ >= 0. focusedBandIndex_ is a private counter, not the real focus view. setActiveBandCount has no caller, so Tab cycles over the band count at open time.
findings.why_wrong: CFrame dispatches to keyboard hooks before the focus view (cframe.cpp:544-552). On Linux, CTextEdit uses VSTGUI's GenericTextEdit (x11frame.cpp:775-778), which takes its keys through that same dispatch. The preset browser's hook, registered later and therefore called first, consumes only Escape and Enter.
findings.consequence: On Linux the arrow keys and Tab do nothing in the preset search field and the Save-preset name field. After one Tab, typing a space in a preset name toggles a band's bypass instead (and bypass is itself a processor no-op). With the browser open, arrow keys change a hidden focused control behind the overlay.
findings.suggested_fix: Return early (not consumed) when the focus view is a CTextEdit or lies inside an open modal overlay; consume arrows only when adjustFocusedParameter actually edited; derive the band from the focus view; call setActiveBandCount from BandCountDisplayController. Test: with a CTextEdit focused, assert that onKeyboardEvent leaves event.consumed false for Left, Space and Tab.
findings.evidence: keyboard_shortcut_handler.cpp:94-95 `adjustFocusedParameter(stepFraction); return true;` ; :73 Tab always true ; :77 Space keyed on focusedBandIndex_ ; grep setActiveBandCount callers: none ; vstgui cframe.cpp:544-546 hooks first
verifier_notes: The finding's main mechanism is wrong. It says Disrumpo's frame hook runs before the Linux text edit. It does not. CFrame::dispatchKeyboardEventToHooks (extern/vst3sdk/vstgui4/vstgui/lib/cframe.cpp:1581-1589) walks the hooks with forEachReverse, so the hook registered last runs first. The finding relies on this order itself for the preset browser. On Linux the platform text edit is STBTextEditView (generictextedit.cpp:51-53), and it is itself an IKeyboardHook. It registers on the frame in attached() (generictextedit.cpp:484-489), i.e. only when a CTextEdit takes focus and builds its platform edit. That happens after Disrumpo registers its handler at editor open (controller.cpp:1417), so the text edit runs before KeyboardShortcutHandler. STBTextEditView::onKeyboardEvent (generictextedit.cpp:332-359) maps Space to 0x20 and arrows to virtual keys, and sets event.consumed = true whenever stb_textedit_key changes the edit state (callSTB, :257-266). So typing a space inserts a space and never reaches handleSpace (keyboard_shortcut_handler.cpp:76-82). Arrows that move the cursor are consumed by the text edit, not by handleArrowKey (:84-96). The claimed results ("arrow keys do nothing in the preset search/save field", "a space in a preset name toggles bypass") do not follow from the code. What is left is minor. (a) Tab: STB returns without consuming it (:341-343), and handleTab (:70-74) consumes it and calls advanceNextFocusView. CFrame's own unconsumed-Tab handling would also advance focus, so this is close to the default. (b) An arrow at a text boundary, or a space typed into a field already at max length, falls through to Disrumpo's hook. adjustFocusedParameter (:146-161) then only acts if the focused CTextEdit's tag is a registered parameter. (c) setActiveBandCount (:58-60) really has no caller: grep finds only its declaration and definition. That is a separate small wiring gap (Tab cycles over the band count taken at open, controller.cpp:1401-1406), not the text-entry defect claimed. (d) The "hidden control behind the browser" scenario is not shown. It needs a focused CControl with a parameter tag to stay focused while the browser is open (PresetBrowserView::open, preset_browser_view.cpp:64-87, does not change focus), and the finding never establishes that state. The headline defect is refuted from source.

I could not refute this. The source confirms the defect.

1. The hook swallows the keys. In keyboard_shortcut_handler.cpp:84-96, handleArrowKey returns true whether or not adjustFocusedParameter edited anything; that function returns early at :151/:154 when the focus view is not a CControl or has no matching parameter. handleTab (:70-74) always returns true. handleSpace (:76-82) depends only on the private focusedBandIndex_ counter and never looks at the real focus view. handleEscape (:98-104) returns true whenever a callback exists. controller.cpp:1408-1415 sets that callback whenever midiCCManager_ exists, so Escape is consumed even when MIDI learn is not active. setActiveBandCount (:58) has no caller anywhere in plugins/; the handler only gets the band count once, at open (controller.cpp:1401-1406).

2. Hooks run before the focused view. In cframe.cpp:540-546, dispatchKeyboardEvent calls dispatchKeyboardEventToHooks and returns if the event was consumed. Hooks are called newest first (cframe.cpp:1583, forEachReverse) and the loop stops once one of them consumes the event.

3. The Linux text-edit path. In x11frame.cpp:775-778, createPlatformTextEdit returns a GenericTextEdit. In generictextedit.cpp:484-489, the STBTextEditView registers itself as a frame keyboard hook. Its onKeyboardEvent (:270-281) first calls CTextEdit::platformOnKeyboardEvent, and ctextedit.cpp:300-304 sends the event back through frame->platformOnEvent, so all frame hooks run again. The recursion guard (:275) skips only the STB view itself, which means Disrumpo's hook does run. Once it marks the event consumed, the STB view returns at :280-281 without passing the key to stb_textedit_key. Result: on Linux, arrow keys never move the cursor in a text field, and a Space typed after one Tab toggles a band's bypass instead of inserting a space.

Windows may be affected too: win32textedit.cpp:199-212 sends virtual keys with character==0 through the same platformOnKeyboardEvent path. I did not check whether Space arrives there with character 0.

4. Nothing upstream stops this. PresetBrowserView::onKeyboardEvent (preset_browser_view.cpp:195-230) consumes only Escape and Return/Enter, so arrows, Tab and Space go on to Disrumpo's hook while the browser is open. The handler has no check for a CTextEdit focus view or an open modal overlay.

Intent: FR-010..016 do specify Tab, Space and arrow shortcuts, but nothing there or in the code comments says text fields should lose those keys, and the handler is never told the current band count. I found no guard that would make the claimed behaviour unreachable. Severity medium is appropriate: it breaks text entry and edits hidden controls, but it does not touch the audio thread.

Two things check out. keyboard_shortcut_handler.cpp:84-96 always returns true for arrow keys, even when adjustFocusedParameter (146-161) returns early and edits nothing. Tab always returns true (70-74). The hook is registered once in didOpen (controller.cpp:1406-1417), and setActiveBandCount has no caller. CFrame::dispatchKeyboardEvent (cframe.cpp:544-546) does run hooks before the focus view, and dispatchKeyboardEventToHooks calls them newest first (forEachReverse, cframe.cpp:1583).

The headline consequence, broken text entry on Linux, cannot happen. The finding assumes GenericTextEdit gets its keys after the focus-view dispatch. It does not. STBTextEditView registers its own frame keyboard hook in attached() (generictextedit.cpp:484-489). It is attached when the CTextEdit takes focus (GenericTextEdit constructor, :193-196), which is always after Disrumpo's hook was registered in didOpen. So it runs before Disrumpo's handler. Its onKeyboardEvent (:270-360) first passes the key to the CTextEdit callback (which handles Enter and Escape). It maps Space to 0x20 (:336-339) and sends arrows to stb_textedit_key, setting consumed whenever the edit state changes (:358-359). A space typed in the preset name or search field is therefore inserted and never reaches handleSpace, so bypass is not toggled. Arrows that move the cursor are consumed before Disrumpo sees them.

Only edge cases reach Disrumpo's hook: Left at position 0, or another arrow that changes nothing. Then the focus view is the CTextEdit, so adjustFocusedParameter acts on its tag, which in practice is not a parameter, and nothing happens. Tab is explicitly not consumed by STB (:341-343). Disrumpo then advances focus, which is the same thing stock VSTGUI does on Tab (cframe.cpp:574-580). Tab leaving the field is not a regression.

What remains: arrow keys are swallowed whenever no text field consumes them. That blocks arrow navigation in the preset browser's list, because the browser hook only handles Escape and Enter (preset_browser_view.cpp:195-205). And if a control behind the overlay holds focus (clicking a control focuses it, cviewcontainer.cpp:1076-1079), arrows can edit that hidden control. These are minor UX defects, with no audio or text-entry impact, so the severity should drop from medium to low.

findings.title: Most sweep controls and the custom-curve editor are absent from the editor
findings.problem: No uidesc control binds to SweepIntensity, SweepFalloff, SweepMorphLink, SweepLFOWaveform, SweepLFOSync, SweepLFONoteValue, SweepEnvSensitivity or Band.NodeBias (0 control-tag uses each). The CustomCurveEditor custom view (controller.cpp:1123-1246) and its 9200 container are never instantiated, so customCurveVisController_ (controller.cpp:1492-1495) watches nothing.
findings.why_wrong: The processor consumes all of these, and the spec defines intensity 0-200%, falloff, LFO shape/sync and the custom curve as user features. A UI that cannot reach them leaves them at their mismatched defaults (intensity default 50% = 1.0 vs DSP 0.5; falloff Hard vs DSP Smooth).
findings.consequence: Users cannot set sweep intensity, falloff, LFO waveform or tempo sync, or envelope sensitivity, node bias, or a custom morph-link curve from the plugin UI; only the host's generic parameter list reaches them. The custom-curve code in the controller is dead code.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the missing controls to the sweep row and the band panel via XSLT, and add the CustomCurveEditor view with its marker, or remove the dead curve plumbing. Test: a uidesc inventory test asserting every automatable sweep param has a control.
findings.evidence: grep -c 'control-tag="SweepIntensity"' etc. = 0 for each listed tag ; grep -c CustomCurveEditor editor.uidesc = 0 ; sweep row controls at editor.uidesc:616-634 cover only Enable/Freq/Width/LFO enable,rate,depth/Env enable,attack,release
verifier_notes:
I could not refute this. The source supports the claim.

- **Sweep row:** The only sweep controls in plugins/disrumpo/resources/editor.uidesc are at lines 614-638. They bind SweepEnable, SweepFrequency, SweepWidth, SweepLFOEnable, SweepLFORate, SweepLFODepth, SweepEnvEnable, SweepEnvAttack and SweepEnvRelease, plus ModPanelVisible.
- **Missing sweep tags:** SweepIntensity, SweepMorphLink, SweepFalloff, SweepLFOWaveform, SweepLFOSync, SweepLFONoteValue and SweepEnvSensitivity are declared as control-tags at lines 48-60, but no view uses them. A grep for numeric tags 358x-361x as control-tag also finds nothing.
- **Band.NodeBias:** It is declared at uidesc:281 and remapped in sub_controllers.h:145. No view uses control-tag="Band.NodeBias". The "Bias" labels in the per-type templates (e.g. uidesc:895-896, 904-905) sit on Band.NodeShape0, which is a shape slot, not kNodeBias.
- **CustomCurveEditor:** The string appears 0 times in editor.uidesc, so the factory at controller.cpp:1123-1144 (tag 9200) is never called. The ContainerVisibilityController at controller.cpp:1492-1495 watches tag 9200, which has no container.
- **Only one uidesc:** resources/editor.uidesc is the only uidesc file, and no custom view creates these controls in code. spectrum_display.cpp only draws an intensity overlay.
- **Processor uses them:** processor_params.cpp:402-487 handles SweepIntensity, MorphLink, Falloff, LFOWaveform, LFOSync and EnvSensitivity, and line 868 handles kNodeBias.

So these features can only be reached through the host's generic parameter list. I did not verify the side claim about default mismatches (intensity, falloff), but it does not affect the main defect. Medium severity is appropriate: features are missing from the UI, but audio is not affected.

The finding holds, apart from one sub-claim that is out of scope by design.

What I confirmed in plugins/disrumpo/resources/editor.uidesc:
- The sweep row at lines 614-634 binds only these control-tags: SweepEnable, SweepFrequency, SweepWidth, SweepLFOEnable, SweepLFORate, SweepLFODepth, SweepEnvEnable, SweepEnvAttack, SweepEnvRelease and ModPanelVisible.
- Grepping the whole file finds SweepIntensity, SweepFalloff, SweepMorphLink, SweepLFOWaveform, SweepLFOSync, SweepLFONoteValue and SweepEnvSensitivity only as `<control-tag name=...>` declarations (lines 48-60). No view uses any of them as a control-tag.
- Band.NodeBias is declared at line 281 and resolved in sub_controllers.h:145, and B*N*Bias tags are declared at lines 176-246. No view binds any of them: a grep for control-tag="Band.NodeBias" or control-tag="B[0-9]N[0-9]Bias" returns 0. The "Bias" labels at lines 895 and 904 sit over Band.NodeShape0 knobs, which are per-type shape slots, not NodeBias.
- CustomCurveEditor and 9200 never appear in the uidesc. The controller still creates the view (controller.cpp:1123-1144, which builds CustomCurveEditor with tag 9200) and installs a visibility controller on 9200 (controller.cpp:1492-1495). That controller therefore watches nothing.

Why this is a real gap:
- The parameters are registered and automatable (parameter_registration.cpp:207, 218, 233, 252, 269, 298) and are saved, loaded and set in controller.cpp:232-278 and 1735-1747.
- specs-overview.md:279-291 (FR-SWEEP-002/003) defines Intensity 0-200%, Falloff Sharp/Smooth and the morph link modes as user parameters.
- tasks-overview.md:204-211 (T8.4 "Add sweep UI controls") explicitly lists an "Intensity knob" and a "Link mode selector" as UI controls.
- None of these are reachable from the editor.

Context that weakens part of the finding:
- roadmap.md:103 lists "Custom curve editor" as Out of Scope (v1.0) ("Use preset linking curves only"), and tasks-overview.md:204 marks "Custom curve (future)". The missing curve editor is therefore a documented deferral; the leftover controller plumbing is dead code, not a wiring defect.
- The ui-mockups.md:53-54 Level-1 sweep box shows only Enable/Freq/Width. The Level-2 mockup (ui-mockups.md:61-82) shows per-node "Drive(●) Bias(◯)" knobs (lines 67, 71) and a "Link" selector under the morph sliders (line 77, "Link: [Sweep Freq ▼]"), so Node Bias and the link selector were meant to have UI.
- I found no spec text or code comment that hides intensity, falloff, morph link, LFO waveform, sync or note value, env sensitivity or node bias on purpose.

Severity: medium stands. The core claim is confirmed for 8 automatable parameters with no UI. Only the custom-curve sub-claim is out of scope by design. I did not check the side claim about default mismatches.

The defect is real, and medium is the right severity.

1. **The tags are declared but no control uses them.** In `plugins/disrumpo/resources/editor.uidesc`, `SweepIntensity` (3587), `SweepMorphLink` (3588), `SweepFalloff` (3589), `SweepLFOWaveform` (3602), `SweepLFOSync` (3604), `SweepLFONoteValue` (3605) and `SweepEnvSensitivity` (3619) appear only as `<control-tag>` definitions at lines 48-60. `Band.NodeBias` (50019) appears only at line 281. A grep for each name, and for each numeric tag value, finds no other occurrence. No view uses `control-tag="...Bias"`.

2. **The sweep row lacks them.** It sits at `editor.uidesc:616-634` and binds only `SweepEnable`, `SweepFrequency`, `SweepWidth`, `SweepLFOEnable`, `SweepLFORate`, `SweepLFODepth`, `SweepEnvEnable`, `SweepEnvAttack`, `SweepEnvRelease` and `ModPanelVisible`.

3. **The curve editor is never built.** `CustomCurveEditor` and `9200` each occur 0 times in the uidesc. The `createCustomView` branch at `controller.cpp:1123-1246` therefore never runs. The `customCurveVisController_` set up at `controller.cpp:1492-1495` watches container tag 9200, which does not exist.

4. **No other path offers these controls.** The views and the keyboard handler only read intensity and falloff to draw: `SweepIndicator` at `controller.cpp:1277-1298` and `spectrum_display.cpp:608`. Nothing in them edits these parameters.

5. **The processor uses them,** so they matter to the sound: `processor_params.cpp:402` (`kSweepIntensity`), `:439` (`kSweepLFOWaveform`), `:451` (`kSweepLFOSync`), `:487` (`kSweepEnvSensitivity`) and `:868` (`kNodeBias`). They are registered as automatable in `parameter_registration.cpp:207`, `:218`, `:233`, `:252` and `:269`.

**Impact:** in any host, the plugin's own editor cannot set sweep intensity, falloff, morph link (and so the custom curve), LFO waveform, sync or note value, envelope sensitivity, or per-node bias. They are still reachable through the host's generic parameter list, automation and presets. That makes this a real missing-feature gap, but it does not corrupt audio, so medium stands.

One caveat: the reviewer's side remark that intensity runs 0-200% does not match the code. The parameter is registered as 0-100 with default 50 (`parameter_registration.cpp:207-210`). This does not change whether the controls are missing.

findings.title: The spectrum Tier-3 fallback is disabled for good after the first editor close
findings.problem: willClose sets sharedDisplay_ = nullptr. The pointer is assigned only in setComponentState, from the instance-id trailer. The didOpen timer requires sharedDisplay_ != nullptr before activating the SharedDisplayBridge fallback.
findings.why_wrong: The bridge lookup refers to processor-owned FIFOs that outlive the editor. Clearing it on editor close discards a lookup that only a host state restore can redo.
findings.consequence: On hosts where DataExchange does not deliver (the reason Tier 3 exists), the spectrum analyzer works the first time the editor opens and stays blank after every reopen in the same session.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep sharedDisplay_ across editor sessions (clear it in terminate), or redo the lookup by instanceId_ in didOpen. Test: lifecycle test with DataExchange disabled: open, close, reopen, tick the timer more than 10 times, and assert that the spectrum display has FIFOs.
findings.evidence: controller.cpp:1581 `sharedDisplay_ = nullptr;` (willClose) ; :645-646 only assignment, in setComponentState ; :1476 `if (!dataExchangeActive_ && sharedDisplay_ && !spectrumDataAvailable_)`
verifier_notes:
Confirmed from source. The only place sharedDisplay_ gets a value is setComponentState (controller.cpp:637-651). It reads the kInstanceIdMarker trailer that processor_state.cpp:355 writes and calls SharedDisplayBridge::lookupInstance(instanceId_) at :645-646. A grep of plugins/disrumpo/src finds no other assignment and no other lookupInstance call. Nothing in controller.cpp's notify path delivers the instance id.

willClose sets sharedDisplay_ = nullptr (:1581), along with dataExchangeActive_ = false and fallbackTickCounter_ = 0 (:1582-1583). instanceId_ is not cleared, so the id survives but nothing uses it again.

didOpen (:1354-1356) only resets editorClosing_ and spectrumDataAvailable_. It does not redo the lookup. The timer created in didOpen (:1466-1490) activates Tier 3 only if `!dataExchangeActive_ && sharedDisplay_ && !spectrumDataAvailable_` (:1476). Once the editor has closed, sharedDisplay_ is null, so on any reopen the fallback cannot wire setSpectrumFIFOs/startAnalysis (:1482-1486). The only way to repopulate it is another setComponentState, which hosts normally call on state load or restore, not on editor reopen.

The result: on a host where DataExchange never delivers (dataExchangeActive_ is set only at :1942), the spectrum works on the first open and stays blank on every later open in the session. Innexus has the same pattern (controller.cpp:1183 and controller_state.cpp:536). That points to a shared copy-paste pattern, not deliberate per-plugin design.

On the fix: keeping the raw pointer past processor terminate could dangle. Redoing the lookup by instanceId_ in didOpen is the safe version, but that is about the fix and does not affect whether the defect exists. Medium severity fits: the impact is limited to Tier-3 hosts and is visual only.

I could not refute this through context. The only place sharedDisplay_ is assigned is setComponentState (controller.cpp:637-651). It is filled from the instance-id trailer through SharedDisplayBridge::lookupInstance. A grep for `sharedDisplay_ =` and `lookupInstance` across plugins/disrumpo finds no other assignment: nothing in didOpen, notify or initialize sets it. willClose clears it unconditionally (controller.cpp:1581), alongside dataExchangeActive_=false and fallbackTickCounter_=0 (1582-1583). didOpen (1354-1511) resets spectrumDataAvailable_=false (1356) and creates a new timer. That timer's Tier-3 branch needs `!dataExchangeActive_ && sharedDisplay_ && !spectrumDataAvailable_` (1476), so after the first close it never fires again unless the host calls setComponentState again. Hosts do not normally do that when an editor reopens. Nothing suggests the clear is intentional for lifetime reasons. The struct it points at is processor-owned and lives as long as the processor instance: it is wired in the Processor constructor (processor.cpp:46-49), registered in initialize (processor.cpp:69-70) and unregistered only in terminate (processor.cpp:81), or re-registered when the processor's setState swaps the id (processor_state.cpp:911-914). So the editor lifecycle gives no reason to drop the lookup. No test pins this behaviour: data_exchange_spectrum_test.cpp only mentions Tier 3 in a comment (line 285), with no open/close/reopen test. Innexus has the same pattern (innexus controller.cpp:1183, controller_state.cpp:536), so this looks like copied code, not a documented design decision. The defect only shows on same-process hosts where DataExchange does not deliver, which is exactly the case Tier 3 exists for. Medium severity stands.

The defect is real. I could not refute it from source.

- The only assignment of `sharedDisplay_` is in setComponentState at controller.cpp:645-646. It runs a `SharedDisplayBridge::lookupInstance(instanceId_)` lookup using the instance-id trailer read at :641-642. A grep of plugins/disrumpo/src finds no other assignment.
- willClose clears it at controller.cpp:1581 (`sharedDisplay_ = nullptr;`). It also resets `dataExchangeActive_` (:1582) and `fallbackTickCounter_` (:1583).
- didOpen resets `spectrumDataAvailable_ = false` (:1356). The timer gate at :1476 is `!dataExchangeActive_ && sharedDisplay_ && !spectrumDataAvailable_`, so on every reopen it fails on the null `sharedDisplay_`. The FIFOs are never wired again (:1482-1486) unless the host calls setComponentState again.
- The bridge entry belongs to the processor and outlives the editor. processor.cpp:69 calls `registerInstance` in initialize, and processor.cpp:81 calls `unregisterInstance` in terminate. processor_state.cpp:911-913 re-registers on setState. So the cached pointer stays valid across editor sessions, and clearing it on close throws away a lookup that only a state restore can redo. instanceId_ survives willClose, so a lookup in didOpen would be cheap.
- Innexus has the same pattern: controller_state.cpp:536-537 assigns it and controller.cpp:1183 clears it. This is worth noting for the fix plan.

Why I downgrade the impact:
1. Only the spectrum display is affected (a visual feature). There is no effect on audio, state or parameters.
2. It only triggers on hosts where neither DataExchange nor the SDK's IMessage fallback delivers spectrum blocks. When DataExchange works, the handler at :1940-1945 sets `dataExchangeActive_` and `spectrumDataAvailable_` again on every open, so mainstream hosts are unaffected.
3. Any host state restore (reloading the project or a preset that calls setComponentState) recovers the display.

On the niche host class the claimed consequence holds exactly: the spectrum works on the first open and is blank on every later open in the same session. Low severity fits better than medium.

findings.title: Spectrum dividers ignore crossover parameter changes, and band-count changes redistribute them in the view only
findings.problem: The dividers are read from the parameters once, in createCustomView. No dependent observes the crossover parameters afterwards. BandCountDisplayController calls setNumBands, which overwrites crossoverFreqs_ with an even log spread inside the view without touching the parameters. The processor applies its own redistribution in CrossoverNetwork::setBandCount, and the controller parameters keep their old values.
findings.why_wrong: The display must reflect the parameter and processor state. A view-local redistribution creates a third crossover state that neither the parameters nor the processor share.
findings.consequence: After automation, a preset load or a band-count change with the editor open, the dividers show frequencies that are neither the processor's nor the parameters'. The next drag of one divider writes one value while the others stay inconsistent, and the next preset save writes the stale parameters.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an IDependent on the 3 crossover params that calls setCrossoverFrequency with the same mapping as the processor. Remove the redistribution from setNumBands, or push the redistributed values to the params with begin/perform/endEdit. Test: setParamNormalized on a crossover and assert the display moves; change the band count and assert display == params.
findings.evidence: spectrum_display.cpp:53-63 setNumBands rewrites crossoverFreqs_ ; visibility_controllers.cpp:57-59 BandCountDisplayController -> setNumBands ; grep for controller callers of setCrossoverFrequency: only createCustomView (controller.cpp:951)
verifier_notes: I traced the code and the defect is real. spectrum_display.cpp:51-67: setNumBands(n) replaces crossoverFreqs_[0..n-2] with an even log2 spread between kMinFreqHz and kMaxFreqHz. It ignores what the parameters say. The view's setCrossoverFrequency (69-74) has one caller in the controller tree, createCustomView (controller.cpp:947-953). That call runs once, when the view is built. Nothing observes the three crossover params 0x0F10-0x0F12 afterwards. A grep of plugins/disrumpo/src for makeCrossoverParamId finds only these: parameter_registration.cpp:153 (registration), controller.cpp:208 (setComponentState setter), controller.cpp:948 (createCustomView), controller.cpp:1729 (preset write) and visibility_controllers.cpp:641 (the CrossoverDragBridge write path). No IDependent is registered on them. The other spectrumDisplay_ users at controller.cpp:1367/1371/1447/1464 are band count, mode, contrast and sweep, none of them crossover. BandCountDisplayController::update (visibility_controllers.cpp:51-61) calls setNumBands. As a result, a band-count change with the editor open moves the dividers to the view-local spread. On the processor side, processor_params.cpp:344-345 calls CrossoverNetwork::setBandCount. That redistribution (crossover_network.h:111-122, 274-297, 301+) keeps the existing crossovers and puts new ones at the midpoints of the largest log gaps, which differs from the view's even spread. It also does not write the param values back. Crossover automation, or a preset load reaching setComponentState (controller.cpp:203-213) while the editor is open, updates the params and the processor (processor_params.cpp:984-993) but not the dividers. There is a knock-on effect: SweepVisualizationController::updateSpectrumBandIntensities (visibility_controllers.cpp:597-603) reads the band centres from the view's getCrossoverFrequency, so the sweep intensity overlay is computed from the wrong edges as well. A later divider drag (CrossoverDragBridge, 637-654) writes only the dragged index, so the other dividers stay out of step. The finding's claim that preset save "writes the stale parameters" is a slight overreach: the params are the controller's authoritative state, and the processor/param divergence after setBandCount is a separate, processor-side issue. The display defect itself is confirmed exactly as described.

I could not refute this from source. The display gets the crossover parameters exactly once, in createCustomView: controller.cpp:947-953 loops over makeCrossoverParamId(i) and calls setCrossoverFrequency. That is the only controller caller of setCrossoverFrequency; I grepped for both the method name and makeCrossoverParamId across src/controller. There is also an ordering problem at creation. setNumBands runs first (controller.cpp:944), and setCrossoverFrequency drops any index >= numBands_-1 (spectrum_display.cpp:70). So if the editor opens at 1 or 2 bands, the higher crossover params never reach the view at all.

No IDependent watches the crossover params. BandCountDisplayController (visibility_controllers.cpp:23-61) observes only the band-count param. SweepVisualizationController (:461-502) observes the sweep params and the mod-frequency output only. CrossoverDragBridge (:634-654) only goes from the view to the params. So automation, preset load or setComponentState (controller.cpp:203-208 writes the crossover params) never moves the dividers while the editor is open.

On a band-count change, BandCountDisplayController::update calls setNumBands (visibility_controllers.cpp:59). setNumBands (spectrum_display.cpp:51-64) overwrites every active crossoverFreqs_ entry with an even log2 spread and never writes the params. The processor does something different. processor_params.cpp:339-346 calls CrossoverNetwork::setBandCount, which per crossover_network.h:111-122 and :274-297 keeps the existing crossovers and inserts new ones at log midpoints of the largest gaps (FR-011a/b). It reinitialises from scratch only when going up from 1 band. That gives three diverging states: the view's even spread, the processor's preserved and inserted values, and the unchanged params. No code comment or spec marks the view redistribution as intentional. The FR-009 log-spread comment is on the processor and is overridden there by FR-011a/b.

There is one more knock-on effect. SweepVisualizationController::updateSpectrumBandIntensities reads display->getCrossoverFrequency (visibility_controllers.cpp:601-602), so the sweep band-intensity overlay is computed from the stale or redistributed view values as well. I found no guard, no reset and no test that keeps the view in sync. The impact stays in the UI and in the save path, since the parameters remain the source of truth for the saved state, so medium severity is appropriate.

I confirmed this from source. (1) In the controller, setCrossoverFrequency is called only from createCustomView (controller.cpp:947-953). No IDependent watches the crossover params: the only crossover-related controller objects are CrossoverDragBridge (view to param, visibility_controllers.cpp:637-654) and parameter registration. So automating a crossover param, setParamNormalized from a preset or setComponentState with the editor open (controller.cpp:203-208 writes the crossover params), or a keyboard shortcut never moves the dividers. (2) BandCountDisplayController::update (visibility_controllers.cpp:51-60) calls SpectrumDisplay::setNumBands, which overwrites crossoverFreqs_ with an even log2 spread over kMinFreqHz..kMaxFreqHz (spectrum_display.cpp:51-64). It ignores the params entirely. (3) The processor does something else again. processor_params.cpp:344-345 calls CrossoverNetwork::setBandCount, which redistributes: on a decrease it keeps the lowest N-1 frequencies, on an increase it keeps the existing ones and inserts new ones at the midpoints of the largest log gaps (crossover_network.h:111-122, 274-339). It does not re-read the param values, and setCrossoverFrequency drops indices at or above numBands-1 (crossover_network.h:128). So view, params and processor can hold three different crossover sets, as the finding says. Example: 3 bands with crossovers at 300 Hz and 3 kHz, change to 4 bands. The view shows an even spread of about 200 / 2k / 20k-log points. The processor keeps 300 / 3k and adds one midpoint. The params keep their old values. Impact is wider than claimed. drawCrossoverDividers and drawCrossoverLabels (spectrum_display.cpp:438-503) show the wrong Hz text. Band-region coloring (spectrum_display.cpp:316, 421-422) is wrong too, and SweepVisualizationController computes per-band sweep intensities from display->getCrossoverFrequency (visibility_controllers.cpp:601-602), so the sweep intensity overlay is wrong as well. Dragging one divider then writes only that param (via CrossoverDragBridge), and the other dividers still show values that match neither the params nor the processor. No test covers controller-to-display crossover sync: the tests only exercise CrossoverNetwork (crossover_network_test.cpp). The audio itself is not corrupted beyond the processor's own redistribution behaviour. The harm is a misleading UI on a core multiband control, plus processor/param divergence that a later save can persist. That fits medium, so I left the severity unchanged.

findings.title: StringListParameter defaults set with setNormalized(), so the host 'default' for Band Count and Oversample Max is 1 band / 1x
findings.problem: bandCountParam->setNormalized(1.0) and oversampleParam->setNormalized(2/3) change only the current value. StringListParameter's constructor fixes info.defaultNormalizedValue = 0 (vstparameters.cpp:235), and VST3Editor passes that 0 to the control as its default value (vst3editor.cpp:270, 287).
findings.why_wrong: The intended defaults (4 bands, 4x) must be in ParameterInfo.defaultNormalizedValue for host reset, for control default-click and for hosts that initialise from getParameterInfo.
findings.consequence: A host 'reset to default' or a control's default gesture collapses the plugin to 1 band and 1x oversampling.
findings.suggested_fix: Set getInfo().defaultNormalizedValue as well (as other plugins do), or use a small subclass. Test: assert that getParameterInfo(BandCount).defaultNormalizedValue == 1.0.
findings.evidence: parameter_registration.cpp:76 `bandCountParam->setNormalized(1.0);` ; :90 `oversampleParam->setNormalized(2.0 / 3.0);` ; vstparameters.cpp:235 `info.defaultNormalizedValue = 0;`
verifier_notes:
I traced the code and the defect is real. In plugins/disrumpo/src/controller/parameter_registration.cpp, lines 65-70 build Band Count with the 6-argument StringListParameter constructor, which takes no default value. Line 76 then calls setNormalized(1.0). Oversample Max is built the same way at lines 80-85, and line 90 calls setNormalized(2.0/3.0).

In extern/vst3sdk/public.sdk/source/vst/vstparameters.cpp, that constructor (lines 225-239) hard-codes `info.defaultNormalizedValue = 0;` at line 235. Parameter::setNormalized (line 62 onward) only clamps and stores valueNormalized; it never touches info.defaultNormalizedValue. So the ParameterInfo the controller reports for both parameters gives a default of 0, which means 1 band and 1x.

VST3Editor reads `parameter->getInfo().defaultNormalizedValue` at vst3editor.cpp:270 and passes it to `c->setDefaultValue` at :287. A control's default gesture therefore sends 0. A host reset driven by getParameterInfo would also use 0.

Searching all of plugins/disrumpo for 'defaultNormalizedValue' finds nothing, so no other code corrects it, and no Disrumpo test checks getParameterInfo defaults.

Spectrum Mode at line 103 has the same pattern, but its intended default is 0, so it is harmless. Low severity fits: the bug only shows on default/reset gestures, and initial state comes from the processor.

I confirmed the defect from source. Nothing elsewhere guards it.

1. plugins/disrumpo/src/controller/parameter_registration.cpp:65-77 creates Band Count with the StringListParameter(title, tag, units, flags) constructor and then calls only `bandCountParam->setNormalized(1.0)`. Lines 80-91 do the same for Oversample Max with `setNormalized(2.0 / 3.0)`.
2. In extern/vst3sdk/public.sdk/source/vst/vstparameters.cpp, that constructor (lines 225-239) hardcodes `info.defaultNormalizedValue = 0` at line 235. Parameter::setNormalized (line 62 onward) clamps the value and writes valueNormalized; it does not touch info.defaultNormalizedValue.
3. In vstgui4/vstgui/plugin-bindings/vst3editor.cpp, updateControlValue reads `parameter->getInfo().defaultNormalizedValue` (around line 270) and passes it to each bound control through `c->setDefaultValue` (around line 287). So a control's default gesture would land on 0, which is 1 band or 1x.
4. A grep of all of plugins/disrumpo for defaultNormalizedValue, getParameterInfo and setDefaultValue found nothing. No later fix-up of the default exists, and no test pins it.
5. Other plugins do set the default explicitly: iterum controller.cpp:200, innexus controller.cpp:471/532, profundum global_params.h:149/156 and morph_mod_params.h:270 all assign getInfo().defaultNormalizedValue. Disrumpo is the outlier, so this is an oversight, not a design decision.

Through getParameterInfo the host therefore sees a default of 0 (1 band / 1x), while the comments state the intended defaults are 4 bands and 4x. Low severity is right: the effect is limited to host reset-to-default, control default gestures and hosts that initialise from ParameterInfo; normal state and audio are not affected.

Confirmed from source. plugins/disrumpo/src/controller/parameter_registration.cpp:65-77 builds Band Count with the 6-argument StringListParameter constructor and then calls only `bandCountParam->setNormalized(1.0)`. Lines 80-91 do the same for Oversample Max with `setNormalized(2.0 / 3.0)`. In the SDK, extern/vst3sdk/public.sdk/source/vst/vstparameters.cpp:225-239 shows that constructor hard-codes `info.defaultNormalizedValue = 0;` (line 235). setNormalized changes only valueNormalized, not info.defaultNormalizedValue. I grepped plugins/disrumpo for `defaultNormalizedValue` and got no hits, so nothing in the controller fixes the default later. The editor side is real too: vst3editor.cpp:270 reads `parameter->getInfo().defaultNormalizedValue` and :287 calls `c->setDefaultValue((float)defaultValue)`, so a bound control's default gesture lands on 0. getParameterInfo therefore reports default 0 for both parameters. Any host action that uses the reported default ("reset parameter to default", a generic-editor reset, hosts that seed from ParameterInfo, a default-click on a bound control) sets 1 band (all multiband processing collapses to one band, so audible) and 1x oversampling (less aliasing protection, a quality drop). It does not touch normal load: the processor's own state defaults and setState are unaffected, and the sound only changes when a user or host explicitly invokes the default. No test covers it: global_controls_test.cpp:94-107 and :218-228 check only the IDs. Low severity is appropriate.

findings.title: Host text for node shape slots is formatted with the band's displayed (selected) node type, not the owning node's type
findings.problem: getParamStringByValue for any node kNodeShape0..9 looks up the band's kBandDisplayedType, which is the selected node's type, and formats the slot with it. It should look up the type of the node encoded in the parameter ID.
findings.why_wrong: The shape-slot meaning depends on the node's own type (mapShapeSlotsToParams uses mn.type); a parameter's string must not depend on which node happens to be selected in the UI.
findings.consequence: Host automation lanes and generic editors show wrong units and labels for nodes B-D whenever their type differs from the selected node's, for example a Tube node's slot shown as a Bitcrush depth.
findings.suggested_fix: Read makeNodeParamId(band, extractNode(id), kNodeType) instead of DisplayedType. Test: give node B a different type from the selected node A, and assert that getParamStringByValue for B's slot uses B's formatter.
findings.evidence: controller.cpp:768-773 `auto displayedTypeId = makeBandParamId(band, BandParamType::kBandDisplayedType); ... int typeIdx = static_cast<int>(dtParam->getNormalized() * 25.0 + 0.5);`
verifier_notes: The defect is real. In controller.cpp:765-777, getParamStringByValue handles every node shape-slot ID (kNodeShape0..9, which are registered per band and per node as automatable RangeParameters in parameter_registration.cpp:948-963). It takes only the band from the ID (extractBandFromNodeParam, line 768) and reads makeBandParamId(band, kBandDisplayedType) (line 769). plugin_ids.h:193 describes kBandDisplayedType as a "Proxy type for UIViewSwitchContainer (mirrors selected node's type)". controller.cpp:596-606 confirms it: DisplayedType is synced from makeNodeParamId(band, selNode, kNodeType), where selNode comes from kBandSelectedNode. The node index in the ID is never used. The processor reads a slot through the owning node's own type: processor_params.cpp:880-892 writes mn.shapeSlots[slot] and calls mapShapeSlotsToParams(mn.type, ...) for that node. So when the host formats node B, C or D's shape slot while a node of a different type is selected, formatShapeSlot (line 775) uses the wrong type's formatter and the host shows the wrong label or unit. The audio is not affected; only host-side text is, so low severity is right. The block at controller.cpp:832 formats the band proxy shape params, which do mirror the selected node, so that path is correct and the defect is limited to lines 765-777.

I could not refute this. controller.cpp:765-777 takes the band from the node param ID (extractBandFromNodeParam, line 768), then reads kBandDisplayedType for that band (lines 769-773). It never uses the node index. kBandDisplayedType is documented as a proxy that "mirrors selected node's type" (plugin_ids.h:193), and it is synced only from the selected node's kNodeType (controller.cpp:595-606, visibility_controllers.cpp:369). The processor does it the other way: it applies a node's shape slots with that node's own type (processor_params.cpp:852 and 892, mapShapeSlotsToParams(mn.type, ...)).

The bug is reachable from a real host. Every node shape slot for every band and node is registered as host-visible and automatable, named "B<b> N<n> Shape <s>" with kCanAutomate (parameter_registration.cpp:948-962). So automation lanes and generic editors call getParamStringByValue for nodes that are not selected.

Nothing marks this as intentional. Using DisplayedType is correct in the band-proxy branch (controller.cpp:826-842, kBandDisplayedShape0..9), since those proxies always show the selected node. Copying that same lookup into the node branch at 765-777 is what causes the defect. No test pins the node shape-slot strings: the tests that mention kNodeShape are processor audio tests (bitcrush_noise_repro_test, processor_audio_output_test, multi_node_distortion_test). The impact is display-only, with no effect on audio or state, so low severity fits.

I could not refute this one, and it stays at low severity. In controller.cpp:765-777, getParamStringByValue picks the formatter for any node kNodeShape0..9 ID from the band's kBandDisplayedType (`int typeIdx = dtParam->getNormalized()*25+0.5`). The node index is thrown away: line 768 extracts only the band. kBandDisplayedType is a proxy for the selected node only. plugin_ids.h:193 says it "mirrors selected node's type", and controller.cpp:598-606 fills it from `makeNodeParamId(band, selNode, kNodeType)` (visibility_controllers.cpp:369 does the same when the selection changes). The node shape slots are real host-visible parameters: parameter_registration.cpp:948-963 registers "B<b> N<n> Shape <s>" for every band and node as RangeParameter with kCanAutomate. On the DSP side, processor_params.cpp:852 and 892 map the slots with `mapShapeSlotsToParams(mn.type, ...)`, which uses the owning node's own type. The audio, the stored state and the normalized values are all correct, and the plugin's own editor edits the selected node through the band proxies (lines 826-839), which are consistent. So low severity is right. A fix would derive the type from `makeNodeParamId(band, extractNode(id), kNodeType)`.

findings.title: GranularDistortion derives a grain's state slot from its position in a rebuilt active list, so grain states are cross-wired and grains are skipped or double-processed when one retires (shared with Ruinae)
findings.problem: triggerGrain and processGrain each find grainIndex by scanning grainPool_.activeGrains() for the grain's position, and index grainStates_/waveshapers_ with it. activeGrains() rebuilds activeList_ in place on every call (grain_pool.h:107-115). The process loop iterates a span over that same array while processGrain rebuilds it.
findings.why_wrong: An index into per-grain state must be stable for the grain's lifetime: its slot in GrainPool::grains_, i.e. grain - grains_.data(). The active-list position shifts whenever a grain with a lower pool slot retires. Because processGrain rebuilds activeList_ while the outer range-for is still walking it, the iteration skips one grain and visits the last one twice once a grain is released mid-loop.
findings.consequence: After the first grain retires, every later grain reads another grain's startBufferPos, grainSizeSamples and waveshaper drive/type. The read position jumps mid-grain (clicks), and a newly triggered grain overwrites a live grain's state. In the sample where a grain ends, one grain is skipped (its envelope stalls) and the last grain is summed twice (level spike). This affects Disrumpo's Granular type and Ruinae (ruinae_voice.h includes GranularDistortion): CROSS-PLUGIN IMPACT.
findings.suggested_fix: Expose a stable slot index from GrainPool (indexOf(grain) = grain - grains_.data()). Use it in triggerGrain/processGrain and stop calling activeGrains() inside processGrain. Iterate over a snapshot copy, or release grains after the loop. Test (dsp_processors_tests): with grain size 10 ms and density 8, record per-grain read positions; each grain's readPos must advance by exactly 1 per sample over its lifetime, and the count of processGrain calls per sample must equal the number of active grains.
findings.evidence: granular_distortion.h:559-566 `for (const Grain* g : grainPool_.activeGrains()) { if (g == grain) { grainIndex = idx; ...` ; :619-626 same in processGrain; :394-396 `for (Grain* grain : grainPool_.activeGrains()) { wet += processGrain(grain); }`; grain_pool.h:109-114 rebuilds activeList_ each call; :666-668 releaseGrain inside processGrain
verifier_notes: I traced the code and the defect is real. grain_pool.h:107-116 activeGrains() rewrites the member activeList_ on every call, in pool-slot order, and returns a span over it. Only the first `count` entries are written, so entries past the new count keep stale pointers. granular_distortion.h:549-561 (triggerGrain) and :619-630 (processGrain) take grainIndex as the grain's POSITION in that rebuilt list, not its pool slot, and use it to index grainStates_ and waveshapers_ (:575, :599, :632-633). That position is not stable over a grain's life. (1) When a lower-slot grain retires, every higher-slot grain moves down one position and then reads the previous grain's startBufferPos, grainSizeSamples and waveshaper. (2) acquireGrain (grain_pool.h:62-68) reuses the lowest inactive slot, so a new grain placed below live grains moves them up one position, and triggerGrain writes its state at a position whose array entry a live grain was reading. (3) The process loop at :395-397 range-fors over the span while processGrain calls activeGrains() again (:622). Say grain i is released at :668-669. On the next iteration, activeList_[i+1] is read before the rebuild, and processGrain's rebuild then shifts the array down. Iteration i+2 now reads the old element i+3, so the old i+2 is skipped. The stale tail entry activeList_[N-1] still holds the old last grain, which the shifted list also holds at N-2, so the last grain is processed twice: its envelope advances twice and its output is summed twice. The bypass path at :371-373 has the same pattern. getGrainIndex at :490-500 has the same flaw (dead helper). GranularDistortion is included by plugins/disrumpo/src/dsp/distortion_adapter.h and plugins/ruinae/src/engine/ruinae_voice.h, so the cross-plugin claim holds. With the default density, grains overlap and retire constantly, so this happens in normal use, not only in an edge case. Severity high stands.

I could not refute this from source. Nothing guards against it, nothing documents it as intended, and it is reachable in a real host.

(1) Per-grain state is indexed by list position, not pool slot. In granular_distortion.h, triggerGrain (lines 549-564) and processGrain (lines 619-630) find grainIndex as the grain's position in grainPool_.activeGrains(). They then use it to index grainStates_ and waveshapers_ (lines 575, 599, 632-633). In grain_pool.h, activeGrains() (lines 107-116) rebuilds activeList_ in pool-slot order on every call, so a grain's position equals the number of active grains in lower pool slots. When a lower-slot grain is released (processGrain line 669 calls releaseGrain), every later grain shifts down one position. It then reads the previous grain's startBufferPos, grainSizeSamples and waveshaper drive/type. The cross-wiring is real.

(2) Grains are skipped and double-processed. The outer loop at line 395 iterates a span over activeList_.data() whose count is fixed when the loop starts. Each processGrain call rebuilds that same array in place before its index search. Traced with 4 active grains [g0,g1,g2,g3]: g0 is released at the end of its processGrain; the outer loop reads g1, and processGrain(g1) rebuilds the array to [g1,g2,g3, stale g3]; the outer loop then reads index 2 = g3 and index 3 = stale g3. g2 is skipped and g3 is summed twice. This needs at least two grains after the released one; with 3 grains the stale entry happens to be correct. The same pattern appears in the dry-bypass loop at lines 371-373.

(3) Reachable in a real host. Disrumpo calls granular_.process at distortion_adapter.cpp:563, with density mapped to [1,8] (line 879) and grain size 5-100 ms (granular_distortion.h:89-92). So 4 or more overlapping grains is a normal operating point. Ruinae also uses the class (ruinae_voice.h:1495, 1728), so the cross-plugin claim holds.

(4) Not intentional. The helper getGrainIndex (lines 488-500) has the comment "We can calculate the index by processing order", and the comment at line 552 calls the approach "awkward". Both describe a mistaken workaround, not a design decision. The `% kMaxGrains` at lines 564 and 630 only keeps the index in bounds; it does not make it stable. The fix the finding suggests (slot index = grain - grains_.data()) is sound.

Severity stays high: a shared Layer-2 processor gets wrong per-grain read positions and gain spikes. The granular character may partly mask the clicks, but the summing error (one grain skipped, one doubled) is deterministic.

I could not refute this. The defect is real and the claimed consequence follows from the code.

1. Per-grain state is keyed by position in the active list, not by pool slot. triggerGrain (granular_distortion.h:549-564) and processGrain (:619-630) both scan grainPool_.activeGrains() for the grain pointer and use that position to index grainStates_ and waveshapers_ (:575, :599, :632-633). GrainPool::activeGrains() (grain_pool.h:107-116) rebuilds activeList_ in pool-slot order on every call. When a grain in a lower slot retires, every live grain above it drops one position.

Worked example: A is in slot 0, B in slot 1, A retires. B now resolves to index 0 and reads A's stale startBufferPos and A's waveshaper settings. When the next grain C fills slot 0 (acquireGrain takes the lowest inactive slot, grain_pool.h:62-68), it overwrites state[0] and B goes back to state[1].

B's read position is startBufferPos + phase*size (:640-642), so it jumps twice in mid-grain. The jump is roughly the time between the two grains' trigger points plus jitter, which is hundreds to thousands of samples. On tonal input that is a waveform discontinuity, scaled by B's envelope, which can be near its peak. With drive variation or algorithm variation on, the drive and waveshaper type also change mid-grain.

2. The list is rebuilt in place while the loop is still walking it. The loop at :395 is a range-for over a span of activeList_ with a fixed end. processGrain releases a grain at :668-669 and then calls activeGrains() at :622. Say grain i is released:
   - Grain i+1 is still processed correctly, because the list has not been rebuilt yet when the loop reads it.
   - processGrain(i+1) then rebuilds the list and shifts every entry down by one.
   - The old grain i+2 is skipped for that sample.
   - The stale last entry is left in place and gets processed a second time. Its phase advances twice and its output is summed twice, a one-sample spike as large as one grain's output.

The bypass path at :371-372 has the same problem.

3. Both plugins reach this code. In Disrumpo, DistortionType::Granular calls granular_.process(input) (distortion_adapter.cpp:561-563) with density mapped to [1,8] (:879). With 1-8 overlapping grains, slots retire out of order all the time, so this fires on most grain retirements, i.e. several times per second at typical settings. Ruinae includes it in ruinae_voice.h, so the cross-plugin flag is correct.

Bounds: there is no NaN and no runaway. The index is reduced mod 64 and the waveshaper output is bounded, so this is a clicks/glitches defect, not a safety one. For a user-selectable distortion type that clicks constantly on sustained input, high severity is justified.

findings.title: Stochastic (and Temporal with Diode/Tube curves) need an external DC blocker per their contract; the adapter gives none, and Stochastic emits noise and DC from silence
findings.problem: updateDCBlockerState enables the adapter DC blocker only for AsymmetricFuzz, FullRectify, HalfRectify and FeedbackDist. StochasticShaper adds jitterOffset (up to ±0.5*amount plus drift) to the INPUT before the waveshaper (`waveshaper_.process(x + jitterOffset)`) and has no DC blocking. TemporalDistortion includes no DC blocker, yet the adapter lets it select WaveshapeType Diode (7) and Tube (8) via dynamicCurve (:761-764).
findings.why_wrong: stochastic_shaper.h:135 states 'No internal DC blocking: Compose with DCBlocker for asymmetric types'. sigmoid diode() is asymmetric (forward bound 1, reverse bound -2, sigmoid.h:358-366), so Temporal with Diode produces a DC offset. The adapter is the composition point and must add the blocker.
findings.consequence: With silent input, a Stochastic node outputs waveshaper(drive*jitterOffset): a wandering noise/DC floor up to about tanh(10*0.5) ≈ full scale at high drive and jitter, with no gate. Temporal with the Diode/Tube curve, and Stochastic with drift, put a DC offset on the band output that sums into the master.
findings.suggested_fix: Add Stochastic and Temporal (at least for curve indices 7 and 8) to updateDCBlockerState. Decide with the user whether Stochastic should gate its jitter on input level, the way FeedbackDistortion gates its feedback. Test: an adapter of type Stochastic (jitter 1, drift 1, drive 5) fed 2 s of silence; output RMS < -90 dBFS and |mean| < 1e-4. Today it is loud.
findings.evidence: distortion_adapter.cpp:588-591 needsDCBlock_ list excludes Stochastic/Temporal; stochastic_shaper.h:583 `float out = waveshaper_.process(x + jitterOffset);`; :135 contract note; temporal_distortion.h:26-30 includes (no dc_blocker); distortion_adapter.cpp:761-764 curve index 0..8 to WaveshapeType
verifier_notes: I traced the call path and could not refute it. (1) distortion_adapter.cpp:586-592: updateDCBlockerState sets needsDCBlock_ only for AsymmetricFuzz, FullRectify, HalfRectify and FeedbackDist. The only other writer is :701, and it covers only Full/HalfRectify. So Stochastic and Temporal never reach dcBlocker_ (:218-220). (2) distortion_adapter.cpp:207-212: Stochastic gets the input with no drive scaling, and :956 does stochastic_.setDrive(commonParams_.drive). (3) In stochastic_shaper.h:530-592, process() builds jitterOffset = jitterAmount*smoothedJitter*0.5 + drift*driftSmoother*0.3 (:562-565), where nextFloat is bipolar [-1,1] per random.h/xorshift32. It then returns waveshaper_.process(x + jitterOffset) (:583). Waveshaper::process applies drive*x (waveshaper.h:212). With x = 0 the output is shape(drive*jitterOffset), so at drive 5, jitter 1 and drift 1 it reaches up to tanh(5*0.8) ≈ 1. Nothing gates this on input level. The adapter's only gate is drive < 0.0001 (:191), and BandProcessor::processWithFactor (band_processor.h:628-630) gates on drive only. No DC blocker exists in band_processor.h, morph_engine.cpp or processor.cpp. (4) The class doc at stochastic_shaper.h:134-135 says "No internal DC blocking: Compose with DCBlocker", so the adapter, as the composition point, should add one. (5) temporal_distortion.h:26-30 includes no dc_blocker, and grep finds no DCBlock in it. distortion_adapter.cpp:761-764 maps dynamicCurve to WaveshapeType 0..8, which includes Diode (7) and Tube (8). sigmoid.h:333-366 shows both curves are asymmetric, so a signal through them gains a DC offset. (6) The adapter tests at distortion_adapter_test.cpp:2093 exercise Stochastic parameters but have no silence or DC case. One small correction: the adapter clamps the Stochastic curve to 0..5 (:952), so all its curves are symmetric. Its DC and silence output come from the jitter/drift offset, which matches what the finding says. The defect stands as described.

I looked for a guard or a documented reason for this and found neither. The defect is real, but it is narrower than the finding says.

Confirmed:
- distortion_adapter.cpp:586-592 turns the adapter DC blocker on only for AsymmetricFuzz, FullRectify, HalfRectify and FeedbackDist; Rectify can also override it via p.dcBlock at :701. That blocker, applied at :218-219, is the only DC blocking in plugins/disrumpo/src (grep found nothing in the band or processor code).
- Nothing gates on silence anywhere in src: grep for silen/kSilence/isSilent found only solo and spectrum-display hits.
- The adapter returns early only when drive < 0.0001 (:191). For Stochastic it passes the raw input on (:207-209) to stochastic_.process (:575).
- In stochastic_shaper.h:530-592 the waveshaper is fed x + jitterOffset (:584), where jitterOffset = jitterAmount*smoothedJitter*0.5 + drift*driftSmoother*0.3 (:562-565). Neither term depends on the input level, so silent input still produces a wandering waveshaper(drive*offset) output.
- The header says 'No internal DC blocking: Compose with DCBlocker for asymmetric types' (:135). processor_params.cpp:271 maps jitter rate to 0.1-100 Hz. At 100 Hz the smoother time is 800/rate = 8 ms (:667-669), so part of this floor falls in the audible LF range, not just DC.
- No test covers silent input for Stochastic. distortion_adapter_test.cpp:2093 only checks parameter round-trips.
- Temporal: temporal_distortion.h:26-30 includes no DC blocker, and adapter :761-764 allows curve indices 7 and 8 (Diode and Tube are asymmetric, waveshaper.h:58-59). So Temporal with those curves leaves DC on a real signal.

Where the finding overstates:
- Stochastic's own curve select is clamped to indices 0-5 (processor_params.cpp:269: slots[0]*5), which covers Tanh through Erf, all symmetric. The header's 'asymmetric types' DC contract therefore never applies to Stochastic's curve.
- The jitter and drift offsets are bipolar random walks, so their long-term mean is near zero. What comes out is low-frequency wander rather than a fixed DC.
- At the default 10 Hz rate (80 ms smoothing) that wander is mostly subsonic.
- The 10 Hz DC blocker suggested as the fix would not remove the 10-100 Hz part of the noise at high jitter rates.
- Stochastic is an opt-in Experimental type, and Temporal's DC from Diode/Tube is a mild, input-dependent offset.

Verdict: a real gap that nothing elsewhere guards, but medium severity rather than high.

Confirmed as real, but with a smaller impact than claimed. Code I read: distortion_adapter.cpp:586-592 turns the DC blocker on only for AsymmetricFuzz, FullRectify, HalfRectify and FeedbackDist. Bitcrush's user toggle at :701 is the only other path. Nothing downstream removes DC: toneFilter_ is a OnePoleLP (distortion_adapter.h:358, cpp:583), and a grep for DCBlocker under plugins/disrumpo/src finds only the adapter's one instance. Distortion runs after the crossover, so DC made in any band reaches the master.

(1) Temporal: the adapter maps dynamicCurve to curve indices 0..8 (cpp:761-764). Diode is index 7 (curve slot near 0.875) and Tube is index 8 (slot 1.0); waveshaper.h:58-59 lists both as asymmetric. temporal_distortion.h:26-34 includes no dc_blocker. sigmoid.h:333-342 tube() = tanh(l + 0.3 l^2 - 0.15 l^3). I computed the mean of this function for a sine through Temporal's baseDrive range 0.5..3 (cpp:754). Tube DC is about +0.31 at drive 3 with a full-scale input (about -10 dBFS, against 0.64 RMS), +0.07 at drive 1.75 / amplitude 0.5, and about 0.01 at -20 dB input. Diode DC is about 0.03-0.05 (about -26..-30 dBFS). The DC follows the envelope, so it moves with the input level: transients thump and the shaper loses headroom. That is a real defect. It needs a non-default curve, though: the default dynamicCurve is 0.5 (h:128), which gives index 4, ReciprocalSqrt, a symmetric curve.

(2) Stochastic: the claim that its contract requires a blocker does not apply here. cpp:952 clamps stochasticCurve to 0..5 (Tanh, Atan, Cubic, Quintic, ReciprocalSqrt, Erf). All six are odd and symmetric, so the "compose with DCBlocker for asymmetric types" note (stochastic_shaper.h:135) does not cover any curve Disrumpo can select. The output from silence is real: stochastic_shaper.h:565/584 computes out = f(drive * (0 + jitterOffset)). The jitter and drift values come from Xorshift32::nextFloat in [-1,1] (random.h:59-62), so they average zero over the long run. They wander, though, at the S&H rate, which processor_params.cpp:271 caps at 0.1..100 Hz, with 8-8000 ms smoothing. With defaults (jitter 0.2, rate 10 Hz) and drive 1, silence gives a sub-10 Hz wander of about ±0.1 (-20 dBFS). With jitter 1 and drive 5-10 it reaches about tanh(5) ≈ 0.99, full scale. drive < 1e-4 is the only gate (cpp:191). This is an infrasonic/rumble floor from silence that a 10 Hz DC blocker would mostly remove at low rates, but not at 100 Hz. It is partly what the type is designed to do (FR-022 jitter offset), not a contract breach.

No test covers either case: the Stochastic tests in distortion_adapter_test.cpp:2093 and the oversampling tests do not check silence or DC.

Downgrade: the defect is real, but the clearly unintended large DC needs the user to choose Temporal Tube (or, smaller, Diode) at high drive and level. The Stochastic part is a design question about gating jitter in silence: its long-term mean is zero, its shaper is symmetric, and the full-scale output needs extreme jitter and drive. Medium fits better than high.
corroborated_by_measurement: probe type:Tube DC: "drive 0.25: -0.00566; 0.75: -0.033; 1.0: -0.041". bias:Tube:bias=-1 / +1: "-0.0673,0,-7.15 / 0.00686,0,-4.38" (threshold |dc| < 1e-3). Code: distortion_adapter.cpp:588 `needsDCBlock_ = (currentType_ == DistortionType::AsymmetricFuzz || ... FeedbackDist);`, with Tube absent.

findings.title: FuzzProcessor's tone is never set by the adapter, so Fuzz/AsymFuzz always run through a hidden ~1.8 kHz biquad lowpass on top of the adapter tone filter
findings.problem: The Fuzz and AsymmetricFuzz routing sets bias, fuzz amount, octave and body but never calls fuzz_.setTone(). FuzzProcessor defaults tone_ = 0.5, which maps to 400*20^0.5 ≈ 1789 Hz, and always applies that Q=0.707 lowpass to the saturated signal. The adapter then applies its own one-pole tone filter.
findings.why_wrong: The primitive's tone control is part of its documented API (setTone, fuzz_processor.h:92, 182). If the plugin does not expose it, the adapter must set it to fully open (tone = 1, 8 kHz) or map it from the node's Tone. Otherwise the user's Tone knob cannot open the sound.
findings.consequence: Fuzz types have a fixed dark 12 dB/oct rolloff the user cannot remove. Combined with the 8x prepare-rate mismatch the corner sits near 224 Hz at 44.1 kHz, making Fuzz nearly muffled.
findings.suggested_fix: Call fuzz_.setTone() in both cases, mapped from commonParams_.toneHz or fixed at 1.0. Test: Fuzz with sustain 0.5 and node tone 8000 Hz, fed a 4 kHz sine; output at 4 kHz must be within 6 dB of the 500 Hz response.
findings.evidence: distortion_adapter.cpp:637-650 (no setTone); fuzz_processor.h:116 kDefaultTone = 0.5f; :134,137 kToneMinHz 400 / kToneMaxHz 8000; :398-399 toneFilter_.configure(Lowpass, 400*20^tone, 0.707); :554 saturated = toneFilter_.process(saturated)

findings.title: Tube multi-stage cascade calls one TubeStage instance up to 4 times per sample, sharing its DC blocker and smoothers between stages
findings.problem: For satStage > 0 the adapter loops `tube_.process(singleSampleBuffer_, 1)` 2-4 times on the SAME TubeStage. Each call advances inputGain/outputGain/saturation smoothers (tube_stage.h:280-282) and runs the single dcBlocker_ (:301), whose one-sample memory then alternates between the stage signals within one sample.
findings.why_wrong: TubeStage::process(buffer, n) treats successive calls as successive time samples of ONE signal. A cascade of S stages needs S instances (or S DC-blocker/smoother states). With a shared instance the DC blocker no longer implements its documented 10 Hz HP per stage, and the smoothing time is divided by S.
findings.consequence: Multi-stage tube settings get a corrupted DC-block/HP response: the high-pass sees an interleaved stage sequence, which leaves stage-to-stage differences and residual DC. Parameter ramps finish S times faster, so zipper noise appears on sag automation. The tonal result of 2-4 stages is not a real cascade.
findings.suggested_fix: Hold std::array<TubeStage,4> in the adapter (prepare and route params to all four) and run stage s through tube_[s]. Test: Tube with satStage 3 and bias 0.5, fed a 100 Hz sine; output mean < 1e-3 after 1 s, and the result must match four independent TubeStage instances within 1e-4.
findings.evidence: distortion_adapter.cpp:313-316 `for (int s = 0; s < stages; ++s) { tube_.process(singleSampleBuffer_, 1); }`; tube_stage.h:278-307 per-call smoother advance + dcBlocker_.process(wet)
verifier_notes: The core claim holds. distortion_adapter.cpp:312-317 writes one input sample to singleSampleBuffer_ and then calls `tube_.process(singleSampleBuffer_, 1)` `stages = clamp(satStage+1,1,4)` times on the single member `Krate::DSP::TubeStage tube_` (distortion_adapter.h:371). satStage comes from processor_params.cpp:58 (`slots[2]*3+0.5`, range 0..3), so 1-4 calls per sample happen. In tube_stage.h:271-308 every process() iteration advances all three OnePoleSmoothers (:280-282) and runs the single `DCBlocker dcBlocker_` (:301, :334). That one-pole high-pass keeps x1_/y1_ state (dc_blocker.h:138-151), so within one sample it sees stage1 input, stage2 input, and so on in turn. It filters a sequence that repeats every S calls instead of S separate 10 Hz high-passes. A one-pole HP fed that repeating sequence only removes the mean taken over all phases. Each phase keeps its own offset from that mean, and the final stage's output is one of those phases. With bias set (setBias at distortion_adapter.cpp:614, asymmetric waveshaper) this leaves DC and a non-cascade response, as the finding says. The 10 Hz cutoff from prepare (:132) also no longer means 10 Hz in real time. The smoothers also advance S times per real sample. That part of the claim is true, but its consequence is overstated: the adapter only routes setBias (not smoothed) and setSaturationAmount (smoothed) at :614-615, and a 5 ms/S ramp of about 1.25 ms is still a ramp, not a zipper. This does not change the main defect. No test in plugins/disrumpo/tests or src references satStage beyond those lines, so no test covers it. The defect is in how the adapter uses TubeStage, not in the shared header, so the fix stays in Disrumpo. Medium severity is appropriate.

I could not refute this from context. The code does what the finding says, and nothing guards it. In distortion_adapter.cpp:309-318, `stages = clamp(satStage+1,1,4)` and the loop calls `tube_.process(singleSampleBuffer_, 1)` 1-4 times per sample on the single `tube_` member (prepared at :35, reset at :107, params routed at :614-615). TubeStage::process (tube_stage.h:278-308) treats every call as the next time sample. Each call advances inputGain/outputGain/saturation smoothers (:280-282) and runs the one `dcBlocker_` (:301, member at :334). So the blocker's one-sample memory sees the interleaved stream stage1(n), stage2(n), ..., stage1(n+1). That is not S independent 10 Hz high-passes: the decay is effectively R^S per real sample, and the stage-to-stage steps within one sample pass straight through.

Nothing upstream or downstream compensates. The adapter's own dcBlocker_ is enabled only for AsymmetricFuzz/FullRectify/HalfRectify/FeedbackDist (distortion_adapter.cpp:586-592, applied at :218-220), so Tube output with bias gets no further DC block. I found no comment, no specs/Disrumpo text (grepped for cascade/multi-stage/satStage: no hits) and no test (no satStage reference anywhere under plugins/disrumpo/tests) that documents or pins this as intentional.

Severity stays as filed. The core defect (a shared DC-blocker state, so it is not a real cascade and some DC can leak with bias) is confirmed. The 'zipper noise' part is overstated. The adapter never sets input/output gain on tube_, so those smoothers sit at target. Only the saturation (sag) smoother ramps, and it ramps S times faster (5 ms becomes 1.25-5 ms). That is still a continuous one-pole curve, not a stepped zipper.

The finding holds, and a measurement I ran confirms the consequence. distortion_adapter.cpp:313-316 runs `tube_.process(singleSampleBuffer_, 1)` 1-4 times per sample on the one `tube_` member. tube_stage.h:278-307 advances the three smoothers (:280-282) and the single dcBlocker_ (:301) on every call. dc_blocker.h:202 (`y = x - x1_ + R_*y1_`) keeps one sample of memory, so with stages 2-4 the blocker sees the interleaved sequence stage1, stage2, ... stageS, stage1'. It removes only the mean DC of all the stages, not each stage's own DC, and its effective cutoff becomes about S x 10 Hz. Nothing downstream catches the leftover DC. distortion_adapter.cpp:586-592 sets needsDCBlock_ only for AsymmetricFuzz, FullRectify, HalfRectify and FeedbackDist, not Tube, and no other Disrumpo source holds a DC blocker (grep of plugins/disrumpo/src: only processor_params.cpp, distortion_adapter.{h,cpp}). The stage count is user-reachable: processor_params.cpp:58 maps a shape slot to satStage 0-3, and drive goes up to 10 (processor_params.cpp:858). I measured it with a standalone probe (scratchpad tube_probe.cpp, clang++ -O2, 44.1 kHz, 1 s settle, then 1 s measured, sag 1.0), comparing the shared instance against S independent TubeStage instances. With 1 stage the two match bit for bit. With 2/3/4 stages at drive 4 and a 100 Hz sine, the shared path leaves an output mean of -0.052/-0.075/-0.094 (bias 0) and +0.035/+0.069/+0.099 (bias 0.5). That is up to about -20 dBFS of DC; the independent cascade gives 0.0000. The waveform differs as well: the difference RMS relative to the true cascade is -14, -5.7 and -0.8 dB at 100 Hz, and -12 to -19 dB at 1 kHz. Level moves by up to 0.74 dB and peaks rise (0.672 vs 0.575). So the multi-stage tube is not a real cascade, and it pushes significant DC into the band sum. The smoother part is real but small: the 5 ms ramp shrinks to about 1.25 ms, and the targets only change when parameters do. Medium severity fits: it needs a non-default stage selection, but then it adds a lot of DC and changes the tone, with no crash or NaN.

findings.title: Feedback type: the 'Curve' knob is never routed to FeedbackDistortion, the 'Lim' off toggle still limits at 0 dB, and 'Thr' is inverted
findings.problem: processor_params maps slot 2 to p.fbCurve, but the FeedbackDist routing never calls feedbackDist_.setSaturationCurve (or setDrive), so the knob does nothing. The limiter-off branch passes 0.0 dB, the primitive's maximum threshold, which still soft-limits to threshold+3 dB. The threshold mapping limThreshold*-24 means turning 'Thr' up LOWERS the threshold.
findings.why_wrong: FeedbackDistortion exposes setSaturationCurve (feedback_distortion.h:400) and its threshold range is [-24, 0] dB with no 'off' value (:111-112). The adapter must route every UI control and implement 'off' itself, for example by skipping the limiter or using a very high threshold if the primitive gains a disable flag.
findings.consequence: The UI shows a 'Curve' knob that changes a stored value with no audible effect. 'Lim' off has almost no effect at normal levels. Users raising 'Thr' to loosen the limiter get maximum limiting at -24 dB instead.
findings.suggested_fix: Route fbCurve to setSaturationCurve (map it like the other 9-type curves) and invert the threshold map (-24 + limThreshold*24). Add a limiter-enable to FeedbackDistortion (a shared header: check consumers). Tests: changing fbCurve from 0 to 1 must change the output RMS by > 1 dB; with limiter on, a higher Thr must give a higher peak output.
findings.evidence: processor_params.cpp:182 `p.fbCurve = slots[2];`; distortion_adapter.cpp:813-819 (no setSaturationCurve); :815 `setLimiterThreshold(p.limiter ? (p.limThreshold * -24.0f) : 0.0f)`; feedback_distortion.h:111-112 kMin/MaxThresholdDb -24/0; :297 limiter active whenever smoothedThreshold > 0; editor.uidesc:1075-1076 'Curve' knob, :1083-1086 'Lim'/'Thr'
verifier_notes:
I re-traced all three parts of the claim from source and each one holds.

1) The Curve knob is never routed. processor_params.cpp:178-182 maps Slot2 ("Curve") to `p.fbCurve = slots[2]`. A grep for fbCurve across plugins/disrumpo/src finds it only in the declaration (distortion_adapter.h:141), in that mapping, and in morph interpolation (morph_engine.cpp:470, :579). The adapter never reads it. Every use of feedbackDist_ in the adapter is at distortion_adapter.cpp:73 (prepare), :114 (reset), :544 (process) and :813-819 (setFeedback, setDelayTime, setLimiterThreshold, setToneFrequency, setFilterType, setStages, setDecay). None of them calls setSaturationCurve (feedback_distortion.h:400) or sets drive. So the stored value has no audible effect. editor.uidesc:1075 does show a "Curve" label in that panel.

2) Lim off still limits. distortion_adapter.cpp:815 passes 0.0f dB when p.limiter is false. setLimiterThreshold (feedback_distortion.h:434-437) clamps to [kMinThresholdDb=-24, kMaxThresholdDb=0] (:111-112), so 0 dB gives a linear threshold of 1.0. The limiter branch at :283 runs whenever `absLevel > smoothedThreshold && smoothedThreshold > 0.0f`, which is always true when the threshold is 1.0. That soft-limits to threshold*(1+0.41*tanh) (:291-298). So "off" is really "limit at 0 dBFS / +3 dB". At normal levels this differs little from on, and it still catches peaks above 1.0.

3) Thr is inverted. Line 815 computes `p.limThreshold * -24.0f`, so slot 0 gives 0 dB and slot 1 gives -24 dB. Raising the "Thr" knob (editor.uidesc:1085) therefore lowers the threshold. The default limThreshold of 0.8 (distortion_adapter.h:145) gives -19.2 dB, which is heavy limiting.
