findings.title: GranularDistortion's internal drive (default 5.0) is never set, so the adapter's drive is multiplied by 5 inside each grain
findings.problem: The adapter pre-scales the Granular input by commonParams_.drive (line 211) and never calls granular_.setDrive(), so baseDrive_ keeps its default 5.0 (clamped [1,20]). Each grain's waveshaper then applies drive 5 times the variation on top. The adapter explicitly fixes the same double-drive problem for Fractal (setDrive(1.0), :943-947) but not for Granular.
findings.why_wrong: GranularDistortion's drive is part of its contract (setDrive, granular_distortion.h:239-241). The adapter must either neutralise it (setDrive(1)) or route the node drive into it instead of pre-scaling.
findings.consequence: Granular is driven 5x harder than the Drive knob shows (drive 2 acts as 10, drive 10 as 50, i.e. tanh hard-clip). The lower half of the Drive range is unusable and every Granular setting is heavily clipped.
findings.suggested_fix: Call granular_.setDrive(1.0f) in the Granular routing, matching Fractal. Test: Granular with drive 1, density 1, and a -20 dBFS sine; peak output < -12 dBFS (unsaturated). Today it is near 0 dBFS.
findings.evidence: granular_distortion.h:713 `float baseDrive_ = 5.0f;`; :239-241 setDrive; distortion_adapter.cpp:878-885 (no setDrive); :211 `wet = input * commonParams_.drive;`; :943-947 Fractal setDrive(1.0f) with the double-drive comment
verifier_notes: I confirmed the defect from source. distortion_adapter.cpp:206-212 pre-scales every type except Temporal and Stochastic: `wet = input * commonParams_.drive;`. Granular is not in that exception list, so its input is pre-scaled before processRaw, which calls granular_.process at :561-563. The Granular routing at :877-886 sets grain size, density, position jitter, drive variation, position, curve and envelope type, but never calls setDrive. A grep of plugins/disrumpo for `granular_.setDrive` finds nothing (only setDriveVariation at :881). setCurve (granular_distortion.h:307-309) only sets curve_, so it does not set drive either. In granular_distortion.h the default is `float baseDrive_ = 5.0f;` (:713). prepare() and reset() snap driveSmoother_ to baseDrive_ (:142, :172). triggerGrain feeds driveSmoother_.process() through calculateGrainDrive into `ws.setDrive(grainDrive)` (:567-576), and processGrain applies `ws.process(bufferSample)` (:648). So every grain waveshapes (node drive x input) with an extra internal drive of 5. The adapter fixes this same double-drive for Fractal with setDrive(1.0f) and a comment (:943-947), and for Stochastic by handling drive internally (:951-956), but does nothing for Granular. kMinDrive = 1.0 (:93), so setDrive(1.0f) is a valid neutral value. No Disrumpo test checks Granular's output level (distortion_adapter_test.cpp covers only latency and category). One overstatement: with a -20 dBFS sine and drive 1, today's output is about tanh(0.5), roughly -6.7 dBFS, not "near 0 dBFS". The core claim, an unintended 5x gain inside each grain, stands. The defect is confirmed from source, and nothing in the code or specs says it is intentional.

1. The adapter's Granular routing (plugins/disrumpo/src/dsp/distortion_adapter.cpp:877-886) sets grain size, density, position jitter, drive variation, position, curve and envelope type. It never calls granular_.setDrive().
2. A grep for setDrive/setBaseDrive across plugins/disrumpo/src finds calls only for tube (:41), tape (:43, :626), temporal (:754), allpass saturator (:830), fractal (:947) and stochastic (:956). No granular call exists anywhere.
3. process() pre-scales the input for every type except Temporal and Stochastic: `wet = input * commonParams_.drive;` (:207-212). Granular is therefore pre-driven.
4. In dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/granular_distortion.h, `baseDrive_ = 5.0f` (:713). prepare() (:142) and reset() (:172) snap driveSmoother_ to baseDrive_. triggerGrain() calls `ws.setDrive(grainDrive)` (:576), where grainDrive is derived from smoothedDrive (:567-568, :510-520, clamped to [1,20]). processGrain() then calls ws.process(bufferSample) (:648) on the already pre-scaled buffer.
5. The effective drive is node drive x 5 (more with drive variation). There is no compensating output gain.
6. The adapter fixes the same double-drive explicitly for Fractal (:943-947, with a comment). No equivalent comment or spec note exists for Granular. specs/Disrumpo mentions per-grain drive variation only (dsp-details.md:510, ui-mockups.md:859).
7. No disrumpo test pins the Granular level. distortion_adapter_test.cpp checks only latency and category for Granular.

Nothing upstream guards or clamps this, and no reset or prepare call overrides baseDrive_. The defect is reachable whenever a node uses type Granular.

The defect is real; I could not refute it. distortion_adapter.cpp:877-886 (Granular routing) sets grain size, density, position jitter, drive variation, position, curve and envelope type. It never calls granular_.setDrive. A grep of every granular_ use in the adapter (lines 83, 120, 563, 878-884) also finds no setDrive call. So granular_distortion.h:713 `float baseDrive_ = 5.0f;` stays at 5. prepare() and reset() snap driveSmoother_ to it (:142, :172). triggerGrain uses smoothedDrive as the grain drive (:567-568). With driveVariation 0, calculateGrainDrive returns it unchanged (:511-512), and ws.setDrive(grainDrive) follows (:576). The Waveshaper then computes `drive_ * x` (waveshaper.h:212), and the default curve is Tanh (granular_distortion.h:719). Before all this, the adapter has already multiplied the input by commonParams_.drive (distortion_adapter.cpp:211). Only Temporal and Stochastic skip that pre-scale (:207-209). The node drive range is 0-10 (processor_params.cpp:858 `value * 10.0f`; band_processor.h:445 and morph_engine.cpp:713 clamp to [0,10]). So the effective Granular gain into tanh is 5 x knob, from 0 to 50. The [1,20] clamp applies only to baseDrive and the per-grain variation (:240, :520), not to the product. Fractal shows the intended contract: :943-947 calls fractal_.setDrive(1.0f), with a comment about exactly this double-drive problem. Granular has no such fix. Impact, computed from these formulas rather than measured: knob 1 on a -20 dBFS (0.1) sine gives tanh(0.5)=0.46 per grain, about -6.7 dBFS and already compressing, instead of about 0.1. That is roughly 13 dB more gain at the default drive of 1 (processor.cpp:113). Grain overlap at densities up to 8 adds more on top. At knob 4 and above, tanh(20x) or harder is essentially hard clipping. One claim is overstated: "the lower half of the Drive range is unusable" is wrong. The calibrated range lies in knob 0-2 (effective 0-10), and it is the upper roughly 80% of the knob that saturates in nearly the same way. No test catches this: distortion_adapter_test.cpp only checks that Granular output is non-zero and that it reports latency. The effect is a level and voicing calibration problem with no safety consequence. Fixing it changes the sound of any preset that uses Granular (a state-compatibility concern). Medium severity fits.

findings.title: setType switches the active processor with no reset, so stateful processors replay stale audio when a node type returns
findings.problem: DistortionAdapter::setType only stores currentType_ and updates DC/latency flags. Processors that were inactive keep whatever they held when last active, because processRaw feeds only the current type's processor. That includes the FeedbackDistortion delay line, the Granular 32768-sample buffer and grain pool, the Spectral STFT/OLA buffers, AllpassSaturator Karplus-Strong/matrix states, and the chaos attractor. MorphEngine::setNodes calls setType on every node-param change, and processSameFamily calls it on blendedAdapter_ every sample with the dominant type.
findings.why_wrong: These primitives assume a continuous input stream between reset() calls. When the caller stops feeding one and later resumes, it must reset() it, or crossfade from a primed state, to avoid emitting stale content.
findings.consequence: Switching a node (or the same-family dominant node) back to Feedback, Granular or Spectral bursts out audio captured seconds or minutes earlier: a comb ringing tail, grains read from the old buffer, an old spectral frame. This is audible as ghost audio or clicks at type changes and morph-dominance changes.
findings.suggested_fix: In setType, call reset() on the newly selected type's processor when the type actually changes. A short output crossfade would avoid the reset click. Test: run FeedbackDist on a loud sine, switch to SoftClip, process 1 s of silence, switch back, process silence; output must be < -90 dBFS.
findings.evidence: distortion_adapter.cpp:142-162 setType (no reset); :542-567 only the active type's processor is processed; morph_engine.cpp:705-706 blendedAdapter_.setType(nodes_[dominantNode].type) per sample
verifier_notes: The defect holds after tracing the code. distortion_adapter.cpp:142-162 setType only assigns currentType_, calls updateDCBlockerState(), and sets the isBlockBased_/blockLatency_ flags. It never calls reset() on anything. processRaw (distortion_adapter.cpp:542-575) feeds only the current type's processor: feedbackDist_.process, granular_.process, spectral_.process, chaos_.process and so on. The inactive processors therefore keep whatever state they had. The only resets are DistortionAdapter::reset() (:98-136), MorphEngine::reset() (morph_engine.cpp:72-94), BandProcessor::reset() (band_processor.h:136-153) and setActive (processor.cpp:149-164). None of these runs on a type change. On the node-type param path, processor_params.cpp:840-853 swaps mn.type and the shape slots, then MorphEngine::setNodes calls adapters_[i].setType at morph_engine.cpp:137, with no reset either. BandProcessor::setDistortionType (band_processor.h:208-212) also calls only setType. Same-family dominance switching is reachable: distortion_types.h:328-330 puts Temporal and FeedbackDist in the Dynamic family, and :338-344 puts Chaos, Formant, Granular, Spectral, Fractal and Stochastic in Experimental. processSameFamily (morph_engine.cpp:696-706) picks the highest-weight node every sample and calls blendedAdapter_.setType on it. So a cursor moving between a Temporal node and a FeedbackDist node, or between a Granular node and a Spectral node, makes the shared blendedAdapter_ return to a processor whose buffers were frozen at their last use. The stale state is real: FeedbackDistortion (dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/feedback_distortion.h:231-330) reads delayLine_ at :261 and writes x + feedbackSignal at :330. Its delay line is cleared only in reset() at :209-215, and its feedback can reach or exceed unity with a limiter for indefinite sustain (:40, :379). When it resumes, the old buffered audio plays out and recirculates. The finding's file and line citations match the code, and its suggested fix (reset the newly selected processor when the type actually changes) addresses this path. Medium severity is appropriate: the result is audible ghost audio or clicks on type and dominance changes, not NaN or a crash.

I could not refute this. The defect holds up in the source.

1. distortion_adapter.cpp:142-162: setType only assigns currentType_, calls updateDCBlockerState and sets isBlockBased_/blockLatency_. It never calls reset(). The only reset() of all the processors is DistortionAdapter::reset() at :98-136.
2. processRaw (distortion_adapter.cpp ~:520-575) only runs the processor of currentType_: feedbackDist_.process, granular_.process, spectral_.process, allpassSaturator_.process, chaos_.process. Every other processor sits frozen with whatever state it last had.
3. Nothing upstream resets on a type change. processor_params.cpp:840-853 handles kNodeType by saving and restoring shape slots and remapping params, with no reset. MorphEngine::setNodes (morph_engine.cpp:131-140) calls adapters_[i].setType/setParams with no reset. MorphEngine::reset (:72-83) and BandProcessor::reset (band_processor.h:136-153) only run from the setActive/prepare path (processor.cpp:149-164).
4. morph_engine.cpp:706 calls blendedAdapter_.setType(nodes_[dominantNode].type) every sample in processSameFamily. The family table (distortion_types.h:297-349) puts Granular, Spectral, Chaos, Formant, Fractal and Stochastic in Experimental, and Temporal with FeedbackDist in Dynamic. So two nodes from one of those families take the same-family path, and the single blended adapter swaps between stateful processors whenever dominance changes, with no reset.
5. The stale state is real. FeedbackDistortion (dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/feedback_distortion.h:209-215, :261, :330) keeps a delay line of up to 100 ms that only reset() or a NaN input clears. When the type comes back, it reads that old content and feeds it back into the loop.
6. I found no design note in specs/Disrumpo about resetting or clearing on type change, and nothing in the code crossfades or primes a processor on a type switch.

One caveat: the stale content is bounded by each processor's buffer (100 ms of feedback delay, 32768 granular samples, the spectral FFT frames). It is not literally "minutes" of audio, but it can be minutes old. The same staleness also affects cross-family adapters skipped below kWeightThreshold (morph_engine.cpp:745); that is a related case, not this finding. Medium severity is fair.

The finding holds, and medium is the right severity.

How it happens:
- distortion_adapter.cpp:142-162 setType only sets currentType_, the DC-blocker flag and the block-latency fields. It never resets anything. reset() (lines 105-123) is the only place the per-type processors get cleared.
- processRaw (around lines 520-575) calls only the current type's processor: feedbackDist_.process, granular_.process, spectral_.process, and so on. Every other processor keeps its delay line, grain buffer or STFT/overlap-add state frozen at the moment it stopped being called.
- The shared processors carry real state across that gap. feedback_distortion.h:231 reads a delay line of up to kMaxDelayMs = 100 ms, with feedback up to 1.5. spectral_distortion.h:217-241 keeps pushing into stft_ and pulling from overlapAdd_, with FFT sizes up to 8192. granular_distortion.h:352 reads buffer_ and keeps a pool of active grains. None of them resets when it starts being called again; they reset only on NaN/Inf input.
- No caller makes up for it. MorphEngine::setNodes (morph_engine.cpp:131-137, reached from band_processor.h:249) calls setType on every adapter and never resets. BandProcessor's 8 ms crossfade (band_processor.h:51, 409-422) runs only when the oversampling factor changes, not when the type changes.

The worst case is in normal morphing, not only in editing. getFamily (distortion_types.h:327-344) puts Temporal and FeedbackDist in one family, Dynamic, and puts Chaos, Formant, Granular, Spectral, Fractal and Stochastic in another, Experimental. When all nodes share a family, process() takes processSameFamily. That function (morph_engine.cpp:~690-706) calls blendedAdapter_.setType with the dominant node's type on every sample. So a cursor moving between a Granular node and a Spectral node, by hand, by automation or through the sweep-morph link, swaps blendedAdapter_ from one processor to the other at the 50/50 point. The newly selected processor then plays out whatever it held when it last lost dominance, at full wet level, since one processor produces 100 % of the output. The switch is also a hard discontinuity. In the cross-family path, a node whose type goes Feedback, then something else, then back to Feedback does the same thing.

Size of the effect: up to about 100 ms of old comb ringing from FeedbackDist, decaying at the feedback rate or held up by the limiter if feedback is above 1; up to 100 ms of grains read from old audio for Granular; up to one FFT frame (8192 samples, about 186 ms at 44.1 kHz) of an old frame for Spectral. All of it arrives as a click plus ghost audio, which is what the reviewer described.

No reset on the type-change path was found in the source read, and the tests seen in distortion_adapter_test.cpp call reset() right after setType, so they never exercise a resumed processor. Severity stays medium: it is audible, it recurs during morph automation within the Dynamic and Experimental families, and it lasts at most a few hundred ms. It is not a NaN or a crash.

One more case: a cross-family node whose weight drops below kWeightThreshold (0.001, morph_node.h:139) is skipped in processCrossFamily (morph_engine.cpp:~760), so its processor also freezes and resumes stale. That fades back in with the node's weight, though, so it is quieter than the same-family switch.

findings.title: Wet-path latency of Spectral (fftSize), Granular and FeedbackDist is never reported or compensated
findings.problem: The adapter computes blockLatency_ for Spectral (fftSize) and Granular (grain samples), but getProcessingLatency() has no caller anywhere in plugins/disrumpo/src. BandProcessor::getLatency is a static that returns 0, and the processor never calls setLatencySamples. SpectralDistortion outputs 0 until the first frame and then lags by fftSize (spectral_distortion.h:225-246). FeedbackDistortion returns only the delayed feedback path, never x (feedback_distortion.h:338-340), so its wet signal is delayed by delayMs.
findings.why_wrong: Primitives with internal buffering must have their latency summed into the reported plugin latency, or have the dry path and other bands delayed to match. The adapter's own API exists for exactly that purpose and is unused.
findings.consequence: A Spectral band lags by 2048-4096 samples at the effective rate, so a band with Spectral sums misaligned with the other bands (smeared transients). At mix < 100 % both the adapter dry/wet blend and the global dry/wet blend comb-filter. Hosts get no PDC.
findings.suggested_fix: Decide the latency policy with the user: fixed max-latency PDC with per-band and dry delay lines, or accept the latency and document it. Then wire getProcessingLatency through MorphEngine/BandProcessor to setLatencySamples. Test: an impulse through a band with a Spectral node at mix 0.5 must give one peak (after compensation), not two separated by fftSize.
findings.evidence: distortion_adapter.cpp:248 getProcessingLatency (grep: only definition and declaration); band_processor.h:376-379 `static int getLatency() noexcept { return 0; }`; spectral_distortion.h:240-246 returns 0 until OLA has samples; feedback_distortion.h:340 `return processed;`
verifier_notes:
I traced the claim through the code and the core of it holds for Spectral.

- The adapter computes the latency but nothing reads it. distortion_adapter.cpp:148-151 sets blockLatency_ = typeParams_.fftSize (and :178-179 does the same in setParams). Granular gets a value at :152-155 / :180-181. getProcessingLatency() at :248-250 returns that value. A grep for getProcessingLatency, getLatency, setLatencySamples and getLatencySamples across plugins/disrumpo finds only that definition, its declaration (distortion_adapter.h:325), unit tests (distortion_adapter_test.cpp:133-149) and BandProcessor::getLatency. BandProcessor::getLatency is `static ... return 0;` (band_processor.h:376-379), and its tests only assert 0 (oversampling_performance_tests.cpp:32-58). A grep for "atency" in plugins/disrumpo/src/processor returns nothing, so the host is never told about any latency.
- The Spectral path really is delayed. processRaw case Spectral (distortion_adapter.cpp:565-567) calls spectral_.process(input). In spectral_distortion.h:217-245 each sample is pushed into the STFT, a frame is analysed and synthesised only when canAnalyze() is true, and the function returns 0.0f until overlapAdd_ has samples. So the wet output lags by about fftSize (default 2048 at distortion_adapter.h:179, range 512-4096).
- The comb filtering at partial mix is real. DistortionAdapter::process blends `dry*(1-mix) + wet*mix` (distortion_adapter.cpp:233-235) with no delay on dry. At mix < 1 the immediate dry and the delayed wet sum, and the global dry/wet blend does the same.
- The spec does not allow this much latency: specs/Disrumpo/specs-overview.md:66 says "Latency < 10ms at highest quality", and :374 says 0-256 samples. 2048 samples at 44.1 kHz is about 46 ms, so this is not a documented design choice.

Weaker parts of the finding:
- FeedbackDist returning only `processed` (feedback_distortion.h:338-340) is commented as deliberate: the effect is meant to be heard as the resonating feedback. Its delay is the effect itself, not unreported latency.
- I did not verify that Granular adds a fixed latency; grain playback from a past-input buffer is more a smear than a fixed delay.

The defect stands as stated for Spectral, and medium severity is appropriate. Separately: distortion_adapter.cpp:894-895 calls spectral_.prepare() from routeParamsToProcessor when fftSize changes, which may allocate on the audio thread; that is a different issue.

I could not refute the Spectral part. Nothing upstream compensates it, no spec records it as a design decision, and no test pins it as intended. The FeedbackDist part, and to a lesser degree the Granular part, is the wrong framing.

What the code shows:
- Latency is computed but nobody reads it. distortion_adapter.cpp:150 and :179 set blockLatency_ = fftSize for Spectral, and :155 and :181 set it to grainSizeMs*sr/1000 for Granular. getProcessingLatency() at :248-250 is only called from tests/unit/distortion_adapter_test.cpp:133-149, never from plugins/disrumpo/src.
- No PDC is reported. Nothing in plugins/disrumpo calls setLatencySamples or getLatencySamples.
- BandProcessor::getLatency is a static that returns 0 (band_processor.h:376-379). Its comment covers only the IIR oversampler (FR-018/019), not adapter latency.
- The header half-documents the issue without solving it. distortion_adapter.h:242-245 says Spectral and Granular "introduce fixed latency. Query via getProcessingLatency()", but nothing queries it. No spec in specs/Disrumpo accepts the latency, and specs-overview.md:66 says "Latency < 10ms at highest quality". fftSize ranges 512-4096 (processor_params.cpp:244), and at the 2048 default that is about 46 ms at 44.1 kHz.
- The STFT delay is real. SpectralDistortion::process returns 0 until the OLA buffer has samples, then the output lags (spectral_distortion.h:226-243).
- The comb filtering is reachable. DistortionAdapter::process blends the undelayed dry signal with the delayed wet signal (distortion_adapter.cpp:198, 234-235). At mix < 1 that is two copies fftSize apart, and the band also sums misaligned against the other bands.

Where the finding is weak:
- FeedbackDistortion returning only `processed` (feedback_distortion.h:332-334) is intentional. The comment reads "we want to hear the resonating feedback, not the dry input". That delay is the comb/resonance effect itself, not a processing latency that should get PDC.
- Granular grain delay is arguably the effect too.

The Spectral case alone carries the medium severity.

The Spectral part of the finding holds at medium severity. The Granular and FeedbackDist parts overreach.

**No caller, no reported latency.**
- `distortion_adapter.cpp:248-250` `getProcessingLatency()` returns `blockLatency_`. Grep across `plugins/disrumpo` finds callers only in `tests/unit/distortion_adapter_test.cpp:133-149`, none in `src/`.
- There is no `setLatencySamples` anywhere in `plugins/disrumpo`.
- `band_processor.h:376-379` `static int getLatency() { return 0; }` covers only the IIR oversampler.

**Spectral delays the band by 512-4096 samples.**
- The adapter calls `spectral_.process(input)` per sample (`distortion_adapter.cpp:565-567`).
- `spectral_distortion.h:217-246` pushes into the STFT, analyses only once a frame is full, and returns 0 until overlap-add has samples. `latency()` returns `fftSize_` (`spectral_distortion.h:492-493`).
- `fftSize` is 512-4096 (`processor_params.cpp:244`), default 2048 (`distortion_adapter.h:179`).
- Spectral runs at 1x (`distortion_types.h:188`, "1x types ... FFT-domain"), so there is no division by an oversampling factor. At 44.1 kHz the delay is about 12-93 ms (46 ms at the default). That breaks the stated budget of "Latency < 10ms" (`specs/Disrumpo/specs-overview.md:66`, `roadmap.md:112`).

**Consequences.**
- A band with a Spectral node sums 46 ms late against the other bands.
- At mix < 1, `distortion_adapter.cpp:235` blends `dry*(1-mix) + wet*mix`. With the wet path that late, the result is a clear slapback double at the default size, not just comb filtering.
- The host gets no PDC, so the track drifts against others in every host.
- No doc records this latency as accepted.

**Overreach.**
- FeedbackDist's delay line (`feedback_distortion.h:333-340`) is the resonator period that gives the effect its sound, not a latency to compensate.
- Granular reads grains from a buffer. The adapter's `grainSizeMs*sr` value is a guessed number for a time-based effect, not a fixed lag.

These two points narrow the scope but do not lower the severity, because the Spectral case alone gives the medium consequence.

findings.title: Bipolar node Bias and the bias mod offset are written into the field FuzzProcessor treats as unipolar, so the negative half pins Fuzz at its most-gated bias
findings.problem: kNodeBias is denormalized to [-1,1] into mn.params.bias. Fuzz/AsymFuzz slot 0 writes a unipolar [0,1] value into the same field (:73, :81). MorphEngine adds biasModOffset_*2 and clamps to [-1,1] (morph_engine.cpp:708, :735). FuzzProcessor::setBias clamps to [0,1], where 0 means the maximum 0.8 offset.
findings.why_wrong: The FuzzProcessor contract is a unipolar bias (fuzz_processor.h:364-365, 1 = centred). A bipolar source must be remapped per type before it reaches setBias, as Tube/Tape already do in the opposite direction.
findings.consequence: For a Fuzz node, the bottom half of the Bias automation range, and any negative bias modulation, all produce the same most-gated sputter. A bias mod route centred on the base value is lopsided.
findings.suggested_fix: Remap the bias per destination type in the adapter (Fuzz: (b+1)/2), or keep separate fields per type. Test: a Fuzz node with kNodeBias norm 0.0 vs 0.25 must give different output RMS.
findings.evidence: processor_params.cpp:870 `mn.params.bias = static_cast<float>(value) * 2.0f - 1.0f;`; :73 `p.bias = slots[0];  // Fuzz bias is unipolar [0,1]`; fuzz_processor.h:365 `bias_ = std::clamp(bias, 0.0f, 1.0f);`; morph_engine.cpp:708 bias + biasModOffset_*2 clamp [-1,1]
verifier_notes: I traced the claimed path through the source and it holds. (1) processor_params.cpp:868-870: kNodeBias (a RangeParameter from -1 to +1 with default 0, registered kCanAutomate at parameter_registration.cpp:930-934) writes `mn.params.bias = value*2-1` and puts no type-specific remap in between. Then :899 pushes the nodes to the BandProcessor through setMorphNodes. (2) For Fuzz and AsymmetricFuzz, mapShapeSlotsToParams writes a unipolar slot into the same field (processor_params.cpp:73, :81, comment "Fuzz bias is unipolar [0,1]"). Tube and Tape remap their slot to [-1,1] instead (:56, :63). (3) The modulation offset goes into the same field and is clamped to [-1,1]. That happens on the same-family path at morph_engine.cpp:709 (`bp.bias = clamp(bp.bias + biasModOffset_*2, -1, 1)`, then blendedAdapter_.setParams), on the cross-family path at :735, and in band_processor.h:449. (4) distortion_adapter.cpp:637 and :646 pass p.bias straight to fuzz_.setBias. (5) FuzzProcessor::setBias clamps to [0,1] (fuzz_processor.h:364-365). In process(), `biasOffset = (1 - biasValue)*0.8` (:492), so 0 gives the maximum 0.8 offset and the most gated sound (doc at :72: "0=dying battery, 1=normal"). Every kNodeBias normalized value in [0, 0.5], which includes the parameter's registered default of 0.0 (norm 0.5), therefore collapses to Fuzz bias 0, the same most-gated setting. A negative bias mod offset also bottoms out at 0 while a positive one tops out at 1, so a route centred on Fuzz's typical bias of 0.7 is lopsided. Processor state round-trips mn.params.bias raw (processor_state.cpp:334, :859), so that path does not mask the problem. The defect is real as stated. Low severity is appropriate: it needs a Fuzz or AsymFuzz node with kNodeBias automation or bias modulation, and the slot-0 path, which is the normal UI path for Fuzz bias, maps correctly.

I could not refute this. The bipolar/unipolar mismatch is real and nothing upstream remaps it.
- processor_params.cpp:868-871: kNodeBias is written as `mn.params.bias = value*2-1`, a range of [-1,1]. It writes into the same field that mapShapeSlotsToParams fills for Fuzz and AsymmetricFuzz with the unipolar slot0 value (:73, :81, both commented "Fuzz bias is unipolar [0,1]"). Tube (:56), Tape (:63) and the wavefolders (:93, :102, :111) convert their slot to [-1,1], so the per-type convention is clear.
- distortion_adapter.cpp:637 and :646 call `fuzz_.setBias(p.bias)` with no remap.
- fuzz_processor.h:364-365 clamps bias to [0,1], and :490-492 sets offset = (1-bias)*0.8, so 0 is the most-gated "dying battery" setting. Any bias at or below 0 therefore gives the same result: the bottom half of the kNodeBias range does nothing for a Fuzz node. The parameter's default (0.0, norm 0.5) also maps to the most-gated bias for Fuzz, while FuzzProcessor's own default is kDefaultBias 0.7.
- Reachability: kNodeBias is registered as an automatable RangeParameter from -1 to 1 (parameter_registration.cpp:930-934). The controller reads and writes it in preset state (controller.cpp:561, :1844). No editor.uidesc control binds Band.NodeBias, so it is reached through host automation and state/preset load rather than the GUI. Still reachable in a real host.
- Mod path: morph_engine.cpp:709 and :735 apply `bias + biasModOffset_*2` and clamp to [-1,1]. For Fuzz the negative half is dead after setBias. The finding's "lopsided around the base" wording is only partly right: with a mid-range base the [0,1] clamp is roughly symmetric. The real effect is that the mod depth is doubled relative to Fuzz's unipolar scale.
- Guards: no test covers kNodeBias with Fuzz. The only test that references it is tests/unit/parameter_encoding_test.cpp, which checks ID encoding. No spec or comment documents this as intended.
Low severity fits: the effect is confined to host automation, state load and modulation, not the visible UI.

The core claim holds, but only on a narrow path. One part of the stated consequence is wrong.

Confirmed in code:
- processor_params.cpp:868-871 sets mn.params.bias = norm*2-1, giving [-1,1].
- processor_params.cpp:73 and :81 write the unipolar Fuzz and AsymFuzz slot 0 into the same field.
- fuzz_processor.h:364-366 clamps setBias to [0,1]. At :490-493 the offset is (1-bias)*0.8, so bias 0 is the most-gated value (+0.8 DC before the clipper).
- distortion_adapter.cpp:637 and :646 pass p.bias straight to fuzz_.setBias with no remap.
- So for a Fuzz node, kNodeBias normalized values from 0.0 to 0.5 all become bias <= 0, clamp to 0, and give identical maximally-sputtery output. Half of that parameter's range is dead.

Impact is narrow because kNodeBias has no visible control:
- The Fuzz and AsymFuzz panels drive Bias through Band.NodeShape0 (editor.uidesc Fuzz and AsymFuzz templates).
- The Band.NodeBias proxy (tag 50019, uidesc:281) is declared but no view uses it.
- kNodeBias is registered as automatable (parameter_registration.cpp:930-934), so only a host automation lane or a generic host editor reaches it.
- When it does, it overwrites the slot-0 value set by the UI knob.

Save and load do not trigger it:
- processor_state.cpp:334 saves the unipolar mn.params.bias, and :859 restores it as-is.
- Neither save, load nor a preset produces a negative value for Fuzz.

The "lopsided mod route" part is wrong:
- morph_engine.cpp:709 and :735 add biasModOffset*2 to the unipolar base (e.g. 0.5) and clamp to [-1,1]. setBias then clamps to [0,1].
- Clamping around a centred base is symmetric; the route is not lopsided.
- The real effect is double sensitivity: offset +/-0.25 already sweeps the whole Fuzz range.

Net: a real but narrow defect. It is reachable only through host automation of a parameter with no UI knob, plus a 2x over-sensitive bias modulation for Fuzz. Low severity is right.

findings.title: Bitcrush maps Bits to [1,16] but BitCrusher clamps to [4,16]: the bottom 20 % of the knob is a dead zone
findings.problem: Slot 0 maps to bitDepth = 1 + slot*15, and the jitter path clamps to [1,16] (distortion_adapter.cpp:463). BitCrusher::setBitDepth clamps to [kMinBitDepth 4, 16].
findings.why_wrong: The plugin mapping must match the primitive's accepted range, or the primitive must support 1-3 bits.
findings.consequence: Bits 1-4 sound identical, so the first 20 % of the knob and of jitter excursions below 4 bits do nothing. setBitDepth also runs std::pow per sample (distortion_adapter.cpp:467).
findings.suggested_fix: Map slot 0 to [4,16] (and clamp jitter to 4), or lower BitCrusher's minimum (a shared header: check consumers). Test: Bitcrush outputs at slot 0.0 and 0.15 must differ.
findings.evidence: processor_params.cpp:131 `p.bitDepth = 1.0f + slots[0] * 15.0f;`; bit_crusher.h:50 kMinBitDepth = 4.0f; :152 clamp(bits, kMinBitDepth, kMaxBitDepth); distortion_adapter.cpp:463 clamp(…, 1.0f, 16.0f)
verifier_notes: I traced the code path and the defect is real. plugins/disrumpo/src/processor/processor_params.cpp:131 sets `p.bitDepth = 1.0f + slots[0] * 15.0f;`, which gives [1,16]. That value goes to DistortionAdapter: setParams at distortion_adapter.cpp:709 calls `rawBitCrusher_.setBitDepth(p.bitDepth)`, and processRaw at distortion_adapter.cpp:454-467 adds the jitter offset, clamps it to `std::clamp(bitDepth + offset, 1.0f, 16.0f)` (:463) and calls `rawBitCrusher_.setBitDepth(bitDepth)` once per sample (:467). rawBitCrusher_ is a `Krate::DSP::BitCrusher` (distortion_adapter.h:405). BitCrusher::setBitDepth (dsp/include/krate/dsp/primitives/bit_crusher.h:151-154) clamps to [kMinBitDepth=4 (:50), kMaxBitDepth=16]. So any slot0 below 0.2 (bitDepth below 4) is clamped to 4 and sounds the same, and jitter can never go below 4 bits. The existing test also says so: distortion_adapter_test.cpp:921 comments 'Slot0 = 0.0 -> bitDepth = 4' even though its own helper at :907 maps 0.0 to 1.0. The DistortionParams doc (distortion_adapter.h:109) says [1,16], which BitCrusher does not support. The side claim holds too: setBitDepth calls updateQuantizationLevels, which runs std::pow (bit_crusher.h:~180), and that happens on every sample in processRaw. This is only a usability and efficiency defect, with no NaN, crash or real-time violation, so severity stays low.

I could not refute this. processor_params.cpp:131 maps the slot with `p.bitDepth = 1.0f + slots[0] * 15.0f; // [0,1] → [1,16]`. The jitter path in distortion_adapter.cpp:463 clamps to [1,16], and :467 then calls rawBitCrusher_.setBitDepth(bitDepth) on every sample. The shared primitive in bit_crusher.h:50 sets `kMinBitDepth = 4.0f`, and setBitDepth at :151-152 clamps to [4,16]; its doc comment (:150) says "[4, 16]". So any bit depth from 1 to 4 comes out as 4 bits. That covers slot values 0 to 0.2, the bottom 20 % of the knob.

Nothing marks this as intended. The Disrumpo specs promise the full range: specs-overview.md:218 says "Bit Depth (1.0-16.0)", ui-mockups.md:474/486 say "1-16" / "1.0 - 16.0", and dsp-details.md:213 says "[1, 16]". The code comment at :131 also says [1,16].

No test pins the low range either. distortion_adapter_test.cpp:794 sets bitDepth = 2.0f but only asserts that the output differs from the input (:804), which passes at the clamped 4 bits too. The tests at :870 and morph_band_integration_test.cpp:370 also use 2.0f without checking 1-3-bit behaviour.

Nothing upstream clamps the value to 4, and setActive does nothing that changes this. The mismatch is real and reachable from any host by moving the Bits knob to its bottom 20 %. Low severity is right, since it loses resolution rather than corrupting audio.

The dead zone is real and the low severity is right. processor_params.cpp:131 sets `p.bitDepth = 1.0f + slots[0] * 15.0f`, so the Bits knob covers 1 to 16 bits. distortion_adapter.cpp:454-467 (per sample) and :709 (on parameter apply) pass that value straight to `rawBitCrusher_.setBitDepth`. The Krate::DSP::BitCrusher there clamps the value to [kMinBitDepth = 4, kMaxBitDepth = 16] (bit_crusher.h:50-51 and :152). So any slot value from 0 to 0.2 (1 to 4 bits) produces exactly the same 4-bit quantizer, with the same levels_ and the same output. Jitter widens it: distortion_adapter.cpp:462-463 adds up to ±2 bits and clamps to [1,16], so near the bottom of the knob every downward jitter excursion is clamped again to 4 inside the primitive. The noise becomes one-sided instead of the symmetric ±2 bits the comment at :456 promises. The cost is usability, not sound: no NaN, no level jump and no click. The lowest reachable depth is still 4 bits (15 levels, roughly 24 dB SNR), and 20 % of the knob travel plus the bottom of the jitter range do nothing. Low severity fits. The secondary point holds: the Bitcrush case calls setBitDepth on every sample (:467), which runs updateQuantizationLevels. That is an efficiency issue, not a correctness one. Not part of the finding: the node-level kNodeBitDepth mapping at processor_params.cpp:878 (`4 + round(v*20)`, range 4 to 24) hits the same primitive's 16-bit ceiling, so the top 40 % of that parameter is also dead. That backs the claim that the plugin's mappings and the primitive's accepted range do not match.

findings.title: AllpassSaturator::process reconfigures 9 biquads/stages (trig) every sample regardless of the active topology
findings.problem: Every sample, process() calls singleStage_.setFrequency, configures all 4 chain allpass biquads (sin/cos), and sets 4 matrix stages' frequency/drive, even when the smoothed frequency is constant and only one topology is in use. Disrumpo calls it per sample per channel (via the shared instance) per node.
findings.why_wrong: Coefficient recomputation should happen only when the smoothed frequency changed, and only for the active topology.
findings.consequence: About 9 coefficient designs (each with trig) per sample per AllpassResonant node, so 4 bands x 4 nodes in cross-family mode costs a large CPU share for no audible benefit.
findings.suggested_fix: Cache the last smoothed frequency and drive, and reconfigure only the active topology when they change. Test: add a CPU-budget case in the [performance] lane, plus a bit-identity case showing output is unchanged.
findings.evidence: allpass_saturator.h:734-735 singleStage_.setFrequency/setDrive; :738-742 chainAllpasses_[i].configure(...) loop; :749-752 matrixStages_ loop, all before the topology switch at :756
verifier_notes: I could not refute this. I traced the code and the claim is accurate. In dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/allpass_saturator.h:715-778, AllpassSaturator::process() advances the smoothers (:728-730) on every call. Without checking whether the smoothed values changed, it then calls singleStage_.setFrequency (:734), which runs allpass_.configure at :471. Next it calls chainAllpasses_[i].configure for 4 biquads (:738-742) and matrixStages_[i].setFrequency for 4 stages (:749-752), each of which also runs Biquad::configure (:471). That is 9 Biquad::configure calls per sample. All of them happen before the topology switch at :756, which uses only one of the three groups (single, chain or matrix; KarplusStrong uses none of them). Biquad::configure (dsp/include/krate/dsp/primitives/biquad.h:330-337) calls BiquadCoefficients::calculate, which computes std::sin and std::cos at :677-678. So each sample costs 9 sin+cos pairs plus the divisions. Disrumpo calls it once per sample through DistortionAdapter (plugins/disrumpo/src/dsp/distortion_adapter.cpp:548, `return allpassSaturator_.process(input);`), and prepare/setters are at :74 and :824-843. The defect is real but only costs CPU: the output is correct, nothing is unsafe for real time, and nothing is audible. Low severity fits.

The defect is real. I found no upstream guard, no documented design decision and no test that pins this behaviour.

In dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/allpass_saturator.h, AllpassSaturator::process (715-778) does the following on every sample, before the topology switch at 756:
- singleStage_.setFrequency at 734. That function is SaturatedAllpassStage::setFrequency (469-472), which calls allpass_.configure(FilterType::Allpass, hz, 10.0f, ...).
- A loop at 738-742 that runs chainAllpasses_[i].configure four times.
- A loop at 749-752 that runs matrixStages_[i].setFrequency four times, and each of those calls configure as well.

That makes 9 Biquad::configure calls per sample. Biquad::configure (dsp/include/krate/dsp/primitives/biquad.h:330-338) calls BiquadCoefficients::calculate (659+), which always computes std::sin(omega) and std::cos(omega) (677-678). Nothing caches the last smoothed frequency. Only one topology is ever processed (756-769), so 3 of the 4 sets of updates do nothing useful each sample.

Disrumpo calls this once per sample through DistortionAdapter (plugins/disrumpo/src/dsp/distortion_adapter.cpp:546-548, `return allpassSaturator_.process(input);`). The setters at 822-843 only update the smoother targets, so the per-sample work in process() stays.

I found no CPU or performance test in dsp/tests/unit/processors/allpass_saturator_tests.cpp, and no comment or spec text saying the per-sample reconfiguration is intended. The finding's own suggested fix (an output bit-identity test plus a [performance] case) is reasonable. Even if the smoother has settled, the trig still runs, because process() has no check for a changed value.

The impact is CPU cost only. The output is correct and nothing is unsafe for the real-time thread (no allocation, no lock), so the low severity is right.

I could not refute it. The source confirms the wasted per-sample work, and the consequence is CPU cost only, which fits "low".

The defect:
- allpass_saturator.h:733-752 runs on every process() call, before the topology switch at :756.
- It calls singleStage_.setFrequency, which does a Biquad configure (:469-472). It also runs 4 chainAllpasses_[i].configure calls (:738-742) and 4 matrixStages_[i].setFrequency calls (:749-752).
- That is 9 calls to BiquadCoefficients::calculate per sample. Each one does a divide plus std::sin and std::cos (biquad.h:659-679), so 18 trig calls per sample.
- Only the active topology uses its own filters. KarplusStrong uses none of the 9 biquads, SingleAllpass uses 1 of 9, AllpassChain uses 4, FeedbackMatrix uses 4.
- After frequencySmoother_ settles, every one of these recomputations is redundant.

How Disrumpo multiplies the cost:
- DistortionAdapter::process calls allpassSaturator_.process(input) per sample (distortion_adapter.cpp:546-548).
- BandProcessor calls morphEngine_->process separately for left and right inside the per-sample oversampled loop (band_processor.h:752-754 and :487-488).
- AllpassResonant's recommended oversampling factor is 4x (distortion_types.h:179-180).
- So one AllpassResonant adapter costs 9 × 2 channels × 4 = 72 coefficient designs (144 sin/cos) per host sample.
- With cross-family morphing (morph_engine.cpp:390-392, :752), several AllpassResonant nodes can sit in one band next to a node of another family, each with its own adapter, and this repeats across up to 4 bands.

Correction to the finding: "4 bands × 4 nodes" overstates the worst case. If all 4 nodes are AllpassResonant they are the same family and collapse into one blendedAdapter_ (morph_engine.cpp:718), so cross-family allows at most 3 per band.

No dsp/tests file has a perf or CPU case for AllpassSaturator.

Impact is CPU only:
- The work is bounded, with no allocation, lock or unbounded loop, so it does not break the real-time rules.
- Output does not change, because recomputing coefficients for unused filters has no audible effect.
- I made a rough estimate of 2-3 µs per 22.7 µs sample period per adapter at 44.1 kHz, which grows linearly with sample rate. I did not measure this.

So "low" is the right severity for an efficiency defect in a shared header.

findings.title: Stream layout v12 has three hand-written codecs with literal denominators; the preset writer has already drifted in three places and no test covers it
findings.problem: Processor::getState/setState (processor_state.cpp), Controller::parseComponentState (controller.cpp:150-617) and Controller::createComponentStateStream (controller.cpp:1687-1866) each re-encode the same positional stream by hand. No field table or schema is shared between them. The preset writer decodes list params through a lambda `getInt8FromList(id, maxVal)` that takes a magic denominator at every call site (5, 12, 25, 3, 2, kMorphLinkModeCount-1), when it could use the constants the other two codecs use.
findings.why_wrong: Every encoder and decoder of one append-only format has to agree field by field. Because each copy carries its own literals, they have already drifted. (1) Routing source is written with denominator 12 (`getInt8FromList(makeRoutingParamId(r, 0), 12)`), but processor_params.cpp:555 and the parse path decode with kUIModSourceCount-1 = 13. (2) activeNodes is written as `round(norm*2)+2`, but the list has 4 entries (1..4, norm k/3). (3) The session writer stores morphMode and morphSmoothing as literals 0 and 0.0f (processor_state.cpp:319, :323), while the preset writer stores the real values (:1829, :1834). (4) The preset writer always writes the 2-point curve (0,0),(1,1) (:1748-1750), while getState writes the real breakpoints.
findings.consequence: User presets and host sessions of the same patch differ. A user preset reload moves routing sources 7..13 one slot down and turns 1-node bands into 2 and 2-node bands into 3. A host session reload drops morph mode and smoothing. grep finds createComponentStateStream only in controller.cpp/.h and in no test, so nothing catches the next drift.
findings.suggested_fix: Fix the three drifts with the shared constants (kUIModSourceCount-1; activeNodes = round(norm*3)+1; write the cache's morphMode/smoothing in getState). Then add a round-trip test: set a non-default value for every parameter on the controller, run createComponentStateStream -> Processor::setState -> Processor::getState -> Controller::parseComponentState, and assert that every normalized value comes back within a list-step tolerance. Longer term, drive all three codecs from one constexpr field descriptor table.
findings.evidence: controller.cpp:1815 `streamer.writeInt8(getInt8FromList(makeRoutingParamId(r, 0), 12));`; :1830-1831 `int activeNodes = static_cast<int>(std::round(activeNodesNorm * 2.0f)) + 2;`; :1748-1750 `writeInt32(2); writeFloat(0.0f); writeFloat(0.0f); writeFloat(1.0f); writeFloat(1.0f);`; processor_state.cpp:319 `writeInt8(static_cast<Steinberg::int8>(0))  // morphMode`, :323 `writeFloat(0.0f)  // morphSmoothing (ms)`; grep -rln createComponentStateStream tests -> no hits.
verifier_notes:
I could not refute it. All four drifts are real in the source.

(1) Routing source. parameter_registration.cpp:563-578 registers a 14-entry StringListParameter, so the normalized value is k/13. processor_params.cpp:555 and controller.cpp:468-469 both decode with kUIModSourceCount-1 = 13 (plugin_ids.h:546). The preset writer at controller.cpp:1815 uses `getInt8FromList(makeRoutingParamId(r, 0), 12)`, which computes round(k/13*12): k=6 gives 6, k=7 also gives 6 (6.46), k=8 gives 7, k=13 gives 12. Every source from 7 to 13 is written one slot low. The processor reads that int8 as the raw ModSource (processor_state.cpp:768-770), so a reloaded user preset routes the wrong source.

(2) activeNodes. The list has 4 entries "1".."4" (parameter_registration.cpp:699-707). The processor decodes it as idx = value*3, count = idx+1 (processor_params.cpp:949-952), and parseComponentState encodes it as (count-1)/3 (controller.cpp:526). The writer at controller.cpp:1831 computes round(norm*2)+2: count 1 is written as 2, count 2 as 3 (round 0.667 = 1), count 3 as 3, count 4 as 4. kMinActiveNodes is 1 and kDefaultActiveNodes is 1 (morph_node.h:132,135), so the default 1-node band comes back as 2 nodes.

(3) Session writer. processor_state.cpp:319 writes morphMode as the literal 0 and :323 writes morphSmoothing as 0.0f. On reload, Processor::setState applies them (processor_state.cpp:827-831) and parseComponentState sets both params from them (controller.cpp:522-529). Controller::getState (controller.cpp:658-677) saves only the MIDI mappings, so nothing else restores these params. A host session reload resets morph mode and smoothing.

(4) Sweep curve. The preset writer always writes the 2-point identity curve (controller.cpp:1748-1750), even though the controller holds the curve as kSweepCustomCurvePointCount/P*X/P*Y params (controller.cpp:1148-1177) and getState writes the real breakpoints (processor_state.cpp:143-148).

Test coverage: createComponentStateStream appears only in controller.h:170 and controller.cpp:117/1687, and grep finds it in no test. The duplication claim holds as well: the literal denominators sit at each call site (lines 1740, 1754, 1770, 1774, 1777, 1811, 1815, 1829, 1838).

The drifts are real. Nothing upstream guards against them, no test pins this code, and I found no comment or spec that calls them a design decision.

(1) Routing source. parameter_registration.cpp:563-578 registers 14 list entries (None..Transient), and plugin_ids.h:546 has kUIModSourceCount = 14, so a step is k/13. The decoders divide by 13: controller.cpp:468-469 (parse) and processor_params.cpp:555 (processor). The preset writer at controller.cpp:1815 uses getInt8FromList(makeRoutingParamId(r,0), 12), which computes round(k*12/13). For k=7 that is round(6.46) = 6, and every k from 7 to 13 lands one slot lower (Macro 3 becomes Macro 2, and so on).

(2) Active nodes. parameter_registration.cpp:702-705 registers a 4-entry list "1".."4". processor_params.cpp:950-952 decodes it as idx = value*3 + 0.5, count = idx + 1, and the parse path controller.cpp:526 writes (count-1)/3. The preset writer at controller.cpp:1831 uses round(norm*2)+2. So 1 node (norm 0) is saved as 2, and 2 nodes (norm 1/3) are saved as round(0.667)+2 = 3. Reload goes through processor_state.cpp:829-830 and controller.cpp:525, which clamp the stored count to [kMinActiveNodes=1, 4] (morph_node.h:132) and take it as is.

(3) Morph mode and smoothing. Processor::getState writes the literals 0 (processor_state.cpp:319, morphMode) and 0.0f (:323, morphSmoothing), even though processor_params.cpp:958-969 applies the real values. setState then restores them as 0 (processor_state.cpp:827-831), and the controller's parse sets the params from the same stream (controller.cpp:523, 529). Controller::getState/setState (controller.cpp:658-700) store only the window size and MIDI-CC data, so nothing else restores these values. A host session reload drops morph mode and smoothing, while the preset writer at :1829 and :1834 saves the real ones.

(4) Sweep curve. The preset writer at :1748-1750 always writes the 2-point curve (0,0),(1,1). This is the weakest of the four, because the breakpoints may not exist as controller params, but it is still a difference between the two writers.

Reachability: createComponentStateStream is the PresetManager state provider (controller.cpp:116-118), so every user preset save goes through it. grep over tests/ finds no reference to createComponentStateStream. Factory presets come from the separate generator, so the defects hit user-saved presets and host sessions. The severity is justified: patches are silently changed with no test catching it.

I checked each drift in the source, and the consequences happen as claimed.

(1) Routing source. parameter_registration.cpp:563-579 registers 14 Route Source entries (None..Transient), so norm = k/13. The preset writer at controller.cpp:1815 writes round(norm*12). Indices 7..13 come out as 6..12: 7/13*12 = 6.46 rounds to 6, and 13 becomes 12. Processor::setState (processor_state.cpp:768-770) reads that int8 back as the source index. A user preset routing Macro 3, Macro 4, Chaos, Rungler, S&H, Pitch or Transient therefore reloads routed from the previous source. The processor's own param path (processor_params.cpp:555) and the controller parse (controller.cpp:468-469) both use kUIModSourceCount-1 = 13, which confirms the writer is the one that drifted.

(2) Active nodes. The list has 4 entries "1".."4" (parameter_registration.cpp:702-706), and its default is norm 0.0, which is "1". kMinActiveNodes = 1 (morph_node.h:132). The processor decodes idx = value*3 (processor_params.cpp:951-952), and the parse encodes (count-1)/3 (controller.cpp:526). The writer instead computes round(norm*2)+2 (controller.cpp:1831): "1" becomes 2, "2" becomes 3 (round(0.667) = 1, plus 2), and "3" and "4" survive. Setting the 2-node case aside, a band left at the default "1" saves as 2 nodes, so a saved user preset morphs in a second node. That is an audible change on the most common setting.

(3) Session state. getState writes a literal 0 for morphMode (processor_state.cpp:319) and 0.0f for morphSmoothing (processor_state.cpp:323). setState then applies those zeros (processor_state.cpp:827-831). Controller::getState/setState (controller.cpp:658-701) store only MIDI CC mappings, so nothing else restores these two values. Every host session reload resets each band to 1D Linear with 0 ms smoothing. Meanwhile the preset writer stores the real values (controller.cpp:1829, 1834).

(4) Sweep curve. The preset writer always writes the identity 2-point curve (controller.cpp:1748-1750), while getState writes the real breakpoints (processor_state.cpp:~140-151).

(5) No tests. grep finds Disrumpo's createComponentStateStream only in controller.cpp/.h (it is the preset stateProvider at controller.cpp:117) and in no Disrumpo test.

Impact: user-preset save and host-session reload both lose data silently, on default and common settings, with no test coverage. High severity holds.

findings.title: Crossover Hz<->normalized log10 mapping is copied in four places, and two controller paths call the linear RangeParameter toNormalized/toPlain instead
findings.problem: The log10 crossover mapping (logMin = log10(kMinCrossoverHz) ...) is written separately in processor_params.cpp:988-991, visibility_controllers.cpp:643-647 (CrossoverDragBridge), crossover_network.h:259-260 and parameter_registration.cpp:145-149. No shared helper exists, so two controller sites fall back to the RangeParameter's linear toNormalized/toPlain. parseComponentState sends `param->toNormalized(freq)`, which is linear. createCustomView seeds the spectrum dividers with `crossoverParam->toPlain(crossoverParam->getNormalized())`, which is also linear.
findings.why_wrong: The processor decodes crossover params as pow(10, logMin + v*(logMax-logMin)). Every writer must therefore use the same log encoding. The drag bridge does; the preset-load path and the divider seeding do not.
findings.consequence: Example: a preset stores crossover 1000 Hz. loadComponentStateWithNotify performEdits the linear norm (1000-20)/19980 = 0.049, and the processor decodes that as 10^(1.301+0.049*3) = ~28 Hz. Preset-browser loads put the crossovers in the wrong place. On editor open, the dividers are drawn at the linear interpretation of the stored normalized value, not where the audio splits.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one pair of inline helpers, crossoverHzToNorm and crossoverNormToHz, in band_state.h (DSP-side, so both processor and controller can include it). Replace all four copies with them and use them at controller.cpp:210 and :950. Test: parseComponentState of a stream with crossover 1000 Hz must produce norm = (3-1.301)/3 (about 0.566), and processParameterChanges with that norm must set crossoverL_.getCrossoverFrequency(0) to 1000 Hz +/-1 Hz.
findings.evidence: controller.cpp:210 `setter(param->getInfo().id, param->toNormalized(freq));`; :950 `float freq = static_cast<float>(crossoverParam->toPlain(crossoverParam->getNormalized()));`; visibility_controllers.cpp:643-647 `const float logMin = std::log10(kMinCrossoverHz); ... double normalized = (logFreq - logMin)/(logMax - logMin)`; processor_params.cpp:988-989 same log10 formula; parameter_registration.cpp:152-158 `new RangeParameter(..., kMinCrossoverHz, kMaxCrossoverHz, defaultFreq, ...)` (linear).
verifier_notes:
The finding holds. The crossover parameter is a linear Steinberg::Vst::RangeParameter(kMinCrossoverHz=20, kMaxCrossoverHz=20000) (parameter_registration.cpp:151-160; band_state.h:67). Its toNormalized/toPlain are therefore linear. The processor, however, decodes crossover normalized values logarithmically: freqHz = 10^(log10(20) + v*(log10(20000)-log10(20))) at processor_params.cpp:984-993. The processor's state stores plain Hz (processor_state.cpp:74-76 writes crossoverL_.getCrossoverFrequency(c); :447-456 reads Hz).

In parseComponentState, controller.cpp:203-210 reads that Hz float and calls setter(id, param->toNormalized(freq)), which is the linear map. On the preset-browser path, controller.cpp:123 calls loadComponentStateWithNotify (1876-1891). That uses the setter editParamWithNotify (1868-1873), which calls performEdit(id, value), so the linear norm goes to the processor. For 1000 Hz the norm is (1000-20)/19980 = 0.049. The processor decodes 10^(1.301 + 0.049*3) = ~28 Hz, which is the misplacement the finding claims.

controller.cpp:950 seeds SpectrumDisplay dividers with crossoverParam->toPlain(getNormalized()), which is also linear. Meanwhile CrossoverDragBridge (visibility_controllers.cpp:637-647) writes log-encoded norms into the same parameter. The encodings are inconsistent. Nothing in the controller re-maps crossover IDs logarithmically: the only log sites are the drag bridge and the registration default computation. The log formula is duplicated at processor_params.cpp:988-991, visibility_controllers.cpp:643-647, crossover_network.h:259-264 and parameter_registration.cpp:145-149, with no shared helper.

A related symptom the finding does not mention: the registered default is defaultFreq passed as a linear plain value. The host's default normalized value is therefore linear, and the processor decodes it logarithmically. This adds to the same root cause. Severity high is justified, because factory and user presets load with the crossovers in the wrong place through the preset browser.

The defect is real and nothing elsewhere guards it. The processor decodes crossover params on a log scale: processor_params.cpp:987-993 computes freqHz = pow(10, log10(20) + v*(log10(20000)-log10(20))). The controller registers the same IDs as a linear RangeParameter(20, 20000) at parameter_registration.cpp:151-160; the log math at :145-149 only sets the default Hz.

The preset-browser load path goes PresetManager loadProvider (controller.cpp:120-124) -> loadComponentStateWithNotify (:1876-1891) -> parseComponentState with a setter that calls editParamWithNotify (:1868-1873), and that calls performEdit. parseComponentState reads the Hz the processor stored (processor_state.cpp:74-78 writes crossoverL_.getCrossoverFrequency) and sends param->toNormalized(freq) at controller.cpp:210, which is linear. A preset at 1000 Hz therefore sends (1000-20)/19980 = 0.049, and the processor decodes that as 10^(1.301+0.049*3) = ~28 Hz.

createComponentStateStream also uses the linear toPlain (getFloat at :1695-1697, :1729). Saving after a log-norm writer (the drag bridge at visibility_controllers.cpp:641-647, or host automation) stores the wrong Hz. Host-generic displays of the parameter, via RangeParameter::toString, are linear and disagree with the audio as well.

The only test, crossover_interaction_test.cpp:283-309, reimplements its own local log2 mapping. It never exercises the controller's toNormalized or the processor decode, so nothing pins the actual behaviour. I found no spec or code comment that documents a linear mapping as intended; the test and the processor comments both say logarithmic.

One correction: right after a plain host setComponentState, controller.cpp:950's linear toPlain round-trips the linear norm that parseComponentState stored, so the dividers draw at the correct Hz. The seeding is only wrong after a log-norm writer such as a drag or automation. The headline defect is unaffected: preset loads through the in-plugin browser move the audible crossovers.

I confirmed this from source. The crossover parameters are registered as linear `RangeParameter(20, 20000)` (parameter_registration.cpp:151-160). The processor decodes the normalized value on a log10 scale: processor_params.cpp:988-991 computes `pow(10, logMin + v*(logMax-logMin))`. The CrossoverDragBridge also writes log-normalized values (visibility_controllers.cpp:643-652).

**Preset-browser load.** `presetManager_->setLoadProvider` calls `loadComponentStateWithNotify` (controller.cpp:120-124). That function uses `editParamWithNotify`, which calls `setParamNormalized` and `performEdit` (controller.cpp:1868-1891). It reaches `parseComponentState`, which reads the crossover in Hz and sends `param->toNormalized(freq)`, the linear value (controller.cpp:204-210). For a 1000 Hz crossover that is (1000-20)/19980 = 0.0490. The processor decodes 0.0490 as 10^(1.30103 + 0.0490*3.0) ≈ 28 Hz. The audible split moves by about 5 octaves on every preset-browser load of a state that holds real Hz. The processor's own getState writes `crossoverL_.getCrossoverFrequency` in Hz (processor_state.cpp:74-76), so states in that format carry real Hz.

**Divider seeding.** controller.cpp:950 seeds the spectrum dividers with linear `toPlain(getNormalized())`. After a drag to 1000 Hz (norm 0.566), the dividers are drawn at 20 + 0.566*19980 ≈ 11.3 kHz on the next editor open, while the audio still splits at 1 kHz.

**Preset save.** `createComponentStateStream` writes crossovers through the same linear `getFloat`/`toPlain` (controller.cpp:1696, 1729). A browser-saved preset of a drag-set 1 kHz crossover therefore stores 11.3 kHz. The processor's setState then applies that value directly (processor_state.cpp:450-456) when the host restores the file.

**Parameter default.** The default norm is the linear normalization of the log-spaced default. Crossover 1 defaults to about 112 Hz, which is norm ≈ 0.0046 linear, and the processor decodes that as about 20.6 Hz. So a host "reset to default" also misplaces it.

No test checks parseComponentState against the processor's crossover frequency; I checked the crossover_interaction and parameter_encoding test greps. The consequence is real, reachable through the preset browser in any host, and large: tens of dB of change in band balance. High severity stands. The real defect is a correctness bug in the encoding, not only duplication.

findings.title: MorphLinkMode curves have two implementations with opposite meanings for the same enum and labels
findings.problem: controller/morph_link.cpp applyMorphLinkMode and dsp/sweep_morph_link.h applyMorphLinkCurve both switch on Disrumpo::MorphLinkMode but implement different curves. EaseIn is sqrt(x) in the controller and x^2 in the DSP. EaseOut is x^2 in the controller and 1-(1-x)^2 in the DSP. HoldRise breaks at 0.5 in the controller and 0.6 in the DSP. Stepped has 5 levels (0, .25, .5, .75, 1) in the controller and 4 levels (0, .333, .667, 1) in the DSP. None returns the manual position in the controller and 0.5 in the DSP. Each copy has its own test file pinning its own version (tests/unit/morph_link_test.cpp vs tests/dsp/sweep_morph_link_tests.cpp).
findings.why_wrong: One enum with one set of user-facing names ('Ease In', 'Ease Out', ...) and one doc comment (plugin_ids.h:644-647, which describes the controller's 5-step Stepped) must map to one curve. Today the controller copy drives the band Morph X/Y Link (MorphSweepLinkController, visibility_controllers.cpp:194-195). The DSP copy is reached only through SweepProcessor::getMorphPosition, which has no caller.
findings.consequence: 'Ease In' means the opposite curve depending on which path reads it. Wiring the sweep-side morph link (kSweepMorphLink) to getMorphPosition, the obvious fix for that dead feature, would make the same label behave differently from the band X/Y links.
