findings.title: Sweep frequency and width denormalisation is copied in about 8 places; the only odd one out is the host-facing registration, and the 0.286 width default is a copy-paste formula slip
findings.problem: The log2 20-20k sweep mapping is re-declared as local constants in processor_params.cpp:381-384, controller.cpp:1280-1285, sweep_lfo.h:232-233, sweep_envelope.h:221-222 and sweep_morph_link.h:38-41. It also appears as natural-log (morph_link.cpp:80-98) and kLogRatio (sweep_indicator.h:155, spectrum_display.h:192) variants. The processor itself inlines the LFO octave-shift math at processor.cpp:347-354 instead of calling SweepLFO::getModulatedFrequency, which duplicates it. The width range 0.5..4 is written as local kMinWidth/kMaxWidth at processor.cpp:280-282, processor_params.cpp:394-397, controller.cpp:1287-1290 and visibility_controllers.cpp:548-551 and :587-590, and as literals at processor_state.cpp:89 and :486. That is despite kMinSweepWidth/kMaxSweepWidth existing at sweep_processor.h:46-49. The one place that does not follow the log mapping is the RangeParameter registration (linear 20..20000 Hz).
findings.why_wrong: A parameter's normalized<->plain mapping must be defined once and shared by registration, processor, state and UI. The atomic default baseSweepWidthNorm_{0.286f} (processor.h:227) equals 1.0/3.5, the width formula with the -0.5 offset dropped. The intended 1.0 oct is (1.0-0.5)/3.5 = 0.143, so 0.286 gives 1.5 oct. That is the kind of slip a single helper prevents.
findings.consequence: The host shows linear Hz for a log-decoded parameter: default 1000 Hz becomes norm 0.049, which the processor reads as ~28 Hz. A fresh instance runs at 1.5 oct width while the registration says 1.0 oct. Seven copies have to be kept in sync by hand for any future range change.
findings.suggested_fix: Use sweep_morph_link.h's normalizeSweepFrequency/denormalizeSweepFrequency and new width helpers built on sweep_processor.h's kMinSweepWidth/kMaxSweepWidth everywhere. Register Sweep Frequency as a Parameter subclass whose toPlain/toNormalized call those helpers, so host text matches the DSP. Set the default norm with the helper. Test: for every sweep param, registration toPlain(defaultNormalized) must equal the processor's decoded value for the same norm.
findings.evidence: processor_params.cpp:381-384 `constexpr float kSweepLog2Min = 4.321928f; ... pow(2, log2Freq)`; controller.cpp:1280-1285 identical local copy; sweep_lfo.h:232-233 and sweep_envelope.h:221-222 `constexpr float kLog2Min = 4.321928f;`; processor_state.cpp:89 `(sweepProcessor_.getWidth() - 0.5f) / 3.5f`; sweep_processor.h:46-49 `kMinSweepWidth = 0.5f; kMaxSweepWidth = 4.0f`; parameter_registration.cpp:183-188 `new RangeParameter(STR16("Sweep Frequency"), ..., 20.0, 20000.0, 1000.0, 0, kCanAutomate)`.
verifier_notes:
The main defect holds up in the source. One sub-claim about the width default has its cause backwards.

1. Frequency. parameter_registration.cpp:182-191 registers Sweep Frequency as a linear RangeParameter(20, 20000, default 1000). The processor decodes the same normalized value on a log2 scale: processor_params.cpp:381-388 does pow(2, 4.321928 + v*9.965784), and processor_state.cpp:480-483 and processor.cpp:270-273 do the same through normalizeSweepFrequency/denormalizeSweepFrequency. Controller::getParamStringByValue (controller.cpp:747-893) has no sweep branch, so it falls through to EditControllerEx1, which formats the value with the RangeParameter's linear toPlain. Re-derived numbers:
   - The registration default normalizes to (1000-20)/19980 = 0.0490. The processor decodes 0.0490 as 2^(4.3219+0.0490*9.966) ≈ 28 Hz.
   - The processor's own state default, 0.566 (processor_state.cpp / controller.cpp:217), is about 1 kHz in log terms. The host displays it as 20 + 0.566*19980 ≈ 11.3 kHz.
   So the host's display and reset-to-default disagree with the DSP. That part of the claim is confirmed.

2. Duplication. The local copies exist as cited: kSweepLog2Min/Max in processor_params.cpp:381-383 and controller.cpp:1280-1282, kMinWidth/kMaxWidth in processor.cpp:280-281, processor_params.cpp:394-395 and controller.cpp:1287-1288, and literals in processor_state.cpp:89 and :486. Shared kMinSweepWidth/kMaxSweepWidth already exist at sweep_processor.h:46-49.

3. Width default (cause wrong, mismatch real). The finding says 0.286 is a copy-paste slip meant to be 1.0 oct. That is wrong. sweep_processor.h:52 sets kDefaultSweepWidth = 1.5f, specs/Disrumpo/specs-overview.md:408 lists the Sweep Width default as 1.5 oct, and (1.5-0.5)/3.5 = 0.2857. So 0.286 at processor.h:227 is correct. The slip is the registration default of 1.0 oct at parameter_registration.cpp:198. A real default mismatch between registration and DSP still exists; it just sits on the registration side, not in the processor atom.

The width mapping itself (linear 0.5..4) is consistent between the RangeParameter and the processor. The finding is not refuted. Medium severity fits: wrong host-facing value, display and reset-to-default for an automatable parameter, plus drift-prone duplication.

The core defect holds; one sub-claim is wrong.

Confirmed:
- processor_params.cpp:381-385 decodes Sweep Frequency on a log2 scale, 2^(log2 20 + v*range).
- parameter_registration.cpp:182-190 registers it as a linear RangeParameter(20, 20000, default 1000). Its own comment says "log scale", but RangeParameter maps linearly.
- Effect on the host side: the normalized default is (1000-20)/19980 = 0.049, which the processor decodes as about 28 Hz. A processor-state norm of 0.566 (the log-1 kHz value used at processor_state.cpp:472 and controller.cpp:219) displays as about 11.3 kHz in the host.
- No test pins the registration mapping. parameter_encoding_test.cpp only checks IDs (lines 54-69, 233-236). No setActive reset or upstream clamp hides the mismatch.
- The duplication is real: the same local constants appear at processor_params.cpp:381-384 and 394-395, controller.cpp:1281-1290, processor.cpp:280-282, and processor_state.cpp:89/486. The shared normalizeSweepFrequency/denormalizeSweepFrequency helpers already exist and are used at processor.cpp:270-273 and processor_state.cpp:481.

Refuted:
- The "0.286 is a copy-paste slip" part is wrong. specs/Disrumpo/specs-overview.md:408 sets the Sweep Width default to 1.5 oct, which is exactly 0.5 + 0.286*3.5. The atomic baseSweepWidthNorm_{0.286f} (processor.h:227) and the state-load defaults (processor_state.cpp:473, controller.cpp:220) are intentional and match the spec.
- The odd one out is the registration default of 1.0 oct (parameter_registration.cpp:198), not the processor. A mismatch still exists, so a fresh instance and reset-to-default disagree, but the fix should change the registration default to 1.5 oct (norm 0.143 becomes 0.286), not the processor default.

Severity stays at medium: the user-facing defects are the wrong host text and automation values for Sweep Frequency and the wrong reset-to-default value.

The finding holds. The consequence is real and about as bad as the reviewer says.

1) Frequency mismatch, checked in code.
- parameter_registration.cpp:183-190 registers Sweep Frequency as a plain linear RangeParameter: 20..20000 Hz, default 1000.
- Controller::getParamStringByValue (controller.cpp:747-893) has no special case for sweep IDs, so it falls through at :893 to EditControllerEx1, which uses the linear toPlain.
- The processor decodes the same normalized value on a log2 scale (processor_params.cpp:381-388). processor_state.cpp:87/481 and processor.cpp:270-273 use the log helpers too.
- The controller's own SweepIndicator also decodes log2 (controller.cpp:1281-1286).
- Default case: the registered default normalizes to (1000-20)/19980 = 0.04905. The processor decodes that as 2^(4.321928 + 0.04905*9.965784) = 2^4.8107, about 28 Hz. VSTGUI's reset-to-default and a host's "reset parameter" both send this default norm, so they move the sweep centre from about 1 kHz down to about 28 Hz.
- Display case: the state default sweepFreqNorm 0.566 (processor_state.cpp:472, controller.cpp:219) is about 997 Hz on the log scale. The controller pushes it straight into the linear parameter (controller.cpp:227-228), so the host and automation lane show 20 + 0.566*19980, about 11.3 kHz.
- Result: host text, typed values (getParamValueByString at :896-900 also falls back to linear) and automation readouts are wrong across the whole range.

2) Width default slip, checked in code.
- processor.h:227 sets baseSweepWidthNorm_{0.286f}. processor.cpp:277-282 re-applies width from that atomic on every block: 0.5 + 0.286*3.5 = 1.5 oct.
- The registration default is 1.0 oct, which is norm 0.143 (parameter_registration.cpp:198).
- So a fresh instance runs at 1.5 oct while the UI shows 1.0 oct, until a state round-trip or a parameter change syncs them. The same 0.286 appears as the fallback in processor_state.cpp:473 and controller.cpp:220.
- The width mapping itself is linear in both places, so only the default differs.

3) Duplication, confirmed: the same local constants appear at processor_params.cpp:381-384 and :394-395, controller.cpp:1281-1290, processor.cpp:280-281, and as literals at processor_state.cpp:89 and :486.

Impact: limited to when sweep is enabled; the state default is sweepEnable 0 (processor_state.cpp:471). There is no audio corruption or crash. Every host shows the wrong frequency text, and reset-to-default sends the sweep to about 28 Hz. That fits medium; no severity change.

findings.title: Morph inverse-distance weights are implemented three times with different epsilons, on-node handling and mode support
findings.problem: MorphEngine::calculateMorphWeights (morph_engine.cpp:170-270) handles the three MorphModes, uses eps 1e-6 and a one-hot on-node snap, then zeroes and renormalises weights below the 0.001 threshold. BandProcessor::computeRawMorphWeights (band_processor.h:576-614) is a second copy: always 2-D Euclidean whatever the mode, eps 1e-8, no threshold step. It drives the oversampling factor. MorphPad::recalculateWeights (morph_pad.cpp:833-868) is a third copy: always 2-D, std::pow(distance, 2), and a cursor on a node gets raw weight 1000 instead of one-hot. It drives node brightness (morph_pad.cpp:522) and connection alpha (:491).
findings.why_wrong: The weights the engine applies are the ground truth. The oversampling selector and the UI display both claim to reflect them, so they should call the same function with the same mode.
findings.consequence: In Linear1D or Radial2D modes, the morph pad's node brightness shows Planar2D weights that differ from what is heard (Linear1D uses X only, Radial uses angle). With the cursor on node A and B at distance 1, the pad shows A at 0.999 and B at 0.001 rather than 1/0. If oversampling is ever wired in, the factor selection would use the wrong weights in non-planar modes.
findings.suggested_fix: Expose a pure static function, e.g. computeMorphWeights(mode, nodes, count, x, y) -> array, from morph_engine.h (or morph_node.h) that holds the mode switch, epsilon, on-node snap and threshold. Call it from MorphEngine, BandProcessor and MorphPad (the pad also needs the band's MorphMode). Test: for each mode and a grid of cursor positions, all three call sites return identical weights.
findings.evidence: morph_engine.cpp:20 `constexpr float kDistanceEpsilon = 1e-6f;` and the :180-242 mode switch; band_processor.h:584-585 `kOnNodeThreshold = 0.001f; kDistanceEpsilon = 1e-8f;` with `const float dist = std::sqrt(dx*dx + dy*dy)` (2-D only); morph_pad.cpp:848-852 `if (distance < kMinDistance) { rawWeights[i] = 1000.0f; } else { rawWeights[i] = 1.0f / std::pow(distance, kDistanceExponent); }`
verifier_notes:
I traced the claim through the source and it holds. There really are three separate weight computations, and they disagree.

1) MorphEngine::calculateMorphWeights (morph_engine.cpp:170-271):
- It switches on mode_ (:179). Linear1D measures distance on X only via calculate1DDistance (:185, :274-276). Planar2D uses Euclidean distance (:217). Radial2D calls calculateRadialWeights (:245, :286-339), which weights by angle around (0.5, 0.5).
- kDistanceEpsilon is 1e-6f (:20).
- When the cursor sits on a node it snaps to one-hot weights (:188-192, :220-224).
- It applies the kWeightThreshold cut and renormalises (:250-265).

2) BandProcessor::computeRawMorphWeights (band_processor.h:576-615):
- It always uses 2-D Euclidean distance (:591-593) and ignores the mode. Its epsilon is 1e-8f (:585), and it has no threshold step. Only the one-hot snap (:596-600) matches the engine.
- BandProcessor::setMorphMode (:260-264) only forwards the mode to morphEngine_ and keeps no copy, so this function cannot know the mode.
- The function is live, not hypothetical. recalculateOversampleFactor (:393-411) calls it at :400 and passes the result to calculateMorphOversampleFactor. setMorphPosition (:277), setMorphEnabled (:324) and setMaxOversampleFactor (:366) all reach that path.
- So the finding's "if oversampling is ever wired in" understates the problem: in Linear1D and Radial2D the oversampling factor is chosen today from Planar2D weights that differ from the weights the engine actually applies.

3) MorphPad::recalculateWeights (morph_pad.cpp:833-869):
- It always uses 2-D distance and std::pow(distance, 2) (:846, :853).
- A cursor on a node gets a raw weight of 1000 instead of a one-hot weight (:849-851). With node B at distance 1 (raw weight 1/1² = 1), A normalises to 1000/1001 ≈ 0.999 and B to 0.001, as the finding says.
- MorphPad does store morphMode_ (:192-195), but recalculateWeights never reads it.
- In Linear1D the pad pins the cursor to Y = 0.5 (:672-674) while the engine uses X only. With the default nodes at y = 0 and y = 1, the 2-D and 1-D weights differ.
- The results feed connection-line alpha (:491) and node brightness (:522).

Severity: medium stands. The UI drift is only cosmetic, but the oversampling selector really does use mode-blind weights, which can pick a lower factor than the heard blend needs.

I confirmed all three copies in the source, and the context lens turns up no guard or design note that covers the mode and epsilon drift.

1. **Engine (ground truth).** morph_engine.cpp:20 and :23 set kDistanceEpsilon = 1e-6f and kOnNodeThreshold = 0.001f. calculateMorphWeights (:170-271) switches on mode_: Linear1D uses calculate1DDistance (X only, :185), Planar2D uses Euclidean distance (:217), Radial2D calls calculateRadialWeights (:245). It then zeroes weights below kWeightThreshold and renormalises (:250-265).

2. **BandProcessor.** computeRawMorphWeights (band_processor.h:576-615) always uses 2-D Euclidean distance (:593), uses eps 1e-8f (:585), and has no threshold step. BandProcessor::setMorphMode (:260-264) passes the mode to morphEngine_ and does not store it, so this function cannot know the mode. It is not dormant. setMorphPosition (:277), setMorphNodes (:254) and setMorphEnabled (:324) all call recalculateOversampleFactor, which feeds these weights into calculateMorphOversampleFactor (:400-402). The finding's hedge "if oversampling is ever wired in" is therefore too weak: the factor selection uses these weights today, so in Linear1D and Radial2D it can differ from what the engine applies.

3. **MorphPad.** recalculateWeights (morph_pad.cpp:833-869) is always 2-D, uses std::pow(distance, 2), and gives 1000.0f to a node under the cursor instead of a one-hot weight (:849-852). Node A on the cursor with node B at distance 1 gives 1000/1001 = 0.999 and 0.001, as claimed. The pad stores morphMode_ (morph_pad.h:310; set at morph_pad.cpp:192-195), but recalculateWeights never reads it. The mode is used only for drawing (:420, :457). The weights drive connection alpha (:491) and node brightness (:522).

**Documentation context.** specs/_archive2_/009-intelligent-oversampling/plan.md:256-261 records a separate computeRawMorphWeights as an intentional deviation. Its reason is to bypass the engine's audio-rate smoother. It says nothing about ignoring MorphMode, changing the epsilon or dropping the threshold, and that reason would be met just as well by a shared pure function. No spec or comment documents the pad's 2-D-only display as an approximation. A grep of plugins/disrumpo/tests found no test that compares weights between these call sites.

**Verdict.** The duplication and its behavioural drift are real, and the oversampler copy is live, so this is not refuted. Medium severity fits: wrong UI feedback plus possibly wrong oversampling factors in two of the three modes, with no audio corruption.

The defect is real, and its audio-side impact is a little larger than the finding claims.

(1) Three separate implementations exist, as described. morph_engine.cpp:170-271 switches on mode_. Linear1D uses calculate1DDistance on X only (:185). Planar2D uses 2-D Euclidean distance (:217). Radial2D calls calculateRadialWeights (:286-331), which weights by polar angle around (0.5,0.5) and gives equal weights at the centre. All three modes snap to one node when the cursor is on it, then apply the kWeightThreshold zero-and-renormalise step (:250-265). band_processor.h:576-615 computeRawMorphWeights always uses 2-D sqrt(dx*dx+dy*dy) with eps 1e-8, has no mode and no threshold step. morph_pad.cpp:833-869 recalculateWeights is 2-D only, uses std::pow(distance,2), and gives raw weight 1000 on a node instead of a one-hot weight.

(2) The finding says "if oversampling is ever wired in". It already is. recalculateOversampleFactor (band_processor.h:393-411) feeds computeRawMorphWeights into calculateMorphOversampleFactor (oversampling_utils.h:77-100). That function takes the weighted average of each node's recommended factor and rounds it up to a power of 2. The result reaches requestOversampleFactor -> startCrossfade, and the factor is used by processBlockInner -> processWithFactor (:548-557, :627+). It is recalculated from setDistortionType, setMorphNodes, setMorphPosition, setMorphEnabled and setMaxOversampleFactor (:211, :254, :277, :324, :366). BandProcessor::setMorphMode (:260-264) does not trigger a recalculation at all.

In Linear1D or Radial2D the engine's audible weights can therefore differ a lot from the Planar2D weights that pick the factor. Example: Radial2D, cursor at (0.6,0.5), which is near the centre but on the east angle. The engine gives that one node almost all the weight; the selector gives roughly even weights. When the weighted average crosses a power-of-2 rounding boundary, the band runs one oversampling step lower than the audible node mix calls for. That means added aliasing from a high-factor shaper. When it lands one step higher, it costs extra CPU. The error is bounded to one rounding step and only appears in non-planar modes, so medium severity fits.

(3) UI side. The pad's mode-specific drawing branches exist (morph_pad.cpp:420, 457, 672, 731, 804, set by setMorphMode at :192). The weights that drive connection alpha (:491) and node brightness (:522) are always computed planar. In non-planar modes the display does not match what is heard, which is a real but cosmetic drift.

The finding's specific on-node example (0.999 vs 0.001) is visually negligible. B's alpha truncates to 0 and its brightness is 0.3007 against 0.3. That part of the consequence is overstated, but the main mode-mismatch drift stands.

findings.title: Shape-slot display formatter re-implements the processor/adapter slot mappings and has already drifted (RingSat Hz in Harmonic mode, Bitcrush shows 1-3 bits)
findings.problem: formatShapeSlot hand-copies the denormalisations from mapShapeSlotsToParams (processor_params.cpp) and routeParamsToProcessor (distortion_adapter.cpp). Each copy carries its own literals, and the formatter has diverged from the DSP. RingSat slot 6 always prints `20*250^v Hz`, but the adapter treats it as a harmonic ratio 1+round(v*15) when the freq mode (slot 5) is Harmonic (distortion_adapter.cpp:803-806). Bitcrush slot 0 prints 1.0..16.0 bit, but BitCrusher clamps to kMinBitDepth = 4 (bit_crusher.h:50,152), so 1-3.9 bit are shown but never applied. The 9-entry waveshape name table is also duplicated inside the same function (lines 52-55 and 94-97).
findings.why_wrong: The text a host or slider shows must be produced by the same mapping the DSP applies. Today the two mappings live in separate TUs with no shared definition.
findings.consequence: In RingSat Harmonic mode, host automation lanes and the value readout show e.g. '354 Hz' while the carrier runs at ratio 8. The bottom 20 % of the Bitcrush Bits knob reads 1-3.9 bit and sounds identical to 4 bit. Any future range edit on one side silently desyncs the readout again.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the per-type slot ranges into one constexpr descriptor table, e.g. in distortion_types.h, giving min/max/curve/unit per (type, slot). findings.title: Mod and sweep denormalisations are written twice (params TU and state TU) as literals, including nine hand-rounded copies of ln(0.01)/ln(20)
findings.problem: Every mod-source and sweep range is encoded once in processParameterChanges and again, as an inverse, in getState/setState, each with literal constants. Examples: env attack 1+v*99 (params :643, state :226 and :655), release 10+v*490, random/S&H/rungler rate 0.1+v*49.9, LFO phase v*360. The LFO-rate log mapping appears as `constexpr float kMinRateLog = -4.6052f; kMaxRateLog = 2.9957f;` nine times: processor_params.cpp:431-432, 579-580, 611-612 and processor_state.cpp:103-104, 163-164, 195-196, 506-507, 583-584, 619-620.
findings.why_wrong: A range belongs in one place. The four-decimal constants are not ln(0.01) = -4.605170 and ln(20) = 2.995732, so the copies agree with each other only because they were all typed identically, not because they derive from the LFO's real range. The registration side (parameter_registration.cpp:364-365, 400-401) uses linear RangeParameters for the same params, which is the drift this layout invites.
findings.consequence: A future range change made in only one of the two TUs silently corrupts session round-trips. This is the same failure class as the preset-writer drift. Today the copies are consistent; the cost is maintenance and the masked linear-vs-log registration mismatch.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one header (e.g. dsp/param_ranges.h in the plugin) with inline toNorm/fromNorm helpers per range, using std::log(0.01f)/std::log(20.0f) computed once. Call them from processor_params.cpp, processor_state.cpp and the registration. Test: for each mod param, fromNorm(toNorm(x)) == x at the endpoints and midpoint, and processParameterChanges(v) followed by getState writes v back within 1e-5.
findings.evidence: processor_params.cpp:431-433 `constexpr float kMinRateLog = -4.6052f;  // ln(0.01) ... exp(kMinRateLog + value*(kMaxRateLog-kMinRateLog))`; processor_state.cpp:105 `(std::log(sweepLFO_.getRate()) - kMinRateLog) / (kMaxRateLog - kMinRateLog)`; params :643 `float ms = 1.0f + value * 99.0f;` vs state :226 `(getEnvFollowerAttack() - 1.0f) / 99.0f` and :655 `1.0f + envAttackNorm * 99.0f`; grep shows the -4.6052/2.9957 literals only in Disrumpo.

2. **A fourth, differently ordered test copy.** `kCanonicalDistortionTypes` in band_strip_test.cpp:29-56 is in D-number order: Temporal at 14, Ring Saturation at 15, Feedback at 16, Aliasing at 17, Bitwise Mangler at 18, Allpass Resonant at 25. The REQUIREs at :131 and :141-163 only index that local array, so the test is tautological.

3. **The tests pin the wrong order.** The comments "Index 25 (Allpass Resonant)" at :217 and :242 are wrong for the product: index 25 is Stochastic and Allpass Resonant is 19.

4. **No other coverage.** A grep of plugins/disrumpo/tests finds no test that reads the registered `StringListParameter` strings or compares them with `getTypeName`. A menu/enum mismatch would therefore pass CI.

**Impact:**
- No audible or visible defect today: 0 dB, all hosts and settings unaffected.
- The risk is future drift. Adding or reordering a type means editing three production lists in step. If one goes out of order, the label shown is wrong for the type that plays, since the processor decodes the index as `round(v*25)` into the enum. The test suite would not catch it and would also mislead whoever reads it.

This is a maintainability and test-gap issue, and low is the right severity.

findings.title: A legacy sweep-only MIDI-learn system runs alongside the shared MidiCCManager; the controller half is dead and the processor half writes state nothing reads
findings.problem: Controller::getMidiControllerAssignment first asks the shared Krate::Plugins::MidiCCManager, then falls back to a plugin-local `assignedMidiCC_` member (controller.h:435, initialised to 128) mapped to kSweepFrequency. Nothing in the controller ever assigns that member (grep shows only its declaration and its read at :720). On the processor side, a parallel implementation exists: processor.h:240 assignedMidiCC_, the CC capture at processor.cpp:409, and the kSweepMidiLearnActive/kSweepMidiCCNumber handlers at processor_params.cpp:527-534. It is a write-only re-implementation of what MidiCCManager does.
findings.why_wrong: MIDI learn already lives in plugins/shared/src/midi/midi_cc_manager.*, which the controller uses (controller.cpp:34). A second, partial, unpersisted copy cannot complete a mapping. Its two automatable parameters are exposed to hosts but change nothing audible.
findings.consequence: Hosts list 'Sweep MIDI Learn' and 'Sweep MIDI CC' as automatable parameters that do nothing. The dead fallback branch in getMidiControllerAssignment, and the processor's per-block CC scan when learn is active, are maintenance noise that hides which system is authoritative.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the controller fallback branch and the controller assignedMidiCC_ member. Retire the processor-side assignedMidiCC_/midiLearnActive_ handling. Keep the two parameter IDs registered but mark them hidden/non-automatable for host compatibility (never reuse the IDs). Test: getMidiControllerAssignment returns kResultFalse for every CC unless MidiCCManager has a mapping.
findings.evidence: controller.cpp:714-723 `if (midiCCManager_) { ... } if (assignedMidiCC_ < 128 && midiControllerNumber == assignedMidiCC_) { id = makeSweepParamId(SweepParamType::kSweepFrequency); return kResultTrue; }`; grep assignedMidiCC_ in controller: only controller.h:435 `int assignedMidiCC_ = 128;` and controller.cpp:720; processor.cpp:409 `assignedMidiCC_ = cc;`, processor_params.cpp:532-533 `assignedMidiCC_ = static_cast<int>(value * 128.0 + 0.5);` with no reader.
verifier_notes: I traced the code and could not refute the finding. Controller side: controller.cpp:714-723 asks midiCCManager_ (created at controller.cpp:110) first, then falls back to `assignedMidiCC_ < 128 && midiControllerNumber == assignedMidiCC_` and maps that CC to kSweepFrequency. A grep of plugins/disrumpo/src finds assignedMidiCC_ in the controller only at controller.h:435 (`int assignedMidiCC_ = 128;`) and controller.cpp:720. Nothing writes it, so it stays 128 and the fallback branch can never be taken. Processor side: processor_params.cpp:527-534 sets midiLearnActive_ and assignedMidiCC_ from kSweepMidiLearnActive / kSweepMidiCCNumber. processor.cpp:392-411 scans inputEvents for kLegacyMIDICCOutEvent (a host never normally delivers that type as input, because VST3 hosts route CCs through IMidiMapping), writes kSweepDetectedCCOutputId (0x0F81), and sets assignedMidiCC_ = cc. assignedMidiCC_ is never read anywhere in the processor (grep hits only processor.h:240, processor.cpp:409, processor_params.cpp:532-533). kSweepDetectedCCOutputId is used only at its registration (parameter_registration.cpp:307) and at the processor write (processor.cpp:403); no controller code reacts to it. processor_state.cpp does not persist either field. I confirmed the claim from source. Controller side: controller.cpp:714-723 checks midiCCManager_ first and then falls back to `assignedMidiCC_ < 128 && midiControllerNumber == assignedMidiCC_`. findings.title: Band Bypass button and Space shortcut do nothing: BandProcessor::process ignores bypassed_ (NFR 'bit-transparent bypass', FR-012)
findings.problem: kBandBypass is handled by bandProcessors_[band].setBypassed() (processor_params.cpp:927-930). bypassed_ is only read in processBlock (band_processor.h:521, comment 'FR-012: Bypass optimization - bit-transparent pass-through'), which the processor never calls. process() never reads bypassed_, and Processor::shouldBandContribute (processor.cpp:563-576) checks only mute and solo. The plugin also registers no kIsBypass parameter.
findings.why_wrong: specs-overview.md 'Audio Quality' NFR requires bit-transparent bypass, and FR-BAND-004 lists 'Solo, Bypass, Mute toggles'. A bypassed band should pass its crossover band signal undistorted.
findings.consequence: The per-band Bypass toggles in the editor (editor.uidesc:1264, 1350, control-tag Band.Bypass) and the Space keyboard shortcut (keyboard_shortcut_handler.cpp:78,129-133) change a parameter with no audible effect. The band stays fully distorted, and users cannot A/B a band. No processor-level bypass test exists; grep for kBandBypass in tests finds only encoding and keyboard tests.
findings.suggested_fix: In BandProcessor::process, when bypassed_ is set, skip sweep and morph and apply only gain/pan/mute (or nothing, per spec intent). Smooth the switch to avoid a click. Add a Processor test: 2 bands, HardClip at drive 10 on band 0, bypass band 0, feed a sine. Assert the output equals the crossover-reconstructed input within 1e-4 (before the fix, THD stays high).
findings.evidence: band_processor.h:521 `if (bypassed_) { return; // Leave input buffers unchanged }` (processBlock only); band_processor.h:473-512 process() has no bypassed_ reference; processor_params.cpp:927-930 `bandStates_[band].bypass = value >= 0.5; bandProcessors_[band].setBypassed(...)`; processor.cpp:563-576 shouldBandContribute reads only mute/solo.
verifier_notes:
I traced the call path and the claim holds. processor_params.cpp:927-929 handles kBandBypass by setting bandStates_[band].bypass and calling bandProcessors_[band].setBypassed(...). setBypassed (band_processor.h:335-336) only stores bypassed_.

The only reader of bypassed_ is processBlock (band_processor.h:519-523). Processor::process never calls processBlock. It calls beginBlockModulation (processor.cpp:463-465), then the per-sample BandProcessor::process(bandL, bandR) (processor.cpp:487 and 494), then endBlockModulation (processor.cpp:507-509).

BandProcessor::process (band_processor.h:473-512) applies sweep, morph or distortion, gain, pan and mute, and never checks bypassed_. Processor::shouldBandContribute (processor.cpp:563-576) checks only mute and solo. bandStates_[].bypass is read only by state save and load (processor_state.cpp:70, 437), never by the DSP.

The UI does wire the control. Control-tag Band.Bypass (editor.uidesc:266) maps to kBandBypass (sub_controllers.h:89-90), and it is used by the ToggleButton at editor.uidesc:1264 and the CTextButton at editor.uidesc:1350. The Space shortcut toggles the same parameter (keyboard_shortcut_handler.cpp:78, 129-133). The parameter is registered as an automatable parameter (parameter_registration.cpp:670-672).

So bypass is saved, restored and automatable, but it has no audible effect. The band stays fully distorted. The defect is confirmed. I would keep the severity: a visible, advertised per-band control and a keyboard shortcut silently do nothing.

I could not refute this. The defect is confirmed in the source.

Code path:
- processor_params.cpp:927-929 sets bandStates_[band].bypass and calls bandProcessors_[band].setBypassed().
- band_processor.h:335-336 stores bypassed_.
- The only reader of bypassed_ is processBlock (band_processor.h:519-523), via `if (bypassed_) return;`.
- Processor::process never calls processBlock. Its band loop (processor.cpp:481-499) calls only bandProcessors_[b].process(bandL, bandR) at lines 487 and 494.
- BandProcessor::process (band_processor.h:473-512) does not read bypassed_. It always applies sweep, then morph or distortion, then gain/pan/mute.
- shouldBandContribute (processor.cpp:563-576) checks only mute and solo.
- A grep for "bypass" across plugins/disrumpo/src finds no other use on the audio path.

Possible defences, none of which hold:
- Not marked as a deliberate deferral. The only hint is the band_state.h:36 comment "Bypass flag (FR-024, for future distortion)". Against that, band_processor.h:333 says "When bypassed, band output is bit-identical to input". The specs require it too: specs-overview.md:174 lists "Solo, Bypass, Mute toggles" and specs-overview.md:379 requires "Bit-transparent bypass". The CHANGELOG says nothing about bypass being deferred.
- Users can reach it in a real host. The editor exposes it at editor.uidesc:1264 and 1350 (control-tag Band.Bypass, tooltip "Bypass band processing"). The parameter is registered for automation at parameter_registration.cpp:670-672, and the Space shortcut toggles it at keyboard_shortcut_handler.cpp:129-133.
- Nothing upstream or downstream bypasses the band for it, and no test pins it.

Result: the toggle has no audible effect. Severity: it is a broken user-facing control, not corrupted or unsafe audio, so high versus medium is a judgment call. I left it unchanged.

I could not refute this. Every link in the claim holds in source. (1) plugins/disrumpo/src/dsp/band_processor.h:473-512: BandProcessor::process(float&, float&) applies sweep, then morph or the single distortion, then gain/pan/mute. It never reads bypassed_. (2) bypassed_ is read only in processBlock at band_processor.h:519-523 ("if (bypassed_) return;"). (3) The processor never calls processBlock. Its grep hits in src/processor are only processor.cpp:320, which is a comment, and :370, which is sweepProcessor_.processBlock and not a BandProcessor. The audio loop at processor.cpp:481-499 calls bandProcessors_[b].process(bandL, bandR) per sample. (4) shouldBandContribute at processor.cpp:563-576 checks only bandStates_.mute and .solo. (5) processor_params.cpp:927-929 sets bandStates_[band].bypass and calls setBypassed(); nothing else reads either value on the audio path. (6) The control is visible to users. editor.uidesc:1350 places a "Bypass" CTextButton (control-tag Band.Bypass, remapped per band by sub_controllers.h:89-90) in the BandExpandedStrip template. That template is instantiated for all four bands through Band1-4ExpandedStrip (editor.uidesc:582-609, 1359-1369). editor.uidesc:1264 adds another in BandMainTab. The host also sees an automatable "Band N Bypass" parameter (parameter_registration.cpp:636-672), and keyboard_shortcut_handler.cpp:129-133 toggles it with Space. (7) Tests: setBypassed appears only in tests/dsp/oversampling_*_tests.cpp, which drive BandProcessor::processBlock directly, so they pass while the plugin path stays broken.
