A bypassed band with HardClip at drive 10 stays fully distorted, so the advertised per-band bypass and A/B feature is completely dead. There is no corruption, NaN or click, but a whole user-facing, host-automatable feature does nothing, so high is defensible and I keep the severity. Note for the fix (STATE-COMPAT): bypass is saved in state (processor_state.cpp:70, 423-437). Any saved project or preset with bypass=1 will change its sound once bypass starts working.
corroborated_by_measurement: probe bypass:all-bands: "max_abs_diff(on vs off),max_abs_diff(on vs dry) = 0,0.6292" (threshold "bypass must change output (FR-012)"). Code: band_processor.h:521 `if (bypassed_) {` exists only in processBlock; process() at :473-512 has no bypass check.

findings.title: MIDI CC sweep control and MIDI Learn cannot work: the processor declares no event input bus (FR-SWEEP-004, FR-028/029, docs and CHANGELOG claims)
findings.problem: Processor::initialize adds only stereo audio in/out (no addEventInput anywhere in plugins/disrumpo/src). The MIDI-learn scan in process() reads data.inputEvents, which a host only supplies for an event bus, and it matches kLegacyMIDICCOutEvent, an output-event type. Controller::getMidiControllerAssignment (controller.cpp:707-726) implements IMidiMapping for bus 0, but there is no event bus 0. Ruinae, for comparison, calls addEventInput (ruinae processor.cpp:61). The processor-side assignedMidiCC_ is write-only, and the controller's assignedMidiCC_ is never assigned (only declared at controller.h:435).
findings.why_wrong: FR-SWEEP-004 lists MIDI CC as a sweep driver. docs/index.html:123 claims 'Full parameter automation and MIDI CC learn support', and CHANGELOG.md:124 claims 'MIDI CC learn for parameter automation'. VST3 IMidiMapping maps CCs arriving on the plugin's event input bus, so a plugin without one receives no CCs.
findings.consequence: The right-click MIDI Learn menu starts a learn that can never complete from incoming MIDI, and learned or saved mappings never move a parameter in hosts that route MIDI only to plugins with an event input. The documented feature is non-functional.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `addEventInput(STR16("Event Input"), 1)` in initialize, and handle kLegacyMIDICCOutEvent removal: a host maps CCs to params via IMidiMapping, so learning should be completed on the controller side. Drop or wire the write-only assignedMidiCC_. Add a test that the processor's bus info reports one event input bus, and a controller test that a learned CC returns the mapped ID from getMidiControllerAssignment(0, ...).
findings.evidence: processor.cpp:62-64 `addAudioInput(...kStereo); addAudioOutput(...kStereo);` (no event bus); grep 'addEventInput' in plugins/disrumpo/src finds nothing; processor.cpp:396 `if (e.type == Steinberg::Vst::Event::kLegacyMIDICCOutEvent)`; controller.cpp:712 `if (busIndex != 0) return kResultFalse;`; controller.cpp:720 `if (assignedMidiCC_ < 128 && ...)` with assignedMidiCC_ never written in controller.
verifier_notes: I traced the code and the defect holds. (1) processor.cpp:63-66 `Processor::initialize` adds only stereo audio in and out. A grep for addEventInput across plugins/disrumpo finds nothing, so the plugin has no event input bus. The controller's IMidiMapping (controller.cpp:707-726) answers only for busIndex 0, and VST3 defines that index against the plugin's event input buses. Hosts route MIDI to, and map CCs for, plugins that expose an event input. (2) The processor's learn scan (processor.cpp:392-414) checks `e.type == Event::kLegacyMIDICCOutEvent`. That event type is for plugin output only. A VST3 host turns incoming CCs into parameter changes through IMidiMapping and never delivers them as input events. So even with a bus added, this branch could not fire. The `assignedMidiCC_` it writes is set at processor.cpp:409 and processor_params.cpp:532, and nothing on the audio path reads it. (3) The processor writes the read-only output param kSweepDetectedCCOutputId (plugin_ids.h:168, registered at parameter_registration.cpp:307) at processor.cpp:403. No controller code consumes it; the grep finds only the registration. (4) The controller's own learn path calls `midiCCManager_->startLearn(paramId)` (controller.cpp:1625). The only call that completes a learn is `MidiCCManager::processCCMessage` (plugins/shared/src/midi/midi_cc_manager.cpp:127), and it is called only from tests (midi_cc_manager_test.cpp, midi_learn_integration_test.cpp, state_persistence_test.cpp), never from plugins/disrumpo/src. So a learn started from the UI can never finish. (5) The controller's `assignedMidiCC_` (controller.h:435) is declared with value 128 and the grep shows no write to it, so the check at controller.cpp:720 can never succeed. Mappings that already exist (loaded at controller.cpp:695) would only take effect in a host that queries IMidiMapping without an event bus. In hosts that require one, they are dead. The tests cover MidiCCManager on its own, not the processor bus setup or the controller learn flow, which is why nothing caught this. The feature claimed in the docs and CHANGELOG does not work. Severity 'high' is reasonable for a documented, user-visible feature that is entirely non-functional, although no audio is harmed, so I leave it unchanged.

I could not refute this finding. The code confirms it, and the learn path is broken in more places than the finding names.
(1) There is no event input bus. processor.cpp:63-64 adds only stereo audio in/out. A grep for addEventInput in plugins/*/src finds it in gradus, innexus, membrum, profundum, ruinae, seraphis and vorago, but not in disrumpo.
(2) The processor's learn scan (processor.cpp:392-413) needs data.inputEvents, and it matches Event::kLegacyMIDICCOutEvent. That is an output event type. A VST3 host turns incoming CCs into parameter changes through IMidiMapping; it does not pass them as input events. When a CC is detected, the code writes kSweepDetectedCCOutputId (0x0F81, plugin_ids.h:168). Nothing in the controller reads that ID: the only reference is its registration at parameter_registration.cpp:307. The processor's assignedMidiCC_ (set at processor.cpp:409 and processor_params.cpp:532-533) is never read for audio.
(3) The controller side never completes a learn either. The context menu calls midiCCManager_->startLearn(paramId) (controller.cpp:1625), but a grep for processCCMessage in plugins/disrumpo/src finds no caller. That is the only MidiCCManager API that finishes a learn (midi_cc_manager.h). So isLearning() stays true until Escape cancels it (controller.cpp:1410-1411), and no mapping is ever created. controller.h:435 assignedMidiCC_ = 128 is never written, so the fallback at controller.cpp:720 is dead code.
(4) getMidiControllerAssignment (controller.cpp:707-726) answers only for busIndex 0, and the plugin declares no event bus 0.
(5) Tests do not cover the real path. midi_learn_integration_test.cpp:21-56 drives MidiCCManager by itself, calling processCCMessage directly. It never checks processor bus info or the controller's learn path.
(6) Nothing marks this as intentional. specs/Disrumpo/specs-overview.md:293-297 (FR-SWEEP-004) lists MIDI CC as a sweep driver, dsp-details.md:1803 section 12 describes MIDI CC integration, and CHANGELOG.md:124 claims "MIDI CC learn for parameter automation".
Severity stays high: a feature that is documented and shipped does nothing, and the right-click Learn item never completes. The audio path is not affected.

The defect is real, and the learn path is dead for more reasons than the missing bus.

1. No event bus. processor.cpp:65-66 adds only stereo audio in/out. A grep for addEventInput under plugins/disrumpo finds nothing.

2. The processor-side learn can never fire. processor.cpp:392-413 only reacts to kLegacyMIDICCOutEvent arriving in data.inputEvents. Hosts never send that output-event type as input; they turn CCs into parameter changes through IMidiMapping. So even after adding an event bus, this branch stays dead. It is armed by kSweepMidiLearnActive (processor_params.cpp:527-533), while the controller's menu sets a different parameter, kGlobalMidiLearnActive (controller.cpp:1626). The kSweepDetectedCCOutputId value it would write (0x0F81) is never read by the controller (grep finds no consumer).

3. The controller-side learn can never complete. The "MIDI Learn" menu item (controller.cpp:1621-1626) calls midiCCManager_->startLearn(paramId). The only function that completes a learn, MidiCCManager::processCCMessage (plugins/shared/src/midi/midi_cc_manager.h:101), is never called anywhere in plugins/disrumpo/src (grep). So no mapping is ever created, and none can be saved or restored (controller.cpp:664-695).

4. getMidiControllerAssignment (controller.cpp:707-726) answers only for bus 0, and the plugin has no event bus 0. Its fallback assignedMidiCC_ (controller.h:435) is never written, so `assignedMidiCC_ < 128` is always false.

Impact: the advertised plugin-side MIDI CC learn, and the CC-driven sweep (FR-SWEEP-004 / FR-028/029), cannot work in any host. The quoted docs and CHANGELOG claims are false.

Severity: downgrade. No audio, state or real-time harm follows. Nothing reaches the output and no preset breaks; the feature simply does nothing. Host-level MIDI learn and automation of the same parameters still work, so users have a workaround. That makes it a medium spec-conformance / dead-feature defect rather than high.

findings.title: Cross-family morph dips about -3 dB at the midpoint (SC-002 '+/-1 dB'); the SC-002 test is relaxed to 3 dB and only tests same-family nodes
findings.problem: processCrossFamily sums nodeOutput * weight * transitionGain. The weights are already normalized to sum to 1, and calculateTransitionGain additionally attenuates every node with w < 0.6 (sin of the zone position). At a 2-node midpoint (w=0.5/0.5), gain = sin(pi/4) = 0.707, so the output is 2*0.5*0.707 = 0.707x the correlated level. At the 4-node centre (w=0.25 each), gain = 0.831, giving -1.6 dB.
findings.why_wrong: SC-002 (cited in tests/approval/morph_artifact_test.cpp:377) requires a cross-family morph to stay within 1 dB of single-type output. FR-MORPH-003 requires artifact-free transitions. A weighted sum with normalized weights is already level-preserving for correlated outputs, and multiplying again by a sub-unity 'transition gain' double-attenuates.
findings.consequence: Sweeping the cursor between, for example, a SoftClip node and a SineFold node at moderate drive produces an audible ~3 dB hole in the middle of the pad, worse than the 1 dB target. Test AP-003 cannot catch it: it builds createSameFamilySetup() (morph_artifact_test.cpp:383), which takes processSameFamily, and asserts diffMid < 3.0 dB (:466) with a comment admitting the relaxation.
findings.suggested_fix: For correlated-output nodes use output = sum(w_i * y_i) with no extra gain. If equal-power behaviour is wanted, normalize the gains so that sum(w_i*g_i) = 1 (or use sqrt weights with a sum-of-squares normalization). Fix AP-003: use two cross-family nodes (e.g. SoftClip and SineFold at drive 0.5, so both are near-linear) and assert |mid - avg| < 1.0 dB per SC-002.
findings.evidence: morph_engine.cpp:751 `const float gain = transitionGains_[i];` :757 `output += nodeOutput * weight * gain;`; :372-378 zone gain = equalPowerGains((w-0.4)/0.2) fade-in, so w=0.5 gives 0.7071; morph_artifact_test.cpp:383 `auto nodes = createSameFamilySetup();` :462-467 'Relaxed to 3dB ... REQUIRE(diffMid < 3.0f)'.
verifier_notes:
I re-derived the defect from source and it holds. morph_engine.cpp:250-265 thresholds the weights and renormalizes them to sum to 1. :268-270 then sets transitionGains_[i] = calculateTransitionGain(weights_[i]). calculateTransitionGain (:352-379) returns 1 only when w >= 0.6 (kTransitionZoneHigh, :33). For 0.4 <= w < 0.6 it returns sin(((w-0.4)/0.2)*pi/2), and for w < 0.4 it returns sin((w/0.4)*pi/2). equalPowerGains (dsp/include/krate/dsp/core/crossfade_utils.h:50-53) is fadeIn = sin(pos*kHalfPi). processCrossFamily (:743-757) sums `output += nodeOutput * weight * gain`, so the normalized weight and the extra sub-unity gain multiply.

2-node midpoint: w = 0.5 gives zonePos = 0.5 and gain = sin(pi/4) = 0.707. Output = 0.5*0.707*yA + 0.5*0.707*yB, which is 0.707y (-3 dB) for correlated node outputs.

4-node centre: w = 0.25 gives gain = sin(0.625*pi/2) = 0.831, so the output is -1.6 dB.

Both numbers match the finding. The same function also has a jump that makes things worse: just below w = 0.4 the gain approaches sin(pi/2) = 1, and at w = 0.4 it falls to sin(0) = 0. Two nodes at w = 0.399/0.601 sum to about 1.0, while 0.4/0.6 sums to 0.6 (about -4.4 dB) in one step. So the gain is not only a dip but a discontinuity. The impact supports high severity.

Test claims: AP-003 (tests/approval/morph_artifact_test.cpp:383) does use createSameFamilySetup() and asserts diffMid < 3.0f at :460 (the finding says :466). Its comment at :457-458 admits the relaxation.

Partial inaccuracy: the finding says the SC-002 test only covers same-family nodes, but a cross-family SC-002 test exists in tests/unit/morph_interpolation_test.cpp:258-306 (createCrossFamilyNodes). It is weaker still: it checks a linear ratio < 3.0 (about 9.5 dB, :305), skips the check entirely when minLevel <= 0.001 (:298), and never samples near w = 0.4. So it cannot catch the -3 dB dip either. The core defect is confirmed.

I could not refute the defect. Two parts of the claim are slightly off, and neither changes the conclusion.

What the code does:
- morph_engine.cpp:250-265 renormalizes the weights so they sum to 1.
- :267-270 sets transitionGains_[i] = calculateTransitionGain(weights_[i]).
- :352-379, with kTransitionZoneLow=0.4 and kTransitionZoneHigh=0.6 at :30/:33: a weight of 0.5 gives zonePos 0.5, so equalPowerGains returns fadeIn = sin(pi/4) = 0.707. A weight of 0.25 gives normalizedPos 0.625, so the gain is about 0.83.
- processCrossFamily at :743-757 does `output += nodeOutput * weight * gain`. At the 2-node midpoint each node therefore contributes 0.354. Correlated outputs come out at 0.707x (-3 dB). Uncorrelated outputs come out at about -6 dB.
- The comment at :754 calls this an "Equal-power weighted sum", which it is not.

It is not a documented design decision:
- specs/Disrumpo/dsp-details.md:1164-1198 specifies the equal-power crossfade as gainA=cos and gainB=sin of the zone position, applied directly. At the midpoint that is 0.707 per node with no extra weight multiplier, and the stated goal is "to maintain perceived loudness".
- The code multiplies by weight and by the sin gain, so it attenuates twice and departs from both the spec formula and its own comment.
- No clamp, makeup gain or normalization elsewhere compensates.

Corrections to the claim:
- It says only same-family nodes are tested. A cross-family level test does exist: tests/unit/morph_interpolation_test.cpp:258-307 (Tube vs Bitcrush, tagged [SC-002]). It asserts maxLevel/minLevel < 3.0 as an amplitude ratio (:305), about 9.5 dB, and its own comments say "SC-002: within 1dB" (:292) and "being generous" (:300). That test cannot catch a -3 dB dip, so the coverage gap stands.
- The approval test AP-003 (tests/approval/morph_artifact_test.cpp:377-460) does use createSameFamilySetup (:383) and only requires a difference under 3 dB (:460), as the claim says.

Severity: I recommend downgrading from high to medium. This is a level and spec-conformance defect in the morph crossfade, about 1.6-3 dB for correlated outputs (worse for uncorrelated). It is not a real-time safety, NaN or crash issue.

I could not refute this. The code confirms it.

- **Weights are normalized.** morph_engine.cpp:204-208, 236-240 and 260-265 make the weights sum to 1. Transition gains are computed per sample from those normalized weights (:267-270). process() recomputes the weights every sample (:672), and BandProcessor::process calls morphEngine_->process (band_processor.h:485-488), so this is the live audio path.
- **The gain is applied on top of the weights.** calculateTransitionGain (:352-379) uses equalPowerGains, whose fadeIn = sin(pos*pi/2) (dsp/include/krate/dsp/core/crossfade_utils.h:50-53). processCrossFamily then sums nodeOutput * weight * gain (:748, :756).
- **2-node midpoint.** With wA = wB = 0.5, zonePos = 0.5 and gain = 0.7071, so the output is 0.7071 times the weighted average. For correlated node outputs (same input, near-linear drive) that is -3.01 dB. For uncorrelated outputs the drop against a single node is about -6 dB, so the dip is at least as bad as claimed.
- **4-node centre.** w = 0.25 takes the <0.4 branch: normalizedPos = 0.625, gain = sin(0.982) = 0.831, which is -1.6 dB. Both numbers match the finding.
- **A worse defect the finding missed.** The gain curve jumps at w = 0.4. Just below it (:364-370) normalizedPos tends to 1, so gain tends to 1. At 0.4 (:374-377) zonePos = 0, so gain = 0, and :749 skips the node. With 2 nodes, a cursor moving through wA = 0.4 drops node A's 0.4 contribution in one sample. For correlated outputs the level goes from about 1.0 to 0.6, a -4.4 dB step. That is an audible click and timbre jump, which breaks FR-MORPH-003 (artifact-free transitions).
- **The test cannot catch it.** morph_artifact_test.cpp:383 uses createSameFamilySetup(), which takes processSameFamily and never reaches this code. :457-460 relaxes the SC-002 1 dB bound to 3 dB (`REQUIRE(diffMid < 3.0f)`).

**Who hits it.** Any host, any sample rate, any preset whose nodes come from different families once the cursor is away from a node. The engine's default node set (SoftClip, Tube, Fuzz, SineFold, :41-44) is already mixed-family.

**Severity.** High is justified for the plugin's central morph feature, especially with the step at w = 0.4. I recommend no change.

findings.title: Latency NFR (0-256 samples, < 10 ms) is violated and unreported: Spectral adds 512-4096 samples, Feedback/Granular add a delay, and no getLatencySamples exists
findings.problem: The Spectral type runs SpectralDistortion per sample, and its latency() equals fftSize (spectral_distortion.h:490-494). processor_params.cpp:244 maps the FFT size to 512-4096. The adapter records blockLatency_ (fftSize, grain samples) but getProcessingLatency (:248) has no caller. Processor has no getLatencySamples override (grep in processor.h/.cpp is empty), and BandProcessor::getLatency is a hard-coded 0 (band_processor.h:376-379).
findings.why_wrong: specs-overview.md NFR 'Latency: 0 samples (1x) to 256 samples (8x)' and success criterion 'Latency < 10ms at highest quality'. Any intrinsic latency must be reported to the host for PDC and aligned between bands and against the dry path.
findings.consequence: One Spectral node at the default fftSize 2048 delays that band by 2048 samples (46 ms at 44.1 kHz; 4096 gives 93 ms), with no host compensation. The band arrives late against the other bands (smeared transients at summation) and against the dry path (comb filtering whenever Global Mix or node Mix is below 100%). The track also drifts out of sync with the rest of the session.
findings.suggested_fix: Either constrain Spectral to a latency within spec, or report the worst-case latency through getLatencySamples and restartComponent(kLatencyChanged) when it changes. Delay-compensate the other bands and the dry path to the max band latency. Add a test: one band Spectral at mix 100%, impulse in. Assert that the measured output peak offset equals Processor::getLatencySamples() (it reads 0 today against an actual ~2048-sample delay).
findings.evidence: distortion_adapter.cpp:150 `blockLatency_ = typeParams_.fftSize;`; :248-250 getProcessingLatency (no callers; grep 'getProcessingLatency' in src finds only the definition and declaration); :567 `return spectral_.process(input);`; spectral_distortion.h:492-494 `latency() ... return fftSize_;`; band_processor.h:376-379 `static int getLatency() noexcept { return 0; }`; processor_params.cpp:244 `p.fftSize = 512 * (1 << ...); // 512-4096`.
verifier_notes:
I traced the call path, and the core claim holds for the Spectral type.

1. Spectral runs one sample at a time through an STFT. distortion_adapter.cpp:565-567 returns `spectral_.process(input)` from inside processRaw. That call starts at spectral_distortion.h:217-243: it pushes one sample into the STFT, analyzes only once `stft_.canAnalyze()` is true (a full fftSize window), and returns 0.0f until the overlap-add output has samples. So the output really is delayed by about fftSize samples; latency() at :492-494 returns fftSize_. The FFT size comes from processor_params.cpp:244 (`512 * (1 << ...)`, so 512-4096), defaults to 2048 (distortion_adapter.h:179), and is applied through `spectral_.prepare(sampleRate_, p.fftSize)` (distortion_adapter.cpp:893-896).

2. Nothing reports or aligns this latency. A grep of plugins/disrumpo for getLatencySamples, kLatencyChanged and setLatency finds nothing in src/processor. getProcessingLatency (distortion_adapter.cpp:248-250) is only called from the unit test distortion_adapter_test.cpp:133-149. BandProcessor::getLatency is a static function at band_processor.h:376 that returns 0, and the tests assert that 0 (oversampling_performance_tests.cpp:40-118). The adapter computes blockLatency_ (cpp:150, 155, 179-181), but no other code reads it. A band using a Spectral node is therefore about 2048 samples late: against the host (no PDC), against the other bands at summation, and against the dry path for any mix below 100%. The adapter's own mix at distortion_adapter.cpp:235 blends the undelayed `dry` with the delayed wet output.

3. The spec does say "Latency < 10ms at highest quality" (specs-overview.md:66) and "0 samples (1x) to 256 samples (8x)" (:374). Spectral at 2048 samples and 44.1 kHz is 46 ms, which breaks both.

Two caveats. The Granular latency claim is weaker: I did not confirm a fixed delay in GranularDistortion, and blockLatency_ there is only bookkeeping. I did not check the Feedback claim. Neither changes the verdict, because the Spectral path alone confirms the defect.

I could not refute the core Spectral claim. Nothing in the code or the specs makes the missing latency report intentional or guards against it.
- The latency is real. dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/spectral_distortion.h:217-244: process(float) pushes one sample into the STFT, analyzes only once stft_.canAnalyze() is true (hop = fftSize/2, :158), and returns 0.0f until overlapAdd_ has samples. latency() at :492-494 returns fftSize_. distortion_adapter.cpp:565-567 calls spectral_.process(input) per sample, so a Spectral node delays its band by about fftSize samples. The default is fftSize = 2048 (distortion_adapter.h:179) and the range is 512-4096 (processor_params.cpp:244).
- Nothing reports it. distortion_adapter.cpp:148-160 and :177-182 set blockLatency_. getProcessingLatency (:248-250) has no callers anywhere in plugins/disrumpo/src. Grepping plugins/disrumpo/src/processor/*.h and *.cpp for getLatencySamples or getTailSamples finds nothing. BandProcessor::getLatency (band_processor.h:376-379) is a static that always returns 0. tests/dsp/oversampling_performance_tests.cpp:32-58 pins it at 0, but only for the IIR oversampling case, not for the Spectral type.
- It was not a design decision. The retired spec 003 (git show b6fe8faa7:specs/003-distortion-integration/spec.md:985) says block-based types add a fixed latency "queryable via getProcessingLatency()" and that it is "reported to the host via getTail()". So the spec meant to report the latency, and that wiring was never built. specs/Disrumpo/specs-overview.md:374 ("Latency: 0 samples (1x) to 256 samples (8x)") and :66 ("< 10ms at highest quality") directly contradict a 2048-sample band delay. No code comment documents an exemption.
- Caveat: the Feedback and Granular parts of the title are weaker. Their delays are arguably the sound of the effect rather than processing latency, and Feedback has no blockLatency_ case at all (:157-160). That does not refute the Spectral defect, which is enough on its own to sustain medium severity: an uncompensated band delay of 46-93 ms, comb filtering against the dry path at mix below 100%, and no PDC.

The defect is real, and medium severity is right. (1) SpectralDistortion::process (dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/spectral_distortion.h:217-245) buffers samples one at a time through STFT and overlap-add. Hop is fftSize/2 (:158). It returns 0.0f until the OLA buffer fills, so the output is delayed by the FFT frame. The header itself declares latency() == fftSize_ (:490-494). Even taking the lower bound of fftSize - hop, the delay is at least 256 samples at the 512 minimum and 1024+ at the default 2048 (distortion_adapter.h:179). That is 23-46 ms at 44.1 kHz, against the specs-overview.md:66 limit of '< 10ms' and the :374 limit of '0 samples (1x) to 256 samples (8x)'. Even the minimum spectral delay of about 512 samples (11.6 ms) breaks both limits. (2) The adapter routes Spectral straight to spectral_.process(input) (distortion_adapter.cpp:565-567). It records blockLatency_ (:148-156, :178-182), but nothing reads it. getProcessingLatency (:248-250) appears in a grep of plugins/disrumpo/src only at its definition and its declaration (distortion_adapter.h:325). (3) No getLatencySamples override exists anywhere in plugins/disrumpo/src; the same grep finds one only in profundum. BandProcessor::getLatency is a hard-coded 0 (band_processor.h:376-379). (4) The FFT size really reaches 512-4096 through processor_params.cpp:244. The adapter re-prepares at that size (distortion_adapter.cpp:893-896); at startup it prepares at maxBlockSize (:84). So the host gets no PDC for a band that is late by an FFT frame. That band is also out of line with the other bands (no compensation at summation) and with the dry path (comb filtering when band or global mix is below 100%). The consequence follows as claimed whenever a user selects the Spectral type. I did not measure the exact sample offset, but it is bounded below by the hop size, which is still far over spec. I left severity at medium: Spectral is one opt-in Experimental type of 26 (distortion_adapter_test.cpp:1333), and the default path has no latency. The Granular part of the claim is weaker (grain lag, not a block delay), but it does not change the verdict.

findings.title: Morph smoothing (FR-MORPH-003, 0-500 ms) runs about 4x slower than set, and host session save drops smoothing and morph mode
findings.problem: MorphEngine::setSmoothingTime configures smootherX_/Y_ with sampleRate_, which is 8x the host rate (prepared from band_processor.h:124). process() advances both smoothers on every call, and BandProcessor calls it twice per host sample (L then R, band_processor.h:487-488). The net time constant is 8/2 = 4x the setting. In addition, Processor::getState writes a literal 0 for morphMode and 0.0f for morphSmoothing (processor_state.cpp:319-323), which setState then applies (:825-831).
findings.why_wrong: FR-MORPH-003 specifies 'Configurable smoothing time: 0ms to 500ms'. The configured time should be the real-time glide, and the value must survive a project reload.
findings.consequence: A 500 ms smoothing setting glides for about 2 s, and the default 10 ms for about 40 ms. After any host project reload, every band's Morph Mode returns to 1D Linear and Smoothing to 0 ms, while the controller still shows the saved values, so the UI and the audio disagree.
findings.suggested_fix: Configure the position smoothers at the rate at which process() advances them, and advance them once per stereo frame (split the smoother tick from per-channel processing, or add a stereo process). Write cache.morphMode / smoothing into getState from stored per-band values. Add tests: (1) BandProcessor with smoothing 100 ms, step X 0 to 1, and assert getSmoothedX() is at least 0.99 after 100 ms of host samples; (2) Processor state round-trip with mode Planar2D and smoothing 250 ms preserved.
findings.evidence: morph_engine.cpp:123-125 `smootherX_.configure(smoothingTimeMs_, static_cast<float>(sampleRate_));`; :667-668 `smootherX_.process(); smootherY_.process();` per call; band_processor.h:124 prepare at `sampleRate * kMaxOversampleFactor`, :487-488 two process() calls per sample; processor_state.cpp:319 `writeInt8(0)  // morphMode`, :323 `writeFloat(0.0f)  // morphSmoothing`.
verifier_notes:
I traced both halves of the finding through the source, and both hold.

(1) Smoothing time scale. BandProcessor::prepare calls morphEngine_->prepare(sampleRate * kMaxOversampleFactor, ...) with kMaxOversampleFactor = 8 (band_processor.h:47, :124-125). MorphEngine::prepare stores sampleRate_ = 8*fs and configures smootherX_/Y_ at that rate (morph_engine.cpp:48-52). setSmoothingTime reconfigures them with the same sampleRate_ (:125-129; the finding cites 122-126 but this is the code). MorphEngine::process advances both smoothers once per call (:667-669), and BandProcessor calls it once for L and once for R (band_processor.h:487-488, and :753-754 on the oversampled path).

In the plugin, morph bands always take the direct 1x path. processWithFactor bypasses oversampling when distortion_.getCommonParams().drive < 0.0001 (band_processor.h:629-635). The legacy distortion_ drive is set to 0 in prepare (:115-119), and setDistortionCommonParams has no caller anywhere in src/ (grep). So the smoothers tick 2 times per host sample against a coefficient built for 8 ticks, which makes the glide 4x slower, exactly as claimed. Even if the oversampled paths were reached, only 4x would come out right; 1x/2x would be 4x/2x slow and 8x 2x fast.

The engine-level tests in tests/unit/morph_transition_test.cpp:30-31 prepare MorphEngine at the host rate directly, so they cannot catch this.

(2) State loss. Processor::getState writes literal values: writeInt8(0) for morphMode and writeFloat(0.0f) for morphSmoothing (processor_state.cpp:319-323). bandMorphCache_ does not hold either value, and processor_params.cpp:958-968 forwards them to the band processors without caching them. setState then applies the stream values through setMorphMode / setMorphSmoothingTime (processor_state.cpp:827-831). So after a reload every band runs in Linear1D with 0 ms smoothing.

One detail of the stated consequence is wrong. Controller::setComponentState reads the same processor stream and sets kBandMorphMode and kBandMorphSmoothing from it (controller.cpp:513-529), so the UI also shows Linear / 0 ms. It does not keep showing the saved values. The UI and the audio agree, but the user's settings are still silently lost on project reload. Only the controller's own preset writer stores the real values (controller.cpp:1829-1834). The defect is real; only that sub-claim is overstated.

Both halves hold up in the code. Nothing upstream clamps or compensates for either one.

(1) Smoother rate. band_processor.h:124 prepares the MorphEngine at `sampleRate * kMaxOversampleFactor` (kMaxOversampleFactor = 8, :47). morph_engine.cpp:125-129 setSmoothingTime configures smootherX_/Y_ with that 8x sampleRate_. morph_engine.cpp:662-669 process() advances both smoothers on every call. BandProcessor::process at 1x calls it twice per host sample, L then R (band_processor.h:487-488), so the effective time constant is 8/2 = 4x the setting. The oversampled path calls it twice per oversampled sample (:753-754), which gives a factor of 8/(2N): 2x slower at 2x oversampling, correct at 4x, 2x too fast at 8x. So the glide time also changes with the oversampling factor, which the reviewer did not mention. The existing tests (tests/unit/morph_transition_test.cpp:112-371) drive a standalone MorphEngine with one process() per sample at its own configured rate, so they cannot see the mismatch at band level. No test pins it.

(2) State. processor_state.cpp:319 writes `writeInt8(0)  // morphMode` and :323 writes `writeFloat(0.0f)  // morphSmoothing`. setState reads them back and applies them (:819-831, setMorphMode / setMorphSmoothingTime). Both are real automatable parameters: plugin_ids.h:186 kBandMorphSmoothing and :189 kBandMorphMode, handled in processor_params.cpp:958-968. No comment calls the zeros intentional. By contrast, the controller's own preset writer (controller.cpp:1829-1834) writes the real values. So a host session save loses both settings.

One correction to the stated consequence: controller.cpp:513-529 setComponentState reads the same zeros from the processor stream and pushes them into the controller parameters. After a reload the UI therefore also shows Linear and 0 ms, so the UI and audio agree, but both have lost the user's setting. That makes it silent data loss rather than a UI/audio mismatch. The defect stands and medium severity is appropriate.

Both parts of the defect are real. Two details in the finding are wrong, but neither changes the severity.

(1) Smoothing rate. band_processor.h:124 prepares the MorphEngine at `sampleRate * kMaxOversampleFactor`, and kMaxOversampleFactor is 8 (:47). morph_engine.cpp:47-52 configures smootherX_/Y_ at that rate, and setSmoothingTime does the same at :125-128 with sampleRate_. MorphEngine::process() advances both smoothers on every call (:667-669). BandProcessor calls process() twice per frame, once for L and once for R: at :487-488 on the 1x path, and at :753-754 inside processOversampledBlock, which runs at the oversampled rate for the 2x, 4x and 8x paths (:709-742). The effective glide time is therefore 8 / (2*OS) times the setting:
- 1x: 4x too slow (500 ms glides for about 2 s, the default for about 40 ms)
- 2x: 2x too slow
- 4x: correct
- 8x: 2x too fast

So "about 4x" holds only on 1x bands. The real defect is a glide time that depends on the oversampling factor, and the factor is chosen per morph weight, so it can also change rate mid-glide when the factor switches.

(2) State loss. processor_state.cpp:319 writes int8 0 for morphMode and :323 writes 0.0f for morphSmoothing. setState reads these at :819-821 and applies them at :827-831 (setMorphMode and setMorphSmoothingTime). No other processor state field carries kBandMorphMode or kBandMorphSmoothing; a grep finds them only at processor_params.cpp:958-968. After a host project reload, every band therefore returns to 1D Linear and 0 ms smoothing.

The finding's claim that "the controller still shows saved values, so the UI and the audio disagree" is wrong. Controller::setComponentState (controller.cpp:619-635) parses the same processor stream and sets kBandMorphMode and kBandMorphSmoothing from the zeros (:522-529). Controller::getState/setState (:658-701) store only MIDI CC data. The UI shows the reset values too, consistent with the audio, so the user's settings are silently lost.

The controller's preset writer (controller.cpp:1829-1834) does write the real values, so factory and user presets keep them. Only host session save/restore, which goes through Processor::getState, drops them.

Net: a user-audible spec violation (FR-MORPH-003 timing) plus state loss on every project reload. Medium severity stands.

findings.title: 1D Linear mode cannot address C and D (FR-MORPH-002 'A<->B<->C<->D'): node positions are fixed at the corners, so C aliases A and D aliases B
findings.problem: Node positions are only set in setupProcessing: A(0,0), B(1,0), C(0,1), D(1,1). No processor path ever changes posX/posY (grep 'posX =' in processor/ and dsp/ finds nothing), and node positions are not in the state stream (processor_state.cpp:834-861 reads only type/common/bias/folds/bitDepth). Linear1D (morph_engine.cpp:180-210) uses posX only, so C shares x=0 with A and D shares x=1 with B. The on-node early return at :188-192 always picks the first index.
findings.why_wrong: FR-MORPH-002 defines 1D Linear as 'Single axis A<->B<->C<->D', and the MorphMode doc says 'Single axis A-B-C-D interpolation using morphX only' (distortion_types.h:378). With 3-4 nodes the axis should visit each node in turn.
findings.consequence: In 1D mode with 3 or 4 nodes, C and D are never reached distinctly: at x=0 only A sounds, at x=1 only B, and in between A/C and B/D are always mixed in equal pairs. Dragging nodes on the MorphPad (morph_pad.cpp keeps its own copy) changes nothing audible in any mode.
findings.suggested_fix: For Linear1D, place active nodes at posX = i/(N-1) along the axis (or define a 1D order independent of the XY corners), or transmit node positions from the editor as parameters and persist them. Add a test: 3 nodes (SoftClip, SineFold, Bitcrush) in Linear1D at X=0.5. Assert that weight[1] (B) is about 1 and weight[2] (C) is distinct from weight[0].
findings.evidence: processor.cpp:114 `MorphNode(0, 0.0f, 0.0f, ...)`, :116 `MorphNode(1, 1.0f, 0.0f, ...)`, :118 `MorphNode(2, 0.0f, 1.0f, ...)`, :120 `MorphNode(3, 1.0f, 1.0f, ...)`; morph_engine.cpp:185 `distances[i] = calculate1DDistance(posX, nodes_[i].posX);` :188-192 on-node early return picks first i; distortion_types.h:378 Linear1D doc.
verifier_notes:
I traced the code and the defect is real.

1. Node positions are fixed at the four corners. processor.cpp:114-121 sets A(0,0), B(1,0), C(0,1) and D(1,1) in setupProcessing, and morph_engine.cpp:41-44 and band_state.h:49-52 use the same defaults.

2. Nothing on the processor side ever moves a node. Searching plugins/disrumpo/src for `posX =`, `posY =` and `MorphNode(` finds writes only in those default constructors and in the editor's own copy (morph_pad.cpp:169-172 and 206-207). That copy never reaches the processor. The only node-related write in processor_state.cpp is shapeSlots at :871, so positions are not part of the state stream either.

3. In Linear1D (morph_engine.cpp:180-210) the distance is `calculate1DDistance(posX, nodes_[i].posX)` (:185), so it uses node X only. C has the same X as A (0) and D has the same X as B (1).
   - The cursor-on-node check at :188-192 returns at the first index under the threshold. At x=0 that is A, at x=1 that is B, so C and D never get full weight.
   - Between 0 and 1, the inverse-distance weights at :196-207 come out equal for A and C, and equal for B and D.

4. The code's own doc and the spec both describe a visit to each node in turn. distortion_types.h:378 says "Single axis A-B-C-D interpolation using morphX only", and specs-overview.md:233 (FR-MORPH-002) says "1D Linear | Single axis A↔B↔C↔D". With 3 or 4 active nodes, C and D can never be reached on their own in 1D mode.

The secondary claim also holds: dragging nodes on the MorphPad changes nothing audible in any mode, because those moves only update the editor's copy (morph_pad.cpp:206-207).

Medium severity fits. The 2-node default is unaffected, but the 3- and 4-node 1D configurations fail to do what the spec says.

The defect is real, and nothing upstream guards it or documents it as a design choice. processor.cpp:114-121 puts the four nodes at the corners: A(0,0), B(1,0), C(0,1), D(1,1). Grepping src/ for posX/posY assignments finds only the MorphNode field declarations (morph_node.h:49/54), read sites in morph_engine.cpp/band_processor.h, and the controller-only copies in views/morph_pad.cpp:169-172 and :206-207. No processor or DSP path ever moves a node. In Linear1D, morph_engine.cpp:185 uses only nodes_[i].posX, so C has the same x as A and D the same x as B. The on-node early return at :188-192 gives 100% to the first index, so at x=0 A takes everything and C is silent. Both settings a user needs are host-exposed parameters: kBandMorphMode (plugin_ids.h:189, handled at processor_params.cpp:964-968) and kBandActiveNodes [2,3,4] (plugin_ids.h:185). In a real host, 1D mode with 3 or 4 nodes is reachable.

I found no documented design decision that excuses it. specs/Disrumpo/custom-controls.md:1013-1016 says "1D Linear Mode ... Nodes arranged along X axis". specs-overview.md:233 and dsp-details.md:151 say "Single axis A<->B<->C<->D". distortion_types.h:378 says "Single axis A-B-C-D interpolation using morphX only". The UI does not arrange nodes for 1D either: morph_pad.cpp:457-469 only draws a centre line, :804-806 pins the cursor Y to 0.5, and nodes are still drawn at their corner positions (:514).

The existing tests do not cover this case. morph_mode_test.cpp:43-50 builds its own 3-node line (0, 0.5, 1) for the 3-node Linear1D test (:115-133), which shows the engine expects nodes along the axis. No test covers the processor's actual corner layout in 1D with more than 2 nodes. Severity stays medium. This is a functional spec gap in a user-selectable mode, not a safety or NaN issue. The default node count is low (morph_node.h:135 kDefaultActiveNodes = 1, and the parameter's lowest choice is 2 nodes), so many users will not hit it.

I could not refute this finding. The source supports both the defect and the claimed consequence.

**Node positions are fixed at the corners.** processor.cpp:114-121 places A(0,0), B(1,0), C(0,1) and D(1,1). Nothing in the processor or dsp code moves them later. A grep for `posX =` and `.posX` across plugins/disrumpo/src finds only these:
- the field declaration at morph_node.h:49
- reads at band_processor.h:591 and morph_engine.cpp:185, 217 and 317
- MorphPad's own copy (morph_pad.cpp:169-172 resets it, :206 sets it)

**Dragging a node on the pad goes nowhere.** morph_pad.cpp:764 calls `listener_->onNodePositionChanged`, but no controller implements that callback (grep in src/controller finds only the interface at morph_pad.h:51). No node-position parameter or message exists, so node drags never reach the processor.

**1D mode puts C on top of A and D on top of B.** Linear1D (morph_engine.cpp:180-210) computes `calculate1DDistance(posX, nodes_[i].posX)` and nothing else, so C (x=0) sits on A and D (x=1) sits on B. The on-node early return at :188-192 returns at the first match. At X=0 only A sounds and C is never reached. At X=1 only B sounds and D is never reached. Between the ends, inverse-distance weighting gives A and C identical weights, and B and D identical weights. Example with 3 nodes at X=0.5: A, B and C each get one third. C or D can never be the dominant or isolated node.

**Impact.** 1D Linear is the default morph mode:
- the StringListParameter at parameter_registration.cpp:688-690 has "1D Linear" as entry 0, the default
- band_state.h:42 defaults to Linear1D
- morph_engine.h:220 defaults to Linear1D

So any user who raises Active Nodes to 3 or 4 without changing the mode hits this. The spec text (specs-overview.md:233, "Single axis A<->B<->C<->D") and distortion_types.h:378 both promise a sequential axis, so this is a real spec-conformance failure with an audible effect: two of the four configured distortion types can never be isolated.

**Severity: medium is right.** The defect produces no NaN, crash, click or level hazard, and the 2D modes still reach every corner. It is more than cosmetic, though, because the feature cannot do what its spec says in the default mode.

findings.title: FR-SWEEP-002 / Appendix A sweep and band-count parameters disagree with the spec at the host boundary (range, scale, defaults)
findings.problem: Sweep Frequency is a linear RangeParameter 20-20000 Hz with default 1000 (comment says 'log scale'), while the processor decodes the normalized value on a log2 scale (processor_params.cpp:381-385). Sweep Intensity is registered 0-100 % with default 50, while the DSP maps norm*2 (0-200 %, processor_params.cpp:404-406). Sweep Width defaults to 1.0 oct, while Appendix A and the processor atomics (processor.h, 0.286 for 1.5 oct) say 1.5. Band Count calls setNormalized(1.0), but ParameterInfo.defaultNormalizedValue stays 0, so the host default is 1 band (Appendix A: 4).
findings.why_wrong: FR-SWEEP-002 specifies Intensity 0-200 %. Appendix A specifies Sweep Freq default 1 kHz, Width default 1.5 oct, Intensity default 50 % and Band Count default 4. The host-facing normalized-to-plain mapping must equal the processor's denormalization, or host readouts and reset-to-default are wrong.
findings.consequence: Host 'reset to default' on Sweep Frequency sends 0.049, which the processor plays as ~28 Hz, not 1 kHz. Host automation lanes and readouts show linear Hz for a log control. Sweep Intensity displays 100 % where the DSP applies 200 %, and its 50 % default is DSP intensity 1.0 while the engine starts at 0.5. Band Count reset gives 1 band.
findings.suggested_fix: Register these as log-mapped parameters (a Parameter subclass whose toPlain/toNormalized use the same log2 / log10 formula the processor uses), register Intensity as 0-200 %, set Width's default to 1.5 oct, and construct list params with the intended default index so defaultNormalizedValue is right. Add a test that iterates the sweep, crossover and band-count params and asserts processor-decoded plain(param->getInfo().defaultNormalizedValue) equals the Appendix A default.
findings.evidence: parameter_registration.cpp:182 comment 'log scale' vs :183-188 `new RangeParameter(... 20.0, 20000.0, 1000.0 ...)`; :197-199 `0.5, 4.0, 1.0`; :203-210 `0.0, 100.0, 50.0` unit %; :75 `bandCountParam->setNormalized(1.0)`; processor_params.cpp:384 `kSweepLog2Min + value * kSweepLog2Range`; :405 `intensity = value * 2.0f`; specs-overview.md Appendix A rows Sweep Freq 1 kHz, Sweep Width default 1.5 oct, Sweep Intensity 0%-200% default 50%, Band Count default 4.
verifier_notes:
I traced every part of the claim through the code and it holds.

(1) Sweep Frequency. parameter_registration.cpp:183-190 registers a plain linear RangeParameter(20, 20000, default 1000). The SDK's RangeParameter ctor (vstparameters.cpp:151) sets defaultNormalizedValue = toNormalized(1000) = (1000-20)/19980 ≈ 0.049. The processor (processor_params.cpp:381-385) decodes the value as 2^(4.3219 + v*9.9658); at v=0.049 that is about 28 Hz, not 1 kHz. The controller's own setComponentState fallback (controller.cpp:219, sweepFreqNorm 0.566) and the processor atomic (processor.h:224, 1000 Hz) both assume the log mapping. getParamStringByValue (controller.cpp:747-894) has no sweep case and falls through to EditControllerEx1, so host readouts show linear Hz. The "log scale" comment at :182 is wrong.

(2) Sweep Intensity. It is registered 0-100 % with default 50 (:205-212), so the default norm is 0.5. The processor maps norm*2 (processor_params.cpp:405), giving intensity 1.0 at that default, while the processor atomic baseSweepIntensityNorm_ starts at 0.25 (processor.h:230) and the controller state fallback also uses 0.25 (controller.cpp:221). The controller's own sweep indicator scales by 2 as well (visibility_controllers.cpp:557). So the host shows 100 % where the DSP applies 200 %, and reset-to-default doubles the intended intensity.

(3) Sweep Width. The registered default is 1.0 oct (:198), which is norm 0.143. The processor atomic is 0.286 (processor.h:227), the controller fallback is 0.286 (controller.cpp:220), and spec Appendix A line 408 says 1.5 oct.

(4) Band Count. The StringListParameter ctor sets info.defaultNormalizedValue = 0 (vstparameters.cpp:235). setNormalized(1.0) at :76 changes only valueNormalized, so the host default is index 0, which is 1 band. Appendix A line 399 says the default is 4. Note that the same row gives the maximum as 8, but that does not affect this claim.

Spec Appendix A (specs-overview.md:407-409) confirms 1 kHz, 1.5 oct, and 0-200 % with default 50 %.

The mismatch only affects the host-facing mapping, defaults and display; the processor's own defaults are correct. So medium severity is appropriate.

Nothing upstream or downstream absorbs the defect, so I could not refute it.

(1) Sweep Frequency: plugins/disrumpo/src/controller/parameter_registration.cpp:182-191 registers a plain linear RangeParameter(20, 20000, default 1000). The SDK sets its default as toNormalized(1000) = 0.049 (vstparameters.cpp:151). processor_params.cpp:381-385 decodes the same normalized value as 2^(log2 20 + v*range), which turns 0.049 into about 28 Hz. The controller's own sweep indicator also decodes on log2 (controller.cpp:1281-1286). So the code itself treats the parameter as log while the host readout and default are linear. The plugin_ids.h:95 comment says "log scale", which shows log was intended and the registration does not deliver it.

(2) Sweep Intensity: the registration is 0-100 %, default 50 (parameter_registration.cpp:204-211). The processor applies value*2 (processor_params.cpp:405, processor.cpp:289) and the controller's indicator does too (controller.cpp:1292). The processor's initial atomic is baseSweepIntensityNorm_{0.25f} (processor.h:230), which is intensity 0.5. The controller default normalizes to 0.5, which is intensity 1.0. The spec (specs-overview.md:409) says 0-200 %, default 50 %.

(3) Sweep Width: the controller default is 1.0 oct (parameter_registration.cpp:198), but processor.h:227 starts at 0.286 norm (1.5 oct) and specs-overview.md:408 says 1.5 oct.

(4) Band Count: the StringListParameter constructor sets info.defaultNormalizedValue = 0 (vstparameters.cpp:235). setNormalized(1.0) at parameter_registration.cpp:76 only changes the current value, so the host default is 1 band. The processor default is kDefaultBands (processor.h:153) and the spec says 4 (specs-overview.md:399).

No test in plugins/disrumpo/tests checks defaultNormalizedValue or the sweep registration mapping. No spec text or code comment documents the linear or 0-100 % registration as a deliberate choice. Medium severity fits: host reset-to-default, readouts and automation lanes are wrong, but the audio thread is safe.

The defect is real and the claimed consequences follow from the code.

1. Sweep Frequency. parameter_registration.cpp:183-190 registers a linear RangeParameter from 20 to 20000 Hz with default 1000, even though the comment at :182 says "log scale". The default normalized value is therefore (1000-20)/19980 = 0.049. The processor decodes on a log2 scale (processor_params.cpp:381-388, `2^(4.3219 + v*9.9658)`). At 0.049 that gives 2^4.81, about 28 Hz. The controller itself also decodes log2: in controller.cpp:1281-1286 for the sweep indicator, and in visibility_controllers.cpp:543 and :585 through denormalizeSweepFrequency. Only the host-facing toPlain/toString is linear. The processor's default is 1000 Hz (processor.h:224), and its state fallback is norm 0.566 (processor_state.cpp:472). When the processor sits at 1 kHz (norm 0.566), the host's generic readout shows 20 + 0.566*19980, about 11.3 kHz. Host "reset to default" sends 0.049, which plays at about 28 Hz.

2. Sweep Intensity. It is registered as 0-100 % with default 50 (parameter_registration.cpp:205-212), so its default norm is 0.5. The DSP applies norm*2 (processor_params.cpp:405, processor.cpp:289, processor_state.cpp:488). The processor's own default norm is 0.25, which means DSP intensity 0.5 (processor.h:230, processor_state.cpp:474, controller.cpp:221). Two results: a host reset gives DSP intensity 1.0, double the engine default, and the readout shows half the applied value (25 % shown for 50 % applied).

3. Sweep Width. Its default is 1.0 oct, which is norm 0.143 (parameter_registration.cpp:198). The processor default norm is 0.286, which is 1.5 oct (processor.h:227, processor_state.cpp:473). A host reset therefore gives a narrower width than the engine default.

4. Band Count. parameter_registration.cpp:76 calls setNormalized(1.0), but nothing in plugins/disrumpo/src writes ParameterInfo.defaultNormalizedValue (grep finds no hits). The SDK's Parameter::setNormalized only sets valueNormalized, so the advertised default stays 0, which is index 0, i.e. 1 band. A host reset collapses the plugin to 1 band, which is audible.

None of these is compensated anywhere. All four are plain RangeParameter or StringListParameter instances with no toPlain/toNormalized overrides. The impact depends on the host: generic-UI readouts are wrong in every host, and reset-to-default or default-value-based automation behaves wrongly in hosts that use defaultNormalizedValue (Cubase, Reaper, Bitwig). Sweep Enable defaults to off, so the frequency error is only heard while the sweep is on, but the band-count reset is heard in every configuration. Medium severity fits.

findings.title: FR-DIST-003 / Appendix A type-parameter ranges drift from the spec, and Bitcrush's 1-4 bit range (bottom 20 % of the knob) is a dead zone
findings.problem: mapShapeSlotsToParams maps slots to ranges wider than the spec: folds 1-12 (spec 1-8; the wavefolder clamps at 10), Temporal attack 1-500 ms (spec 1-100), release 10-5000 ms (spec 10-500), Aliasing freq shift +/-5000 Hz (spec +/-1000), Chaos attractor speed 0.01-100 (spec 0.1-10), Formant shift +/-24 st (spec +/-12). Bitcrush maps bits to 1-16 per spec, but the shared BitCrusher clamps to [4,16] (bit_crusher.h:50,152).
findings.why_wrong: FR-DIST-003 and Appendix A define these ranges. The adapter header comments (distortion_adapter.h) repeat the spec ranges, so code, header and spec disagree. For Bitcrush, the spec's 1-16 range is displayed but bits below 4 are unreachable.
findings.consequence: Knob travel does not match the documented ranges (most knob travel spent outside the musical range on Temporal/Chaos). The lowest ~20 % of the Bitcrush Bits knob (1-4 bits) sounds identical to 4 bits.
findings.suggested_fix: Decide per parameter whether spec or code is authoritative and make spec, header comments and mapping agree. For Bitcrush, either lower BitCrusher::kMinBitDepth (shared primitive: CROSS-PLUGIN, check consumers) or map the slot to [4,16]. Add a mapping test that asserts each slot's 0 and 1 endpoints equal the Appendix A min and max.
findings.evidence: processor_params.cpp:90 `p.folds = 1.0f + slots[0] * 11.0f; // [1,12]`; :131 `p.bitDepth = 1.0f + slots[0] * 15.0f; // [1,16]`; :159 `p.attackMs = 1.0f + slots[3] * 499.0f;` :160 `p.releaseMs = 10.0f + slots[4] * 4990.0f;` :194 `* 5000.0f`; :207 `0.01f + slots[1] * 99.99f`; :219 `* 24.0f`; bit_crusher.h:50 `kMinBitDepth = 4.0f`, :152 `bitDepth_ = std::clamp(bits, kMinBitDepth, kMaxBitDepth)`; specs-overview.md FR-DIST-003 lists Folds (1-8), Attack (1-100ms), Release (10-500ms), Attractor Speed (0.1-10.0), Formant Shift (-12 to +12), Bit Depth (1.0-16.0).
verifier_notes:
The code says what the finding claims. In processor_params.cpp the Bitcrush slot is mapped at :131 as `p.bitDepth = 1.0f + slots[0] * 15.0f`. distortion_adapter.cpp:709 passes that value to `rawBitCrusher_.setBitDepth(p.bitDepth)`. Its type is Krate::DSP::BitCrusher (distortion_adapter.h:405), and that setter clamps with `std::clamp(bits, kMinBitDepth, kMaxBitDepth)` (bit_crusher.h:152), where kMinBitDepth = 4.0f (bit_crusher.h:50). Any slot value below 0.2 gives a raw value under 4, so it clamps to 4 bits: the bottom 20 % of the knob does nothing. The modulation path at distortion_adapter.cpp:463 also clamps to [1,16] before the same setter, so the dead zone is there too.

The other spec drifts are also real. The mappings are folds 1-12 (:90/:99/:108), attack 1-500 ms and release 10-5000 ms (:159-160), freq shift +/-5000 Hz (:194), attractor speed 0.01-100 (:207) and formant shift +/-24 st (:219). The spec says Folds 1-8, Attack 1-100 ms, Release 10-500 ms, Attractor Speed 0.1-10 and Formant Shift +/-12 (specs-overview.md:217-221 and :422/:428/:430), and Freq Shift +/-1000 Hz (ui-mockups.md:571, specs-overview.md:422). The DistortionTypeParams field comments repeat the spec ranges (distortion_adapter.h:99, 109, 125, 126, 149, 156, 162), so the spec, the header comments and the mapping disagree.

One mitigating point: the shared processors accept the wider ranges. TemporalDistortion allows 0.1-500 ms attack and 1-5000 ms release (temporal_distortion.h:130-135), AliasingEffect allows +/-5000 Hz (aliasing_effect.h:88-89) and FormantDistortion allows +/-24 st (formant_distortion.h:85-86). So for those parameters the mapping matches the DSP limits on purpose and only the docs drift; they are not dead zones.

The finding understates one dead zone. Both fold processors clamp at 10 (wavefolder_processor.h:125 kMaxFoldAmount = 10.0f; wavefolder.h:150 clamps to [0,10]). With folds = 1 + s*11, any slot value above about 0.818 clamps, so the top ~18 % of the Folds knob is dead as well.

I could not confirm the secondary claim that the UI displays a 1-16 range; I found no display formatter for the shape slot. The core defect (an unreachable knob range for Bitcrush, and for Folds) is confirmed from source. It is a usability and spec-conformance problem with no safety impact, so low severity fits.

Confirmed from source. processor_params.cpp:131 maps Bitcrush slot0 to `1.0f + slots[0]*15.0f` (range [1,16]). distortion_adapter.cpp:709 passes that to rawBitCrusher_ (Krate::DSP::BitCrusher, distortion_adapter.h:405), and the jitter path at :463 clamps to [1,16] before calling setBitDepth at :467. BitCrusher::setBitDepth (bit_crusher.h:152) clamps to kMinBitDepth=4 (:50). The controller's format_helpers.h:124 still shows `1.0 + v*15.0` "bit", so knob values 0 to 0.2 read "1.0 bit" to "4.0 bit" but all sound like 4 bits. That is a real dead zone with a misleading readout. Nothing documents or guards it, and distortion_adapter_test.cpp:1032 even sets bitDepth=1 as if it were reachable.

The range drift is also real against the spec. specs-overview.md:217-221 (FR-DIST-003) and Appendix A :413-430 give Folds 1-8, Attack 1-100, Release 10-500, Freq Shift +/-1000, Attractor Speed 0.1-10 and Formant +/-12. The code uses wider ranges, and distortion_adapter.h:99,125,126,149,156,162 still states the spec ranges. Mitigating context: the wider mappings match the shared processors' own limits (temporal_distortion.h:131,135 attack max 500 / release max 5000; aliasing_effect.h:88-89 +/-5000 Hz; formant_distortion.h:85-86 +/-24 st), and the controller display (format_helpers.h:70,75) agrees with the code. So most of the drift looks like a deliberate code-side decision the docs never caught up with, not a bug. The exception is folds: the mapping goes to [1,12] but wavefolder.h:150 clamps at 10, so the top of that knob is also dead. The finding holds at low severity: documentation drift plus two small dead zones (Bitcrush 1-4 bits and folds above 10).

The consequence is real and low severity is the right rating.

Bitcrush dead zone, confirmed from code:
- processor_params.cpp:131 maps `bitDepth = 1 + slots[0]*15`.
- distortion_adapter.cpp:709 and :467 pass that value to `rawBitCrusher_`. That member is a `Krate::DSP::BitCrusher` (distortion_adapter.h:405).
- bit_crusher.h:50/152 clamps it to [4,16].
- So for slot values 0 to 0.2, bitDepth runs 1 to 4 and every value is clamped to 4. The bottom 20 % of the knob travel does nothing audible.
- The controller still shows it as 1.0 to 4.0 bit (format_helpers.h:124 `1.0 + v*15.0`), so the user sees values change while the sound stays the same.
- Jitter is affected too. distortion_adapter.cpp:463 clamps the jittered depth to [1,16], but anything below 4 is then floored to 4 by the BitCrusher. Near low depths the jitter therefore only moves upward.

Folds have the same problem:
- processor_params.cpp:90/99/108 map folds to [1,12].
- wavefolder.h:146-150 clamps them to [0,10].
- So slot values from about 0.818 to 1.0 (roughly 18 % of travel) are also dead.

Range drift from the spec is confirmed:
- specs-overview.md:217-221 and the Appendix A rows at 422/428/430 give Folds 1-8, Attack 1-100 ms, Release 10-500 ms, Attractor Speed 0.1-10, Formant Shift +/-12 st and Freq Shift +/-1000 Hz.
- The code maps wider ranges.
- Those wider ranges deliberately match the shared processors' own clamps: temporal_distortion.h:131/135 (500 ms / 5000 ms), chaos_waveshaper.h:121-122 (0.01-100), formant_distortion.h:85-86 (+/-24), aliasing_effect.h:88-89 (+/-5000).
- That part is a documentation and spec mismatch, not a functional bug. The claim that most knob travel is spent outside the musical range is a judgement call, not a defect.

Impact: no crash, no NaN, no state break. The symptom is UI dishonesty plus a dead stretch of knob travel on Bitcrush Bits and on Folds. Low severity stands.

findings.title: Global metering (spec 3.7: input/output stereo peak+RMS, per-band indicators) is not implemented
findings.problem: No meter view, meter parameter or level message exists. grep -i 'meter|peak|rms' over src/controller and editor.uidesc finds nothing outside parameter names, and the processor sends only spectrum mono blocks.
findings.why_wrong: specs-overview.md 3.7 Global Controls: 'Metering: Input/Output stereo peak+RMS, per-band indicators'.
findings.consequence: Users cannot see input or output level or per-band activity while gain-staging a distortion that can add +24 dB of band gain and drive 10. This is a missing specified feature.
findings.suggested_fix: Either implement the meters (processor computes peak/RMS per block and sends them through the existing DataExchange block, and the editor adds meter views) or strike the line from the spec. If implemented, add a controller test that a meter tag exists and receives non-zero values from a test block.
findings.evidence: specs-overview.md 3.7 'Metering: Input/Output stereo peak+RMS, per-band indicators'; Bash grep -rn -i 'meter|peak\b|rms' over src/controller/*.cpp, src/controller/*.h and resources/editor.uidesc (excluding 'parameter') returned no output.
verifier_notes:
I could not refute this. The spec does require metering, and the code has none.

The implementation: I counted every view class in plugins/disrumpo/resources/editor.uidesc. They are ArcKnob, COptionMenu, CParamDisplay, CScrollView, CSegmentButton, CSlider, CTextButton, CTextLabel, CView, CViewContainer, ModSlider, ToggleButton and UIViewSwitchContainer. The custom-view-names are CheckForUpdatesButton, DynamicNodeSelector, MorphPad, NodeEditorBorder, PresetBrowserButton, SavePresetButton, SpectrumDisplay, SweepIndicator, UpdateBanner and VersionLabel; none of them is a meter. src/controller/views/ holds no meter view either. I could not refute this. specs/Disrumpo/specs-overview.md:366 lists "Metering: Input/Output stereo peak+RMS, per-band indicators" under 3.7 Global Controls.
