findings.title: Docs and CHANGELOG claim features the code does not deliver (intelligent oversampling, MIDI CC learn, 120 presets)
findings.problem: The public docs advertise automatic 2x/4x oversampling and MIDI CC learn, neither of which works in the plugin (see the oversampling and event-bus findings), and '120 factory presets' while 121 .vstpreset files ship (factory_preset_validation_test.cpp expects 121) and the generator emits 119. CHANGELOG.md:121 and :124 (0.9.0) make the same oversampling and MIDI-learn claims.
findings.why_wrong: User-facing documentation must describe the shipped behaviour. The preset count should match the files and the generator that produces them.
findings.consequence: Users rely on oversampling to avoid aliasing and on MIDI learn for performance, and get neither. The preset count claim disagrees with the product, and regenerating presets from the tool would drop two shipped presets.
findings.suggested_fix: After fixing or ruling on oversampling and MIDI, update docs/index.html:118 and :123. Reconcile the preset count (disk 121, generator 119, docs 120) by adding the two missing presets to tools/disrumpo_preset_generator.cpp and stating 121, or removing the extras.
findings.evidence: docs/index.html:118 'Intelligent oversampling — automatically selects 2x or 4x oversampling per algorithm'; :121 '120 factory presets across 11 categories'; :123 'Full parameter automation and MIDI CC learn support'; CHANGELOG.md:121 'Intelligent oversampling for alias-free distortion', :124 'MIDI CC learn for parameter automation'; inventory count: 121 files on disk, generator 119 PresetDef blocks.
verifier_notes:
I checked all three claims against the source and could not refute any of them.

(1) Oversampling. docs/index.html:118 and CHANGELOG.md:121 say oversampling is selected automatically. The machinery exists in band_processor.h: processWithFactor at 627-650, processWithOversampling2x/4x/8x at 709-743, and processBlock/processBlockInner at 548-556. The audio path never reaches it. processor.cpp:467-503 loops per sample and calls bandProcessors_[b].process(bandL, bandR) at 494, and the same call at 487 for muted or non-soloed bands. That is the per-sample BandProcessor::process(float&, float&) at band_processor.h:473-494, which calls morphEngine_->process or distortion_.process directly at 1x with no oversampler. On top of that, distortion_ and morphEngine_ are prepared at sampleRate * kMaxOversampleFactor (8x, band_processor.h:111 and 124) but run at 1x. So the shipped plugin never oversamples.

(2) MIDI CC learn. docs:123 and CHANGELOG:124 advertise it. processor.cpp:65-66 adds only stereo audio in and out, with no addEventInput. Gradus, Innexus and Membrum do add one. Without an event input bus, VST3 hosts neither route MIDI to the component nor query IMidiMapping (controller.cpp:707), so data.inputEvents is empty. The learn scan at processor.cpp:392-412 also matches only kLegacyMIDICCOutEvent. Learn state is split across two IDs as well: the controller sets kGlobalMidiLearnActive (controller.cpp:1626), while the processor reacts to kSweepMidiLearnActive (processor_params.cpp:527). The advertised feature cannot work in a host.

(3) Preset count. docs:121 and CHANGELOG say 120 presets in 11 categories; there are 11 category directories. There are 121 .vstpreset files on disk. factory_preset_validation_test.cpp:144 checks size() == 121, while its header comments at lines 4 and 8 still say 120. tools/disrumpo_preset_generator.cpp has 119 "PresetDef p;" blocks. Diffing names, the two files on disk with no generator entry are Experimental/Formant_Shift (the generator places Formant Shift only under Morph) and Init/Init_5_Bands (an Init preset for 5 bands, though the maximum is 4). Regenerating would therefore drop two shipped files, and the three counts (121 / 119 / 120) disagree as claimed.

Low severity fits a documentation and consistency defect: the real impact is already carried by the separate oversampling and event-bus findings.

I could not refute any of the three claims. Each one is backed by the code.

1. Docs text: plugins/disrumpo/docs/index.html:118 advertises "Intelligent oversampling ... automatically selects 2x or 4x". :121 says "120 factory presets across 11 categories". :123 says "Full parameter automation and MIDI CC learn support". CHANGELOG.md 0.9.0 makes the same claims about oversampling, 120 presets and MIDI CC learn.

2. Oversampling: the shipped signal path never uses it. processor.cpp:466-499 runs the band loop one sample at a time and calls bandProcessors_[b].process(bandL, bandR) (lines 487 and 494). BandProcessor::process (band_processor.h:473-494) calls morphEngine_->process / distortion_.process directly at the base rate. The only routes to oversampler2x_/4x_/8xInner_ are processBlock -> processBlockInner -> processWithFactor (band_processor.h:519-652, 708-737), and the processor never calls processBlock. So recalculateOversampleFactor and setMaxOversampleFactor (processor_params.cpp:360) have no audible effect. On top of that, the adapter and morph engine are prepared at sampleRate*8 (band_processor.h:111, 124) but run at 1x. Nothing guards this elsewhere, and no design note calls it intentional.

3. MIDI CC learn: the processor adds only one stereo audio input and one stereo audio output, with no addEventInput (processor.cpp:65-66). Hosts therefore send no MIDI to the plugin and have no event bus to query IMidiMapping against (controller.cpp:707-726). The processor's learn scan (processor.cpp:392-411) also looks for Event::kLegacyMIDICCOutEvent, an output event type that hosts do not deliver as input. The learn UI exists (controller.cpp:1590-1655), but the end-to-end feature cannot work in a real host as wired.

4. Preset count: 121 .vstpreset files are under resources/presets. factory_preset_validation_test.cpp:144 checks size()==121, while its header comments at lines 4 and 8 still say 120. tools/disrumpo_preset_generator.cpp holds 119 PresetDef entries: 122 grep hits minus the struct, the vector and the function-signature lines. Docs, disk and generator disagree, as the finding says.

No upstream guard, no documented design decision and no pinning test excuses these claims. Low severity fits: this is a documentation finding, and the real defects (oversampling never reached, no event bus) are separate findings.

I could not refute this. All three documentation claims are false for the shipped plugin.

(1) Oversampling. docs/index.html:118 says it "automatically selects 2x or 4x oversampling per algorithm", and CHANGELOG.md:121 makes the same claim. In processor.cpp:466-500 the per-sample loop calls only bandProcessors_[b].process(bandL, bandR) (lines 487 and 494). BandProcessor::process (band_processor.h:473-514) calls morphEngine_->process or distortion_.process directly at the base rate. No oversampler is involved. The oversampled path (processBlock -> processWithFactor -> processWithOversampling2x/4x/8x, band_processor.h:519, 627, 709-742) is never called from the processor; a grep finds no processBlock call on a band. recalculateOversampleFactor (band_processor.h:392) only changes state that the live path never reads. Every shaper therefore runs at 1x, so the advertised alias suppression is absent.

(2) MIDI CC learn. docs/index.html:123 and CHANGELOG.md:124 advertise it. Controller::getMidiControllerAssignment exists (controller.cpp:707-726) and only answers for busIndex 0 (line 712). The processor registers only an audio input (processor.cpp:65) and has no addEventInput. The busIndex in IMidiMapping refers to an event input bus, so with no event bus a host has no MIDI to route and never asks for these mappings. Learn cannot work in Cubase, Reaper or Bitwig.

(3) Preset count. docs/index.html:121 and CHANGELOG say "120 factory presets", and the comments in tests/integration/preset/factory_preset_validation_test.cpp:4 and :8 say 120. However, `find resources/presets -name '*.vstpreset'` counts 121 files, and the same test asserts presetFiles.size() == 121 at line 144. The count is internally inconsistent, as claimed.

Impact: this finding is documentation only. The real consequences (aliasing, no MIDI learn) belong to the separate oversampling and event-bus findings. For this item, users are misled about features and the preset count is off by one. Low severity is correct.

findings.title: Stale spec and code comments: 1-8 bands and default 2 morph nodes vs the shipped 4 bands and 1 node; FR-019 processor-cap tests are vacuous
findings.problem: FR-BAND-001 / Appendix A say 1-8 bands and FR-MORPH-001 says 'Default: 2 nodes'. The code ships kMaxBands=4 (band_state.h:61) and kDefaultActiveNodes=1, a deliberate change (CHANGELOG.md:86), yet comments still say 'Current band count (1-8)' (processor.h:150) and '(1-8)' (crossover_network.h:110). FR-019's dynamic-threshold constants kMaxWeightThreshold/kWeightThresholdIncrement/kMaxGlobalProcessors are defined but no code uses them. The FR-019 tests (unit/morph_processor_cap_test.cpp:122-145) only assert activeCount <= 16 for one engine (at most 4), so they cannot fail.
findings.why_wrong: The spec, the comments and the tests should describe the shipped limits. A test named for a requirement should exercise that requirement.
findings.consequence: This is a maintenance trap: readers and future agents size buffers or tests for 8 bands, and the FR-019 'cap' looks tested but is enforced nowhere (it holds only because 4 bands x 4 nodes = 16).
findings.suggested_fix: Update specs-overview FR-BAND-001/Appendix A to 1-4 bands and FR-MORPH-001 to a default of 1 node, and fix the '(1-8)' comments. Either delete the unused FR-019 constants and tests or implement the cap with a test that would fail without it.
findings.evidence: morph_node.h:135 `kDefaultActiveNodes = 1;` :141-148 FR-019 constants; band_state.h:61 `kMaxBands = 4`; processor.h:150 `/// @brief Current band count (1-8)`; crossover_network.h:110 `@param numBands New number of bands (1-8)`; morph_processor_cap_test.cpp:144 `REQUIRE(activeCount <= Disrumpo::kMaxGlobalProcessors);` for one 4-node engine; specs-overview.md FR-BAND-001 'Range: 1 to 8 bands', FR-MORPH-001 'Default: 2 nodes (A and B)'.
verifier_notes:
I checked each claim against the source and could not refute any of them.

- **Node defaults:** morph_node.h:135 has `kDefaultActiveNodes = 1`. The FR-019 constants are at :142 (`kMaxWeightThreshold = 0.25f`), :145 (`kWeightThresholdIncrement = 0.005f`) and :148 (`kMaxGlobalProcessors = 16`).
- **FR-019 constants are unused in src:** grepping all of plugins/disrumpo/src and tests for the three names finds no use in src. They appear only in morph_node.h and in tests/unit/morph_processor_cap_test.cpp:144 and :164-166.
- **Band limit:** band_state.h:61 has `kMaxBands = 4`.
- **Stale comments:** they say "(1-8)" at processor.h:152 (the finding said 150), crossover_network.h:78 and crossover_network.h:110.
- **Spec text:** specs/Disrumpo/specs-overview.md says "(1-8)" at :145, "Range: 1 to 8 bands" at :158, and "Default: 2 nodes (A and B)" at :228.
- **Deliberate change:** CHANGELOG.md:86 (0.9.4) records that the default is now 1 node per band.
- **Vacuous test:** in morph_processor_cap_test.cpp:122-145, the "dynamic threshold raises" case builds one MorphEngine with 4 nodes. It counts active processors over a 4-entry weight array, so the count is at most 4. It then asserts `activeCount <= kMaxGlobalProcessors` (16), which cannot fail. The comment at :129 ("For now, test the single-engine threshold behavior") admits the cross-band cap is not exercised. No code raises the threshold.

The defect is real but only affects documentation and test quality; it changes no runtime behaviour. Low severity is right.

I checked every part of the claim against source and found nothing that answers it.
- morph_node.h:135 has `kDefaultActiveNodes = 1`.
- morph_node.h:142/145/148 define kMaxWeightThreshold, kWeightThresholdIncrement and kMaxGlobalProcessors. A grep over plugins/disrumpo finds them used only in tests/unit/morph_processor_cap_test.cpp:144 and :164-166, never in src. So no code enforces the FR-019 dynamic-threshold cap.
- band_state.h:61 has `kMaxBands = 4`.
- The stale "(1-8)" comments are at processor.h:152 (the finding said 150), crossover_network.h:78 and :110, plugin_ids.h:383 and spectrum_display.h:61.
- specs/Disrumpo/specs-overview.md:145 and :158 say 1-8 bands. Line 228 says "Default: 2 nodes (A and B)". dsp-details.md:177 still shows `kMaxBands = 8`.
- CHANGELOG.md 0.9.4 records the move to a 1-node default as a deliberate change, but nobody updated the spec. That makes the drift a documented design change with stale docs, not a guarded case that refutes the finding.
- The test at morph_processor_cap_test.cpp:122-145 says "For now, test the single-engine threshold behavior". It asserts `activeCount <= kMaxGlobalProcessors` (16) for one engine with 4 nodes, so it cannot fail. That matches the "vacuous" claim.
- The cap holds only because 4 bands x 4 nodes = 16. Nothing breaks at runtime, so the finding stays a doc and test maintenance issue at its stated low severity.

Every cited fact checks out in source, apart from one line-number drift. morph_node.h:135 has `kDefaultActiveNodes = 1`. morph_node.h:141-148 defines kMaxWeightThreshold=0.25f, kWeightThresholdIncrement=0.005f and kMaxGlobalProcessors=16. band_state.h:61 has `kMaxBands = 4`. The stale '(1-8)' comments are at processor.h:152 (the finding says 150), crossover_network.h:78 and crossover_network.h:110. specs/Disrumpo/specs-overview.md:158 says 'Range: 1 to 8 bands' and :228 says 'Default: 2 nodes (A and B)'. A grep across plugins/disrumpo shows the three FR-019 constants are used only in tests (morph_processor_cap_test.cpp:144,164,166), never in src/, so no code applies a dynamic threshold. The test 'dynamic threshold raises when exceeding limit' (morph_processor_cap_test.cpp:122-145) admits in its own comment 'For now, test the single-engine threshold behavior'. It sets up one 4-node engine and asserts activeCount <= 16, which cannot fail. Impact: the shipped limits (4 bands x at most 4 active nodes per band = 16) meet the FR-019 cap by construction, so nothing is audible and nothing is at runtime risk. The real cost is maintenance: comments and spec that mislead, and a test that cannot fail. That matches the claimed 'low' severity, so it stays unchanged.

findings.title: Same-family morph through a Spectral node re-prepares the STFT (heap allocations + state wipe) every sample
findings.problem: MorphEngine::processSameFamily calls blendedAdapter_.setParams(interpolateParams()) on every sample (morph_engine.cpp:706-710). interpolateParams() builds fftSize by summing truncated integer terms: result.fftSize starts at 0 (morph_engine.cpp:497) and adds static_cast<int>(w * p.fftSize) per node (:606). For two Spectral nodes at 2048 with weights 0.3/0.7 that gives 614 + 1433 = 2047. routeParamsToProcessor then compares p.fftSize (2047) with spectral_.getFftSize(), which is always a power of two because SpectralDistortion::prepare rounds up (spectral_distortion.h:150-154). The values never match, so spectral_.prepare() runs on every sample.
findings.why_wrong: SpectralDistortion::prepare is not real-time safe. It calls stft_.prepare and overlapAdd_.prepare, which run fft_.prepare: pffft_new_setup plus three makeAlignedBuffer allocations (fft.h:157-166). It also assigns Window::generate(), which returns a new std::vector (stft.h:72, :244), and it resets all STFT state. The comment 'allocates, but only on user param change' is false, because this runs from the per-sample morph path. CLAUDE.md forbids allocation on the audio thread. An STFT that is reset every sample never completes a frame.
findings.consequence: Two or more Experimental-family nodes (for example Spectral+Spectral, or Spectral dominant over Chaos/Granular) with the cursor off a node cause roughly 10 heap allocations per sample per channel. The same engine is called for L and R. Expect CPU overload and dropouts. The Spectral wet path stays silent or garbage because the STFT is wiped before it fills a frame. Clean only when the cursor sits exactly on a node (weights one-hot).
findings.suggested_fix: Do not interpolate fftSize. Take discrete/structural fields such as fftSize, magnitudeBits and stages from the dominant node, the same way the other discrete fields are handled. Then move the FFT-size change out of setParams: pre-prepare at kMaxFFTSize in prepare() and switch the active size without allocating, or defer the change to a non-audio thread. Test: a hidden [.]-tagged probe builds MorphEngine with two Spectral nodes (fftSize 2048), cursor X=0.3, runs 8192 samples under the allocation-counting operator new hook (tools/lint-allocation-operator-overrides pattern), and asserts zero allocations and non-silent output after 2*fftSize samples.
findings.evidence: morph_engine.cpp:497 `result.fftSize = 0;` :606 `result.fftSize += static_cast<int>(w * static_cast<float>(p.fftSize));` :706-710 `blendedAdapter_.setType(...); auto bp = interpolateParams(); ... blendedAdapter_.setParams(bp);` (in process(), per sample). distortion_adapter.cpp:893-896 `// Slot 1: FFT size — re-prepare if changed (allocates, but only on user param change) if (static_cast<std::size_t>(p.fftSize) != spectral_.getFftSize()) { spectral_.prepare(sampleRate_, ...p.fftSize); }`. spectral_distortion.h:150-154 rounds to pow2; fft.h:157 `setup_.reset(pffft_new_setup(...))`; stft.h:72 `window_ = Window::generate(...)`.
verifier_notes:
I could not refute this. Every step of the claimed path checks out in source.

1. Per-sample call. BandProcessor sends every sample through `morphEngine_` when `morphEnabled_` is set (band_processor.h:485, :752). `setMorphNodes` sets that flag (:250). `MorphEngine::process` (morph_engine.cpp:662-683) runs per sample through processBlock (:685-689). When `isSameFamily()` is true it calls `processSameFamily`. `isSameFamily()` (:385-397) only compares `getFamily()` results, and distortion_types.h:337-344 puts Chaos, Formant, Granular, Spectral, Fractal and Stochastic all in Experimental. So Spectral+Spectral, or Spectral with any other Experimental node, takes the same-family path. Nothing excludes that family, despite the "Parallel blend" comment.

2. Truncated sum. `processSameFamily` calls `setType` on the dominant node's type, then `setParams(interpolateParams())` on every sample (:706-710). `interpolateParams` sets `result.fftSize = 0` (:497). It then adds `static_cast<int>(w * p.fftSize)` for each node with w >= kWeightThreshold (:527-529, :606). With 2048 at weights 0.3/0.7 that is 614 + 1433 = 2047. For general float weights the truncated terms sum to less than 2048 unless every product happens to be an integer. Nodes skipped by the threshold lower the sum further.

3. Mismatch every sample. `DistortionAdapter::setParams` calls `routeParamsToProcessor` (distortion_adapter.cpp:173-175). In the Spectral case (:888-896) the comparison `p.fftSize != spectral_.getFftSize()` is true. `SpectralDistortion::prepare` (spectral_distortion.h:145-157) rounds 2047 up to 2048 and stores that in `fftSize_`. The next sample computes 2047 again, so the mismatch repeats and `prepare` runs again, on every sample.

4. Allocation and state wipe. `prepare` calls `stft_.prepare` and `overlapAdd_.prepare`. In stft.h, line 72 assigns `Window::generate`, :78/:81 resize the buffers, :244 assigns `Window::generate`, and :266/:269 resize again. `inputSpectrum_` and `outputSpectrum_` go through `SpectralBuffer::prepare` (spectral_buffer.h:63-65 resize). fft.h:157 calls `pffft_new_setup` and :164-166 call `makeAlignedBuffer`. That is heap allocation on the audio thread, and the STFT state is reset every sample. The comment at :893 ("only on user param change") is wrong for the morph path.

5. Precondition. The Spectral case only runs when the dominant node is Spectral (setType :706, switch on `currentType_`). `fftSize` comes from 512 * 2^k (processor_params.cpp:244), and the struct default is 2048 (distortion_adapter.h:179). So any off-node cursor position with two or more Experimental nodes and a Spectral dominant triggers the per-sample re-prepare. When the cursor sits exactly on a node the weights are one-hot and the sum is exact, so that case is clean.

Severity: critical stands. This is a hard real-time violation (allocations per sample per channel), and the Spectral wet path is broken whenever two or more Experimental nodes are off-node with Spectral dominant.

I could not refute this. Nothing upstream guards the path and the code is reachable in normal use.

1. Per-sample call chain. band_processor.h:752-754 calls morphEngine_->process() once per sample for L and once for R, inside processOversampledBlock. morph_engine.cpp:662-683 then routes to processSameFamily whenever isSameFamily() is true. isSameFamily (morph_engine.cpp:385-397) only compares families. The comment at distortion_types.h:337 says "Experimental - Parallel blend with output crossfade", but no code acts on it. Spectral is Experimental (distortion_types.h:341), so Spectral+Spectral or Spectral+Chaos/Granular/etc. takes the same-family path. processSameFamily calls blendedAdapter_.setParams(interpolateParams()) on every sample (morph_engine.cpp:706-710).

2. Truncated fftSize. interpolateParams zeroes result.fftSize (morph_engine.cpp:497). It then adds static_cast<int>(w * fftSize) for each node at or above kWeightThreshold (:606). Weights below the threshold are skipped, and each term truncates toward zero. So the sum lands below the power-of-two node value except at exact splits (one-hot, 0.5/0.5).

3. Mismatch on every call. DistortionAdapter::setParams always calls routeParamsToProcessor (distortion_adapter.cpp:173-175). The Spectral case compares p.fftSize with spectral_.getFftSize() (:894). getFftSize always returns a power of two because SpectralDistortion::prepare clamps and rounds up (spectral_distortion.h:145-157). A value like 2047 never equals 2048, so prepare() runs again on every sample.

4. Allocation and state wipe. prepare reassigns windows from Window::generate (stft.h:72, :244) and resizes buffers (stft.h:78/81/266/269, spectral_distortion.h:185). It re-prepares stft_, overlapAdd_ and the spectra (spectral_distortion.h:162-169), which also resets their STFT state. The code comment "allocates, but only on user param change" is wrong for this caller.

5. No test pins it. I found no test of a Spectral node under morph: the only fftSize hits in plugins/disrumpo/tests are a getter/setter check (distortion_adapter_test.cpp:2069-2074) and analyzer configs.

The same truncated-int pattern also hits stages, magnitudeBits and iterations (:576, :607, :614). Real-time allocation on every sample, plus a wet path that never fills a frame, justifies critical.

I traced the whole path in source and the defect is real at the claimed severity.

1. Per-sample call. BandProcessor calls morphEngine_->process(left) and process(right) for every sample, also inside the oversampled loop (band_processor.h:487-488, :752-754). MorphEngine::process (morph_engine.cpp:662-683) takes processSameFamily when every node is in one family. Chaos, Formant, Granular, Spectral, Fractal and Stochastic are all in the Experimental family (distortion_types.h:338-344), so any all-Experimental node set takes this path. processSameFamily runs blendedAdapter_.setType(dominant) and then blendedAdapter_.setParams(interpolateParams()) on every call (morph_engine.cpp:706-710).

2. fftSize stops being a power of two. interpolateParams sets result.fftSize = 0 (:497) and adds static_cast<int>(w * p.fftSize) for each node above the weight threshold (:606). Every term is truncated, so any weights that are not one-hot and not exact binary fractions give a value below the power of two. Example: 0.3/0.7 over 2048 gives 614 + 1433 = 2047. Skipping nodes under kWeightThreshold (:529) can only make the sum smaller.

3. Re-prepare on every call. DistortionAdapter::setParams always calls routeParamsToProcessor (distortion_adapter.cpp:173-175). With a Spectral dominant node it compares p.fftSize against spectral_.getFftSize() (:894). SpectralDistortion::prepare clamps and rounds up to a power of two before storing fftSize_ (spectral_distortion.h:147-157). The stored size is therefore never 2047, the comparison never matches, and prepare runs on every call, even after the cursor smoother settles.

4. The work done there allocates and is not real-time safe. SpectralDistortion::prepare is marked 'NOT real-time safe (allocates memory)' (spectral_distortion.h:144). It calls stft_.prepare and overlapAdd_.prepare. Each runs fft_.prepare, which allocates a new pffft setup (pffft_new_setup) and three aligned buffers (fft.h:157-166), and each assigns a new window vector from Window::generate (stft.h:72, :244). Counting the two FFTs and two windows, that is at least 10 heap allocations and 10 frees per call. pffft_new_setup also recomputes its twiddle tables, O(N) work, on every call. The vector resizes do not reallocate because the size stays the same.

5. The STFT is wiped every call. stft_.prepare sets writeIndex_ = 0 and samplesAvailable_ = 0 (stft.h:84-85). No analysis frame ever fills, so the Spectral wet signal stays at zero or garbage.

Impact: the call happens twice per sample (L and R share one engine), and more often inside an oversampled band. At 48 kHz that is about 2 million or more heap operations per second, plus repeated twiddle computation, on the audio thread. That is a hard real-time violation that will very likely overload the CPU and cause dropouts in any host. On top of that the Spectral type is silent in this morph state. The trigger is a user-reachable state: two or more Experimental-family nodes, a Spectral node dominant, and the cursor anywhere except exactly on a node. Cross-family morphing passes each node's own power-of-two fftSize (morph_engine.cpp:734-736) and does not trigger it. I found nothing that guards or mitigates this, so critical stands.

findings.title: Two contradictory implementations of the MorphLinkMode curves (controller vs DSP)
findings.problem: The same enum MorphLinkMode (plugin_ids.h:640-650) is evaluated by two functions with different math. The live one is controller/morph_link.cpp applyMorphLinkMode, called by MorphSweepLinkController (visibility_controllers.cpp:194-195). The DSP one is sweep_morph_link.h applyMorphLinkCurve, reached only via SweepProcessor::getMorphPosition (sweep_processor.h:308), which nothing calls. They differ as follows. EaseIn: sqrt(x) in the controller vs x^2 in the DSP (opposite curvature). EaseOut: x^2 vs 1-(1-x)^2. HoldRise: threshold 0.5 vs 0.6. Stepped: 5 levels (0,.25,.5,.75,1) vs 4 levels (0,.333,.667,1). None: manual position vs 0.5. The DSP version and its tests (dsp/sweep_morph_link_tests.cpp) pin behaviour that does not ship. plugin_ids.h:647 documents the controller's 5-step version.
findings.why_wrong: One enum should have one transfer function. The DSP copy is dead but tested, so it reads as authoritative. Anyone who wires sweep->morph linking into the processor (the intended FR) will silently invert EaseIn/EaseOut relative to what users hear today.
findings.consequence: Maintenance trap. The spec, docs and tests disagree about the curve shapes. A future processor-side link changes the sound of every preset that uses EaseIn, EaseOut, HoldRise or Stepped.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep one implementation in a shared header that both controller and DSP include (both are plugin-local and not processor/controller headers), and delete the other. Add a test that asserts the shared function's values at x = 0.25/0.55/0.75 for each mode.
findings.evidence: controller/morph_link.cpp:44-47 `case MorphLinkMode::EaseIn: return std::sqrt(sweepNorm);` :49-52 EaseOut `return sweepNorm * sweepNorm;` :54-59 HoldRise `if (sweepNorm < 0.5f) return 0.0f;` :61-65 Stepped `std::min(std::floor(sweepNorm * 5.0f) / 4.0f, 1.0f)`. dsp/sweep_morph_link.h:98-100 EaseIn `return x * x;` :102-104 EaseOut `1.0f - (1.0f - x) * (1.0f - x)` :106-112 HoldRise `if (x < 0.6f)` :114-118 Stepped `std::min(std::floor(x * 4.0f), 3.0f) / 3.0f`; :86-88 None `return 0.5f;`.
verifier_notes:
I traced the call paths and the finding holds. sweep_morph_link.h:81-126 `applyMorphLinkCurve` gives None→0.5 (:86-88), EaseIn→x*x (:98-100), EaseOut→1-(1-x)^2 (:102-104), HoldRise with a 0.6 threshold (:109-112) and Stepped as min(floor(4x),3)/3, 4 levels (:118). controller/morph_link.cpp:27-70 `applyMorphLinkMode` gives None→manualPosition (:34), EaseIn→sqrt (:47), EaseOut→x^2 (:52), HoldRise with a 0.5 threshold (:56-59) and Stepped as min(floor(5x)/4,1), 5 levels (:65). findings.title: Processor reports kNoTail although several types ring after input stops
findings.problem: Processor does not override getTailSamples, so it inherits AudioEffect's `return kNoTail;` (vstaudioeffect.h:84). Several shipped types sustain output after the input goes silent: FeedbackDistortion (delay line with feedback up to 1.5), AllpassSaturator KarplusStrong/feedback topologies (feedback up to 0.999), the Granular circular buffer, Spectral overlap-add, and the Stochastic/Chaos shapers.
findings.why_wrong: IAudioProcessor::getTailSamples tells the host how long output continues after silent input. Hosts use it to stop calling process() on silent tracks (silence suspend/auto-bypass) and to size offline render tails.
findings.consequence: Feedback/allpass/granular tails are truncated in exports and when the host suspends silent tracks. When processing resumes, stale buffer contents (granular grains, feedback delay, spectral OLA) play back as a burst. Behaviour depends on the host and its suspend settings.
findings.suggested_fix: Override getTailSamples to return a bound derived from the active types: the maximum feedback decay plus the delay, the granular buffer length and the FFT size, or kInfiniteTail while any feedback-capable node is active. Test: a processor-level case that calls getTailSamples() after loading a FeedbackDist preset and asserts a value > 0.
findings.evidence: grep for getTailSamples / canProcessSampleSize in plugins/disrumpo/src: no hits. extern/vst3sdk/public.sdk/source/vst/vstaudioeffect.h:84 `uint32 PLUGIN_API getTailSamples () SMTG_OVERRIDE { return kNoTail; }`.
verifier_notes:
I could not refute this. A grep for getTailSamples, kNoTail and kInfiniteTail under plugins/disrumpo finds nothing. Processor derives directly from Steinberg::Vst::AudioEffect (plugins/disrumpo/src/processor/processor.h:43), so it inherits `getTailSamples() { return kNoTail; }` (extern/vst3sdk/public.sdk/source/vst/vstaudioeffect.h:84).

The tail the finding describes really exists. The adapter holds Krate::DSP::FeedbackDistortion feedbackDist_ (distortion_adapter.h:378), GranularDistortion granular_ (:383) and AllpassSaturator allpassSaturator_ (:387). Their feedback is set from the band parameters (distortion_adapter.cpp:813 setFeedback(p.feedback), :826 allpassSaturator_.setFeedback). FeedbackDistortion's own doc gives its path as Input -> [+] -> DelayLine -> Waveshaper -> Biquad -> DCBlocker -> SoftLimiter (feedback_distortion.h:60), with kMaxFeedback = 1.5f (:98). The comment at :40 says the soft limiter turns runaway into "indefinite" sustain, so this type can go on producing output after the input stops. distortion_adapter.h:243 also says Spectral and Granular run on internal ring buffers.

The processor never checks input silence flags (processor.cpp:196 only has the numSamples == 0 early-out), and nothing tells the host that output continues. Other plugins in the repo do override this: Iterum returns kInfiniteTail (iterum processor.h:90), and Vorago (processor.cpp:700) and Profundum (processor.cpp:574) compute an estimate. That shows the omission in Disrumpo is a gap, not a design choice.

How bad the result is depends on the host (silence suspend, offline render tail), so medium severity is appropriate.

I could not refute this one. The claim holds up against the source:
(1) No Disrumpo source or test file mentions getTailSamples, kNoTail or kInfiniteTail. A grep over plugins/disrumpo returned nothing, so the Processor inherits extern/vst3sdk/public.sdk/source/vst/vstaudioeffect.h:84 `return kNoTail;`.
(2) Disrumpo does ship a type that rings after the input stops. processor_params.cpp:177-180 maps FeedbackDist feedback to slots[0]*1.5 (range 0 to 1.5). distortion_adapter.cpp:812-819 passes that value to Krate::DSP::FeedbackDistortion, a feedback comb with a delay of up to 100 ms (feedback_distortion.h:91, 254). processor_params.cpp:284 maps allpassFeedback up to 0.99, and distortion_adapter.cpp:826 passes it to the AllpassSaturator. Both are recirculating structures whose output continues after the input goes silent.
(3) Nothing guards this elsewhere. processor.cpp has no silenceFlags handling; its only early exit is `data.numSamples == 0` at line 196. There is no design-decision note in specs/Disrumpo: the only grep hits for "tail" are "detail" and "dsp-details". There is no code comment like the one Seraphis has (seraphis processor.cpp:1776-1781), where the SDK default is kept on purpose.
(4) Sibling plugins with tails override the method: Iterum processor.h:90 returns kInfiniteTail, and Vorago and Profundum compute a value and have tests for it. That shows the project treats tail reporting as required behaviour, not an oversight it accepts.
The impact depends on the host (whether it suspends silent tracks, and how it renders offline tails), so medium severity is appropriate.

The defect is real. Grep for getTailSamples/kInfiniteTail/kNoTail across plugins/ finds overrides in Iterum (processor.h:90), Vorago (processor.h:91, processor.cpp:700) and Profundum (processor.h:95, processor.cpp:574). Disrumpo has none, so it inherits `return kNoTail;` from extern/vst3sdk/public.sdk/source/vst/vstaudioeffect.h:84.

The tails exist and are long:
- processor_params.cpp:180-181 maps FeedbackDist to `p.feedback = slots[0] * 1.5f` and `p.delayMs = 1 + slots[1]*99`. feedback_distortion.h:98 sets kMaxFeedback = 1.5, and its own doc at :77 says `setFeedback(1.2f); // Self-sustaining`. That tail is infinite while the limiter holds the loop.
- processor_params.cpp:284-285 sets allpassFeedback up to 0.99 and decayTimeS from 0.01 to 10 s. distortion_adapter.cpp:826-827 routes these to allpassSaturator_, which gives tails of up to about 10 s.
- distortion_adapter.cpp:148-156 treats Spectral (fftSize) and Granular (grain size) as block-based with buffered history.

processor.cpp:196 only special-cases numSamples == 0. Nothing tells the host there is a tail. Hosts that act on kNoTail cut these tails. Cubase and Nuendo do this through 'suspend VST3 processing when no audio signal is received'. Hosts that size the offline-render tail from getTailSamples do it too.

Impact: only presets or nodes that use FeedbackDist, AllpassSaturator, Granular or Spectral are affected. Most of the 26 types are memoryless shapers with no tail. The 'burst on resume' claim is weaker than stated. A suspended host just stops calling process(), so on resume the leftover delay/OLA content plays out as the rest of the cut tail, not a new transient. That point is plausible but overstated.

Truncated multi-second feedback and allpass tails in a common host feature fit medium severity. The severity stays where it is.

findings.title: Crossover divider drag calls std::clamp with lo > hi when neighbouring crossovers are under one octave apart
findings.problem: leftBound is the left neighbour times 2^0.5 and rightBound is the right neighbour times 2^-0.5. When the two neighbours of the dragged divider are less than one octave apart, or a right neighbour is below 28 Hz for divider 0, leftBound > rightBound and std::clamp(newFreq, leftBound, rightBound) is called with inverted bounds. The view's crossover values are seeded from the controller parameters (controller.cpp:946-951, via linear toPlain). Those values can be arbitrary from automation or a preset, because neither the processor nor the parameters enforce ordering or spacing.
findings.why_wrong: std::clamp has the precondition !(hi < lo). Violating it is undefined behaviour. MSVC debug STL and libstdc++ with _GLIBCXX_ASSERTIONS / libc++ hardened modes assert on it. In release builds every implementation returns lo when v < lo, so the divider jumps past its right neighbour.
findings.consequence: Debug builds assert during a mouse drag. In release, dragging produces crossover frequencies out of order (crossover[i] > crossover[i+1]). These are sent to the processor through CrossoverDragBridge, and the cascaded LR4 network then no longer reconstructs flat (SC-001).
findings.suggested_fix: If leftBound > rightBound, either reject the move or collapse both bounds to the midpoint, then clamp. Also observe the crossover parameters so the view never starts from an unordered state. Test: SpectrumDisplay unit test with setCrossoverFrequency(0,500), (1,600), (2,700); drag divider 1; assert the result is ordered and no std::clamp precondition is violated.
findings.evidence: spectrum_display.cpp:382-386 `leftBound = crossoverFreqs_[draggingDivider_ - 1] * std::pow(2.0f, kMinOctaveSpacing);` :388-392 `rightBound = crossoverFreqs_[draggingDivider_ + 1] * std::pow(2.0f, -kMinOctaveSpacing);` :395 `newFreq = std::clamp(newFreq, leftBound, rightBound);`. spectrum_display.h:195 `kMinOctaveSpacing = 0.5f`. controller.cpp:946-951 seeds crossoverFreqs_ from params.
verifier_notes:
I traced the code and the defect is real. It is reachable in normal use, not only from hostile automation.

What the drag code does:
- spectrum_display.cpp:383-393 builds leftBound as crossoverFreqs_[i-1]*2^0.5 and rightBound as crossoverFreqs_[i+1]*2^-0.5 (kMinOctaveSpacing = 0.5f, spectrum_display.h:195).
- :396 then calls std::clamp(newFreq, leftBound, rightBound) without checking that leftBound <= rightBound.

Nothing upstream keeps the view's values ordered:
- SpectrumDisplay::setCrossoverFrequency (:69-74) only clamps each value to [20, 20000].
- controller.cpp:947-952 seeds the view once, when the view is created. It is the only caller of setCrossoverFrequency in the controller (grep), so the view never watches the parameters.
- The processor does not enforce order either. processor_params.cpp:984-994 maps each value from normalized to Hz on a log scale on its own. crossover_network.h:127-134 only clamps each value to its range.

A worse seeding problem makes this happen without any automation:
- parameter_registration.cpp:151-160 registers each crossover as a plain Steinberg RangeParameter, so toPlain is linear: 20 + n*19980.
- CrossoverDragBridge::onCrossoverChanged (visibility_controllers.cpp:643-652) writes the value on a log scale: n = log10(f/20)/3.
- controller.cpp:950 reads it back with the linear toPlain. So every value that was dragged comes back distorted on the next editor open.

Concrete sequence:
1. 4 bands, default state. The view is seeded at about 112, 632 and 3557 Hz (the linear round trip of each RangeParameter default).
2. Drag divider 0 to 100 Hz. The bridge stores n = log10(5)/3 = 0.233.
3. Close and reopen the editor. Divider 0 is now seeded at 20 + 0.233*19980 = about 4675 Hz, and divider 2 stays at 3557 Hz.
4. Drag divider 1. leftBound = 4675*1.414 = about 6611 and rightBound = 3557/1.414 = about 2515, so std::clamp is called with lo > hi. That is undefined behaviour by the standard's precondition, and the MSVC debug STL asserts "invalid bounds arguments passed to std::clamp".

In release builds the result is some value outside [left neighbour, right neighbour]. It is written to crossoverFreqs_ (:399) and pushed through the bridge with performEdit (visibility_controllers.cpp:650-653), so the processor gets crossovers out of order.

One detail in the finding is wrong: MSVC's release clamp tests hi < v first, so it does not always return lo. That does not change the defect.

Severity stays medium. This is UI-thread UB that produces crossover settings out of order, not a crash or a fault on the audio thread. The linear-vs-log seeding mismatch is the larger underlying bug and likely deserves its own finding.

I found no guard, clamp, design note or test that makes this unreachable.

1. spectrum_display.cpp:380-396 computes leftBound = crossoverFreqs_[d-1]*2^0.5 and rightBound = crossoverFreqs_[d+1]*2^-0.5. It then calls std::clamp(newFreq, leftBound, rightBound) without checking that leftBound <= rightBound.

2. Nothing keeps the view's crossoverFreqs_ ordered or half an octave apart.
   - setCrossoverFrequency (spectrum_display.cpp:69-74) only clamps each value to [20, 20000].
   - setNumBands (:51-67) writes ordered log-spaced defaults, but controller.cpp:947-952 overwrites them right after with values from the parameters.
   - Those parameter values are not ordered either. The processor (processor_params.cpp:984-994) and CrossoverNetwork::setCrossoverFrequency (crossover_network.h:127-134) only clamp the range.

3. The seed makes the inverted case easy to hit. The crossover parameters are linear Steinberg RangeParameters over [20, 20000] (parameter_registration.cpp:151-160). The processor (processor_params.cpp:987-991) and CrossoverDragBridge (visibility_controllers.cpp:643-648) treat the normalized value as log-scaled. The view, however, is seeded through the linear toPlain (controller.cpp:950). Every normalized value of 0.5 or above, which is any crossover at or above about 632 Hz, therefore lands in 10010-20000 Hz in the view, a span under one octave.
   - Example: a 4-band preset with crossovers at 700 Hz, 2 kHz and 6 kHz has normalized values 0.515, 0.667 and 0.826.
   - The view sees about 10310, 13340 and 16520 Hz.
   - Dragging divider 1 gives leftBound about 14580 and rightBound about 11680, so lo > hi. This violates the std::clamp precondition, which is undefined behaviour.

4. Nothing else catches it.
   - The only setter call on the view is controller.cpp:951, at creation. Nothing re-syncs the view later.
   - crossover_interaction_test.cpp:70-86 re-implements the bound logic in an anonymous namespace. It never drives SpectrumDisplay::onMouseMoved and never tests inverted bounds.

5. The consequence is real.
   - The MSVC debug STL asserts on inverted bounds.
   - In release, MSVC checks hi first and libstdc++/libc++ check lo first. Either way the result falls on the wrong side of one neighbour.
   - CrossoverDragBridge then sends that value to the processor, so the crossovers end up out of order.

One detail in the finding is wrong: it says "every implementation returns lo", but MSVC returns hi when v > hi. This does not change the verdict. Severity stays medium: the assert only fires in debug builds, and the release result is a mis-ordered crossover rather than a crash.

The inverted clamp is real and easy to reach, but the most serious consequence the finding claims (SC-001 reconstruction breaks) cannot happen.

Code path. spectrum_display.cpp:383-396 sets leftBound = crossover[i-1]*2^0.5 and rightBound = crossover[i+1]*2^-0.5, then calls std::clamp(newFreq, leftBound, rightBound). Nothing checks that leftBound <= rightBound. In-session drags keep 0.5-octave spacing, and setNumBands (lines 55-63) resets to a log spread. The view is seeded only once, at controller.cpp:947-951, and that seed is wrong:
- The parameters are linear RangeParameters (parameter_registration.cpp:151-160).
- The processor reads the normalized value as LOG (processor_params.cpp:988-991).
- CrossoverDragBridge writes LOG-normalized values (visibility_controllers.cpp:643-652).

So after a reopen the view gets linear toPlain() of log values. That squeezes the upper crossovers together. Example: processor crossovers 1262/2518/5024 Hz (log-norm 0.6/0.7/0.8, one octave apart) seed the view as 12008/14006/16004 Hz. Dragging divider 1 then gives leftBound 16982 > rightBound 11317. So inverted bounds come from ordinary settings after an editor reopen, not only from odd automation.

Impact.
- Debug builds: MSVC _STL_ASSERT and libstdc++ _GLIBCXX_ASSERTIONS do fire. Only developers see this; shipped Release builds do not.
- Release builds: both the MSVC and libstdc++ implementations reduce to `v<lo ? lo : (hi<v ? hi : v)`. With lo > hi the divider snaps either to leftBound or to rightBound, and rightBound is below the left neighbour. So the divider jumps across a neighbour and the bridge sends an out-of-order crossover. That part of the claim is right.
- SC-001: the claim is wrong. crossover_network.h:209-227 is a cascade with D'Appolito allpasses. The bands sum to LP0·AP1·AP2 + HP0·LP1·AP2 + HP0·HP1·LP2 + HP0·HP1·HP2. Because LR4 LP+HP = AP at any frequency, this collapses to AP0·AP1·AP2 whatever the ordering, so the magnitude stays flat. The processor also accepts unordered crossovers from automation by design (setCrossoverFrequency only clamps the range, lines 127-134).

What the user actually gets: a UI divider that jumps past its neighbour and a nearly empty middle band. That is a UI/UX bug, not an audio-integrity or reconstruction bug. The bigger defect is the linear-vs-log seeding mismatch, which is a separate issue.

Verdict: the defect is real, but its claimed consequence is overstated, so severity goes down from medium to low.

findings.title: Dead members bloat every DistortionAdapter (24 per plugin instance) and get memset on every prepare/reset
findings.problem: saturation_ (SaturationProcessor) is prepared and reset but never processed. tubeShaper_ and tapeShaper_ are configured in prepare but never used in processRaw, even though the comment says 'These are used instead of the block-based processors'. inputRingBuffer_ and outputRingBuffer_ (2 x 4096 floats), ringWritePos_/ringReadPos_ and isBlockBased_ are written but never read. blockLatency_ is read only by getProcessingLatency(), which has no callers. Processor::crossoverFrequencies_ (processor.h:179) is likewise declared and never used.
findings.why_wrong: Comments claim behaviour that does not exist, and dead state costs memory and per-reset work. The project already hit stack-overflow problems with this object (stack_footprint_test.cpp, MorphEngine 936 KB).
findings.consequence: About 32 KB of dead ring buffer per adapter. With 6 adapters per band (1 legacy + 4 nodes + 1 blended) x 4 bands, that is about 768 KB per plugin instance, plus 32 KB of fill() per adapter on every prepare() and setActive reset. Readers are misled into thinking block-based latency handling exists.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete saturation_, tubeShaper_, tapeShaper_, the ring buffers and their positions, isBlockBased_, and Processor::crossoverFrequencies_. Either wire getProcessingLatency into latency reporting or remove it. stack_footprint_test then covers the size reduction.
findings.evidence: grep in plugins/disrumpo/src: saturation_ appears only at distortion_adapter.cpp:34 (prepare) and :106 (reset); tubeShaper_/tapeShaper_ only at :40-43; inputRingBuffer_/outputRingBuffer_ only at :89-92, :132-135 (fill/zero); isBlockBased_ written at :149,:153,:158 and never read; getProcessingLatency defined at :248 with no caller. processor.h:179 `std::array<std::atomic<float>, kMaxBands - 1> crossoverFrequencies_{};` has no use in processor/*.cpp.
verifier_notes:
I checked the claim against the source and it holds, apart from one small inaccuracy.

Grep over plugins/disrumpo/src:
- saturation_ (distortion_adapter.h:370) appears only at distortion_adapter.cpp:34 (prepare) and :106 (reset). Nothing processes it. The live paths use tube_ and tape_ instead: tube_.process at :315, tape_.process at :335.
- tubeShaper_ and tapeShaper_ (h:396, :399) are only touched at cpp:40-43, where setType and setDrive are called. They are never used for processing, so the header comment ("These are used instead of the block-based processors") is wrong.
- inputRingBuffer_ and outputRingBuffer_ are each std::array<float, 4096> (h:440-442), so 2 x 16 KB = 32 KB per adapter. They are only filled at cpp:89-90 and :132-133. ringWritePos_ and ringReadPos_ are only zeroed at :91-92 and :134-135.
- isBlockBased_ is written at cpp:149, :153 and :158 and never read.
- blockLatency_ is read only by getProcessingLatency() (cpp:248-249). That function has no production caller in processor/, band_processor.h or morph_engine.*. The one inaccuracy: tests/unit/distortion_adapter_test.cpp:133-149 does call it, so "no callers" should read "no production callers".
- Processor::crossoverFrequencies_ (processor.h:179) has no use in processor/. Every other crossoverFrequencies_ hit belongs to CrossoverNetwork's own separate member (crossover_network.h:428).

The memory arithmetic checks out:
- Each band has one DistortionAdapter distortion_ (band_processor.h:803).
- Each band's MorphEngine (heap-allocated via unique_ptr, band_processor.h:808) adds std::array<DistortionAdapter, kMaxMorphNodes> (morph_engine.h:242) plus blendedAdapter_ (:245).
- That is 6 adapters per band. With std::array<BandProcessor, kMaxBands=4> (processor.h:176), it makes 24 adapters per instance, or about 768 KB of dead ring buffer.

The defect is real: dead state, a misleading comment and wasted reset work. It has no audible or correctness effect, so low severity is right.

I grepped plugins/disrumpo/src and read the code. The dead state is real and nothing guards or justifies it.
- distortion_adapter.h:370 `saturation_` is used only at distortion_adapter.cpp:34 (prepare) and :106 (reset).
- distortion_adapter.h:396/399 `tubeShaper_` and `tapeShaper_` are used only at cpp:40-43, where setType/setDrive are called. They are never processed, even though the comment at h:391-393 says "These are used instead of the block-based processors".

Nothing in specs or code comments makes this intentional. The finding is a valid low-severity cleanup and dead-code issue.

The dead state is real. A grep over plugins/disrumpo shows: saturation_ (distortion_adapter.h:370) is touched only by prepare (distortion_adapter.cpp:34) and reset (:106). tubeShaper_ and tapeShaper_ (h:396, :399) are only configured at cpp:40-43, and the comment at h:392-393 says "used instead of the block-based processors", which is false. inputRingBuffer_ and outputRingBuffer_ (h:441-442, kMaxBlockBufferSize=4096 at h:440) are only filled at cpp:89-90 and :132-133. ringWritePos_ and ringReadPos_ are only zeroed. isBlockBased_ is written at cpp:149/153/158 and never read. blockLatency_ is read only by getProcessingLatency (cpp:248-249). That function has no production caller (no hits in processor/ or dsp/). Its only callers are tests (tests/unit/distortion_adapter_test.cpp:133-149), so "no callers" is slightly overstated. processor.h:179 crossoverFrequencies_ is never used in processor/*.cpp; the same-named hits in crossover_network.h:428 are a different member.

Checking the claimed consequence: each adapter holds 2 x 4096 x 4 B = 32 KB of ring buffers. Each band has 6 adapters: the legacy adapter (band_processor.h:803), plus a MorphEngine with 4 node adapters and 1 blended adapter (morph_engine.h:242, :245). There are 4 BandProcessors (processor.h:176, kMaxBands=4 at band_state.h:61). That gives 24 adapters and about 768 KB of dead memory per instance, which matches the claim.

The stack-overflow angle is weak. The Processor is heap-allocated by the factory and MorphEngine sits behind a unique_ptr (band_processor.h:807), so this memory is on the heap, not the stack. The fill() cost is about 768 KB of memset per prepare/setActive reset. setType and setParams (cpp:142-183) never call reset, so nothing runs per block on the audio thread. Nothing is audible and real-time safety is unaffected. The real costs are memory footprint and misleading comments and accessors, so low severity is correct.

findings.title: Unused <windows.h> include in the controller TU (Windows-only macro pollution)
findings.problem: controller.cpp includes <windows.h> under #ifdef _WIN32, but no Win32 API is used anywhere in plugins/disrumpo/src (grep for OutputDebugString/HWND/DWORD/WINAPI/GetModule finds nothing). It was added in commit 4bcd6e5f (Morph UI) and never removed.
findings.why_wrong: CLAUDE.md allows platform-specific code only for guarded debug logging or approved workarounds. windows.h brings in min/max, near/far, ERROR and other macros on one platform only, so the TU compiles differently on Windows than on macOS/Linux, and `std::max(0.0, std::min(1.0, value))` (:1869) works only because something else defines NOMINMAX.
findings.consequence: Windows-only compile hazard. A later change that adds an identifier colliding with a windows.h macro fails only on Windows, or worse, compiles to something different there.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the include block, rebuild on Windows, and check tools/check-portability.js stays clean.
findings.evidence: controller.cpp:57-59 `#ifdef _WIN32 #include <windows.h> #endif`; no Win32 symbols in plugins/disrumpo/src (grep OutputDebugString|GetTickCount|MessageBox|HWND|WINAPI|DWORD|GetModule: 0 hits); git log -S shows it was introduced in 4bcd6e5f.
verifier_notes: The include does exist (controller.cpp:58-60, not 57-59), and no Win32 API is called directly in controller.cpp. But the harm the finding describes does not follow from it. Line 36 of the same TU already includes "display/display_bridge_log.h", and plugins/shared/src/display/display_bridge_log.h:18-26 does `#ifdef _WIN32 / #define WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN / #define NOMINMAX / #include <windows.h>`. That header uses OutputDebugStringA (:38) as guarded debug logging, which CLAUDE.md explicitly allows. VSTGUI's vstguibase.h:74-79 also defines NOMINMAX and WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN on Windows. So by the time line 59 runs, windows.h has already been included with NOMINMAX set, and the second include does nothing because of its include guard. Deleting lines 58-60 leaves the TU's Windows macro set exactly as it is. The claimed "Windows-only macro pollution" and later collision risk come from the shared header and VSTGUI, not from this line. The suggested fix would change nothing. The std::max/std::min at :1869 is safe because NOMINMAX is reliably defined before windows.h is first included, so it does not "work by accident". What remains is a redundant include with no effect, which is a cleanup nit, not a portability defect.

findings.title: Comments that contradict the code at load-bearing spots
findings.problem: Several comments describe behaviour the code does not have. (a) BandProcessor::process is documented as 'Applies sweep, distortion/morph with oversampling', but it runs MorphEngine at the host rate with no oversampler (band_processor.h:473-512), and it is the only path Processor::process uses. (b) plugin_ids.h:156 says output params 'use standalone IDs outside the encoding scheme', but 0x0F80/0x0F81 fall inside the global 0x0Fxx range, where isGlobalParamId() returns true. (c) isNodeParamId's doc says 'band nibble = 0-7', but the code accepts 0-3 (plugin_ids.h:318 vs :334). (d) MorphEngine documents setMorphPosition/setMode/setNodes as 'Thread-safe parameter updates' (morph_engine.h:40); they are plain non-atomic member writes. (e) processor_params.cpp:456 says the note index is '[0,15]', but it uses kNoteValueCount-1 = 29. (f) controller.h:299 calls the duplicated SharedDisplay struct a 'Forward declaration'. It is a second definition with a layout identical to processor.h:268, punned through void* with no static_assert.
findings.why_wrong: These comments sit on the exact assumptions a fixer relies on (oversampling, thread safety, ID classification, bridge layout). Each one points a reader toward the wrong fix.
findings.consequence: Maintenance traps. For example, a developer trusting (d) could call setNodes from the UI thread. A change to one SharedDisplay struct without the other silently mis-reads FIFO pointers in the Tier-3 fallback.
findings.suggested_fix: Correct the comments. Move SharedDisplay into one neutral plugin-local header that both sides include, or at minimum add static_asserts on sizeof and offsetof in both TUs.
findings.evidence: band_processor.h:466 `/// Applies sweep, distortion/morph with oversampling.` vs :486-489 `left = morphEngine_->process(left); right = morphEngine_->process(right);`. plugin_ids.h:156 'Output parameters use standalone IDs outside the encoding scheme' vs :164 `kSweepModulatedFrequencyOutputId = 0x0F80` and :83-84 isGlobalParamId `(paramId & 0xFF00) == 0x0F00`. morph_engine.h:40 'setMorphPosition/setMode/setNodes: Thread-safe parameter updates' vs morph_engine.h:219-259 non-atomic members. processor_params.cpp:456-458. controller.h:299-304 '/// Forward declaration of processor's shared display struct' followed by a full struct definition.

I could not refute any of the six sub-claims. Each was checked against the source.

(a) band_processor.h:465-466 documents process() as "Applies sweep, distortion/morph with oversampling". The body at :473-512 calls morphEngine_->process(left/right) at :487-488, or distortion_.process at :493-494, with no oversampler. Processor::process calls only bandProcessors_[b].process(...) (processor.cpp:487 and :494). processBlock (band_processor.h:519) is not called from processor.cpp.

(b) plugin_ids.h:156 says output params use "standalone IDs outside the encoding scheme". But :164 sets kSweepModulatedFrequencyOutputId = 0x0F80 and :168 sets kSweepDetectedCCOutputId = 0x0F81, and isGlobalParamId at :83-84 ((id & 0xFF00) == 0x0F00) returns true for both.

(c) The isNodeParamId doc at plugin_ids.h:318 says "band nibble = 0-7", but the code at :334-335 accepts only bandNibble <= 3.

(d) morph_engine.h:40 calls setMorphPosition/setMode/setNodes "Thread-safe parameter updates". The state they write (morph_engine.h:219-249: mode_, targetX_/Y_, nodes_, activeNodeCount_, allSameFamily_) is plain non-atomic members.

(e) processor_params.cpp:456 comments the index range as "[0,15]", but :458 uses kNoteValueCount - 1, and plugin_ids.h:704 defines kNoteValueCount = 30, so the range is 0-29.

(f) controller.h:299 says "Forward declaration of processor's shared display struct". It is followed by a full second definition at :300-304, identical to processor.h:268-272. Neither header has a static_assert tying the two layouts together.

So every comment contradicts its code as the finding says. None of this changes runtime behaviour today, because the two SharedDisplay layouts currently match. That fits the claimed severity of low, so no adjustment.

(e) processor_params.cpp:456 says "[0,15]", but the code uses kNoteValueCount - 1, and kNoteValueCount = 30 (plugin_ids.h:704). (f) controller.h:298-303 labels a full struct definition a "Forward declaration". It duplicates processor.h:268-272 field for field, and grep found no static_assert in the processor or controller TUs. findings.title: std::isnan/std::isinf NaN guard in a fast-math test TU (folded away on macOS)
findings.problem: The cross-family BitwiseMangler test sanitises its output with `if (std::isnan(output[i]) || std::isinf(output[i])) { WARN(...); output[i] = 0.0f; }`. This TU is not in the -fno-fast-math list (tests/CMakeLists.txt:181-203), so on the macOS leg Apple clang folds the checks to false and the NaN diagnostic and sanitisation never run.
findings.why_wrong: CLAUDE.md requires finiteness checks to use Krate::DSP::detail::isFinite/isNaN in fast-math code, or the TU to be listed among the IEEE sets. The other morph tests that use std::isnan are in the IEEE list. This one was missed.
findings.consequence: On macOS a NaN regression in this path gives no 'NaN/Inf at sample' diagnostic and fails later on an unrelated-looking RMS assertion. It is a diagnostic gap, not a false green.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the check with Krate::DSP::detail::isNaN/isInf, or add the file to the IEEE set_source_files_properties block.
findings.evidence: multi_node_distortion_test.cpp:693 `if (std::isnan(output[i]) || std::isinf(output[i])) {`; tests/CMakeLists.txt:181-203 IEEE list does not contain integration/multi_node_distortion_test.cpp; tools/lint-nonfinite-symbols.js reports clean only because it guards src, not this test usage.
verifier_notes: I could not refute this. The source shows what the finding says. In plugins/disrumpo/tests/integration/multi_node_distortion_test.cpp at lines 693-696, the loop over engine->process() output runs `if (std::isnan(output[i]) || std::isinf(output[i])) { WARN("NaN/Inf at sample " << i); output[i] = 0.0f; }`. The file is compiled into disrumpo_tests (tests/CMakeLists.txt:129). The IEEE override block at tests/CMakeLists.txt:181-205 sets `-fno-fast-math -fno-finite-math-only -ffp-contract=off` on 21 TUs, and integration/multi_node_distortion_test.cpp is not one of them. The other morph tests (unit/morph_*.cpp, approval/morph_artifact_test.cpp) and integration/band_management_integration_test.cpp are in that list. The fast-math comes from extern/vst3sdk/cmake/modules/SMTG_PlatformToolset.cmake:42-46: under `if(XCODE)` it calls `add_compile_options(-ffast-math -ffp-contract=fast)` at directory scope, so every disrumpo_tests TU outside the list gets it on the macOS leg. -ffast-math implies -ffinite-math-only, and under that flag clang folds std::isnan and std::isinf to false. On macOS the check is therefore dead code: no "NaN/Inf at sample" warning is printed, and a NaN is not zeroed before calculateRMS. That makes the claim correct. The impact is also as the finding states: if a NaN appears, the test still fails (or behaves unpredictably) at the later RMS/autocorr REQUIRE lines (710-712), but without the per-sample diagnostic. It is a diagnostic gap in a test TU, not shipped code, so severity stays low. The fix is valid: either use Krate::DSP::detail::isNaN/isInf, or add the TU to the IEEE set_source_files_properties list.

Confirmed from source. plugins/disrumpo/tests/integration/multi_node_distortion_test.cpp:693 reads `if (std::isnan(output[i]) || std::isinf(output[i])) { WARN(...); output[i] = 0.0f; }`. That is the only finiteness check in the file. findings.title: Morph-mode / smoothing round-trip tests compare getState to getState, hiding that the processor saves literal 0 for both
findings.problem: writeNonDefaultV6Preset writes morphMode = b % 3 per band (line 226). The 'MorphMode values round-trip' section and 'v6 full parameter set' then do setState(input) -> getState(stream1) -> setState(stream1) -> getState(stream2) and compare only stream1 with stream2 (compareV6PresetStreams). Nothing compares stream1 with the input stream.
findings.why_wrong: A round-trip test has to compare the output with what went in. Processor::getState writes writeInt8(0) for morphMode and writeFloat(0.0f) for morphSmoothing (processor_state.cpp:319, 323). So stream1 and stream2 both carry 0 and the test passes, even though the input's morph modes 1 and 2 were lost. The section is named for exactly the property that is broken.
findings.consequence: A host project save loses every band's Morph Mode (Planar/Radial) and Morph Smoothing, and the suite stays green. The same blind spot covers any other field that getState rewrites to a constant or a modulated snapshot (sweep width/intensity/frequency, saved from the modulated sweepProcessor_ values).
findings.suggested_fix: In 'Serialization round-trip: enum types preserved' / 'MorphMode values round-trip', parse stream1 and REQUIRE each band's morphMode == b % 3 and morphSmoothing == the written value (make the input non-zero first, e.g. 50 ms). Do the same for sweep width/intensity, and compare against the input with a tolerance rather than stream1 vs stream2. The test goes red until processor_state.cpp:319/323 writes the real values.
findings.evidence: serialization_round_trip_test.cpp:226 `s.writeInt8(static_cast<Steinberg::int8>(b % 3)); // morphMode (0,1,2 cycling)`; :896-898 `REQUIRE(compareV6PresetStreams(*stream1, *stream2));`; processor_state.cpp:319 `if (!streamer.writeInt8(static_cast<Steinberg::int8>(0)))  // morphMode`, :323 `if (!streamer.writeFloat(0.0f))  // morphSmoothing (ms)`

The test input writes a real morph mode per band: serialization_round_trip_test.cpp:226 writes morphMode = b % 3. setState reads it and applies it: processor_state.cpp:819 readInt8(morphMode), :827-828 bandProcessors_[b].setMorphMode(clamp(morphMode,0,2)), :831 setMorphSmoothingTime(morphSmoothing). getState then writes constants instead of the band's real values: processor_state.cpp:319 writeInt8(0) // morphMode, :323 writeFloat(0.0f) // morphSmoothing. So a host project save loses Planar/Radial, and the controller reads these 0s back on reload (controller.cpp:523/529 setComponentState sets kBandMorphMode/kBandMorphSmoothing from the stream). The test structure matches the claim. 'v6 full parameter set' (:463-501) and the 'MorphMode values round-trip' SECTION (:875-899) both run setState(input) -> getState(stream1) -> setState(stream1) -> getState(stream2) and only REQUIRE(compareV6PresetStreams(*stream1,*stream2)) (:495, :898). The 'initial setState values are preserved' test (:503-527) only checks that stream1 differs from the default state somewhere, so it cannot catch this. The finding partly concedes this by suggesting a non-zero input. The morph-mode part, the main claim, holds. Severity stays as filed: the section is named for exactly the property that is broken, and the real-world result is lost user state.
