The test section named for this property passes while the property is broken. 'high' fits a test gap that masks a shipped state-loss bug. I did not verify the secondary sweep claim (that the getWidth/getIntensity/getTargetFrequency values are modulated) and it is not needed for this verdict.

findings.title: No test follows the host call order; setActive(true) wipes restored mod routings and setupProcessing wipes restored morph nodes
findings.problem: Every state test builds its processor as initialize -> setupProcessing -> setState -> getState (factory_preset_validation_test.cpp:98-111, serialization_round_trip_test.cpp:48-62). None calls setActive(true) after setState, and none calls setState before setupProcessing. That is the order hosts normally use: initialize, setState, setupProcessing, setActive, process.
findings.why_wrong: Processor::setActive(true) calls modulationEngine_.reset() (processor.cpp:164). That reset sets every routing to ModRouting{} and clears the macros (modulation_engine.h:152-157). Processor::setupProcessing rebuilds bandMorphCache_[i].nodes as four SoftClip nodes with activeNodeCount = kDefaultActiveNodes and pushes them to the band processors (processor.cpp:111-127). getState reads routings from modulationEngine_ (processor_state.cpp:298-307) and nodes from bandMorphCache_. A setState -> setActive(true) -> getState test would therefore come back with empty routings, and a setState -> setupProcessing test with SoftClip nodes. The suite never runs either sequence.
findings.consequence: In normal use, loading a project restores routings and macros that are then erased when the host activates the plugin. A host that calls setupProcessing after setState also loses the node types. No test can catch this.
findings.suggested_fix: Add TEST_CASE "State survives host activation order" in serialization_round_trip_test.cpp. Run initialize -> setState(non-default v12 stream) -> setupProcessing -> setActive(true) -> process 1 block -> getState, then REQUIRE that the routing slots, macros, node types and activeNodeCount match the input. Also render one block with an LFO->band-gain routing and REQUIRE that the output level varies. Run the factory-preset round-trip with the same order.
findings.evidence: processor.cpp:164 `modulationEngine_.reset();` in setActive(true); modulation_engine.h:152-155 `// Reset routings  for (auto& r : routings_) { r = ModRouting{}; }`; processor.cpp:114-121 `cache.nodes[0] = MorphNode(0, 0.0f, 0.0f, DistortionType::SoftClip); ... cache.activeNodeCount = kDefaultActiveNodes;`; factory_preset_validation_test.cpp:98-111 createTestProcessor calls setupProcessing only, with no setActive.
verifier_notes:
Every part of the claim holds up in the source.
(1) processor.cpp:144-164: Processor::setActive(true) calls modulationEngine_.reset(). modulation_engine.h:152-160 inside reset() does `r = ModRouting{}` for every routing and `m = MacroConfig{}` for every macro.
(2) Routings and macros are stored only inside modulationEngine_. The only places they are set are setState (processor_state.cpp:751-760 for macros, :798 setRouting) and processParameterChanges (processor_params.cpp:551-572, which does getRouting -> modify one field -> setRouting, and :765-817 for macros). No shadow copy exists, and nothing re-applies them after reset. getState reads them back from the engine (processor_state.cpp:289, :299). So setState followed by setActive(true) leaves the routings and macros empty, and the next getState writes empty routings.
(3) processor.cpp:111-127: setupProcessing unconditionally sets bandMorphCache_[i].nodes[0..3] to SoftClip with kDefaultCommon and activeNodeCount = kDefaultActiveNodes, then pushes them through setMorphNodes. setState fills those same cache entries (processor_state.cpp:824-897). So setupProcessing after setState (for example a sample-rate change: setActive(false) -> setupProcessing -> setActive(true)) throws away the restored node types, drive/mix/tone, shape slots and active node count.
(4) Test gap: createTestProcessor (factory_preset_validation_test.cpp:99-111) calls only initialize + setupProcessing. A grep for test files that call both setActive and setState in plugins/disrumpo/tests returned no files, so no test runs the host-order sequence.
The defect behind the gap is real, and it hits ordinary host behaviour: activation after a project load, and any reactivation or sample-rate change. High severity is warranted.

I could not refute this. Nothing upstream guards against it, nothing documents it as intended, and no test covers it.

(1) Processor::setActive(true) calls modulationEngine_.reset() at processor.cpp:164. ModulationEngine::reset() in modulation_engine.h:152-160 sets every routing to ModRouting{} and every macro to MacroConfig{}. The only comment at that point is "Activating: reset processing state" (processor.cpp:148), which does not say that clearing user routings is intended.

(2) Processor::setupProcessing rewrites bandMorphCache_[i].nodes[0..3] as SoftClip nodes with default common params and sets activeNodeCount = kDefaultActiveNodes (processor.cpp:111-122). It then pushes those to the band processors (processor.cpp:125-127). setupProcessing also calls modulationEngine_.prepare() (processor.cpp:139), and prepare() itself calls reset() (modulation_engine.h:123). So setupProcessing after setState wipes the routings as well, not only the nodes.

(3) setState writes routings and macros only into the engine: setRouting at processor_state.cpp:798, setMacro* at processor_state.cpp:751-760. Nothing else is set and nothing is re-applied after a reset. The only other place that calls setRouting is the parameter-change handler (processor_params.cpp:572), and it runs only when the host sends a change. Hosts do not re-send parameters after activation. getState reads back from the engine and the cache (processor_state.cpp:289-307, 314).

(4) Test coverage: no test file under plugins/disrumpo/tests calls both setState and setActive (grep of the tests directory returned no file). createTestProcessor in factory_preset_validation_test.cpp:99-111 runs only initialize -> setupProcessing.

The order initialize -> setState -> setupProcessing -> setActive is normal on project load. The common deactivate -> setupProcessing -> setActive cycle that hosts run on a sample-rate or buffer-size change hits the same path even after a correct load. The defect and the missing test are both real.

I could not refute this. I read each step in the source and it holds.

**Mod routings and macros**
- setState writes routings straight into the engine (processor_state.cpp:798 `modulationEngine_.setRouting(r, routing)`) and macros the same way (processor_state.cpp:751-760). No shadow copy exists. A grep of plugins/disrumpo/src for setRouting/setMacro finds only these lines and the per-parameter handlers (processor_params.cpp:572, 765-817).
- Processor::setActive(true) then calls `modulationEngine_.reset()` (processor.cpp:164). That reset sets `r = ModRouting{}` for every routing and `m = MacroConfig{}` for every macro (modulation_engine.h:152-160).
- Nothing puts them back afterwards, and hosts do not re-send unchanged parameter values to the processor after setState.
- Result: after setState -> setActive(true), every routing is inactive and every macro is at its default. Modulation depth is zero; LFO, envelope and macro routings simply stop moving anything.

**Morph nodes**
- setState fills bandMorphCache_[b].nodes and pushes them to the band processors (processor_state.cpp:824-897).
- Processor::setupProcessing overwrites all four nodes of every band with SoftClip, sets activeNodeCount = kDefaultActiveNodes and pushes those defaults (processor.cpp:111-127).
- Result: any setupProcessing after setState drops the saved node types and node count. Every band reverts to SoftClip, which changes the sound completely, not by a few dB.

**How often hosts trigger it**
- The VST3 lifecycle activates after state restore (initialize -> setState -> setupProcessing -> setActive), so routings are lost on ordinary project reload in every conforming host.
- Hosts also toggle setActive on bypass, transport/engine restarts and offline render. Each toggle wipes routings even when setState came while active.
- setupProcessing is re-called on any sample-rate or buffer-size change (deactivate -> setupProcessing -> activate). Even a session that never reloads loses its node types and routings that way.

**The test gap itself**
- No test calls both. grep shows setActive(true) only in bitcrush_noise_repro_test, data_exchange_spectrum_test, multi_node_distortion_test and processor_audio_output_test, none of which calls setState.
- The six setState test files never call setActive.
- factory_preset_validation_test.cpp:100-111 createTestProcessor runs initialize -> setupProcessing and nothing else, so setState always comes after setupProcessing with no activation.

The impact matches the claim: saved projects silently lose modulation routings, macros and node types under normal host use, and no test can catch it. High severity stands.

findings.title: All oversampling, bypass (SC-011) and alias-suppression tests run BandProcessor::processBlock, which the plugin never calls
findings.problem: The seven dsp/oversampling_*.cpp files and the SC-011 'bypassed band output is bit-identical' case drive bp.processBlock(...), usually on the legacy setDistortionType path. Processor::process only calls the per-sample BandProcessor::process (processor.cpp:487, 494). That function never reads bypassed_ and never oversamples (band_processor.h:473-512). The bypass check and the oversampling path exist only in processBlock (band_processor.h:519-523).
findings.why_wrong: The tests prove FR-012 bit-transparent bypass, SC-006 alias suppression and the FR-017 8 ms factor crossfade on a code path the shipped processor never runs. They stay green while the plugin runs every shaper at 1x and treats kBandBypass as a no-op. The adapters are also prepared at sampleRate*8 (band_processor.h:111,124) while they run at 1x, and no test catches that either.
findings.consequence: Users get unmitigated aliasing on the 4x-profile types (HardClip, folds, fuzz, rectifiers), a band bypass that does nothing, and an Oversample Max control that does nothing, while every spec-009 test reports green.
findings.suggested_fix: Add processor-level cases in processor_audio_output_test.cpp. (1) "Processor HardClip 5 kHz aliasing drops with Oversample Max 4x vs 1x": set the node type, drive and kOversampleMaxId through IParameterChanges, render, FFT, and REQUIRE an alias-bin reduction > 6 dB. (2) "Processor band bypass is bit-transparent": 1 band, kBandBypass = 1, REQUIRE output == input sample-for-sample at mix 1. Both should fail today.
findings.evidence: processor.cpp:494 `bandProcessors_[b].process(bandL, bandR);` (the only band entry; grep finds no processBlock in src/processor); band_processor.h:519-523 `void processBlock(...) { if (bypassed_) { return; }`; band_processor.h:473-512 process() never references bypassed_; oversampling_single_type_tests.cpp:203 `bp.processBlock(left.data(), right.data(), kNumSamples);`
verifier_notes:
I could not refute this. The code does what the finding says.

1. The processor only calls the per-sample path. processor.cpp:467-504 loops over every sample and calls bandProcessors_[b].process(bandL, bandR) at line 494, plus line 487 for muted or non-soloed bands. A grep for "processBlock(" across plugins/disrumpo/src finds only processor.cpp:370, which is sweepProcessor_.processBlock and has nothing to do with BandProcessor. The other matches are the definitions in sweep_processor.h, morph_engine and distortion_adapter, and BandProcessor's own definition at band_processor.h:519. Nothing in the processor calls BandProcessor::processBlock.

2. process() never checks bypass and never oversamples. band_processor.h:473-512 runs sweep, then the morph engine or distortion_ at the base rate, then gain/pan/mute. It never reads bypassed_, oversampler2x_/4x_/8xInner_ or currentOversampleFactor_.

3. Bypass and oversampling only exist inside processBlock. The `if (bypassed_) return;` check is at band_processor.h:521-523. The oversampling paths run from processBlockInner (line 548) to processWithFactor (line 627) to processWithOversampling2x/4x/8x (lines 709-742), and the 8 ms crossfade (line 653) is reached only through processBlockInner.

4. Bypass is stored but has no effect. processor_params.cpp:927-929 sets bandStates_.bypass and calls setBypassed(), which only writes bypassed_ (band_processor.h:335-336). shouldBandContribute (processor.cpp:563-575) checks only mute and solo, not bypass. So in the shipped plugin, kBandBypass changes nothing.

5. The tests run the dead path. oversampling_single_type_tests.cpp:203, :220 and :289 call bp.processBlock(...) after the legacy setDistortionType at :176 and :270. The SC-011 case (:171-209) and the SC-006 case (:247-292) therefore check code the processor never runs. A grep of plugins/disrumpo/tests for kBandBypass and kOversampleMaxId finds only ID-encoding and keyboard-shortcut tests (parameter_encoding_test, band_state_test, keyboard_shortcut_test). None of them render audio through Processor::process, so no processor-level test covers either feature.

6. The sample-rate claim also holds. band_processor.h:111-112 and :124-125 prepare distortion_ and morphEngine_ at sampleRate * kMaxOversampleFactor (8), but the shipped path runs them once per base-rate sample. Anything in the adapters that depends on sample rate (tone filter coefficients, temporal and feedback processors) is set up for 8x the rate it actually runs at, and no test checks this.

Severity stays at high. The gap hides real behaviour: oversampling never runs, the bypass control does nothing, and the adapters are configured for the wrong rate. All of that ships while the spec-009 tests stay green.

I confirmed this from the source. In processor.cpp:467-504 the per-sample loop is the only place bands are processed, and it calls `bandProcessors_[b].process(L,R)` at :487 and :494. Grep finds no processBlock call anywhere in src/processor; the only processBlock in processor.cpp is sweepProcessor_ at :370. BandProcessor::process (band_processor.h:473-512) runs the morph engine or the adapter at the base rate. It never reads bypassed_ and never touches oversampler2x_/4x_/8xInner_ or the crossfade state. Bypass is honoured only at band_processor.h:519-523, inside processBlock. Oversampling is dispatched only through processBlockInner -> processWithFactor (:548-557, :627-649), which also lives only on the processBlock path. The processor does forward the parameters: processor_params.cpp:360 calls `bp.setMaxOversampleFactor(factor)` and :929 calls `setBypassed(...)`. Both only set fields that the per-sample path ignores. The adapter and morph engine are prepared at sampleRate*kMaxOversampleFactor (band_processor.h:111-112, 124-125) but run at 1x, so the rate mismatch is real too. The SC-011 test (oversampling_single_type_tests.cpp:171-209) and the SC-006 alias test (:263-289) both call `bp.processBlock(...)` directly on the legacy setDistortionType path. In plugins/disrumpo/tests, kBandBypass appears only in ID-encoding and keyboard tests and kOversampleMaxId never appears, so no processor-level test covers either feature. Nothing marks this as intentional: the only related comment is processor.cpp:444 'FR-001a: sample-by-sample processing', and grep over specs/ finds no FR-001a definition and no design decision that drops oversampling or band bypass in the shipped processor. The tests are therefore green on a path the plugin never runs, and they hide the dead features. High severity fits.

I read the code and found nothing that refutes the finding.

- processor.cpp:467-504: the sample loop calls only `bandProcessors_[b].process(bandL, bandR)` (lines 487 and 494). A grep of src/ finds no call to BandProcessor::processBlock. The only processBlock calls are sweepProcessor_ (line 370) and the separate DistortionAdapter/MorphEngine overloads.
- band_processor.h:473-512: process() runs the smoothers, then morphEngine_->process or distortion_.process at the base rate, then gain/pan/mute. It never reads bypassed_ and never touches oversampler2x_/4x_/8xInner_.
- The bypass early return (band_processor.h:521-523), oversampling (processWithFactor, line 627 onward) and the crossfade (processBlockWithCrossfade, line 653) are reachable only through processBlock at line 519.
- Bypass is not handled anywhere else. processor_params.cpp:927-929 stores bandStates_.bypass and calls setBypassed, and shouldBandContribute (processor.cpp:563-576) checks only mute and solo. So kBandBypass does nothing audible in the plugin.
- kOversampleMaxId (processor_params.cpp:349-362) calls bp.setMaxOversampleFactor, which only changes currentOversampleFactor_. Nothing in the process() path reads that value, so the control does nothing.
- band_processor.h:111 and 124 prepare distortion_ and morphEngine_ at sampleRate*8 (kMaxOversampleFactor), but process() runs them at 1x. Any rate-dependent coefficient inside them (tone filter, temporal/feedback times) is therefore set for a different rate than the one they run at.
- Tests: oversampling_single_type_tests.cpp:203, 220 and 289 call bp.processBlock. No test under plugins/disrumpo/tests sends kBandBypass or kOversampleMaxId through the processor; grep finds kBandBypass only in ID-encoding tests (band_state_test, parameter_encoding_test, keyboard_shortcut_test).

The claimed consequence can occur. The aliasing amount is my estimate, not a measurement. At 44.1 kHz with HardClip, folds or fuzz on a 5 kHz input, harmonics from the 5th upward fold back into the audible band at full 1x level. That is the SC-006 margin the test credits to oversampling, which the test requires to be at least 48 dB. A band bypass that does nothing and a dead Oversample Max control happen with every host and every setting.

The finding is a test gap. Its real weight comes from the shipped defects it hides, and the existing suites stay green regardless. High severity is justified.

findings.title: Controller state paths (preset writer, setComponentState, Controller get/setState) have zero tests, while hand-copied 'mirror' helpers test the correct formula
findings.problem: No test calls Controller::createComponentStateStream, parseComponentState, setComponentState, loadComponentStateWithNotify or Controller::getState/setState (grep of tests finds none). state_persistence_test instead re-implements the formulas: controllerNormalizeSource uses /(kModSourceCount-1) (:276-278), and 'Full routing slot binary round-trip' writes and reads its own byte buffer. 'SC-011: All state persists together' copies local floats into other locals and asserts they are equal; it never touches the Controller.
findings.why_wrong: The real preset writer has different formulas from the mirrors. It writes the routing source as getInt8FromList(id, 12), i.e. round(norm*12), while the load side uses 13 (controller.cpp:1699-1700, 1815). It writes active nodes as round(norm*2)+2 for a 4-entry list (controller.cpp:1830-1831). Window size and expand state are not persisted at all. The tests can only fail if the helper formulas disagree with each other, never if the shipped code is wrong.
findings.consequence: A user preset saved from the browser loads routings from sources 7-13 one source lower and changes 1-node bands to 2 nodes and 2-node bands to 3. SC-011 is reported as covered while it is not.
findings.suggested_fix: Add TEST_CASE "Controller preset stream round-trips through processor". Initialize a Controller, set non-default params (routing source 13 on slot 0, active nodes 1 on band 0, morph mode 2, smoothing 100 ms), call createComponentStateStream, feed the stream to Processor::setState then getState, and REQUIRE source == 13, activeNodes == 1 and morph mode == 2. Add a Controller::getState/setState round-trip for the MIDI CC blob. Delete or rewrite the tautological SC-011 sections.
findings.evidence: controller.cpp:1815 `streamer.writeInt8(getInt8FromList(makeRoutingParamId(r, 0), 12));`; controller.cpp:1831 `int activeNodes = static_cast<int>(std::round(activeNodesNorm * 2.0f)) + 2;`; state_persistence_test.cpp:276-278 `static double controllerNormalizeSource(int8_t source) { return static_cast<double>(source) / (Krate::DSP::kModSourceCount - 1); }`; :123-130 `restoredExpandStates[i] = serializedExpandStates[...]; float restoredModPanel = serializedModPanel;`
verifier_notes:
I traced the code and the finding holds.

1) The preset save path really goes through the controller writer. controller.cpp:116-118 hooks presetManager_->setStateProvider up to createComponentStateStream(), and :120-124 hooks the load provider up to loadComponentStateWithNotify().

2) The writer formulas are wrong.
- Routing source: controller.cpp:1815 writes getInt8FromList(makeRoutingParamId(r,0), 12), and getInt8FromList is round(norm*maxVal) (:1699-1700). The parameter is a 14-entry StringListParameter, "None" through "Transient" (parameter_registration.cpp:562-577), so norm = k/13. The load side divides by kUIModSourceCount-1 = 13 (controller.cpp:467-469; plugin_ids.h:546 sets kUIModSourceCount=14). So source k is written as round(12k/13), which is k-1 for k>=7. For example Transient (13) becomes 12 (Pitch), and Macro 3 (7) becomes 6.
- Active nodes: the parameter has 4 entries "1".."4" (parameter_registration.cpp:699-706). The loader maps count to (count-1)/3 (controller.cpp:525-526), and kMinActiveNodes=1 (morph_node.h:132). The writer computes round(norm*2)+2 (controller.cpp:1831). So norm 0 (1 node) is written as 2, norm 0.333 (2 nodes) as 3, norm 0.667 (3 nodes) as 3, and only 4 nodes survives. This matches the stated consequence exactly.

3) The tests never reach these paths. A grep of plugins/disrumpo/tests finds no call to createComponentStateStream, parseComponentState, setComponentState or loadComponentStateWithNotify, and no Controller getState/setState round-trip. preset_save_test.cpp builds its own state stream by hand (createMinimalStateStream, around :150-192) and passes a PresetManager with a null controller. factory_preset_validation_test.cpp only exercises processor->setState/getState (:163-210).

4) The mirror helpers do not even match the shipped code. state_persistence_test.cpp:276-278 divides by Krate::DSP::kModSourceCount-1 = 17 (modulation_types.h:63 sets it to 18), while the controller divides by 13. In the SC-011 section (:100-130), local floats are copied into other locals and compared, and no Controller is involved.

I did not separately verify the claim that window size and expand state are not persisted, but the main defect (the test gap hiding real wrong-formula bugs in the shipped preset writer) is confirmed from source. Severity high is appropriate: user-saved presets silently corrupt routing sources and active-node counts.

I could not refute this finding. The code confirms it.

Test gap. A grep of plugins/disrumpo/tests finds no call to createComponentStateStream, parseComponentState, setComponentState, loadComponentStateWithNotify or Controller get/setState. Only two test files construct a Disrumpo::Controller, editor_lifecycle_test.cpp:17,35 and data_exchange_spectrum_test.cpp, and neither covers state. preset_integration_test.cpp includes only the shared preset_manager headers and passes its own stateProvider lambda (:219), so the real controller writer is never exercised. state_persistence_test.cpp:34-140 ("SC-011") copies local arrays and floats into other locals and never touches a Controller. The mirror helpers at :275-278 also do not match the shipped code. They normalize the routing source by (Krate::DSP::kModSourceCount - 1) = 17 (modulation_types.h:63), while the real load path at controller.cpp:467-469 divides by kUIModSourceCount - 1 = 13 (plugin_ids.h:546). So even the mirror tests a formula the controller does not use.

Shipped writer bugs.
- Routing source (sources 7 and up save one lower). parameter_registration.cpp:563-578 registers 14 list entries (None through Transient, step count 13). The writer at controller.cpp:1815 calls getInt8FromList(..., 12), which computes round((s/13)*12). That gives 6 for source 7, 7 for source 8, and so on up to 12 for source 13.
- Active nodes (a 1-node band saves as 2, a 2-node band as 3). parameter_registration.cpp:700-707 registers 4 list entries ("1" to "4", norm = (count-1)/3), and the load side agrees (controller.cpp:525-526 sets (count-1)/3.0). The writer at controller.cpp:1830-1832 computes round(norm*2)+2, which saves 1 node as 2 and 2 nodes as 3, while 3 and 4 survive.

Both bugs are reachable in a real host. createComponentStateStream is the preset-save state provider (controller.cpp:117), and loadComponentStateWithNotify is the preset load (controller.cpp:123, 1876-1896). Nothing upstream clamps or corrects these values, and no code comment or spec calls the mismatch intentional.

The severity of high stands: the missing coverage hides two confirmed, user-visible corruptions of user presets.

I could not refute this. The test gap is real, and the two writer bugs it hides corrupt user presets.

User preset save goes through the controller writer. controller.cpp:113-118 builds PresetManager with a null processor and sets stateProvider to createComponentStateStream. In preset_manager.cpp:309/361/417/449, useStateProvider = (processor_ == nullptr && stateProvider_), so every browser save runs controller.cpp:1687 onward. The load path is controller.cpp:120-124, loadComponentStateWithNotify.

Routing source bug:
- The writer is controller.cpp:1815: `getInt8FromList(makeRoutingParamId(r,0), 12)`, which is round(norm*12).
- The reader is controller.cpp:466-469, which divides by kUIModSourceCount-1. The processor (processor_params.cpp:555) uses the same denominator, and plugin_ids.h:546 sets kUIModSourceCount = 14, so the denominator is 13.
- A source k has norm k/13 and is written as round(12k/13). That gives 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,6,7,8,9,10,11,12 for k = 0..13. Sources 7 to 13 are saved one lower, and sources 6 and 7 collapse to the same value. Any routing on those sources changes after a save and reload.

Active nodes bug:
- The parameter is a 4-entry StringListParameter (parameter_registration.cpp:699-702), so norm = (count-1)/3. Both readers agree: processor_params.cpp:951-952 and controller.cpp:525-526.
- The writer at controller.cpp:1831 computes round(norm*2)+2, which maps 1→2, 2→3, 3→3 and 4→4.
- kDefaultActiveNodes is 1 (morph_node.h:135), so every default band in a user preset reloads with 2 nodes. Morph processing switches on and the sound changes.

No test exercises this path. A grep of plugins/disrumpo/tests for createComponentStateStream, parseComponentState, setComponentState, loadComponentStateWithNotify and Controller get/setState finds only comments (state_persistence_test.cpp:260, 275, 427). The routing helpers are hand copies: controllerNormalizeSource at :276-278 even divides by Krate::DSP::kModSourceCount-1 rather than the shipped kUIModSourceCount-1. The SC-011 case (:99-237) copies local values into other locals (:123-133) and asserts they are equal, so it can never catch a defect in shipped code.

The consequence matches the claim: every user preset that uses those routing sources, or has a band with 1 or 2 nodes (including the default of 1), loads changed. That is silent state corruption on a user-facing path, so high severity holds.

findings.title: Factory-preset tests never render a preset and never compare the load against the preset file; 119 of 121 presets go through the v10 migration unchecked
findings.problem: 'Factory presets load without error' only checks setState() == kResultOk. setState returns kResultOk for almost any stream after the globals, including a truncated band count (processor_state.cpp:408-411). The round-trip case compares processor output with processor output and allows up to 16 differing bytes. No preset is ever processed. I measured the 'Comp' chunk versions of the shipped presets: {v6: 1 (Init/Init_5_Bands), v8: 1 (Experimental/Formant_Shift), v10: 119}. So every preset loads through the v<=11 routing-destination migration (processor_state.cpp:775-790) and the v<=7 8-band path, and nothing checks the migrated values. The category test pins Init 5 / Experimental 16, which counts the two orphan files the generator does not emit. tools/disrumpo_preset_generator.cpp has 'Formant Shift' only under Morph.
findings.why_wrong: SC-004 'all factory presets pass validation' should mean that each preset loads the intended parameters and produces finite, non-silent, bounded audio. The current test only shows that the reader does not crash.
findings.consequence: A preset that renders NaN, silence, runaway feedback or DC, or whose routings migrate to the wrong band slot, ships green. An 'Init 5 Bands' preset that can only produce 4 bands is protected by the count test.
findings.suggested_fix: Add TEST_CASE "Every factory preset renders finite bounded audio" (tag [long] if > 15 s). For each preset: setState, setActive(true), 2 s of pink noise at 44.1 kHz; REQUIRE that every sample is finite (use Krate::DSP::detail::isFinite), peak < +12 dBFS, |DC| < 0.01 and RMS > -60 dBFS. Add a migration case that reads one v10 preset's raw routing dests and REQUIRE that getState shows the remapped kBandBase + band*8 + param. Decide on the two orphan presets and fix the expected counts.
findings.evidence: factory_preset_validation_test.cpp:165 `CHECK(result == Steinberg::kResultOk);` (the only assertion); :242 `CHECK(differingBytes <= 16);`; :256-259 expected counts `{"Init", 5} ... {"Experimental", 16}`; measured by a node script over the Comp chunks: `{"6":1,"8":1,"10":119}`, with v6 = Init_5_Bands.vstpreset and v8 = Experimental/Formant_Shift.vstpreset; generator grep: only `p.name = "Formant Shift"; p.category = "Morph";` (line 1674).
