findings.title: No test feeds different L and R signals through a morph-enabled band, so the shared L/R MorphEngine is untestable
findings.problem: BandProcessor::process runs left and then right through ONE MorphEngine (band_processor.h:487-488). Every morph test feeds identical L/R values (e.g. morph_band_integration_test.cpp:103-104, 202-203; morph_artifact_test feeds input[i] to both and reads only left). The processor fixture uses identical sines on both channels. IT-006 'Full stereo signal path' does use 1 kHz / 500 Hz, but on BandProcessors that never get setMorphNodes. Those have morph disabled and legacy drive 0 (band_processor.h:116), so they pass the signal through untouched.
findings.why_wrong: Interleaving L and R through one stateful engine causes crosstalk and halves filter time constants. With identical channels the interleaved state looks like a mono run, so the defect cannot show. A stereo test must use decorrelated channels with the live morph path enabled.
findings.consequence: Cross-channel bleed and a doubled cursor-smoother speed on every stereo source go undetected.
findings.suggested_fix: Add TEST_CASE "Morph band keeps L and R independent" in morph_band_integration_test.cpp. setMorphNodes with Tube + FeedbackDist, L = 440 Hz sine, R = silence; REQUIRE R RMS < -90 dBFS after settling, and REQUIRE that L matches a mono run of the same engine type within 1e-4. The same check at processor level: L sine, R zeros, REQUIRE output R ~ 0 at mix 1.
findings.evidence: band_processor.h:487-488 `left = morphEngine_->process(left); right = morphEngine_->process(right);`; band_management_integration_test.cpp:261-266 BandProcessors created with prepare() only and no setMorphNodes; :272-273 L 1000 Hz / R 500 Hz; band_processor.h:116 `defaultParams.drive = 0.0f;  // Bypass distortion by default`
verifier_notes:
I could not refute this. The code does share one stateful engine between L and R, and no test exercises that with different channels.

1. **One engine, interleaved L then R.** BandProcessor has a single `std::unique_ptr<MorphEngine> morphEngine_` (band_processor.h:808). process() calls it for left and then right on every sample pair (band_processor.h:487-488), and processBlock does the same (band_processor.h:753-754). MorphEngine::process (morph_engine.cpp:662-683) advances smootherX_ and smootherY_ on every call, so they step twice per stereo frame. It also runs the input through one blendedAdapter_ (morph_engine.cpp:706-718) or the per-node adapters, which carry filter, feedback and oversampler state. Feeding L and R alternately through the same state is exactly the crosstalk and doubled smoothing speed the finding describes.

2. **The live plugin always takes this path.** The processor calls setMorphNodes on every band at processor.cpp:126, processor_params.cpp:899/954 and processor_state.cpp:894, so every real band runs the shared engine.

3. **The cited test does not touch it.** IT-006 (band_management_integration_test.cpp:241-308) does use 1 kHz on L and 500 Hz on R (:263-264). But its BandProcessors only get prepare() (:255-258) and never setMorphNodes. That leaves morph disabled and the legacy drive at 0 (band_processor.h:116), so band_processor.h:492 skips distortion entirely.

4. **Every morph-enabled test uses identical channels.** I grepped all 7 files that call setMorphNodes. Each feeds L and R the same signal: oversampling_crossfade_tests.cpp:67-68, 114-115, 123-124, 202-203; oversampling_integration_tests.cpp:62-64, 114-115; oversampling_limit_tests.cpp:208-209; morph_band_integration_test.cpp:266, 283, 310-311. The processor-level test also generates the same 1 kHz sine on both channels (processor_audio_output_test.cpp:158).

5. **None of them checks channel independence.** No test asserts that silence on R stays silent while L carries signal, or that L matches a mono run. The test gap is confirmed.

I could not refute this. The shared L/R engine is real, and nothing in the source or the specs marks it as a design decision.
- band_processor.h:487-488 (per-sample path) and :752-754 (oversampled block path) both call morphEngine_->process(left) and then morphEngine_->process(right) on the one MorphEngine created at :123.
- morph_engine.cpp:662-683 MorphEngine::process advances smootherX_/smootherY_ on every call (:668-669), so the cursor smoother runs at twice its intended speed. processSameFamily (:691-718) and processCrossFamily (:721+) send both channels through the same stateful blendedAdapter_ and per-node adapters, so L and R interleave through shared filter and shaper state.
- No comment in morph_engine.h/.cpp or distortion_adapter.h mentions stereo, mono or per-channel. A grep of specs/Disrumpo/*.md finds no design note on a shared stereo morph state.

The test gap is also real:
- band_management_integration_test.cpp:255-258 creates the BandProcessors with prepare() only (no setMorphEnabled or setMorphNodes). Their default drive is 0 (band_processor.h:116), and at :492 the legacy path skips distortion below drive 0.0001. So IT-006's decorrelated 1 kHz / 500 Hz input (:263-264) never reaches a morph engine.
- Every morph-enabled BandProcessor test I checked feeds identical channels: multi_node_distortion_test.cpp:1265-1270 (inputL = inputR = s), :1399 and :1407 (l = r = input[i]). The oversampling_* tests set constant or identical-sine right channels.
- A grep over plugins/disrumpo/tests turns up no case with R silent or decorrelated through a morph-enabled band, and no processor-level crosstalk check.

The finding stands as stated. Severity stays medium: this is a test-gap entry, and the defect behind it is its own finding.

I could not refute this. Every link in the claim checks out in source, and the defect it hides is real and audible.

(1) One engine serves both channels. band_processor.h:487-488 runs `left = morphEngine_->process(left); right = morphEngine_->process(right);` through a single MorphEngine. The oversampled path does the same at band_processor.h:753-754. The legacy path at :493-494 and :756-757 also sends L and R through one `distortion_` adapter.

(2) The engine is stateful per call. morph_engine.cpp:668-669 advances smootherX_ and smootherY_ on every process() call. That is two steps per stereo frame, so the cursor glide runs at twice its designed speed. The call goes on to blendedAdapter_.process (:718) or adapters_[i].process (:752). DistortionAdapter::process (distortion_adapter.cpp:189-225) runs a stateful dcBlocker_ (:219), toneFilter_ (:583) and the stateful KrateDSP processors behind processRaw (e.g. fractal_ and stochastic_ at :571 and :575).

(3) What interleaving does. One filter fed alternating L,R,L,R samples behaves like a filter at twice the rate on an interleaved signal. It splits into (L+R)/2 at baseband plus (L-R)/2 shifted up to the new Nyquist. So R's output contains a large, low-passed copy of L. This is not a sub-dB effect: with R silent, the R output carries signal at roughly the same order as L. That is gross channel bleed on every stereo source whenever drive is above 0.0001 (gate at distortion_adapter.cpp:191) and the type uses the tone filter or DC blocker, i.e. most types and every default setting a user hears.

(4) No test catches it. IT-006 (band_management_integration_test.cpp:241-309) does feed 1 kHz on L and 500 Hz on R (:263-264). But its BandProcessors only get prepare() (:255-258), never setMorphNodes. With the default drive of 0 (band_processor.h:116) and the drive gate (:492), the signal passes through untouched, so no shared state is exercised. Its assertions only check that both channels have RMS above 0.1 and that the L/R ratio is about 1 (:303-308). Even an active engine with bleed would pass those, so the test has no crosstalk check at all. A grep of plugins/disrumpo/tests for crosstalk, bleed, independence or "L and R" finds only the comment at :246; no other test checks channel independence.

So the consequence holds as stated: the doubled smoother speed and the cross-channel bleed both go undetected. Medium is the right severity for the test gap itself. The underlying shared-engine defect is more serious and deserves its own high-severity finding, but this test-gap row does not need to change.

findings.title: Cursor-on-node tests check weights only; nothing covers the skipped transition-gain update in cross-family output, and SC-002 was relaxed to 3 dB, same-family only
findings.problem: 'cursor at node position gives 100% weight' asserts only getWeights(). In calculateMorphWeights the on-node branch fills weights and returns before transitionGains_ is recomputed (morph_engine.cpp:188-192, 220-224, vs 266-269). processCrossFamily multiplies by the stale transitionGains_[i] (morph_engine.cpp:747-756). No test renders cross-family audio with the cursor parked exactly on a node after arriving from a distant position. morph_artifact_test 'Output level consistency during morph' (SC-002, spec says 1 dB) asserts diffMid < 3.0 dB on same-family nodes (morph_artifact_test.cpp:455-460).
findings.why_wrong: The early return is exactly where a divide-by-zero guard can create a level or silence bug. With 0 ms smoothing and a jump from node B to node A, node A's gain keeps the value computed when its weight was below 0.001, which is 0. The band then goes silent while sitting on A. SC-002 needs a cross-family 1 dB assertion. The cross-family path sums w*gain with normalized weights, which gives about -3 dB at the 50/50 point.
findings.consequence: Users hear silence or a level dip when the morph cursor snaps onto a node, and a mid-morph level dip in cross-family blends, with no red test.
findings.suggested_fix: Add TEST_CASE "Cross-family cursor jump onto node keeps unity node level" in morph_transition_test.cpp. Nodes SoftClip + Bitcrush, smoothing 0, position 1.0 for 2000 samples, then 0.0. REQUIRE that the output RMS equals a single SoftClip adapter's RMS within 0.5 dB. Restore SC-002 to 1 dB with a cross-family node pair.
findings.evidence: morph_engine.cpp:188-192 `if (distances[i] < kOnNodeThreshold) { weights_.fill(0.0f); weights_[i] = 1.0f; return; }`; :266-269 the transitionGains_ loop sits after the return; :756 `output += nodeOutput * weight * gain;`; morph_artifact_test.cpp:459-460 `float diffMid = std::abs(levelMid_dB - avgRef_dB); REQUIRE(diffMid < 3.0f);`
verifier_notes:
The code and test claims hold, but the failure scenario the finding gives cannot happen.

What holds:
1. morph_engine.cpp:188-192 (Linear1D) and :220-224 (Planar2D) do `weights_.fill(0); weights_[i]=1; return;` before the transitionGains_ loop at :267-270. So when the cursor is on a node, transitionGains_ keeps its old values.
2. processCrossFamily (:743-757) reads that stale `transitionGains_[i]`, skips the node if gain < kWeightThreshold (:749) and outputs `nodeOutput*weight*gain` (:756).
3. morph_weight_computation_test.cpp:58-83 only calls calculateMorphWeights and checks getWeights(). It renders no audio.
4. approval/morph_artifact_test.cpp:377-460 (the file is under approval/, not unit/) uses createSameFamilySetup(). The comment at :455-458 says SC-002 is 1 dB, yet :460 asserts `diffMid < 3.0f`.
5. The cross-family mid-point dip is real. At weight 0.5, calculateTransitionGain (:373-378) returns equalPowerGains(0.5).fadeIn = 0.707. Each node contributes 0.5*0.707, so correlated node outputs sum to 0.707 (-3 dB). A cross-family 1 dB SC-002 assertion would catch that, and none exists.

What does not hold: "0 ms smoothing, jump from B to A, silence". MorphEngine::setSmoothingTime (:125-129) configures OnePoleSmoother, and smoother.h:82 clamps the time to kMinSmoothingTimeMs = 0.1 ms. The smoother only snaps within 1e-4 (smoother.h:197), so the cursor still slides there over several samples. process() (:668-672) recomputes the weights every sample. The last off-node update therefore happens within about 0.003 of A, where A's weight is about 0.99999, so its gain is 1. A cursor move cannot leave a stale gain of 0.

The same stale gain is reachable another way. setNodes (:131-151) recalculates the weights at the current smoothed position without resetting transitionGains_ (only reset() at :87 does). processor_params.cpp:899 calls setMorphNodes when the active node count changes, and the nodes sit at fixed corners (processor.cpp:114-120). Example: with 4 nodes, the cursor rests near B, so node C gets a gain of 0. The count drops to 2, the cursor moves to (0,1), then the count goes back to 3 or 4. C is now on-node with weight 1 but gain 0, so a cross-family band goes silent while the cursor stays there.

So the mechanism is real and untested, and the SC-002 relaxation is real. The silence consequence is overstated: it needs a node-count change with the cursor parked on a corner, not a cursor move. I left severity unchanged because the -3 dB cross-family dip with no cross-family 1 dB assertion is enough for a medium test gap.

I tried to refute this from the source and could not. The code defect it describes is real and reachable in the default configuration, and no test covers it.

1. **The stale gain is real.** In morph_engine.cpp:170-271, calculateMorphWeights clears weights_. In Linear1D (lines 188-192) and Planar2D (lines 220-224), the on-node branch sets weights_[i]=1 and returns. That return skips the transitionGains_ loop at lines 267-270. transitionGains_ is reset to 1 only in reset() (line 87); no other code writes it. processCrossFamily (lines 743-757) reads that stale gain: line 749 skips the node when gain < kWeightThreshold (0.001, morph_node.h:139), and line 756 computes `output += nodeOutput * weight * gain`. isSameFamily() depends on node types, not weights, so a cross-family node pair still takes this path when the cursor sits on a node. calculateTransitionGain (lines 352-379) returns 0 for weight <= 0.001 and about 0.707 for weight 0.5. So with no smoothing, a jump from 0.5 onto node A plays A at about -3 dB. A jump from close to node B (A's weight <= 0.001) silences the band.

2. **Not guarded by smoothing in practice.** With smoothing above zero the cursor passes through positions where A's weight is above 0.6, so the gain reaches 1 before the on-node branch fires. But the effective smoothing is 0 ms:
   - parameter_registration.cpp:717-719 registers Band Morph Smoothing as 0-500 ms with default 0.0.
   - processor_state.cpp:323 always writes 0.0f for morphSmoothing.
   - processor_state.cpp:815-831 reads it back and calls setMorphSmoothingTime(0) after any state load.
   - MorphEngine::setSmoothingTime (lines 125-129) accepts 0.
   - The position is pushed every block from processor.cpp:316 and on parameter changes at processor_params.cpp:935-944.
   
   Clicking the pad corner where node A sits is therefore an instant jump. I found no design note or comment that makes this intentional.

3. **No test covers it.** morph_weight_computation_test.cpp:58-83 checks only getWeights(). The cross-family on-node renders in multi_node_distortion_test.cpp (1197-1222, 1284-1313) use the engine's default 10 ms smoothing or fresh BandProcessors, whose gains start at 1 from reset. They also assert only RMS > 0.01 and difference > 0.1, not level. approval/morph_artifact_test.cpp:377-460 (AP-003, SC-002) has a comment saying cross-family within 1 dB. It actually uses createSameFamilySetup() with 0.1 ms smoothing and asserts diffMid < 3.0f; the comment at lines 455-458 admits the relaxation.

The test gap and the defect it hides both hold. Medium is appropriate for a test-gap finding; the underlying defect is reachable by default and should be tracked as its own correctness finding.

I confirmed the bug behind this test gap from the source, and the consequence can happen with default settings.

**The bug**
- morph_engine.cpp:188-192 (Linear1D) and :220-224 (Planar2D) fill weights_ and `return` before the transitionGains_ loop at :267-270. So while the cursor sits on a node, transitionGains_ keeps the value from the last off-node sample.
- The path is live. BandProcessor calls morphEngine_->process() at band_processor.h:487-488 and :753-754. MorphEngine::process (morph_engine.cpp:672) calls calculateMorphWeights on every sample, and the early return repeats each time, so the stale gain stays until the cursor leaves the node.
- processCrossFamily skips a node when `gain < kWeightThreshold` (:748-749) and otherwise outputs `nodeOutput * weight * gain` (:756).
- calculateTransitionGain (:352-379) returns 0 for weight <= 0.001, sin(pi/4) = 0.707 at weight 0.5, and 1 only at weight >= 0.6.
- reset() (:87) sets the gains to 1, but setState and parameter changes do not call it.
- Morph smoothing defaults to 0 ms (parameter_registration.cpp:718-719 default 0.0; processor_state.cpp:323 writes 0.0f). The smoother then jumps the cursor in one step.

**Quantified with 2 nodes at 0 and 1, Linear1D, cross-family**
- Cursor at 0.5 (gain_B = 0.707), then a jump to exactly 1.0 (automation step, preset load, morph link or pad snap): band B is stuck at -3.0 dB.
- Arriving from 0.9 (w_A = 0.012, gain_A = sin(0.03*pi/2) = 0.047): -26.5 dB.
- Arriving from any x >= ~0.969 that is not on node B (w_A = 1.063/1111 ≈ 0.00096, below the 0.001 threshold, so gain_A = 0): node A is skipped at :749 and the band is silent while parked on A.
- 4 nodes in Planar2D, from the centre (w = 0.25, gain = 0.83): -1.6 dB.
- A slow drag, or smoothing above 0, passes through weights >= 0.6 before reaching the node, so gain is 1 and the bug does not show. That is why it is easy to miss.

**Correction to the finding**
The claim that no test renders cross-family audio parked on a node after a distant position is not quite right. morph_interpolation_test.cpp:258-306 does exactly that: smoothing 0, positions 0 then 0.5 then 1.0, cross-family nodes. At 1.0, gain_B is the stale 0.707, so the level is about 3 dB low. The test still passes for two reasons:
- It asserts a linear ratio `ratio < 3.0f` (:305), which is about 9.5 dB, not 1 dB.
- It skips the check entirely when `minLevel <= 0.001` (:298), so outright silence also passes.

So the test exists but has no teeth, and the gap stands. The SC-002 relaxation is real, though the file is tests/approval/morph_artifact_test.cpp, not unit: line 378 states the 1 dB spec, :457-460 assert `diffMid < 3.0f`, and the setup is createSameFamilySetup (:383).

**Severity**
Medium is appropriate for a test gap. The bug it hides (a stuck -3 dB, or silence, on a cross-family band) is real under default 0 ms smoothing. No severity change.

findings.title: FR-019 / SC-009 processor-cap tests are vacuous: no global cap or dynamic threshold exists in the code
findings.problem: 'dynamic threshold raises when exceeding limit' builds ONE engine, counts active weights (at most 4) and REQUIREs activeCount <= kMaxGlobalProcessors (16). That is always true. 'threshold never exceeds 0.25' checks that center weights of 0.25 are >= 0.24. kMaxGlobalProcessors and kMaxWeightThreshold are only defined (morph_node.h:142, 148) and nothing in src reads them.
findings.why_wrong: The tests carry FR-019/SC-009 tags while no threshold-raising algorithm exists. They cannot fail for any implementation, including none.
findings.consequence: FR-019's 16-processor global cap is reported as covered while it is unimplemented. Four bands of 4-node cross-family morphs run 16 adapters, plus the blended adapters, with no limit.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the vacuous cases or replace them with a Processor-level test. 4 bands x 4 cross-family nodes at the center; count adapters processed per sample through a test hook; REQUIRE <= 16 and REQUIRE that the effective threshold rose above 0.001. It stays red until FR-019 is implemented or formally dropped from the spec.
findings.evidence: morph_processor_cap_test.cpp:143-144 `int activeCount = countActiveProcessors(weights, 4); REQUIRE(activeCount <= Disrumpo::kMaxGlobalProcessors);`; grep of src for kMaxGlobalProcessors|kMaxWeightThreshold: only morph_node.h:142 and :148
verifier_notes:
The finding is correct, but its consequence is overstated.

Confirmed from source:
- morph_processor_cap_test.cpp:122-145 builds one engine, puts the cursor at the centre and checks `activeCount <= kMaxGlobalProcessors` (16). countActiveProcessors (lines 58-67) loops over at most activeNodeCount=4, so the count can never pass 16. The test cannot fail.
- Lines 147-168 only check that the centre weights (about 0.25 each) are >= kMaxWeightThreshold - 0.01. That is the plain inverse-distance result. No threshold is ever raised.
- A grep of plugins/disrumpo/src finds kMaxGlobalProcessors (morph_node.h:148), kMaxWeightThreshold (:142) and kWeightThresholdIncrement (:145) only where they are defined. The only threshold logic used is the fixed kWeightThreshold=0.001 (morph_engine.cpp:250-263, 361, 529, 647, 745). No code anywhere enforces a cap across bands.
- The retired spec specs/_archive2_/005-morph-system/spec.md:198 (FR-019) and :228 (SC-009) require this algorithm. Its compliance table still marks both MET (:317, :326), citing this test file. tasks.md:469-479 shows T5.16a/b/c, the cap tests and the cap implementation, left unchecked. So the claim that tests carrying FR-019/SC-009 tags give false coverage stands.

Why severity goes down: FR-019 was written for 5 bands (spec.md:150, 228). The code allows at most 4 bands (band_state.h:61, crossover_network.h:46) and kMaxMorphNodes=4 (morph_node.h:86). So at most 4x4 = 16 node processors can be active, which is exactly the cap. The cap is unimplemented but in practice unreachable. The finding says this setup runs with no limit, which overstates the real-time risk. What remains is a vacuous test plus a false MET entry in the compliance table; there is no live CPU-overrun path.

The literal observation is correct. morph_processor_cap_test.cpp:143-144 asserts that the active weights of one 4-node engine are at most kMaxGlobalProcessors (16), and :165-166 asserts that 0.25 is at least 0.24. Neither can fail. kMaxGlobalProcessors and kMaxWeightThreshold (morph_node.h:142, :148) are not read anywhere in plugins/disrumpo/src (grep). The case comment at :129 ("For now, test the single-engine threshold behavior") admits it is a placeholder.

The defect claimed, though, is an unimplemented cap with unlimited processors, and that cannot happen. The 16-processor cap holds by construction, so the over-cap condition is unreachable in a real host:
(1) band_state.h:61 sets kMaxBands = 4 and morph_node.h:86 sets kMaxMorphNodes = 4.
(2) Each band owns exactly one MorphEngine (band_processor.h:808, unique_ptr<MorphEngine> morphEngine_).
(3) MorphEngine::process dispatches to either processSameFamily or processCrossFamily (morph_engine.cpp:679/681), never both. processSameFamily runs only blendedAdapter_ (one processor, :718). processCrossFamily runs at most activeNodeCount_ (at most 4) node adapters and never the blended adapter (:743-757), skipping weights below kWeightThreshold (:745, :749).
So one band runs at most 4 adapters and all bands together at most 4 x 4 = 16, which equals kMaxGlobalProcessors. The finding's claim that 16 adapters run "plus the blended adapters, with no limit" is false: the blended adapter does not run in cross-family mode.

FR-019's dynamic threshold triggers only when the count would EXCEED 16, and with the current band and node maxima that branch can never be taken. The suggested fix is also wrong. It would REQUIRE the threshold to rise at 4 bands x 4 nodes, but at exactly 16 FR-019 does not call for a raise, so that test would encode wrong behaviour.

What remains is cosmetic and not a functional defect or a real coverage gap: three test cases with misleading FR-019 tags, and two unused constants. At most it is a low-priority cleanup: retag or delete the cases, or replace them with a static_assert(kMaxBands * kMaxMorphNodes <= kMaxGlobalProcessors).

The test-gap is real. morph_processor_cap_test.cpp:139-144 computes the weights of ONE engine with 4 nodes and REQUIREs activeCount <= kMaxGlobalProcessors (16). countActiveProcessors (:58-67) can return at most activeNodeCount = 4, so the case cannot fail. The case at :160-167 checks that center weights of about 0.25 are >= 0.24, which is a weight-calculation check and has nothing to do with a threshold cap. In src, kMaxWeightThreshold (morph_node.h:142), kWeightThresholdIncrement (:145) and kMaxGlobalProcessors (:148) are defined and never read. Only kWeightThreshold (0.001, :139) is used, at morph_engine.cpp:253, :529, :647 and :745. So no dynamic threshold-raising algorithm exists, and the FR-019-tagged cases are vacuous, as claimed.

The claimed consequence does not happen, though. kMaxBands = 4 (band_state.h:61, crossover_network.h:46) and kMaxMorphNodes = 4 (morph_node.h:86). Each BandProcessor owns exactly one MorphEngine (band_processor.h:123, :808). Per sample, processCrossFamily (morph_engine.cpp:743-757) runs at most activeNodeCount_ (<= 4) adapters_[i], and processSameFamily (:691-719) runs only the single blendedAdapter_. The two paths are alternatives, so the blended adapter is never added on top of the per-node adapters. The worst case is therefore 4 bands x 4 adapters = 16, which equals the cap. The finding's 'plus the blended adapters, with no limit' is wrong. The cap is met by construction, and the threshold-raising algorithm could never trigger under the current band and node limits. The test comment at :127 ('5 bands * 4 nodes = 20') refers to a band count that no longer exists.

So the real issue is misleading test names/tags and three dead constants. There is no unbounded CPU or over-cap case to protect against, and no audible or performance consequence. Severity should drop from medium to low (cleanup: delete the vacuous cases and dead constants, or replace them with a static_assert(kMaxBands * kMaxMorphNodes <= kMaxGlobalProcessors) that documents why FR-019 holds).

findings.title: Disrumpo lacks the registered-defaults probe and any registration-vs-processor mapping test
findings.problem: Ruinae, Seraphis, Vorago and Profundum each have a lifecycle case calling Krate::TestSupport::parametersStartingOffTheirDefault (tests/test_helpers/registered_defaults_probe.h), which 'each plugin's controller lifecycle test lists ... and requires none'. Disrumpo's editor_lifecycle_test has no such case. No Disrumpo test touches a registered Parameter object: grep for getParameterObject/registerAllParameters finds only display_format_test. Nothing compares Parameter::toPlain with the processor's denormalization.
findings.why_wrong: Band Count and Oversample Max are StringListParameters whose start value comes from setNormalized(1.0) / setNormalized(2.0/3.0) while ParameterInfo.defaultNormalizedValue stays 0 (parameter_registration.cpp:76, 90). The probe flags exactly that. The 40 registration/processor mismatches in the params inventory (linear RangeParameter vs log2/log10/exp processor maps for sweep frequency, crossovers, LFO rates; 6-string Sweep Morph Link vs round(v*7)) all exist because no test pairs the two sides.
findings.consequence: Host 'reset to default' puts Band Count at 1 and Oversample at 1x. Host-displayed values disagree with the audio, e.g. sweep frequency default 1000 Hz is heard as ~28 Hz. None of this can go red.
findings.suggested_fix: Add TEST_CASE "Disrumpo parameters start on their registered default" calling parametersStartingOffTheirDefault(controller) with REQUIRE(mismatches.empty()). Add TEST_CASE "Registered plain value matches processor denormalization": for each continuous param, take norm n in {0, 0.25, 0.5, 1}, send it through processParameterChanges, read the processor value via a getter, and REQUIRE it is within 1% of controller param->toPlain(n). Start with sweep frequency, crossovers, LFO rates and morph link.
findings.evidence: parameter_registration.cpp:76 `bandCountParam->setNormalized(1.0);  // Default to index 3`; :90 `oversampleParam->setNormalized(2.0 / 3.0);`; grep shows parametersStartingOffTheirDefault used in profundum/ruinae/seraphis/vorago editor_lifecycle_test.cpp and absent from plugins/disrumpo/tests
verifier_notes:
I checked every claim against the source and none of it is wrong.

1. **The probe is missing from Disrumpo.** Grepping plugins/ for parametersStartingOffTheirDefault or registered_defaults_probe finds it in Gradus (editor_lifecycle_test.cpp:61), Vorago (:300), Iterum (editor_open_close_test.cpp:61), Profundum (:455), Seraphis (:498) and Ruinae (:57). There is nothing under plugins/disrumpo/tests. plugins/disrumpo/tests/unit/controller/editor_lifecycle_test.cpp has only two cases: the UAF cycle and the shared-views count. It does not include the probe header.

2. **No Disrumpo test reads a registered Parameter.** Grepping plugins/disrumpo/tests for getParameterObject, registerAllParameters or toPlain matches only unit/display_format_test.cpp. Nothing pairs a controller toPlain with the processor's denormalization.

3. **The probe would go red on Band Count and Oversample Max.** The probe (tests/test_helpers/registered_defaults_probe.h:33-35) compares getParamNormalized(id) with info.defaultNormalizedValue. The SDK's StringListParameter constructor (extern/vst3sdk/public.sdk/source/vst/vstparameters.cpp:235) sets info.defaultNormalizedValue = 0. parameter_registration.cpp:76 then calls setNormalized(1.0) and :90 calls setNormalized(2.0/3.0), and neither touches defaultNormalizedValue. No file in plugins/disrumpo/src writes defaultNormalizedValue (the grep is empty). So a host's reset-to-default goes to normalized 0, which is Band Count 1 and Oversample 1x, while a fresh instance starts at 4 bands and 4x.

4. **Sweep frequency disagrees between the two sides.** parameter_registration.cpp:183-189 registers a linear RangeParameter over 20-20000 Hz with default 1000, so the default normalized value is 980/19980 = 0.049. processor_params.cpp:378-388 maps the value on a log2 scale: 2^(4.3219 + 0.049 × 9.9658) is about 28 Hz. The host shows 1000 Hz while the processor runs at about 28 Hz.

I did not check every item of the claimed 40-mismatch inventory. Even so, the test gap is real, and the problems it lets through are real and reachable.

I could not refute it. Each part of the claim checks out against the source.

(1) Probe missing. plugins/disrumpo/tests/unit/controller/editor_lifecycle_test.cpp has two TEST_CASEs only, at lines 14 and 32: the UAF lifecycle case and the shared-views count. A grep for parametersStartingOffTheirDefault returns tests/test_helpers/registered_defaults_probe.h plus the lifecycle tests of vorago, seraphis, ruinae, profundum, iterum (editor_open_close_test.cpp) and gradus. Nothing under plugins/disrumpo matches. The probe's header comment (registered_defaults_probe.h:12) says "Each plugin's controller lifecycle test lists the disagreements and requires none", so leaving it out is not an intentional exception for Disrumpo.

(2) The probe would catch a real problem. In parameter_registration.cpp, Band Count calls setNormalized(1.0) at :76 and Oversample Max calls setNormalized(2.0/3.0) at :90. Both are StringListParameters, and the SDK constructor leaves ParameterInfo.defaultNormalizedValue at 0. A grep for defaultNormalizedValue or setDefault in plugins/disrumpo/src finds nothing, so no code fixes the default afterwards. Host "reset to default" therefore goes to index 0 ("1" band, "1x").

(3) Nothing pairs registration with the processor. Grepping disrumpo tests for getParameterObject, getParameterInfo, getParameterCount and toPlain finds only display_format_test.cpp, and that file simulates toPlain by hand at :56. Sweep Frequency is registered as a linear RangeParameter(20, 20000, default 1000) at parameter_registration.cpp:182-190. The processor maps it on a log2 scale at processor_params.cpp:378-386, and the controller's own SweepIndicator uses log2 too (controller.cpp:1280-1285). The registered default normalizes to (1000-20)/19980 ≈ 0.049, and the log2 map turns that into 2^(4.32 + 0.049*9.966) ≈ 28 Hz. Host-displayed plain values disagree with what the audio does, and no test can go red on it.

No spec or code comment calls either mismatch a deliberate design decision. Severity stays medium: this is a test gap, and it hides real but non-crashing defaults and display mismatches.

I confirmed the finding against the source; none of it is refuted.

(1) The test gap is real. In plugins/disrumpo/tests/unit/controller/editor_lifecycle_test.cpp:1-47 there are only two cases: the UAF lifecycle case and the shared-views case. Neither includes registered_defaults_probe.h. A grep for parametersStartingOffTheirDefault finds it in the lifecycle/open-close tests of vorago:300, iterum:61, gradus:61, seraphis:498, ruinae:57 and profundum:455, and nowhere in Disrumpo. A grep for getParameterObject/getParameterInfo/defaultNormalizedValue under plugins/disrumpo hits only src/ and no test file.

(2) The probe would go red. The StringListParameter constructor sets info.defaultNormalizedValue = 0 (extern/vst3sdk/public.sdk/source/vst/vstparameters.cpp:235). parameter_registration.cpp:76 then calls setNormalized(1.0) for Band Count and :90 calls setNormalized(2.0/3.0) for Oversample Max. Nothing in Disrumpo writes defaultNormalizedValue afterwards. The probe (tests/test_helpers/registered_defaults_probe.h:33-35) compares getParamNormalized with info.defaultNormalizedValue, so it would report both. When a host resets to the registered default it sends normalized 0, which means Band Count "1" and Oversample "1x" instead of "4" and "4x".

(3) The mapping mismatch the second suggested test would catch is real. parameter_registration.cpp:183-187 registers Sweep Frequency as a linear RangeParameter(20, 20000, default 1000). Its registered default normalizes to (1000-20)/19980 = 0.04905. processor_params.cpp:381-385 maps normalized values to Hz as 2^(log2(20) + n*log2(1000)). For n = 0.04905 that is 2^(4.3219 + 0.04905*9.9658) = 2^4.810, about 28 Hz, as the finding says. Controller::getParamStringByValue (controller.cpp:747-893) has no sweep or frequency handling and falls through to the base class, so the host display stays linear. A normalized 0.5 shows as 10010 Hz but sounds at about 632 Hz.

Medium severity fits a test gap that hides several real, user-audible default and display defects in every host.

findings.title: Keyboard, global-control and visibility tests are tautologies, and two of them pin an obsolete 8-band /7 mapping
findings.problem: global_controls_test and visibility_test define lambdas such as `index / 7.0f` and `round(n*7)+1` and assert the lambdas' own arithmetic (e.g. 'Normalized 1.0 gives band count 8'). keyboard_shortcut_test.cpp:20-146 increments local ints (`focusedBandIndex++`) and asserts `REQUIRE(fineStep == 0.01f)` after assigning 0.01f, without ever constructing KeyboardShortcutHandler. band_strip_test.cpp:140-162 asserts a local string array against itself, never against getTypeName or the menu, and that array's order 14-25 differs from the enum.
findings.why_wrong: The real Band Count is a 4-entry list with normalization k/3, and visibility uses threshold (b-0.5)/3 (controller.cpp:171, 1362). The tests encode the old 8-band design and would stay green whatever the controller does. A test that never calls production code verifies nothing.
findings.consequence: Real defects in this area have no coverage: KeyboardShortcutHandler::setActiveBandCount has no caller, the frame hook swallows arrows and Space typed into the preset-name field, and visibility thresholds could be wrong. The stale tests also tell maintainers the plugin has 8 bands.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace them with tests that call production objects. Construct KeyboardShortcutHandler with a stub frame, send a Tab VstKeyCode and REQUIRE the band focus advance; send an arrow key while a CTextEdit is focused and REQUIRE handled == false. For visibility, instantiate ContainerVisibilityController with the real Band Count StringListParameter from registerAllParameters and REQUIRE band b visible iff count > b for counts 1-4. For band_strip_test, compare against getTypeName(static_cast<DistortionType>(i)) and the registered NodeType list strings.
findings.evidence: global_controls_test.cpp:68-71 `int index = static_cast<int>(std::round(normalized * 7.0f)); return index + 1;` and :82-84 `REQUIRE(normalizedToBandCount(1.0f) == 8);`; controller.cpp:1362 `float threshold = (static_cast<float>(b) - 0.5f) / 3.0f;`; keyboard_shortcut_test.cpp:91-94 `float fineStep = 0.01f; REQUIRE(fineStep == 0.01f);`
verifier_notes:
I could not refute this. The core claim holds in source.

1. global_controls_test.cpp:25-58 divides local ints by 7.0f and checks the result against itself. :68-71 is a lambda `round(normalized*7)+1`, and :81-83 asserts `normalizedToBandCount(1.0f) == 8`. :118-120 and :155-159 are lambda thresholds `b/7.0f`. The only production code it touches is makeGlobalParamId / isGlobalParamId (:94-108, :199-229), which is the param-ID encoding, not the band-count mapping or visibility.

2. visibility_test.cpp:26-66, 77-95, 106-142, 152-158, 205-209 and 276-279 all use local `/7.0f` arithmetic. Its only include is plugin_ids.h (:16), and it never builds a ContainerVisibilityController.

3. Production uses 4 bands, not 8:
- parameter_registration.cpp:67-75 registers Band Count as a list parameter with strings 1..4, so normalization is k/3.
- controller.cpp:171 normalizes with `(clampedCount-1)/3.0f`.
- controller.cpp:1362 sets the threshold to `(b-0.5f)/3.0f`.
So these tests pin a stale 8-band /7 design and would stay green whatever the controller does.

4. keyboard_shortcut_test.cpp:20-62 increments and decrements a local `focusedBandIndex`. :93 and :98 assert step constants against literals assigned just before. :136 and :141 pin a 1/7 step. Its only include is plugin_ids.h (:12), so KeyboardShortcutHandler is never constructed.

5. band_strip_test.cpp:29 defines a local `kCanonicalDistortionTypes` array, and :135-162 asserts that array against string literals. getTypeName is never called. The array puts "Allpass Resonant" at index 25, but the enum in distortion_types.h:32-63 has AllpassResonant at index 19 (SoftClip=0 … Quantize=13, Aliasing=14, BitwiseMangler=15, Temporal=16, RingSaturation=17, FeedbackDist=18, AllpassResonant=19). So the order does differ from the enum.

6. The only hits for KeyboardShortcutHandler::setActiveBandCount are its definition (keyboard_shortcut_handler.cpp:58) and declaration (.h:41). It has no caller in src or tests.

I did not verify the side claim that the frame hook swallows arrow keys typed into the preset-name field. The test-gap finding stands without it. Medium severity fits: these are tests that cannot fail, they encode a wrong band count, and the code they appear to cover is effectively untested. No production behaviour is wrong because of them.

I read the code and the finding holds. No guard, design note or other test makes these tests meaningful.
- global_controls_test.cpp:25-58 divides a local segmentIndex by 7.0f and checks the result against the same expression. The lambda at :68-71 is `round(normalized*7)+1`, and :81-83 asserts `normalizedToBandCount(1.0f) == 8`. :118-120 and :155-159 build their own b/7 threshold lambdas. The only parts that call production code are the ID-encoding cases at :94-108 and :199-229.
- The production controller uses a 4-entry mapping instead: controller.cpp:171 `(clampedCount - 1) / 3.0f`, :1362 `threshold = (b - 0.5f) / 3.0f` and :1716 `* 3.0f`. So the 8-band /7 model in the tests is out of date. It is not a deliberate alternative.
- visibility_test.cpp:26-36, 77-95, 106-142, 152-158, 205-209 and 276-279 all build local /7.0f thresholds. None of them constructs ContainerVisibilityController, even though the test case at :106 is named after it.
- keyboard_shortcut_test.cpp:20-142 never includes or constructs KeyboardShortcutHandler. It increments local ints, and :91-98 assigns `fineStep = 0.01f` and then requires it to equal 0.01f. :133 still says "Band Count has 8 values". A search of plugins/disrumpo/tests finds KeyboardShortcutHandler only in that file's header comment, so no other test covers the handler.
- band_strip_test.cpp:137-165 checks the local kCanonicalDistortionTypes array against itself. Its order does not match the enum: distortion_types.h:32-63 puts AllpassResonant at index 23 (after RingSaturation and FeedbackDist), but the test expects "Allpass Resonant" at [25] and "Fractal" at [23].
These are plain tautologies: they would stay green whatever the controller does. Nothing in the code or specs marks them as intentional.

Severity stays medium. The defect is a test-only gap with no runtime effect, but it leaves the band-count visibility and keyboard handling with no real coverage, and the tests describe an 8-band plugin that no longer exists.

I read every file the claim depends on, and it holds. global_controls_test.cpp:25-58 computes `segmentIndex / 7.0f` locally and asserts that result. :68-88 defines the lambda `round(normalized*7)+1` and asserts `normalizedToBandCount(1.0f) == 8`. :118-193 defines threshold lambdas `b/7.0f` and asserts their own output. The file includes only plugin_ids.h (line 17), so it never touches the controller. visibility_test.cpp has the same `/ 7.0f` lambdas (lines 36, 83, 157, 208, 278) and includes only catch2 and plugin_ids.h (lines 13-18). It never constructs ContainerVisibilityController, although its header says so (line 5) and a case is named after it (line 106). keyboard_shortcut_test.cpp:20-62 increments local ints; :91-94 assigns `fineStep = 0.01f` and then REQUIREs that it equals 0.01f; :133-141 uses stepCount 7 ("Band Count has 8 values"). It includes only plugin_ids.h (line 12) and never builds a KeyboardShortcutHandler. band_strip_test.cpp:130-163 compares the local kCanonicalDistortionTypes array with literals. The production code uses a different, 4-band mapping: parameter_registration.cpp:64-75 registers Band Count as a 4-entry StringListParameter, controller.cpp:171 normalizes with `(count-1)/3.0f`, controller.h:328 has kMaxBands = 4, and controller.cpp:1362 sets the visibility threshold to `(b-0.5)/3.0f`. None of these tests would fail if that production logic changed. The consequence is also real. The only occurrences of KeyboardShortcutHandler::setActiveBandCount are its definition (keyboard_shortcut_handler.cpp:58) and its declaration (.h:41), so nothing in src calls it. activeBandCount_ is fixed at construction (cpp:20) and bounds Tab cycling (cpp:107-118), so a coverage gap hides a live controller defect. Severity stays at medium. There is no audio or runtime harm, only false coverage plus stale 8-band documentation in the tests. That fits a medium test-gap because it masks at least one real, untested controller defect.

findings.title: Crossover tests pin the missing spacing rule, measure band-count changes only after settling on DC, and never load state into an instance with fewer bands
findings.problem: 'CrossoverNetwork minimum spacing constraint' sets crossovers at 1000 and 1200 Hz (0.26 octave) and REQUIREs that 1200 is kept, so the test asserts the violation of FR-BAND-002 (>= 0.5 octave, kMinCrossoverSpacingOctaves in band_state.h:69). IT-003 'Band count change maintains output stability' (band_management_integration_test.cpp:137-176) uses DC input and measures only after 4000 settle samples, so the switch transient is never observed. DC sums to 1 for any LR4 topology, so the assertion cannot fail. No test calls Processor::setState on an instance whose current band count is lower than the stream's. In that case setCrossoverFrequency silently drops index >= numBands_-1 (crossover_network.h:127-129) because processor_state.cpp:446-458 sets crossovers before setBandCount (:461-462).
findings.why_wrong: These are the riskiest crossover behaviours: ordering, spacing, a mid-stream band-count change and a load-order dependency. The tests either assert the wrong behaviour or measure where the defect cannot appear. Every serialization test starts from a fresh 4-band processor (kDefaultBands = 4), so the drop never triggers.
findings.consequence: Loading a 4-band project into an instance set to 2 bands replaces the saved crossovers 2-3 with log midpoints. Band-count automation clicks. Crossover automation can cross adjacent frequencies and break reconstruction. All of this is unobserved.
findings.suggested_fix: (1) Change the spacing test to REQUIRE f1 >= f0*2^0.5, or record a spec ruling that spacing is not enforced. (2) Add TEST_CASE "Band count 4->3 switch is click-free" with a 1 kHz sine through Processor: send kBandCountId mid-render and REQUIRE max |y[n]-y[n-1]| near the switch < 2x the steady-state maximum. (3) Add TEST_CASE "setState restores crossovers when current band count is lower": set band count 2 via params, setState with a 4-band stream at 200/1500/6000 Hz, then getState and REQUIRE all three frequencies within 1 Hz.
findings.evidence: crossover_network_test.cpp:415-416 `network.setCrossoverFrequency(1, 1200.0f); REQUIRE_THAT(network.getCrossoverFrequency(1), WithinAbs(1200.0f, 0.01f));`; crossover_network.h:127-129 `if (index < 0 || index >= numBands_ - 1) { return; }`; processor_state.cpp:452-462 setCrossoverFrequency loop, then `crossoverL_.setBandCount(bandCount);`
verifier_notes:
I could not refute the finding. Every point checks out against the source.

(1) The spacing test at crossover_network_test.cpp:402-417 sets crossover 0 to 1000 Hz and crossover 1 to 1200 Hz, then REQUIREs that 1200 Hz is kept. The comment at :412-414 says this is deliberate ("no automatic clamping", "spec ... doesn't require automatic enforcement"). That part is a missing spec ruling rather than a hidden bug. Still, the test pins behaviour that contradicts kMinCrossoverSpacingOctaves = 0.5f (band_state.h:69).

(2) IT-003 at band_management_integration_test.cpp:137-172 feeds DC (1.0f), lets the filters settle for 4000 samples, calls setBandCount(3), settles another 4000 samples, and only then sums the bands. The switch transient is never observed. Settled DC through the LP/HP/allpass cascade sums to about 1 for any band count, so the assertions at :170-171 cannot catch a click.

(3) The load-order defect is real:
- processor_state.cpp:450-459 calls crossoverL_/R_.setCrossoverFrequency(c, freq) for c = 0..2 BEFORE crossoverL_/R_.setBandCount(bandCount) at :462-463.
- crossover_network.h:127-129 returns early when index >= numBands_ - 1, so with a current count of 2, indices 1 and 2 are dropped without any signal.
- setBandCount(4) then runs redistributeCrossovers -> redistributeIncreasing (:287-290, :301-364), which keeps the existing crossover 0 and fills the gaps with logMidpoint values (:353).
- Nothing else re-applies the saved values. The processor's crossoverFrequencies_ atomic (processor.h:179) is never written in setState. getState reads crossoverL_.getCrossoverFrequency (processor_state.cpp:76), so the loss persists into the next save.
- In processor_params.cpp, setBandCount is at :344 and setCrossoverFrequency at :992. That is the same ordering hazard for a parameter flush.

(4) The test gap is real. Every setState caller I checked builds a fresh processor first: factory_preset_validation_test.cpp:159/183/200/325 and serialization_round_trip_test.cpp:479/487/807. kDefaultBands = 4 (band_state.h:62), so the drop path never runs in any test.

Part (1), the spacing test, is a documented design decision and not a defect. The test comment at crossover_network_test.cpp:412-414 says the DSP accepts manual frequencies as-is ("spec mentions spacing constraint but doesn't require automatic enforcement"). The 0.5-octave rule is enforced in the UI divider drag instead, and crossover_interaction_test.cpp:155-176 ("Divider movement respects minimum octave spacing", T095) pins that. So the test does not assert a spec violation; it pins the intended split between the DSP and the UI.

The other two parts are confirmed from source:
- IT-003 (band_management_integration_test.cpp:137-172) feeds only DC (1.0f). It settles for 4000 samples before and after setBandCount(3) and checks only that the band sum is near 1.0. It never looks at the transient, and DC sums to unity for any LR4 cascade, so the test cannot fail on a click.
- The load-order dependency is real. processor_state.cpp:413 stores bandCount_ (the atomic) but does not update the crossover networks. At :450-457 it calls crossoverL_/R_.setCrossoverFrequency(c, freq) while the networks still have their old numBands_. crossover_network.h:127-129 returns early when index >= numBands_-1, so with a current count of 2, indices 1 and 2 are dropped. Then at :462-463 setBandCount(4) runs redistributeIncreasing (crossover_network.h:287-290, 301+), which inserts log midpoints instead of the saved values.
- Nothing guards this elsewhere: processor_params.cpp:343-345 is the only other setBandCount caller.
- No test exercises it: no test uses kBandCountId, and every processor in serialization_round_trip_test.cpp comes from createTestProcessor() (:48) at the default 4 bands.

The test gap therefore covers a reachable state-load defect: loading a 4-band preset into a running instance set to 2 bands. Medium severity stands, even though the spacing sub-claim is refuted on context.

All three parts check out in the source, and the defect the missing tests would catch is real.
(1) crossover_network_test.cpp:402-417 sets 1000 Hz and then 1200 Hz (log2(1.2)=0.26 oct) and REQUIREs that 1200 is kept (line 416). Its own comment (412-414) says spacing is not enforced. band_state.h:69 defines kMinCrossoverSpacingOctaves = 0.5f, and nothing in src uses it, so the test locks in the missing rule.
(2) band_management_integration_test.cpp:137-172 (IT-003) runs a CrossoverNetwork alone (not the Processor) on a constant 1.0f input. It settles 4000 samples before and after setBandCount(3) and only checks |sum-1|<0.1. The switch transient is never sampled, and a settled LR4+allpass sum of DC is 1 for any topology, so the test cannot fail.
(3) The setState drop is real. crossover_network.h:127-129 returns early when index >= numBands_-1. processor_state.cpp:450-459 calls setCrossoverFrequency for c=0..2 BEFORE setBandCount(bandCount) at :462-463. If the running instance has 2 bands (processor_params.cpp:339-345 calls crossoverL_.setBandCount on a kBandCountId change), crossovers 1-2 are dropped. setBandCount(4) then goes through redistributeIncreasing (crossover_network.h:301-365), which puts log midpoints of the largest gaps in their place. If the instance had 1 band, all three saved crossovers are dropped and initializeLogarithmicDistribution (:280-283) replaces them.
Impact: the drop does not hit a fresh project load, because a new instance starts at 4 bands. It does hit a host-side .vstpreset or state load into a running instance with fewer bands. The controller's setComponentState then shows the saved crossovers while the processor runs the midpoints. getState (processor_state.cpp:76 reads crossoverL_.getCrossoverFrequency) writes the wrong values back, so the corruption persists on the next save. The audible effect is band edges moved by up to an octave or more, which changes the distortion character per band. It is not a crash or NaN.
No test calls Processor::setState after changing band count: setBandCount/kBandCountId appear only in the two DSP-level test files above. Medium severity fits a test gap that hides a real, user-reachable state-restore bug. No adjustment.

findings.title: Latency tests cannot fail (static return 0) and carry [performance], so per-push lanes skip them; real wet-path latency is never measured
findings.problem: 'getLatency returns 0 (IIR mode)' (SC-012), 'uses ZeroLatency oversampling mode' (FR-018), 'latency does not change when factors change' and 'end-to-end latency does not exceed 10ms' (SC-004) all assert BandProcessor::getLatency(), a `static ... return 0;` (band_processor.h:376-379). They carry the [performance] tag, which CI and run-gate.js exclude, although none of them is a timing test. No test measures the wet path's actual delay: Spectral outputs zero for fftSize samples, FeedbackDistortion returns only the delayed path, and Granular reads from the past. No test compares an impulse's peak position across bands or against the dry path.
findings.why_wrong: A latency test has to measure an impulse response. Asserting a constant only re-states the claim. Tagging correctness cases [performance] also moves them into the isolated CPU lane, so they do not run per push.
findings.consequence: Unreported and uncompensated latency (Spectral fftSize at the 8x-prepared rate, 1-100 ms feedback delay) comb-filters against the dry path at mix < 100% and smears phase between bands. The latency claims stay green.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove [performance] from the four correctness cases. Add TEST_CASE "Per-band wet latency matches reported latency" in processor_audio_output_test.cpp. For each of SoftClip, Spectral, FeedbackDist and Granular at mix 1: send an impulse through Processor::process, find the peak index of the output, and REQUIRE it equals the processor's reported latency (once getLatencySamples exists) and is equal across bands.
findings.evidence: band_processor.h:376-379 `[[nodiscard]] static int getLatency() noexcept { return 0; }`; oversampling_performance_tests.cpp:33 tags `"[oversampling][performance][SC-012]"`, :67 `[FR-018]`, :105 `[latency-stability]`, :254 `[SC-004]`

findings.title: Sweep LFO, envelope and modulation 'audio path' tests run the components directly; the processor's once-per-block calls are never tested
findings.problem: sweep_lfo_tests.cpp:150-190 checks rate by calling SweepLFO::process() once per sample, with zero-crossing margins of +/-1 (Approx(2).margin(1), i.e. 50%). Processor::process calls sweepLFO_.process() once per block and feeds the envelope follower one sample per block (processor.cpp:340-351). modulation_audio_path_test, despite its name and FR-093 tag, only drives a standalone Krate::DSP::ModulationEngine and getModulatedValue. It never constructs a Processor or BandProcessor and never measures audio.
findings.why_wrong: The suite verifies each part, not how the processor clocks them. At 512-sample blocks the sweep LFO advances at 1/512 of its nominal rate, and the envelope follower sees 1 of every 512 samples. A per-sample unit test cannot see this.
findings.consequence: A 1 Hz sweep LFO actually cycles about every 8.5 minutes at 512-sample blocks, its rate changes with host buffer size, and the envelope sweep barely follows the input. All green.
findings.suggested_fix: Add TEST_CASE "Processor sweep LFO rate is independent of block size" in sweep_band_intensity_test.cpp. Enable sweep and sweep LFO at 2 Hz, render 2 s through Processor at block sizes 64 and 512, and read kSweepModulatedFrequencyOutputId from outputParameterChanges. REQUIRE 4 +/- 0.25 cycles at both sizes. Add a processor-level routing test: an LFO1->band0 gain routing set through params, with output block RMS varying by > 6 dB over 1 s.
findings.evidence: processor.cpp:340-342 `float inputMono = (inputL[0] + inputR[0]) * 0.5f; (void)sweepEnvelope_.processSample(inputMono);`; :349-350 `if (sweepLFO_.isEnabled()) { float lfoValue = sweepLFO_.process();` (once per block); sweep_lfo_tests.cpp:170 `REQUIRE(zeroCrossings == Approx(2).margin(1));`; modulation_audio_path_test.cpp:33-34 `ModulationEngine engine; engine.prepare(...)` with no Processor.
verifier_notes:
I could not refute this. Every part of the claim matches the source.

1. **The processor clocks both modulators once per block.** In plugins/disrumpo/src/processor/processor.cpp:
   - Lines 340-343 call `sweepEnvelope_.processSample(inputMono)` once per process() call, and `inputMono` is built from `inputL[0]` / `inputR[0]` only.
   - Lines 349-350 call `sweepLFO_.process()` once per process() call.
   - Lines 368-370 then hand the one resulting frequency to `sweepProcessor_.setCenterFrequency` and `processBlock(numSamples)`.
   - No per-sample loop or advance-by-N exists anywhere in this path.

2. **Both components assume they are called once per sample.**
   - SweepLFO::process() at plugins/disrumpo/src/dsp/sweep_lfo.h:201-206 returns `lfo_.process() * depth_`.
   - Krate::DSP::LFO::process() at dsp/include/krate/dsp/primitives/lfo.h:113-114 is documented "Generate one sample of LFO output" and steps its phase accumulator by one sample per call. At 512-sample blocks the effective rate is therefore nominal/512, and it changes with host buffer size.
   - SweepEnvelope::processSample at sweep_envelope.h:187-193 likewise advances the follower by one sample per call, so it sees 1 of every N input samples.

3. **The existing tests do not exercise the processor's clocking.**
   - sweep_lfo_tests.cpp:151-191 calls `lfo.process()` once per sample for 44100 samples, with `REQUIRE(zeroCrossings == Approx(2).margin(1))` at line 170 and `Approx(4).margin(1)` at line 190.
   - modulation_audio_path_test.cpp:32-77 only constructs `ModulationEngine` and reads `getModulatedValue`. It includes band_processor.h but never instantiates a Processor or a BandProcessor, and never measures audio.
   - sweep_band_intensity_test.cpp drives `SweepProcessor` and `BandProcessor` directly. Grep over plugins/disrumpo/tests finds no use of `kSweepLFO*`, `kSweepEnv*` or `kSweepModulatedFrequencyOutputId`, so no processor-level test enables the sweep LFO or envelope.

The test gap is real, and it hides a real, reachable defect: block-rate clocking of a per-sample LFO and envelope follower. I left the severity at medium because the finding is classed as a test gap. The underlying runtime bug may deserve its own, higher-severity finding.

I could not refute it. Nothing guards the gap: no test pins the behaviour, no code compensates for it, and no comment documents it as intended.

(1) processor.cpp:340-343 feeds the envelope follower exactly one sample per block: `float inputMono = (inputL[0] + inputR[0]) * 0.5f; (void)sweepEnvelope_.processSample(inputMono);`. processor.cpp:349-350 calls `sweepLFO_.process()` once per block.

(2) sweep_lfo.h:199-206 documents process() as "Process one sample of LFO output" and returns `lfo_.process() * depth_`. sweep_lfo.h:80-83 prepares the LFO at the audio sample rate (`lfo_.prepare(sampleRate)`), not at the block rate. Nothing upstream scales the rate by numSamples, so the LFO really does advance by 1/blockSize of its nominal rate.

(3) modulation_audio_path_test.cpp:13-16 includes only modulation_engine.h and band_processor.h. All four TEST_CASEs (lines 32-186) construct a standalone `ModulationEngine` and only read getModulatedValue/getModulationOffset. None builds a Processor or BandProcessor, and none renders audio, despite the FR-093 "audio path" header.

(4) Grepping plugins/disrumpo/tests for sweepLFO|SweepLFO|kSweepLFO|kSweepModulatedFrequencyOutputId|LFORate matches only tests/dsp/sweep_lfo_tests.cpp, which exercises the component on its own. No processor-level test covers how the sweep LFO or envelope is clocked, or the kSweepModulatedFrequencyOutputId output.

The processor comment at processor.cpp:333-337 ("FR-007: Process sweep smoother for the entire block") does not justify one LFO tick per block. The gap is real and it hides a real block-size-dependent rate bug. Severity stays medium for the test-gap finding itself; the bug it hides should be reported as its own correctness finding.

I could not refute this. Every part of it checks out in the source.

(1) The processor clocks both sweep sources once per block. processor.cpp:340-343 calls sweepEnvelope_.processSample(inputMono) once, using only sample 0 (inputL[0], inputR[0]). processor.cpp:349-350 calls sweepLFO_.process() once per process() call.

(2) Each of those calls advances the LFO by exactly one sample's worth of phase. SweepLFO::process (sweep_lfo.h:201-206) returns lfo_.process()*depth_. Krate::DSP::LFO::process (dsp/include/krate/dsp/primitives/lfo.h:114-173) advances phaseAcc_ once per call (line 159), and the LFO was prepared at the audio sample rate (sweep_lfo.h:80-84, processor.cpp:135). At 44.1 kHz with 512-sample blocks, a 1 Hz LFO therefore needs 44100 calls, which is 44100 blocks, about 512 s (8.5 min) per cycle. The effective rate is rate/blockSize, so it depends on the host buffer size, exactly as claimed.

(3) The envelope has the same problem. SweepEnvelope::processSample (sweep_envelope.h:187-194) feeds an EnvelopeFollower prepared at the sample rate (line 87-92). One sample per block stretches the attack/release time constants by the block size: a 10 ms attack becomes about 5 s at 512. The follower also sees only 1 of every 512 samples.

(4) Nothing tests the processor-level path. modulation_audio_path_test.cpp:32-77 builds only a standalone ModulationEngine and reads getModulatedValue. It includes band_processor.h but never constructs a Processor or BandProcessor and never measures audio. sweep_lfo_tests.cpp:151-190 calls lfo.process() once per sample with Approx(2).margin(1) and Approx(4).margin(1). I searched plugins/disrumpo/tests for SweepParamType::kSweepLFO*, kSweepEnv*, kSweepLFOEnable, kSweepEnvEnable and kSweepModulatedFrequencyOutputId. Nothing matched. The only hits for SweepLFO/SweepEnv are the two per-sample unit test files, sweep_lfo_tests.cpp and sweep_envelope_tests.cpp.

Impact: the gap hides a real defect that makes the feature effectively unusable. At typical buffers (256-1024) the sweep LFO is close to frozen, and the envelope sweep barely follows the input. The whole suite stays green. One part of the finding overreaches: ModulationEngine::process receives numSamples, so the ModulationEngine routing path is probably correctly clocked, and missing processor coverage there is a smaller issue. As a test-gap finding, medium severity fits. The underlying clocking bug itself deserves a higher severity, but that belongs to a separate signal-path finding.

findings.title: Assertions that cannot fail: REQUIRE(true) smoothing cases, an ignored truncated-stream result, and a 'real-time safety' case with no allocation tracking that never reaches the allocating path
findings.problem: 'BandProcessor morph smoothing time configurable' has both sections end in REQUIRE(true), with no timing or level check. serialization_round_trip_test.cpp:660-689 'truncated stream loads partial data' does `(void)result;` and checks only that getState still works, so nothing is verified as loaded. distortion_adapter_test.cpp:1907-1965 'UT-DI-008: Real-time safety' only calls setType and process, so it never reaches setParams, where spectral_.prepare re-allocates whenever p.fftSize != getFftSize() (distortion_adapter.cpp:894-896). That mismatch always holds at first use: prepare passes maxBlockSize*8 as the FFT size (:84). The case also does not use tests/test_helpers/allocation_detector.h, which other plugins use, and ends in CHECK(true).
findings.why_wrong: Each of these cases is named for a property it does not check. An allocation detector exists in the repo, so the real-time claim can be asserted, and the allocating path should be exercised.
findings.consequence: A real-time violation, allocation inside processParameterChanges -> setMorphNodes -> setParams on the audio thread, and any smoothing regression pass silently.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace REQUIRE(true) with a measured check: the cursor-weight midpoint is crossed in the expected window for 5 ms / 200 ms, scaled by host rate. In UT-DI-008, wrap setParams + process for all 26 types (Spectral with fftSize 1024/2048/4096) in the allocation detector and REQUIRE zero allocations. It fails today on the Spectral re-prepare. In the truncated test, truncate after the band count and REQUIRE that inputGain is applied and the bands keep their defaults.
findings.evidence: morph_band_integration_test.cpp:270-271 `// No crash or artifacts expected  REQUIRE(true);`; serialization_round_trip_test.cpp:684 `(void)result;`; distortion_adapter_test.cpp:1937 `CHECK(true);  // If we got here, no crashes occurred`; distortion_adapter.cpp:894-896 `if (static_cast<std::size_t>(p.fftSize) != spectral_.getFftSize()) { spectral_.prepare(sampleRate_, static_cast<std::size_t>(p.fftSize)); }`
verifier_notes:
I checked each of the three claims against the source, and all three hold.

(1) morph_band_integration_test.cpp:248-290, 'BandProcessor morph smoothing time configurable': both SECTIONs (5 ms at 257-272, 200 ms at 274-289) call setMorphPosition, run a process loop on throwaway locals, and end in `REQUIRE(true);` (lines 271 and 288). Nothing measures timing, level or cursor progress, so any smoothing regression passes.

(2) The truncated-stream case is at plugins/disrumpo/tests/unit/preset/serialization_round_trip_test.cpp:660-685. The finding's path leaves out the `preset/` folder. It writes the version plus inputGain only, calls setState, discards the result with `(void)result;` at :680, and asserts only `getState == kResultOk` at :684. Nothing checks that anything was loaded or that defaults survived.

(3) distortion_adapter_test.cpp:1907-1965, UT-DI-008: it only calls prepare, setCommonParams, setType and process, never setParams. It ends in `CHECK(true);` at :1937, and its own comment at :1961-1964 says no allocation tracking is done. tests/test_helpers/allocation_detector.h exists in the repo.

The allocating path is real. distortion_adapter.cpp:894-896 calls `spectral_.prepare(sampleRate_, p.fftSize)` from routeParamsToProcessor whenever p.fftSize != getFftSize(). That prepare (spectral_distortion.h:145-169) re-prepares the STFT, the overlap-add and the spectrum buffers; the class holds std::vector members (:1086-1092), so this allocates. The finding says prepare passes maxBlockSize*8 at :84. Line 84 itself passes maxBlockSize, but band_processor.h:111-112 and 124-125 call distortion_.prepare and morphEngine_->prepare with `maxBlockSize_ * kMaxOversampleFactor`. So the spectral FFT size starts at (host block x 8), clamped to [256, 8192]: 4096 for a 512-sample block, against the default params fftSize of 2048 (distortion_adapter.h:179). That is a mismatch.

MorphEngine::prepare (morph_engine.cpp:63-66) calls setParams after prepare. This fixes the mismatch off the audio thread only for nodes that are already Spectral. routeParamsToProcessor switches on currentType_ (:601), so a node switched to Spectral later, or an fftSize change, re-prepares inside setNodes or setParams (morph_engine.cpp:136-139, 736; band_processor.h:231, 450, 460) during processing. So the suggested allocation-tracked test would plausibly fail today.

The finding's minor citation slips (the missing preset/ subfolder, the :84 attribution) do not change any claim. Severity stays low because these are coverage gaps, not shipped defects.

Confirmed from source. morph_band_integration_test.cpp:257-289: both SECTIONs of "BandProcessor morph smoothing time configurable" run the processor and then assert only REQUIRE(true) at lines 271 and 288. They make no timing or level check, so a smoothing regression cannot fail them. plugins/disrumpo/tests/unit/preset/serialization_round_trip_test.cpp:660-685 (the finding gives a slightly wrong path): the result goes to `(void)result;` at line 680, and the only assertion is that getState succeeds (line 684). Nothing checks that the truncated data was loaded or that defaults were kept. distortion_adapter_test.cpp:1907-1965 "UT-DI-008": it only calls prepare, setCommonParams, setType and process, ends with CHECK(true) at line 1937, and says in its comments (1908-1909, 1961-1964) that it does not track allocations. That comment is a documented limitation, not a guard. tests/test_helpers/allocation_detector.h exists in the repo, so the comment's premise ("would require custom allocators") is out of date. The allocating path the test never reaches is real. distortion_adapter.cpp:893-896 calls spectral_.prepare() when p.fftSize != getFftSize(). The code comment there admits "allocates, but only on user param change". spectral_distortion.h:172-185 resizes std::vectors inside prepare. setParams is reached from the audio thread: processor_params.cpp:899 and :954 call setMorphNodes; morph_engine.cpp:65, 138, 710 and 736 call setParams; band_processor.h:231 and 450 do too. Correction: distortion_adapter.cpp:84 passes maxBlockSize, not maxBlockSize*8. The mismatch still holds in practice, because the DistortionParams default fftSize is 2048 (distortion_adapter.h:179) and processor_params.cpp:244 maps it to 512-4096, while the host's block size is usually different. Also, morph_engine.cpp:606 weight-blends fftSize, which can produce sizes that are not powers of two. None of these gaps is guarded elsewhere, and no case pins the behaviour. Low severity is right for a test-gap finding: the real-time defect it hides is a separate finding.

Every vacuous assertion the finding names is in the code as quoted. In morph_band_integration_test.cpp:248-290 both SECTIONs end in `REQUIRE(true)` (271, 288) and check no level or timing. In tests/unit/preset/serialization_round_trip_test.cpp:660-686 (the finding's path drops `preset/`) the result is thrown away with `(void)result;`, and the only check is that getState returns kResultOk. In distortion_adapter_test.cpp:1907-1965, UT-DI-008 only calls setType and process and ends in `CHECK(true)`. Its own comment says allocation tracking was not done.

The real-time violation the test misses is real. With the current type set to Spectral, distortion_adapter.cpp:894-896 calls spectral_.prepare, and spectral_distortion.h:160-183 then resizes several std::vectors and re-prepares the STFT and overlap-add, which allocates. That setParams is reached on the audio thread every sample: morph_engine.cpp:710 calls `blendedAdapter_.setParams(bp)` inside processSameFamily, and morph_engine.cpp:736 calls the per-node adapters when modulation is active. It is also reached from processParameterChanges through setMorphNodes (processor_params.cpp:899/954). The mismatch is reached in practice. MorphEngine prepare (morph_engine.cpp:59-66) prepares adapters with the default SoftClip type, so setParams does not touch Spectral then, and DistortionAdapter::prepare:84 prepares spectral_ with maxBlockSize. A node switched to Spectral with the default fftSize of 2048 (distortion_adapter.h:179) therefore re-prepares on the audio thread unless the block size happens to round to 2048.

One detail in the finding is wrong: line 84 passes `maxBlockSize`, not `maxBlockSize*8`. This does not change the conclusion.

No Disrumpo test uses allocation_detector.h (grep of plugins/disrumpo/tests for allocation_detector or AllocationDetector finds nothing). The approval tests in morph_artifact_test.cpp do call setMorphSmoothingTime and check artifacts, which covers part of the smoothing gap. Impact is a test-coverage gap that hides an existing one-shot allocation on a parameter or type change. That is not a per-block audio defect in itself, so "low" is the right severity.

findings.title: DataExchange delivery test is [!mayfail] on every platform, including Windows where the pump works
findings.problem: The only end-to-end spectrum delivery case is tagged [!mayfail] unconditionally, and the comment justifies it with the missing macOS CFRunLoop pump. The project rule (CLAUDE.md 'Linux test harnesses have no run loop') is to gate such non-vacuity checks by platform, not to make them non-failing everywhere.
findings.why_wrong: [!mayfail] turns every failed REQUIRE into a pass. A Windows regression in the processor->controller spectrum pipeline (block sizing, the aligned_alloc rounding, editorClosing_ guard) can no longer go red anywhere.
findings.consequence: A spectrum display that silently goes dead would not be caught by CI.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop [!mayfail]. Wrap the delivery REQUIREs in `#if defined(_WIN32)` (or a platform check where a timer exists), and on the other platforms assert only that sendSpectrumBlock wrote the Tier-3 shared FIFO.
findings.evidence: data_exchange_spectrum_test.cpp:200-202 `// CFRunLoop pump, so spectrum data is never delivered. [!mayfail]  TEST_CASE("DataExchange delivers audio samples to controller local FIFOs", "[disrumpo][data-exchange][integration][!mayfail]")`
verifier_notes:
I could not refute this. The finding holds as stated.

1. **The tag is unconditional.** At plugins/disrumpo/tests/integration/data_exchange_spectrum_test.cpp:199-202 the case is tagged "[disrumpo][data-exchange][integration][!mayfail]" with no platform check. The comment blames only the missing macOS CFRunLoop pump. `pumpMessages` (lines 46-64) does pump on Windows via PeekMessageW/DispatchMessageW under `#ifdef _WIN32`. On other platforms it only sleeps.

2. **This is the only test of delivery.** I searched all of plugins/disrumpo for isSpectrumDataAvailable, getLocalInputFIFO and mayfail. The only hits are in this case and in controller.h. No other test asserts that the controller receives spectrum data. The other cases in the file only check lifecycle: init, connect, and that process() works without connect.

3. **The path it covers is real and can regress.** In processor_messaging.cpp:90-143, `sendSpectrumBlock` throttles to about 30 Hz, writes the Tier-3 shared FIFOs, then calls getCurrentOrNewBlock and sendCurrentBlock. In controller.cpp:1924-1950, `onDataExchangeBlocksReceived` checks the `editorClosing_` guard and the block size, pushes into the local FIFOs and sets `spectrumDataAvailable_`. A regression in any of these would only fail a REQUIRE inside a [!mayfail] case, which Catch2 does not count as a run failure.

4. **The pump works on Windows, measured.** I ran the case by name with build/windows-x64-release/bin/Release/disrumpo_tests.exe and -s. Every assertion passed: spectrumDataAvailable = 1, inputFIFO and outputFIFO totalWritten = 1536 each, maxVal = 0.999994, "All tests passed (10 assertions in 1 test case)". So the tag is not needed on Windows and only hides failures there.

5. **Project rule.** CLAUDE.md "Linux test harnesses have no run loop" says to gate such non-vacuity checks by platform, not make them non-failing everywhere. The comment is also incomplete: Linux has no pump either, since `pumpMessages` only sleeps there.

Nothing in the file is gated by platform except pumpMessages (lines 46-64): it uses PeekMessage/DispatchMessage under _WIN32 and only sleeps elsewhere, so the Windows path really does run the SDK timer fallback.

I ran this one case on Windows (build/windows-x64-release/bin/Release/disrumpo_tests.exe) and it passed: "All tests passed (10 assertions in 1 test case)". So on Windows the delivery is reliable, and [!mayfail] there only hides regressions.

No other Disrumpo test covers this path. A grep of plugins/disrumpo/tests for SharedDisplayBridge, sendSpectrumBlock and isSpectrumDataAvailable found only this file. Its other cases are lifecycle-only or a static trivially-copyable check (lines 193-374), so none checks that the controller receives data.

The project rule in CLAUDE.md ("Linux test harnesses have no run loop ... Gate such non-vacuity checks on Linux instead of asserting them") calls for gating by platform, not a blanket mayfail. No spec or design note explains why the tag also covers Windows; the comment's justification is about macOS only.

Severity stays low: this is a test gap, not a product defect. Innexus has the same pattern (test_data_exchange_pipeline.cpp:213, 234), which suggests it was copied but does not make it right.

I could not refute this. The defect is real, and low is the right severity.

1. **Tagged `[!mayfail]` on every platform.** `data_exchange_spectrum_test.cpp:199-202` puts `[!mayfail]` on the delivery case with no platform guard. The comment gives the missing macOS CFRunLoop pump as the reason. Yet the file already has a Windows-only pump: `pumpMessages` at lines 46-64 uses `#ifdef _WIN32` with PeekMessage/DispatchMessage, and on other platforms it only sleeps. So the delivery REQUIREs at lines 219-244 can never fail, not even on Windows, where the pump exists to make delivery happen.

2. **It is the only end-to-end delivery test.** A grep of `plugins/disrumpo/tests` finds DataExchange, SpectrumBlock and sharedDisplay only in this file and in CMakeLists.txt. Nothing else checks `isSpectrumDataAvailable` or `getLocalInputFIFO`.

3. **What it fails to guard.** Two code paths could regress without any test going red:
   - Processor side, `processor_messaging.cpp:42-59` and `:90-147`: the block size rounded up for aligned_alloc, the ~30 Hz throttle, and the lockBlock/sendCurrentBlock calls.
   - Controller side, `controller.cpp:1924-1954`: the `editorClosing_` guard, the `blocks[i].size >= sizeof(SpectrumBlock)` check, the push into the local FIFOs, and the setting of `spectrumDataAvailable_`.

4. **Impact.** Real hosts have a Tier-3 fallback. `sendSpectrumBlock` always pushes into the shared FIFOs (`processor_messaging.cpp:112-121`). The controller switches to `SharedDisplayBridge` after about 330 ms if DataExchange never delivers (`controller.cpp:1476-1478`, instance found through the state trailer at `:637-646`). So a break in the DataExchange tier alone would probably degrade the display rather than kill it. That makes "spectrum display silently goes dead" overstated for some regressions.

   The display could still go dead in at least two cases, and CI would not notice:
   - A regression in `onDataExchangeBlocksReceived` after `dataExchangeActive_` has been set. The fallback only starts when `!dataExchangeActive_`.
   - A host where the bridge lookup fails.

5. **Project rule.** CLAUDE.md says Linux non-vacuity checks should be gated by platform, not asserted. Making the case non-failing everywhere goes against that.

This is a genuine but low-severity test gap, so the severity stays as filed.

findings.title: No test injects NaN/Inf input or runs at 192 kHz, a mono bus, or numSamples 0 at processor level
findings.problem: grep for quiet_NaN, infinity() or NaN bit patterns in plugins/disrumpo/tests finds nothing. The 'NaN' checks in distortion_adapter_test only check that finite input gives finite output. 192000/176400 appear only in crossover_network_test. No test calls setBusArrangements with a mono bus or process() with numSamples = 0, numChannels = 1 or null buffers. The ProcessorFixture hard-codes 44.1 kHz, 2 channels and 512 samples.

findings.consequence: A single NaN from a host or a modulation source can permanently poison a band's IIR state, and high-rate behaviour is unknown, with no failing test.

Add sample-rate sections 44.1/96/192 kHz to 'Processor produces audio output with default parameters', and a setBusArrangements(mono) REQUIRE == kResultFalse case.
findings.evidence: grep `quiet_NaN|infinity()|0x7FC00000|nanf` over plugins/disrumpo/tests returns no hits; grep `192000|176400` matches only unit/crossover_network_test.cpp; processor_audio_output_test.cpp:84-88 setup.sampleRate = kSampleRate, maxSamplesPerBlock = kBlockSize, two channels only
