The test gap is real. I grepped plugins/disrumpo/tests for quiet_NaN, infinity(), 0x7FC00000, 0x7F800000, nanf, NAN and INFINITY and got no hits. The only NaN checks (distortion_adapter_test.cpp:1732-1957 and 2274-2537, multi_node_distortion_test.cpp:692-694) feed finite input and check that the output stays finite, using std::isnan. 192000 appears only in unit/crossover_network_test.cpp:265 and :589. No test calls setBusArrangements or uses kSpeakerMono.

Impact, part by part:
(1) "A NaN permanently poisons a band's IIR state" is mostly wrong for the band path. Host input reaches the bands only through CrossoverLR4, which is built from Biquads (crossover_filter.h:373-376 and 599-853). Biquad::process resets and returns 0 on non-finite input (biquad.h:353-356), so the adapters never see a host NaN.
(2) The NaN-latch consequence is still real through a different path. processor.cpp:340-342 feeds inputL[0]/inputR[0] to SweepEnvelope::processSample (sweep_envelope.h:192), which calls EnvelopeFollower::processSample. That function says "Does NOT validate input" (envelope_follower.h:163), so a NaN latches in its state. The resulting modulatedFreq NaN goes through std::clamp at processor.cpp:365 unchanged, because clamp passes NaN through, and then into sweepProcessor_.setCenterFrequency. The same kind of EnvelopeFollower sits inside ModulationEngine (modulation_engine.h:812), fed from processor.cpp:246.

findings.title: Factory preset test finds presets via a hard-coded F:/ path although DISRUMPO_RESOURCES_DIR is defined

findings.title: setupProcessing recreates the MorphEngine; per-band morph mode and smoothing are never re-applied, and setState before setupProcessing writes into a null engine
findings.problem: BandProcessor::prepare() does `morphEngine_ = std::make_unique<MorphEngine>()`, which gives mode_ = Linear1D and smoothingTimeMs_ = 10 (morph_engine.h:220-221). Processor::setupProcessing re-pushes nodes and position but not mode or smoothing (processor.cpp:125-127). The processor does not store either value: kBandMorphMode and kBandMorphSmoothing go straight to the BandProcessor (processor_params.cpp:958-969) and are not kept in BandMorphCache. A further ordering hazard: before the first setupProcessing morphEngine_ is null, so setState's setMorphMode, setMorphSmoothingTime, setMorphNodes and setMorphPosition (processor_state.cpp:827-831, 893-897) are silent no-ops behind `if (morphEngine_)`.
findings.why_wrong: Configuration set by parameters or state must survive setupProcessing. The processor needs to keep the authoritative copy and re-apply it after re-preparing DSP objects. The registered smoothing default is 0 ms (parameter_registration.cpp:717-719), but the engine runs at 10 ms.
findings.consequence: A sample-rate or block-size change, or any host that calls setupProcessing before activation, silently resets every band's Morph Mode to 1D Linear and smoothing to 10 ms while the UI still shows 2D Planar/Radial. With 4 nodes, 1D aliases nodes C and D onto A and B, so the sound changes. In the common host order (initialize, setState, setupProcessing), the state's morph configuration never reaches the engine. This compounds the separately known node-cache reset in setupProcessing.
findings.suggested_fix: Add morphMode and morphSmoothingMs to BandMorphCache. Set them in the param handlers and setState, write them in getState (this also fixes the literal 0 writes at processor_state.cpp:319/323), and re-apply them in setupProcessing after prepare. Test: setState with mode Planar2D and smoothing 50 ms, then setupProcessing twice (44.1 then 96 kHz), and assert that getMorphEngine()->getMode() and the smoothing time are preserved.
findings.evidence: band_processor.h:123 `morphEngine_ = std::make_unique<MorphEngine>();`; band_processor.h:260-264 `void setMorphMode(MorphMode mode) noexcept { if (morphEngine_) { morphEngine_->setMode(mode); } }`; morph_engine.h:220-221 `MorphMode mode_ = MorphMode::Linear1D; float smoothingTimeMs_ = 10.0f;`; processor.cpp:125-127 re-push nodes and position only; processor.h:165-172 BandMorphCache has no mode or smoothing fields.
verifier_notes:
I traced the code and the claim holds. band_processor.h:121-125: prepare() runs `morphEngine_ = std::make_unique<MorphEngine>()` and then morphEngine_->prepare(). The fresh engine starts with mode_ = Linear1D and smoothingTimeMs_ = 10.0f (morph_engine.h:220-221). processor.cpp:105-128 (setupProcessing) calls bandProcessors_[i].prepare(sampleRate_) and then re-pushes gain, pan, mute, setMorphEnabled, setMorphNodes and setMorphPosition. It never calls setMorphMode or setMorphSmoothingTime. The processor has no stored copy to re-apply: BandMorphCache (processor.h:165-172) holds only nodes, activeNodeCount, morphX/Y and shapeShadow. processor_params.cpp:958-969 sends kBandMorphSmoothing and kBandMorphMode straight to the BandProcessor without caching them.

The setters at band_processor.h:260-287 are all guarded by `if (morphEngine_)`. Processor::initialize does not prepare the band processors; only setupProcessing does (grep found prepare only at processor.cpp:106). So a setState that arrives before the first setupProcessing calls the setters at processor_state.cpp:827-831 and 893-897 on a null engine, and they do nothing. The setupProcessing that follows then overwrites the morph cache with defaults anyway (processor.cpp:112-124).

The registered smoothing default is 0 ms (parameter_registration.cpp:717-719), while a fresh engine runs at 10 ms. A user who sets the mode to Planar2D or Radial2D and then changes the sample rate or block size gets Linear1D back, while the UI still shows the old mode.

One caveat that narrows the state path: getState already writes a literal 0 for both morphMode and morphSmoothing (processor_state.cpp:319-323). So the mode was never persisted through state in the first place. Even so, the parameter-driven mode and smoothing are really lost on every setupProcessing. I am keeping medium severity.

Confirmed from source. band_processor.h:123 recreates the engine in prepare() with `morphEngine_ = std::make_unique<MorphEngine>()`. That engine starts at the defaults `mode_ = MorphMode::Linear1D` and `smoothingTimeMs_ = 10.0f` (morph_engine.h:220-221). MorphEngine::prepare (morph_engine.cpp:47-67) only sets up the smoothers with that 10 ms default and copies node types; it never restores a mode. Processor::setupProcessing (processor.cpp:104-128) calls prepare() for each band, resets the cache nodes and pushes setMorphNodes and setMorphPosition. It never calls setMorphMode or setMorphSmoothingTime. A grep of src/processor finds only two callers of those setters: the param handlers at processor_params.cpp:958-969 and setState at processor_state.cpp:827-831. Neither one stores the value anywhere.

BandMorphCache (processor.h:165-172) has no field for mode or smoothing. getState writes the literal values 0 and 0.0f for them (processor_state.cpp:319, 323), so no saved copy exists to re-apply. setMorphMode and setMorphSmoothingTime (band_processor.h:260-264, 283-287) are guarded by `if (morphEngine_)`, so a call before the first setupProcessing does nothing. setupProcessing also resets the node cache to SoftClip defaults (processor.cpp:111-122), which overwrites node data that setState wrote before preparation.

Mode does change the output: morph_engine.cpp has separate Linear1D, Planar2D and Radial2D branches at :180, :212 and :244. The registered smoothing default is 0 ms (parameter_registration.cpp:718-719), but the engine runs at 10 ms. Nothing re-sends parameters after setupProcessing, no test pins mode across a re-prepare, and no spec or comment calls this intentional. Medium severity is fair, because the mode is lost only when it was changed from the default and the host then calls setupProcessing again. The literal-0 getState write already loses the mode on any state round-trip, so this finding adds the re-prepare and param-before-prepare paths on top of that.

I could not refute this finding. Every link in the claim holds in source.

**Mode and smoothing are dropped on re-prepare.**
- band_processor.h:123 recreates the engine with `morphEngine_ = std::make_unique<MorphEngine>()`.
- That resets the engine to its defaults (morph_engine.h:220-221): `mode_ = Linear1D`, `smoothingTimeMs_ = 10.0f`.
- processor.cpp:105-128 (setupProcessing) re-pushes only gain, pan, mute, nodes and position. It never calls setMorphMode or setMorphSmoothingTime.
- The processor keeps no copy of either value. BandMorphCache (processor.h:165-172) holds nodes, activeNodeCount, morphX/Y and shapeShadow only.
- The parameter handlers forward mode and smoothing straight to the BandProcessor (processor_params.cpp:958-969).
- Hosts do not re-send parameter values after setupProcessing, so the values are lost.

**Who triggers it.** A sample-rate or block-size change does. So does an offline bounce in hosts that switch processMode via setActive(false) → setupProcessing(kOffline) → setActive(true), as Cubase and Reaper do. The export then renders in Linear1D while live playback used Planar2D or Radial2D.

**The sound changes.** Linear1D weighting (morph_engine.cpp:180-209) uses only posX. With the default node layout (processor.cpp:114-121: A(0,0), B(1,0), C(0,1), D(1,1)), A and C are equidistant from any cursor, and so are B and D. That gives 2-D-identical pairs equal weights whatever the cursor's Y. With four nodes, morph Y has no effect, and the blend differs from what the 2-D UI shows. With 2 nodes (A, B) the modes differ less. Default mode is Linear (distortion_types.h:378), so only users who picked 2D are affected.

**Smoothing.** The engine falls back to 10 ms while the registered default is 0 ms (parameter_registration.cpp:717-719) and the UI may show anything up to 500 ms. This mismatch exists from the first prepare, not only after a re-prepare. It is minor: a short cursor lag.

**Null-engine ordering is real but partly moot.**
- In setState (processor_state.cpp:827-831, 893-897), setMorphMode, setMorphSmoothingTime and setMorphNodes are no-ops while `morphEngine_` is null (band_processor.h:248, 261, 271, 284).
- However, the next setupProcessing overwrites the node cache with defaults anyway (processor.cpp:112-122; the finding notes this as known separately).
- getState writes literal 0 for both mode and smoothing (processor_state.cpp:319, 323), so state never carries them in any case.

The state-ordering half therefore adds little beyond the existing getState bug and the cache reset. The live-session reset of mode after setupProcessing is real, audible, and reached through ordinary host actions. Medium severity fits.

findings.title: Spectrum feed is spliced from disjoint block fragments: the 30 Hz throttle sends only the triggering block's samples
findings.problem: sendSpectrumBlock adds numSamples to an accumulator and returns until about 30 ms have accumulated. It then pushes only the CURRENT block's first min(numSamples, 2048) samples into sharedInputFIFO_/sharedOutputFIFO_ and the DataExchange block. The samples of the skipped blocks are never sent. The controller appends each received block to localInputFIFO_ (controller.cpp:1937), and SpectrumAnalyzer FFTs readLatest(2048) of that FIFO (spectrum_analyzer.h:107-108).
findings.why_wrong: An FFT window has to cover contiguous audio. The throttle should limit how often messages are sent while still delivering contiguous audio, for example by accumulating the last 2048 samples in a ring and sending that.
findings.consequence: At 44.1 kHz with 128-sample blocks, one 128-sample fragment is sent every ~32 ms. The 2048-point analysis window then holds 16 fragments taken from ~0.5 s of audio, with 15 phase discontinuities. A pure sine is displayed as a broad smeared skirt, and the input-vs-output comparison shows distortion that is not there. The display is only correct when the host block is ≥ 2048 samples, which is rare.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep a 2048-sample mono ring for input and output that is written every block. When the throttle fires, copy the latest 2048 contiguous samples into the block and the Tier-3 FIFOs, or push every block's samples to the Tier-3 FIFOs unthrottled, since they are lock-free. Test: drive the processor with a 1 kHz sine at 64-sample blocks, collect the DataExchange or shared FIFO, and assert the sample sequence is continuous (no phase jumps) and that the analyzer's bins beyond 2 octaves from 1 kHz are below -60 dB.
findings.evidence: processor_messaging.cpp:103-107 `spectrumSendAccumulatorSamples_ += numSamples; if (... < spectrumSendIntervalSamples_) return; ... %=`; :109-113 `const auto count = std::min(numSamples, kSpectrumBlockMaxSamples); sharedInputFIFO_.push(spectrumBlockBuffer_.inputSamples, count);`; processor.cpp:222-226 fills inputSamples from the current block only; spectrum_analyzer.h:108 `fifo->readLatest(windowedSamples_.data(), config_.fftSize)`.
verifier_notes: I traced the code and could not refute it. processor.cpp:221-227 builds spectrumBlockBuffer_.inputSamples from the current host block only, for min(numSamples, 2048) samples. processor.cpp:514 calls sendSpectrumBlock once per process() with that block's outputL/R. In processor_messaging.cpp:103-105 numSamples is added to the accumulator and the function returns early while the total is below the interval (sampleRate*0.03, set at :101). Those skipped blocks' samples are thrown away: nothing else writes sharedInputFIFO_/sharedOutputFIFO_; the only push sites are :113 and :119, per grep. When the throttle fires, :109-120 pushes only `count` samples of the current block to the Tier-3 shared FIFOs, and :134-143 copies the same fragment into the DataExchange block. On the controller side, onDataExchangeBlocksReceived (controller.cpp:1937-1938) appends each fragment to localInputFIFO_/localOutputFIFO_ (SpectrumFIFO<8192>). SpectrumAnalyzer::process (spectrum_analyzer.h:101-119) runs a Hann-windowed FFT over readLatest(fftSize=2048, :27) of that FIFO. So with a 128-sample block at 44.1 kHz (interval 1323 samples), one 128-sample fragment arrives about every 11 blocks, and the 2048-sample window is 16 non-contiguous fragments with phase jumps at each seam. That smears the spectrum, and the analyser runs the same way on both the input and output FIFOs. The display is only contiguous when the host block is at least as large as the throttle interval, and full-window only when it is at least 2048 samples. This affects only the UI display, not the audio, so medium severity is reasonable.

Confirmed from source. processor.cpp:221-228 writes only the current block's mono input (min(numSamples, 2048)) into spectrumBlockBuffer_.inputSamples on every block. processor_messaging.cpp:103-107 adds numSamples to the accumulator and returns until about 30 ms (sampleRate*0.03, line 101) has built up. On the block that fires, lines 109-119 push just that block's `count` samples into sharedInputFIFO_ and sharedOutputFIFO_, and lines 135-143 put the same fragment into the DataExchange block. Samples from the skipped blocks never reach any FIFO. On the controller side, controller.cpp:1937-1938 appends each received fragment to localInputFIFO_/localOutputFIFO_. SpectrumAnalyzer::process (spectrum_analyzer.h:101-119) reads readLatest(fftSize=2048, line 27) from that FIFO, applies a Hann window and FFTs it. With 128-sample blocks at 44.1 kHz, the 2048-sample window is therefore built from about 16 non-contiguous fragments.

I found nothing that makes this intentional or harmless. The throttle came from commit 7309ee32 (CHANGELOG:56, "Throttled spectrum data sends to ~30Hz"), which fixed queue overflow and did not address contiguity. No spec or code comment says fragmenting the stream is acceptable. The Tier-3 shared FIFO is lock-free and has no queue-depth reason to be throttled, yet it is throttled the same way. No test checks that the stream is continuous; the CHANGELOG:72 DataExchange integration test only covers that blocks arrive. The display is correct only when the host block is at least 2048 samples.

The impact is limited to the editor display (no audio effect), so medium severity fits.

I confirmed the defect from source. processor.cpp:221-227 fills spectrumBlockBuffer_.inputSamples from the current block only, for min(numSamples, 2048) samples. processor_messaging.cpp:103-107 adds numSamples to the accumulator and returns early until spectrumSendIntervalSamples_ (sampleRate*0.03, line 101) is reached. Nothing from the skipped blocks is kept. Once the throttle fires, :109-120 pushes only the current block's `count` samples into sharedInputFIFO_/sharedOutputFIFO_, and :135-143 copies the same current-block samples into the DataExchange SpectrumBlock. kSpectrumBlockMaxSamples is 2048 (spectrum_block.h:21). On the receiving side, controller.cpp:1937-1938 appends every received block to localInputFIFO_/localOutputFIFO_. SpectrumAnalyzer::process (spectrum_analyzer.h:101-119) then does readLatest(fftSize=2048, spectrum_analyzer.h:27), applies a Hann window and runs the FFT. The analysis window is therefore built from non-contiguous fragments.

Quantified impact. At 44.1 kHz the interval is 1323 samples.
- With 128-sample blocks, one fragment is sent about every 11 blocks (~32 ms). A 2048-sample window holds 16 fragments covering ~0.5 s of audio, with 15 phase discontinuities.
- With 512-sample blocks, the window holds 4 fragments with 3 discontinuities.

Each discontinuity in a tonal signal spreads broadband splatter that buries the real harmonics, so a pure sine shows as a wide skirt. The Tier-3 shared-FIFO fallback is fed the same way (:113-119), so it is affected too. The window is contiguous only when the host block is at least 2048 samples. The claim that this shows distortion that is not there is somewhat overstated: input and output are spliced identically, so both traces smear the same way. The absolute spectra are still wrong, though, and the real harmonics the plugin adds get masked by the splatter.

The consequence is display-only. Audio output is unaffected, there is no real-time-safety issue, and it does not affect other plugins. The spectrum is still a primary visual of this multiband effect and is wrong at typical host block sizes, so medium is defensible. I recommend no severity change.

findings.title: Dead processor state: maxOversampleFactor_ is written and never read; crossoverFrequencies_ atomics are unused; band default limit 8x vs processor default 4x
findings.problem: maxOversampleFactor_ (default 4) is stored in processor_params.cpp:357 and never read anywhere. It is not saved and not pushed to the bands at setup, so each BandProcessor keeps its own default maxOversampleFactor_ = kMaxOversampleFactor = 8 (band_processor.h:836) until the parameter arrives. The crossoverFrequencies_ array of atomics ('Crossover frequency targets (normalized, for smoothing)') is never written or read. The processor.h comments also still say 'band count (1-8)' and 'bandIndex (0-7)'.
findings.why_wrong: State that is written but never read, plus two defaults for one setting, is a maintenance trap. When oversampling is wired in, the FR-OS default of 4x will not hold until the host sends the parameter.
findings.consequence: No audible effect today, because the oversampling path is dead. When it is revived, bands default to an 8x limit instead of the specified 4x, and the 'smoothing' atomics invite someone to build on non-functional plumbing.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove crossoverFrequencies_. Either remove maxOversampleFactor_ or make it authoritative: push it to the bands in setupProcessing and persist it, which ties into the known Oversample-Max-not-saved finding. Fix the stale 1-8 comments. A test that a fresh processor's bands report a 4x limit would catch the default mismatch.
findings.evidence: grep over src/processor: `maxOversampleFactor_` appears only at processor.h:145 and processor_params.cpp:357 (store); `crossoverFrequencies_` appears only at processor.h:179; band_processor.h:836 `int maxOversampleFactor_ = kMaxOversampleFactor;` (=8, :47); processor.h:152 `/// @brief Current band count (1-8)`.
verifier_notes:
I read the code and every part of the claim holds. Searching the whole of plugins/disrumpo for `maxOversampleFactor_|crossoverFrequencies_` gives these results.

(1) Processor::maxOversampleFactor_ is declared at processor.h:145 (`std::atomic<int> maxOversampleFactor_{4};`). Its only other appearance is the store at processor_params.cpp:357. The same case (processor_params.cpp:358-361) also loops `bp.setMaxOversampleFactor(factor)`, but nothing ever reads the processor's atomic back, so it is dead state.

(2) Processor::crossoverFrequencies_ is declared at processor.h:179 and appears nowhere else in the processor. The other matches belong to CrossoverNetwork's own private member (crossover_network.h:133-428), which is a different variable. The processor's atomics are never written or read.

(3) Two defaults exist for one setting. `setMaxOversampleFactor` is called only at processor_params.cpp:360. Nothing calls it in setupProcessing or setActive. So each BandProcessor keeps `int maxOversampleFactor_ = kMaxOversampleFactor;` (band_processor.h:836, with kMaxOversampleFactor = 8 at band_processor.h:47) until the host sends kOversampleMaxId (0x0F04). That value feeds the factor selection at band_processor.h:402/406, while processor.h:144 says the default is 4x.

(4) The comment at processor.h:152 still says "Current band count (1-8)", but kMaxBands = 4 (band_state.h:61) and the band-count clamp at processor_params.cpp:342 caps it at 4.

Severity stays low. This is maintenance debt plus a latent default mismatch, not something audible today.

I could not refute any factual claim in the finding. Each one checks out against the source.

1. `Processor::maxOversampleFactor_` is written and never read. It is declared at `processor.h:145` (`std::atomic<int> maxOversampleFactor_{4};`). Grepping `plugins/disrumpo` finds only one use of the processor member: the store at `processor_params.cpp:357`. That same case block (lines 358-361) also forwards the factor to the bands through `bp.setMaxOversampleFactor(factor)`, so the atomic is redundant: nothing reads it back. `processor_state.cpp` never mentions `kOversampleMaxId` or the factor, so the value is also not saved.

2. `crossoverFrequencies_` at `processor.h:179` is never used. Every other hit is the unrelated private member of `CrossoverNetwork` (`crossover_network.h:133-428`). No code in `src/processor` reads or writes the processor's array of atomics.

3. The two defaults disagree. The band default is `int maxOversampleFactor_ = kMaxOversampleFactor;` at `band_processor.h:836`, with `kMaxOversampleFactor = 8` at `band_processor.h:47`. The processor and controller default to 4x (`parameter_registration.cpp:90`, `setNormalized(2.0/3.0)`). Nothing pushes 4x to the bands at setup. The only caller of `setMaxOversampleFactor` is `processor_params.cpp:360`.

4. The 'no audible effect today' claim also holds. `Processor::process` calls the per-sample `bandProcessors_[b].process(bandL, bandR)` at `processor.cpp:487/494`. That function (`band_processor.h:473-512`) runs the morph engine or adapter directly and never calls an oversampler. The oversampling path (`processBlock` -> `processBlockInner` -> `processWithFactor`, `band_processor.h:519-556`) is never reached from the processor, so the 8x-vs-4x mismatch is latent.

5. The stale comment at `processor.h:152` ('band count (1-8)') is present, while the band count is clamped to 1-4 at `processor_params.cpp:342`.

Nothing documents this as a design decision. No upstream clamp or `setActive` reset makes the band default 4x, and I found no test that pins it. It is a real but harmless maintenance defect, and low severity is appropriate.

Every factual claim in the finding checks out in the source. processor.h:145 declares `std::atomic<int> maxOversampleFactor_{4};`. Its only other use is the store at processor_params.cpp:357. A grep over plugins/disrumpo/src finds no read of it anywhere and no use in getState or setState. The same case (processor_params.cpp:359-361) pushes the factor to every band, but nothing pushes the processor's default of 4 to the bands in setup. So each band keeps `int maxOversampleFactor_ = kMaxOversampleFactor;` (band_processor.h:836, =8 per :47) until the host sends kOversampleMaxId. The controller registers the default as "4x" (parameter_registration.cpp:79-82). processor.h:179 `crossoverFrequencies_` (atomics) has no other reference in src/processor; the crossoverFrequencies_ hits in crossover_network.h are a separate member of CrossoverNetwork. The stale comment "Current band count (1-8)" is at processor.h:152.

The impact claim also holds. Processor::process drives the bands one sample at a time: `bandProcessors_[b].process(bandL, bandR)` at processor.cpp:494 and `process(discardL, discardR)` at :487. It never calls BandProcessor::processBlock (band_processor.h:519). Only processBlock leads to processBlockInner -> processWithFactor -> the 2x/4x/8x oversamplers (band_processor.h:548-557, 627-649). So the band's maxOversampleFactor_ only feeds recalculateOversampleFactor/currentOversampleFactor_ (band_processor.h:393-411), and nothing the plugin plays depends on it. The default mismatch (8x in the band vs 4x in the spec and controller) therefore has no audible or CPU effect today. The finding says exactly this.

Low severity fits a dead-state and maintenance-trap finding whose consequence only appears if the processBlock path is ever wired in. I see no reason to change it.

findings.title: Shape-slot 2 stepCount 8 makes VSTGUI wipe the custom menu-items: Tube Stage, AsymFuzz Trans, Serge Model, Bitcrush Mode and SampleReduce Mode menus show "0".."8"
findings.problem: Every band's 'Displayed Shape 2' proxy (and every node's real Shape 2) is registered as RangeParameter(0,1) with stepCount 8 (`int32_t stepCount = (s == 2) ? 8 : 0;`). BandSubController::verifyView adds the uidesc `menu-items` entries to each COptionMenu and then delegates to VST3Editor::verifyView. That creates a ParameterChangeListener. For a parameter with stepCount>0, its updateControlValue calls `optMenu->removeAllEntry()` and appends stepCount+1 entries from getParamStringByValue(i/8). formatShapeSlot only formats slot 2 for Temporal and RingSaturation, so for the other types the call falls through to RangeParameter::toString, which prints the integer step 0..8. Five slot-2 menus are affected: TypeParams_Tube 'Stage' (12AX7,EL84,6L6,300B), AsymFuzz 'Trans' (Germanium,Silicon), SergeFold 'Model' (Simple,Serge,Buchla,Lockhart), Bitcrush 'Mode' (Truncate,Dither) and SampleReduce 'Mode' (ZOH,Linear). Each loses its names and shows nine numeric entries.
findings.why_wrong: The code assumes the slot params have stepCount 0, so VSTGUI's auto-population is skipped. The comment at sub_controllers.h:191-194 says so, and so does the menu_items_test.cpp header ('Shape slot parameters are RangeParameter(0,1, stepCount=0)'). For slot 2 that assumption is false. With stepCount 8 the SDK RangeParameter also treats plain values as step indices 0..8 (vstparameters.cpp:200-205), so the menu's index range and the DSP's ranges no longer match. Tube satStage is round(slot*3) (processor_params.cpp:58), so entries 0..8 select stage 0,0,1,1,2,2,2,3,3. SergeFold foldModel uses the same mapping. AsymFuzz transistor is round(slot), so entries 0-3 select Germanium and 4-8 select Silicon. The same root cause has a second effect: the HalfRectify 'DC Block' ToggleButton on slot 2 (uidesc:996) gets min/max 0..8. With the slot default of 0.5, toPlain gives 4, so the toggle draws OFF while the DSP sees dcBlock = (0.5 >= 0.5) = true.
findings.consequence: On five distortion types the user sees a menu of '0'..'8' instead of tube, transistor, fold model, crush mode or reducer mode names. They cannot tell which tube or model they picked, and several entries select the same DSP value. The HalfRectify DC-block toggle shows the opposite of what the DSP is doing until it is clicked. Hosts also show 'B1 N1 Shape 2' as a nine-step integer for every type.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not quantize slot 2 globally. Register every shape slot with stepCount 0, and quantize the 9-curve Temporal/RingSat selector in formatShapeSlot and in the processor (both already round v*8). Alternatively, give the menus a per-type list parameter, which is not possible with one shared slot. Add a headless-editor test that opens TypeParams_Tube (and SergeFold, AsymFuzz) for band 0 and asserts that the COptionMenu has 4 (or 2) entries with the uidesc names, and that choosing entry 1 sets the proxy normalized value to 1/3 (or 1.0). Update the false comment in sub_controllers.h and in menu_items_test.cpp.
findings.evidence: parameter_registration.cpp:820 `int32_t stepCount = (s == 2) ? 8 : 0;` (proxy) and :957 (node params). sub_controllers.h:191-194: 'Shape slot parameters are RangeParameter(stepCount=0), so VSTGUI's auto-populate ... is skipped ... Our entries survive.' extern/vst3sdk/vstgui4/vstgui/plugin-bindings/vst3editor.cpp:273-276 (isStepCount when stepCount>0) and :325-330 (`optMenu->removeAllEntry (); for (i = 0; i <= stepCount; i++) optMenu->addEntry (getParamStringByIndex (i)...)`). vstparameters.cpp:160-166 (RangeParameter::toString prints the int step when stepCount>1). format_helpers.h:48-141 (slot 2 handled only for Temporal/RingSat). editor.uidesc:900, 935, 974, 996, 1005, 1016 (slot-2 COptionMenus and ToggleButton). processor_params.cpp:58, 83, 110, 126, 133, 141.
verifier_notes:
I traced the whole path in source and the defect is real.

1. Both the band proxy and the node param give slot 2 a step count of 8. parameter_registration.cpp:820 (band proxy) and :957 (node param) both have `int32_t stepCount = (s == 2) ? 8 : 0;` and pass it into RangeParameter(0,1,0.5,stepCount).
2. The slot-2 menus bind to that proxy. sub_controllers.h:151-160 maps "Band.NodeShape2" to makeBandParamId(band, kBandDisplayedShape2). The uidesc puts five COptionMenus on that tag, each with menu-items: :900 Tube, :935 AsymFuzz, :974 Serge, :1005 Bitcrush and :1016 SampleReduce. A ToggleButton sits on the same tag at :996.
3. The custom entries are added first, then VSTGUI overwrites them. BandSubController::verifyView (sub_controllers.h:195-203) adds the menu-items entries and then calls DelegationController::verifyView (:205). That reaches VST3Editor::verifyView (vst3editor.cpp:1042-1063), which builds a ParameterChangeListener for the proxy tag. Its constructor runs addControl and then parameter->changed() (:112-114). The update() at :174-179 then calls updateControlValue. With stepCount != 0, isStepCount is true (:273-280). The COptionMenu branch (:325-330) runs `optMenu->removeAllEntry()` and adds stepCount+1 = 9 entries from getParamStringByValue(i/8).

Controller::getParamStringByValue (controller.cpp:826-841) sends band shape proxies to formatShapeSlot. formatShapeSlot (format_helpers.h:48-141) only formats slot 2 for Temporal (:51) and RingSaturation (:93). It returns false for Tube, AsymmetricFuzz, SergeFold, Bitcrush and SampleReduce. The call then falls back to EditControllerEx1, which uses RangeParameter::toString. With stepCount > 1 that prints the integer step toPlain (vstparameters.cpp:158-166), so the menus show "0".."8".
5. The comment at sub_controllers.h:192-194 says the slot params have stepCount=0. That is false for slot 2.
6. The toggle side effect also holds. updateControlValue sets min and max to toPlain(0)=0 and toPlain(1)=8 (:278-279), and the value goes in as a plain step (vstparameters.cpp:201-202), so the toggle range becomes 0..8.

I found no override anywhere in the controller that re-adds the entries afterwards. Grep for removeAllEntry and menu-items in src/controller turns up only the sub_controllers.h site. The line-820 code came unchanged from the controller split (7587f4a1). I see no test in plugins/disrumpo/tests/unit/controller that opens a TypeParams template and checks the menu entries.

I kept the severity at high. Five distortion types show unlabeled menus whose entries map to DSP values out of step with the uidesc names, and the DC-block toggle state is shown wrong. The audio stays correct and every DSP value can still be reached, so this is a UI correctness defect, not an audio one.

I found no guard, intent comment or test that refutes this, and the source confirms it.

**Where the step count comes from.**
- parameter_registration.cpp:820 sets `int32_t stepCount = (s == 2) ? 8 : 0;` for the per-band "Displayed Shape" proxy, a RangeParameter(0,1,0.5,stepCount). Line 957 does the same for the node shape params.
- The uidesc placeholder tag Band.NodeShape2 (editor.uidesc:285, tag 50023) is remapped to kBandDisplayedShape0+2 by BandSubController::getTagForName (sub_controllers.h:154-157). So the slot-2 controls bind to the stepped proxy.
- Five slot-2 COptionMenus use it: editor.uidesc:900 Tube "12AX7,EL84,6L6,300B", :935 "Germanium,Silicon", :974 "Simple,Serge,Buchla,Lockhart", :1005 "Truncate,Dither", plus the SampleReduce "ZOH,Linear" menu. The HalfRectify ToggleButton at :996 is also on slot 2.

**How VSTGUI wipes the entries.**
- BandSubController::verifyView (sub_controllers.h:195-203) adds the menu-items entries, then calls DelegationController::verifyView (:204), which reaches VST3Editor.
- VST3Editor creates a ParameterChangeListener (vst3editor.cpp:752). Its constructor and addControl (:103-153) call parameter->changed()/deferUpdate(), which leads to updateControlValue.
- With stepCount != 0, updateControlValue sets isStepCount (:273-280). For a COptionMenu it calls `optMenu->removeAllEntry()` and adds stepCount+1 = 9 entries from getParamStringByValue(i/8) (:325-330). The custom entries are destroyed.
- For non-steppable controls it sets min/max to toPlain(0..1) = 0..8 and calls setValue(plain) (:308-345). That is the ToggleButton min/max claim; I did not trace further how the toggle draws 4 within 0..8.

**Why the entries show numbers.**
- Controller::getParamStringByValue, proxy branch (controller.cpp:826-838), calls formatShapeSlot.
- formatShapeSlot (format_helpers.h:48-141) handles slot 2 only for Temporal and RingSaturation.
- Tube, AsymFuzz, SergeFold, Bitcrush and SampleReduce therefore fall through to EditControllerEx1 / RangeParameter::toString (controller.cpp:893) and print the step integers.

**Mismatch with the DSP mapping.** The processor maps slot 2 coarsely: satStage = round(s*3), transistor/bitcrushMode/sampleMode = round(s), foldModel = round(s*3), dcBlock = s >= 0.5 (processor_params.cpp, the slots[2] lines). Nine entries therefore map many-to-one onto 2-4 DSP values.

**The code and test assume otherwise.** The comment at sub_controllers.h:191-194 says shape slots are stepCount=0 so auto-populate is skipped. The header of tests/unit/menu_items_test.cpp:8 says the same. Both are false for slot 2.

**Nothing else repairs it.** No other code re-adds entries: the only addEntry calls in src are the context menu (controller.cpp:1629-1657) and sub_controllers.h:200. menu_items_test only tests parseMenuItems, not the live editor.

**Intent.** History (commit 70c96aa9) shows stepCount 8 was added for the Temporal waveshape selector. The other slot-2 menus were never considered, so this is not a documented design decision.

**Severity.** The impact is UI-only plus misleading host display, with no audio-safety risk, but it breaks five menus. I kept the severity as filed.

I confirmed the defect in source. parameter_registration.cpp:820-823 registers the per-band proxy 'Displayed Shape' with `stepCount = (s == 2) ? 8 : 0`, and :957-961 does the same for the per-node Shape 2. In the uidesc, Band.NodeShape2 is bound to COptionMenus with custom menu-items: editor.uidesc:900 (Tube, 12AX7..300B), :935 (AsymFuzz, Germanium/Silicon), :974 (SergeFold, Simple..Lockhart), :1005 (Bitcrush, Truncate/Dither) and :1016 (SampleReduce, ZOH/Linear). There is also a ToggleButton at :996 (HalfRectify DC Block).

BandSubController::verifyView (sub_controllers.h:195-205) adds the menu-items and then delegates to VST3Editor::verifyView. The ParameterChangeListener constructor (vst3editor.cpp:103-115) calls parameter->changed(), which reaches updateControlValue. When stepCount != 0 (:273-280), that path does `optMenu->removeAllEntry()` and re-adds stepCount+1 = 9 entries from getParamStringByValue(i/8) (:325-330). Controller::getParamStringByValue (controller.cpp:826-841) goes to formatShapeSlot. formatShapeSlot (format_helpers.h:48-141) handles slot 2 only for Temporal and RingSaturation (Bitcrush only for slots 0/1/3), so it returns false. The call then falls through to RangeParameter::toString, which prints the integer plain value 0..8 when stepCount > 1 (vstparameters.cpp:158-166). So the five menus lose their names and show '0'..'8'.

The comments at sub_controllers.h:191-194 and menu_items_test.cpp:8 say these parameters are stepCount=0, which is no longer true. Git history shows this is a regression: menu-items arrived in f2cf88e1 (2026-02-01), and stepCount 8 was added later for the Temporal waveshape selector in 70c96aa9 (2026-03-15).

The claimed DSP mapping holds. processor_params.cpp:58 (Tube satStage = round(s*3)), :110 (SergeFold), :83/:126/:133/:141 (transistor, dcBlock, bitcrushMode, sampleMode) mean 9 entries collapse onto 4 or 2 values, so entries map to the right DSP state but cannot be told apart by name.

Impact: it reproduces on every host whenever one of these five types is shown. It is UI-only (audio is correct and selections still apply), but the controls cannot be read. Two side effects are noted but not quantified: the ToggleButton at :996 gets min/max 0..8, and every slot-2 ArcKnob for other types is quantized to 9 steps. Severity 'high' is defensible for a broken user-facing selector on five types, and nothing here argues for an upgrade, so it stays unchanged.

findings.title: MIDI Learn / MIDI CC mapping cannot work: no event input bus, the learn flag never reaches the processor, and the processor watches a different param ID
findings.problem: Every control's right-click menu offers 'MIDI Learn'. Its action calls `midiCCManager_->startLearn(paramId)` and `setParamNormalized(kGlobalMidiLearnActive, 1.0)`, which only changes controller-side state: no performEdit, so the processor never sees it. The processor's CC scan is keyed on a different parameter, kSweepMidiLearnActive (0x0E50, processor_params.cpp:527-528). It only looks at kLegacyMIDICCOutEvent in data.inputEvents (processor.cpp:392-397). The processor never declares an event input: initialize only calls addAudioInput/addAudioOutput (processor.cpp:65), so hosts never deliver MIDI and inputEvents is null. The detected-CC output parameter kSweepDetectedCCOutputId is never read by the controller (no match in src/controller), and nothing calls a learn-completion API on MidiCCManager. getMidiControllerAssignment (controller.cpp:707-726) also needs an event bus for hosts to query it. Its fallback reads the controller's `assignedMidiCC_` (controller.h:435), which is never assigned.
findings.why_wrong: VST3 hosts route MIDI CC to a plugin, and query IMidiMapping for the event bus index, only when the component exposes an event input bus. A learn mode also needs a completion path: either the processor reports the CC and the controller maps it, or the controller implements IMidiLearn::onLiveMIDIControllerInput. Here the UI flag (0x0F07) and the processor flag (0x0E50) are different parameters, the processor flag is never written by any UI, and the processor's report (0x0F81) has no listener. Each half was built against a different design (spec 012 global learn vs FR-028 sweep-only learn) and the two were never connected.
findings.consequence: The user right-clicks a knob and chooses MIDI Learn, moves a controller, and nothing happens. Learn mode stays armed in MidiCCManager until Escape. Mappings loaded through Controller::setState (MidiCCManager blob) are never exercised because no CC ever reaches the plugin. 'Clear MIDI Learn' and 'Save Mapping with Preset' operate on mappings that cannot exist. A user-visible feature (FR-028/029/031) is dead in every host.
findings.suggested_fix: Pick one design. (a) Add `addEventInput(STR16("MIDI In"), 16)` to Processor::initialize. Implement IMidiLearn::onLiveMIDIControllerInput in the controller to complete midiCCManager_ learning, call restartComponent(kMidiCCAssignmentChanged), and keep IMidiMapping as the host-side routing. (b) Remove the context-menu entry and the dead params (kGlobalMidiLearnActive/Target, kSweepMidiLearnActive/CCNumber, kSweepDetectedCCOutputId, assignedMidiCC_ in both processor and controller). Test: a controller unit test that runs startLearn, then a simulated onLiveMIDIControllerInput(cc 7), then asserts that getMidiControllerAssignment(0, 0, 7, id) returns the learned param. A processor test that asserts getBusCount(kEvent, kInput) == 1.
findings.evidence: controller.cpp:1623-1627 `midiCCManager_->startLearn(paramId); setParamNormalized(makeGlobalParamId(GlobalParamType::kGlobalMidiLearnActive), 1.0);`. processor.cpp:65 `addAudioInput(...)` is the only bus besides the output (grep addEventInput in src/processor: none). processor.cpp:392 `if (midiLearnActive_ && data.inputEvents)`, :397 `kLegacyMIDICCOutEvent`, :402-405 write kSweepDetectedCCOutputId. processor_params.cpp:527-528 `case SweepParamType::kSweepMidiLearnActive: midiLearnActive_ = (value >= 0.5);`. A grep for kSweepDetectedCCOutputId/IMidiLearn/onLiveMIDIControllerInput in src/controller finds no consumer. controller.cpp:720 `if (assignedMidiCC_ < 128 && ...)`. controller.h:435 `int assignedMidiCC_ = 128;` is never assigned.
verifier_notes:
I could not refute the finding. Every link in the claimed chain checks out in source:
(1) No event input bus. processor.cpp:65-66 are the only bus calls (addAudioInput/addAudioOutput). A grep for addEventInput across plugins/disrumpo/src finds nothing.
(2) The learn action is controller-local. controller.cpp:1623-1627 calls midiCCManager_->startLearn(paramId) and then setParamNormalized(kGlobalMidiLearnActive, 1.0), with no beginEdit/performEdit, so the processor is never notified. Escape at :1410-1412 also stays controller-local.
(3) The processor watches a different param. midiLearnActive_ is set only from kSweepMidiLearnActive (processor_params.cpp:528). The controller only registers that param (parameter_registration.cpp:347) and never writes it.
(4) The processor's CC scan cannot fire. processor.cpp:392-413 needs both midiLearnActive_ and data.inputEvents, and it matches Event::kLegacyMIDICCOutEvent. That is the output-direction CC event type. Hosts turn incoming CCs into parameter changes via IMidiMapping, not into input events, so the scan is dead twice over.
(5) No listener for the processor's report. kSweepDetectedCCOutputId (0x0F81) is only registered read-only (parameter_registration.cpp:307). Nothing in src/controller reads it.
(6) Learning is never completed. MidiCCManager::processCCMessage (shared midi_cc_manager.h:101) completes a learn, and nothing in plugins/disrumpo/src calls it. The controller implements only IMidiMapping (controller.h:62,222); there is no IMidiLearn or onLiveMIDIControllerInput.
(7) The fallback is dead too. The controller's assignedMidiCC_ (controller.h:435, =128) is never assigned (controller.cpp:720 only reads it), so the fallback branch in getMidiControllerAssignment (controller.cpp:707-726) is unreachable. It also answers busIndex 0, but the component has no event bus 0.
Net effect: the context-menu MIDI Learn, Clear, and Save-with-Preset items operate on mappings that can never be created through learn. Restored mappings can never be exercised, because no event input bus exists for hosts to route CCs through.
Severity stays as reported: it is a user-visible dead feature, though not an audio-safety defect.

(1) The context menu at controller.cpp:1623-1627 calls `midiCCManager_->startLearn(paramId)` and then `setParamNormalized(kGlobalMidiLearnActive, 1.0)`. There is no beginEdit/performEdit, so the processor is never told. The Escape path at controller.cpp:1408-1412 likewise only cancels on the controller side.

(2) Processor::initialize (processor.cpp:64-65) adds only `addAudioInput` and `addAudioOutput`. A grep of plugins/disrumpo/src for addEventInput or kEvent finds nothing. Without an event input bus, hosts deliver no events and have no bus to query IMidiMapping against. `getMidiControllerAssignment` (controller.cpp:707-726) asks for busIndex 0, a bus that does not exist.

(3) The processor's CC scan (processor.cpp:392-411) depends on `midiLearnActive_`. That flag is set only by `SweepParamType::kSweepMidiLearnActive` (processor_params.cpp:527-528, ID 0x0E50 per plugin_ids.h:135). It is a different parameter from the UI's kGlobalMidiLearnActive (0x0F07, plugin_ids.h:69). The scan also filters on `kLegacyMIDICCOutEvent`, which is an output-event type: VST3 hosts send CC through IMidiMapping as parameter changes, not as input events. So even with a bus this branch would not fire.

(4) The processor's report goes to `kSweepDetectedCCOutputId` (0x0F81). That ID is only registered as read-only (parameter_registration.cpp:307), and nothing in src/controller reads it.

The tests do not catch this. tests/integration/midi_learn_integration_test.cpp drives MidiCCManager on its own (startLearn plus processCCMessage, lines 27-47) and never touches the plugin's wiring, buses or getMidiControllerAssignment. No spec note or code comment says the feature is meant to be inert; the comments cite FR-028/029 as implemented.

On severity, high stands: a user-visible menu feature does nothing in every host, though no audio is corrupted.

Confirmed from source. controller.cpp:1623-1627: the "MIDI Learn" action only calls midiCCManager_->startLearn(paramId) and setParamNormalized(kGlobalMidiLearnActive, 1.0). That is controller-local, with no beginEdit/performEdit. processor.cpp:65-66: the processor declares only addAudioInput and addAudioOutput, and a grep for addEventInput/kEvent across plugins/disrumpo finds nothing. So even with a bus and the flag set, it would never fire. kSweepDetectedCCOutputId (0x0F81) is registered read-only (parameter_registration.cpp:307), but nothing in src/controller consumes it. MidiCCManager::processCCMessage (midi_cc_manager.cpp:127), the API that completes a learn, is called only from tests (tests/unit/midi_cc_manager_test.cpp, tests/integration/midi_learn_integration_test.cpp, state_persistence_test.cpp) and never from plugins/disrumpo/src. Those tests drive the manager directly and never exercise the plugin wiring. There is no audio corruption or crash: learn mode just stays armed until Escape (controller.cpp:1410-1412), and hosts' own parameter automation and learn still work. High fits a user-visible feature (FR-028/029) that is dead everywhere, so I keep the severity.

findings.title: Sweep-to-morph link runs only while the editor is open, follows only the Sweep Frequency parameter (not LFO/envelope), and writes automation without begin/endEdit
findings.problem: The only working implementation of the per-band Morph X/Y Link feature (FR-034, the 'Morph X Link'/'Morph Y Link' COptionMenus at editor.uidesc:1353-1355) is MorphSweepLinkController. That is an IDependent created in didOpen and destroyed in willClose (controller.cpp:1535-1538). It observes kSweepFrequency, maps it through applyMorphLinkMode, and calls setParamNormalized + performEdit on kBandMorphX/Y (visibility_controllers.cpp:197-209). The processor ignores kBandMorphXLink/YLink (processor_params.cpp:971-972, no-op), and SweepProcessor::getMorphPosition is never called. With the editor closed, nothing links morph to sweep. Even with the editor open, the link follows only the base parameter: the sweep LFO, sweep envelope and mod-matrix offsets move the audible sweep inside the processor and never change the kSweepFrequency parameter, so the morph cursor does not follow them.
findings.why_wrong: A sound-shaping link that the user sets in the editor must behave the same whether the editor is open or not, and the same during offline render. A UI-lifetime object cannot carry DSP behaviour. The controller also issues performEdit without beginEdit/endEdit from inside IDependent::update, which fires during host automation playback of Sweep Frequency. That writes Morph X/Y automation (in Touch/Latch modes it records it) and competes with existing Morph X/Y automation lanes. VST3 requires performEdit to be bracketed by beginEdit/endEdit.
findings.consequence: A preset that links Morph X to the sweep sounds different depending on whether the editor window is open. With the editor closed, during an offline bounce, and on a second instance with no editor, the morph stays put. A sweep driven by the sweep LFO or envelope never morphs, which is the usual way a sweep is animated. When the editor is open during automation playback, the host may record spurious Morph X/Y automation. The loop also walks bands 4-7, which do not exist (visibility_controllers.cpp:156).
findings.suggested_fix: Move the link into the processor. In Processor::process, after the sweep's modulated frequency is computed, apply the link curve per band from bandStates' X/Y link mode to the morph position passed to setMorphPosition, as an offset or a replacement. Persist the link modes in state. Remove MorphSweepLinkController and the controller-side performEdits. Test: a processor-level test (no controller) that sets kBandMorphXLink=SweepFreq, sweeps kSweepFrequency from 0 to 1, renders, and asserts that the band's morph weights change. A second test enables the sweep LFO with the base frequency fixed and asserts that the morph position moves.
findings.evidence: controller.cpp:1454-1456 `if (sweepFreqParam) morphSweepLinkController_ = new MorphSweepLinkController(this, sweepFreqParam);` (didOpen only). controller.cpp:1535-1538 deactivate + null in willClose. visibility_controllers.cpp:155-157 `float sweepNorm = sweepFreqParam_->getNormalized(); for (int band = 0; band < 8; ++band)`. visibility_controllers.cpp:198-201 `controller_->setParamNormalized(...kBandMorphX, newX); controller_->performEdit(...kBandMorphX, newX);` with no beginEdit/endEdit. processor_params.cpp:971-972 `case BandParamType::kBandMorphXLink: case BandParamType::kBandMorphYLink:` fall into the no-op group. editor.uidesc:1353,1355 are the user-facing link menus.
verifier_notes:
The source confirms every part of the claim.

1. **The link exists only while the editor is open.** controller.cpp:1454-1456 creates MorphSweepLinkController in didOpen. controller.cpp:1535-1538 deactivates it and sets it to null in willClose. Nothing else creates it; a grep for morphSweepLinkController_ finds only controller.h:341 and these two places.

2. **The processor does nothing with the link.** processor_params.cpp:971-972 puts kBandMorphXLink and kBandMorphYLink in the "UI-only params ... no processor action" no-op group, together with kBandExpanded and the other UI-only params. SweepProcessor::getMorphPosition (sweep_processor.h:297) is never called from any file under src/; the only callers are tests/dsp/sweep_processor_tests.cpp:334-425. The global kSweepMorphLink is stored by processor_params.cpp:410-413 and saved in processor_state.cpp:95, but its output is never read, so the processor-side curve is dead too. With the editor closed or during an offline render, no code links morph position to sweep.

3. **The link follows only the Sweep Frequency parameter.** visibility_controllers.cpp:154-157 reads sweepFreqParam_->getNormalized() inside IDependent::update. That fires only when the controller's kSweepFrequency Parameter object changes. The sweep LFO, envelope and mod offsets live inside the processor and never write that parameter, so the morph cursor ignores them.

4. **performEdit is not bracketed by beginEdit/endEdit.** visibility_controllers.cpp:198-201 and 205-208 call setParamNormalized + performEdit on kBandMorphX/Y without beginEdit/endEdit. Other code in this plugin brackets its edits correctly (controller.cpp:1180-1181, morph_pad.cpp:641-647), so this site is the odd one out. update() fires on host-driven setParamNormalized of Sweep Frequency, because the SDK's Parameter::setNormalized calls changed(). So during automation playback it can write or record Morph X/Y edits.

5. **The loop walks bands that do not exist.** visibility_controllers.cpp:156 loops band 0..7. For bands 4-7, getParameterObject returns null and the function returns at line 168, so this part is harmless.

Severity stays high: a sound-shaping feature that users can set in the editor behaves differently with the editor closed or during an offline bounce, and it can write spurious automation.

I could not refute this finding. Every part of the claim matches the source.

1. The link only exists while the editor is open. MorphSweepLinkController is created in didOpen (controller.cpp:1454-1456) and deactivated and nulled in willClose (controller.cpp:1535-1537). Nothing else references it (grep of plugins/disrumpo shows only controller.h:341, controller.cpp and visibility_controllers.{h,cpp}).

2. The processor ignores the per-band link params. processor_params.cpp:971-979 sends kBandMorphXLink and kBandMorphYLink to a no-op group with the comment "UI-only params (sweep-morph link, ...): no processor action". That comment says what the code does. It is not a documented design rationale: specs-overview.md:287-291 (FR-SWEEP-003) and roadmap.md:460-472 describe sweep-morph linking as audio behaviour (milestone M5 "Sweep with morph linking functional"), and the CHANGELOG says nothing about it.

3. The processor-side link is dead code. The global kSweepMorphLink is parsed (processor_params.cpp:410-413) and saved and restored (processor_state.cpp:95, 476-493). However, SweepProcessor::getMorphPosition (sweep_processor.h:297-308) has no caller anywhere in src: a grep for getMorphPosition, getMorphLinkMode and applyMorphLinkCurve in src/processor finds only the state and param code.

I found no upstream guard, setActive reset or spec decision that makes the editor-only behaviour intentional. A host renders offline with the editor closed, so the failure is reachable.

The defect is real and I confirmed each part of it in the source.
(1) The link lives only for the editor's lifetime. controller.cpp:1454-1456 creates MorphSweepLinkController in didOpen, and controller.cpp:1535-1537 deactivates it and nulls it in willClose.
(2) The processor ignores the per-band link params. processor_params.cpp:971-979 puts kBandMorphXLink and kBandMorphYLink in the "UI-only params ... no processor action" no-op group. A grep over src/ finds SweepProcessor::getMorphPosition only at its definition (sweep_processor.h:297) and no caller. That means the global kSweepMorphLink, which the processor does store (processor_params.cpp:410-413, processor_state.cpp:95/491), is never applied to any band's morph position either.
(3) The link follows only the base parameter. visibility_controllers.cpp:148-159 reads sweepFreqParam_->getNormalized() inside IDependent::update. The processor-side LFO, envelope and mod-matrix offsets never touch that controller Parameter, so a sweep animated that way never moves the morph.
(4) There is no begin/endEdit. visibility_controllers.cpp:197-209 calls setParamNormalized + performEdit on kBandMorphX/Y without bracketing. This fires during host automation playback of Sweep Frequency, so a host in Touch/Latch can record Morph X/Y automation, and hosts that drop unbracketed performEdit never forward it at all. The behaviour is host-dependent.
(5) The loop over bands 0-7 (visibility_controllers.cpp:156) is harmless: getParameterObject returns null for bands that do not exist, and line 168 returns early.
One part of the stated consequence needs correcting, and it makes the defect worse: band link modes are not persisted anywhere. The processor state ignores them, and Controller::getState (controller.cpp:658-677) writes only a version, two unused doubles and the MIDI CC mappings. So a preset or project cannot carry a Morph X Link at all, and it resets to None on reload. The "preset sounds different depending on editor" scenario cannot happen across a reload. Within a session, a link the user sets makes the audible result depend on whether the editor is open and on offline versus realtime render, and LFO-driven sweeps never morph.
Impact: a user-facing, sound-shaping feature (FR-032/033, editor.uidesc link menus) is effectively non-functional in the DSP. It is also unpersisted, and it can pollute automation when the editor is open. There is no crash and no NaN, but for a headline "sweep-morph linking" feature, high severity is defensible.

findings.title: Morph cursor smoothing is about 4x slower than set (10 ms reads 37 ms)
findings.problem: smootherX_/Y_.configure(smoothingTimeMs_, sampleRate) receives the 8x sample rate (band_processor.h:124). process() advances the smoothers once per call, and it is called twice per host sample (L then R, band_processor.h:487-488). The net effect is 8/2 = 4x the configured time. setSmoothingTime at :127 uses the same rate.
findings.why_wrong: FR-MORPH-003 says the smoothing time is in ms of real time (0-500 ms). The smoother must be configured at the rate it is advanced at and advanced once per sample.
findings.consequence: Morph motion lags 4x behind the setting. The 500 ms maximum becomes about 2 s, and automation and modulation of morph X/Y feel sluggish.
findings.suggested_fix: Configure the smoothers at the actual processing rate and advance them once per frame, not once per channel. Promote the morph-smoothing:default probe: time to 99 % = 10 ms +/- 30 %.
findings.evidence: probe morph-smoothing:default: "time_to_99pct_ms 37.33" (threshold "10 ms +/- 30 %"). Code: morph_engine.cpp:51 `smootherX_.configure(smoothingTimeMs_, static_cast<float>(sampleRate));`
verifier_notes:
Confirmed from source. band_processor.h:123-124 calls `morphEngine_->prepare(sampleRate * kMaxOversampleFactor, ...)` with kMaxOversampleFactor = 8 (band_processor.h:47). morph_engine.cpp:51-52 then configures smootherX_/Y_ (OnePoleSmoother, morph_engine.h:228-229) with smoothingTimeMs_ (default 10 ms, morph_engine.h:221) at that 8x rate. setSmoothingTime at morph_engine.cpp:127-128 reuses sampleRate_, which is the same 8x rate. smoother.h:156-158 documents configure() as time-to-99 % at the given sample rate. MorphEngine::process (morph_engine.cpp:662-669) calls smootherX_.process() and smootherY_.process() on every call. The callers run it once per channel:
- 1x path, which is also the drive-bypass path: processWithFactor (band_processor.h:632-635) calls process(L,R), which calls morphEngine_->process(left) and then (right) (:487-488). That is 2 advances per host sample against a coefficient sized for 8 per sample, so 8/2 = 4x slower: 10 ms becomes about 40 ms. The probe's 37.33 ms matches.
- Oversampled paths: processOversampledBlock (:752-754) also advances twice per oversampled sample. That gives 2x slower at 2x, correct at 4x, and 2x too fast at 8x.

So the claim is right for the 1x path the probe measured. The wider defect is that the morph smoothing time depends on the oversampling factor and is not real time; it is not a constant 4x. The suggested fix is still correct: configure the smoothers at the rate they are advanced at, and advance them once per frame, not once per channel. Severity medium is appropriate: it is a functional timing error and not a safety issue.

The defect is real. Nothing in the source guards against it or documents it as intended.
- band_processor.h:124 calls morphEngine_->prepare(sampleRate * kMaxOversampleFactor, ...). morph_engine.cpp:51-52 configures smootherX_/Y_ at that 8x rate, and setSmoothingTime (:126-128) does the same through sampleRate_.
- MorphEngine::process (morph_engine.cpp:662-669) advances both smoothers once per call, and the BandProcessor calls it once per channel. In the 1x path, and whenever drive < 0.0001 (processWithFactor :632-636 -> process() :487-488), it runs twice per host sample, L then R. In the oversampled path (processOversampledBlock :752-754) it runs twice per oversampled sample.
- So the real smoothing time is set_ms * 8 / (2 * factor): 4x too slow at 1x, 2x too slow at 2x, correct only at 4x, and 2x too fast at 8x.
- The only related comment ("prepare at 8x to support all oversampling factors", band_processor.h:109-110, :121) explains the adapter rate. It does not say the smoothing time is meant to scale.
- No upstream clamp corrects it: setMorphSmoothingTime is called from processor_params.cpp:961 and processor_state.cpp:831 with plain ms. The tests that set 5-20 ms (morph_artifact_test.cpp, morph_band_integration_test.cpp) check for clicks, not timing, so no test pins the rate.
- The measured 37.33 ms against a 10 ms setting is 3.7x, which matches the 1x-path prediction.
- It is not unreachable: the 1x path is the default whenever drive is 0 or the types' profiles select 1x.
Severity stays medium. One addition: the error also varies with the selected oversampling factor, so the same smoothing setting behaves differently whenever the factor changes. The fix should configure the smoothers at the base rate and advance them once per host frame.

The defect is real. The claimed consequence holds on the 1x path but the magnitude depends on the oversampling factor, so "always 4x" overstates it. The code path:

- BandProcessor::prepare calls morphEngine_->prepare(sampleRate * kMaxOversampleFactor (8), ...) (band_processor.h:123-125).
- MorphEngine::prepare configures smootherX_/Y_ (Krate::DSP::OnePoleSmoother, morph_engine.h:228-229) at that 8x rate (morph_engine.cpp:51-52). setSmoothingTime reconfigures with the same sampleRate_ (morph_engine.cpp:125-129). smoother.h:74/156 defines the configured time as time to 99 %.
- MorphEngine::process advances both smoothers on every call (morph_engine.cpp:668-669).
- process is called twice per frame, once for L and once for R, in both BandProcessor::process (band_processor.h:487-488) and processOversampledBlock (band_processor.h:753-754).

So the smoothers advance 2*F times per host sample while configured for 8 steps. The effective time is configured * 8 / (2F):
- 1x (and whenever drive < 0.0001, which goes through process(), band_processor.h:632-635): 4x slow. 10 ms reads about 40 ms, matching the measured 37.33 ms; 500 ms reads about 2 s.
- 2x: 2x slow.
- 4x: correct.
- 8x: 2x fast (5 ms).

During an oversampling crossfade, processBlockWithCrossfade runs the same morphEngine_ through both factor paths (band_processor.h:659-663), so the smoother advances more again. The smoothing time therefore also jumps whenever the intelligent oversampler changes factor.

Impact: the probe's default case (1x) and the 500 ms to about 2 s claim are correct. At 4x the timing is right and at 8x it is too fast. That inconsistency is part of the defect, not a reason to refute it. Medium severity fits: a user-facing timing parameter misbehaves on the common 1x/2x paths, with no audio corruption, NaN or crash.

findings.title: Cross-family morph dips 13-19.5 dB and clicks: outputs are summed linearly with double attenuation, and skipped nodes re-enter with stale state
findings.problem: processCrossFamily computes `output += nodeOutput * weight * gain` with normalized weights times transitionGains_. Below 0.6 weight a node is attenuated by both w and sin(w/0.4*pi/2). Nodes with w < kWeightThreshold are `continue`d (:745) and never processed, so their filters, delays and RNG go stale and are fed live audio again when the weight rises.
findings.why_wrong: FR-007/FR-008 and SC-002 require an equal-power crossfade, with level within 1 dB across a cross-family morph and no artifacts (SC-003). A linear sum of decorrelated outputs dips, and the extra transition gain removes still more level.
findings.consequence: Sweeping the cursor across cross-family nodes drops the level by up to 19.5 dB, with 54 clicks on a 4-node sweep (jump ratio 9.9).
findings.suggested_fix: Use sqrt(w) (equal-power) gains normalised so that the sum of squares is 1, drop the double transition gain, and keep processing low-weight nodes (or crossfade them in from a primed state). Test: the morph-sweep probes must show |level dev| <= 1 dB (SC-002) and jump_ratio <= 1.3.
findings.evidence: probe morph-sweep:4node-crossfamily-planar: "jump_ratio 9.90, clicks_sweep 54, clicks_static 0, start_dB -6.62, end_dB -17.82, max_level_dev_dB -19.51". morph-sweep:2node-crossfamily(SoftClip-SineFold): "1.83,1,0,0,-6.62,-14.66,-12.95" (threshold jump_ratio <= 1.3, |level dev| <= 3 dB). Code: morph_engine.cpp:745 `if (weight < kWeightThreshold) continue;`, :756 `output += nodeOutput * weight * gain;`
verifier_notes:
I traced the code and it confirms the defect. I did not run the probe. It exists at specs/disrumpo-audit/probes/audit_probes.cpp.txt:1045-1046, and I took the quoted numbers as given.

1. **Linear sum with two gains.** morph_engine.cpp:740-757 (processCrossFamily) computes `output += adapters_[i].process(input) * weight * gain`. `weight` is the normalised inverse-distance weight, which sums to 1 (:196-208, :228-240, renormalised at :260-265). `gain` is transitionGains_[i] = calculateTransitionGain(w) (:268-270). So every node is scaled twice: linearly by w, then by a sine gain. This is not an equal-power crossfade, even though the comment at :722 says it is.

2. **Level at the midpoint.** calculateTransitionGain (:352-379) uses equalPowerGains (dsp/include/krate/dsp/core/crossfade_utils.h:50-53, fadeIn = sin(pos*pi/2)). With w=0.5 for both nodes, zonePos = (0.5-0.4)/0.2 = 0.5 and the gain is 0.707. The output is then 0.354*(a+b): -3 dB if a and b are correlated, about -6 dB if they are decorrelated. That matches the probe's start_dB of -6.62.

3. **A worse defect the finding missed: the gain is discontinuous at w = 0.4.**
   - Just below 0.4 (branch at :364-370), normalizedPos = w/0.4 is about 1, so the gain is sin(pi/2) = 1.0.
   - At w = 0.4 (branch at :374-378), zonePos = 0, so the gain is sin(0) = 0.
   - A node's gain therefore steps from 1 to 0 as its weight crosses 0.4. In a 2-node layout that happens when the weights pass 0.6/0.4: one node drops out entirely and the output becomes 0.6*b. This step explains both the clicks and the large dips (-13 to -19.5 dB) in the sweep probes.

4. **Stale state.** Nodes with weight below kWeightThreshold (0.001, morph_node.h:139) are skipped at :745 and :749, so their adapters are never called. Nothing resets them on re-entry; the only adapter reset is MorphEngine::reset at :80-83. The adapters therefore hold stale filter, delay and RNG state.
   - This part has less impact than the finding implies. A node re-enters at a gain of about sin(0.001/0.4*pi/2), roughly 0.004, so the stale state is heavily attenuated.
   - The main click source is the gain step in point 3.

5. **Spec conflict.** FR-007/FR-008/SC-002 require an equal-power crossfade and level within 1 dB. Neither the double attenuation nor the 1-to-0 step can meet that.

Severity: high, unchanged. Even the default 2-node cross-family layout dips and clicks audibly on every morph sweep. The default nodes are SoftClip and Tube (:41-42); I did not check whether those two count as different families.

I could not refute the level dip, and the source shows a further defect that the finding does not mention.

What the code does:
- morph_engine.cpp:756 sums the node outputs linearly, scaling each by its normalised IDW weight times transitionGains_[i]. The weights sum to 1 (renormalised at :260-265).
- transitionGains_ comes from calculateTransitionGain (:352-379):
  - At or above 0.6 the gain is 1.
  - Below 0.4 it is sin(w/0.4·π/2), the fadeIn from equalPowerGains.
  - From 0.4 to 0.6 it is sin((w-0.4)/0.2·π/2).

What that produces:
- At a 2-node 50/50 position, each node gets 0.5 × sin(π/4) ≈ 0.354. That is the double attenuation the finding describes.
- Discontinuity at w = 0.4: just below 0.4 the gain approaches sin(π/2) = 1. At exactly 0.4, zonePos is 0, so the gain is sin(0) = 0. A node crossing 40 % weight therefore jumps from full gain to zero gain, which gives a click and a deep dip. This fits the measured 54 clicks and the -19.5 dB minimum.

Is it intentional or already guarded?
- No. The design in specs/Disrumpo/dsp-details.md:1150-1198 differs: gainA = 1 below 0.4, then a complementary cos/sin crossfade inside 0.4-0.6, plus a 7 ms TransitionFader for cold-state entry (:1201-1229). The code applies a fade-in gain on top of the IDW weights, so it does not implement that crossfade. The fader does not exist either.
- No test pins the correct behaviour. In tests/unit/morph_interpolation_test.cpp:305 the SC-002 cross-family check is `REQUIRE(ratio < 3.0f)`, an amplitude ratio of about 9.5 dB, labelled "generous margin". The approval test AP-003 (tests/approval/morph_artifact_test.cpp:383) uses createSameFamilySetup, so it never reaches processCrossFamily.
- Nothing upstream clamps or compensates. process() (:662-683) sends every mixed-family node set into processCrossFamily.

One part of the claim is weaker. Skipping nodes whose weight is below kWeightThreshold (:745, and :253-258) is the intended FR-015 optimisation, so stale state on re-entry is a known consequence of a deliberate design, not a separate bug. It is still a click source, because the spec's fade-in that would cover it was never built.

The main defect is confirmed in source and by the quoted probe numbers. I see no reason to change the severity.

Confirmed from source. morph_engine.cpp:743-757 (processCrossFamily) sums `nodeOutput * weight * gain` linearly. The weights are IDW-normalized so they sum to 1 (:196-208, :228-240, renormalized at :260-265). transitionGains_ comes from calculateTransitionGain (:352-379), which multiplies in a second attenuation on top of the weight. It also has a hard discontinuity that the finding understates. For 0.01 < w < 0.4 the gain is sin((w/0.4)*pi/2), which approaches 1.0 as w approaches 0.4. At w = 0.4 the zone branch takes over with zonePos = 0, so the gain is sin(0) = 0. A node crossing w = 0.4 therefore drops from about 0.4*1.0 of the output to 0 within one sample. Because weights are recomputed per sample from the smoothed cursor (:668-672), that step lands mid-block, and it fits the measured clicks (jump ratio 9.9 on 4 nodes, 1.83 on 2 nodes). Level: at the 2-node midpoint (w = 0.5/0.5) each node gets 0.5 * sin(pi/4) = 0.354, about -9 dB per node. The sum of two partly decorrelated distortion outputs then falls several dB below either endpoint. This matches the measured dips (-12.95 dB on 2 nodes, -19.51 dB on 4 nodes, both against a dB-linear start/end path). The probe exists at specs/disrumpo-audit/probes/audit_probes.cpp.txt:957-1046: 220 Hz at -12 dBFS, cursor swept over 2 s, block-rate automation. The setup is ordinary: cross-family nodes, drive 0.3, a single band. The skipped-node claim is also accurate: :745 and :749 `continue` before adapters_[i].process, so the filter/DC/RNG state of a low-weight node is never advanced. It is the weaker part of the finding, because SoftClip and SineFold carry little state. The dominant effects are the gain discontinuity at w = 0.4 and the linear double attenuation. Any host that automates or drags the morph cursor between cross-family nodes triggers this. Morphing is the plugin's headline feature, so high severity stands. It violates FR-007/FR-008 (equal-power crossfade) and SC-002/SC-003 as claimed.

findings.title: Band-count changes click: crossover topology switches instantly with no crossfade
findings.problem: kBandCountId stores bandCount_ and calls crossoverL_/R_.setBandCount on the audio thread. CrossoverNetwork::setBandCount (crossover_network.h:111-122) changes numBands_ and redistributes or reconfigures allpasses at once. The sample loop (processor.cpp:483) then starts or stops summing bands, and newly active bands carry stale filter and adapter state.
findings.why_wrong: Discrete structural parameter changes on the audio path need a short crossfade (old vs new topology) or a ramp to avoid discontinuities.
findings.consequence: Audible clicks when the band count is automated or changed during playback.
findings.suggested_fix: Crossfade the output over about 10 ms when the band count changes (render old and new topology, or fade the bands in and out through their mute smoothers), and reset newly enabled bands' state. Test: the automation:bandcount probe jump ratio must be <= 1.3.
findings.evidence: probe automation:bandcount2-4-1 (step1, step2): "jump_ratio,clicks_step = 3.78,1 / 3.90,1" (threshold jump_ratio <= 1.3). Code: processor_params.cpp:344 `crossoverL_.setBandCount(clamped);`
verifier_notes: I could not refute this. The source and the measurement both show the defect. processor_params.cpp:339-346 handles kBandCountId on the audio thread. It stores bandCount_ and calls crossoverL_/R_.setBandCount(clamped) directly, with no ramp. crossover_network.h:111-122 setBandCount sets numBands_ = newBandCount at once and calls redistributeCrossovers, so nothing is crossfaded. From the next sample, CrossoverNetwork::process (crossover_network.h:185-228) runs a different number of cascaded LR4 splits (loop at line 211) and allpass compensation stages (lines 222-226); with 1 band it passes the input through unchanged (line 195-197). The summed signal's phase response therefore jumps at that sample, and with it the waveform. The crossovers and allpasses that were not used before resume from stale or zeroed state, because process() only runs indices below numBands_-1. processor.cpp:257 reads numBands once per block, and the loop at processor.cpp:481 only calls bandProcessors_[b].process for b < numBands. Bands above the old count therefore never ran their smoothers or adapters and start from stale state. They also get no fade-in: the mute/solo smoothing is gated by shouldBandContribute (processor.cpp:563), not by band count. The measurement agrees. In f:/tmp/disrumpo-audit/probe-results.txt, lines 27-28 read automation:bandcount2-4-1 step1 = 3.78, clicks 1, and step2 = 3.90, clicks 1, against an ok threshold of 1.3. Pre and post levels are equal (-18.23/-18.24 dB, -18.23/-18.22 dB), so this is a short transient at the switch, not a level change. That probe (specs/disrumpo-audit/probes/audit_probes.cpp.txt:1190-1191, 220 Hz sine at -12 dBFS, block 512) is the only test I found for a band-count change during audio. Other structural switches measured clean in the same run (mute, solo and OS max all had jump_ratio <= 1.0), which points the click at the band-count path specifically. Medium severity fits: an automated or live band-count change gives an audible click, but there is no NaN or level fault.

I could not refute this. The code and the measurement agree.

1. processor_params.cpp:339-346: kBandCountId stores bandCount_ and calls crossoverL_/R_.setBandCount(clamped) straight away on the audio thread. There is no ramp and no fade state.

2. crossover_network.h:111-122: setBandCount sets numBands_ at once and calls redistributeCrossovers (274-297). That function either re-initialises the frequencies (initializeLogarithmicDistribution + updateAllpassCoefficients when the old count was 1) or recomputes the allpasses. It does not reset filters or crossfade. process() at 195-198 passes the input straight to bands[0] when numBands_==1, so a change to 1 band drops the LR4 and allpass paths within one sample.

3. processor.cpp:463-499: beginBlockModulation and the per-sample band loop run only for b < numBands. Inactive BandProcessors are never processed. A band that comes back carries frozen filter, smoother and adapter state from whenever it was last active. Nothing in setActive or the kBandCountId path resets them.

4. The behaviour is not a design decision. The retired spec specs/_archive2_/002-band-management/spec.md requires the opposite: FR-010 (line 260) says "Band count changes MUST apply parameter smoothing ... to prevent clicks", SC-002 (line 337) says "Band count changes complete without audio glitches (no clicks detected in summed output during transition)", and the edge case at line 230 says "smoothly reconfigures without clicks". The 004 spec (line 135) says the same.

5. No existing test pins the transition. IT-003 (band_management_integration_test.cpp:137-172) feeds DC through a bare CrossoverNetwork and compares only the settled sums, 4000 samples before and after the change. It never looks at the transition samples, and it bypasses the processor and the band processors.

6. The measurement is sound. specs/disrumpo-audit/probes/audit_probes.cpp.txt:1190-1191 drives band count 2->4->1 on a 220 Hz, -12 dBFS sine. continuityAround (943-955) compares the largest sample-to-sample jump in the 50 ms after the step with the larger of the pre- and post-step baselines. Ratios of 3.78 and 3.90, each with 1 detected click, are real discontinuities, not a level change.

The fix is reachable in a real host because band count is an automatable parameter. Medium severity stands: it is a discrete control that is seldom automated, but the click is audible and it breaks a stated SC.

I could not refute this. The code and the measurement both confirm the claim.

Code path:
- processor_params.cpp:339-346 handles kBandCountId inside processParameterChanges on the audio thread. It stores bandCount_ and calls crossoverL_/R_.setBandCount(clamped) with no ramp.
- crossover_network.h:111-122: setBandCount sets numBands_ = newBandCount at once, then calls redistributeCrossovers (274-297). That function re-tunes the crossovers (redistributeIncreasing 301-365 calls setCrossoverFrequency on crossovers_[i]) and calls updateAllpassCoefficients (380-397).
- It never resets the filter state of the newly used crossovers_[k] or allpasses_. The splits used before keep their state but now have a different job. In 2 -> 4, band 1 changes from "everything above f0" to HP(f0)*LP(f1).
- process() (185-228) switches its loop bounds to the new numBands_ on the next sample. 4 -> 1 jumps straight to bands[0] = input (195-198).
- processor.cpp:100 is the only prepare call for the crossovers; it is in setupProcessing and not on this path.
- processor.cpp:463-499: the per-sample loop `for b < numBands` starts or stops summing bandProcessors_[b] on the same sample. A newly added BandProcessor joins with whatever state it had when it last ran, with no fade-in.
- Even with ideal filter state the change cannot be smooth. A 2-band and a 4-band LR4+allpass sum differ in their allpass phase response, so the waveform jumps in phase at the switch sample, while the steady-state level is the same.

Measurement: f:/tmp/disrumpo-audit/probe-results.txt lines 27-28.
- automation:bandcount2-4-1 step1 reads jump_ratio 3.78 with clicks_step = 1. Step2 reads 3.90 with clicks_step = 1. clicks_pre_samelen is 0 for both.
- pre/post levels are -18.23 / -18.24 dB and -18.23 / -18.22 dB. The level is unchanged, so the transient is a pure discontinuity, not a gain change.
- Control rows from the same run are clean. mute-band0 and solo-band1 read 0.92-1.00 with 0 clicks (they go through BandProcessor smoothers). drive, mix and osmax steps read 1.00.
- The probe method (audit_probes.cpp.txt:1123-1157, continuityAround 943-955) compares the largest sample-to-sample jump in the 50 ms after the step against the steady state before and after it.
