Size: for a 220 Hz sine at about -18 dB RMS, the largest steady-state step is about 0.005, so 3.8x is roughly a 0.02 step (about -34 dBFS). That is audible as a tick on clean or sustained material. It would be less visible on heavily distorted, bright signals.

Reach: parameter_registration.cpp:65-77 registers Band Count with kCanAutomate, so it can be automated from the host. It is also changed from the UI during playback.

Severity: medium stands. This is a click on an automatable structural parameter. There is no NaN and no runaway output.

findings.title: Node type change swaps the adapter type instantly (small level jump)
findings.problem: The kNodeType handler changes mn.type and re-maps the slots, and setMorphNodes then makes MorphEngine/DistortionAdapter::setType switch processRaw at once, with no state reset or crossfade.
findings.why_wrong: Changing the transfer function on the audio path should be crossfaded to avoid a discontinuity.
findings.consequence: A slight jump (ratio 1.37) when the type is automated or switched during playback.
findings.suggested_fix: Crossfade old and new type over a few ms in the adapter or MorphEngine. Test: the automation:type-switch jump ratio must be <= 1.3.
findings.evidence: probe automation:type-switch (SoftClip drive 3 -> SineFold): "jump_ratio 1.37, clicks 0" (threshold <= 1.3). Code: processor_params.cpp:847 `mn.type = newType;` then :852 `mapShapeSlotsToParams(mn.type, mn.shapeSlots, mn.params);`
verifier_notes:
The claimed code path is accurate. processor_params.cpp:840-853: kNodeType sets `mn.type = newType` (848), restores the shadow slots (850) and re-maps them with mapShapeSlotsToParams (852). Then :899 calls `bandProcessors_[band].setMorphNodes(cache.nodes, ...)`. MorphEngine::setNodes (morph_engine.cpp:131-140) calls `adapters_[i].setType(nodes_[i].type)` for every node. DistortionAdapter::setType (distortion_adapter.cpp:142-162) only sets currentType_, updates the DC-blocker state and sets the block-based flags. The very next processed sample therefore goes through the new transfer function. Nothing on this path crossfades or ramps. BandProcessor's only crossfade (band_processor.h:651-706, 8 ms) fires on an oversampling-factor change, not a type change. The cross-family equal-power blend in the MorphEngine (morph_engine.cpp:722-755) follows the cursor weights, not a node's type changing.

The measurement is real. The finding quotes the code correctly (its "847" is really 848, a trivial offset). /f/tmp/disrumpo-audit/probe-results.txt:38 has `automation:type-switch ... = 1.37,0,0,0,-6.62,-14.66`, rated suspicious against a <=1.3 threshold. The probe (audit_probes.cpp.txt:1199-1201) does step to SineFold, as the finding says, although its label still says HardClip. The ratio comes from continuityAround (audit_probes.cpp.txt:943-955): the largest sample-to-sample jump in the 50 ms after the step, divided by the larger of the steady-state jumps before and after. The after window is already SineFold, so the 1.37 cannot be explained by SineFold simply having steeper slopes. It is a real transient at the switch. No spec in specs/Disrumpo asks for a crossfade on type change, so this is a quality defect, not a spec violation.

Two caveats keep the severity at low. First, the click detector found 0 clicks. Second, most of the "level jump" (pre -6.62 dB, post -14.66 dB) is the built-in level difference between SoftClip and SineFold, which a few-ms crossfade would not remove; a crossfade only softens the waveform step.

I could not refute this. The swap is instant in source, the spec asks for a crossfade, and nothing upstream guards it.
(1) processor_params.cpp:840-853: the kNodeType case sets `mn.type = newType` (848), reloads the shadow slots (850) and remaps the params (852). Then processor_params.cpp:899 calls `bandProcessors_[band].setMorphNodes(cache.nodes, ...)`.
(2) band_processor.h:247-253 forwards to `morphEngine_->setNodes`. morph_engine.cpp:131-140 then calls `adapters_[i].setType(nodes_[i].type)` straight away, with no fade and no state handover.
(3) distortion_adapter.cpp:142-162 setType only assigns `currentType_`, updates the DC-blocker state and sets the block-based flags. It has no crossfade or ramp.
(4) The only crossfade on this path is BandProcessor's 8 ms oversampling-factor crossfade (band_processor.h:51-52, 409-427, 653-676). It fires only when the OS factor changes, and both sides of it run the new type, so it does not blend old type into new.
(5) The spec does not treat this as a design choice. It asks for the opposite: specs/Disrumpo/dsp-details.md:2122, section 16.1 Automation Smoothing, says "Discrete (type, mode) | 5 ms crossfade | Prevent clicks". So the code also falls short of the documented spec.
(6) The measurement is real. specs/disrumpo-audit/probes/audit_probes.cpp.txt:1199-1201 steps the node type from SoftClip to SineFold in a 1-band setup with drive 0.3 normalized (3). `jump_ratio` (943-949) is the largest sample-to-sample jump in the 50 ms event window divided by the larger of the steady-state pre and post maxima. A value of 1.37 means the switch makes a step bigger than either waveform makes on its own; the probe grades anything above 1.3 as suspicious (1149).
(7) No test pins or excuses the behaviour.
Minor note: the probe's label says "-> HardClip", but the code switches to SineFold, as the finding says.
Low severity is right: the probe counted 0 clicks and the ratio is only just over the bar. Type is a discrete parameter, so automating it during playback is uncommon, but it is reachable from any host.

I could not refute this. The switch is instant, and the project's own spec asks for a crossfade.

Code path:
- processor_params.cpp:840-853: the kNodeType handler quantizes `value*25+0.5` and assigns `mn.type = newType` (:848). It swaps the shape-slot shadow (:847/:850), calls mapShapeSlotsToParams (:852), and then pushes the change through `bandProcessors_[band].setMorphNodes(cache.nodes, ...)` (:899).
- MorphEngine::setNodes (morph_engine.cpp:131-140) calls `adapters_[i].setType(nodes_[i].type)` directly for every node.
- DistortionAdapter::setType (distortion_adapter.cpp:142-162) only assigns `currentType_`, runs updateDCBlockerState() and updates the block-latency flags. Nothing in that path ramps the change, resets state or keeps an old/new pair for a crossfade.
- The blended path (morph_engine.cpp:706) also switches `blendedAdapter_.setType(...)` instantly.
- So on the next sample the output jumps from f_old(x) to f_new(x).

Spec: specs/Disrumpo/dsp-details.md:2117-2122 says "All parameters use smoothing", with "Discrete (type, mode) | 5 ms crossfade | Prevent clicks". This is therefore a documented spec deviation, not an intentional design choice.

Impact, quantified from the probe code (specs/disrumpo-audit/probes/audit_probes.cpp.txt):
- How the metric works:
  - The automation() helper (:1123-1157) and continuityAround() (:943-955) compute jump_ratio. That is the largest sample-to-sample step in the 50 ms after the change, divided by the larger of the largest steady-state steps before and after.
  - The setup is 1 band, 220 Hz at -12 dBFS, 48 kHz, block 512.
- What it measured:
  - The type-switch case (:1199-1201, SoftClip drive 3 -> SineFold) read 1.37, with 0 clicks from the click detector.
  - The probe's own scale puts 1.37 in the "suspicious" band (<=1.3 ok, <=2 suspicious; level 1), not the defect band.
  - The probe's description says "-> HardClip" but the code sets SineFold. The label is wrong; the measurement is not.
- So the claimed consequence, a slight single-sample jump on type automation, does occur, and at the claimed size.
- Only one type pair at moderate drive was measured. Pairs with very different outputs (e.g. a fuzz or bit-crusher next to a gentle saturator at high drive) could step by up to |f_new(x)-f_old(x)|, near full scale, but no number was measured for that.
- The type parameter is a 26-entry list, so the switch happens only on a discrete edit or automation step.

Low severity stands on the measured evidence.

findings.title: Stochastic type outputs -10 dBFS of noise from digital silence: jitter offset is added to the input before the shaper and nothing blocks DC
findings.problem: `const float jitterOffset = jitterAmount_ * smoothedJitter * kMaxJitterOffset + driftOffset;` and then `float out = waveshaper_.process(x + jitterOffset);`. With x = 0 the output is waveshaper(offset), a wandering noise/DC signal. The adapter adds no DC blocker or gate for Stochastic (distortion_adapter.cpp:586-591, processRaw :573-575).
findings.why_wrong: A distortion effect must be silent for silent input. The jitter should modulate the shaper's transfer function around the signal, or be subtracted (out - shaper(offset)), so that 0 maps to 0.
findings.consequence: With Stochastic selected the plugin emits -10 dBFS of noise when the input stops (-5.7 dBFS in the tail). Stochastic_Burst also shows DC 0.156. StochasticShaper is a shared KrateDSP primitive, but grep finds Disrumpo as its only consumer.
findings.suggested_fix: Subtract shaper(jitterOffset) from the output (keeping silence at 0), or add a DC blocker and silence gate in the adapter for Stochastic. Test: the selfnoise:Stochastic probe must read <= -90 dBFS. Add a dsp_primitives test that StochasticShaper outputs 0 for input 0.
findings.evidence: probe selfnoise:Stochastic: "rms_dBFS -10.4, nonfinite 0" (threshold <= -90 dBFS), "The tail 1-1.5 s after input stops is -5.7 dBFS". Code: stochastic_shaper.h:563 `const float jitterOffset = jitterAmount_ * smoothedJitter * kMaxJitterOffset + driftOffset;`, :583 `float out = waveshaper_.process(x + jitterOffset);`
verifier_notes:
The code does what the finding says. stochastic_shaper.h:565 computes `jitterOffset = jitterAmount_ * smoothedJitter * kMaxJitterOffset + driftOffset`, with kMaxJitterOffset = 0.5 (:166) and kDriftMaxOffset = 0.3 (:171). :584 then runs `waveshaper_.process(x + jitterOffset)`. Nothing subtracts shaper(offset) and nothing gates the output, so for x = 0 the output is waveshaper(offset): a random signal driven by the RNG (:541-552) that keeps running with no input.

Disrumpo's default is jitterAmount = 0.2 (distortion_adapter.h:200), so the offset is non-zero by default. On the adapter path, DistortionAdapter::process (distortion_adapter.cpp:189-236) passes the input straight to processRaw for Stochastic (:207-209). processRaw hands it to stochastic_.process (:573-575). The DC blocker runs only when needsDCBlock_ is set (:218). updateDCBlockerState (:586-592) sets it only for AsymmetricFuzz, FullRectify, HalfRectify and FeedbackDist, so Stochastic gets no DC blocking. The only gate is drive < 0.0001 (:191), which does not apply at normal drive. The tone filter and mix follow, and neither removes DC or the noise.

The measurement agrees: f:/tmp/disrumpo-audit/probe-results.txt:421 reads `selfnoise:Stochastic ... rms_dBFS -10.4, nonfinite 0 | bad`, and every other type reads <= -86 dBFS. :461 reads `tail:Stochastic ... -5.7`. :329 reads `preset:Experimental/Stochastic_Burst ... |dc| 0.156`. The probe source is specs/disrumpo-audit/probes/audit_probes.cpp.txt:500-511.

The archived spec's FR-022 does define output = waveshaper(input + jitterOffset), so the formula is deliberate. Even so, a distortion effect putting out -10 dBFS of noise from digital silence is still a real defect, and the finding's claim holds.

The defect is real. Nothing upstream or downstream guards it, no test pins the behaviour, and no spec calls it intended.

1. The code matches the claim. stochastic_shaper.h:565 computes `jitterOffset = jitterAmount_ * smoothedJitter * kMaxJitterOffset + driftOffset`, and :583-584 sets the drive and calls `waveshaper_.process(x + jitterOffset)`. When x = 0 the output is waveshaper(offset), not 0. The output smoother at :587-590 only low-passes that value.

2. The primitive does this on purpose and hands DC removal to whoever uses it. The header says "No internal DC blocking: Compose with DCBlocker for asymmetric types" (:22, :135, :157), and FR-022 defines the offset that way. So the fault is in Disrumpo's adapter, which uses the primitive without that protection. It is not in the shared primitive.

3. The adapter does not add any protection.
   - distortion_adapter.cpp:207-209 passes the raw input to Stochastic, and :215 calls `processRaw`, which calls `stochastic_.process` (:573-575).
   - :218 runs the DC blocker only if `needsDCBlock_` is set. `updateDCBlockerState` (:586-592) sets it only for AsymmetricFuzz, FullRectify, HalfRectify and FeedbackDist; Stochastic is not in the list.
   - The adapter's only gate is the drive gate at :191 (drive < 0.0001). There is no silence gate.
   - Routing (:951-963) passes the shipped default jitterAmount 0.2 and coefficientNoise 0.1 (distortion_adapter.h:200-202), so the default patch is affected.
   - A grep of plugins/disrumpo/src finds no other DC blocker or silence gate in the band or processor code.

4. Neither the spec nor the tests treat it as a design decision.
   - specs/Disrumpo/dsp-details.md:543-548 describes D25 as a "randomized transfer function simulating analog component tolerance variation", with "Analog warmth" as the use case. That is a varied curve around the signal, not a noise source.
   - No Disrumpo test checks Stochastic with silent input (distortion_adapter_test.cpp:2093 only checks parameters), and stochastic_shaper_test.cpp has no silence or DC test.

5. The quoted measurement is sound. audit_probes.cpp.txt:499-512 renders 1 s of silence at drive 1.0 after a fresh activate and takes the RMS of the last 0.5 s. With drive 1.0 and offsets of about ±0.1 through tanh, an output near -10 dBFS is plausible. The probe's `noiseByDesign` exemption (:411-414) applies only to the adapter-vs-processor check, not to self-noise.

The severity of high is correct. One caveat on the fix: the adapter's 10 Hz DCBlocker (:31) alone would not remove a 10 Hz wandering offset. Subtracting shaper(jitterOffset) or adding a silence gate is the effective fix.

The code path is real. stochastic_shaper.h:565 computes `jitterOffset = jitterAmount_ * smoothedJitter * kMaxJitterOffset + driftOffset` (kMaxJitterOffset 0.5 at :166, kDriftMaxOffset 0.3 at :171), and :584 returns `waveshaper_.process(x + jitterOffset)`. With x = 0 the output is therefore shaper(offset), which is not zero. Disrumpo's default `jitterAmount = 0.2f` (distortion_adapter.h:200) gives an offset of up to ±0.1. For Stochastic the adapter does not pre-scale the input (distortion_adapter.cpp:207-209); it passes the drive in through `stochastic_.setDrive(commonParams_.drive)` (:956), and drive is the normalized value ×10 (processor_params.cpp:858). At drive 1.0 that is tanh(±1), about 0.76 peak, so the probe's -10.4 dBFS RMS is consistent with the code. Nothing removes it: `needsDCBlock_` covers only AsymmetricFuzz, FullRectify, HalfRectify and FeedbackDist (distortion_adapter.cpp:588-591). The primitive's header says at line 21 that it does no internal DC blocking (Principle X), which makes blocking the caller's job, and the adapter does not do it. The only drive gate is drive < 0.0001 (:191). The probe (specs/disrumpo-audit/probes/audit_probes.cpp.txt:500-512) measures this directly: fresh activate, silent input, drive 1.0, RMS of the last 0.5 s. So the defect is confirmed.

Severity should drop to medium:
(1) The jitter is a sample-and-hold at jitterRate (default 10 Hz, samplesPerUpdate = sr/rate at :685), smoothed by a one-pole of 800/rate ms (80 ms at default, :666-678). The "noise" is therefore mostly sub-10 Hz wander and DC rather than broadband hiss. It is mostly inaudible rumble, although it still eats headroom, moves meters and limiters, and drives speaker excursion. Only high jitter rates (up to 100 Hz) make it an audible rumble.
(2) -10 dBFS is the maximum-drive case (normalized 1.0 = 10x). At drive 1x the floor is about tanh(0.1), roughly -20 dBFS peak and lower in RMS.
(3) It happens only when Stochastic is the active type with jitter > 0.

The claim that the defect lives in the shared primitive is partly wrong. The primitive behaves as documented (spec FR-022 and the line-21 "no internal DC blocking" note), so the fix belongs in the Disrumpo adapter: add Stochastic to `needsDCBlock_` and/or subtract shaper(offset). It does not need a change to KrateDSP's contract.

findings.title: Quantize maps silence to a non-zero level (-49 dBFS from silent input)
findings.problem: `index = (input + 1)/stepSize; index += quantOffset; index = round(index) - quantOffset;`. With an even or fractional level count, or a non-integer offset, input 0 rounds to a level that is not 0. Quantize also skips the DC blocker and the tone filter.
findings.why_wrong: The quantiser should be mid-tread around 0 (or have its DC removed) so that silence stays silent.
findings.consequence: A constant offset or idle tone at -49 dBFS whenever Quantize is active and the input is silent. It adds to the DC found in presets.
findings.suggested_fix: Quantize on a grid centred at 0 (round(x/step)*step), apply the offset as a symmetric shift, and add Quantize to the DC-block list. Test: the selfnoise:Quantize probe must read <= -90 dBFS.
findings.evidence: probe selfnoise:Quantize: "rms_dBFS -49.0" (threshold <= -90 dBFS), "the tail is -48.8 dBFS". Code: distortion_adapter.cpp:487 `float index = (input + 1.0f) / stepSize;`, :501 `index = std::round(index) - typeParams_.quantOffset;`
verifier_notes: I traced the code and the finding holds. In distortion_adapter.cpp:482-510, numLevels = 2 + quantLevels*62 and step = 2/(N-1). For input 0, index = 1/step = (N-1)/2. Line 489 adds quantOffset, line 492-501 adds TPDF dither, and line 505 does round(index) - quantOffset. A node starts with every shape slot at 0.5 (morph_node.h:43, mapped at processor_params.cpp:145-151), so a fresh Quantize node has quantLevels 0.5 (N=33, index 16), dither 0.5 and quantOffset 0.5. The index then sits at 16.5 plus TPDF dither in [-0.5, 0.5]. round() gives 16 or 17, and after the offset is subtracted that is 15.5 or 16.5. The output is therefore -1/32 or +1/32 (-30 dBFS) on every silent sample. It passes the smoothing lowpass (smoothness 0.5 > 0.001, line 513), which fits the measured -49 dBFS. With dither 0 it becomes a constant DC of +1/32. An even or fractional N (any quantLevels other than k/62 with odd N) also puts input 0 at a half-step or other non-zero level, so the "even or fractional level count" part of the claim is right. The claim that Quantize skips both cleanups is also confirmed: needsDCBlock_ covers only AsymmetricFuzz, FullRectify, HalfRectify and FeedbackDist (lines 586-592), and the tone filter is explicitly skipped for Quantize (lines 225-231). The drive gate (line 191) does not apply at drive 1.0. The quoted probe (audit_probes.cpp.txt:499-511) uses default slots, fresh activate, silent input and drive 1.0, which matches this analysis. The comment at line 488 says the offset is meant to shift the grid, but turning silence into audible -49 dBFS hiss or DC at default settings is a real defect. Medium severity is appropriate.

I could not refute this from the code. Only one part of it is intentional.

**The defect holds with the default parameters.**
- morph_node.h:43-44 starts every shape slot at 0.5.
- processor_params.cpp:145-151 maps those slots straight through: quantLevels=0.5, dither=0.5, smoothness=0.5, quantOffset=0.5.
- distortion_adapter.cpp:482-483 then gives N = 2 + 0.5*62 = 33 levels, so step = 1/16.
- For silent input, :486 gives index = 16 and :489 adds the offset, making it 16.5.
  - With dither 0, std::round(16.5) = 17, and :505 subtracts the offset to leave 16.5. :509 then outputs 16.5/16 - 1 = +0.03125, a constant -30 dBFS DC before the smoothing filter.
  - With the default dither 0.5, the TPDF term at :501 is ±0.5 index, so the rounding flips between 16 and 17. The output is then ±0.03125 of idle noise.
- With offset 0 and an even N (2-level at quantLevels=0), 0 maps to ±1.
- So "undo offset" leaves a half-step bias. This is not a mid-tread grid.
- The probe that measured -49 dBFS is real: specs/disrumpo-audit/probes/audit_probes.cpp.txt:499-511 (fresh activate, silence, drive 1.0, default slots). The figure fits the -30 dBFS raw level after the 0.5 smoothing lowpass at :513-514.

**Nothing downstream guards it.**
- DistortionAdapter::process (:189-236) has only a drive gate at :191, and drive is 10 here.
- updateDCBlockerState (:586-592) applies the DC blocker only to AsymmetricFuzz, FullRectify, HalfRectify and FeedbackDist. Quantize gets none.

**Not a documented design decision.**
- The shared BitCrusher primitive (dsp/include/krate/dsp/primitives/bit_crusher.h:92-101) records exactly this pattern as a fixed bug: "OLD BUG: Round-trip through [0,1] created 0.0 -> 0.00002 offset; NEW: Symmetric quantization guarantees 0.0 -> 0.0". Quantize still uses that [0,N-1] round trip.
- The comment at :488 only says the offset shifts the grid "for asymmetric harmonics". It does not say silence should produce output.
- No test pins silent-input behaviour. distortion_adapter_test.cpp:2566 only allows zero to round either way in the 2-level, offset-0 case. Tests :2616 and :2653 only check that offset and dither change a non-zero input.

**The one intentional part:** skipping the tone filter for Quantize (:222-229) is a deliberate design choice, so that sub-claim is refuted. It does not cause the silence-to-noise defect.

Medium severity stands, because the factory default slots already trigger it.

The defect is real, and it shows up with the default parameters. Only part of the "constant offset / DC" wording holds.

Code path:
- distortion_adapter.cpp:189-215: silence is only passed through when drive < 0.0001. Otherwise wet = 0*drive = 0 goes into processRaw.
- Quantize (482-517): numLevels = 2 + quantLevels*62, step = 2/(N-1), index = (0+1)/step = (N-1)/2, then index += quantOffset, optional TPDF dither, then index = round(index) - quantOffset, and out = index*step - 1.
- Defaults: a fresh node's shape slots are all 0.5 (morph_node.h:43). processor_params.cpp:145-151 maps them to quantLevels 0.5, dither 0.5, smoothness 0.5 and quantOffset 0.5.
- With those values, N = 33 and step = 0.0625. Silence gives index 16.5 + u, where u is the TPDF dither in (-0.5, 0.5). That rounds to 16 or 17, which becomes 15.5 or 16.5 once the offset is removed. The output is ±step/2 = ±0.03125 (about -30 dBFS) chosen at random.
- That noise then goes through the smoothing lowpass at 513-515. This matches the probe's -49 dBFS RMS from silence (audit_probes.cpp.txt:499-511: fresh activate, drive 1.0, RMS of the last 0.5 s).
- Nothing removes it downstream. Quantize is not in needsDCBlock_ (586-591) and is excluded from applyTone (225-229).

Impact:
- With dither at its default 0.5 the output is zero-mean hiss at about -49 dBFS, not DC. The finding's "adds to the DC found in presets" claim only applies when dither is 0 and the offset is not an integer. Then round-half-away gives a constant +step/2 (about -30 dBFS DC for N = 33; up to -36 dB at N = 64).
- With offset 0 and an odd N, silence stays silent. With an even or non-integer N, silence gives a DC error of up to ±1/(N-1).
- A -49 dBFS noise floor whenever a Quantize node is active, from the default parameters, is clearly audible in quiet passages. Medium severity stands.
- Caveat: a dithered lo-fi quantiser making some noise is partly by design. But the size of this one comes from the generic default slot value of 0.5 putting the grid in mid-rise, not from a deliberate per-type choice.

findings.title: Factory presets and digital types peak above 0 dBFS (up to +11 dBFS): drive multiplies into non-saturating shapers with no output normalisation
findings.problem: `wet = input * commonParams_.drive;` (drive 0-10) feeds Aliasing, SampleReduce, BitwiseMangler, Granular, Chaos and Spectral, which do not bound their output. Nothing compensates gain or limits after the adapter.
findings.why_wrong: Drive should push the signal into a shaper, not act as a +20 dB linear gain on transparent digital types. Factory presets should not clip from a -12 dBFS input.
findings.consequence: 11 factory presets exceed 0 dBFS from a -12 dBFS input (Spectral_Morph +4.84 dBFS), and digital types reach +11 dBFS, clipping the host bus.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply drive-dependent output compensation for the non-saturating types, or bound their output, and re-level the affected presets. Test: all presets peak <= 0 dBFS at -12 dBFS input, and each type peaks <= +6 dBFS at drive 1.0.
findings.evidence: probe preset levels: peak above 0 dBFS (11 presets): "Spectral_Morph +4.84, Digital_Organic +4.41, Granular_Crush +3.94, Ring_Mod_Lead +3.09, Fractal_Noise +3.02, ...". type: peak above 0 dBFS: "Aliasing +8.55/+11.10; SampleReduce +8.49/+10.96; BitwiseMangler +2.48/+4.98; Granular +1.4..+4.6; Chaos +1.7/+3.6; Spectral +0.46/+2.96". Code: distortion_adapter.cpp:211 `wet = input * commonParams_.drive;`
verifier_notes:
Code matches the claim. distortion_adapter.cpp:206-212 does `wet = input * commonParams_.drive` for every type except Temporal and Stochastic. Drive's plain range is 0-10 with default 1.0 (parameter_registration.cpp:912-915). For Aliasing (:520-522 aliasing_.process), SampleReduce (:474-476 srReducer_.process) and BitwiseMangler (:524-526), processRaw passes the scaled signal to processors that do not change its level. After that the adapter applies only an optional DC blocker (:218), tone (:225-231, skipped for these digital types) and the dry/wet mix (:234-235). Processor.cpp has no limiter or clamp on the output: grepping it for clamp/limit/tanh finds only the sweep-frequency clamp at :365.

The measurements in f:/tmp/disrumpo-audit/probe-results.txt match the quoted numbers:
- Aliasing: -0.94 / +8.55 / +11.10 dBFS at normalized drive 0.25 / 0.75 / 1.0.
- SampleReduce: -1.06 / +8.49 / +10.96 dBFS, i.e. -6 dBFS input times drive, as plain gain.
- Bitcrush stays at -3.01 dBFS and Quantize at about -5 dBFS. Those two types bound their output and Aliasing and SampleReduce do not, so the digital types are inconsistent with each other.
- 11 presets peak above 0 dBFS from a -12 dBFS input, including Spectral_Morph +4.84, Digital_Organic +4.41, Granular_Crush +3.94 (RMS +0.06 dBFS, a gain of about 12 dB) and Ring_Mod_Lead +3.09.

So the defect is real. Severity should go down, for three reasons:
1. The per-type numbers come from a -6 dBFS input at the top of the drive range (7.5x and 10x), not from a typical setting.
2. Line 211 does not explain all of the over-0 dBFS presets. Stochastic_Burst uses a type that is exempt from the drive multiply (:207-209). Chua_Circuit, Chaos_Lead, Fractal_Noise and Spectral_Morph carry large DC (|dc| 0.11-0.205), which points to a separate DC/bias cause rather than drive gain.
3. A float VST3 output above 0 dBFS does not clip inside the plugin or on a floating-point host bus, so "clipping the host bus" overstates the consequence.

What remains is a level-staging and preset-levelling problem, not signal corruption.

The code matches the claim, and nothing upstream or downstream guards against it. distortion_adapter.cpp:206-212 multiplies every type except Temporal and Stochastic by commonParams_.drive. The spec sets that range at dsp-details.md:165-167 (kMaxDrive 10, default 1). For the digital types, processRaw just forwards the driven sample: SampleReduce `srReducer_.process(input)` (:476), Aliasing `aliasing_.process(input)` (:522), BitwiseMangler (:526), Chaos (:555), Granular (:563), Spectral (:567). Their setters (:716-737) set no amplitude bound. After processRaw there is only the optional DC blocker, a tone filter (skipped for Aliasing, SampleReduce and BitwiseMangler, :225-231) and the dry/wet mix (:234-235). There is no output compensation or limiter, and the only global stage left is the user-set output gain. specs/Disrumpo has no design note on auto-gain, gain compensation or preset level matching (grep of specs/Disrumpo found nothing), and no test pins preset peak levels (grep of plugins/disrumpo/tests found nothing). The presets are not re-levelled: tools/disrumpo_preset_generator.cpp:237 sets outputGain = 0.5f (0 dB) for every preset. Spectral Morph (:1644-1671) sets drive 2.0-2.5 on Spectral, Granular and Fractal nodes, so a -12 dBFS input coming out at about +5 dBFS is consistent with the code. The probe code that produced the numbers is real: specs/disrumpo-audit/probes/audit_probes.cpp.txt:420-466 for the per-type test and :1490-1544 for the presets. I cannot refute the finding, but I recommend downgrading it. The per-type "+11 dBFS" readings are taken at normalized drive 0.75 and 1.0 (linear 7.5 and 10) on a -6 dBFS sine (audit_probes.cpp.txt:429, :439). That is the specified maximum drive behaving as linear gain on amplitude-transparent types: a gain-staging and UX choice, not a computation error. The output is 32-bit float, so nothing clips inside the plugin; it clips only if the host's master bus or converter is driven past full scale, and the user's output gain can correct it. The real defect is the 11 factory presets running about +12 to +17 dB louder than bypass with no level matching, which makes this low severity.

Code confirmed: distortion_adapter.cpp:206-212 multiplies the input by commonParams_.drive (0-10) for every type except Temporal and Stochastic. The wet signal then goes through processRaw (:215), an optional DC blocker (:218-220) and tone, which is skipped for SampleReduce, Aliasing and BitwiseMangler (:225-231), and the mix (:234-235). No gain compensation is applied. processor.cpp has no limiter or output clamp: a grep for clamp/limit/tanh/compensat finds only the sweep-frequency clamp at :365. So for types that do not bound level, drive works as a linear gain of up to +20 dB.

The quoted numbers match the probe setup in specs/disrumpo-audit/probes/audit_probes.cpp.txt:429-466. The input there is a -6 dBFS sine at normalized drive 0.25, 0.75 and 1.0, which means drive 2.5, 7.5 and 10. For Aliasing, 0.5 x 7.5 gives +11.5 dBFS and 0.5 x 10 gives +14 dBFS. The measured +8.55 and +11.10 dBFS are close to plain linear gain, so the mechanism is confirmed. Presets were rendered with a 440 Hz sine at -12 dBFS (:1541), and 11 of them peak above 0 dBFS.

The impact is overstated, which is why I downgrade it.
(1) The per-type peaks above 0 dBFS come only from extreme user settings: drive 7.5 or 10 with a -6 dBFS input. A drive knob that adds gain on a non-saturating digital type is a gain-staging and design weakness, not a malfunction, and the user has output gain and mix to correct it.
(2) "Clipping the host bus" does not happen in floating-point hosts (every mainstream DAW). Values above 0 dBFS pass through intact and only clip at a fixed-point output or converter, so the damage is a loudness jump and a risk of clipping downstream, not distortion inside Disrumpo.
(3) The real user-facing part is 11 factory presets peaking +3 to +4.8 dBFS from a -12 dBFS sine, a gain of roughly 15-17 dB. That is a preset levelling problem that output gain in the presets can fix.
(4) I did not check that every over-level preset (Spectral_Morph, Digital_Organic, Ring_Mod_Lead, Fractal_Noise) is driven over by drive on a non-saturating type rather than by band or output gain, so the stated root cause covers only part of the preset list.

NaN/Inf and DSP correctness are not affected. Real but overstated: low severity.

findings.title: SergeFold (and the Sine/Triangle folds) are nearly silent in the plugin (-36 to -47 dBFS peak from -6 dBFS input)
findings.problem: SergeFold feeds the shared WavefolderProcessor one sample at a time inside the adapter, which is prepared at 8x and processes L and R interleaved (band_processor.h:111,124,487-488). The same adapter at 48 kHz mono gives normal output. The loss therefore comes from the Disrumpo wiring: the rate mismatch and shared state on wavefolder_'s smoothers and DC blocker, plus the tone LP at about 1 kHz removing the fold harmonics. The exact split between those causes was not isolated.
findings.why_wrong: A distortion type at full drive should produce output near the input level, as the adapter does when prepared and clocked correctly.
findings.consequence: Three wavefolder types are nearly unusable, and their energy is dominated by non-harmonic content.
findings.suggested_fix: Fix the 8x prepare and the L/R sharing, then re-measure. Test: type:SergeFold peak within 6 dB of the adapter@48k and centroid ratio 0.85-1.15.
findings.evidence: probe type:SergeFold (drive 0.25/0.75/1.0): "-14.2,-3.7e-08,0,-47.18 | 17.3,2.2e-08,0,-47.52 | 24.6,-5.2e-09,0,-35.93" (nonharm_dB,dc,nonfinite,peak_dBFS). "The adapter at 48k gives a 6424 Hz centroid; the Processor gives 497 Hz." type:SineFold/TriangleFold drive=1.00 peak "-31.04" dBFS. Code: distortion_adapter.cpp:413 `float biased = input + typeParams_.bias;`, :415 `wavefolder_.process(singleSampleBuffer_, 1);`
verifier_notes:
The low processor levels are measured (f:/tmp/disrumpo-audit/probe-results.txt:521-526). The finding's explanation for them does not hold up against the code or against its own probe numbers.

1) The claim that "the same adapter at 48 kHz mono gives normal output" is contradicted by the probe. Row 18 (adapter-vs-processor:SergeFold) gives rms_diff(proc-adapter) = -11.92 dB. That row compares against keep075, which is oL at drive 0.75 (audit_probes.cpp.txt:467, 526-532). Row 522 puts the processor peak for that render at -47.52 dBFS. RMS can never exceed peak, so the adapter's RMS is at most about -35.6 dBFS. That is not "near the input level" (-6 dBFS peak). The adapter itself, prepared at 48 kHz with the same DistortionParams (audit_probes.cpp.txt:516-524), is nearly as quiet. So the loss does not come from the Disrumpo 8x/L-R wiring.

2) The extra loss that is specific to the fold types is small. Non-fold types show about -6 dB processor-vs-adapter everywhere: SoftClip -6.14, Tube -5.99, HardClip -6.17 (rows 14, 20, 26). The fold types show -11.4 to -11.9 dB, so only about 5-6 dB is fold-specific. The 48 kHz adapter runs SergeFold without oversampling (centroid 6424 Hz, i.e. heavy aliased content). The processor runs it at its 4x profile (distortion_types.h:173-181) and the downsampler removes that aliased energy. The comparison is therefore apples-to-oranges and accounts for part of the gap. It does not support "nearly silent because of wiring".

3) The proposed mechanism does not apply to the probe's conditions:
- Rate mismatch: the adapter is prepared at sampleRate*8 (band_processor.h:111-112, 124-125). In the 4x path (band_processor.h:719-723, 744-758), processOversampledBlock calls morphEngine_->process for L and then R on the same instance. That is 2 x 4 x fs = 8 fs calls per second, which equals the prepared rate.
- Shared L/R state: the probe drives L = R (r.render(in, in, ...), audit_probes.cpp.txt:442), so each oversampled sample is simply presented twice. The fold primitive is memoryless: wavefolder.h:263-266 (sineFold), and WavefolderProcessor::process at wavefolder_processor.h:337-377 is offset -> fold -> DC blocker -> mix. The DC blocker (10 Hz), the smoothing LP and the tone LP are LTI one-poles running at their prepared rate, and the 5 ms smoothers are in steady state. Duplicated, identical L/R samples through a memoryless fold plus LTI filters at the matched rate cannot cause a 30-40 dB level loss.
- Tone LP: for the same reason, the "tone LP at about 1 kHz" (4000 Hz / 8 x 2) is not what the filter does under these conditions.

4) The adapter code at distortion_adapter.cpp:410-424 does what it says: bias, then wavefolder_.process, then an optional triangle crossfade, then the smoothing filter. Parameter routing is at :676-690. Nothing there attenuates the signal by 30-40 dB.

Interleaved L/R state sharing is a real but separate defect: it only matters when L differs from R, and the probe's stereo-leak rows report it on their own. The finding's stated cause, its premise ("adapter@48k is normal") and its proposed fix/test (peak within 6 dB of adapter@48k) are not supported, and its own numbers already show the adapter quiet. Refuted on correctness. Whatever makes the fold types quiet sits in the adapter/type defaults or the shared folder, not in the Disrumpo wiring the finding blames.

The symptom is real, but the cause the finding gives is wrong, and so is its premise that the adapter at 48 kHz "gives normal output".

1. The probe's own numbers rule out "normal output at 48k". In f:/tmp/disrumpo-audit/probe-results.txt:18, adapter-vs-processor:SergeFold reads rms_diff(proc-adapter) = -11.92 dB. Line 522 gives the Processor peak at drive 0.75 as -47.52 dBFS, so the Processor RMS is at most -47.5 dBFS. That puts the adapter alone at 48 kHz mono at about -35.6 dBFS RMS or lower, at least 26 dB below the -9 dBFS RMS input. It is nearly silent too. Its 6424 Hz centroid is aliasing at 1x, not a healthy fold. About -6 dB of the -11.9 dB gap appears for every type: SoftClip -6.14, Tube -5.99, and Spectral -6.03 at a pure 1031 Hz centroid (lines 20, 26, 21). That is the -3 dB centre pan law (band_processor.h:500-511) plus the tone LP that the 8x prepare pulls down to about 1 kHz (tone-response rows 466-469: implied fc about 1 kHz instead of 4 kHz; the separate rate-mismatch defect). Only about 6 dB is specific to the folds.

2. The L/R sharing cannot cause the loss. Wavefolder::process is stateless (wavefolder.h:182-205). WavefolderProcessor's only state is three one-pole smoothers whose targets are reset to the same value every sample, plus a 10 Hz DC blocker (wavefolder_processor.h:157-183, 337-377). The probe feeds identical L and R. Interleaving them through band_processor.h:487-488 just shows each stateful element a sample-held signal, so it cannot take 25-40 dB out of a 1 kHz tone.

3. The real cause is the default fold parameters. ShapeShadowStorage sets every slot to 0.5 (morph_node.h:102-106). processor_params.cpp:106-113 maps those to folds = 6.5 and smoothness = 0.5; for SergeFold it also gives foldModel = int(0.5*3+0.5) = 2, which is Buchla259 rather than Serge. Lines 88-104 give the same folds and smoothness to SineFold and TriangleFold. At drive 7.5 with a 0.5 amplitude input, sin(6.5 * 3.75 * x) folds the signal into dense high harmonics. distortion_adapter.cpp:664/673/689 then send it through wavefoldSmoothFilter_ at 20000*(0.025)^0.5 ≈ 3.2 kHz (halved again by the 8x prepare / 4x run mismatch, band_processor.h:111). After that comes the tone LP (distortion_adapter.cpp:230). Little energy is left near the fundamental, which explains the low level in both the adapter and the Processor.

Nothing in specs/Disrumpo or the code comments says these levels are intended, and no test pins them. So a fold type picked at default slots giving -36 to -47 dBFS peak from -6 dBFS input is still a real usability defect.

The suggested fix (8x prepare plus L/R separation) would recover only about 6 dB. The proposed test bar ("within 6 dB of adapter@48k") compares against an adapter that is itself nearly silent, so it could pass while the types stay unusable. The rate mismatch and the L/R sharing are separate findings. Downgrade from high, and send the fix to the default fold, smoothing and model mappings and to output make-up gain.

The measured consequence is real. /f/tmp/disrumpo-audit/probe-results.txt:521-523 has the Processor path for SergeFold at -47.18, -47.52 and -35.93 dBFS peak from a -6 dBFS input, with nonharm +17/+24 dB. Lines 524-526 and 542-544 have SineFold and TriangleFold at -23.2, -26.6 and -31.0 dBFS. The probe drives Processor::process directly (specs/disrumpo-audit/probes/audit_probes.cpp.txt:420-467), so this is what a user hears from a fresh node of these types.

The finding's root-cause story is only partly right, and the suggested fix would not bring the level back near the input:

(1) The plugin wiring problem exists. band_processor.h:111-125 prepares the adapter and MorphEngine at sampleRate*8 whatever the active factor is, and the fold types run at 4x. band_processor.h:487-488 and the legacy path at :494-495 feed L then R through the same adapter. The adapter's one-pole tone filter and wavefoldSmoothFilter_ (distortion_adapter.cpp:27-28, 55-56, 230, 389/406/422) therefore run at a quarter of their design cutoff. The smoothers and DC blocker inside WavefolderProcessor (wavefolder_processor.h:164-180, 339-373) do not matter at steady state: a 10 Hz DC blocker and 5 ms smoothers, fed identical L/R, cannot remove 40 dB.

(2) The probe's own adapter@48k comparison contradicts the claim that "the same adapter at 48 kHz mono gives normal output". probe-results.txt:18 has SergeFold rms_diff(proc-adapter) of only -11.92 dB. With a Processor peak of -47.5 dBFS, the adapter at 48k must also be around -35 to -40 dBFS. About 6 dB of the 11.92 dB gap is common to every type: SoftClip -6.14, Tube -5.99, Spectral -6.03 at lines 20, 26, 21. That leaves roughly 6 dB as fold-specific wiring loss.

(3) Most of SergeFold's quietness comes from its default parameters. MorphNode shape slots default to 0.5 (morph_node.h:43). processor_params.cpp:108-113 maps these to folds = 1 + 0.5*11 = 6.5 and foldModel = int(0.5*3 + 0.5) = 2, which is Buchla259 (distortion_adapter.cpp:678-685), not Serge or Lockhart. applyBuchla259 (wavefolder_processor.h:411-448) triangle-folds at thresholds {0.2..1.0}/6.5 and normalises by the gain sum. That caps the output near 0.07 (about -23 dBFS peak) before any filtering, and makes it dense high-frequency content, which explains the 6424 Hz adapter centroid. The shape=0.5 crossfade with wavefoldTriangle_ (threshold 1/6.5, about -16 dB) at :418-420 adds little level.

So fixing the 8x prepare and the L/R sharing, as suggested, would recover about 6-12 dB. SergeFold would still sit around -35 dBFS. For SineFold and TriangleFold the fix would recover most of the 11.4 dB gap (probe-results.txt:19, 25, centroid ratio 0.494).

Impact: a fresh node of these three types is 17-41 dB quieter than its input. That is a real and audible defect. It is not "unusable": lowering Folds or choosing another model restores the level, and output gain can compensate. The finding also blames the wrong cause for the worst case (SergeFold). Not refuted; severity downgraded.

findings.title: Bands misalign at summation by 3-4 samples depending on type: the mis-rated tone LP is applied to some types and skipped for digital ones
findings.problem: The one-pole tone LP is applied to analog types and skipped for Bitcrush/SampleReduce/Quantize/Aliasing/BitwiseMangler. Because of the 8x prepare and L/R double stepping, the LP sits at about 1/4 of its set cutoff, so its group delay is several samples. Bands with different types therefore get different delays. The 3-sample HardClip-vs-SoftClip difference was not isolated (memoryless processRaw at :261-305).
findings.why_wrong: Per-band paths must stay time-aligned (or report and compensate their latency) for the crossover sum to reconstruct.
findings.consequence: Phase smear and comb colouring at crossovers when adjacent bands use different types.
findings.suggested_fix: Fix the tone filter rate (prepare at the real rate) and re-measure. If misalignment remains, add per-band delay compensation. Test: the band-latency probes must show 0 samples relative delay.
findings.evidence: probe band-latency:processor:HardClip-vs-Bitcrush: "b0_factor,b1_factor,b0_extra_delay_smp,b1_extra_delay_smp,relative_smp = 4,1,4,0,4". HardClip-vs-SoftClip: "4,2,4,1,3" (threshold relative 0). Code: distortion_adapter.cpp:225 `if (currentType_ != DistortionType::Bitcrush && ...` then `wet = applyTone(wet);`
verifier_notes:
The bands do arrive at different times; the probe numbers show that. But the finding blames the wrong mechanism, and the source and the probe's own control case contradict it.

1. The tone LP cannot move an impulse peak. OnePoleLP::process (dsp/include/krate/dsp/primitives/one_pole.h:114) computes `state_ = (1-a)*x + a*state_`. Its impulse response is largest at n=0 and decays from there. The probe (specs/disrumpo-audit/probes/audit_probes.cpp.txt, bandPeak lambda ~:845-852) measures delay as the index of max |oL|. So the tone filter adds about 0 samples to that number, whether it is applied or skipped (distortion_adapter.cpp:225-231).

2. The probe's own control case rules the tone filter out. In HardClip-vs-SoftClip both bands apply the tone filter (neither type is in the skip list at distortion_adapter.cpp:225-229), yet they still differ by 3 samples (factors 4 vs 2). What changes with the factor is the oversampler, not the tone filter.

3. The real source is the oversampler. The 'drive 0' reference takes the direct path with no oversampling (band_processor.h:630-636: `if (bypassDistortion || factor == 1)` processes directly). With drive > 0 the band goes through oversampler2x_/4x_ (band_processor.h:709-727). Those are prepared as Economy/ZeroLatency (band_processor.h:99-104), which are 8-pole IIR filters (oversampler.h:53,60). IIR filters have group delay that depends on the frequency and on how many stages are cascaded. So the measured 'extra delay' of 4/1/0 samples for factors 4/2/1 is the oversampler's IIR group delay. BandProcessor::getLatency() still reports 0 (band_processor.h:376-379).

4. The '1/4 of set cutoff' claim is also wrong for this probe. The adapter is prepared at 8x the rate (band_processor.h:111) but runs at factor 4, so one channel alone would see 1/2 the cutoff. The probe feeds identical L and R (r.render(imp, imp)) into one shared filter state (band_processor.h:756-757 / morph engine L then R). That steps the state twice per oversampled sample, about 384 kHz in total, which puts the cutoff back near the set value.

The suggested fix (prepare the tone filter at the real rate) would leave the misalignment in place. The misalignment itself is real, but it belongs in a separate finding about oversampler IIR group delay that differs by factor and is reported as 0 latency, not in this one about the tone filter. The shared L/R filter state is a separate stereo-state issue as well.

The finding blames the tone LP skip at distortion_adapter.cpp:225-232, but its own probe numbers point to the oversampler instead.

(1) The reference render in the probe (specs/disrumpo-audit/probes/audit_probes.cpp.txt:840-861) is drive 0. At drive 0, BandProcessor::processWithFactor (band_processor.h:629-636) takes the direct path with NO oversampling. So the "extra delay" is mostly the delay of the minimum-phase IIR oversampler for that band's factor, not the tone filter.

(2) The extra delays follow the factor, not whether the tone filter runs:
- HardClip, factor 4, tone applied: 4 samples
- SoftClip, factor 2, tone applied: 1 sample
- Bitcrush, factor 1, no oversampler, tone skipped: 0 samples

HardClip and SoftClip both pass through applyTone (:230), yet they differ by 3 samples. The tone filter cannot be the variable.

(3) The probe measures the index of the impulse-response peak. A one-pole LP (OnePoleLP toneFilter_, distortion_adapter.h:358; applyTone at distortion_adapter.cpp:582-583) has an impulse response that peaks at its first sample and then decays, so it barely moves the peak index. The tone filter does run at the wrong rate: prepare is at 8x (band_processor.h:111) and one adapter processes L and R in turn (band_processor.h:493-494, 756-757). That is a separate issue and not what this probe measured.

(4) The real source of the misalignment is deliberate. Every oversampler is prepared with OversamplingMode::ZeroLatency (band_processor.h:99-107), which the header defines as "IIR filters (minimum-phase, no latency)" (oversampler.h:60). BandProcessor::getLatency returns 0 with the comment "FR-018, FR-019: IIR mode = 0 latency always" (band_processor.h:374-379). Phase delay that varies with the factor is the known cost of that zero-latency choice, not a defect in the lines the finding cites.

(5) The skip list at :223-224 is also documented in its comment: the digital types keep their staircase on purpose.

The suggested fix (prepare the tone filter at the real rate) would not change the 3-4 sample relative delays the probe reports. A finding about per-band IIR phase mismatch would need to target band_processor.h and the ZeroLatency design.

The bands really do arrive at different times, but the cause is not the tone LP, and the suggested fix (re-rate the tone filter) would not change the measured numbers.

1) What the probe measures (specs/disrumpo-audit/probes/audit_probes.cpp.txt:835-861). It records the index of the output's peak |sample| for an impulse, then subtracts the same reading taken at drive 0. At drive 0, BandProcessor::processWithFactor (band_processor.h:629-636) sets bypassDistortion and runs the direct 1x path: no oversampler, no adapter. So "extra delay" is the oversampler round trip plus everything the adapter does.

2) The tone LP cannot move a peak index. OnePoleLP::process (dsp/include/krate/dsp/primitives/one_pole.h:114) is y = (1-a)x + a*y[n-1]. Its impulse response decays monotonically from n=0, so it peaks at n=0. Whatever its mis-rated cutoff, it adds 0 samples to the probe's peak-index metric.

3) The data contradict the tone-LP explanation and fit the oversampling factor exactly:
- 4x gives 4 samples, 2x gives 1, 1x gives 0.
- HardClip and SoftClip both apply the tone filter (distortion_adapter.cpp:225-230), yet differ by 3 samples.
- If the mis-rated tone LP did add delay, it would add more at 2x than at 4x. distortion_ is prepared at 8x fs (band_processor.h:111-112), and L/R double-step one shared filter (band_processor.h:756-757). That puts its effective cutoff at about factor/4 of the set value, so SoftClip at 2x would show more delay than HardClip at 4x. The measurement shows the opposite (1 vs 4).
- The real source is the group delay of the "ZeroLatency" IIR oversamplers (band_processor.h:99-107). That delay depends on the factor, nothing compensates it, and getLatency() (band_processor.h:376-377) returns 0.

4) Impact as stated. Bitcrush and SoftClip are aligned with HardClip only because they run at 1x and 2x. The skipped tone filter plays no part.

Conclusion: refuted. The title, mechanism and fix attribute the misalignment to the tone LP, and the evidence rules that out. A correctly attributed finding (uncompensated, factor-dependent IIR oversampler group delay between bands, with getLatency claiming 0) would stand on its own. At 44.1 kHz, 3-4 samples is about 68-91 us: under 6 deg at a 200 Hz crossover, but about 65 deg at 2 kHz. That finding should be filed separately against band_processor.h, not under this one.

findings.title: BandProcessor::getLatency reports 0 while the 'ZeroLatency' IIR 4x oversampling path adds 4.4 samples of group delay
findings.problem: getLatency() is a static that returns 0 (comment: Economy/ZeroLatency mode = 0 latency). Measured through processBlock, the 4x path delays the impulse peak by 7 samples and adds 4.38 samples of group delay at 1 kHz relative to 1x. The plugin also never calls setLatencySamples.
findings.why_wrong: The IIR oversamplers have no constant latency, but they do have real group delay. Bands at different factors, and the dry path, misalign unless that delay is compensated.
findings.consequence: Latent today (the Processor does not use processBlock). Once oversampling is wired in, bands at different factors and the dry/wet mix will comb.
findings.suggested_fix: When wiring processBlock, align the bands, for example by running all bands at the same factor, adding matching allpass or delay compensation, or using linear-phase mode and reporting its latency through setLatencySamples. Test: the os-latency probe's relative group delay must be <= 0.5 samples, or be compensated.
findings.evidence: probe os-latency:bandprocessor-block: "factor@1x,factor@max8,peak_idx@1x,peak_idx@max8,gd1k_smp@1x,gd1k_smp@max8,relative_gd_smp = 1,4,1,8,3.04,7.42,4.38" (threshold "|relative group delay| <= 0.5 smp (getLatency() returns 0)"). Code: band_processor.h:376 `[[nodiscard]] static int getLatency() noexcept {` ... :378 `return 0;`
verifier_notes:
The literal observation holds. band_processor.h:376-378 returns 0, and the ZeroLatency IIR oversamplers prepared at band_processor.h:99-107 do add frequency-dependent group delay when processBlock() runs them. That does not make it a live defect, for three reasons.

(1) It cannot happen in the shipped plugin. Processor::process calls only the per-sample BandProcessor::process(float&, float&) (processor.cpp:487 and :494, inside the sample loop at :467-504). That function, band_processor.h:473-512, applies sweep, then morphEngine_->process or distortion_.process, then gain/pan/mute. It never touches oversampler2x_/4x_/8xInner_. Nothing in src/ calls processBlock()/processWithFactor(); Grep finds them only in tests. So in production, bands at different factors never exist, the dry and wet paths are not misaligned by oversampler group delay, and 0 is the correct latency for the code that runs. The finding admits this ("Latent today (the Processor does not use processBlock)"), so its consequence is a guess about future wiring, not a current bug.

(2) Returning 0 is intended by the spec. specs/_archive2_/009-intelligent-oversampling/spec.md:151-152 (FR-018/FR-019) requires IIR minimum-phase mode and says the reported latency "MUST be 0 samples regardless of the active oversampling factors". spec.md:112-113 explains why, and tests/dsp/oversampling_performance_tests.cpp:40-118 locks it in.

(3) The suggested remedy does not fit an IIR path anyway. Minimum-phase IIR group delay changes with frequency, so no integer setLatencySamples value can compensate it. setLatencySamples only applies to a linear-phase mode, which the spec puts out of scope for v1.0. Grep finds no getLatencySamples/setLatencySamples anywhere in plugins/disrumpo/src, which matches the spec's zero-latency ruling.

The real underlying issue is that the oversampling path is dead in production. That is a different finding. As stated, this one is unreachable and intentional.

The shipping plugin cannot reach this path, and the zero latency is a documented, tested design decision.
(1) Unreachable: processor.cpp:467-503 runs every band one sample at a time with bandProcessors_[b].process(bandL, bandR) at :487 and :494. It never calls BandProcessor::processBlock (band_processor.h:519), and processBlock is the only way into processWithFactor and the 2x/4x/8x oversamplers (band_processor.h:635-640, 710-734). A grep of plugins/disrumpo/src finds no call to BandProcessor::processBlock. Within the plugin, getLatency() is called only from tests. The oversampler group delay the probe measured therefore never reaches the plugin's output, and dry and wet stay aligned today. The finding itself says it is "Latent today".
(2) Intentional: the oversamplers are built with OversamplingMode::ZeroLatency (band_processor.h:101-107). oversampler.h:60 defines that mode as "IIR filters (minimum-phase, no latency)", and oversampler.h:53 describes the Economy preset as "IIR 8-pole ... 0 latency". getLatency's own comment cites FR-018/FR-019 ("IIR mode = 0 latency always"). The test "BandProcessor: getLatency returns 0 (IIR mode)" [SC-012] in tests/dsp/oversampling_performance_tests.cpp:32-58 pins this behaviour.
(3) Reporting a latency would not fix it anyway: a minimum-phase IIR has group delay that varies with frequency, so it has no single latency in samples to report. setLatencySamples could not compensate it.
What remains is advice for a future refactor that wires in processBlock, not a defect in the code as it stands.

The measured delay is likely real, but under the impact lens the claimed consequence cannot happen in the shipped plugin, and the finding says so itself ("Latent today").

1. The oversampled path never runs in production. Processor::process feeds each band one sample at a time through `bandProcessors_[b].process(bandL, bandR)` at processor.cpp:494, and `process(discardL, discardR)` at :487 for non-contributing bands. Both calls sit inside the per-sample loop at processor.cpp:467-504. The only processBlock call in processor.cpp is `sweepProcessor_.processBlock` at :370. A grep for processBlock over plugins/disrumpo/src finds no call to BandProcessor::processBlock (band_processor.h:519). The IIR path at band_processor.h:719-727 (processWithOversampling4x -> oversampler4x_.process) is reached only through processBlock -> processBlockInner -> processWithFactor (:519-557, :627-649).
2. Only tests use that path: tests/dsp/oversampling_*_tests.cpp, tests/integration/multi_node_distortion_test.cpp and others. So the 4.38-sample relative group delay from the os-latency probe exists only in a test harness. No host or setting puts bands at different factors, or puts the dry path against a 4x wet path. In the shipped signal, wet and dry are both 0-latency 1x paths summed at processor.cpp:502-503.
3. Under the current wiring, `getLatency()` returning 0 (band_processor.h:376-379) and the missing setLatencySamples are both correct, because the processor adds no latency. getLatency() has no caller in src/. An IIR oversampler's group delay also depends on frequency, so no single integer setLatencySamples value could cancel it anyway. The real remedy is a design decision (equal factors, allpass matching or linear-phase) for whenever processBlock gets wired in.
4. The suggested fix only makes sense once someone wires oversampling into Processor::process. That missing wiring is the real defect: oversampling is advertised but inactive. A delay inside unreachable code does not cause comb filtering at medium severity.

If this is kept at all, it should be a low-severity design note attached to the "wire oversampling in" task, not a medium defect.

findings.title: AsymmetricFuzz, BitwiseMangler and Tape emit low-level output from digital silence (-86 to -89 dBFS)
findings.problem: From silent input these types produce a small non-zero output. For Tape, the flutter AM and TapeSaturator run on the shared, 8x-prepared adapter. For AsymmetricFuzz, asymBias is added before the fuzz and subtracted after it at unit scale (see processRaw). For BitwiseMangler, the XOR pattern maps 0 to a non-zero value. The cause of each type's floor was not isolated individually.
findings.why_wrong: Silence in should give <= -90 dBFS out.
findings.consequence: A faint noise floor on idle tracks.
findings.suggested_fix: Re-measure after the rate and stereo fixes. Then add a silence gate or DC blocking where needed. Test: the selfnoise probes must read <= -90 dBFS.
findings.evidence: probe selfnoise: AsymmetricFuzz/BitwiseMangler/Tape: "rms_dBFS -86.2 / -89.2 / -89.2" (threshold <= -90 dBFS).
verifier_notes:
The -86/-89 dBFS numbers are real (F:/tmp/disrumpo-audit/probe-results.txt:402,404,422, the same in every gate log). What is wrong is calling them a persistent self-noise floor. What the probe measured is the DC blocker settling after a fresh activate.

1. How the probe measures. specs/disrumpo-audit/probes/audit_probes.cpp.txt:500-511 calls reactivate(), renders 1 s of zeros at drive 1.0, and takes the RMS of 0.5-1.0 s only. That window sits right after activation.

2. All three types end in a one-pole DC blocker. Each maps zero input to a constant, and that constant then decays geometrically.
   - AsymmetricFuzz: fuzz(0+asymBias)-asymBias (distortion_adapter.cpp:357-368) is a constant. needsDCBlock_ is true for this type (cpp:588), so it goes through dcBlocker_ (cpp:218-219).
   - BitwiseMangler: XOR of 0 with the pattern gives a constant (bitwise_mangler.h:253-258). It then passes the mangler's own dcBlocker_ (bitwise_mangler.h:216-217).
   - Tape: TapeSaturator runs its wet output through its own dcBlocker_ (tape_saturator.h:12, 376).
   For constant input, DCBlocker::process y = x - x1 + R*y1 (dc_blocker.h:202) gives x - x1 = 0 exactly, so y shrinks by R every sample down to zero.
   It settles slowly because the adapter and its processors are prepared at 8x the rate (band_processor.h:111-112, 124-125) and R is clamped to at most 0.9999 (dc_blocker.h:237-240). That leaves residual DC in the 0.5-1.0 s window. It is not a noise source.

3. The same run disproves the 'faint noise floor on idle tracks' consequence. The tail probe uses the same types, drive 1.0 and bias, and measures 1.0-1.5 s of silence after the input stops (audit_probes.cpp.txt:469-478). It reads AsymmetricFuzz -134.6, BitwiseMangler -157.5 and Tape -157.3 dBFS (probe-results.txt:442,444,462), all far below the -90 dBFS bar. Idle output after signal does decay to nothing.

4. The finding also says 'the cause of each type's floor was not isolated', so the mechanisms it gives are guesses. The flutter AM (cpp:323-329) multiplies the input, so it gives 0 for 0 input and cannot add output from silence.

The real side effect is a short DC transient right after activate. A slow 10 Hz blocker, a consequence of the 8x-rate prepare, makes it last longer. That rate mismatch is a separate finding, not a lasting -86 to -89 dBFS output from digital silence.

The audit's own probe data shows there is no steady noise floor. The numbers are real (f:/tmp/disrumpo-audit/probe-results.txt:402/404/422: -86.2/-89.2/-89.2 dBFS), but they only come from the "selfnoise" probe. That probe reactivates the processor and then measures RMS just 0.5-1.0 s after activate (specs/disrumpo-audit/probes/audit_probes.cpp.txt:500-511). The "tail" probe uses the same three types at the same drive 1.0. It goes reactivate, 0.68 s sine, then 1.5 s silence, and measures 1.0-1.5 s after the stop, about 1.7-2.2 s after activate (audit_probes.cpp.txt:468-478). It reads -134.6 dBFS for AsymmetricFuzz, -157.5 for BitwiseMangler and -157.3 for Tape (probe-results.txt:442/444/462). So an idle track does not keep "a faint noise floor": the -86..-89 reading is a start-up transient that decays below -130 dBFS within about a second.

The source also shows why it is a decaying DC settle and not noise. Each of the three types has a static DC source at zero input, and each one sits in front of a DC blocker:
- AsymmetricFuzz: asymBias in and out, plus FuzzProcessor biasOffset (fuzz_processor.h, "saturated -= biasOffset" followed by dcBlocker_.process). The adapter also adds its own DC blocker for this type (distortion_adapter.cpp:218-220, needsDCBlock_ at :588).
- BitwiseMangler: XOR maps 0 to a constant pattern value. That value goes through the mangler's DC blocker, which is on by default (bitwise_mangler.h:216-218, dcBlockEnabled_ = true at :308).
- Tape: TapeSaturator bias/hysteresis output passes through its internal 10 Hz DC blocker (tape_saturator.h:376). Flutter AM on a zero input stays exactly zero (distortion_adapter.cpp:329, input * (1 + lfo*depth)).

DCBlocker is y = x - x1 + R*y1 with R clamped to [0.9, 0.9999] (dc_blocker.h:202, 240). A constant input only gives an exponentially decaying step response after activation. That matches the measured decay from about -86 dBFS (0.5-1 s) down to -134..-157 dBFS (about 2 s).

The finding's other claims do not hold up either:
- The named mechanisms (bias add/subtract, XOR of 0, flutter) all produce DC that is blocked, so they cannot cause a persistent floor.
- The finding admits the cause was never isolated.
- The -90 dBFS bar is the probe author's own "ok" line, and the probe grades the result "suspicious", not "bad".
- specs/Disrumpo has no silence or noise-floor requirement (a grep for silence / noise floor / -90 dB finds nothing).

At most this is a sub-second, sub-audible DC settle after setActive. It is not the claimed idle-track noise floor.

The claimed consequence, a lasting faint noise floor on idle tracks, is contradicted by the same probe run. In specs/disrumpo-audit/probes/audit_probes.cpp.txt:433-436, 440 and 468-478, the 'tail' probe uses the same Rig and the same settings as 'selfnoise': 1 band, mix 1, bias 0.5, drive 1.0. It feeds 1.5 s of silence and measures the last 0.5 s. For exactly these three types, f:/tmp/disrumpo-audit/probe-results.txt reads tail:AsymmetricFuzz -134.6 dBFS (line 442), tail:BitwiseMangler -157.5 (line 444) and tail:Tape -157.3 (line 462). The -86.2 / -89.2 / -89.2 readings (lines 402, 404, 422) come only from the 'selfnoise' probe (audit_probes.cpp.txt:500-512). That probe calls reactivate(), feeds 1 s of silence and measures the window 0.5-1.0 s after activation. So the energy is a decaying start-up transient after setActive, not a floor that persists with silent input. The mechanisms the finding names would all give a lasting output: in distortion_adapter.cpp:357-368, fuzz(asymBias) - asymBias is a constant DC term, and the BitwiseMangler mapping 0 to a non-zero value would also be constant. If any of these were real, the tail measurement would show it, and it reads 45-70 dB lower. Tape at distortion_adapter.cpp:320-341 multiplies the input (0) by the flutter LFO, so flutter cannot create output from silence. The finding also admits 'the cause of each type's floor was not isolated'. In size, even the transient is -86 dBFS RMS at maximum drive, under the 16-bit noise floor at ordinary listening levels, and it happens only once in the first second after activation. It does not occur on idle tracks during playback. The -90 dBFS bar is the probe's own heuristic, not a spec requirement.
