findings.why_wrong: The project requires zero warnings. Third-party headers should be included as SYSTEM includes, or the warning should be suppressed around the include.
findings.consequence: Warning noise in every KrateDSP build, which hides new warnings. All plugins are affected, since KrateDSP is shared.
findings.suggested_fix: Mark the Highway include directory SYSTEM (or /external:I with /external:W0 on MSVC), or wrap the include in `#pragma warning(push/disable:4127)`. Check: a clean build log has 0 warnings.
findings.evidence: build lane: "warning C4127: conditional expression is constant [KrateDSP.vcxproj] (appears 4 times; third-party Highway header included from KrateDSP)" at math-inl.h "1026,24".
verifier_notes: I confirmed this from both the source and the measured log. In the build log f:/tmp/disrumpo-audit/build.log, lines 25, 54, 83 and 112 each read "math-inl.h(1026,24): warning C4127: conditional expression is constant [...\dsp\KrateDSP.vcxproj]". That is 4 hits, and they are the log's only warnings (grep -c warning = 4). At build/windows-x64-release/_deps/highway-src/hwy/contrib/math/math-inl.h:1026 the code is `if (kAllowSubnormals == true) {`, a compile-time constant tested with a plain `if` instead of `if constexpr`, which is exactly what C4127 reports. The include path: dsp/include/krate/dsp/core/spectral_simd.cpp:15-17 includes hwy/foreach_target.h, hwy/highway.h and hwy/contrib/math/math-inl.h. foreach_target re-includes the TU once per target ISA, which explains the repeat count. Highway is not treated as a system include. Root CMakeLists.txt:336-345 calls FetchContent_Declare/FetchContent_MakeAvailable(highway) without SYSTEM, and dsp/CMakeLists.txt:35 is a plain `target_link_libraries(KrateDSP PRIVATE hwy hwy_contrib)`. Neither file has /external:W0 or a pragma around the include. The project already handles the VST3 SDK this way (CMakeLists.txt:241-251, `target_include_directories(${target} SYSTEM INTERFACE ...)`), so the gap for Highway is real and the fix pattern already exists in the repo. The defect is genuine but it is build hygiene in shared KrateDSP, not a Disrumpo runtime bug, so severity stays low.

I could not refute this, either from the code or from the build log. The warning is real: f:/tmp/disrumpo-audit/build.log lines 25, 54, 83 and 112 each show "math-inl.h(1026,24): warning C4127: conditional expression is constant [dsp/KrateDSP.vcxproj]" while compiling dsp/include/krate/dsp/core/spectral_simd.cpp. The instantiation comes from spectral_simd.cpp(175,24), which calls hwy::Log10, then Log, then impl::Log<D,V,true>. Line 1026 of math-inl.h is `if (kAllowSubnormals == true) {`, and kAllowSubnormals is a template constant, which is the textbook trigger for C4127. Nothing guards against it: spectral_simd.cpp:15-17 includes hwy/foreach_target.h, hwy/highway.h and hwy/contrib/math/math-inl.h with no `#pragma warning(push/disable)` around them. dsp/CMakeLists.txt:35 links `hwy hwy_contrib` the normal way, and :47 compiles KrateDSP at /W4, the level C4127 belongs to. The root CMakeLists.txt:244-262 already has a smtg_mark_includes_as_system helper that marks third-party includes SYSTEM, but it only runs on the VST3 SDK and VSTGUI targets. Highway's FetchContent block (:335-348) never calls it and is not declared SYSTEM. I also searched dsp/ for an accepted-warning note or a 4127 suppression and found none. This conflicts with the CLAUDE.md zero-warnings rule. Severity stays low: the warning is in third-party code and harmless at runtime. It is not specific to Disrumpo; it fires in KrateDSP, which every plugin builds.

I could not refute this. The source shows how the warning arises, and the consequence the finding claims (warning noise only) is what happens.

How the warning arises:
- Line 1026 of build/windows-x64-release/_deps/highway-src/hwy/contrib/math/math-inl.h is `if (kAllowSubnormals == true) {`.
- `kAllowSubnormals` is a template bool parameter (math-inl.h:987, `template <class D, class V, bool kAllowSubnormals = true>`). It is instantiated with both true (line 1553) and false (lines 1334, 1387, 1577).
- Because it is a plain `if` on a compile-time constant rather than `if constexpr`, MSVC raises C4127 at /W4. Several instantiations explain the count of 4.
- dsp/core/spectral_simd.cpp:17 includes "hwy/contrib/math/math-inl.h".
- dsp/CMakeLists.txt:46-51 builds KrateDSP with `/W4` and only `/wd4100` disabled.
- dsp/CMakeLists.txt:35 links hwy and hwy_contrib normally (`target_link_libraries(KrateDSP PRIVATE hwy hwy_contrib)`).
- In root CMakeLists.txt:336-345, Highway is fetched by FetchContent_Declare with no SYSTEM option. No `/external:W0` or `/external:I` flag exists anywhere. The repo's `smtg_mark_includes_as_system` helper (CMakeLists.txt:244-262) covers only the VST3 SDK and VSTGUI targets, not hwy.
- So Highway's headers are compiled at /W4 as ordinary user headers, and the warning in the build lane is consistent with the source.

Impact:
- The cost is build-log noise only. There is no runtime, audio or state consequence, and no change to Disrumpo's output.
- No /WX is set, so no build fails.
- It hits every KrateDSP consumer equally. It is a build-hygiene issue, not a Disrumpo defect.
- It does break the project's "zero warnings" rule.
- The claimed consequence (noise that can hide new warnings, every plugin affected through the shared KrateDSP) is accurate, and "low" is the right severity.

Limit: I found no KrateDSP MSBuild .log on disk (dsp/KrateDSP.dir/Release/*.log is absent), so I could not recount the 4 instances myself. The warning's cause is confirmed from source and flags alone.

findings.title: Measured: the stale transition gain on an on-node cursor is reachable through a MorphMode switch (-23.5 dB) and through Linear1D with 3-4 nodes (-3.0 dB); the cursor-jump path is not reachable
findings.problem: When any node is within 0.001 of the cursor, calculateMorphWeights returns early (morph_engine.cpp:186-192 for Linear1D, 218-224 for Planar2D). That skips the transitionGains_ update at :267-270. processCrossFamily then multiplies the one-hot node by whatever gain was left over (:748-756). setMode (:107-109) only assigns mode_ and recomputes nothing. Two paths leave a stale gain below 1. (a) Switch from Planar2D to Linear1D while x is 0: the node at x=0 becomes one-hot but keeps its small Planar2D gain. (b) Linear1D with 3-4 nodes: C and D share posX with A and B, so on the way to x=0 the weights of A and C are both about 0.5 and the gain is 0.707. At <0.001 A becomes one-hot and the 0.707 freezes.
findings.why_wrong: With the cursor on a node, the output must equal that node alone (FR-014, 100 % weight). The weights report 1.0/0/0/0, but the audio is attenuated by a gain left over from a previous position or mode.
findings.consequence: A Planar2D-to-Linear1D mode change with the cursor on the left edge drops the band by up to 26.5 dB against the node alone, and the level stays there until the cursor moves more than 0.001. Every 3-4-node Linear1D band parked at either end of the axis sits a constant 3.01 dB low. The prior hypothesis (silence after a smoothing-0 cursor jump) is NOT reproduced: the morph smoother's 0.1 ms floor (smoother.h:58, 82) walks the cursor through intermediate positions that refresh the gains, giving 0.00 dB delta in all 10 jump cases.
findings.suggested_fix: Update transitionGains_ on the on-node branch too: set the one-hot node's gain to 1 and the others to 0, or fall through to the common threshold/gain block instead of returning. Recompute weights and gains in setMode and setNodes. Regression test: 4-node cross-family band, cursor (0,0.9) Planar2D, render, switch mode to Linear1D, render. The level must be within 0.5 dB of node A alone. A fresh Linear1D 4-node band at x=0 must also be within 0.5 dB of node A alone.
findings.evidence: Probe 'stale transition gain on node' (48 kHz, 220 Hz -12 dBFS, drive 3). Reference: SoftClip alone = -6.62 dB. All jump cases at smoothing 0 and 10 ms, Linear1D and Planar2D (0.99->0, 0.5->0, 1.0->0, 0.99->0.01) read -6.62 dB, delta 0.00. onnode:planar-to-linear1d-switch: y=0.90 gives -33.15 dB after the switch against -9.63 dB for fresh Linear1D (delta -23.52; -26.5 dB against SoftClip alone), weights 1/0/0/0. y=0.70 gives delta -2.71. y=0.50 gives delta -14.68. Fresh Linear1D 4-node at x=0 = -9.63 dB, which is -3.01 dB against SoftClip alone with weights 1/0/0/0 (0.707 gain). Code: morph_engine.cpp:188-192 'weights_.fill(0.0f); weights_[i] = 1.0f; return;' and :748 'const float gain = transitionGains_[i];'.
verifier_notes:
I traced both paths in the source, and both are real. One detail in the finding is wrong: setMode (morph_engine.cpp:107-113) does recompute. It calls calculateMorphWeights(smoothedX, smoothedY) at :112. That recompute takes the same early return, so the mechanism still holds.

How the gain goes stale:
- The on-node branches return before the threshold and gain block. Linear1D does this at :188-191 and Planar2D at :220-223, both with `weights_.fill(0); weights_[i]=1; return;`.
- transitionGains_ is written in only two places. reset() at :87 sets it to 1, and :268-270 recomputes it. The on-node return never reaches :268-270.
- MorphEngine::process (:662-682) calls calculateMorphWeights every sample (:672). Every later sample with the cursor still on the node takes the same early return, so the stale gain stays until the cursor moves more than 0.001 (kOnNodeThreshold, :23).
- processCrossFamily multiplies by the stale gain: `output += nodeOutput * weight * gain` with `gain = transitionGains_[i]` (:748, :756).

Path (b), Linear1D with 3-4 nodes:
- The processor places the nodes at fixed corners (processor.cpp:114-120): A(0,0), B(1,0), C(0,1), D(1,1).
- Linear1D uses only posX (:185), so A and C sit at the same x.
- As x moves toward 0, A and C each weigh about 0.5. calculateTransitionGain (:352-380) maps that to zonePos 0.5 and equalPowerGains returns sin(pi/4) = 0.707 (crossfade_utils.h:50-52).
- At x < 0.001, A is index 0 and becomes one-hot first, so its 0.707 gain freezes. That is the measured -3.01 dB.

Path (a), Planar2D to Linear1D switch:
- At (0, 0.9) the squared inverse distances are A 1.23, C 100, B 0.55, D 0.99. A's normalized weight is about 0.012.
- kWeightThreshold is 0.001 (morph_node.h:139), so A is kept. It falls in the below-0.4 branch, giving sin(0.03 * pi/2) = 0.047, about -26.5 dB. This matches the probe.
- The mode change is reachable at runtime through the parameter path (processor_params.cpp:967) and through state load (processor_state.cpp:827), both via BandProcessor::setMorphMode, which calls morphEngine_->setMode (band_processor.h:260-262).
- The recompute makes A one-hot at x=0, returns early, and keeps the 0.047 gain.

Conclusion: the weights read 1/0/0/0 while the audio is scaled by the stale gain. That contradicts the 100 %-weight-on-node requirement. The arithmetic matches the quoted measurements (-3.01 dB, about -26.5 dB). The stated severity is reasonable: the drop is large on a mode switch and is a constant 3 dB at the axis ends with 3-4 cross-family nodes.

I confirmed this from the source. I found no guard, reset, test or documented design decision that covers it.

1. **The on-node branch returns before the gains are updated.** In MorphEngine::calculateMorphWeights, the Linear1D branch (morph_engine.cpp:188-192) and the Planar2D branch (:220-224) both run `weights_.fill(0.0f); weights_[i] = 1.0f; return;`. That return skips the only place transitionGains_ is written outside reset(), the loop at :267-270.

2. **The cross-family path uses that stale gain.** processCrossFamily reads `const float gain = transitionGains_[i];` (:748) and outputs `nodeOutput * weight * gain` (:756). The one-hot node therefore gets whatever gain the previous position or mode left behind.

3. **Nothing upstream fixes it.** The per-sample process() (:668-672) calls the same function, so it hits the same early return. reset() (:87) sets the gains to 1 only on reset or setActive. setNodes (:151) also goes through calculateMorphWeights.

4. **One detail in the finding is wrong, but the conclusion holds.** The finding says setMode "only assigns mode_ and recomputes nothing". In fact setMode (:107-113) does call calculateMorphWeights(posX, posY). That call early-returns in the on-node case, so the gains stay stale anyway.

5. **Path (b) is reachable with the factory defaults.** processor.cpp:114-120 places the nodes at A(0,0), B(1,0), C(0,1) and D(1,1). In Linear1D only X counts, so A and C share posX = 0.
   - Just above x = 0.001, A and C each weigh about 0.5. calculateTransitionGain(0.5) falls in the 0.4-0.6 equal-power zone (:374-378) and gives about 0.707.
   - Below 0.001, A becomes one-hot and keeps the 0.707, which is the measured -3.01 dB.

6. **Scope and test coverage.** Only cross-family bands are affected; processSameFamily does not use transitionGains_. BandProcessor routes through MorphEngine (band_processor.h:247-285), so a real host reaches this through the morph mode parameter and cursor automation. No test in plugins/disrumpo/tests pins on-node transition gains.

**Severity: unchanged at high.** The measured drops (-23.5 dB on a mode switch, a constant -3 dB at the axis ends with the default 4-node layout) are audible level errors in normal use.

I confirmed this from source; I did not re-run the probe. One detail in the finding is wrong: setMode does recompute. morph_engine.cpp:107-113 calls calculateMorphWeights(smoothed X, Y). That recompute still leaves the gain stale, because of the early return described next, so the defect stands.

How the stale gain arises:
- Linear1D (morph_engine.cpp:188-192) and Planar2D (:220-224) both return early when the cursor is on a node, setting a one-hot weight. They return before the transitionGains_ update at :267-270, so the old gains stay.
- MorphEngine::process (:662-683) runs calculateMorphWeights on every sample, but the early return happens there too, so the gain never refreshes while the cursor stays on the node.
- processCrossFamily (:743-756) outputs nodeOutput * weight(1.0) * transitionGains_[i]. The output is therefore scaled by the leftover gain.
- Only reset() (:87) sets the gains back to 1.

Both paths are reachable in the plugin:
- The node positions are fixed at A(0,0), B(1,0), C(0,1), D(1,1) (processor.cpp:114-120). In Linear1D, A and C share posX=0 and B and D share posX=1.
- Moving the cursor toward x=0 makes the A and C weights about 0.5 each. calculateTransitionGain (:374-378) then gives a zonePos of 0.5 and an equal-power fade-in of sin(pi/4) = 0.707. Once the cursor is within 0.001, the gain freezes at 0.707. That is a constant -3.01 dB for as long as the cursor stays parked at the axis end.
- The mode switch comes from the per-band kBandMorphMode parameter (processor_params.cpp:964-968) through BandProcessor::setMorphMode (band_processor.h:260-262).
- In Planar2D at (0, 0.9) my hand calculation gives A a weight of about 0.012. calculateTransitionGain (:364-370) then returns sin(0.03 * pi/2), about 0.047, or -26.5 dB. That matches the probe.
- Moving Y does not clear it in Linear1D. Only an X move of more than 0.001 does.
- The audio path is real: BandProcessor calls morphEngine_->process per sample (band_processor.h:487-488, 753-754).

Scope:
- The defect needs nodes from different families. processSameFamily (:691-719) never reads transitionGains_. The processor's default nodes are all SoftClip (processor.cpp:114-120), which is the same-family path, so a default band is not affected.
- There is no NaN and no crash. The effect is a level error that persists.

Severity: I left it unchanged. A -26 dB drop that stays after a mode change, and a constant -3 dB at the axis ends, are real audible level errors. Both are reached by ordinary actions: dragging the cursor to the pad edge, or changing the mode. Both break FR-014, which requires the output to be the on-node node alone.

findings.title: Rectified_Drums root cause: after a host state restore its HalfRectify band compares the signal against the default threshold 0.7, so the 440 Hz band outputs exactly 0
findings.problem: The preset sets band 1 (150-4500 Hz, which carries the 440 Hz test tone) to HalfRectify with slots {threshold 0.3, smooth 0.15, dcBlock 1} and drive 2.0 (tools/disrumpo_preset_generator.cpp:2630-2631, shapeHalfRect at :621-624). The host setState path (processor_state.cpp:852-889) restores the type, drive, mix, tone, bias, folds and bitDepth plus the raw shapeSlots, but never runs mapShapeSlotsToParams. typeParams_.threshold therefore keeps the DistortionParams default of 0.7 (distortion_adapter.h:85) and smoothness keeps 0.0. HalfRectify then computes `(input >= thresh) ? input : 0.0f` on the driven sample. The driven peak is 0.251 x 2.0 = 0.502, below 0.7, so every sample of band 1 is 0. What is left in the -50.8 dBFS render is band 0's LR4 skirt at 440 Hz: (440/150)^4 = 74, about -37.5 dB, then FullRectify and its DC transient. The 8x-rated smooth filter and the 1.25 Hz DC blocker (the brief's other suspects) are not the cause: smooth is 0 on this path and is skipped (cpp:443), and the DC blocker only removes DC.
findings.why_wrong: The preset is meant to render the half-rectified mid band at about -12 dBFS. The parameter path (processor_params.cpp:852, 892) and the preset-browser path both re-derive threshold = slots[0] = 0.3 (processor_params.cpp:122-126). The host restore path is the one a DAW uses on project reload, and on it the stored threshold is ignored and a default above the signal level wins.
findings.consequence: Reloading a project that uses Rectified_Drums, or any preset or session with a HalfRectify node whose driven peak is under 0.7, silences that band. The preset drops from about -12 dBFS to -50.8 dBFS peak / -62.2 dBFS RMS (probe-results.txt:301). The host-order probe (probe-results.txt:145) shows a 43 dB difference against the SoftClip nodes that setupProcessing reinstates. This is the audible worst case of the already-reported 'setState never re-derives type-specific DistortionParams' defect; for HalfRectify it is a hard mute, not a timbre change.
findings.suggested_fix: In Processor::setState, after the slot loop for each node (processor_state.cpp:874), call the same mapShapeSlotsToParams(mn.type, mn.shapeSlots, mn.params) that processParameterChanges uses. Expose it from processor_params.cpp, for example as a private static member, instead of the file-static. Re-apply the stream's bias, folds and bitDepth only where they are not slot-derived. Test: load Drums/Rectified_Drums.vstpreset through Processor::setState on an active processor, render 440 Hz at -12 dBFS, and assert RMS > -30 dBFS (it fails today at -62.2). Also assert that the band-1 node's getNodeParams(0).threshold equals 0.3 within 1e-6.
findings.evidence: distortion_adapter.cpp:441-442 `const float thresh = typeParams_.threshold; float result = (input >= thresh) ? input : 0.0f;`. distortion_adapter.h:85 `float threshold = 0.7f;`. processor_state.cpp:859-861 restore only bias/folds/bitDepth, and :871 writes shapeSlots with no mapShapeSlotsToParams. Probe path: audit_probes.cpp.txt:1502-1504 (fresh Rig, setStateBytes, render), so the probe measured the host path. Node.js replica (scratchpad rect_sim.js; LR4 150/4500 Hz, FullRectify band 0 at drive 1.5, HalfRectify band 1 at drive 2, filters designed at 8x and double-clocked, -3 dB centre pan): threshold 0.7 / smooth 0 gives peak -62.86 dBFS, RMS -67.49. The preset's intended threshold 0.3 / smooth 0.15 gives peak -12.04 dBFS, RMS -18.61. The remaining ~12 dB gap to the measured -50.76 matches the preset's Transient->bandDrive(0) route at amount 0.4 (generator :2634; drive offset x10 takes 1.5 to 5.5, +11.3 dB), which the replica leaves out.
verifier_notes: I could not refute this from source. processor_state.cpp:852-861 restores only the type, drive, mix, toneHz, bias, folds and bitDepth into bandMorphCache_[b].nodes[n]. The v9 block at :865-874 copies the raw values into shapeSlots[s] and never calls mapShapeSlotsToParams. A grep of plugins/disrumpo/src finds that function only in processor_params.cpp (definition at :39, calls at :852 and :892, both inside processParameterChanges). Nothing in dsp/ (BandProcessor, MorphEngine, DistortionAdapter) reads shapeSlots, so nothing downstream re-derives threshold either. Next, :892-897 pushes the nodes through setMorphNodes. MorphEngine then blends p.threshold across nodes (morph_engine.cpp:429, :538), and every node still holds the DistortionParams default threshold = 0.7f (distortion_adapter.h:85) and smoothness = 0.0f (:111). The mapping that should apply here is HalfRectify threshold=slots[0], smooth=slots[1], dcBlock=slots[2]>=0.5 (processor_params.cpp:122-127). The adapter scales by drive before shaping (distortion_adapter.cpp:211, `wet = input * commonParams_.drive`). HalfRectify then does `(input >= thresh) ? input : 0.0f` (:441-442) and skips the smooth filter because smoothness is 0 (:443). The preset generator sets band 1 to HalfRectify at drive 2.0 with shapeHalfRect(0.3, 0.15, true) (tools/disrumpo_preset_generator.cpp:2630-2631, :621-624), and its routes modulate bandDrive(0) and bandDrive(2), never band 1 (:2634-2635). So a -12 dBFS 440 Hz tone reaches about 0.50 after drive, which is under 0.7, and band 1 outputs exactly 0. The probe's preset lane loads the preset bytes into a fresh Rig through Processor::setState (specs/disrumpo-audit/probes/audit_probes.cpp.txt:1502-1504), so it measured this host path. I could not open the cited probe-results.txt, because the probes dir holds audit_followup_results.txt and audit_band_arrival_results.txt instead. The -50.8 dBFS number is therefore unchecked, but the mechanism is fully confirmed from code. High severity stands: reloading a project silences one band of a factory preset.

I could not refute this. The source and the quoted measurement both confirm it.

(1) Host restore skips the slot mapping. processor_state.cpp:852-862 restores type, drive, mix, toneHz, bias, folds and bitDepth into bandMorphCache_. :865-873 writes only the raw shapeSlots[s] (and the per-type shadow at :876-887). :891-895 then pushes the nodes to setMorphNodes. Nothing in this path re-derives the type-specific params.

(2) No other code repairs it later. grep finds mapShapeSlotsToParams only as a file-static at processor_params.cpp:39, with its two callers at :852 (type change) and :892 (slot param change). setActive, setupProcessing, BandProcessor and MorphEngine never call it, so nothing upstream or downstream corrects threshold after a restore. The HalfRectify mapping sits at processor_params.cpp:122-126 (threshold = slots[0], smoothness = slots[1], dcBlock = slots[2]). It runs only on the parameter path.

(3) The default wins. DistortionParams::threshold defaults to 0.7f (distortion_adapter.h:85). MorphEngine blends p.threshold by weight (morph_engine.cpp:538), so the stale 0.7 reaches the adapter.

(4) The comparison is made after drive. distortion_adapter.cpp:211 applies `wet = input * commonParams_.drive`. HalfRectify at :441-442 then computes `(input >= thresh) ? input : 0`. A driven peak of about 0.5 against 0.7 gives zero output. Smoothness keeps its default and is skipped at :443.

(5) The preset intends threshold 0.3. tools/disrumpo_preset_generator.cpp:2630-2631 calls shapeHalfRect(...0.3f, 0.15f, true), which writes slots {0.3, 0.15, 1} (:621-624).

(6) The measurement matches. f:/tmp/disrumpo-audit/probe-results.txt:301 reads Rectified_Drums peak -50.76 dBFS, RMS -62.22 dBFS, against the probe's rms > -60 bar. Line 145 shows the separate host-order delta.

Not intentional or guarded. The VST3 host restore path (setState on project or preset load) does not normally get parameter changes resent to the processor, so a real host does not mask this. No test covers threshold surviving setState: grep of plugins/disrumpo/tests finds none.

It may duplicate a broader finding ("setState never re-derives type-specific params"), but that does not make it wrong. HIGH stays appropriate, because this case is a hard mute of a factory preset's band on project reload.

I confirmed the mechanism in source, and the logged measurement backs it up. processor_state.cpp:836-874 reads each node's type, drive, mix, tone, bias, folds and bitDepth into bandMorphCache_, then writes the raw shapeSlots (:871) and the shadow slots. It never calls mapShapeSlotsToParams. grep finds that function only in processor_params.cpp, defined at :39 and called at :852 and :892 (the parameter-change path). The setState block ends at :881-889 with setMorphNodes(bandMorphCache_[b].nodes, ...), so the nodes carry the DistortionParams defaults. Those defaults are threshold = 0.7f (distortion_adapter.h:85) and smoothness = 0.0f (:111). The HalfRectify mapping at processor_params.cpp:122-126 (threshold = slots[0], smoothness = slots[1]) never runs on this path.

The adapter applies drive first (wet = input * drive, distortion_adapter.cpp:211), then HalfRectify computes `(input >= thresh) ? input : 0.0f` (cpp:440-441). Smoothing is skipped because smoothness is 0 (cpp:442). The preset generator (tools/disrumpo_preset_generator.cpp:2630-2631) sets every band-1 node to HalfRectify at drive 2.0 (setBandType at :511-515 loops over all nodes). Only node 0 gets slots {0.3, 0.15, 1}. With a 440 Hz tone at -12 dBFS (0.251) in the 150-4500 Hz band, the driven peak is about 0.50. That is below 0.7, so band 1 outputs exactly 0. Every node of the band is HalfRectify, so the same-family interpolation (morph_engine.cpp:538) also gives a threshold of 0.7.

The probe output bears this out. f:/tmp/disrumpo-audit/probe-results.txt:301 records Drums/Rectified_Drums after setState on an active processor at peak -50.76 dBFS and RMS -62.22 dBFS ('bad'). Line :145 records the host-order variant with rms_delta 43.43 dB.

On impact: Processor::setState is the path every DAW uses to reload a project, and host-side preset loading goes through it too. On that path a factory preset, and any session with a HalfRectify node whose driven peak stays under 0.7, effectively mutes the band (it drops about 40-50 dB). The other default-threshold types (HardClip and the others the mapping covers) get a timbre or level change instead. A shipped factory preset that goes near-silent on project reload justifies high severity. I am not refuting the finding, and the severity stays as reported.

One caveat: the claim that the preset is "intended" to render at about -12 dBFS depends on the replica. Nodes 1 and up keep default slots, so the intended level depends on the cursor and the node weights. That does not change the defect.

findings.title: SineFold and TriangleFold produce the same output at default settings: both compute 0.5*sineFold + 0.5*triangleFold of the same signal
findings.problem: SineFold runs WavefolderProcessor in the Serge (sine) model and crossfades toward wavefoldTriangle_ (triangle) by `shape`. TriangleFold runs the Simple (triangle) model and crossfades toward wavefoldTriangle_ switched to Sine by `angle`. Both crossfade controls come from slot 2, and slot 2 defaults to 0.5 (processor_params.cpp:92, 101; morph_node.h:43-44). Folds is 1+0.5*11 = 6.5 for both and symmetry is 0 for both. So both types compute result = 0.5*sin(6.5x) + 0.5*tri(x, 1/6.5), then the same smooth and tone filters. The only differences are WavefolderProcessor's internal 10 Hz DC blocker and smoothers, which are inaudible here.
findings.why_wrong: D07 and D08 are offered as two distinct algorithms (the spec family table lists Sine Fold and Triangle Fold separately; the TypeParams templates give each its own panel). The crossfade parameter should default to 0, the pure algorithm, as DistortionParams already does (`float shape = 0.0f;`, distortion_adapter.h:100). The generic 0.5 slot default turns both into the same 50/50 blend.
findings.consequence: Picking Triangle Fold instead of Sine Fold, or morphing between them, makes no audible difference until the user finds the Shape/Angle knob. Every probe row for the two types is identical to 0.02 dB, which would also mislead any listening test or preset design built on 'Sine vs Triangle'.
findings.suggested_fix: Give slot 2 a per-type default of 0.0 for SineFold and TriangleFold in ShapeShadowStorage, as the constructor already special-cases BitwiseMangler at morph_node.h:111-113. Apply the same default in the controller's shapeShadowStorage_ and the uidesc/registration default for Shape2. Test: render a fresh SineFold node and a fresh TriangleFold node (defaults, drive 5, 1 kHz -6 dBFS) and assert their spectral centroids differ by more than 20 % or their RMS difference exceeds 1 dB. Today both read identical.

Probe: type:SineFold peaks -23.23/-26.64/-31.04 vs type:TriangleFold -23.25/-26.65/-31.04 (probe-results.txt:524-526 vs 542-544). adapter-vs-processor -11.39 dB / centroid 2246->1110 Hz (line 19) vs -11.38 dB / 2246->1110 Hz (line 25). In wavefolder_processor.h:391-392, Serge maps to WavefoldType::Sine. wavefoldTriangle_ is a Wavefolder primitive, set to Triangle at :59, with setFoldAmount(p.folds). - SineFold (distortion_adapter.cpp:376-391): wavefolder_ is set to the Serge model at :657. Severity: medium stands. Nothing breaks or corrupts, but two of the advertised 26 types sound the same until the user moves slot 2.

The defect is confirmed from source, and the consequence holds at the stated severity.

Slot mapping (processor_params.cpp:86-101):
- SineFold: folds = 1 + slot0*11, symmetry = slot1*2-1, shape = slot2, bias = slot3*2-1.
- TriangleFold: the same, except slot2 becomes angle.

Defaults (morph_node.h:43-44 and ShapeShadowStorage at morph_node.h:103-113): every slot is 0.5. Only BitwiseMangler gets a special case. So both types default to folds = 6.5, symmetry = 0, bias = 0, and shape = angle = 0.5.

routeParams:
- SineFold (distortion_adapter.cpp:656-665) sets wavefolder_ to the Serge model and wavefoldTriangle_.setFoldAmount(6.5).
- TriangleFold (:667-674) sets wavefolder_ to the Simple model with the same fold amount on both folders.

WavefolderProcessor (wavefolder_processor.h:358-363, 386-392):
- Serge maps to the primitive's WavefoldType::Sine and Simple maps to WavefoldType::Triangle.
- Both call the same Layer-1 Wavefolder primitive with the same smoothed foldAmt. The symmetry offset is sym/foldAmt = 0, mix is 1, and a 10 Hz DC blocker follows (:373).

processRaw:
- SineFold (:379-389) computes 0.5*Sine(x,6.5) [with DC block] + 0.5*Triangle(x,6.5) [wavefoldTriangle_].
- TriangleFold (:395-406) computes 0.5*Triangle(x,6.5) [with DC block] + 0.5*Sine(x,6.5) [wavefoldTriangle_, switched to Sine and back].
- Both then go through the same wavefoldSmoothFilter_.

So at defaults the two types are the same 50/50 blend. The only difference is which half passes through the 10 Hz DC blocker. With symmetric input, bias 0 and symmetry 0 there is no DC to remove, so that blocker only adds a phase shift below about 10 Hz, which is inaudible. This matches the quoted probe numbers (-23.23 vs -23.25 dB peaks, identical centroids).

Context:
- The code comments themselves say slot 2 is a crossfade "between sine fold (0) and triangle fold (1)" (:383, :399). The 0.5 default is the generic slot default, not a deliberate per-type choice.
- DistortionParams' own field default for shape is 0.
- The controller keeps a mirror of the same ShapeShadowStorage (controller.h:355), so a freshly chosen SineFold or TriangleFold node starts at 0.5 there too.

Impact: two of the 26 types sound the same when first picked, and morphing between them does nothing until the user moves Shape/Angle away from 0.5. There is no crash, NaN or real-time violation, and presets that set slot 2 explicitly are unaffected. Medium is appropriate.

findings.title: SergeFold defaults to the Buchla259 model, and the triangle and Buchla folders' output peak is 1/folds regardless of input, so SergeFold peaks at -22 dBFS even with every filter off
findings.problem: Two level problems stack. (1) The model slot defaults to 0.5, and `static_cast<int>(slots[2]*3.0f + 0.5f)` = 2 indexes models[2] = Buchla259 (distortion_adapter.cpp:678-685), so a fresh 'SergeFold' node is a Buchla 259 folder. (2) The triangle and Buchla folders scale their threshold by 1/foldAmount and never apply makeup gain. Wavefolder::applyTriangle uses threshold = 1/foldAmount, so |out| <= 1/folds. applyBuchla259 sums triangleFold(x, T_i/fold) weighted by G = {1,.8,.6,.4,.2} and divides by sum(G) = 3, so |out| <= 1.4/(3*fold). At the default folds of 6.5 the triangle branch peaks at 0.154 (-16.3 dBFS) and Buchla at 0.072 (-22.9 dBFS), whatever the input level. Raising Folds to 12 lowers them further, to -21.6 and -28.2 dBFS. The adapter forwards p.folds unchanged (cpp:658, 669, 686-688), and the SineFold/SergeFold 'shape' crossfade mixes in the same triangle branch (cpp:418-421).
findings.why_wrong: A fold-count or 'Folds' control should change the harmonic density. It should not act as a 16-28 dB attenuator, and a wavefolder fed a full-scale signal should produce close to full-scale output. The Sine model already does: sin() peaks at 1 for any gain. The type is named and documented as a Serge folder (specs-overview.md D09; adapter comment cpp:677 '0=Serge'), but the default slot lands on the third entry.
findings.consequence: The default SergeFold node renders -47.5 dBFS peak from a -6 dBFS input in the plugin (probe-results.txt:522). Even at the correct sample rate with smooth and tone off, the replica gives -21.7 dBFS. The Folds knob works backwards: more folds means quieter. Morphing Serge against any saturation type gives a 20+ dB level hole.
findings.suggested_fix: In the adapter, not the shared primitive (its 1/fold contract is documented and other KrateDSP consumers may rely on it), multiply the Simple and Buchla259 outputs, and the wavefoldTriangle_ branch, by foldAmount: Buchla by 3*fold/1.4, or by a measured RMS-matching factor. Change the SergeFold model default to index 0 (Serge): either a per-type slot-2 default of 0.0 in ShapeShadowStorage, or reorder the table. Keep the menu labels consistent with the inventory finding that labels 0 and 1 are swapped. Test: for SergeFold at every model and SineFold/TriangleFold at shape 0, a 1 kHz -6 dBFS sine at drive 5 must give peak within 6 dB of the SoftClip type's peak at folds 2 and at folds 12.

I could not refute this. The code supports the level defect at roughly the claimed size. The finding has two inaccuracies, and neither removes the consequence.

How the defaults land on Buchla259:
- Every shape slot defaults to 0.5 (morph_node.h:43, and ShapeShadowStorage at :102-103).
- processor_params.cpp:108 maps slot 0 to p.folds = 1 + 0.5*11 = 6.5.
- :110 maps slot 2 to p.foldModel = int(0.5*3 + 0.5) = 2.
- distortion_adapter.cpp:678-685 indexes models[2], which is Buchla259.
- The spec mockup (ui-mockups.md:397) shows the default model as Lockhart, so defaulting to Buchla is a real deviation. Neither spec asks for the Serge model: specs-overview.md:89 lists Lockhart and Buchla259 for D09. The "should default to Serge" part of the finding is weak; the deviation is only that Buchla was not the intended default.

Why the output level is capped:
- applyBuchla259 (wavefolder_processor.h:430-446) adds up triangleFold(x, T_i/fold) weighted by gains {1,.8,.6,.4,.2}, with thresholds {.2..1} (:456-463), then divides by the gain sum of 3.
- triangleFold keeps its output within ±threshold (wavefold_math.h:287-312, which maps into [-t, t]).
- So |out| <= (0.2+0.32+0.36+0.32+0.2)/3/fold = 0.467/fold. At fold 6.5 that is 0.072 (-22.9 dBFS), whatever the input level.
- The Wavefolder primitive's triangle path uses threshold = 1/foldAmount (wavefolder.h:257-259), so |out| <= 0.154 (-16.3 dBFS) at 6.5.
- The default shape of 0.5 mixes the two (adapter :418-421), which caps the peak near 0.11 (about -19 dBFS).

No makeup gain anywhere on the path:
- DistortionAdapter::process (cpp:189-236) applies drive, processRaw, the DC blocker, tone and mix, with no output compensation.
- WavefolderProcessor::process (:354-376) has no compensation either.
- Drive scales the input but cannot raise these caps.

The Folds knob works backwards, as claimed: at folds 1 the Buchla cap is -6.6 dBFS, and at higher folds it is lower. A 16-23 dB level hole when morphing against saturation types is real.

Corrections to the finding:
(a) WavefolderProcessor clamps foldAmount to kMaxFoldAmount = 10 (wavefolder_processor.h:125, 261), and the primitive also clamps to 10 (wavefolder.h:150). So the 12-fold figures should be the folds-10 values: -20 dBFS for triangle and -26.6 dBFS for Buchla, not -21.6 and -28.2.

Severity stays medium. This is a large, audible level and usability defect on one of the 26 types at default settings, but nothing becomes unsafe and no NaN is produced.

findings.title: Wavefold level collapse (-23 to -47 dBFS) fully accounted for: default Smooth LP on an FM-index-24 spectrum, filters rated for 8x and clocked twice per sample, and centre-pan -3 dB; level drops as drive rises
findings.problem: A Node.js replica of the adapter chain reproduces all nine probe measurements within 0.9 dB. The chain: drive x input -> fold -> WavefolderProcessor DC blocker -> 50/50 shape blend -> wavefoldSmoothFilter_ at 20000*(500/20000)^0.5 = 3162 Hz (the Smooth slot defaults to 0.5, so the LP is on by default) -> tone LP 4 kHz -> centre pan. In the plugin both one-poles carry coefficients for 8x the rate (band_processor.h:111,124). They are also clocked twice per output sample because L and R share one MorphEngine, so effective cutoffs are fc/4: 790 Hz and 1 kHz. Default folds are 6.5, so the sine fold sin(6.5 x 3.75 sin wt) has a modulation index of 24.4 rad and a Carson bandwidth of about 26 kHz. Its energy sits above Nyquist (aliased) and far above the effective LPs, which remove most of it. More drive pushes energy higher, so the output gets quieter: probe -23.2, -26.6, -31.0 dBFS for drive 2.5, 7.5, 10.
findings.why_wrong: Drive should raise or saturate the level, not lower it monotonically. 'Smooth' is an optional tone control, but here it defaults to a 3.16 kHz low-pass (and about 790 Hz effective in the plugin). The fold spectrum at default Folds x Drive does not fit under Nyquist at 1x, so the type is mostly alias energy before the filters remove it.
findings.consequence: The three wavefolders sit 20-45 dB below the other types at default settings and lose level as the user turns Drive up. This explains D-145. It also explains the -11.4 to -11.9 dB adapter-vs-processor gaps (probe lines 18, 19, 25), which the replica predicts as -11.4 dB (Sine/Triangle) and -12.4 dB (Serge). Breakdown at SineFold drive 7.5: shape blend -5.4 dB, default smooth plus tone LP at the correct rate -4.1 dB peak (-7.9 dB RMS), 8x mis-rating with double clocking -13.8 dB, pan -3 dB. Only the mis-rating and the double clocking are already-reported defects; the default Smooth of 0.5, the 0.5 shape blend and the folds-x-drive index are not.
findings.suggested_fix: Besides the reported 8x-rate and shared-L/R fixes: default the Smooth slot to 0 for SineFold, TriangleFold, SergeFold, FullRectify and HalfRectify; default Folds to 1-2 (slot near 0-0.1) so the default index fits under Nyquist; and consider normalising the drive into the fold (fold gain on a unit-peak signal) instead of multiplying drive x folds. Promote the replica as a processor-level test: SineFold, all defaults, drive 2.5/7.5/10, 1031.25 Hz at -6 dBFS, 48 kHz; peak must stay within 6 dB across the three drives and above -12 dBFS.
findings.evidence: distortion_adapter.cpp:664, 673, 689 `wavefoldSmoothFilter_.setCutoff(20000.0f * std::pow(500.0f / 20000.0f, p.smoothness));` with p.smoothness = slots[4] or slots[5], default 0.5 (processor_params.cpp:94, 103, 113). OnePoleLP coefficient a = exp(-2*pi*fc/fs) with fs taken at prepare (one_pole.h:136-139). Probe settings: audit_probes.cpp.txt:433-441 (only type, mix, bias and drive set; slots stay at 0.5). Replica fold_sim2.js (double-clocked, then -3 dB pan) vs probe peak dBFS: Sine 2.5/7.5/10 = -23.31/-26.54/-31.88 vs -23.23/-26.64/-31.04; Serge = -46.81/-47.38/-36.00 vs -47.18/-47.52/-35.93. Same chain at the adapter's own correct 48 kHz rate: Sine -7.82/-9.71/-15.68 dBFS peak, Serge -31.83/-33.25/-25.87.

I could not refute it under the context lens. The defaults the finding relies on are real in code. Nothing upstream guards them, and they contradict the spec rather than following it.

(1) Every slot starts at 0.5. That holds for MorphNode::shapeSlots (morph_node.h:43-44) and for the ShapeShadowStorage constructor, which sets all types to 0.5 and gives only BitwiseMangler its own values (morph_node.h:102-114). On a type change, processor_params.cpp:844-852 loads those 0.5 slots and calls mapShapeSlotsToParams. The controller also registers every node shape slot with default 0.5 (parameter_registration.cpp:821-823 and the kNodeShape0 loop at :948ff). A real host therefore starts at these values too.

(2) The mapping at processor_params.cpp:88-114 turns slot 0.5 into these values:
- SineFold and TriangleFold: folds = 1 + 0.5*11 = 6.5 and shape/angle = 0.5. Smoothness = 0.5 is slot 4.
- SergeFold: the same 6.5 folds, with smoothness in slot 5.

(3) The adapter applies all of this.
- distortion_adapter.cpp:664/673/689 sets wavefoldSmoothFilter_ to 20000*(0.025)^0.5, about 3162 Hz.
- processRaw runs that filter on every wavefold sample (:389, :406, :422). Unlike Rectify (:432, :443), the wavefold types have no smoothness>0.001 bypass.
- The 50/50 blend with the second folder is active because shape is above 0.001 (:384-386, :418-420).
- Drive multiplies the input before the fold (:211).

(4) This is not a documented design decision. specs/Disrumpo/ui-mockups.md:354-358, 382-386 and 410-415 give different defaults:
- SineFold: Folds 2, Shape 0.0, Smooth 0.3.
- TriangleFold: Folds 2, Smooth 0.3.
- SergeFold: Folds 3, Smooth 0.3.
- Rectify (:437, :459): Smooth 0.2.
The generic 0.5 defaults therefore depart from the spec. That backs the finding's point that the default Smooth, the Shape blend and the Folds index are new causes, separate from the already-reported 8x mis-rating and shared L/R clocking.

I did not re-run the Node replica. The code path it models matches what I read, so the measured monotonic level drop with drive is consistent with the source. Medium severity stands: the level loss is audible and partly caused by defaults that are off-spec. Part of the magnitude comes from defects that are already reported.

I could not refute the measured consequence.

**What the source confirms**
- MorphNode shape slots default to 0.5 (morph_node.h:43-44), and ShapeShadowStorage restores 0.5 on a type change (morph_node.h:102-106). With those defaults, processor_params.cpp:90-94 maps SineFold to folds 6.5, shape 0.5 and smoothness 0.5. TriangleFold (99-103) and SergeFold (108-113) map the same way; for SergeFold, slot 2 = 0.5 gives foldModel int(1.5+0.5) = 2, which is Buchla259, not Serge.
- distortion_adapter.cpp:664/673/689 sets the smoothing LP to 20000*(0.025)^0.5 = 3162 Hz, so the LP is on by default. processRaw at lines 376-423 runs the chain as claimed: fold, then the 50/50 shape blend, then the smoothing LP. Drive multiplies the input before the fold (line 211).
- band_processor.h:111 and :124 prepare the adapter and the MorphEngine at sampleRate*8. Lines 487-488, 493-494 and 753-757 clock one adapter/engine for both L and R.
- applyOutputStage uses equal-power pan, so centre pan costs -3 dB (band_processor.h:770-780).

**Probe measurements (f:/tmp/disrumpo-audit/probe-results.txt, lines 521-544)**

| Type | Peak dBFS at drive 0.25 / 0.75 / 1.0 |
|---|---|
| SineFold | -23.23 / -26.64 / -31.04 |
| TriangleFold | -23.25 / -26.65 / -31.04 |
| SergeFold | -47.18 / -47.52 / -35.93 |
| SoftClip | -4.67 / -4.06 / -3.99 |
| HardClip | about -9.1 to -9.6 |

So the fold types sit about 18-43 dB below the clippers at default settings. The adapter-vs-processor gaps are also present: -11.39 dB (SineFold, line 19), -11.38 dB (TriangleFold, line 25) and -11.92 dB (SergeFold, line 18).

**Replica check**
I ran the replica at scratchpad/fold_sim2.js. With the 8x mis-rating and double clocking it gives Sine -20.31/-23.54/-28.88 dBFS before pan, which is -23.3/-26.5/-31.9 after pan. That matches the probe within 0.9 dB, as claimed.

**Corrections to the finding**
- Level falls monotonically with drive only for Sine and Triangle. SergeFold gets louder at drive 1.0 (-47.5 to -35.9 dBFS).
- The quoted "correct 48 kHz" figures (-7.82/-9.71/-15.68) do not come out of the current script. It gives -6.41/-7.72/-10.87 before pan, which is about -9.4/-10.7/-13.9 after pan.
- The replica also shows how much of the loss is new versus already reported. At the correct rate, with smoothing off and tone off, the Sine fold is flat at about -6 dBFS (-5.89/-5.61/-6.22). With smoothing at its 0.5 default it falls 4.5 dB in peak and 9 dB in RMS as drive rises. So the defaults alone still cost about 4-9 dB of drive-dependent loss and leave the folds 5-10 dB below SoftClip. The default Buchla259 model for SergeFold stays around -21 to -28 dBFS even with no filters.

**Severity**
The largest share of the collapse (about 13.8 dB) belongs to the defects that are already reported: the 8x coefficients and the shared L/R clocking. The new part (defaulting smoothing and shape to 0.5, folds x drive) still has an audible effect of medium size on three default-selectable types. I am keeping the severity at medium.

findings.title: The probe's 121-preset baseline table measures the host-restore defect, not the presets: every type-specific field is at its DistortionParams default in those renders
findings.problem: The preset probe loads each .vstpreset with Processor::setState into a fresh active Rig and renders. That path never calls mapShapeSlotsToParams (processor_state.cpp:852-889), so the threshold, curve, sag, feedback, folds and similar fields stay at the defaults left by setupProcessing's SoftClip nodes. The peak/RMS/DC numbers per preset (probe-results.txt preset:* rows, e.g. :301) describe presets with their shape settings discarded.
findings.why_wrong: A baseline used to judge preset levels (rms > -60, peak <= 0 dBFS) should reflect what the preset sounds like on the path that maps its slots, or should be labelled as the host-restore path. Rectified_Drums shows the gap: -50.8 dBFS measured vs about -12 dBFS intended.
findings.consequence: The report's preset level tables and any 'preset X is too quiet/loud' findings derived from them can be wrong in either direction. A fix-plan task that promotes these numbers to goldens would pin the bug.
findings.suggested_fix: When promoting the probe, render each preset twice: once via setState (host path, expected to match after the setState mapping fix) and once by replaying every parameter through processParameterChanges (preset-browser path). Assert the two agree within 1e-4 and gate levels on the replayed render.
findings.evidence: audit_probes.cpp.txt:1502-1504 `Rig r(sr); okA = setStateBytes(*r.p, bytes); r.render(in, in, aL, aR);` and :1541 'setState on active proc'. processor_state.cpp:871 writes shapeSlots only. distortion_adapter.h:85 threshold default 0.7. findings.title: No evidence that any preset falls below -60 dBFS after the round trip: the probe never measures the reloaded render's level, and bounds put 22 of 35 at -38.9 dBFS RMS or higher
findings.problem: The preset probe reports peak, RMS and DC only for render 'a' (load(file) on an active processor), and only maxAbsDiff for the reloaded render 'b'. 'Lose audio' cannot be read off these numbers. From the triangle inequality, rms_b >= rms_a - maxdiff and peak_b >= maxdiff - peak_a. Applied to the 35 flagged presets, 22 have rms_b at -38.87 dBFS or higher (lowest Random_Scan; most are above -30). Pitch_Tracker (peak_b >= +0.62 dBFS) and Sharp_Focus (peak_b >= -13.07 dBFS, against peak_a -31.74) get louder after reload, not quieter. The remaining 11 (Wide_Sweep, Step_Scanner, Synced_Pulse, Chaos_Morph_4, Chaotic_Sweep, Evolving_Texture, Three_Node_Blend, Chaos_Engine, Serge_Madness, All_Types_Morph, Spectral_Scatter) are unbounded either way.
findings.why_wrong: A claim that audio is lost has to come from a level measurement of the reloaded render. The only preset under -60 dBFS RMS in the whole run is Drums/Rectified_Drums (-62.22 dBFS), and that is already the level of a fresh file load. Its round trip is clean (rt 9.3e-10), so its quietness is a load or DSP issue (rectifier types), not a serialisation issue. None of the three identified mechanisms (baked sweep centre, mode forced to Linear1D, smoothing forced to 0) mutes the signal. They change the sweep position, the morph weights and the glide.
findings.consequence: The report should not carry 'presets lose audio after save/reload' as a severity driver. The real consequence is that the sound changes, by up to 1.25 full-scale and sometimes louder. Any residual silence risk is limited to the 11 unbounded presets and stays unmeasured.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the probe (and the promoted regression test) to emit peak, RMS and DC for render b as well as the rms delta b-a in dB. Assert rms_b > -60 dBFS and |rms_b - rms_a| < 0.1 dB in addition to maxdiff <= 1e-5. Separately, treat Rectified_Drums' -62 dBFS fresh-load level as its own item.
findings.evidence: audit_probes.cpp.txt:1522-1533 compute pk/rms/dc from aL/aR only and `rt = max(maxAbsDiff(dL,bL), maxAbsDiff(dR,bR))`.
