findings.title: DCBlocker latches NaN/Inf permanently, and the adapter puts it straight after shapers that pass NaN through: one bad sample silences the band's wet path for good (in other plugins the output stays NaN)
findings.problem: DCBlocker::process computes y = x - x1_ + R_*y1_, then stores x1_ = x and y1_ = flushDenormal(y), with no finiteness check. flushDenormal (db_utils.h:263-265) returns NaN unchanged, because both of its comparisons are false for NaN. After one NaN input, x1_ and y1_ are NaN and every later output is NaN until reset(). One +/-Inf input sets x1_ = Inf, and the next sample computes x - Inf + R*Inf = NaN, so Inf latches too. In Disrumpo the adapter's own dcBlocker_ runs on the wet signal for AsymmetricFuzz, FullRectify, HalfRectify and FeedbackDist (distortion_adapter.cpp:218-220, 586-592). FullRectify passes NaN straight in: std::abs(NaN) at cpp:431, and the smoothing filter is skipped when smoothness <= 0.001 (cpp:432). HalfRectify passes +Inf through (cpp:442). The shared TubeStage, FuzzProcessor, WavefolderProcessor and TapeSaturator all have zero isNaN/isFinite checks and an internal DCBlocker (tube_stage.h:301, fuzz_processor.h:551, wavefolder_processor.h:373, tape_saturator.h:376), so they latch the same way.
findings.why_wrong: A filter state must not keep a non-finite value forever. The project rule says NaN/Inf must never reach the output, and the sibling primitives OnePoleLP (one_pole.h:107-111) and Biquad reset and return 0 on non-finite input. FR-016 ('NaN propagates') is a per-sample contract. The DC blocker turns it into a permanent latch, and its tests only check the first output (dc_blocker_test.cpp:543-581), never recovery.
findings.consequence: Disrumpo in 1-band mode passes input straight to the bands with no biquad in between (crossover_network.h:194-198). One NaN or Inf sample from the host then poisons the node's DC blocker. The adapter's tone OnePoleLP sees NaN on every following sample, resets and returns 0 (one_pole.h:107-111). The node's wet path stays at digital silence until setActive or prepare. At mix 100 % the band is muted for the rest of the session, and that sample's dry NaN also reaches the output. Every other plugin that composes TubeStage, Fuzz, Wavefolder or Tape (amp_channel.h, fuzz_pedal.h, tape_machine.h, distortion_rack.h, bass_character_stage.h, seraphis_engine.h, vorago_engine.h, ruinae_voice.h) has no trailing OnePoleLP, so for them the output stays NaN permanently. CROSS-PLUGIN IMPACT.
findings.suggested_fix: In DCBlocker::process, after computing y, test with detail::isFinite(y) (never std::isnan). If it fails, reset x1_ and y1_ to 0 and return 0, matching OnePoleLP and Biquad, and update the FR-016 doc. Add a test to dc_blocker_test.cpp (in dsp_ieee_tests, since it injects NaN): feed 10 normal samples, one NaN, then 100 normal samples, and assert the last output is finite. Do the same for +Inf. Add a Disrumpo test: 1 band, node FullRectify, mix 1, feed one NaN sample then a sine, and assert non-zero finite output after 100 samples.
findings.evidence: dc_blocker.h:202-208 `float y = x - x1_ + R_ * y1_; x1_ = x; y1_ = detail::flushDenormal(y); return y;`. db_utils.h:263-265 `return (x > -kDenormalThreshold && x < kDenormalThreshold) ? 0.0f : x;` (NaN is returned unchanged). distortion_adapter.cpp:431 `float result = std::abs(input);`, :442 `(input >= thresh) ? input : 0.0f`, :218-220 `if (needsDCBlock_) wet = dcBlocker_.process(wet);`. one_pole.h:108-111 resets and returns 0. crossover_network.h:195-197 `if (numBands_ == 1) { bands[0] = input; return; }`. grep -c isNaN|isFinite|isInf gives 0 for tube_stage.h, fuzz_processor.h, wavefolder_processor.h and tape_saturator.h. Lead 3 is refuted: FormantDistortion has no guard (formant_distortion.h:169-195), but FormantFilter's Biquads return 0 on NaN (formant_filter.h:534-537), so its DCBlocker sees finite input. Its envelope NaN is unused because envelopeFollowAmount_ defaults to 0 (:465) and the adapter never sets it (distortion_adapter.cpp:862-874), so no latch is reachable there.
verifier_notes:
The latch mechanism holds up in source, but in Disrumpo it is only reachable in a narrower case than the finding claims.

Confirmed:
- dc_blocker.h:202-208 computes `y = x - x1_ + R_*y1_; x1_ = x; y1_ = detail::flushDenormal(y); return y;` with no finiteness check.
- flushDenormal (db_utils.h:264-266) returns NaN unchanged, because both comparisons are false for NaN.
- So one NaN leaves x1_ and y1_ as NaN, and every later output is NaN until reset().
- One Inf sets x1_ = Inf, and the next sample computes x - Inf + R*Inf, which is NaN or Inf, so Inf latches too.

Disrumpo wiring:
- distortion_adapter.cpp:218-220 applies dcBlocker_ when needsDCBlock_ is set. updateDCBlockerState (:586-592) sets it for AsymmetricFuzz, FullRectify, HalfRectify and FeedbackDist.
- FullRectify (:431-434) passes NaN through std::abs, and its filter is skipped when smoothness <= 0.001.
- After the DC blocker, toneFilter_ (OnePoleLP, one_pole.h:108-111) sees NaN, resets and returns 0, so wet = 0. At mix 1 (:247-248) the node's wet output stays silent. That matches the claimed consequence.
- `grep isNaN|isFinite|isInf|sanitize` over plugins/disrumpo/src returns no matches, so nothing in the plugin guards host input.
- crossover_network.h:195-197 passes input straight through in 1-band mode.
- BandProcessor::process (band_processor.h:473-496) hands the sample to morphEngine_ or distortion_ with no guard.

Where the finding overstates reachability:
- BandProcessor::processWithFactor (band_processor.h:627-650) routes factors 2, 4 and 8 through the Oversampler. Its Economy/ZeroLatency mode uses BiquadCascade filters (oversampler.h:374-375).
- Biquad::process (biquad.h:352-356) resets and returns 0 on non-finite input, so a host NaN becomes 0 before it reaches the adapter.
- The DC-blocked types default to 4x or 2x (distortion_types.h:172-203).
- So a host NaN reaches the latch only on the 1x direct path: factor == 1 at band_processor.h:632, or the global kOversampleMaxId set to 1x. A NaN generated inside the shaper itself would still latch at any factor.

The cross-plugin latch follows from the same unguarded primitive. I did not trace each consumer's host-input guards.

The FR-016 "NaN propagated" comment documents per-sample propagation, not permanent poisoning. The project rule says NaN must never reach the output, so this is a real defect.

Severity is downgraded: in Disrumpo the trigger needs a non-finite host sample plus the 1x path. The default 2x/4x oversampling path neutralises it.

The latch is real, and nothing in its context guards against it. dc_blocker.h:202-208 computes `y = x - x1_ + R_*y1_`, then stores x1_ = x and y1_ = flushDenormal(y) with no finiteness check. Once a NaN gets into x1_/y1_, every later output is NaN until reset(). The FR-016 note at :192 ("NaN inputs are propagated") and the test at dc_blocker_test.cpp:543-557 only pin that the first output is NaN. Neither documents permanent latching as intended, and nothing tests recovery. The retired spec specs/051-dc-blocker is not in the tree.

Disrumpo has no input sanitisation anywhere. A grep for isNaN|isFinite|isInf over plugins/disrumpo/src finds nothing. The path the finding needs is reachable:
- 1-band mode bypasses the crossover (crossover_network.h:194-198).
- 1x oversampling is a user-selectable mode: kOversampleMaxId index 0 = 1x (processor_params.cpp:349-361).
- At 1x, distortion_adapter.cpp:215-220 runs processRaw, then dcBlocker_ for AsymmetricFuzz, FullRectify, HalfRectify and FeedbackDist (:586-592). FullRectify is std::abs(input) with the smoothing filter skipped when smoothness <= 0.001 (:430-434), so the NaN goes straight in.
- The tone OnePoleLP then resets and returns 0 on every following NaN (one_pole.h:107-111). The wet path stays silent until DistortionAdapter::reset() (:98-103), which only runs via BandProcessor::reset / processor reset.

So the claimed consequence holds in that configuration.

Mitigating context, which supports a downgrade but not a refutation:
1. At 2x/4x/8x the IIR oversampler uses BiquadCascade (oversampler.h:372-375). Biquad::process resets and returns 0 on non-finite input (biquad.h:354-357), so the adapter never sees NaN there. Multi-band mode likewise goes through the crossover's filters. The latch therefore needs 1 band plus an effective factor of 1x. The four DC-blocked types all recommend 2x or 4x (distortion_types.h:170-200), so 1x comes from the user's max-oversample choice (or a dominant 1x node).
2. The trigger is a non-finite sample from the host, which is a host fault. That same NaN already reaches Disrumpo's output through the dry term (:235) whatever the DC blocker does.

The defect is real, but narrower than "medium" implies.

The DCBlocker latch is real. dc_blocker.h:202-208 computes y = x - x1_ + R_*y1_, stores x1_ = x and y1_ = flushDenormal(y), and never checks finiteness. A NaN or Inf input therefore stays in the state until reset(). The adapter puts it on the wet path at distortion_adapter.cpp:218-220. FullRectify (abs, :431) and HalfRectify (:442) pass a non-finite input through to it.

In Disrumpo the claimed consequence only happens in one narrow setup, because a NaN normally never reaches the adapter:
(1) The default oversampling routes around it. All four DC-blocked types (AsymmetricFuzz, FullRectify, HalfRectify, FeedbackDist), and Tube, Tape and Fuzz with their internal DCBlockers, have a recommended factor of 4 or 2 (distortion_types.h:170-203). The default max factor is 4 (processor.h:145, maxOversampleFactor_{4}). So the band takes processWithOversampling2x/4x (band_processor.h:637-642), not the direct path. The Economy/ZeroLatency oversampler runs BiquadCascade::processBlock on the zero-stuffed input (oversampler.h:595-626). Each stage calls Biquad::process (biquad.h:374-377, 471-474), which resets and returns 0 on non-finite input (biquad.h:354-357). The adapter only ever sees finite samples, so the DC blocker cannot latch.
(2) The latch is reachable only when the user sets Oversample Max to 1x (processor_params.cpp:349-361 maps index 0 to 1), so that processWithFactor takes the factor == 1 direct path (band_processor.h:632-636). The plugin must also be in 1-band mode (crossover pass-through), and the host or an upstream plugin must deliver a NaN or Inf sample, which is already a malformed stream. In that case the band's wet path does go silent until reset, as claimed. With FullRectify/HalfRectify smoothness > 0.001, the smoothing filter runs first, which probably breaks the chain too.
(3) The cross-plugin claim, that other plugins' outputs stay NaN for good, is not shown. The finding cites no trace through any of those engines' input paths or output guards.

Verdict: a real latent primitive defect worth hardening, but in Disrumpo it needs a non-default 1x setting, 1 band and non-finite host input. The impact is lower than medium. Downgrade to low.

findings.title: RingSaturation at Mod Depth 0 skips its soft limiter and DC blocker: up to +8 dB level jump between depth 0 and depth 0+
findings.problem: process() returns the input unchanged when depth_ == 0 (lines 270-272). For any depth > 0 the signal goes through the stages, then softLimit(x) = 2*tanh(x/2) (line 418) and dcBlocker_ (lines 279-280). As depth approaches 0, processStage approaches input + 0*ringModTerm (line 337), so the depth-0+ output is 2*tanh(x/2) of the input while depth 0 gives x raw. Disrumpo maps the RingSat Mod Depth knob (slot 0) directly to depth (processor_params.cpp:168, distortion_adapter.cpp:776), and the adapter feeds input*drive with drive up to 10 (distortion_adapter.cpp:211). Lead 2 (NaN passthrough) is refuted: lines 262-264 return before touching any state, so it is stateless. The NaN then hits the adapter tone OnePoleLP, which zeroes it.
findings.why_wrong: A 'depth 0 = no ring mod' bypass must be continuous with small depths. Here the limiter and DC blocker, which belong to the processor's output stage rather than to the modulation, switch in and out on an exact-equality test. The output is bounded to +/-2 for depth > 0 and unbounded at depth 0. Sliding Mod Depth fully down, or morphing to a node with modDepth 0 (morph_engine.cpp:577 interpolates modDepth linearly), crosses that edge.
findings.consequence: With the input driven to x = 5 (drive 10, -6 dBFS input), depth 0.001 gives 2*tanh(2.5) = 1.97 and depth 0 gives 5.0: an +8.1 dB jump and a click as the knob reaches its end stop. At x = 1.25 (drive 2.5) the jump is +1.0 dB. The DC blocker's state also freezes while depth is 0 and resumes with stale state.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the depth_ == 0 early return, or keep it only for the ring-mod term and always apply softLimit and dcBlocker_ so depth 0 means 'saturate and limit without ring mod'. Alternatively, crossfade the bypass over the depth range [0, 0.01]. Add a dsp_primitives test: feed a sine at amplitude 2.5 with depth 0 and depth 1e-4, and require the RMS difference to be within 0.1 dB.
findings.evidence: ring_saturation.h:270-272 `if (depth_ == 0.0f) { return input; }`. :279-280 `signal = softLimit(signal); signal = dcBlocker_.process(signal);`. :337 `float output = input + ringModTerm * depth_;`. :417-418 `return kSoftLimitScale * Sigmoid::tanh(x * 0.5f);` with kSoftLimitScale = 2.0f (:84). processor_params.cpp:168 `p.modDepth = slots[0];`. Computed: 2*tanh(2.5) = 1.973 vs 5 (-8.07 dB); 2*tanh(0.625) = 1.109 vs 1.25 (-1.04 dB).
verifier_notes:
I could not refute it. The source does what the finding says.

- **Exact-zero bypass:** dsp/include/krate/dsp/primitives/ring_saturation.h:270-272 has `if (depth_ == 0.0f) { return input; }`. It sits after the NaN check (:262-264) and the Inf check (:266-268), and before the stage loop, `softLimit` (:279) and `dcBlocker_.process` (:280).
- **Small depth is close to identity before the limiter:** processStage (:336-337) computes `output = input + (input*saturated*(carrier+bias_) - input) * depth_`. As depth goes to 0 this tends to `input` in every stage, so the depth-0+ output tends to `softLimit(input)` = `2*tanh(input/2)` (:417-418, kSoftLimitScale = 2 at :84), then a 10 Hz DC blocker. At depth == 0 the raw input is returned. So the transfer function is discontinuous at depth 0 for any input that is not tiny: about -0.7 dB at x = 1, -1.04 dB at x = 1.25, -8.07 dB at x = 5.
- **Disrumpo reaches that edge.** processor_params.cpp:168 sets `p.modDepth = slots[0]` (raw [0,1]). distortion_adapter.cpp:776 calls `setModulationDepth(p.modDepth)`, which clamps to [0,1] (:183). distortion_adapter.cpp:211 feeds `input * commonParams_.drive`. Drive is `value * 10` (processor_params.cpp:858) and is clamped to [0,10] (band_processor.h:445, morph_engine.cpp:713). The Mod knob at its lower end stop gives exactly 0.0f. morph_engine.cpp:577 accumulates `w * p.modDepth` linearly.
- **Intentional?** dsp/tests/unit/primitives/ring_saturation_test.cpp:302-307, :1602 and :1637 test the depth-0 bypass as specified behaviour (SC-002), so "depth 0 = dry" is the intended contract. The tests do not cover continuity near 0. Because the output limiter is always on for depth > 0, the contract and the limiter together create the jump the finding describes. The defect is real.
- **DC blocker:** the claim that its state freezes while depth is 0 is also correct (:280 is skipped).

**Severity: unchanged (none).** The jump happens only at the exact end stop, or when the morph result is exactly 0. The largest +8 dB case needs high drive with the RingSat type selected. Medium is reasonable.

I confirmed the defect from source, and nothing upstream masks it. ring_saturation.h:270-272 returns `input` raw when `depth_ == 0.0f`. For any depth above 0, process() goes through processStage, then softLimit (`2*tanh(x/2)`, :417-418, kSoftLimitScale=2 at :84), then dcBlocker_ (:279-280). As depth goes to 0, processStage returns `input + ringModTerm*depth_` (:337), which approaches `input`. So depth 0+ gives 2*tanh(x/2)·DCblock(x) and depth 0 gives x. The output is discontinuous at exactly 0.

Disrumpo can reach that point:
- Slot 0 maps straight to modDepth (processor_params.cpp:168, `p.modDepth = slots[0]`), so normalized 0 gives exactly 0.0.
- The adapter forwards it unchanged (distortion_adapter.cpp:776).
- The adapter feeds `input * drive` into processRaw (distortion_adapter.cpp:211 → :540).
- Drive reaches 10: processor_params.cpp:858 `value * 10.0f`, band_processor.h:445 clamps to [0,10].
- The morph engine interpolates modDepth linearly (morph_engine.cpp:577), so a cursor sitting on a modDepth-0 node also lands on exactly 0.

On the context lens: the depth-0 bypass itself is intentional. It is pinned by dsp/tests/unit/primitives/ring_saturation_test.cpp:302-329 (SC-002, "returns input unchanged"). That test only checks inputs within ±1 at drive 2 on the bare primitive. No test checks continuity, and I found no spec or code comment that accepts the limiter/DC-blocker switching at the edge. specs/Disrumpo/dsp-details.md:460-463 describes D16 only as self-modulation. So the intended bypass is implemented with a side effect nobody documented: the output stage switches with it. That is not a deliberate design decision.

The magnitude depends on drive. At drive 1 and a 0.5 input the jump is about 0.18 dB. At drive 10 it is about 8 dB, which matches the finding's arithmetic (2*tanh(2.5)=1.97 vs 5). The jump happens only at the end stop or exactly on a node, so medium severity stands. The NaN aside in the finding (:262-264 is stateless) is accurate and does not change the verdict.

The source confirms the claim. In ring_saturation.h:270-272, `depth_ == 0.0f` returns the input raw. For any depth above 0 the signal goes through processStage, where :337 gives `output = input + ringModTerm*depth_`, so the result tends to `input` as depth tends to 0. It then goes through softLimit (:417-418, 2*tanh(x/2), kSoftLimitScale=2 at :84) and dcBlocker_ (:279-280). Depth 0+ is therefore about 2*tanh(x/2) of the input, while depth 0 is x itself.

How Disrumpo drives it:
- The input reaching processRaw is `input * commonParams_.drive` (distortion_adapter.cpp:211). RingSaturation is not exempt the way Temporal and Stochastic are (:207-208).
- processRaw sends it straight to `ringSaturation_.process(input)` (:538-540). After that there is only the adapter tone filter and the dry/wet mix (:225-234).
- needsDCBlock_ (:588-591) does not include RingSaturation, so nothing downstream bounds the depth-0 path.
- Mod Depth maps 1:1 from slot 0 (processor_params.cpp:168 to distortion_adapter.cpp:776). The slot reaches exactly 0.0 at the knob's end stop. It also does when the morph weights land on modDepth-0 nodes (morph_engine.cpp:468/577, a linear weighted sum).

The numbers check out: 2*tanh(2.5)=1.973 vs 5 gives -8.07 dB, and 2*tanh(0.625)=1.109 vs 1.25 gives -1.04 dB. With drive 10 the depth-0 path is a plain 10x gain (+20 dB) with no limiting, so the jump can exceed 8 dB.

Limits on the impact:
- It only matters once the driven input is above about 1. At x=0.5 the difference is about 0.1 dB, and the 10 Hz DC blocker's effect is negligible.
- The default modDepth is 0.5 (distortion_adapter.h:136), so the default sound is unaffected.
- The depth-0 bypass itself is intentional and tested (SC-002, ring_saturation tests :302-307, :1602 'depth=0 is pure bypass'). That intent covers passing the signal through unchanged at 0, not the discontinuity at depth 0+. The fix would have to keep SC-002 at 0, for example by crossfading over small depths.

The parameter is set per block with no smoothing, so crossing the edge is a step and therefore a click. It is a shared primitive, so the impact may reach other plugins. Medium severity stands.

findings.title: Crossover3Way/Crossover4Way allpass compensation uses Q = 0.5 where LR4 needs Q = 1/sqrt(2): about -0.13 dB sum error at one-octave spacing, which breaks their own SC-004/SC-005 0.1 dB spec
findings.problem: Both classes configure their D'Appolito compensation allpasses with kAllpassQ = 0.5f and the comment 'matches LR4 phase'. For an LR4 crossover, LP + HP = (s^2 - sqrt2*s + 1)/(s^2 + sqrt2*s + 1), a second-order allpass with Q = 0.7071. Disrumpo's own crossover_network.h uses 0.7071 correctly. With Q = 0.5 the compensated low band is out of phase with the mid+high path near the lower crossover. Crossover4Way's sub band passes through two mismatched allpasses (lines 806-808), which adds to the error.
findings.why_wrong: Phase compensation only works when the compensating allpass matches the phase of the higher crossover's LP+HP sum exactly. The SC-004/SC-005 tests (crossover_filter_test.cpp:1738-1827) pass only because they space the crossovers a decade apart (300/3000 Hz), where the mismatch is -0.018 dB.
findings.consequence: No production code currently enables compensation (grep: setAllpassCompensation is called only from crossover_filter_test.cpp). FractalDistortion's Crossover4Way (fractal_distortion.h:683, 965-967) runs uncompensated. The defect is latent, but the shared API ships with a wrong constant. The next consumer that turns compensation on with one-octave crossovers gets a -0.13 dB dip, more than the 0.1 dB the class promises. CROSS-PLUGIN.
findings.suggested_fix: Set kAllpassQ = 0.70710678f in both classes and fix the comment. Add flat-sum test sections with one-octave spacing (e.g. 300/600 Hz and 80/160/320 Hz), which fail at Q = 0.5 (-0.129 dB) and pass at 0.7071.
findings.evidence: crossover_filter.h:423 and :643 `static constexpr float kAllpassQ = 0.5f;  ///< Q for 2nd-order allpass (matches LR4 phase)`. :594 `lowBandAllpass_.configure(FilterType::Allpass, freq, kAllpassQ, 0.0f, srFloat);`. Analog model (scratchpad apq.js) of the Crossover3Way sum LP1*AP(f2,Q) + HP1*LR4sum(f2), worst-case deviation: f1=300/f2=3000: Q0.5 -0.018 dB; 300/1200: -0.082 dB; 300/600: -0.129 dB at 292 Hz; 1000/2000: -0.129 dB; 80/300: -0.089 dB. Q=0.7071 gives 0.000 dB in every case.
verifier_notes:
I could not refute the finding. Every claim checks out against the source.

1. The constant. crossover_filter.h:423 and :643 both declare `kAllpassQ = 0.5f` with the comment "matches LR4 phase". It is used at :594 (`lowBandAllpass_`) and at :839, :840 and :843 (the sub-band allpasses at lowMid and midHigh, and the low-band allpass at midHigh).

2. The LR4 it is meant to match. CrossoverLR4::updateCoefficients (:360-365) cascades two Butterworth stages, both at kButterworthQ = 0.7071 (biquad.h:56). process() (:315-322) returns LP and HP without inverting either, so LP + HP = (1 + s^4)/(s^2 + sqrt2*s + 1)^2 = (s^2 - sqrt2*s + 1)/(s^2 + sqrt2*s + 1). That is a second-order allpass with Q = 1/sqrt2.

3. What Q = 0.5 actually builds. Biquad's Allpass case (biquad.h:725-729) is the RBJ form: b0 = 1 - alpha, b1 = -2cos, b2 = 1 + alpha, with alpha = sin/(2Q). Its analog prototype is (s^2 - s/Q + 1)/(s^2 + s/Q + 1). At Q = 0.5 that is ((s-1)/(s+1))^2, which does not match the LR4 sum's phase.

4. The topology is otherwise right. In the 3-way (:554-566), the low band skips crossover2, while split1.high goes through crossover2, whose LP+HP is the LR4 allpass at f2. The low band therefore needs AP(f2, 0.7071). In the 4-way (:793-814), the sub band needs AP(lowMid)·AP(midHigh) and the low band needs AP(midHigh), which is exactly what the code applies. The only defect is the Q value.

5. The numbers. I re-ran the analog model myself (scratchpad apq_verify.js). With Q = 0.5 the worst-case error is -0.018 dB at 300/3000 Hz, -0.082 dB at 300/1200 Hz, -0.129 dB at 300/600 Hz and -0.129 dB at 1000/2000 Hz. With Q = 0.7071 it is 0.000 dB in every case. This matches the finding: the decade-spaced SC tests hide the error, and at one-octave spacing it exceeds the 0.1 dB the doc comments promise (:408, :628).

6. Scope. A grep for `setAllpassCompensation(true` finds it only in dsp/tests/unit/processors/crossover_filter_test.cpp, so no production consumer enables compensation. Disrumpo's own crossover_network.h:55 uses kAllpassQ = 0.7071f. The defect is real but latent, and the low severity is appropriate.

I could not refute this. crossover_filter.h:423 and :643 set `kAllpassQ = 0.5f` with the comment "matches LR4 phase". :594 and :839-843 pass it into `Biquad::configure(FilterType::Allpass, ...)`. biquad.h:725-732 and :859-866 are the standard RBJ allpass: b0 = 1-alpha, b2 = 1+alpha, with alpha = sin(w)/(2Q). So Q = 0.5 gives (s-1)^2/(s+1)^2, which is two first-order allpasses in series. CrossoverLR4 (crossover_filter.h:360-365) cascades two Butterworth stages (`kButterworthQ`). Its LP+HP sum is therefore (s^2 - sqrt2*s + 1)/(s^2 + sqrt2*s + 1), an allpass with Q = 0.7071, not 0.5. Disrumpo's own plugins/disrumpo/src/dsp/crossover_network.h:52-55 uses `kAllpassQ = 0.7071f` and states that LR4 is two cascaded Butterworth Q = 0.7071 sections, which contradicts the shared header. No guard elsewhere fixes it. I found no spec or code comment that records 0.5 as a deliberate choice; the class doc at :405-408 promises a 0.1 dB flat sum. The SC-004/SC-005 tests (crossover_filter_test.cpp:1738-1827) use only 300/3000 Hz and 80/300/3000 Hz with a 0.1 dB margin, so they never test a narrow spacing. I re-ran an analog model of Crossover3Way's compensated sum (scratchpad ap.js). With Q = 0.5 the worst deviation is -0.018 dB at 300/3000, -0.082 dB at 300/1200 and -0.129 dB at 300/600. With Q = 0.7071 it is 0.000 dB in every case. The 300/600 figure breaks the class's own 0.1 dB promise. A grep for `setAllpassCompensation` outside the header finds only crossover_filter_test.cpp:1692-1730, so no production consumer turns compensation on. The defect is therefore latent in a shared API and not audible in Disrumpo today. Low severity fits.

The defect is real and I reproduced its numbers in the digital domain. It is latent and small, so "low" is the right severity.

Source:
- crossover_filter.h:423 and :643 set `kAllpassQ = 0.5f`.
- :594 and :839-843 build the compensation stages with `Biquad::configure(FilterType::Allpass, f, kAllpassQ, ...)`.
- biquad.h:725-731 builds the allpass from the RBJ cookbook formula (b0 = 1-alpha, b2 = 1+alpha, alpha = sin(w)/(2Q)). Its analog prototype is (s^2 - s/Q + 1)/(s^2 + s/Q + 1).
- CrossoverLR4 (:360-365) cascades two Butterworth biquads (kButterworthQ). Its LP+HP sum is (s^2 - sqrt2*s + 1)/(s^2 + sqrt2*s + 1), an allpass with Q = 0.7071.
- At Q = 0.5 the compensator becomes (s-1)^2/(s+1)^2, which is not the LR4 sum, so the phase match fails.
- Topology checked. Crossover3Way::process (:548-566) applies the allpass to the low band. Crossover4Way::process (:787-814) applies AP(f2)*AP(f3) to the sub band and AP(f3) to the low band. That is the correct D'Appolito structure, so the Q constant is the only error.

Measurement: I wrote a double-precision Node evaluation of the exact RBJ biquads at fs = 44.1 kHz (scratchpad apq_dig.js) and took the worst-case deviation of the summed bands.

| Crossovers (Hz) | Q = 0.5 | Q = 0.7071 |
|---|---|---|
| 3-way 300/3000 | -0.018 dB | 0.0000 dB |
| 3-way 300/1200 | -0.082 dB | 0.0000 dB |
| 3-way 300/600 | -0.129 dB @ 292 Hz | 0.0000 dB |
| 3-way 1000/2000 | -0.129 dB | 0.0000 dB |
| 3-way 80/300 | -0.089 dB | 0.0000 dB |
| 4-way 80/300/3000 | -0.089 dB | 0.0000 dB |
| 4-way 80/160/320 | -0.149 dB @ 84 Hz | 0.0000 dB |
| 4-way 100/200/400 | -0.149 dB | 0.0000 dB |

The 3-way values match the reviewer's analog model, and the 4-way values add to the claim. At one-octave spacing the sum misses the 0.1 dB SC-004/SC-005 promise.

Why the tests miss it: the strict tests (crossover_filter_test.cpp:1738-1827) use 300/3000 and 80/300/3000 with a 0.1 dB margin. The worst case there is -0.018 dB for the 3-way and -0.089 dB for the 4-way, so both pass. The FFT allpass tests (:1932-2010) allow 5 dB and 7 dB and catch nothing.

Impact:
- No plugin code calls setAllpassCompensation or uses Crossover3Way/Crossover4Way; the grep of plugins/ for those names returns nothing.
- The only production user is FractalDistortion's Crossover4Way (fractal_distortion.h:682, :1013), and it runs without compensation.
- The flaw is latent: a magnitude error of at most about 0.15 dB that only shows when a future consumer turns compensation on with closely spaced crossovers.

The claim, its severity and its CROSS-PLUGIN tag are accurate. No severity change.

findings.title: LFO random generator is not MINSTD: the uint32 multiply wraps before the modulus, giving a 79,493-step cycle instead of 2^31-2, reseeded to 12345 on every reset
findings.problem: nextRandomValue computes randomState_ * 48271u % 2147483647u in uint32. The product wraps mod 2^32 before the % 2^31-1, so this is not the MINSTD generator the comment names. Measured from the fixed seed 12345: a 68,319-step tail, then a 79,493-step cycle. State 0 is a fixed point with one reachable 31-bit preimage (1622613393, which maps to 0). It is not on the 12345 orbit, so the generator does not stick at 0 from the default seed. reset() reseeds every LFO to 12345 (line 98), so every LFO instance draws the same S&H/SmoothRandom sequence.
findings.why_wrong: MINSTD needs a 64-bit intermediate (uint64_t(x)*48271 % 2147483647) for its full period and its statistics. The code's comment claims MINSTD parameters, and its behaviour has neither property.
findings.consequence: Audible impact is small: one draw per LFO cycle at 20 Hz repeats only after about 2 h (tail plus cycle). Disrumpo's LFO1 and LFO2, and any two LFOs in Ruinae/Profundum (morph_state.h:265 and profundum_morph_modulator.h:133 expose SmoothRandom), produce identical random step sequences that restart on every setActive. Two 'Random' modulators at the same rate move in lockstep. CROSS-PLUGIN.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a 64-bit intermediate: randomState_ = static_cast<uint32_t>((uint64_t{randomState_} * 48271u) % 2147483647u). Guard a 0 seed. Let callers seed per instance (e.g. setSeed), and have the ModulationEngine give LFO1 and LFO2 different seeds. Add a dsp_primitives test: two LFOs on SampleHold with different seeds produce different first values, and the generator reproduces the known MINSTD sequence from seed 1 (48271, 182605794, ...).
findings.evidence: lfo.h:477 `randomState_ = randomState_ * 48271u % 2147483647u;`, :98 `randomState_ = 12345u;` in reset, :560 `uint32_t randomState_ = 12345u;`. Measured by scratchpad lcg.js (Brent cycle detection, Math.imul semantics): 'cycle length lambda=79493', 'tail mu=68319', 'preimage of target 2147483647: x=1622613393 ... step(x)=0'. Mean of the first 1e6 outputs is 0.00151.
verifier_notes:
I could not refute this. The source matches the finding, and the cycle numbers reproduce exactly.

**Source (dsp/include/krate/dsp/primitives/lfo.h):**
- Line 476 has the comment "LCG parameters (same as MINSTD)".
- Line 477 is `randomState_ = randomState_ * 48271u % 2147483647u;`. `randomState_` is a `uint32_t` (line 560), so the multiply is done in 32-bit unsigned arithmetic. It wraps mod 2^32 before the `% 2147483647u` is applied, so this is not MINSTD.
- Line 98: `reset()` hard-sets `randomState_ = 12345u`. The class has no `setSeed` and no other seed path (grep for seed/randomState finds only lines 97, 98, 477, 479 and 560).
- So every LFO instance draws the same sequence after `prepare`/`reset`.

**Measurement:** I ran my own Brent cycle detection in node, using `Math.imul(x, 48271) >>> 0`, which matches uint32 wrap semantics, then `% 2147483647`. From seed 12345 it printed `lambda 79493 mu 68319`, the same as the finding.

**Severity:** Low still fits. The impact is identical random sequences across LFO instances and a short period. There is no crash, no NaN and no real-time safety problem. The output mapping at line 479 stays in about [-1, 1].

I did not trace the ModulationEngine's LFO1/LFO2 construction to confirm that neither applies a phase offset or desynchronises them some other way. Even so, the LFO class itself offers no way to seed an instance differently, so identical sequences after reset follow from lfo.h alone.

I could not refute it, and the context lens finds no guard. lfo.h:477 is `randomState_ = randomState_ * 48271u % 2147483647u;` with `uint32_t randomState_` (lfo.h:560), so the multiply wraps mod 2^32 before the modulus. The comment at :476 says "same as MINSTD", so this is not a documented design choice. It contradicts its own comment. The header has no other seed path: a grep for randomState/setSeed/seed in lfo.h finds only :97-98 (reset reseeds to 12345u), :477, :479 and :560. Nothing seeds per instance, so ModulationEngine's `LFO lfo1_; LFO lfo2_;` (modulation_engine.h:810-811) both get the same 12345 seed and the same S&H/SmoothRandom step sequence after every reset. I reproduced the quoted measurement with node using Math.imul and uint32 semantics from seed 12345: tail mu=68319, cycle lambda=79493. That matches the finding. No spec or comment says the lockstep or the short period is intended. Low severity fits: one draw per LFO cycle makes the period hard to hear, and the main practical effect is that LFO1 and LFO2 on Random move in lockstep across plugins.

I confirmed the defect from source and by measuring it again. dsp/include/krate/dsp/primitives/lfo.h:477 computes `randomState_ = randomState_ * 48271u % 2147483647u;` with randomState_ declared `uint32_t` (line 560). The multiply wraps mod 2^32 before the modulus, so this is not the MINSTD generator the line-476 comment names. reset() at lines 98-101 reseeds to 12345u and draws current/target from there. retrigger() at lines 273-277 does not reseed; it keeps drawing from the shared sequence. I re-ran the cycle measurement with Math.imul semantics from seed 12345 and got mu=68319 and lambda=79493, the same as the finding. In modulation_engine.h, lines 128-129 call lfo1_.reset() and lfo2_.reset(), so both LFOs start from the same seed and produce the same random value sequence. They step in lockstep when they run at the same rate, waveform and phase. At different rates they draw the same values at different times. The impact matches the claimed low severity. A 147,812-draw orbit at one draw per cycle repeats only after about 2 h at 20 Hz, so you cannot hear the short period. The visible effect is that Random/S&H LFOs are correlated across instances and repeat the same sequence after every setActive or reset. That is a predictability and quality issue, not a level, click or safety hazard. NaN cannot occur: the output is bounded in [-1, 1] and 0 is not on the 12345 orbit. Low is the right severity, and the CROSS-PLUGIN reach through the shared primitive holds.

findings.title: FastMath::fastTanh returns the numeric_limits quiet_NaN() constant in a header compiled with -ffast-math on macOS
findings.problem: For NaN input, fastTanh returns std::numeric_limits<float>::quiet_NaN(). The finiteness test itself is correct (detail::isNaN). Producing a NaN constant in fast-math code is what the project rule forbids: it is undefined behaviour under -ffinite-math-only, and clang warns with -Wnan-infinity-disabled. The site is a known debt ratcheted at tools/lint-nonfinite-symbols-baseline.json:3 ('fast_math.h': 1). The header is included by 13 dsp/include headers and called by distortion_adapter.cpp:282 (SoftClip).
findings.why_wrong: The documented contract 'NaN input returns NaN' (fast_math.h:55) can be met without the constant: returning x propagates the incoming NaN. On the macOS leg the compiler may assume a fast-math function never returns NaN and fold away the caller's downstream detail::isNaN checks, or treat the branch as unreachable.
findings.consequence: The NaN path can behave differently on macOS than on Windows and Linux, and it keeps one entry in the non-finite-symbol lint baseline that could be removed. No audible effect on Windows or Linux. CROSS-PLUGIN (every fastTanh caller).
findings.suggested_fix: Replace `return std::numeric_limits<float>::quiet_NaN();` with `return x;`, keeping constexpr. Remove the fast_math.h entry from tools/lint-nonfinite-symbols-baseline.json so the ratchet goes down. The existing fastTanh NaN test in dsp_ieee_tests still passes because x is NaN.
findings.evidence: fast_math.h:66-68 `if (detail::isNaN(x)) { return std::numeric_limits<float>::quiet_NaN(); }`. lint-nonfinite-symbols-baseline.json:3 `"dsp/include/krate/dsp/core/fast_math.h": 1`. distortion_adapter.cpp:282 `headroom * Krate::DSP::FastMath::fastTanh(excess * curveDrive)`. `grep -rln fast_math.h dsp/include | wc -l` gives 13.
verifier_notes:
The code says what the finding claims. dsp/include/krate/dsp/core/fast_math.h:65-69 is `constexpr float fastTanh(float x)`, and its first branch is `if (detail::isNaN(x)) { return std::numeric_limits<float>::quiet_NaN(); }`. The header is not compiled -fno-fast-math, and the project rule (root CLAUDE.md fast-math section; dsp/CLAUDE.md table row 2) forbids quiet_NaN()/infinity() constants in fast-math code. tools/lint-nonfinite-symbols-baseline.json:3 records this exact site as ratcheted debt (`"dsp/include/krate/dsp/core/fast_math.h": 1`). The site is reachable from Disrumpo: plugins/disrumpo/src/dsp/distortion_adapter.cpp:282 calls `Krate::DSP::FastMath::fastTanh(excess * curveDrive)`. Returning `x` keeps the documented "NaN input returns NaN" contract (fast_math.h:56) without the constant, and the existing test at dsp/tests/unit/core/fast_math_test.cpp:99-101 (`REQUIRE(isNaN(fastTanh(nan)))`) would still pass. That test is listed under two targets in dsp/tests/CMakeLists.txt (lines 37 and 994; the second is presumably the IEEE target).

One part of the consequence is overstated. Downstream `detail::isNaN` checks would not be folded away: db_utils.h:100-133 implements isNaN/isFinite through an opaqueFloatBits barrier documented as surviving -ffast-math. So the realistic effect is the UB constant itself, which can fold to a finite value or trigger -Wnan-infinity-disabled under -ffinite-math-only, plus one lint-baseline entry that could be removed. The same pattern also appears at db_utils.h:169 and :221, which are covered by that file's own 5-entry baseline.

Verdict: a real but minor portability and rule-conformance defect, correctly rated low. Not refuted.

Confirmed from source. dsp/include/krate/dsp/core/fast_math.h:67-68 reads `if (detail::isNaN(x)) { return std::numeric_limits<float>::quiet_NaN(); }`. The NaN test is the approved Krate::DSP::detail::isNaN (aliased at fast_math.h:36), but the return value is the numeric_limits NaN constant. Project CLAUDE.md forbids that constant in fast-math code, even as a seed or a return value, because it is undefined behaviour there and trips clang -Wnan-infinity-disabled. I looked for context that would make it intentional or guarded and found none. The only mention of it is tools/lint-nonfinite-symbols-baseline.json:3 (`"dsp/include/krate/dsp/core/fast_math.h": 1`). CLAUDE.md describes that file as a ratchet over pre-existing hits, which records debt to pay down and does not approve the use. No comment in fast_math.h or in specs explains choosing the constant over `return x`. The doc contract at fast_math.h:56 ('NaN input returns NaN') is met equally by returning x, so the fix is behaviour-preserving. The header is shared (namespace Krate::DSP::FastMath, Layer 0), and Disrumpo calls it at plugins/disrumpo/src/dsp/distortion_adapter.cpp:282 (`headroom * Krate::DSP::FastMath::fastTanh(excess * curveDrive)`), with the include at line 11. That makes the cross-plugin portability label accurate. The real-world impact is only reachable when a NaN already reaches the shaper, and this applies only to the macOS fast-math leg, so the stated 'low' severity fits. Nothing I found refutes the finding.

The code is as the finding says. dsp/include/krate/dsp/core/fast_math.h:67-68 is `if (detail::isNaN(x)) { return std::numeric_limits<float>::quiet_NaN(); }`. tools/lint-nonfinite-symbols-baseline.json:3 records it as ratcheted debt (`"dsp/include/krate/dsp/core/fast_math.h": 1`). Under the project rule (CLAUDE.md:241, no quiet_NaN() constant in fast-math code) it is a real violation, and the proposed `return x;` meets the contract at fast_math.h:56 ("NaN input returns NaN") without the constant.

The stated consequence is overstated, though:
1. The claim that the compiler "may fold away the caller's downstream detail::isNaN checks" cannot happen. detail::isNaN (db_utils.h:100-104) reads the bits through opaqueFloatBits (db_utils.h:69-73), whose empty `__asm__("" : "+r"(bits))` is there precisely to cut the finite-math value facts. So no NaN/Inf guard that uses it can be folded by any assumption about fastTanh's return value.
2. The output is NaN either way. In the Disrumpo caller (distortion_adapter.cpp:263-284, SoftClip), a NaN input fails `absX <= threshold` and reaches fastTanh(NaN * curveDrive); both the current constant and the proposed `return x` give NaN, which then goes to `sgn * (threshold + headroom*NaN)`. Nothing changes in dB, in samples, or for any host or setting, on any OS.
3. The NaN branch only runs when NaN is already in the signal path, which is a separate upstream defect.

What remains is a lint-baseline/rule-hygiene item (one ratchet entry, and a possible clang -Wnan-infinity-disabled diagnostic on the macOS leg). It has no audible effect and no observable behavioural difference across platforms. It is not refuted because the rule violation and the baseline entry are real, but the impact is below 'low': a nit-level cleanup.

findings.title: WaveshapeType::Diode is documented UNBOUNDED but is bounded to (-2, 1); the overflow-to-Inf lead does not hold, and the -Inf input case returns NaN despite the 'Infinity handled gracefully' contract
findings.problem: waveshaper.h:44 and :58 say Diode 'can exceed [-1,1]', UNBOUNDED. Asymmetric::diode (sigmoid.h:358-366) is 1 - exp(-1.5x) for x >= 0, bounded below 1, and x/(1 - 0.5x) for x < 0, which tends to -2. So the output lies in (-2, 1) for every finite input and cannot overflow to Inf. With drive up to 10, the Granular 5x and feedback loops, nothing escalates: AllpassSaturator and FeedbackDistortion soft-clip the feedback to +/-2 (allpass_saturator.h:351-352, 498, 811, 845). For x = -Inf the reverse branch evaluates -Inf/Inf = NaN, which contradicts process()'s '@note Infinity inputs are handled gracefully' (waveshaper.h:204). waveshaper_test.cpp:577-581 accepts that as 'indeterminate'.
findings.why_wrong: The doc should state the real bound so consumers size their headroom correctly, and the Inf contract should hold for every type. Disrumpo reaches Diode via Temporal curve index 7 (distortion_adapter.cpp:761-764), which has no DC blocker or limiter, so the negative half peaks at -2.0 (+6 dBFS). That is a bounded, documentable figure, not 'unbounded'.
findings.consequence: Documentation drift only, plus one edge case: -Inf into Diode gives NaN, and NaN then latches downstream DC blockers (see the DCBlocker finding). No overflow path exists. Recorded so the lead is closed with evidence.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the doc to 'Diode: bounded to (-2, 1), asymmetric: +6 dB headroom needed on the negative half'. In Asymmetric::diode, return -2.0f when x is -Inf, tested via detail::isInf, never std::isinf. Tighten waveshaper_test.cpp:577 to REQUIRE(output == -2.0f) in dsp_ieee_tests.
findings.evidence: sigmoid.h:359-365 `if (x >= 0.0f) return 1.0f - std::exp(-x * 1.5f); else return x / (1.0f - 0.5f * x);`. waveshaper.h:58 `Diode = 7, ... (UNBOUNDED - can exceed [-1,1])`. :204 `@note Infinity inputs are handled gracefully`. allpass_saturator.h:351-352 `return Sigmoid::tanh(x * 0.5f) * 2.0f;` used at :498, :811, :845. distortion_adapter.cpp:761-764 maps curve to WaveshapeType index 0..8 for Temporal.
verifier_notes: I re-derived the claim from source and it holds. sigmoid.h:358-366 Asymmetric::diode returns `1.0f - std::exp(-x * 1.5f)` for x >= 0, which lies in [0, 1). For x < 0 it returns `x / (1.0f - 0.5f * x)`, which decreases monotonically toward -2 as x goes to -inf. That makes the output bounded to (-2, 1) for every finite input. Even at x = -FLT_MAX the denominator 1 + 0.5*FLT_MAX stays finite and the result is about -2, so no finite input overflows. waveshaper.h:44 ("Unbounded types (Diode only): Output can exceed [-1, 1]") and :58 ("UNBOUNDED - can exceed [-1,1]") are therefore imprecise. The output does exceed [-1,1] on the negative half, but it is not unbounded: it stops at -2. For x = -Inf, process() (waveshaper.h:205-216) computes drive*x + asym = -Inf, and applyShape (:259-260) calls diode. That evaluates -Inf / (1 - 0.5*(-Inf)) = -Inf / +Inf = NaN under IEEE, which contradicts the "@note Infinity inputs are handled gracefully" at :204. waveshaper_test.cpp:577-584 accepts any of Inf, NaN or finite, so the case is untested in practice; its comment at :581 itself calls the result "indeterminate". Disrumpo reaches Diode through Temporal curve index 7 (distortion_adapter.cpp:761-764, `p.dynamicCurve * 8.0f + 0.5f`, clamped 0..8) and also through AllpassSaturator kSatTypes[2] (distortion_adapter.cpp:833-840), RingSaturation (:780-783), Spectral (:898-900) and Fractal (:934-936). The finding's own conclusion is correct: no overflow path exists, so this is documentation drift plus one IEEE edge case (-Inf input). Under the macOS -ffast-math leg an Inf input is undefined anyway, and normal audio never produces one. Low severity is appropriate.

The maths in the finding is right, but what it describes is documented and pinned by tests, so it is not a defect.

(1) The word "UNBOUNDED" is defined where it is used. waveshaper.h:42-45 splits the types into "Bounded types ... Output is bounded to [-1, 1]" and "Unbounded types (Diode only): Output can exceed [-1, 1]; users responsible for post-shaping limiting". :58 says the same thing: "UNBOUNDED - can exceed [-1,1]". Both statements are true. Asymmetric::diode (sigmoid.h:358-366) is x/(1-0.5x) for x < 0, which reaches -1.2 at x = -3. waveshaper_test.cpp:660-671 ("Diode type (only unbounded type) can exceed [-1,1] bounds") pins exactly this: REQUIRE(output < -1.0f). The header never says the output can overflow to Inf. The "overflow-to-Inf lead" is the reviewer's own conjecture, and the finding itself refutes it.

(2) A NaN from -Inf is a deliberate, test-pinned design choice. waveshaper_test.cpp:577-584 runs -Inf through Diode and says in its comment that "-inf / inf (indeterminate) ... may be NaN, -Inf, or a finite value". It then accepts all three results. Tube's ±Inf sections (around :512-517 and :568-575) accept NaN in the same way. So "handled gracefully" (waveshaper.h:204, FR-029) has a known per-type meaning for the two polynomial/rational asymmetric types: no crash or UB trap, with an indeterminate result allowed. The Diode case is not a special exception.

(3) The class also documents that the caller handles post-conditioning. waveshaper.h:44-45 says "users responsible for post-shaping limiting", and :86-87 and :102-103 say to compose with DCBlocker. An Inf sample can only reach this point if the host feeds Inf audio. Under the macOS -ffast-math leg the -Inf behaviour is not defined anyway, so no test there could tighten it portably.

The finding's own consequence line reads "Documentation drift only ... No overflow path exists. Recorded so the lead is closed with evidence". That is the reviewer closing a dead lead, not reporting a defect.

Confirmed from source. sigmoid.h:358-366: Asymmetric::diode returns 1 - exp(-1.5x) for x >= 0, which stays below 1, and x/(1 - 0.5x) for x < 0, which tends to -2. Every finite input therefore lands in (-2, 1). waveshaper.h:44 and :58 call Diode "UNBOUNDED". That word is wrong, but the phrase next to it, "can exceed [-1,1]", is still true, because the negative half reaches about -2 (+6 dBFS). For x = -Inf the reverse branch computes -Inf/(1+Inf) = -Inf/Inf = NaN, which contradicts the "Infinity inputs are handled gracefully" note at waveshaper.h:204. waveshaper_test.cpp:577-584 accepts any result there, Inf, NaN or finite. Diode is reachable in Disrumpo: distortion_adapter.cpp:761-764 maps the Temporal curve (index 0..8) to WaveshapeType, and index 7 is Diode.

On impact, the consequence is smaller than claimed. (1) The doc problem is one wrong word; the claim that the curve exceeds [-1,1] still holds. (2) The -Inf to NaN case adds no consequence of its own. Disrumpo does not check host input for finiteness: grepping processor.cpp, band_processor.h and distortion_adapter.cpp for isFinite/isNaN/isInf/sanitize finds nothing. So a host -Inf goes through input gain and the CrossoverLR4 biquads before any band shaper. Those biquads already turn Inf into Inf/NaN state (Inf - Inf in the recursion), and the Temporal envelope follower would track Inf too. The output is broken before Diode's own NaN matters. (3) The "handled gracefully" contract already fails for Tube in the same way (waveshaper_test.cpp:568-575 explicitly accepts NaN for Tube), so Diode is not the odd one out. (4) Under the macOS -ffast-math build, Inf arithmetic is undefined anyway, so making Diode return -2 at -Inf would not hold there unless an isInf branch is added. The finding is real but it is documentation accuracy only, with no reachable audible or stability effect, so it ranks below "low".

findings.title: Serge Fold 'Model' menu labels are swapped for entries 0/1, and the default slot value runs Buchla259 instead of Serge
findings.problem: The SergeFold Model COptionMenu lists 'Simple,Serge,Buchla,Lockhart'. The processor decodes slot 2 as foldModel = int(slot*3+0.5), so the value maps to the menu index. The adapter then indexes models[] = {Serge, Simple, Buchla259, Lockhart}, which is not in WavefolderModel enum order (Simple=0, Serge=1, Buchla259=2, Lockhart=3). Menu entry 'Simple' selects the Serge model and entry 'Serge' selects Simple. The default shape slot is also 0.5: ShapeShadowStorage sets every slot to 0.5 and the node registration default is 0.5. 0.5 decodes to int(2.0)=2, which is Buchla259, so a newly chosen 'Serge Fold' node does not run the Serge model at all.
findings.why_wrong: A list control's label must name the DSP state it selects. The adapter comment ('0=Serge, 1=Simple') shows a deliberate reorder that the uidesc was never updated to match. The type is called Serge Fold and its default should be the Serge model, but the 0.5 default lands on index 2.
findings.consequence: Today the already-reported slot-2 stepCount-8 defect hides this, because VSTGUI replaces the menu items with '0'..'8'. Once that is fixed, picking 'Serge' gives the plain Simple triangle fold and picking 'Simple' gives Serge. Every default Serge Fold node, including factory presets that never set slot 2, runs Buchla259. Host text has no Serge-specific formatter (format_helpers.h has no SergeFold case), so nothing reveals the mismatch.
findings.suggested_fix: Make one table authoritative. Either reorder the adapter's models[] to the enum order and the uidesc labels to match, or change the uidesc to 'Serge,Simple,Buchla,Lockhart'. Give the SergeFold slot 2 a ShapeShadowStorage default that selects Serge. Fix this together with the slot-2 stepCount (stepCount 3, or a StringList proxy). Test: drive DistortionAdapter SergeFold through mapShapeSlotsToParams with slot2 = k/3 for k=0..3, assert getModel() equals the model named by uidesc menu entry k, and assert the default slot decodes to WavefolderModel::Serge. Add a controller test that reads the uidesc menu-items for TypeParams_SergeFold.
findings.evidence: editor.uidesc:974 menu-items="Simple,Serge,Buchla,Lockhart" (control-tag Band.NodeShape2); processor_params.cpp:110 p.foldModel = static_cast<int>(slots[2] * 3.0f + 0.5f); distortion_adapter.cpp:677-685 '// 0=Serge, 1=Simple, 2=Buchla259, 3=Lockhart' models[] = {Serge, Simple, Buchla259, Lockhart}; wavefolder_processor.h:56-60 Simple=0, Serge=1, Buchla259=2, Lockhart=3; morph_node.h:102-106 all shadow slots default 0.5f; parameter_registration.cpp:957-961 shape slot default 0.5, stepCount 8 for s==2.
verifier_notes: I traced the full path from source and could not refute it. (1) editor.uidesc:974: the SergeFold Model COptionMenu on Band.NodeShape2 has menu-items="Simple,Serge,Buchla,Lockhart". (2) processor_params.cpp:110 decodes slot 2 as p.foldModel = static_cast<int>(slots[2] * 3.0f + 0.5f), so menu index k (normalized k/3) gives foldModel k. (3) distortion_adapter.cpp:677-685 indexes models[] = {Serge, Simple, Buchla259, Lockhart}, with the comment "0=Serge, 1=Simple". (4) The shared enum at dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/wavefolder_processor.h:56-60 is Simple=0, Serge=1, Buchla259=2, Lockhart=3. So the menu's index-0 label "Simple" runs WavefolderModel::Serge, and index-1 "Serge" runs Simple. (5) distortion_adapter.cpp:410-416 sends the SergeFold signal through wavefolder_.process using the model set at :685, so the model choice is audible. (6) Defaults: morph_node.h:43-44 (MorphNode::shapeSlots all 0.5f) and morph_node.h:102-106 (ShapeShadowStorage sets every slot to 0.5f; only BitwiseMangler gets an override) both start slot 2 at 0.5. parameter_registration.cpp:961 also registers the shape-slot default as 0.5, and :957 gives slot 2 stepCount 8. 0.5*3+0.5 = 2.0, int 2, models[2] = Buchla259, so a fresh Serge Fold node runs Buchla259, not Serge. No test pins label against model: distortion_adapter_test.cpp:375-395 only sets params.foldModel directly and never checks the uidesc order or the default decode. The mismatch is real. Medium severity fits: the wrong model is audible and the labels mislead, but nothing crashes and no NaN reaches the output.

I could not refute this. I read every link in the chain and found nothing that guards against it or documents it as intended.
(1) editor.uidesc:974: the COptionMenu bound to Band.NodeShape2 has menu-items="Simple,Serge,Buchla,Lockhart".
(2) processor_params.cpp:106-110: for SergeFold, slot 2 decodes as p.foldModel = int(slots[2]*3+0.5). Menu index k at value k/3 therefore gives foldModel k.
(3) distortion_adapter.cpp:676-685: the adapter maps that through models[] = {Serge, Simple, Buchla259, Lockhart}, and its comment says "0=Serge, 1=Simple". processRaw at :410-412 does not override the model.
(4) wavefolder_processor.h:56-60: the enum order is Simple=0, Serge=1, Buchla259=2, Lockhart=3. So menu entry 0 "Simple" runs Serge and entry 1 "Serge" runs Simple. Entries 2 and 3 match.
(5) morph_node.h:102-114: ShapeShadowStorage defaults every slot to 0.5. Only BitwiseMangler gets an override; SergeFold gets none.
(6) parameter_registration.cpp:957-961: the shape-slot default is 0.5, with stepCount 8 for s==2. 0.5 decodes to int(2.0)=2, which runs Buchla259.

Nothing intentional explains this. No spec under specs/Disrumpo documents the model order. The archived spec 003 (tasks.md:118) and the distortion_types.h:44 comment say SergeFold should use Lockhart, so a Buchla259 default contradicts the documented intent as well.

The only test, distortion_adapter_test.cpp:358-404, sets foldModel 0, 1 and 3 directly on DistortionParams. It only checks that the outputs differ, and it never checks the uidesc labels or the default slot.

Factory presets that call shapeSergeFold encode model/3 (preset_generator.cpp:607-612) and use the generator's own index, so they are self-consistent. Presets and new nodes that leave slot 2 at its default still land on Buchla259.

The finding says the label mismatch is partly masked today by the separate slot-2 stepCount-8 issue. That is consistent with the code, and it does not make the mapping correct. Medium severity stands.

The source facts check out, but neither claimed consequence can happen in the shipped code, so the impact lens refutes the finding at medium severity.

What is true:
- editor.uidesc:974 has menu-items="Simple,Serge,Buchla,Lockhart" on control-tag Band.NodeShape2.
- processor_params.cpp:110 decodes foldModel = int(slot2*3+0.5).
- distortion_adapter.cpp:677-685 maps models[] = {Serge, Simple, Buchla259, Lockhart}.
- wavefolder_processor.h:56-60 declares Simple=0, Serge=1, Buchla259=2, Lockhart=3.
- The defaults are 0.5 (morph_node.h:102-106, parameter_registration.cpp:961 and the proxy at :823). 0.5 decodes to index 2, which is Buchla259.

Why the label swap has no effect:
- The menu is bound to the band proxy kBandDisplayedShape2, a RangeParameter with stepCount 8 (parameter_registration.cpp:820-823). The node param also has stepCount 8 (:957).
- For any parameter with stepCount > 0, VST3Editor clears the menu and rebuilds it from getParamStringByValue (extern/vst3sdk/vstgui4/vstgui/plugin-bindings/vst3editor.cpp:325-330, optMenu->removeAllEntry() then addEntry for i=0..stepCount). So the uidesc menu-items string is never displayed.
- The same holds after either fix the finding suggests. With stepCount 3 on a RangeParameter, the menu shows the parameter's number strings. With a StringListParameter, it shows the list's own strings. The uidesc labels only matter if stepCount drops to 0, which nobody proposes.
- The "Simple and Serge are swapped" consequence only arises from a hypothetical future change and is overwritten under the proposed fixes. Today it has no audible or visible effect. At most it is a low-severity stale-string cleanup inside the already-reported slot-2 stepCount defect.

Why the Buchla259 default is not a defect:
- The finding argues the "Serge Fold" type should default to the Serge model. The project's own spec does not say that. specs/Disrumpo/specs-overview.md:89 lists D09 Serge Fold as `Wavefolder::Lockhart`, `WavefolderProcessor::Buchla259`. dsp-details.md:117 and roadmap.md:1124 map SergeFold to Lockhart. D07 Sine Fold is the type mapped to WavefolderProcessor::Serge (specs-overview.md:87, roadmap.md:1122).
- So the Buchla259 default is consistent with the spec's backend for D09. No preset or user sees a wrong model against any documented requirement.
- No audio defect follows: no level jump, NaN, aliasing or state break. The fold model is chosen by name only, and the DSP runs a valid model in every case.

Test coverage: distortion_adapter_test.cpp:368-404 exercises foldModel 0, 1 and 3 on the adapter directly and pins nothing about labels.

Net: the claimed medium-severity consequence cannot occur. What remains is a latent stale-string tidy-up.

findings.title: Base-Parameter mod registrations carry ms/Hz/%/deg units but no range: host and automation text shows the raw normalized value
findings.problem: LFO 1/2 Phase (deg), Env Attack/Release (ms), Env Sensitivity (%), Random Rate (Hz), Random Smoothness (%), S&H Rate (Hz), S&H Slew (ms), Pitch Min/Max (Hz), Pitch Tracking (ms), Transient Attack/Decay (ms) and Rungler Rate (Hz) all use the plain Parameter overload (title, units, stepCount, normalizedDefault, flags, id). Its toPlain is identity, so the displayed value is the normalized 0..1 number followed by the unit. The processor denormalizes these to real ranges: phase x360, attack 1+99v ms, release 10+490v ms, random/S&H/rungler 0.1+49.9v Hz, slew 500v ms, pitch min 20+480v, pitch max 200+4800v, tracking 10+290v, transient attack 0.5+9.5v, decay 20+180v. Controller::getParamStringByValue (controller.cpp:747-893) formats only node drive/mix/shape slots, band gain/displayed drive/mix/shape/pan and the global mix/gain, so every mod ID falls through to the base formatter. Route Amount is a RangeParameter -1..1 labelled '%', so +50 % reads '0.50 %'.
findings.why_wrong: VST3 hosts show ParameterInfo.units next to Parameter::toString(normalized). The pair must read in the unit the DSP uses, through a RangeParameter with the real min/max or a getParamStringByValue override. Here the unit label claims a physical value that the number does not express.
findings.consequence: In any host automation lane, generic editor or parameter readout, Env Attack's default 10 ms shows as '0.091 ms', Pitch Max 2000 Hz shows as '0.375 Hz', LFO Phase 180 deg shows as '0.5 deg', and a +100 % route amount shows as '1.00 %'. Users cannot type real values: getParamValueByString uses the identity mapping, so entering '50' for 50 ms clamps to normalized 1.0, which is 100 ms.
findings.suggested_fix: Register these as RangeParameter with the processor's min/max for the linear maps (attack 1..100, release 10..500, rates 0.1..50, slew 0..500, pitch 20..500 / 200..5000, tracking 10..300, transient 0.5..10 / 20..200, phase 0..360). Display Route Amount as a percentage (RangeParameter -100..100 '%' with the processor mapping unchanged, or a formatter). Take the ranges from one shared constant used by processor_params.cpp and processor_state.cpp. Test: for each mod ID, assert that getParamStringByValue(id, n) parses back to the processor's denormalized value for n in {0, 0.5, 1}.

- **Processor mapping:** processor_params.cpp maps the same IDs onto real ranges:
