findings.title: Expanded band panel is not tied to Band Count: it stays on screen for a band that was just removed, and an expand request made while the band is hidden is lost
findings.problem: AnimatedExpandController observes only the band's Expanded parameter. While the parent band is hidden, update() returns early on an expand request and stores nothing. Nothing calls it again when Band Count later reveals the band (didOpen wires the band-count ContainerVisibilityControllers only to tags 9000+b). The expanded containers (tags 9100-9103) are also siblings of the band containers in editor.uidesc, not children. When Band Count drops below b while band b is expanded, ContainerVisibilityController hides Band{b}Container but leaves the expanded strip visible.
findings.why_wrong: The expanded detail panel belongs to its band: the code comment cites FR-004 ('guard against expanding a hidden band'). Visibility should be a function of (Expanded && band visible) and should be re-evaluated when either input changes. Here it is evaluated on Expanded edges only.
findings.consequence: (a) Reducing Band Count from 4 to 2 with band 3 expanded leaves band 3's 690x290 expanded strip (morph pad, node selector, type params) covering the band columns, while it edits a band that no longer processes audio. (b) If a preset or host automation sets Expanded=1 for a hidden band and the band count is then raised, the band appears with its chevron 'on' and no panel. Toggling twice is the only recovery. Note: the cancel-callback concern from the map is not a defect (VSTGUI nulls the done notification on cancel unless notifyOnCancel).
findings.suggested_fix: Give AnimatedExpandController a second dependency on the Band Count parameter, or have the band ContainerVisibilityController notify it. In update(), compute shouldShow = expanded && bandVisible and apply it, collapsing the strip when the band hides and expanding it when a band appears with Expanded=1. Test (editor lifecycle harness): open the editor, set Band Count=4 and Band3Expanded=1, set Band Count=2, and assert the 9102 container is not visible. Set Band Count=4 again and assert it is visible with the expanded height.
findings.evidence: animated_expand_controller.cpp:79-81 'if (shouldExpand && !isParentBandVisible()) { return; }'; :37-42 addDependent only on watchedParam_ (Expanded); controller.cpp:1359-1366 band-count ContainerVisibilityController for containerTag 9000+b only; controller.cpp:1373-1381 AnimatedExpandController(&activeEditor_, expandedParam, 9100+b, 290, 250, 9000+b, b, 690); editor.uidesc:575-609 expanded containers (Band1..4ExpandedContainer markers) declared as siblings after Band4Container (565-574).
verifier_notes: I traced the code and could not refute the finding. (1) animated_expand_controller.cpp:37-42: the constructor calls addDependent only on watchedParam_, which is the band's Expanded param. Nothing else subscribes it. (2) :79-81 returns early when shouldExpand is true and the parent band is not visible. No pending state is stored, and nothing ever calls update() again. (3) controller.cpp:1359-1366 creates one ContainerVisibilityController per band on the Band Count param, with containerTag 9000+b only. controller.cpp:1373-1381 creates the AnimatedExpandController for 9100+b with parentBandTag 9000+b, and that tag is used only for the isParentBandVisible() query at :130-142. (4) visibility_controllers.h:175-195: ContainerVisibilityController::update calls setVisible only on the container that holds the 9000+b control, which is Band{b}Container. (5) editor.uidesc:535-574 holds Band1..4Container. :577-609 holds the expanded containers: four CViewContainers sized 690x290, visible=false, marked by Band{b}ExpandedContainer CParamDisplays. They are siblings inside the same 960x350 parent (line 534), not children of the band containers. So hiding Band3Container does not hide the expanded container. (6) No other controller code ties kBandExpanded to Band Count. Grepping controller/ for "Expanded" and kGlobalBandCount finds only registration, the sub-controller tag mapping and these two wiring sites. Both scenarios follow. (a) Band 3 is expanded and Band Count drops to 2: the 690x290 strip stays visible over the band area. (b) Expanded=1 is set while the band is hidden, then Band Count is raised: nothing re-evaluates, so the chevron is on but no panel shows. Medium severity is fair for a visible UI-state inconsistency with no audio impact.

Not refuted. The code confirms both halves of the claim, and I found nothing that guards or documents them.

(1) The expanded panel only watches its own Expanded parameter. animated_expand_controller.cpp:37-42 calls addDependent only on watchedParam_, which is the Expanded parameter passed in at controller.cpp:1374-1381. update() at :65-100 runs only when that parameter changes, and :79-81 returns early when shouldExpand is true and the parent band is hidden. That early return stores no pending state.

(2) Band Count changes never reach the expanded panel. controller.cpp:1359-1366 wires a ContainerVisibilityController to the band-count parameter for tags 9000+b only. Its update() (visibility_controllers.h:175-193) only calls setVisible on that one container. editor.uidesc:555-609 declares the four expanded containers (tags 9100-9103, mapped at uidesc:301-304) as siblings that come after Band4Container, not as children of it. So hiding Band3Container does not hide 9102.

(3) No other path resets Expanded or collapses the panel when Band Count changes. Searching the controller for kBandExpanded finds only registration (parameter_registration.cpp:709-711) and the didOpen wiring. The Controller has no setParamNormalized override that reacts to Band Count, and editParamWithNotify (controller.cpp:1868) is a plain setter.

(4) Case (b) can even happen without host automation. At editor open, the band controllers are built before the expand controllers (controller.cpp:1359-1366, then 1373-1383). Each one queues its first update with deferUpdate. A saved Expanded=1 on a hidden band therefore hits the early return and is never applied once the band is shown.

(5) The only test is expand_collapse_test.cpp:257-276. It checks a local boolean (shouldExpand && parentBandVisible) and never drives the real controller or a Band Count change.

The FR-004 comment covers only the expand direction. Nothing in specs/Disrumpo says the panel should stay up after its band is removed. Severity stays medium: a large stale panel covers the band columns and edits a band that no longer processes audio, but it does not affect the audio itself.

The defect is real, but it only affects the UI. animated_expand_controller.cpp:37-42 subscribes only to watchedParam_ (Band N Expanded). At :79-81 an expand request is dropped when the parent band is hidden, nothing is stored, and no later trigger retries it. controller.cpp:1359-1366 wires Band Count only to the ContainerVisibilityControllers for tags 9000+b. controller.cpp:1373-1381 builds the AnimatedExpandControllers with no Band Count dependency. Nothing else in src/controller reacts to kGlobalBandCount (grep shows only state load, the spectrum view, didOpen and the keyboard handler band count). editor.uidesc:535-574 holds the BandNContainer views (tags 9000-9003), and editor.uidesc:577-612 holds the expanded containers (9100-9103 markers) as siblings in the same 960x350 parent, not as children. So hiding Band3Container leaves a visible 9102 strip in place. positionContainerForBand puts band index 2 at x=min(480, 960-690)=270, so the strip covers the band 2-3 columns.

Scenario (b) also happens. Band N Expanded is registered with kNoFlags (parameter_registration.cpp:709-711), so host automation cannot set it. It can still get stuck at 1 while the band is hidden: expand band 3, then lower Band Count, or close and reopen the editor while Expanded=1 and the band is hidden. In the second case the constructor's deferUpdate hits the :79 early return, so raising Band Count later shows the chevron 'on' with no panel.

Impact: this is UI state only. No audio is affected (no dB, sample or NaN consequence), no data is lost, and no automation is involved. Recovery takes one click on the strip's own collapse chevron (editor.uidesc:1314, Band.Expanded toggle) or two clicks on the band chevron. This is a cosmetic or stale-UI inconsistency, so medium severity overstates it. Downgrade to low.

findings.title: Temporal mode: shape-slot default selects Derivative ('Transient') instead of EnvelopeFollow, and the adapter comment and spec list only 3 modes
findings.problem: The UI menu 'Follow,Inverse,Transient,Hyst' maps index k to TemporalMode k (EnvelopeFollow, InverseEnvelope, Derivative, Hysteresis), and processor_params decodes int(slot0*3+0.5). That wiring is consistent. The default slot0 is 0.5 (ShapeShadowStorage and the node registration default), which decodes to int(2.0)=2. A newly chosen Temporal node therefore runs Derivative, not the EnvelopeFollow mode implied by DistortionParams::dynamicMode = 0. The adapter header documents '0=Envelope, 1=Inverse, 2=Derivative' and specs-overview.md:219 lists 'Mode (Envelope/Inverse/Derivative)'. Both omit the reachable Hysteresis mode, and the Hysteresis-only Depth/Hold group is conditional on it.
findings.why_wrong: The neutral or documented default of a mode selector should be its first (classic) mode, and both documentation sites should list all four reachable modes. 0.5 is a continuous-knob centre that lands on an arbitrary enum member when reused for a list slot.
findings.consequence: Temporal nodes start in the transient-only mode: sustained material is barely distorted, which reads as 'Temporal does nothing' until the user finds the menu. Docs and spec under-describe the shipped feature.
findings.suggested_fix: Give list-type slots per-type defaults in ShapeShadowStorage (Temporal slot0 = 0.0, as is already done for BitwiseMangler slot0). Update distortion_adapter.h:127 and specs-overview.md:219 to the four modes with their UI names. Test: a default-constructed ShapeShadowStorage loaded for Temporal and passed through mapShapeSlotsToParams yields dynamicMode == 0.
findings.evidence: processor_params.cpp:156 p.dynamicMode = static_cast<int>(slots[0] * 3.0f + 0.5f); morph_node.h:102-113 all slots 0.5 except the BitwiseMangler override; editor.uidesc:1034 menu-items="Follow,Inverse,Transient,Hyst"; temporal_distortion.h:51-66 EnvelopeFollow=0 ... Hysteresis=3; distortion_adapter.h:127 'Mode: 0=Envelope, 1=Inverse, 2=Derivative'; specs-overview.md:219 'Mode (Envelope/Inverse/Derivative)'; distortion_adapter.cpp:745-746 clamps 0..3 and calls setMode.
verifier_notes:
I traced the code and the defect holds.

**The default lands on Derivative.**
- processor_params.cpp:156 decodes the mode as `p.dynamicMode = static_cast<int>(slots[0] * 3.0f + 0.5f)`. At slot0 = 0.5 that is int(2.0) = 2.
- temporal_distortion.h:51-66 numbers the modes EnvelopeFollow=0, InverseEnvelope=1, Derivative=2, Hysteresis=3. So 2 is Derivative.
- distortion_adapter.cpp:745-746 clamps the value to 0..3 and passes it to `temporal_.setMode`.

**Where the 0.5 comes from:**
- The ShapeShadowStorage constructor (morph_node.h:102-114) sets every slot of every type to 0.5. Only BitwiseMangler slot0 gets an override (0.0, line 110). Temporal gets none.
- MorphNode's own `shapeSlots` start at 0.5 (morph_node.h:43-44).
- The controller registers each shape parameter with default 0.5 (parameter_registration.cpp:958-961).

**Both type-change paths load that 0.5:**
- Processor: processor_params.cpp:844-852 saves the old type's slots, loads the new type's slots from the shadow storage, and calls `mapShapeSlotsToParams`.
- Controller: `NodeSelectionController::copyDisplayedTypeToSelectedNode` (visibility_controllers.cpp:445-453) loads the shadow slots and calls `editParam` on each proxy.

A newly chosen Temporal node therefore runs Derivative ("Transient" in the UI), not the EnvelopeFollow mode that `DistortionParams::dynamicMode = 0` implies.

**The docs are stale:**
- distortion_adapter.h:127 says "Mode: 0=Envelope, 1=Inverse, 2=Derivative".
- specs-overview.md:219 says "Mode (Envelope/Inverse/Derivative)".
- Both leave out the Hysteresis mode, which is reachable: the UI menu at editor.uidesc:1034 offers "Follow,Inverse,Transient,Hyst".

**No test pins the default:** the only `dynamicMode ==` check is distortion_adapter_test.cpp:2032, a get/set round-trip.

This is a default-value and documentation issue, not a crash or safety issue, so the low severity stands.

Confirmed from source. processor_params.cpp:156 decodes `dynamicMode = int(slots[0]*3 + 0.5)`. ShapeShadowStorage (morph_node.h:102-106) sets every slot to 0.5, and MorphNode::shapeSlots (morph_node.h:43-44) does the same, which gives int(2.0) = 2 (Derivative). The only per-type override is BitwiseMangler (morph_node.h:108-113); its comment already spells out the int(x*3+0.5) decode, so list-slot defaults were known to need care, and Temporal never got one. I found no comment or design note that calls Derivative the intended default. The spec in fact says the opposite: specs/Disrumpo/ui-mockups.md:634 lists the Temporal Mode dropdown default as "EnvelopeFollow". The adapter's own DistortionParams::dynamicMode default is 0 (distortion_adapter.h:127), and that comment lists only Envelope/Inverse/Derivative. specs-overview.md:219 also lists only three modes, while dsp-details.md:451-456 and ui-mockups.md:634 list all four, Hysteresis included. So the docs disagree with each other. No test pins the default: the only dynamicMode test is distortion_adapter_test.cpp:2025-2032, which sets mode 1 explicitly. Nothing upstream clamps or remaps the value, because distortion_adapter.cpp:745 only clamps it to 0..3. The defect is reachable whenever a user picks Temporal on a node that still holds default slots. Impact is cosmetic or default-behaviour only: the user can change the mode and saved state is unaffected. Low severity is right.

The mechanism holds. In morph_node.h:102-114, ShapeShadowStorage sets every slot to 0.5 and only BitwiseMangler gets an override (slot0 = 0.0). The type-change path loads those shadow defaults on both sides: processor_params.cpp:845-851 (shadow.load, then mapShapeSlotsToParams) and visibility_controllers.cpp:445-452 (controller editParam). processor_params.cpp:156 decodes int(0.5*3+0.5) = 2, and in temporal_distortion.h:51-66 that is TemporalMode::Derivative. The doc drift is also real. distortion_adapter.h:127 reads "0=Envelope, 1=Inverse, 2=Derivative" and specs-overview.md:218 reads "Mode (Envelope/Inverse/Derivative)". Both leave out Hysteresis = 3, which is reachable through the menu at editor.uidesc:1034 ("Follow,Inverse,Transient,Hyst").

The stated consequence is wrong, though. The finding says "sustained material is barely distorted" in Derivative mode. temporal_distortion.h:472-477 computes Derivative drive as baseDrive_ * (1 + driveModulation_ * |d env| * k). On a steady signal the derivative goes to 0, so drive settles at baseDrive_, the node's full drive. EnvelopeFollow (lines 455-459) gives that same baseDrive_ when the input sits at the -12 dBFS reference level. With drive modulation at zero, both modes return baseDrive_ (lines 450-452). So a new Temporal node distorts sustained material at its set drive and adds a boost only on transients. It does not do "nothing".

The UI shows the same thing: the COptionMenu bound to NodeShape0 displays "Transient" for 0.5, so the user sees the active mode. There is no mismatch between what is shown and what runs. What is left is a debatable choice of default (index 2 instead of 0) and documentation that misses one mode. That is a polish issue with no audible defect. I am downgrading it below low (cosmetic / doc).

findings.title: DataExchange queue is opened only in setActive(true): a connect() or reconnect that arrives while active leaves the spectrum queue closed
findings.problem: connect() creates a new DataExchangeHandler and calls onConnect only. onActivate(processSetup), which opens the queue, is called only from setActive(true) (processor.cpp:167-168). disconnect() calls onDisconnect (closeQueue) and destroys the handler. If the host connects after activation, or disconnects and reconnects while active, the new handler is never activated. The SDK's getCurrentOrNewBlock/lockBlock then has no open queue and sendSpectrumBlock returns at the invalid-block check on every block. sendModOffsetsMessage likewise runs only in setActive(true), so a late-connected controller never receives the mod-offsets pointer.
findings.why_wrong: The handler needs onActivate whenever it exists while the processor is active. The SDK sample opens it in setActive because it assumes connect precedes activation, but the VST3 spec does not guarantee that order for reconnects.
findings.consequence: In hosts that (re)connect components while processing, the spectrum analyser silently falls back to the Tier-3 SharedDisplayBridge path, or shows nothing if that lookup fails, and the mod-slider overlays stay dead until the next deactivate/activate.
findings.suggested_fix: In connect(), if the processor is already active (track an isActive_ flag set in setActive), call dataExchange_->onActivate(processSetup) and sendModOffsetsMessage() immediately. Test: initialize, setupProcessing, setActive(true), then connect a mock connection point, run process(), and assert a DataExchange block or fallback message was sent.
findings.evidence: processor_messaging.cpp:61-63 dataExchange_ = make_unique<DataExchangeHandler>(...); dataExchange_->onConnect(other, getHostContext()); (no onActivate); processor.cpp:166-170 'if (dataExchange_) dataExchange_->onActivate(processSetup); sendModOffsetsMessage();' inside setActive(true) only; vst3sdk dataexchange.cpp:337-351 onActivate opens the queue, :373-378 getCurrentOrNewBlock -> impl->lockBlock(); processor_messaging.cpp:127-130 returns on InvalidDataExchangeBlockID.
verifier_notes: The defect is confirmed from source. processor_messaging.cpp:36-72: connect() creates a new DataExchangeHandler (:61-62) and calls only onConnect (:63). In the SDK, onConnect (extern/vst3sdk/public.sdk/source/vst/utility/dataexchange.cpp, DataExchangeHandler::onConnect) only stores connectionPoint, hostContext and exchangeHandler; it does not open a queue. The queue is opened only by onActivate -> impl->openQueue, and Disrumpo calls onActivate only from Processor::setActive(true) (processor.cpp:167-168). disconnect() (processor_messaging.cpp:78-82) calls onDisconnect, which runs closeQueue, and then resets the handler. So a connect, or a disconnect followed by a connect, that arrives while the processor is active leaves a handler whose queue was never opened. Impl::lockBlock (dataexchange.cpp:245-249) returns InvalidDataExchangeBlock when !isOpen(), so sendSpectrumBlock returns at processor_messaging.cpp:127-130 on every block until the next deactivate/activate cycle. sendModOffsetsMessage (processor_messaging.cpp:149-165) is likewise called only from setActive(true) (processor.cpp:170), so a peer that connects after activation never receives the ModOffsets pointer. Two things keep the impact small. First, the Tier-3 shared FIFOs are always fed (processor_messaging.cpp:112-121), so the spectrum still has a fallback path. Second, standard hosts connect components after initialize and before setActive, so the window opens only when a host reconnects while active. Low severity fits. One related note: a disconnect or connect while active also swaps or resets dataExchange_ on the UI thread while process() reads it, which is an unsynchronised access, but that is a separate issue.

The code does what the finding says. processor_messaging.cpp:61-63 creates the handler and calls only onConnect. In the SDK, dataexchange.cpp onConnect (around :319-324) just stores the connection point, the host context and the IDataExchangeHandler cast; it opens no queue. The queue opens only in DataExchangeHandler::onActivate, which runs configCallback and openQueue. Disrumpo calls onActivate only from Processor::setActive(true) (processor.cpp:166-168), and sendModOffsetsMessage likewise only from there (processor.cpp:170). disconnect() (processor_messaging.cpp:78-81) closes the queue and destroys the handler. So a handler created by a connect() that arrives while the processor is active never opens its queue. getCurrentOrNewBlock then calls impl->lockBlock() with no queue, and sendSpectrumBlock exits at the invalid-block check (processor_messaging.cpp:127-130).

I found nothing that guards this: no isActive flag, and no re-activation in connect(). The only ModOffsets sender is processor.cpp:170. The controller's cachedModOffsets_ (controller.cpp:1966-1971) is filled only from that message, so a controller that connects late gets no mod overlays.

Two things limit the impact, which is why severity stays low:
1. The standard VST3 workflow connects the components right after initialize, before setupProcessing/setActive. The SDK's own DataExchange pattern also opens the queue in setActive. So the trigger needs a non-standard connect, or a reconnect while active, in the host.
2. The spectrum path keeps working through the Tier-3 shared FIFOs, which are pushed before the dataExchange_ check (processor_messaging.cpp:112-121). Only the mod-offset overlay has no fallback.

The defect is real but latent and depends on the host's call order, so it is not refuted and the severity is unchanged.

The code path is real. processor_messaging.cpp:61-63 builds a new DataExchangeHandler in connect() and calls only onConnect(). The SDK's onConnect (vst3sdk public.sdk/source/vst/utility/dataexchange.cpp:321-326) only stores the connection point, host context and exchange handler. The queue is opened only in onActivate (dataexchange.cpp:337-351, impl->openQueue), and processor.cpp:166-168 calls onActivate only inside setActive(true). disconnect() (processor_messaging.cpp:78-81) closes the queue and destroys the handler, so a reconnect while active leaves a handler whose queue was never opened. lockBlock then returns an invalid block, and sendSpectrumBlock exits at processor_messaging.cpp:127-130 on every block. sendModOffsetsMessage is called only at processor.cpp:170 inside setActive(true). If that happens before any peer is connected, the message is lost. The controller only gets cachedModOffsets_ from the "ModOffsets" message (controller.cpp:1966-1971) and has no other path, so the mod-slider overlays (controller.cpp:1470) stay dead until the next activate.

The impact is narrow, though:
(1) The normal VST3 host sequence (initialize, connect, setupProcessing, setActive) never triggers this. It needs a host that connects late or reconnects while the processor is active. That is legal but uncommon, and no specific host is named.
(2) The spectrum does not go dark. sendSpectrumBlock always pushes to the Tier-3 shared FIFOs before the DataExchange check (processor_messaging.cpp:112-121), and the controller looks the instance up through SharedDisplayBridge (controller.cpp:637-646). So the analyser keeps working in-process, and only the mod overlays are actually lost.
(3) The effect is UI-only. Audio output does not change: no dB, sample or latency effect.

It is a real lifecycle gap with a cosmetic, host-dependent effect. Low is the right severity.

findings.title: Bitwise Mangler 'Bits' slider is permanently hidden dead markup bound to a shape slot nothing reads
findings.problem: TypeParams_Bitwise still declares a 'bits' group with a CSlider bound to Band.NodeShape3. BitwiseOpController always hides that group (showBits = false, 'BitRotate/BitShuffle removed'). mapShapeSlotsToParams reads only slots 0-2 for BitwiseMangler, and DistortionParams::bitwiseBits is documented 'reserved, unused'. The slot stays host-automatable and persisted (node Shape3) with no audible effect for this type.
findings.why_wrong: Removed features should take their view, visibility branch and reserved field with them. Keeping a hidden control bound to a live parameter invites a future 'fix' that unhides it without a consumer.
findings.consequence: No user-visible defect today: the group is never shown. It is maintenance clutter and an automatable no-op for Bitwise nodes, and the inventory's '4 Bitwise controls vs 3 consumed' reading is explained by this hidden group.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the bitwise-group="bits" container from TypeParams_Bitwise (via XSLT, per project rule), remove bitsContainer_ handling from BitwiseOpController and the reserved bitwiseBits field, and drop the 'reserved' shadow default in morph_node.h:113.
findings.evidence: editor.uidesc:1107-1110 <view class="CViewContainer" bitwise-group="bits" ...><view class="CSlider" control-tag="Band.NodeShape3" .../>; sub_controllers.h:338-339 '// Bits control is no longer used (BitRotate/BitShuffle removed)' bool showBits = false; processor_params.cpp:197-202 BitwiseMangler reads slots[0..2] only; distortion_adapter.h:121 bitwiseBits '(reserved, unused)'; morph_node.h:113 typeSlots[bmIdx][3] = 0.5f; // (reserved).
verifier_notes:
I could not refute this finding. Every claim in it matches the source.
- editor.uidesc:1107-1110: TypeParams_Bitwise does declare a bitwise-group="bits" CViewContainer holding a CSlider bound to Band.NodeShape3.
- sub_controllers.h:305-306: BitwiseOpController captures that container as bitsContainer_.
- sub_controllers.h:338-344: updateVisibility always sets it hidden ("Bits control is no longer used (BitRotate/BitShuffle removed)", bool showBits = false). No other code makes it visible again. The only bitwise-group references are uidesc:1103/1107 and sub_controllers.h:300.
- processor_params.cpp:197-202: the BitwiseMangler mapping reads only slots[0..2] (Op, Intensity, Pattern). Nothing reads slot 3 for this type.
- distortion_adapter.h:121: bitwiseBits is commented "(reserved, unused)". A grep of plugins/disrumpo finds no reader anywhere.
- morph_node.h:113: typeSlots[bmIdx][3] = 0.5f; // (reserved).

So the hidden slider is dead markup. For a Bitwise node, Shape3 is persisted and automatable but has no effect.

Two things to add to the finding:
1. The Shape3 parameter itself is not dead. Other types use it, e.g. Chaos "Coup" at uidesc:1121. It is a no-op only while the node's type is Bitwise.
2. The hidden container is load-bearing as written. sub_controllers.h:313 sets the initial visibility only when bitsContainer_ is non-null. If the XML is deleted without changing that condition, the Pattern group's initial visibility is never applied. The suggested fix does say to remove the bitsContainer_ handling, which covers this, but the executor must also edit line 313.

There is no user-visible defect, so low severity is right.

The dead markup is real, and nothing I found makes it intentional or pins it in place.

- editor.uidesc:1107-1110 declares the bitwise-group="bits" container with a CSlider on Band.NodeShape3.
- sub_controllers.h:338-339 hard-codes showBits = false, with the comment "Bits control is no longer used (BitRotate/BitShuffle removed)". Lines 343-344 hide the container every time visibility updates, so it can never be shown.
- processor_params.cpp:197-200 maps only slots 0-2 for BitwiseMangler (Op, Intensity, Pattern).
- distortion_adapter.h:121 marks bitwiseBits as "(reserved, unused)", and a grep finds no consumer of it anywhere in src.
- No test refers to bitwise-group or bitwiseBits. The only test hit, multi_node_distortion_test.cpp:733, is a stale comment that still mentions BitRotate. The archived 006-morph-ui plan lists a "Bit Range" control, which the code comment says was later removed.

So this is leftover markup and code, not a documented design choice.

Two caveats for the fix plan:
- The "automatable no-op" point is overstated. NodeShape3 is a generic per-node shape slot that other types use (TypeParams_Chaos binds it to "Coup" at editor.uidesc:1121), and many types leave some slots unused. The parameter itself must stay. Only the hidden Bitwise view is dead.
- The container is weakly load-bearing. The initial-visibility check at sub_controllers.h:313 requires bitsContainer_ to be non-null. If the container is deleted without also removing that condition, initial Pattern visibility is never set when the editor opens.

No user-visible defect, so low severity stands.

Every cited line checks out. editor.uidesc:1107-1110 has the bitwise-group="bits" CViewContainer with a CSlider on Band.NodeShape3, inside TypeParams_Bitwise (template starts at 1097). In sub_controllers.h, line 306 captures bitsContainer_, lines 338-339 say "Bits control is no longer used (BitRotate/BitShuffle removed)" with bool showBits = false, and lines 343-344 always call setVisible(false). processor_params.cpp:196-201 maps BitwiseMangler from slots[0..2] only (Op, Intensity, Pattern). A grep for bitwiseBits across plugins/disrumpo/src finds only the declaration at distortion_adapter.h:121 ("reserved, unused"), so no adapter or processor code reads it. morph_node.h:113 defaults typeSlots[bmIdx][3] = 0.5f, marked "(reserved)". On the impact lens: the finding itself says there is no user-visible effect. The group is never shown. Automating node Shape3 while the node type is Bitwise only writes a per-type slot that nothing consumes, so the audible effect is 0 dB in every host and setting. That matches the claimed consequence: maintenance clutter plus a host-visible no-op on an automatable parameter. The defect is real as stated and the impact matches "low". No severity change.

I ran them through run-gate.js --share 4, sharded into 36 shards on 7 workers: GATE GREEN, wall 12.5 s, so the 8-minute budget is no concern. The final run printed 551 PROBE lines to f:/tmp/disrumpo-audit/probe-results.txt (raw shard logs in f:/tmp/gate/20261105-203701). Two procedure notes: the filter needed the ~[performance]~[perf]~[benchmark]~[!benchmark] exclusions because run-gate.js refuses a filter without them, and the crossover probes needed a 0.3 s pre-roll because the CrossoverLR4 frequency smoothers ramp after prepare(). The TU is saved at specs/disrumpo-audit/probes/audit_probes.cpp.txt. CMakeLists.txt is reverted, the audit/ folder is deleted, and git status --porcelain plugins/disrumpo is empty. The built exe in build/ still contains the probe cases until the next rebuild.

Main measured defects:
(1) The Processor never oversamples. processor.cpp:487/494 calls BandProcessor::process() per sample, which skips the oversamplers. Aliasing at the 1x and 8x OS limits is identical (-43.3 dB). BandProcessor::processBlock does oversample (18.4 dB less aliasing), but nothing calls it from the Processor.
(2) One mono MorphEngine is shared by L and R (band_processor.h:487-488) and is prepared at 8x the sample rate (band_processor.h:111,124). Effects: R leaks to within 0-1 dB of L for every stateful type tested; the 4 kHz tone filter acts at about 1 kHz; morph smoothing takes 37 ms instead of 10 ms; time-based types are off (adapter-vs-processor centroid ratio 0.08 for SergeFold, 0.28 for FeedbackDist, 0.36 for RingSat).
(3) setupProcessing wipes state. It resets node types and crossover frequencies (processor.cpp:101,114-120). 120 of 121 presets change when setState runs before setupProcessing; 114 change level by more than 1 dB, and Sharp_Focus drops by 187 dB.
(4) Band bypass does nothing on the Processor path. Only processBlock checks bypassed_ (band_processor.h:521).
(5) Neutral settings give -3.01 dB, not 0 dB. This is the centre-pan law (band_processor.h:502-510), and it also leaves a -16.6 dB notch at global mix 50 %.
(6) The sweep is broken in four ways. The LFO advances once per block (processor.cpp:350): 0.24 octave range and 0 cycles where about 4 octaves and 10 cycles were expected. The envelope follower reads one sample per block (processor.cpp:342): 320 ms to 63 % against a 10 ms attack. Bands away from the sweep centre are muted (-125 dB). Intensities above 100 % are clamped away (band_processor.h:197).
(7) Morph clicks: the 4-node cross-family sweep has a jump ratio of 9.9 with 54 clicks, and level dips 13-19.5 dB below the start/end level line. Changing the band count clicks (jump ratio 3.8-3.9).
(8) Silent-input noise and DC: Stochastic outputs -10 dBFS from silence; FeedbackDist and Quantize still sit at -48 dBFS 1 s after the input stops; Tube has DC of -0.04 to -0.067.
(9) Presets: 35 lose audio in a getState/setState round trip. Two fresh loads match exactly, so this is state loss: the files are v10, saves are v12, and repeated saves are not stable (first drift at byte 92, the sweep LFO rate field). 11 presets peak above 0 dBFS from a -12 dBFS input, 39 have |DC| above 0.01, and Rectified_Drums is below -60 dBFS.

What passed: crossover reconstruction after settling (SC-001, max deviation 0.004 dB); the cursor parked exactly on a node (weights finite and sum to 1); no NaN or Inf anywhere, including at 192 kHz; gain, mute, solo, drive and mix steps are click-free.

The measurements list carries every non-ok line, either as its own entry or grouped by class (all 70 bad and suspicious preset lines are in the grouped preset entries, and every preset-hostorder line is in one entry); most ok lines are counted in summary entries. probe-results.txt has every line.

measurements.name: drywet-mix50:bands=2/4
measurements.setup: Processor, all drives 0, global mix 0.5, 0.3 s pre-roll, unit impulse
measurements.note: The dry path is raw input (processor.cpp:502), while the wet path carries the LR4 allpass phase plus the -3 dB pan law, so parallel mixing combs. Dry has no phase compensation.

measurements.name: morph-sweep:4node-crossfamily-planar
measurements.setup: 1 band, 4 nodes planar (SoftClip, SineFold, FullRectify, RingSat) drive 3, 220 Hz -12 dBFS, cursor (0,0)->(1,1) over 2 s, block-rate automation
measurements.note: The largest jump (0.229 at t=1.28 s) happens while the weights move smoothly (0.409/0.220/0.220/0.150), so it is not a weight step. Likely causes: (a) adapters skipped below kWeightThreshold (morph_engine.cpp:745) keep stale state and click on re-entry; (b) four cross-family outputs summed linearly, not with equal power (morph_engine.cpp:756), which explains the 19.5 dB dip; (c) shared L/R state.

measurements.name: morph-sweep:2node-crossfamily(SoftClip-SineFold)
measurements.setup: 1 band 2 nodes Linear1D, cursor x 0->1 over 2 s
measurements.note: The level falls 13 dB below the start/end line mid-path: a linear weighted sum of decorrelated outputs (morph_engine.cpp:756). The spec says equal-power crossfade.

measurements.name: morph-sweep:2node-samefamily(SoftClip-Tube)
measurements.setup: 1 band 2 nodes, cursor x 0->1 over 2 s
measurements.note: The same-family interpolation path (morph_engine.cpp:691-718) is continuous.

measurements.name: morph-onnode (exact/near/close node1, exact node0, centre)
measurements.metric: weights, weight_sum, nonfinite, level delta vs exact
measurements.value: on/near node: w=1.0000 for that node, sum 1.00000, nonfinite 0, level delta 0.000 dB; centre: 0.25 x4
measurements.threshold: weights finite, sum 1, near-node within 0.5 dB
measurements.note: The IDW on-node branch (morph_engine.cpp:217-222, band_processor.h:596-600) handles the singularity.

measurements.name: morph-smoothing:default
measurements.setup: 1 band 2 nodes, default smoothing (10 ms to 99 %), x step 0->1, block 32, 48k, read MorphEngine::getSmoothedX
measurements.note: The smoother is configured at 8x the rate (band_processor.h:124 -> morph_engine.cpp:50-51) and advanced twice per sample (L+R, band_processor.h:487-488): 10*8/2 = 40 ms expected, 37 measured. Every smoothing-time setting is 4x slow.

measurements.name: automation:bandcount2-4-1 (step1, step2)
measurements.setup: default nodes, band count 2 -> 4 at 0.49 s -> 1 at 0.99 s, 220 Hz -12 dBFS
measurements.note: setBandCount changes crossover topology at once (crossover_network.h:111-121, processor_params.cpp:339-346). Bands appear or disappear in the per-sample loop (processor.cpp:483) with no crossfade.

measurements.name: automation:type-switch
measurements.setup: 1 band SoftClip drive 3 -> SineFold node-type step
measurements.note: Type changes swap the adapter type at once (processor_params.cpp:840-855 -> morph_engine.cpp:706).

measurements.name: automation: ok steps
measurements.setup: drive 0->1, global mix 0->1, node mix 0->1, band gain -24->+24 dB, mute band0 on/off, solo band1 on/off, OS max 1x->8x
measurements.value: all jump_ratio 0.92-1.00, clicks 0, nonfinite 0
measurements.note: Smoothed gain, pan and mute work. The OS step is click-free only because oversampling is never active on the Processor path.

measurements.name: bypass:all-bands
measurements.setup: 4 bands SoftClip drive 10, all band bypass on vs off, 220 Hz -12 dBFS
measurements.note: Bypass is honoured only in BandProcessor::processBlock (band_processor.h:521). Processor::process calls process() (processor.cpp:494), which ignores bypassed_, so the band bypass parameter has no audible effect.

measurements.name: sweep:lfo-rate
measurements.setup: sweep on, base 1 kHz, LFO sine 5 Hz depth 1, env off, 2 s, block 512; modulated-freq output param per block
measurements.threshold: about 4 oct range and about 10 cycles
measurements.note: sweepLFO_.process() is called once per block (processor.cpp:350), advancing one sample per 512, so the LFO runs 512x slow and is effectively static.

measurements.name: sweep:env-attack
measurements.setup: sweep on base 200 Hz, env on, sens 1, attack ~10 ms, 0.5 s silence then 1 kHz -3 dBFS
measurements.note: The envelope follower is fed only inputL[0]/inputR[0] once per block (processor.cpp:340-343): decimated by the block size, it is 32x slow and misses transients.

measurements.name: sweep:off-centre-band-level
measurements.setup: 4 bands default, 11 kHz sine -12 dBFS, sweep off vs on (centre 100 Hz, 100 %)
measurements.note: The sweep intensity multiplies the band input before distortion (band_processor.h:481). Bands far from the sweep get intensity about 0 and are muted rather than left dry. Band centres are hard-coded at 100/600/3000/12000 Hz (processor.cpp:422), whatever the crossovers are. Also explains the near-silent Sweep presets.

measurements.name: sweep:band-intensity:intensity=200%
measurements.setup: SweepProcessor direct, width 1.5 oct, centre 100->10k Hz
measurements.note: setIntensity accepts 0-2 (processor_params.cpp:402-408), but BandProcessor::setSweepIntensity clamps to 1 (band_processor.h:197), so 100-200 % is inert.

measurements.name: sweep:band-intensity:intensity=100%
measurements.setup: SweepProcessor direct
measurements.note: No NaN; bounded.

measurements.name: sweep:full-automation
measurements.setup: 4 bands SoftClip drive 3, 4-sine input, sweep 100 %, freq 100->10k over 2 s, LFO 5 Hz, env on
measurements.note: Continuous and finite. The 9 dB level loss with the sweep on is the off-centre muting above.

measurements.name: samplerate:44.1k/48k/96k
measurements.setup: 4 bands Tube/SoftClip/Fuzz/Tape drive 4, 1 kHz -12 dBFS, last 0.5 s, ref 48k

measurements.name: samplerate:192k
measurements.setup: same chain at 192 kHz
measurements.note: No NaN at 192k. The level and brightness drift: band processing is prepared at 1.536 MHz (band_processor.h:111,124), so filter and smoother clamps likely engage.

measurements.note: setupProcessing overwrites every band's morph cache with SoftClip defaults and pushes them (processor.cpp:114-124). crossoverL_.prepare re-runs the log distribution (processor.cpp:101 -> crossover_network.h:79-94). Any sample-rate or block-size change by the host loses the patch.

inventories.summary: Parameter plumbing cross-reference for Disrumpo (read-only). Sides: plugin_ids.h enums and make*ParamId helpers; parameter_registration.cpp (controller registrations); processor_params.cpp processParameterChanges plus processor.h atomics; processor_state.cpp getState/setState; controller.cpp parseComponentState, setComponentState, and createComponentStateStream (the preset writer); editor.uidesc via tools/uidesc-inventory.js (JSON at f:/tmp/disrumpo-audit/uidesc-inventory.json, 453 controlTags, 42 templates). Registered IDs: 621 (globals 9, crossover 3, sweep 35 + 2 read-only outputs, mod 54 + routing 128 = 182, band 4x30 = 120, node 4x4x17 = 272). Every registered ID is consumed by processParameterChanges except the no-op and discarded ones listed below; no consumed ID is unregistered. The 35 sweep-group, 54 mod-group and 16 band-level uidesc tags all resolve to registered IDs. The mismatches cluster into: (a) linear RangeParameter registrations where the processor denormalizes logarithmically (sweep frequency, sweep LFO rate, mod LFO rates, crossover); (b) defaults that differ across registration, atomics, state fallbacks and DSP defaults; (c) preset-writer vs session-writer disagreements (morph mode/smoothing, active nodes, routing source, custom curve); (d) params that are registered and automatable but never persisted (oversample max, band morph links, sweep MIDI); (e) UI-edited custom-curve points that the processor never consumes; (f) uidesc tags for bands 5-8 and crossovers 4-7 that point at unregistered IDs.

mismatches.what: Sweep Frequency registered as linear RangeParameter but processed on a log2 curve
mismatches.where: plugins/disrumpo/src/controller/parameter_registration.cpp:187 (RangeParameter 20.0, 20000.0, 1000.0) vs plugins/disrumpo/src/processor/processor_params.cpp:384-385 (log2Freq = kSweepLog2Min + value * kSweepLog2Range; pow(2, log2Freq))
mismatches.detail: Host normalized default for 1000 Hz is 0.049 on the linear registration; the processor reads 0.049 as ~28 Hz. Controller sweep indicator (controller.cpp:1283-1285) uses the log map, so the readout and the indicator disagree. Also sweep_morph_link.h:52-67 defines the log map.

mismatches.what: Sweep LFO Rate registered linear, processed exponentially
mismatches.where: plugins/disrumpo/src/controller/parameter_registration.cpp:247-248 (0.01, 20.0, 1.0) vs plugins/disrumpo/src/processor/processor_params.cpp:430-434 (exp(kMinRateLog + value*(kMaxRateLog-kMinRateLog)))
mismatches.detail: Default 1.0 Hz is stored as normalized 0.0495 by the host; processor computes exp(-4.2292) = ~0.0146 Hz. processor_state.cpp:497 and controller.cpp (sweep LFO fallback) use the log normalization, so save/load is consistent but the host-facing value is not.

mismatches.what: LFO 1 Rate registered linear, processed exponentially
mismatches.where: plugins/disrumpo/src/controller/parameter_registration.cpp:364-365 vs plugins/disrumpo/src/processor/processor_params.cpp:581-582
mismatches.detail: Same class as Sweep LFO Rate. Default 1.0 Hz maps to ~0.015 Hz in the engine when the host sends the default normalized value.

mismatches.what: LFO 2 Rate registered linear, processed exponentially
mismatches.where: plugins/disrumpo/src/controller/parameter_registration.cpp:400-401 (0.01, 20.0, 0.5) vs plugins/disrumpo/src/processor/processor_params.cpp:612-614
mismatches.detail: Default 0.5 Hz is read as ~0.0146 Hz...

mismatches.what: Crossover frequency registered linear, processed log10; load path normalizes linearly
mismatches.where: plugins/disrumpo/src/controller/parameter_registration.cpp:150-160 (RangeParameter kMinCrossoverHz..kMaxCrossoverHz) vs plugins/disrumpo/src/processor/processor_params.cpp:988-991 (logFreq = logMin + value*(logMax-logMin); pow(10, logFreq)); controller.cpp:210 setter(param->getInfo().id, param->toNormalized(freq))
mismatches.detail: UI edits and preset loads (loadComponentStateWithNotify -> editParamWithNotify) send a linear normalized value that the processor interprets on a log scale, so the audible crossover differs from the displayed Hz. Session restore (processor_state.cpp:451-455) sets Hz directly and is correct, so the two load paths disagree.

mismatches.what: Crossover default frequencies: three different sets
mismatches.where: plugins/disrumpo/src/controller/parameter_registration.cpp:147-149 (log-spaced: 112.2, 632.5, 3556 Hz) vs plugins/disrumpo/src/dsp/crossover_network.h:428-430 (200.0f, 1500.0f, 6000.0f) vs plugins/disrumpo/src/processor/processor_state.cpp:451 and plugins/disrumpo/src/controller/controller.cpp:205 (1000.0f fallback)
mismatches.detail: Processor starts with 200/1500/6000 Hz (no setCrossoverFrequency in processor.cpp setup), the host default is 112/632/3556 Hz, and a truncated stream falls back to 1000 Hz for all three.

mismatches.what: Sweep Intensity displayed 0-100 % but DSP runs 0-200 %
mismatches.where: plugins/disrumpo/src/controller/parameter_registration.cpp:206-209 (0.0, 100.0, 50.0, unit %) vs plugins/disrumpo/src/processor/processor_params.cpp:405 (intensity = value * 2.0f, comment 0-200%) and processor.cpp:289 (modIntNorm * 2.0f)
mismatches.detail: Default 50 % (norm 0.5) produces intensity 1.0 while the atomic default (processor.h:230) and sweep_processor.h:58 kDefaultIntensity = 0.5 correspond to 0.25 normalized.

mismatches.what: Sweep Morph Link: six UI labels, eight processor modes, wrong mapping
mismatches.where: plugins/disrumpo/src/controller/parameter_registration.cpp:217-228 (None, Linear, Inverse, Ease In, Ease Out, Ease In-Out) vs plugins/disrumpo/src/processor/processor_params.cpp:412 (round(value*(kMorphLinkModeCount-1)), 8 modes) and plugins/disrumpo/src/controller/controller.cpp:237 (writes /(kMorphLinkModeCount-1))

inventories.summary: Cross-referenced Disrumpo presets (filesystem, test expectations, generator, preset browser config, CHANGELOG), versions (version.json, version.h, win32resource.rc, CHANGELOG, update config, installers), docs/index.html numeric and feature claims vs code constants, and plugins/disrumpo/CLAUDE.md vs the filesystem. Versions: version.json, version.h, win32resource.rc and the CHANGELOG top entry all agree on 0.9.11. Docs: 26 types and 7 families agree with code; the oversampling description and the Feedback family placement disagree. CLAUDE.md: all listed directories and files exist; controller.cpp is 1991 lines vs the claimed ~2004 (within 20 percent).

gaps.detail: Denormals/FTZ: the brief lists 'denormals in long-tailed filters' as a hazard, but no finding and no probe touches it. grep for _MM_SET_FLUSH_ZERO_MODE/FTZ/ScopedNoDenormals over plugins/disrumpo/src returns nothing (and nothing in any plugins/*/src/processor/*.cpp either), so Processor::process (processor.cpp:180-520) relies on the host for FTZ/DAZ. With the 10 Hz DC blockers running at an effective 1.25 Hz (D-009) and AllpassSaturator/FeedbackDist tails, decays into the denormal range are long. dsp-numerics produced nothing here and no probe timed a decaying tail.

Rectified_Drums renders at -62 dBFS RMS (probe-results.txt:301) but no finding root-causes it. HalfRectify uses an ABSOLUTE amplitude threshold (distortion_adapter.cpp:441-442 `(input >= thresh) ? input : 0`), so a -12 dBFS signal below the threshold is silenced, and the rectify smooth filter cutoff `20000*pow(500/20000, smoothness)` (distortion_adapter.cpp:664-689) is computed for the 8x rate and runs at 1x, i.e. 8x lower in real Hz. The preset (tools/disrumpo_preset_generator.cpp:2623-2636) uses HalfRectify thresh 0.3 / smooth 0.15 on the band that holds 440 Hz. Same hazard class as D-145 (SergeFold nearly silent), whose cause the verifiers also left open.

Inventory mismatches that reach the user but were never elevated to findings: Serge Fold model menu order (editor.uidesc:974 'Simple,Serge,Buchla,Lockhart' vs distortion_adapter.cpp:676-684 models[]={Serge,Simple,...}: labels swapped for two entries; D-135 hides the menu today, but fixing D-135 exposes the swap); Temporal mode labels 'Follow,Inverse,Transient,Hyst' vs enum names and adapter/spec listing only 3 modes (uidesc:1034, temporal_distortion.h:51-70, distortion_adapter.h:127); Bitwise 'Bits' slider bound to Band.NodeShape3 with no consumer (uidesc:1111-1113 vs processor_params.cpp:197-202, distortion_adapter.h:121 'reserved, unused').

Fourteen mod-system parameters are registered with the base Parameter overload carrying unit strings ('ms','Hz','%','deg') but no range (parameter_registration.cpp:378, 435-439, 452-454, 482-506), so hosts and the generic slider text show the raw normalized 0..1 with a unit suffix while the processor denormalizes to 1..100 ms, 0.1..50 Hz, x360 deg (processor_params.cpp:591, 643-746). D-101 covers only sweep/band-count; Route Amount shows -1..1 as '%' (parameter_registration.cpp:602-603). No finding.

Shared-DSP leads from the maps that no finder turned into findings (cross-plugin): Crossover3Way/4Way kAllpassQ = 0.5 with comment 'matches LR4 phase' (crossover_filter.h:423, 643; LR4 sum needs Q 0.7071, as Disrumpo's own network uses) with fractal_distortion.h as a consumer; RingSaturation returns NaN input unchanged (ring_saturation.h ~257); FormantDistortion::process has no finiteness guard (formant_distortion.h:169-195); Waveshaper Diode is documented UNBOUNDED (waveshaper.h:44, :58) and is reachable through curve index 7 in Temporal/RingSat/Spectral/Fractal/AllpassResonant (distortion_adapter.cpp:761-765, 780-784, 833-837, 899, 934) with drive up to 10 and feedback loops; lfo.h:477 `randomState_ * 48271u % 2147483647u` multiplies in uint32 (overflows before the modulus, can reach state 0 and stick) and is used by Profundum's morph modulator S&H/SmoothRandom; fastTanh returns numeric_limits::quiet_NaN() at fast_math.h:68 (ratcheted in tools/lint-nonfinite-symbols-baseline.json:3) and is included by 18 shared headers plus distortion_adapter.cpp.

Oversampler Economy/ZeroLatency IIR attenuation: the shared-infra map computes about -8 dB at 0.5 fs and -14 dB at 0.55 fs for the 8th-order Butterworth at 0.45 fs (oversampler.h:495-519) against the header's '48 dB/oct' claim. Nothing measured it. It matters for the fix plan: the fix for D-017/D-027 is to wire processBlock in, and that would ship this filter as the only anti-alias protection.

The probes lane summary says '35 presets lose audio in a getState/setState round trip'. The preset probe lines only record roundtrip_maxdiff (e.g. Pitch_Tracker 1.25, Chaos_Morph_4 0.226, Chaotic_Sweep 0.163, Pitch_Drive 0.0842; probe-results.txt:286-309); no post-round-trip RMS was measured, and the divergent presets are the ones driven by chaos/pitch sources, where a 1e-5 drift in a saved parameter (D-091's hand-rounded log constants; the preset-rt-bytes lines put the first unstable byte at offsets 92, 136 and 149) diverges a chaotic trajectory without any state being lost. No finding decodes those offsets to fields or shows that audio is actually lost.

D-012/D-120 (stale transitionGains_ when the cursor is exactly on a node): the morph-onnode probe (probe-results.txt morph-onnode:* lines, all 'ok') only PARKED the cursor at exact/near node positions and measured a static level. The failing scenario in the finding (cross-family, smoothing 0, jump from node B to exactly node A so the previous w<=0.001 gain of 0 is kept) was never rendered. The three D-120 verifiers disagree on reachability (first says the scenario cannot happen, the other two say it is reachable with defaults). A measurement would settle it.

No allocation counter and no CPU number back the critical RT findings. D-001/D-002/D-007/D-106 (Spectral re-prepare mallocs per sample) and D-005 (per-sample routeParamsToProcessor) were confirmed by reading only; D-127 notes no allocation tracking exists in the suite, run-cpu-tests.js was not run, and the spec NFR 'CPU < 15 % at 4 bands' is unmeasured for the default same-family path.

No NaN/Inf was ever injected at the processor input. The 'no NaN or Inf anywhere' probe verdict used finite input only. D-013 (EnvelopeFollower latch, sweep centre collapses to 0 Hz) and the Biquad state-wipe click (biquad.h:354) are therefore unmeasured consequences, and D-129 records that the suite has no injection test either.

D-146 was refuted although all three verifiers agree that 'the bands do arrive at different times'. The refutation is on mechanism (tone LP cannot move an impulse peak; the probe's drive-0 reference and processBlock path point at the oversampler), not on existence. The probe ran BandProcessor::processBlock, which the plugin never calls, so the live per-sample path (processor.cpp:467-504) with mixed types per band was never measured for inter-band alignment. Needs a tie-break plus a live-path measurement.

D-021 (centre pan -3 dB, neutral settings not unity): the single refute vote calls the pan law 'a recorded design decision (FR-022)'. specs/Disrumpo/specs-overview.md has no FR-022 and no pan-law text (grep finds only 'Pan: -100% L to +100% R' at :173 and :402); the only FR-022 reference is the code comment in band_processor.h:499. The probe measured -3.01 dB at defaults and a -16.6 dB notch at mix 50 %. The finding stays PLAUSIBLE but the refute vote cites intent without a spec line.

Verifier notes that disagree on CONFIRMED findings and need a synthesizer ruling: D-026, D-081 and D-098 (two of three verifiers call the Feedback and Granular parts overstated; only the Spectral latency is solid); D-066 (one verifier wants low: no audible effect because the link is not in the DSP at all, D-039); D-045 (one verifier says the crash consequence is theoretical and the bounds-check sub-claim does not hold); D-109 (one verifier rules out the SC-001 consequence); D-143 (only part of the DC wording holds). Also an interplay note for the fix plan: the measured 37 ms smoothing (D-138/D-099) is 8x/2 because L and R advance the shared smoothers twice per sample (D-016); fixing D-016 alone makes smoothing 8x slower until D-009 is fixed too.

DataExchange opened only when connect() precedes setActive(true): processor_messaging.cpp:61-63 creates the handler in connect() but onActivate is called only from setActive(true) (processor.cpp:167). A host that connects after activation never gets spectrum data. Two D-004 verifiers noted this while refuting D-004; it did not become a finding.

Files with no finder citation at all: plugins/disrumpo/src/update/*, entry.cpp, controller/animated_expand_controller.cpp (expand request silently dropped when the band is hidden and never re-applied when band count rises, lines 76-81; I checked the cancel-callback concern from the map and it is NOT a defect: VSTGUI Animator::removeAnimation nulls the notification unless notifyOnCancel is set, animator.cpp:308-309), controller/views/sweep_indicator.cpp, node_editor_border.cpp, dsp/sweep_envelope.h (envelopeLevel_ never cleared on disable; RMS > 1 unclamped before the octave shift).

followup_finders.prompt: Tie-break input for D-146 (REFUTED on mechanism, not existence). Measure inter-band arrival time on the LIVE path only: Processor::process at plugins/disrumpo/src/processor/processor.cpp:467-504 (per-sample BandProcessor::process, never processBlock). Build a hidden [.][audit-probe] case in the style of specs/disrumpo-audit/probes/audit_probes.cpp.txt:770-861 that renders an impulse (and a 0.3 s pre-roll) through 2 and 4 bands with each band set to a different type (SoftClip vs Bitcrush vs FeedbackDist vs Spectral vs SergeFold) at drive 1, and records the peak-sample index per band output and of the sum. Compare against all bands SoftClip. Hazard: per-band latency mismatch at summation (phase smear) in the shipped path, the FeedbackDist delay (dsp/include/krate/dsp/processors/feedback_distortion.h:231-340, delayMs 1-100 ms, returns the delayed path), Spectral fftSize latency (spectral_distortion.h:217-249), and whether the tone-LP skip at plugins/disrumpo/src/dsp/distortion_adapter.cpp:225-232 moves anything at all.
